reviews.comment: Her power points are very informative. She is a bit tougher than other teachers, but you are more prepared than other students with easier professors. Overall, almost all of her exams and quizzes are fair. You will just have to study a lot to do well.
Goes too fast with the material. If you take her, don't rely on her lectures. Just study the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I enjoyed this class Professor Stec makes you think. I studied her lecture notes, homework, and discussion worksheets. I ended up with an A, she curves at the end. She tells you what will be on the exam so study it - not that hard. Will take her for gen chem.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I had Stec for 101 and will have her again for 122. Do not buy the book because most of her notes are on powerpoint, which you will have access to. She does rush through things, but if you visit her during her office hours and regularly attend Discussion, then you will be fine.
She has an attitude sometimes. she goes really fast because she put the PowerPoint online. Don't buy the book
Not easily accessible outside of class. Not a good professor. Would not recommend.

WARNING: Go to lectures. Don't expect to pass this class without doing 1) your online homework, 2) reading over the lecture slides and 3) completing the weekly Discussion worksheets. That said, you don't need the book so save yourself the money. Also, be respectful. She really hates people walking out halfway through class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Not a good teacher. Doesn't seems like she wants to be. Avoid if you can.

Stec is honestly an amazing teacher. Most people who say she's terrible don't even show up to class. (You can get away with ditching but you kind of have to show up because lectures are crucial.)  I struggled with chemistry in high school but she teaches well. Some tests are a bit difficult, but  show up and pay attention and you'll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Don't listen to anyone who says she is horrible!!! They are clearly not the sharpest crayons in the box.  I had her for Chem 101 and 112. All you need to do is attend lectures and note what she writes in RED or BLUE on her slides. She hints things that would be on exams and quizzes too. Her tests were based off the lecture notes and worksheets.
Reads off of PowerPoint, you really need to study using the book and basically teach yourself since she goes so fast and sometimes you can't even understand what she's saying.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: WORST TEACHER EVER! HER CLASS IS ALOT HARDER THAN OTHER 123 PROFESSORS! SHE IS THE ABSOLUTE WORST AND DOES NOT EXPLAIN ANYTHING WELL.

Of all of the chemistry professors at UIC, DO NOT TAKE STEC. She has a thick accent that can be difficult to understand. She goes through lessons so quickly, that it is difficult to understand how to do anything. She doesn't really thoroughly explain things. You have to do a lot of learning on your own. She does i-clicker sessions often.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: So much homework now that they separated the labs, its extra work!! Its like taking 2 courses of chemistry. The lecture has a lot of reading & too many online assignments every week. Just attend lecture for iclicker, professor goes real fast... have to self study everything. Also lab TA's are very unhelpful and tough graders.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: If you go to the lectures, you will pass, and well. She makes everything very straightforward. There's a bit of memorization, but honestly it's not bad. She makes things easy to understand by taking concepts like food, and relating it to Chemistry. Don't take her class though if you talk during class or text, she'll call you out.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Respected by students--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Stec is a good and funny professor. She is somewhat demanding, but only because she has high expectations for what students will take away from her course. Yet, she is very reasonable. Exam questions resemble worksheet problems and in lecture examples. With Dr. Stec if you put in the work, you will succeed.

Her class is whatever.  Nothing too incredibly difficult.  She doesn't put anything on the tests that you've never seen before.  Her explaining the lecture notes didn't do anything for me but the notes themselves were useful.

She definitely understands that she isn't the best teacher. However, she curved my class EXTREMELY. Just don't depend on it. Most quizzes were based of the discussion worksheets and problems in the textbook. If you read the textbook and understand it, easy A. Gives easy extra credit :)

The class itself isn't that bad. However, Professor Stec is by far the least helpful professor Ive ever had. First off she has a heavy accent and would always call people out during lecture, which would waste a lot of learning time. Going to her office hours is even worse, she has a very sarcastic tone, and expects you to know everything.
She came in mid-semester and she was much worse than the professor that "resigned"
I would take her class and, in fact, I will be doing so for CHEM 112. She's a good professor. A lot of it is self teaching but if you read the book and do the homework there should be no issues.

It would be a good idea to know the basics of Chemistry. In other words, if you take her class, you better have taken AP Chemistry in your senior year of high school. She goes really fast on the slides, and although she puts the notes online, you end up teaching yourself most of the time. Great personality, but not recommend for learning.

Dr. Stec is a great professor. Her lectures are very straightforward and she does examples in class which are very helpful. Her tests aren't hard if you study and do practice problems. She has a sarcastic attitude, but it's funny and makes the class go by faster. Definitely recommend her.

Dr. Stec is not a professor for everyone. If you think you'll struggle in chemistry, I'd suggest taking another professor. However if you know basic chemistry, she teaches quickly and by showing examples, which is how I learn. Show respect in class and she'll be cool as well.
Very easy class, as long as you show up and read your book you can get an easy A. I got a 106% and a 96% on the first exam/midterm.

She isn't there to help you when you need it. The TA's will be your best friend if you want to pass. Her lectures are just copied and pasted from the book. Very confusing in lectures because she makes tons of mistakes. Expect quiz or exam every Friday, so go to lecture. She likes to have pop quizzes. Very boring and confusing class. Try to switch.

Taught my summer Phys 142. Let me take my 1st exam a week late, explains concepts in ways which allow everyone to understand.Most people in these comments are rating him low due to the slow grading please note that is not his fault, the TA's are the ones who take forever, he frequently emails them requesting for them to be done in a timely manner.
Does not answer to mails. Only reads lecture slides like student
Just reads lecture slides, doesn't answer to mails, and submitted grades 2 weeks after deadline so we were unable to check solutions and ask for regrade requests

He never replies to any email and grades so late. I understand there is alot of homework to grade but I never know what my true grade is unless I use chatgpt. I learned nothing in this class. He reads off of his slides and doesnt do example problems ever. By far one of the worst Professors.

Class content is easy but his lectures are all over the place, he keeps zooming into his slides randomly and is pretty confusing during class. Kinda hard to reach via email so office hours is the move

Professor was alright at explaining concepts. Exams resembled the quizzes and practice exam. My issue is with how tedious and annoying the class structure is. You have a weekly quiz on Tuesday, weekly online hw, weekly written hw, weekly lab starting week 3. It just seems like a lot of unnecessary work and time for a simple class
Do the work and you'll be fine. Professor is super approachable and chill even if you go up to him with no basic understanding he will take the time to explain using different prespective.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: nice dude, very smart, and helpful one on one. However if you don't know much about physics he doesn't take time to go over concepts you technically should know for this class. Most of his lectures are deriving equations and doing practice problems but skipping half the steps. If you want a more all rounder teacher who explains go w hazleton.
personally, lectures were too fast-paced and it was hard to keep up with his teaching style in real time. chad's prep carried me in this class.
Understanding professor, and will help with the material if you reach out. He's also flexible and clear with his lectures.

Would not recommend if you need to take a physics course. He's not the worst professor at UIC, but there are a lot better professors for the same subjects. 

He has his powerpoints and all he does is read from them, monotone voice, not lenient at all. 

PHYS 132 is not that difficult, but this prof seems to make it more difficult than needed.

I would say Randall Espinoza is the most average out of the three in the Physics 142 department, there's a professor worse than him and there's a professor better than him. Physics 142 is already difficult and he teaches on a PowerPoint, but his lectures are still manageable to learn from. Definitely not a class for the occasional ditch

Espinoza is the worst professor I've had. He makes the exams unnecessarily hard without any extra credit or a final curve, unlike literally every other semester for PHYS142 at UIC. He also is rude to students and blames us for not understanding his terrible lectures, where he talks way too fast and does random examples that aren't even on the tests

Solid choice for a professor. His lectures are clearly well-prepared, he makes all resources accessible, organizes the blackboard in a way that makes sense, and is always pretty straightforward with what he expects from you. I like that his lectures are a good mix of thetheory that he explains first, and then practice problems so you can apply it.
Most of the bad things about the class were 100% on the department and not Espinoza. He's a solid option for this weeding out class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I'll start by saying that I don't think that Professor Espinoza is a bad person. In terms of teaching the material, he's average. He isn't horrible, but he isn't exceptional. His main faults are that he doesn't respond to emails, doesn't show up to zoom meetings, is bad at providing disability related accommodations, and hardly grades assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I found his class to be the hardest class I have ever taken at UIC. Most of the question on the exams and quizzes are not from any of the lecture, homework, or study guide. The book can either help a little or not at all. Also note that you are competing against student majoring in physics, so the curve its not that great. Good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This prof explains physics so well during lecture! He really makes you understand the concepts, which makes all the math fall right into place. DO EVERYTHING HE SAYS IN TERMS OF HOMEWORK AND PRACTICE!! ALL of this is necessary in order to do well on the exams and this course in general. This class is v hard, but with practice you'll GREAT!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Doesn't follow the syllabus so scheduled quizzes basically become pop quizzes. Spends a whole hour explaining how to derive a formula rather than explaining how to use it. Literally watched a 15 minute youtube video of something I was learning in class and understood it, while Mr. Randall here spent an entire week trying to teach it. Worst Prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Amazing lectures, don't really have to read the textbook. Just do the end of chapter problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He is an awesome professor. You might feel lost in the class, but trust me you will come through, His teaching might be a little fast, but he is accessible outside of class and he always ready to help. if you study his nits and go through the practice problems you will be fine. Just do your work on time and you will come through

Don't listen to anyone. Espinoza is the BEST professor I have ever had! He comes off as sarcastic sometimes, but if you go to office hours he is super duper down to Earth. Gotta love that guy. #TeamEspinozaForTheWin
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Literally works through examples all period just to have made mistakes in them confusing you even more. Speaks extremely fast and doesn't explain well. Typical for UIC

Always open for questions. His lectures consist of him writing on the board and conceptually explaining physics using his most famous props: phone, headphones, water bottle. The key to doing well in his class is PRACTICE. Do ALL practice problems, ALL homework (but don't restudy those), practice exams, PRACTICE. Attend lecture, take colorful notes
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Definitely the best of the 3 mediocre Phys 142 profs. Usually late/absent for office hours. Manageable quizzes, covers material well . Exams much harder than what he covers since the course coordinator writes them - he has final say. Understanding of engineering rigor, so likely to give points back/curve. Can't mess up a single exam for the A.

Very lazy. He shows up to office hours 45 mins late and thinks it's ok to do so. He does not respond to emails and he purposely disconnected his office phone so that he does not answer. Never went to lecture. I read from the book and got a B. Don't waste your time with someone who does not care.

Professor Espinoza is really good at explaining the concepts. He makes physics look easier. He's very approachable and very helpful if you go to his office hours. He's very sarcastic. Overall, if you do the masteringphysics assignments, go to lecture everyday, take good notes and do the practice exams, getting an a shouldn't be hard.

This class is easier than 141 because of the class structure. The homework is optional and the quizzes are similar to the homework. Exams are more challenging but not impossible. Espinoza is a very nice guy and a good lecturer, but his notes can be hard to follow unless you keep up. Overall good professor and funny too.
One of the better professors I have had. He does a good job in his lectures, and will answer questions you may have. Do the written hw before the quizzes and you will do good.

Very entertaining and always willing to help you plus for the most part clear with his explanations. That's pretty much all you can ask for the physics professor because the class is going to be difficult  no matter what. My only compliant was that he was disorganized and his lectures could seem a little disjointed but nothing too bad.

Espinoza is one of the best teachers I've had at UIC. He actually seems to care about teaching, unlike other professors. His explanations in class are very clear, and his notes are super helpful when studying and doing homework. He's also helpful in office hours. Even though the course is difficult, I still enjoyed it due to his lectures.
This guy is awesome! If all the professors at UIC taught classes the way he does, UIC would be in a much better place.

Really smooth going class, just take notes, re-read them before exam and UNDERSTAND the concepts, memorizing will guarantee a solid D. So just understand how to use the equations and do examples from the book. He also helps if you go in his office hours, he is in office majority of time too.

Fun ans smart. He's unorganized and always late to class, but knows his stuff. He's willing to help, but sometimes talks really quickly. BUY THE BOOK, you will need it understand the material. This class is very hard, but if you study and not fall asleep (it's hard not to) you can do well. Heck, I got an A.

I love astronomy, hated this class. Book is helpful and easy to comprehend, however the chapters are long. online homework on mastering astronomy that is based directly on info from the book. 3 test they are very hard. Do not seem to be 100 level tests. talks fast  and flies through slides. Labs are totally useless. Curves tests & final grade.

Espinoza is...confusing. He seems like a great guy outside of class, but he doesn't seem to be big on astronomy. Hard to understand in lecture due to him not talking loudly. MasteringAstronomy homework makes or breaks you. Tests are very difficult.
He does try to explain thing the best he can, and he actually does a great job. Unfortunately I fell asleep whenever I tried to pay attention to him.

Ezpinoza was really awesome. Randomly always came in a couple minutes late in the 9 am lecture. Really great at explaining the concepts and very easygoing and willing to answer any questions even is they seem dumb. Even though you should do as much problems as possible to do well on the tests
Espinoza is an excellent professor.  He gives quality notes and prepares you for the exams.  His explanations are clear and he answers questions fully.  You won't need the book.
Espinoza is an excellent professor.  He gives quality notes and prepares you for the exams.  His explanations are clear and he answers questions fully.

PHYS 142 is hard so don't let the low easiness score scare you.  If you want to be taught 142 by anyone at UIC it's Espinoza.  Really cool and nice guy.  Not much to say, just go to lecture and take notes.
PHYS 142 is not a hard class if you try to understand the material. I thought he was pretty good. Although lectures could have been more interesting.

Very clear and knows his physics. He works out lots of examples in lecture which are helpful on the homework. Posts past exams online. However, since he is not the "head" of the Physics department he never knows what the curve or when the exams will be finished graded. He's also always around 5 minutes late to class. Good professor overall!

He has been incredibly helpful in explaining the concepts in the homework. He has willingly helped me beyond his scheduled office hours many times. His lectures are well organized and he explains everything very thoroughly.

His notes are very messy, not very clear, and ultimately useless for helping you with homework and preparing you for exams.  The class is horribly structured.  The lab, homework, and lectures are all over the place in relation to each other.  Learn from the book as much as possible.

One of the best professors for physics at UIC. If you need help, his door is always open and he will explain it until you understand it. Great examples in class and his tests are very similar to the hw and practice tests.

He is one of the few best professors I've had. I definitely recommend him when taking physics. He is genuinely nice and helpful towards students. Posts practice exams and is just always willing to help you. He's funny too.
He is an awesome professor. Explains material very well. He knows his stuff. He is very helpful. It is not him that us hard, it is the material; physics is a very tough class.

He was very bad at teaching. It was very hard to understand him and he talked very quietly for a big lecture class. The lectures were extremely boring, he just went over powerpoint slides. And the lab classes dont have anything to do with the actual class. He even put questions on the test that were from homework he hadnt assigned already.

He is a very nice professor, easy to approach, even for the more quiet students. He took time to go over countless problems before the exams, during class and also during his office hour. People who criticized him below, did not put in the effort for this class( PHYS 105 or 107). You can get a B if you just try a little. I  recommend taking him.

Solid physics prof, very helpful with homework problems. Enjoyable teaching style. And my favorite thing: he draws the straightest lines I have ever seen. I mean seriously, nobody draws a tangent line like this guy.

He's extremely helpful if you your time to go to his office and ask questions. He's funny and approachable, so PLEASE is you don't understand something, go to his office and he'll be more than willing to help you. He's probably one of the best teachers for physics at UIC! Also he's always in his office, so use his help and you will do well!!! :)
He knows physics but is horrible at teaching. Its hard to understand what he says. He loves to derive formulas and he is not helpful at all. There is usually a big curve in the class

I've had Espinoza for 105 and 107..already having a degree from another university and countless of other teachers he's in my top 5 worst teachers.  -Talks quiet.  -Late to class (10-15 minutes).  -Have made countless office appointments with him only to have him not show up. -Never at office hours.  UIC needs to revamp this class.
Great teacher, very helpful. The course is difficult but nothing that cannot be mastered. I love Espinoza!

Of all the terrible teachers I've had in my life, this guy is in the top three. he had no motivation to teach and that was evident in his lectures where it seemed he would slump over his lectern and nearly fall a sleep as he explained complex physics to us.The avg grade on his test were F's,but he does curve. Basically avoid him like the PLAGUE!

He is nice teacher, but speakes very softly. There is a lot of info to memorize and tones of HW which is due every monday. So be ready to study a lot. Also his midterms are extremely hard and do not match the book.

He does talk very quietly so I would recommend sitting in the front. I would not say his accent is so thick that it's impossible to understand though. However, he is able to explain and diagram problems very clearly on the board. The only problem is that he does not design the course/test so he doesn't know about grades/curves/tests/etc.

Nice guy, but stinks at explaining things. Hard to understand what he was saying because hes such a lowtalker and because of his thick accent. I'm sure he knows what he's talking about, but I sure didn't. My suggestions; read the book a lot or try a different professor.

Electricity and Magnetism is much harder than Kinematics.  As said by practically everyone, he is probably the best teacher to have in the Physics department.  I got a B in the class even though I'm more of a Chemistry guy.

This is a really difficult class, but Espinoza is the best professor at UIC for the physics department! HE ACTUALLY DOES EXAMPLES! He doesn't teach everything in theory like all the other professors! If you can take him DO IT! Go to his office hours he is so helpful!
great teacher, tough class. what can you do? its physics. Espinoza is there to help you succeed, and he is pretty funny
Extremely hard class, but that doesn't mean it's the teachers fault. Espinoza is extremely helpful if you go see him, and trust me, you need to. Physics is HARD!

I love Espinoza. He made physics incredibly easy. He gave loads of examples in class while also showing how to derive the formulas. I never even had to open the book to study. I only used it for practice problems. He's also really funny.
wow, this guy, do not take him, really hard to understand, all he does is examples, just avoid him, PERIOD! take anybody else if you can.
He's is hard to understand at times but he is a pretty good teacher and funny too! I would suggest buying the book because it is very helpful!

Class is impossible but he'll do anything he can to help.  Offers tons of office hours, and extra practice problems.  He needs to be more intouch with the course coordinator so he can better answer questions about the class.  No clue about what will be on  the exam or what the grading scale was.

This class is hard no matter who teaches but there is always a curve.  Definitely go to class, he wants to help, he'll post extra problems to help on the exam.  Worst part is the coordinator does the exam so he doesn't know what will be there.

He doesnt know how to teach at all, very clueless, doesnt even know what the curve policy for the class is or what edition of the book we are using, the only thing he knows is physics, but he cannot teach, all he does is derive formulas, do not take him

This is a highly practical, project-based course. I discussed the projects during my internship interviews, and they played an important role in helping me secure my internship, I use the knowledge I learned from the course at my internship daily. Dr. Esmailbeigi is very supportive of her students and her advice helped plan my path.
Not worth the stress or impracticable teaching practices. Hananeh elucidates the worse of UIC and I implore you not to take her course as it's not worth your valuable educational journey and time.

This class was one of the best and most creative courses I have taken. We worked on six projects, and the professor was incredibly supportive and consistently provided inspiring, constructive feedback. I learned so much throughout the semester and now have a strong portfolio of work that reflects my growth and accomplishments in the class.
One of the best professors at UIC. She is very knowledgeable about her field and explains the material very well.

Dr. Esmailbeigi is one of the best professors I have had at UIC. She creates a very welcoming environment for her students to learn. CS 479 isn't a hard course, but you HAVE TO put in the work and work with your team. I highly recommend and enjoy the course!

This course gave me experiences that I ended up using in my PhD research. The projects I developed helped me land the position I had always dreamed of. Thanks to the Professor, I got into my dream school.

This course opened my eyes to possibilities I hadn't considered before! She is passionate about helping students explore diverse career paths and opportunities. She brings in inspiring speakers, shares valuable resources, and connects us with professionals in the field.

Professor Esmailbeigi is incredibly knowledgeable, passionate, and supportive. Her courses are very engaging, and you learn a lot. She genuinely cares about her students' success. Challenging but fair, one of the best professors I've ever had.

Dr. Hananeh Esmailbeigi is an incredible professor who consistently goes above and beyond for her students. I had the privilege of taking three courses with her: BME 479, BME 494 and BME 576. In each of these, she pushed me to think critically, expand my creativity, and deepen my understanding of biomedical engineering.
It was a very useful class; I learned a lot and enjoyed it more.
Be precise, on time, and put effort into what to do, and it will be a wonderful course.
Took CS 479 with her. If you enjoyed the Arduino part of CS 362, you'll like this class. You're put into groups of four and work on a few two week long labs, and then final project of your choosing.

479 wearable tech- the professor just explains the basic concepts to make the device, and provides videos which walk you through it, which was very helpful. wish we got more guidance on the cs side. lab period isn't enough so be prepared to work outside of class A LOT. Grading wasn't harsh, just make sure to have most of the necessary components.
Useless class for a senior or junior. Mandatory attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very harsh professor. Assigns groups you stick with through out the semester and if your group isnt good, good luck. Workload is super heavy.

What a disaster she should not be teaching classes. Do not take this class as every resource provided is unclear and full of mistakes. Barely updates the class with details even for the final there is no write up. Go watch some youtube videos on what you can do with arduino and youll be better off
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: BioE 240 is simply Matlab coding. Just attend the classes and pay close attention to the lectures. She is always open to take questions so go to office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She can come off as rude or demeaning at times, but she means to be motivating whenever she addresses her students. If you're not up to her par with your abilities in class, she will let you know bluntly. Take this as a challenge, instead of a personal attack, and she will push you to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: The material learned in this class is interesting and can be even fun, but the professor is super condescending and rude. She says she wants you to ask questions if you do not understand s/t but then when you do she makes you feel stupid. I would not take her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Overall, she is a good professor. I just wish it was not so fast in the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Esmailbeigi is exceptionally passionate about bioengineering, and it carries over to her lectures. She clearly wants all of her students not only to succeed, but to master the material, and the class is set up to facilitate that. The projects are fun and do not exceed the scope of the class. The TAs give good feedback, and exams are manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed the class, and I felt like I got so much out of it. Yes, coding can be hard, so if you ever are struggling, go to her office hours. Falling behind sucks because everything just builds upon each other. Take notes in class, and always review the powerpoints. You need to put in the effort to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Cares a lot about her students' learning. Overall a great professor.
Professional Development course, zero credit but required for graduation.

Great professor, it was my first time working with MATLAB and i really struggled but she helped me through it outside of class and I am a much better coder now because of it ! I have used MATLAB in every course since

Pay attention in class! Practice outside of class. Help is there just don't procrastinate and wait at the last min to ask! straightaway. Professor is interactive so don't be shy to ask questions. Exams are a little difficult but they are manageable. DON'T SKIP CLASS, b/c quizzes. Stuff you will learn is important in later classes, so learn it!

Even though it is just workshop, it such a great help! it helps you orient your goals and how to prepare for them. PARTICIPATE in this class it is very student focused and what we want to learn and talk about. the feedback is what you're after in this class so take it seriously even if it is a 'workshop class'

This class is really helpful to build your resume, interview skills, whatever. What you do in class is based on what people in the class want help with. Awesome class that is very easy and very helpful.
The class requires a lot of coding in Matlab. If you are good at coding the homework is not too hard, but if you aren't it can take a long time.

Dr. Esmailbeigi is a great professor. She makes the class engaging instead of her just talking the entire time. She will teach you how to use MATLAB and then use it to analyze signals. You must put in the effort and practice if you want to be  good at MATLAB .

Hananeh is a one of kind professor, and I don't mean that in a good or bad way. She does things very differently but expects you know alot of things. First exam was all MATLAB and very difficult, average was a 50. To get an A, you have to study like crazy, b/c alot of surprise questions appear on the exams and the final as well

The class was almost entirely run by the TAs which definitely knew how to help you. This is a laboratory class, so there isn't much you can say about the instructor. I guess she did a good job introducing each of the labs you had to do, but I can't recall a single instance in which she successfully troubleshooted a circuit. She tries though...

Dr. Esmailbeigi is the instructor for this bioinstrumentation lab. She is in attendance in all labs, and she or the teachers assistants are available for help. She cares about all students, and expects them to work hard. Be sure to understand the prelabs before coming to lab. The lab assignments need to be taken seriously from the start.

Dr. Esmailbeigi is a fantastic instructor for this course. She cares about her students success and their comprehension of the material taught. She teaches students how to use MATLAB, and then challenges them to apply it in signal processing problems. I do not believe that this course is difficult, but you need to approach it maturely.

She genuinely wants to see students learn the material, and she's happy to answer questions in class. The presentations can be a bit lengthy, but they're posted online for ample reviewing before quizzes/tests.

Your circuits will fail numerous times due to human error. However, you will learn to troubleshoot circuits, which is a vital skill. The instructor balances circuit theory with applications. You have two weeks for a lab with open lab hours. An "A" is earned, not given. Do the work and ASK for help, don't wait around. The instructor WILL help you.

She is one of the worse professors in BioE department. She changed the syllabus and way class was run a few times  before she made up her mind. She only used 1st chapter of the "required" textbook (which is free to view on amazon). However, she is still a new professor, so she will most likely get better at teaching after few years.
hard but useful class.
Favorite professor ever

During this class, I could tell that she was passionate about what she was teaching. She entered every lecture with laughs and smiles and was happy to tell stories. There is a lot of reading required for the class as well as attendance quizzes (super easy if you do the reading). She is very understanding and adjusts for her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Her lectures are very informative and they incorporated discussions. She is very accommodating and will work with you. There are only 2 essays with a few small assignments but that's it. Attendance is counted through short quizzes on the readings due for that class but she does drop the lowest 5 quizzes. Apply effort and it's an easy course.

Professor Vasquez was super cool. We had such amazing enlightening discussions in her class. I learned so much information, a lot of it very sad. Structure of the class was a 1-2 short assignments and 2 readings per week, and a case-study research based essay for the final (worked on throughout the semester). She is very accommodating & kind.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This professor is great, he teaches very well you just have to pay attention, his explanations are good too however he does have a accent, its not as bad but you can tell. He also takes questions between the topics to check if anybody is falling behind, however he does have a strict policy against cheating and using AI so please don't do them.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He's genuinely so funny and passionate about what he teaches. His lectures are as engaging as can be and he's extremely clear about what's expected of you. He does go fast and will get mad if you're visibly distracted or on your phone. Email warrior, but you will appreciate the constant reminders for upcoming due dates and exams.

Previous ratings are over-exaggerated. Kobotis is just a professor with traditional expectations: students are expected to pay attention to lectures, take notes strictly, and ask questions at appropriate times. His teaching style is clear, and repetition works. Exams are the same as practice guides. It's just on you to review after break.

He has a unique teaching style. For example, he will call you out if you're talking or using your phone but he's an excellent explainer, and I learned a lot from him. However, his exams carry a lot of weight, so doing poorly on even one can cause your grade to drop by an entire letter.
Dont expect to use your digital note taking apps to take notes. It will backfire on you. Just consider other sections with someone else.
Not nice, but very good at teaching
Very eccentric professor Teaches well, but seems angry often for very silly reasons
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He will literally hold your hand through the entire course and lead you to passing with an A. I'd recommend watching the lectures beforehand, and then going to class. Very straightforward and easy to understand. He's quite strict during lecture but it is understandable, not to mention he's funny. Shout out to his amazing TA, Ryan Carpenter.

Professor Kobotis gives feedback on graded assignments before they're due and is an easy grader. He doesn't require note-taking, as his lectures are structured like storytelling. He is, however, extremely strict with assignment submissions and will not accept them even if they are a bit late, so either notify him beforehand or complete them early.

in person lectures are not helpful, he vaguely explains the material and will waste 5 minutes of class time if he is 'interrupted' (someone checking their phone), also rambles about being disliked and a bit rude. video lectures and practice problems are uploaded almost daily, and the exams are exactly like the given study guides. grading is relaxed

He's a great professor who wants his students to do well. He lays out his rules very clearly in the syllabus and on the first day of lecture. Is he strict with his rules on phones and computers? Yes, but he laid that out in the syllabus and all he asks is for your attention and respect in lecture. All lectures, study guides are all uploaded.
He loves Mathematics and hates the movie good will hunting.

Kobotis gives really good lectures. He is also the only professor who seems to actually enforce his rules.   If you talk/use headphones/scroll during lecture be prepared for a death sentence. AMAZING TAs (Ryan Carpenter). The only downsides to this class were the MyLabs (useless) and it being 8AM. also he tells u EXACTLY whats on the midterms lol.

He is strict and expects a lot of respect. He will call you out for whispering or being on your phone. However, he creates short and detailed videos that are extremely helpful for each rule and problem, which is soo beneficial for exam preparation.

Like the other reviews say, he is strict. But if you're respectful and do whats expected he's fair. He prepares you well for the quizzes/exams, we had two exams and a one question quiz almost every lecture. Homework was worth ~25% and overall massive curves.
All i did was show up, jot down notes during lecture, do the homework, and passed easily with an A

dr. kobotis is one of the few professors who actually cares about his students. he indeed has some rules that may seem a little odd, like not chewing gum or resting your feet on the seats, but realistically, as long as youre a respectful and decent human being, you're gonna be just fine. if you behave, he's a cutie pie! loved him and his class

I get it with the cell phone policy and all of that, but if I'm just taking notes on my IPad, I have to sit in the front 3 rows to do that or I get called out for it? Pretty dumb rule but oh well I guess. I'll just be sticking to notebook for this year.

Kobotis craves power and control, enforcing strict rules that create a good learning environment. However, he's rude and treats people poorly, acting like an emotionally immature parent. After just two days with him, he seems like a good teacher but an impolite person who yells when you don't immediately follow his instructions.

I enjoyed his class a lot. He makes it clear that he wants all his students to succeed and his actions and teaching reflects that 100%. Just go to lecture, PLEASE go to discussion, and do the easy homework assignments. If you do all these things, the exams will be super easy!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Honestly a great professor, he can make the class laugh while providing a good teaching experience, just don't get on his bad side and everything will be fine

He can be a bit harsh especially if you're on your phone, talking, or putting your feet on a chair. He'll take time out of class to talk about these things. But he's an incredible and very clear lecturer. He gives great examples in class and answers questions very well. He's overall a brilliant instructor.

Such an annoying professor, always gets bothered by everything. I have never met another professor who takes the time out of lectures to call people out for being in their phone or being seated a certain way. Do not recommend, and would not take again!

I think that Professor Kobotis is a great professor, what he teaches in lecture directly reflects what is on the homework, quizzes, and exams. I also think he was great at explaining concepts and answering questions. The only thing is that it got annoying how he would call out people in class for the dumbest things like being on their phone.

Good professor who knows what he is doing and is passionate about what he teaches. He often provides examples in class which can help you understand the concept more and he cracks occasional jokes. However, he does often call students out for chewing gum, talking, whispering, or being on your phone which got very annoying. Very solid professor.

Kobotis runs a tight ship, but engaging with his system pays off. Lectures are worth attending to understand the concepts. Supplementing with resources like chatGPT and unstuckstudy AI can really help make this course manageable.

I took this prof because everyone said he was great, it turned out to be both true and false. He is great at calculus, though he is terrible at applied linear algebra. He skips steps, doesn't explain concepts well, makes many mistakes, repeatedly complains, and more. Avoid him for Math 310.

I have mixed feelings about this professor. He is extremely strict in the classrooms, attendance is mandatory, condescending tone, etc. However, I believe he really cares about his students and want them to succeed. His classroom rules are only there for you to focus and pay attention.

This professor has been course coordinator of Calculus 3 for over 10 years. Everything becomes muscle memory for him. In lecture he skips steps and just writes the solutions because he's taught it so much. His exams are copy and paste from previous semesters with values switched. I don't like his serious demeanor and  he has an arrogance to him.

Professor Kobotis knows his stuff, sure, but he thinks his knowledge gives him an excuse to be rude and condescending to students. I tried to get help from him after class and I could not believe how rude he was. Only take his class if you are an emotional masochist.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Definitely take Kobotis for Calc 3

Kobotis is an amazing professor. He has some rules (no talking, no chewing gum), but they are totally reasonable as you go to lecture to learn. Class overall was fairly easy. Homework is easy (if you need help on it, look at the exam guides!). Exams are also easy if you look at the exam guides for review.

Kobotis is an amazing professor who clearly loves mathematics. Most classes are lectures and there are quite a few quizzes (really easy, pretty much memorization). There are two group papers and presentations, and there are quite a few movie reviews as well. It is really easy to get an A as long as you do your work. I would for sure take him again.

Kobotis is a Good Professor who very clearly cares about mathematics, but he is quite strict about classroom rules (Gum, whispering, leaving early, being on your phone etc.) and is known to call students out during class and presentations.
Easy

I have a high A in this class without attending lecture ONCE, but beware that your lack of attendance will drop ALL grade letters. So I dropped it at the end-of-semester. My advice, just take calculus online in Chicago Community Colleges for a lower price. Also Kobotis was rude until I gave him my letter of accommodations. Proves that he's biased.

Despise his power trips and big ego, he has a reputation. Beware of him walking up to you and calling you out over nothing. I watched him accuse people, then actually he laughs as if that wasn't embarrassing for him. If you got Covid or are sick, he'll force you to come to class anyways. Okay class though. Just avoid the professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: As course coordinator, Kobotis has been teaching this course for 5+ years. He knows the material like the back of his hand. The Mylabs should be scrapped, they don't relate to lecture material and are brownie points that don't contribute much gradewise. During exams, he tensely stares at students for long periods to make sure no one is cheating.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very direct and expects you to be good at what is presented. Use the study guides for tests and do the homework for an easy A. My only issue is how much attitude he gives when answering students as if we should be reading his mind. He had us learn how to solve a rubix cube for easy extra credit and he is also quite an interesting guy. Alsono phones
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Tends to overcomplicate almost every topic taught. He's also very hard to understand because his explanations are very vague. He also tends to get offended when answering questions during lecture. I 100% say that his TA's teach the course rather than himself...

He is the BEST math teacher! His lectures are really interesting. We had 2-3 homework per week and 1 quiz per discussion. Pay attention in class and you'll do fine. The exams were SUPER easy, they are the same as his study guide, except he only changes a few numbers. He gives extra credit if you know how to solve a Rubik's cube.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Genuinely an amazing math teacher. Lectures are captivating and he explains everything so well. For Math 170, there was a pretty substantial amount of homework but it was easy. I sometimes asked my TA to solve the problems during discussion if I was stuck. Do the exam review guides! If you feel confident in those, you'll do amazing on exams!

Class is easy and the material is easy. Never paid attention in class and did well. Although the course is easy he on the other hand has made me dislike the class. He's very uptight and rude. Unlike other professors who understand that we're adults and treat us as such, he treats people with condescension. He also over complicates stuff.

Math 210 is a very well designed course. even if kobotis is not your instructor you can trust that as long as he is the course coordinator the expectations and course layout us very clear and easy to learn as long as you give it a good but of effort. 

exams are near identical to practice tests and HW. Use this!

Professor Kobotis was a very fair professor who had a clear grading scale (81+ was an A, 65-80% a B). I am not the best at math (which as a STEM major, yikes!) but lessons were transparent and easy to understand. He has answer keys for midterm exams, final exams, and quizzes that are similar to the ones you'll take. Make sure to practice!

He is an extremely fair professor. Everything on exam study guides will be on an exam. He also has two extra credit opportunities. One is a presentation of a mathematician, the other is to learn and solve a rubiks cube. He sometimes does have power trips and goes off on tangents but it is bearable. He is also very funny.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Has fair grading scale with an A=81%+ and B=65-80%. Funny guy that is not afraid to call you out in the middle of lecture to tell you to put your phone away or feet off the chairs.12 HW probs a week so not bad. Final counts as 30% of your grade and both exams count for another 30%. If you miss a couple of days and he drops a letter grade so prepare
There were way too many mylabs assigned. Calls you out in class if you leave early or on your phone for a few seconds. The lectures are okay but often times it's hard to understand him.

I'm a STEM major but I'm terrible at math. This class was the only required math course for my major. Honestly, I dreaded this class because I have never taken a calculus course before. I passed this class because the structure of the course is super transparent and it's always clear what you have to study to pass. Just practice the material a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: When is comes to calc 3 he's very bad at explaining concepts and gets side tracked a lot.
His passion for math clearly shows and he explains things really well.

Every test is exactly like the study guide given, the problems are the same except with some numbers changed. If you do the study guides before tests and know them very well, you will 100% get a good grade in the class. Very clear and easy when compared to MATH180. Also the grading scale for the class is very generous, a low 80 being an A.

It was one of the most experiences of my life taking this class back in 2018. He is so rude and will have constant power trips interrupting the class for the dumbest reasons ever.I talked to him several times about help and he was plain rude! thanks to him I changed my major. AVOID HIM
He's a fair professor.
Do not recommend.

Made the material very easy to understand and allowed plenty of practice for the class to catch on and learn thoroughly. He is stern about showing respect in the classroom, so no talking or texting, but I think that shouldn't bother people too much. He also offers extra credit by learning to solve a Rubiks cube.

reviews.comment: Showing up to class is pointless he sucks, just read the book!

I think Prof Kobotis is the only actually good professor at UIC. He is a little strict about talking and chewing gum. The homework is easy, he gives the quiz answers the night before the quiz. Attendance isn't mandatory but there are daily quizzes so it would be hard to pass if you don't ever attend. I miss this class so much.

reviews.comment: I finished this class with a C unfortunately even though I rated this professor 4 stars because his class materials were fair.  I didn't pay attention to his lectures. reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Tbh I took this class years ago but just remembered his weird power complex and wanted to write that in here. Class not impossible just time consuming.

reviews.comment: Class is about prime numbers and some theory around it. He goes off tangent a lot, but there are like 6 quizzes. There is a final project too but it's simple
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: The class itself is pretty easy; discussions always have quizzes though they're very easy and if you miss it just email your TA. Study guides will help for exams and ask him if you need more help. He takes attendance seriously and has his own way where he says a word and asks you to type it in the chat before he types done. Try not to miss it lol.
Awesome funny dude. Makes topics very interesting and literally tells you exactly what kind of questions are gonna be on his exam.

Terrible at online teaching. Attendance is like that State Farm fishing meme of "you almost had it" because of you send the key word a split second after he says done he says it won't count towards attendance but it's okay because "you can skip 3 or 4 before dropping a letter grade" even though it happens often.

Terrible online professor. I can tell he is a good teacher but his method of synchronous teaching is a awful. Simply must be told to anyone looking to take his courses. AVOID HIS SYNCHRNONOUS CLASSES! Synchronous is where you have to show up on Zoom with him and follow along. Overall, good professor just absolutely awful online.
prof Kobotis is so passionate about math and honestly his class just made me excited to learn again. he's super funny too. and story times in class are absolutely amazing

reviews.comment: Its a shame that a professor who is passionate about mathematics is horrible at running a class. There have been instances where a student asks a genuine question and is told its too basic for him to answer.
