Very knowledgeable professor, with a well-respected career in Jazz. Homework was only a multiple choice test per unit that you can retake as many times as you wanted. Only "hard" part was that you have to attend a Jazz concert in person. A bit of a tough grader with the concert review paper but there's an easy bonus quiz that should make up for it.
This class is easy but he does not accommodate students with disabilities!
Very good, easy online class in which you could tell the professor cared about the subject matter.

Would have given Professor Ibragon 5/5 had it not been for one thing in particular: the writing assignments. Don't get me wrong his class is not difficult at all and it is interesting, but for the writing assignments he gives us vague prompts with no rubric and grades it, leaving my classmates and I to wonder what we did wrong with no feedback.

Everyone knows he uses the same exams and homeworks from previous years, so you need a plug from previous semesters. For me he used all the same problems but would change the numbers. Final exam is difficult to find though since it is graded after you are out, and the exams are 70% of the grade.

The course is structured well, and the homework is not too bad. The course content itself is very important to understand, especially for mechE's, and Iranmanesh teaches it well. The only issue is that he is boring, but I found him very concise in the lecture, and he will give hints for the exams.

The professor was very respectful to the students and truly wants them to learn. At times, I did find myself falling asleep in lecture. Nonetheless, the syllabus is very straightforward. As long as you have done the homework and show up to lecture, you will do well on the exams and in the course.
The lectures were really boring, he's a mellow guy. Just go to class and take the notes. Try homework without external help (AI) and you should be good. He also makes the exams very simple
Attend lecture and take good notes and you can pass easily.
Content is pretty hard but the professor makes it easier since he gives guided notes. Exams are open notes.

The class material is hard but the professor makes it manageable by letting you use notes on exams. The lectures do drag and get boring sometimes and the professor can be hard to reach by email sometimes. Hes very nice and knowledgeable and this class is an easy B if you study the practice exam the night before
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took him for the 301 and 310. He gives lots of examples and handouts which are extremely helpful for note-taking and the open book exams. I think Professor Issa and Professor Iranmanesh alternate each semester for teaching the concrete courses. If I had to choose, I'd go with Iranmanesh every time, hands down. Will be taking him next semester too.

One of the nicest professors Ive ever had. He gives practice exams that you can use during the exam since it is open notes and open book. He goes over examples step by step with the class to make sure everyone is doing it right. Only assigned 8 homework assignments. Only bad thing about him is that he teaches at a very slow pace that can be boring

He is extremely thorough with his notes. CME 310, being a design class, requires a lot of calculations and step-by-step solutions. Professor Iranmanesh shows examples clearly and asks the class to solve along with him to catch any errors if any. His PowerPoint slides are not pretty but have all information needed. Great guy nonetheless.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is one of the best professors I have ever had. His knowledge and passion for the subject got me interested in the subject, which I did not expect. He was extremely thoughtful of his students' needs and always had a positive attitude. The class material was hard but his explanations were right on the money and he was accessible outside of class.

Igor is a great professor for learning; he explains concepts clearly and knows the material well. However, he accused me of using AI to copy assignments, even when I used AI only as a learning tool for a few questions. Despite defending myself, he didn't respond to emails and gave zeros for HW, costing me 10%. 
My advice: Only write enough info.
He understands his material so well and will actually explain anything to you. truly cares about his area of research and is highly respected. Also funny.

Dr. Paprotny is the best professor & researcher for MEMS at UIC. ECE 449 is the only class where you can get hands-on and valuable experience in process engineering. This class is a must-take; the labs are exciting, fun, and you will learn a lot. Dr. Paprotny is also a very cool and friendly guy. He inspired me to pursue a career in MEMS.

Professor Paprotny well known MEMs professor at UIC. He inspired me to pursue a path of research in nanotechnology. He helped grasp very complex topics and provided confidence in learning things way above my head. You will love any class he teaches.
The best professor. He is an expert in MEMS. ECE449 has wonderful laboratory with real clean room experience and fabrication. Must Take class. Lot of knowledge and exposure.
Great professor, Great guy.

His lectures are posted on Blackboard making studying for exams much easier.  Allows an 8.5" X 11" cheat sheet for exams and the final.  The lectures are interesting and content is expanded upon very well. He is able to offer help with the Cadence projects.
He's a very nice professor. He takes time during lecture to answer any questions you might have during class. Very knowledgeable. Wish he could be my professor for my other math classes too
He is very sweet and tries to make math more fun that's i think in my opinion he is such an amazing math professor and he has drop in hours that are very helpful. I would diff take again

He is a very knowledgeable and straightforward professor. He is always looking to maximize class time and may sometimes speed through some lectures, but when there is confusion or questions, he'll take time to elaborate. Nice and funny vibes from the guy, would highly recommend.

Class was all group work and 0 lecturing. This class was really dependent on working together with others. Must go over and understand content by yourself outside of class or you WILL be lost. He was very funny and supportive, but was unclear with why things were wrong. With the nature of the class its hard to give feedback but I got close to none.
Not recommended. There are no formal lectures, and you have to read everything on your own.

This class is probably unlike most classes you've taken for math. There is rarely one answer for a problem, and as long as you can make a valid case as to why your answer is correct, and you made no mistakes, you'll get full credit. He is extremely helpful for this type of class as he will really read over every single word and give good feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: He never lectures: you read a bit on the concept of the day/week & do worksheets / present problems on those in class. Honestly, the exams aren't bad at all. He wants good formatting on proofs, which seems to get many people tripped up. Honestly, just make your work look good. HE isn't difficult; the class material is. (& all textbooks are free!)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
(MTH 215) There are no lectures; class time focuses on group problem solving, with independent study required. The course progresses quickly, assuming prior knowledge. 
A more balanced exam, covering all units equally, would be nice. The focus on later topics and fewer, high-value questions was chosen, and this approach wasn't ideal for most of us.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Made me actually enjoy my 8am class. Great way to start off the day!
He would be the most amazing professor you ever had in your life

I thought he was okay teacher. Our class was loud so it was hard to hear him. I think his teaching style could be better as he goes into things that aren't always on the test. Overall decent teacher probably would not take again.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I like him a lot
Amazing teaching style. Funny and makes class less boring.

Daniel is really funny and really cares about his students. attendance is not taken each class. but pop quizzes are given out weekly usually on Fridays to track attendance. All homework assignments are done online through blackboard. go to every class so that you stay focus and talk to classmates about stuff going on.
I recommend going to his office hours
Great professor! Helps students a lot.
Lectures are okay!
Best professor teaching math 090 in UIC
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: He is a good instructor even though he tends to make mistakes. He is funny. TA's are okay. You'll pass the class.

Daniel is a super cool and funny guy that is passionate about teaching math. Though some content can be somewhat boring and obvious, he tries his best to make things fun. He does give out quizzes randomly for attendance purposes, but just do your work and keep up with the content and youll pass with an easy A.

i really enjoyed her course! all exams are open book and note, so doing the homework is vv beneficial. she's never made me feel silly for getting the wrong answer, and is so unbelievably helpful and motivating in office hours. wish i could take every class w her!!!

This professor was really helpful in helping students in office hours understand the material well, even when they felt unsure. One thing to keep in mind is that lectures are written on the board and may not be posted, so it's important to attend and take notes in class.
Dr. Nenciu is an excellent analysis professor.  Her homework was divided into theory and exercises, theory being theorems to learn (statement and proof).  I really liked this organization.

(1/2) DO NOT TAKE HER!!! MATH 313 with this teacher is the worst decision you could make. She gives a lot of homework every week (which is not graded nor reviewed so you don't know if you did it right or wrong). She quizzes you every week too on the homework. As a result you have around 15 homework problem to study for the weekly quiz and she will

(2/2)only choose 2. In other words you have to MEMORIZE EVERYTHING! At some point you end up with 50 homework problems for the midterm, and she only chooses 5, yes only 5 for both midterms. The final is cumulative. Sadly I have to retake this course because of the bad structure of the class but I hope you guys, that read this, can save yourselves.

The best Dif eq professor. She is the best math professor I have had. Her tests are a bit harder than other professors but they are also very fair. She goes at a good speed and clearly answers questions. The quizzes and tests are just like the homework. I would take her again in a heartbeat

If allowed I would give her a zero, reciting from the book verbatim does not qualify as teaching. I realized what was happening when i brought my textbook to help me understand the lectures (recitals?), she was reciting the examples in the book without changing numbers on most occasions. Skip if schedule permits, or teach yourself from the book
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Best diff eq prof ever! Exams are fair and reflect the content we've learned in class. All the profs wrote the spring 2017 final, so thatwas hard. Diff eq in general has long problems, so getting through only 3-4 per lecture is normal. She loves questions and will answer them well. She helped a lot in dealing with a bad TA.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She's literally one of the best diff eq professors, she explains really well and her exams are really fair. I dont get why past reviewers said her exams were really bad because i saw other professors exams & it seemed worse. She also doesnt use powerpoints to lecture, her notes are really thorough and she understands we're all struggling engineers

Nenciu is a nice person but when It comes to test us, one feels like is getting punished. Exams are extremely difficult and final exam is impossible to be solved. The coordinator for the course makes the final and doesn't care if we fail or not.
Very clear and very nice, does an amazing time going slow and allowing the class to participate. By far my best math science professor at UIC.

You better like doing long examples because we never did more than 3 or 4 examples in class without the time running out. Most concepts were easy to understand when she taught them but I learned most of the material from my TA and from other classmates. Pop quizzes are a guarantee.
math dept makes the exams so work hard at your grade

Her lectures are boring and very confusing. She over-complicates things. If you take her, you better hope you have a good TA like I did. She is not a very considerate grader either. She's nice, just not a good teacher.
She is a very very nice person. However this class was a disaster. Class average was like a G rather than an F. Avoid her or don't take this class with her.

To be fair, she gives the most organized lecture ever in UIC math department, she is also very nice, somewhat helpful in office hours. That being said, lecture sessions were okay to follow but homework problems were hard, quizzes were straight from the homework, and most importantly, exams were impossibly hard. The class average was below F range.

She is great at lecturing the material and she tries to make sure everyone is keeping up with her and really great at helping during office hrs... The course is not easy and requires a lot of time put into it and the exams are not easy but they are not impossible

She was fantastic at teaching such a hard subject. The book was pretty useless, and sometimes she moved quickly through the lectures, but if you go to office hours, she's genuinely interested in helping. She is nice, approachable, yet tough. You learn a lot from her. I recommend her as a professor to anyone.
Her level of professionalism is unmatched by any professor I've ever had.  Make sure to attend office hours if anything is unclear, though.
She is very understanding and helpful.  notes really dont help, office hours do-a ton!
She is extremely helpful and teaches at a good pace. If you listen in lecture the book becomes obsolete. She's also very nice about office hours and helping students with comprehension. A++
Very nice class if you like rhetorics and writing opinionated essays.

I absolutely loved his class. I joined a week late and he made an effort to meet one on one and get me up to date. He's super funny and gives extremely detailed and helpful advice on drafts. The syllabus did change a lot, but only because he saw the class struggling so much and made it easier. His grading is also VERY lenient.
His syllabus changed quite often, and the discussions were tedious at times. He will call on students who don't talk, so don't take this class if you are an introvert.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. Sharpe is genuinely very sweet and understanding. However, as a student it was hard to keep up with his syllabus, and did not enjoy that lectures were all just discussions about the readings. Readings were interesting, but at times slightly unreasonable. Would recommend if you do not like a professor who lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Sharpe is one of the better profs here, he actually reads your paper and gives helpful and personal feedback. He's funny and relatable. I kinda like writing now.

Absolutely life changing. Mr. Sharpe's class genuinely challenged my thinking and perspectives, and he is by far the best English teacher I've ever had. The workload wasn't easy yet, so worth it because everything he assigned taught me something great and left me with a brand new view of everything. I would take his class again if I had the chance.

Very kind and understanding professor. Honors the grading contract and accepts late work within reason. Made the class fun and interesting. There arent many assignments until the end or the course but they aren't difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Hilarious

reviews.comment: This guy changed my life.

I really enjoyed taking p381 with Julia! They make it clear that she cares very much about the work they do and the students they teach. She's always very willing to help a student when they need it and she clearly believes in her students and their ability to succeed. The class is also very easy, as long as you attend lecture and participate.

PSCH272. Dr. K-C is the most pretentious teacher I've ever had the displeasure of taking. Instead of feedback she sends class wide emails indirectly addressing students. Every class is pseudo-therapy and meditation when I'm here to LEARN. She loves to share the fact that she taught at Yale and that UIC is her charity case. Easy but intolerable.

I am so sad to see people rating her low! Shes super understanding and cares a lot about her students. She gives people chances to use their voices on things they feel passionate about. I've taken two classes from her already it was so fun! We only meet on Thursdays most of the work is online. I highly suggest her resilience class.

Very kind and contentious, a great teacher when it comes to learning about interviewing. I have been pretty dissatisfied with other psych classes but I feel like I have truly learned a lot from this class in particular. There weren't many assignments, there is a grace period for late work and it is graded very forgivingly.

Dr. KC is great! She is so empathetic and so caring about the content she is teaching. While her lectures sometimes may be boring, you can tell she is passionate with the content. She also gives a lot of extra credit opportunities! Just be willing to learn and listen and you will succeed in this class.

Julia is passionate about what she teaches, and incorporates current events into her lectures. She has a tendency to take up class time that's meant for practicing in groups, so practice outside of class is emphasized. There are 2 practice interviews and a report for each. She's picky with attendance but she's flexible and gives extensions.

Course: PSCH 385. She spent most of the class talking about politics bc she thinks we're unaware of what's going on. But she's talking to a room filled with students of color. Like please teach us how to write concisely & synthesize ideas more than once, not be passive aggressive about the use of AI. She cares about mental health, but so unhelpful.

Julia and her TA Victor are caring and compassionate; they centered classes around the wellbeing and growth of students. The course used an "ungrading" approach when I took it, and there were few assignments aside from readings. There were two papers and one group project, and students decided their final grade (though it was up for discussion).

I took it as a summer class. It was okay, lectures were long. Tests and homework were released on Fridays. There is one group project and one final paper. For these you are going to have to know about what was covered throughout the semester.

She can be disorganized and many things don't follow the syllabus but she does provide extra credit. There's weekly lectures and assignments with quizzes some weeks, a group project, and final paper. No tests or final exam. She's kind and very understanding. Overall class isn't difficult can just be difficult to follow at times.
She is amazing and smart and I loved her class.

The issue is how it is set up, like attendance. They do not use a good attendance method and miss collecting attendance from students and penalize them for that mistake and do not bother to correct it. Not understand if you are between grades even if you are at that .5 .t is tough to communicate with them they will reply once and never reply.

Dr.K-C is such a sweetheart, she always makes sure you are doing well and breaks down her recorded lecture in class. Her class is reading heavy but the article and books are very interesting. Their weekly assignment for this class are fun activities to do and I highly will recommend this class to anyone who would like to learn to become resilient.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Extremely disorganized, couldn't follow her own syllabus. She was nice at the start of the semester before she switched to apathetic after midterms. If you don't do the practice interviews precisely as she would personally, she will nitpick everything you did differently, even if the interview goes well. Very condescending when giving feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Save yourself. If you don't write things exactly as she would say herself, you're failing. She assigns useless busy work and grades it like a professional journal article. I had an A until the week final grades were released because even her TAs can't keep up with her pace.

Professor Kim Cohen at the beginning of the course was very sweet but getting close to the last few weeks of the course she was very hard on students. Her course is difficult to manage because there are quizzes and a group project which is very tedious where called the book club she is very strict about deadlines. Her TA is the best though.

If you can take your course with her. Shes super nice and understanding. And you actually learn in her class. We are graded based of 2 papers, 3 interviews, an exam, and project. This is all very manageable.

One of my favorite professors at UIC. If you want to learn something thats useful and you'll use in the future, take her class. She is really caring as well! Grade consisted of 2 exams, presentation, attendance, 3 practice interviews, and two reports.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: To be honest she wasn't the best but wasn't the worst. Everyone says how nice and sweet she is but it felt really fake to me, she also is so slow with responding to emails. Her class wasn't difficult, she was just annoying about format of the final paper. Her quizzes aren't bad as long as you read the 4 articles she assigns and her boring lectures.

Dr. Kim-Cohen is an okay professor. The class was interesting at first but then seemed almost repetitive. The professor had a hard time uploading lecture videos in a timely manner even though students have spoken up about that. Quizzes are difficult, but she drops one. She gives many long articles to read each week.

I took this class completely online and it was my favorite out of all my courses. Dr. K-C is understanding, responsive, and is more concerned about students being able to use the material she provides versus their letter grade. Definitely would take her again.

Professor Kim-Cohen is amazing. She is one of the sweetest professors I have ever had. She also knew how to run the online class smoothly during COVID. The class is interactive and you learn a lot. You do some small homework and a couple papers. Her exams are extremely fair as well. Take this class with her! She is so smart and understanding.

Dr. K-C is so understanding and provides many resources to succeed in this course and life in general. The content is fascinating and Dr. K-C explains these concepts really well by giving examples and keeping the class engaged. Would definitely recommend her for psychopathology!

Class can be a little lecture heavy but you can survive. There was a presentation to do and 2 papers, along with 2 tests. The only thing I HATE is that she kept us 5-10mins extra. She did this a lot, so if you have a class far, good luck. There is an interview session, which I did not like so make sure you can find people to volunteer. Okay class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Kim-Cohen is an amazing professor. The class consists of 2 papers, 3 quizzes, and 2 short presentations. If you don't come to class, participate, and take notes you'll have a difficult time. Don't be afraid to ask questions, she's more than willing to help her students out! If you put in work, you'll get an A. *LOTS of opportunities for E.C.*

I had Dr. Kim-Cohen before for 270 and wanted to take her again for 381. She's a wonderful instructor. The class isn't that tough. 6 journal entries, 3 interviews, 2 papers, 1 culture presentation, and 2 tests. The hardest part was trying to find someone to volunteer to be interviewed because most of my friends live nowhere close to UIC.

Professor Kim-Cohen is a great professor. Her classes are lecture heavy, but she does make an effort to make them interesting and incorporate lots of videos. It's hard to not pass her class, as her assignments and tests are really straight forward and she gives a ton of extra credit. She's really nice and its not a super hard class
Professor Cohen makes the class real fun! Just study her lectures well. There are many extra credit opportunities throughout the semester.

Dr. Kim-Cohen is a great professor! You can tell she really cares about both the course content and the success of her students. Her lectures can be a little dry at time, but she definitely adds some humor and videos once in a while to shake things up. Super interesting class overall, and I defo recommend her as your professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Such a wonderful human being! So sweet but firm when it comes to assignments & grading. If you like hands-on interactive learning, this is the class for you. Not lecture heavy, mostly participation and role plays. There was 6 short journal entries, 2 papers, 3 interviews & a presentation. Such a great learning exp!Dr. K-C rly prepares u for 385

She was okay. Only 3 exams and a 8-10pg paper so do not mess up on anything if you want a good grade.  Gives a nice amount of extra credit though. She didn't answer emails timely if at all. And she always had technical difficulties during lecture which got annoying. But the class is really easy no doubt.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Teacher is beyond amazing, truly cares toward each individual. Taking her right now. 2 papers. 1 of which is a group project but written individually, submission one section at a time and you get to revise it for extra credit. 3 simple quizzes. 2 very informal presentation (1 with group and 1 solo). I def. recommend taking her for developmental lab
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dr. Kim-Cohen is such a sweet person and has such a calming nature about her. I took her Abnormal Psychology class and she's very well-informed about mental illness, especially considering she's a licensed therapist. She assigned an 8-10 page paper which was a bit difficult but other than that, her class was amazing!

Dr. Kim-Cohen is a talented and brilliant woman who makes learning about psychology fun! She cultivates a great learning environment and makes an effort to learn names in a class of 120. She assigned an 8-10 page paper this year, but gave us a lot of time to work on it and even had a class devoted to working on the paper. She's awesome!

She is an awesome professor! Lots of videos, class discussion/participation, and is pretty funny and entertaining. Offers a 10pt extra credit video opportunity, but there is an 8-10 page research paper, but she gives you two months to do it. There are three exams, no final, mostly on lecture notes and vocab in book.
Very good lectures. Writes notes instead of using slides and which are very easy to understand and follow. Go to class and do some practice problems outside of class and it shouldn't be too hard.

So he is not my linear algebra professor but I still decided to watch him since he was great. The grades were very well distributed and HW was fair. He was a very funny professor and knew exactly what he was doing. He would write notes every time instead of using slides which helps students follow what he is doing. Best class so far!
Really nice guy, and the curriculum is easy. If I had a question, he would answer it in detail. Great professor would take it again and knows his stuff.

One of my favorite professors so far. He walked around to check if everyone was on the right track and made sure to answer students' questions clearly. I really love his humor. He taught the class with great passion, and I enjoy the memes he sometimes shares. I highly recommend taking him if possible.

The class itself was easy, but the lectures were not very helpful as he spent a lot of time debugging, looking up the Google definitions of relevant terms, and fielding feedback from students, reflecting a lack of preparation. Didn't get to a number of topics on the syllabus. Much easier to learn from the free online textbook.

He's good at explaining calculus and walks around to make sure everyone is understanding. Whenever I knew the content and kind of mind off, he would notice. He's really good at what he does and the homework wasn't that hard. If you pass the first exam with a 75+ you will be alright this whole course.

Prof Steenbergen is the person who literally got zero haters. The best math professor i have ever seen. He explains even the toughest concepts so easily and is really caring about his students. If you have an opportunity, take the class with him without any doubts, you are not gonna regret it.
Great professor overall and wants his students to succeed.

Prof Steenbergen is great! He is of great help at office hours, answering questions in class, & responding to emails. I also had him for calc 3 and he made it a class you looked forward to go to. Same for MCS 260. This was my first ever cs class and he made it very worthwhile. Would take again 10/10!
Professor Steenbergen was amazing to have! His lectures were so easy and he explained everything so well. It was super easy to talk to him and reach out for help. He is also just a little princess.
Easy to follow lectures, answers questions clearly, and always has positive energy.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I loved Calc I with Prof Steenbergen. Even when taking this class over the summer, I found the course to be fun and chill because of him. He always replies to emails and is super funny in lectures... If you have the option to take a class with him, do it!

I took this class with professor Steenbergen over the summer and it was a breeze. His lectures are clear and takes time to answer any questions even if it puts us behind schedule. I would definitely take him for Calc 3 as he doesn't teach Calc 2.

Dr. Steenbergen is the best Calculus professor and quite frankly, the best professor in the Math Department at UIC. He blows all of these other Math professors out the water. He actually cares about his students and wants them to succeed. He's not smug, cocky, rude, arrogant, intimidating, none of that. If only the other professors were like him...

Professor Steenbergen was amazing! His lectures were always enjoyable and the curriculum was very straight forward. He responds fast on email, and all the lectures are posted to blackboard. 10/10 professor!
Really good professor for Calc 3. Explains the concepts very slowly, clearly, and concisely and is always willing to help out. Can't forget about "Lagrange James" either!

Very good professor. Easy to understand his lessons. Very cheesy and funny. Wish he had more time to finish going over problems in class instead of rushing through it, but I know that's probably not his fault. Easy class as long as you show up, do your homework, and study!
Hard class on a personal level, but this Professor made things much clearer to understand which I appreciated. Going to lectures is vital & I felt that I learned a lot from them.

Awesome professor! His lectures were easy to follow and his humor definitely helped to keep me engaged. MATH 180 isn't structured the best, but that's on the course coordinator. Steenbergen also has a pretty cool fountain pen. If you are able to, take him!
He is an amazing professor! I love the way he teaches and the pace is easy to follow. I wish I could have gotten him for math 181, but he teaches math 210
Clearly explains conceptual topics.

This is an amazing and caring prof. Originally started with a different prof but started going to all of his lectures instead of my actual prof (besides attendance). He does daily reminders at the start of class, provides extra practice problems, and always reference old material when teaching. I go to his office hrs every week, sometimes for fun.

He is a man of class and an excellent instructor. His lectures are the reason I woke up in the morning to attend class. He made differential calculus a very enjoyable subject. You can tell he truly loves to teach the subject. Out of the many professors I've given a 5/5 here, he is the one who deserves it more than anyone. What a brilliant man!

He is very funny and explains things very well, unfortunately I am just not very good at math and this class was very difficult for me. If math isn't your strong suit I definitely recommend doing extra practice and going to office hours so you don't get behind.
Amazing professor. He explained the hardest units very easily and takes his time during class.
very good, very nice, he made me giggle, im a math major and he slay like soooo good bro like actually bless fam a sweet ting

If you're looking for a great MATH 180 professor, it will be professor Steenbergen. In his lectures, you can tell he enjoys teaching and cares about the quality of education. Whether you've taken calculus or not, he does not leave you behind. His pacing is on the slower end, but that wasn't a problem for me.
Great professor who explains everything very well. Kind as well.
Isn't too overwhelming of a teacher, provides good content and explains things very well, and has office hours and is mostly open throughout the week for appointments.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is the best professor I have had at UIC so far. He answers your questions well and cares about students. I enjoyed his class and I thank John for being such a caring professor. As long as you do all the assignments you will pass the class. We had a final but it was pretty easy since the questions were similar to our in-class quizzes.

He was an amazing professor. The class is structured very well. Best class I have taken at UIC. He explains things so clearly. If you pay attention, and take notes. Then, this class shouldn't be too hard for you.
Best professor. Cares about his students. Wants everyone to get an A

Can't go wrong with Steenbergen. Great lecturer and you will be able to digest the material thoroughly. The only thing is that Steenbergen is not great at stopping student distractions in class which deter from the lesson. Also, I strongly dislike the way the tests are designed but that is on the course coordinator, not Steenbergen.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class and professor combo was incredible. He is quirky in a good way and funny. Real Talk: If you are taking this class you have to fill out the lecture worksheets during class. This is half the homework and you will use it like the bible to study. Pay attention and ask questions you have. This class is difficult but everyone can pass it.

The amount of homework is light (1-2 math problems and 1-2 MyLabMath assignments a week), lenient with extensions on assignments if you are behind, entertaining and engaging lectures, really good at explaining concepts in a way that makes sense. Overall, a great professor that makes calculus so much less intimidating. Also uses a cool fountain pen.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: His classes are enjoyable, easy to follow, and explains everything clearly. His sense of humor made me sit in his class every day. He cares about the students and loves to help them if they have any difficulty.

Proffesor Steenbergen is a great guy and he's really funny. His teaching is thorough and even though I have ADHD, I almost never dose off during his online lectures. The only thing is that he can be a bit disorganized, but it's not a problem since he always manages to teach effectively.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. I'm not usually good in math, but he explains things really well in lectures. He's also very hilarious so lectures don't seem boring at all. Lecture attendance isn't mandatory, there are lecture recordings. However, he takes long to reply to an email, so better email Martina Bode if it's urgent

Prof. Steenbergen is such an amazing person. Lecture sessions are optional, but his humor makes attending them worth it. Explanations are clear and he will clear things up for you if you have any questions. There are also mandatory discussion sessions (teached by a TA) and you're assigned a team to work in these, so be prepared to participate.
Best professor I've ever had.

Id give him a 10/10 when it comes to teaching and explaining concepts, but a 2/10 when it comes to controlling the classroom. One-on-one or with small groups he is very helpful and caring, but at times while lecturing the class got so loud that it was impossible to make out what he was saying, much less focus. Even so, it is not a difficult class.

Steenbergen is an awesome professor who truly respects and empathizes with his students. If you ever have any issues, don't feel afraid to bring them up with him as he is very understanding and will do his best to help you. For the class, go to lectures, do all the homework and start watching extra YouTube videos for sequences/series (Hard topic)

Steenbergen is a fantastic professor and a very kind person. My only concern with Steenbergen is he does not control his classes. Students will talk loudly in the class and rather than telling them to "be quiet", he just tries to talk over them. It is unfair that students, who want to learn the material, but can barely make out what he is saying.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Hilarious professor and very friendly. He is readily available during his office hours if you don't have time during the lecture. Pay attention in his class! It just makes everything easier. His notes are really helpful.

He is a very easy-going person who is absolutely hilarious. He makes everyone happy with they way he interacts with the class. He is really good at math and also has a lot of knowledge of computer science. He helps everyone understand at their own pace and is always there to help you out.
nice professor

He is always in a good mood, I have never seen him angry or sad throughout the whole semester. He's always ready to help students and never disappoints anyone. He has so much knowledge that he shares in all lectures. I never got bored in his lecture.

He is very kind and tries to help each table but he rushes through the lectures. He wasn't assertive enough to quiet the class down effectively. I didn't feel the most prepared for the exams. Read the book, skim notes, practice problems, attend class and office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Steenbergen is awesome:) His teaching style is pretty good, he just goes through worksheets during lectures tho. I wish he would not rush things and give lot of time. Didnt like space where class held, it was too loud and I like it lecture style, quiet, or else i cant focus. he definitely wants to help, but go to office hrs, no time during lecture.

He gives great notes and leads you to solve problems. He's a nice guy who he makes you strongly feel respected, and he would listen to your words and questions patiently. My own experience is I found calculus easy, and I'm not forgetting it after the course.

Not great at explaining in lcture due to the time crunch and massive class sizes. A student in my class asked for him to clarify a rather straightforward topic and he left it at "just think about it!". Good guy but there may be better professors.

Beautiful hair, great looks, fantastic speaker. Theres nothing more that I could ask of a professor. I enjoyed coming to class just to hear him speak! If youre looking to take calculus, take it with John! Every class he will hand out problems and, after a brief intro on the material, walk throughout the class helping students who dont understand
He is honestly one of the best math teachers I've ever had!! He is great at explaining and answering all of my questions. Calc 1 wasn't so hard because of having him as a teacher!!!
Great professor, the lectures were sometimes a little too fast paced but he explains very well and is accessible to answer questions
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He is accessible outside of class, very understanding, hilarious, and has a clear grading criteria. He is a great guy. I learned a lot in this class that I never thought I would. If you ever want to take an MCS class in the future, I recommend him. The class will be lots of work, but he's understanding with projects and he knows computers very well

Such a great professor! MCS 260 can be difficult to those who have no programming background. He goes at a nice pace and is very reasonable with giving sufficient time to complete assignments. I have no complaints.

I had him for Math181 and, for being the hardest calc of the calc sequence, he really made it a lot easier to understand. He is laid back and engaging during lecture, and gives great note to study from. Make sure to pay attention and go to his office hours if you are confused! If you wait, it just makes it worse. 10/10 would recommend and/or smash.

I had him for MATH180 as well and he is my favorite professor at UIC. He speaks loud and clear and his lectures are easy to understand. As long as you take notes, do the homework, and do a few problems from the book, the exams are an easy A. Responds to emails quickly and is very helpful. He's also extremely nice and a overall chill person.

He is better than other Calc teachers.  There are 2 exams and 1 final exam. There are crowdmark hw and also the MathLab. It's manageable if you study and work hard. I would recommend looking notes and practicing the past exam as much as possible.  There are also pop- quizzes for attendance. Go to TA hours and also MLC it is really helpful.

Great professor. Calc is hard in general but he is a very clear and loud speaker. He will answer any questions you have during class and office hours. Expect lots of amazing dad jokes. Exams weren't too bad if you paid attention. DO MyMathLab because they help a lot. Also, he will give pop quizzes around the 40 minute mark and they're worth 2pts
BEST CALC TEACHER YOU CAN HAVE VERY GOOD AT EXPLAINING EVERYTHING AND ANWSERS ALL QUESTION IN CALL ALWAYS AWESOME DUDE!!

He is great, easy-going ,and goes through all the material in a timely manner and does it well. He's pretty dorky, but you can tell he likes what he's teaching. Attending lectures is a must, it's super helpful if you do. He gives pop quizzes. Studying is a must. Overall pretty good class!

Steenbergen is as straightforward a Professor you will find. Expect pop quizzes once a week and online & written homework. Two midterms and one Final exam. Is always willing to help and clarify for you. Tests can be tough because you apply what you learn to problems you have never seen or practiced. There is a big curve in the class.

Steeny was a great teacher when it comes to clarity and teaching the content.  However you must know how to both work through the problems and present them as points will be taken off for "bad notation".  Also another piece of advice would be to find a study buddy or two as it helps a lot in this class. Finally stay on top of the homework deadlines

Steenbergen is the best!! He's always willing to  go the extra mile in order to help his students so go to his office hours if you don't understand anything in lecture. His lectures are straightforward and he's very open towards any questions. His expressions and reactions are HILARIOUS. If you put in some effort, you'll ace Calc.
Took him for calc 180 and im taking him for 181. amazing teacher. very clear and helpful. go to office hours!

It was fun taking Calc 180 . You need to teach yourself. Seek for help. I would definetly recommend him. He gives pop quizes in lecture which are pretty easy. Grading scale is preety good. If you study, you will pass.
Professor Steenbergen is an amazing professor! He is easy going, helps you on the quizzes and he is super chill! I would love to take his class again!

Amazing professor, extremely respectful, understanding, and does an amazing job breaking down more complicated topics into easy-to-understand lectures. Seriously, just come to his lectures, take ACTUAL notes (if he write something, you write it down as well), do the MyMathLab homework (which is beyond easy), and study before every test. Easy A
The BEST calc professor! So nice, down to earth, a true nerd when it comes to the subject (good thing!). Make sure you take him if you can
Most amazing professor for calc at UIC
My fav professor so far. His lectures are surely boring but very helpful. He gives lots of examples. Easy A if you focus on his lectures. Would definitely take him again.

Very helpful and the best math teacher at uic for me thus far. If you are struggling with hw or need help in general go to his office hours, he will explain it to you and help you out so that you will understand it. 1010 would take again if I can.

Steenbergen is relatively new at UIC but is definitely the best professor I have had here, and I have had almost all of them at one point or another. He also has classes after noon which is rare for good calc professors. You can't go wrong with Steenbergen
Phenomenal professor. Take him if you can, he's new so not many students know about him yet.

I cannot recommend her enough. If you like linguistics or are curious about it then you'll definitely enjoy her class. There is one group project at the end but you get to choose your topic of interest and she'll group with other students based off what you chose. Also, the textbook was really easy to find online.

Jess was awesome! She gives extensions if you simply ask before it's due. The coursework included readings, weekly hw assignments (not too hard), and online tests. I quite enjoyed her passion for linguistics. Also, the group project is fairly manageable if everyone carries their weight, and it's in place of a final. Great class all together.

This professor is great and really makes the class engaged. She is a Student at UIC I believe but teaches like a PHD 20 year professor. She really helps you to understand everything and will slow down when needed. Highly recommend.

His classes are really cool and I love how he actually talks about cases that has been swept under the rug. The exams I took were written about 3 exams and 6-8 questions,the exams questions aren't difficult but make sure you read both the text and all the ppts because he sometimes throws in questions that we don't think is that important of a topic

He is a very nice professor. I have taken two classes with him and have gotten As in the two. He genuinely cares about his students, and he makes the subject easy to understand. For the exams, I had to study a lot, but as long as you like law, you'll find it interesting.

The professor was great and very caring. The exams required studying but were fair and easy because he taught exactly what was necessary. He gave good feedback and explained everything in a way that was easy to follow. He is very knowledgeable and clearly knows what he is teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: His style of presenting is very easy to follow. You can tell he is very knowledgable and cares a lot about what he's teaching. As long as you sure to really give yourself enough time to study for the tests because the study guides are longer than the tests, you will do well! Super chill and sweet guy and would 100% recommend.

Lots of lecture info which is accessible via slides, but lecture can be a tad bit hard for note-taking. Exams aren't bad, study guide is just more overwhelming than the exams actually are lol. Chill and clearly knowledgable guy, not a lot of work like 2-3 papers and 3 exams. Don't need the book tbh but it helps. Interesting content fr though.

Easy to follow lectures, there is something about the way he speaks that is so personal. You'll be able to pass without reading the Calavita book, but I do recommend reading it. He is very professional and makes sure to put his students first.

Kurwa is knowledgeable & great at explaining complex legal topics/historic eras and condensing heavy lectures into the main important taweaways. He has alot of wisdom about the field, social issues, and cares for students. great person overall. Two essays of 2-5 pages, three exams based on review guides. Readings weren't mandatory, but helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Kurwa was one of the most caring professors I've had. He was flexible and thoughtful of his students, allowing for assignment accommodations. Lectures are interesting, but there is a lot covered in each lecture. There are three in-person exams and two papers; attendance is required for both the lecture and discussion.

Dr. Ros is a great professor! She's extremely passionate about the material she teaches and is a very fair grader. Syllabus looks scary at first, but everything listed is doable and she gives a lot of time to do the assignments. Lecture heavy but they're engaging. Would take another course of hers!
Harsh, Not Paced, Clear, No HW, No Projects, No Exams, Essays, Quizzes, Attendance Required, Hard Gen-ED
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Truly one of the best profs on campus. Definitely taking another class with her. She's an expert in what she teaches and truly cares to pass on her knowledge to all of us. She offers a ton of extra credit, and if you ever need help, she makes time. The course load is challenging, but if you pay attention and take good notes, you're fine. Funny too.

She's clearly an expert in this subject and shows she cares. It can be difficult studying for the quizzes/tests at first because of the sheer amount of content, but you get the hang of it after the first few weeks. Studying for tests never gets less time-consuming, though. Missing one lecture sets you back significantly, so try not to miss class.

One of the best professors on campus. She gives a lot of extra credit, on one exam I got an 85, but she gave everyone extra points and I ended up with a 90 on it. Outside of exams, there is SO many opportunities to get extra credit. No pop quizzes, and the study guides are always clear. She is kind, funny, and intelligent. Take her classes!
Dr. Ros is a very kind professor and will answer the questions you have. Not an easy Gen Ed though and need to memorize a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Quiz every Monday, but they are super helpful for the exams. Make flashcards on Quizlet and study them! Take notes and attend all classes, or you will miss crucial information.

Ros was a great prof; you could probably get away with not even reading anything because her lectures were so in-depth and engaging. The tests weren't very tricky, and she always gave clear instructions on her essay projects. Overall, one of my favorite classes. Ros is very passionate about what she teaches and makes the class a lot of fun!

In this class, you will be taking a dive into classical Greek Literature. I came into this class knowing absolutely nothing about ancient Greek culture. The readings are slightly difficult as they should be, but if you want a professor who goes over the readings in the best way possible, providing questions to guide you along the way, TAKE DR. ROS!

Took this class as a gen ed not knowing anything about classics but it has become my favorite class. While we are required to read more than a "normal" amount, majority of the texts are easy to digest and the denser material will be expanded on. She's passionate about what she teaches and the class is engaging and interesting. Recommend taking!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Ros gives students many extra credit opportunities and is very passionate of what she teaches. Missing out one lecture or even five minutes of lecture can seriously tank your grade. Overall, the class requires a lot of memorization from lecture. You don't need the textbook, even though it's listed as required. She's fun and overtly clear!

Passionate about teaching. This specific course had easy 5 question weekly quizzes, more note-taking than participation, extra credit opportunities, easy writing assignments, and take-home midterm and final.

I took a class with Dr. Ros in Fall 2000, and then I did an independent study with her a year later. I am presently doing another class with her as a graduate student because there is no professor like Dr. Ros at UIC. She cares about her students and loves what she does. I think the fact that 23 years later I'm back taking her class says it all.

Yes, a very lecture-heavy teacher, but otherwise it is extremely easy to get an A. Not sure why people are claiming the essays were hard, as long as you followed the (extremely detailed) instructions you'd get an A. Also, attendance is very important and you'll be taking a lot of notes, but if you find the subject interesting, you'll like it.
Super hard and does not recognize this is just for general education. She discouraged me from persuing any more classes taken by her
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is a very boring and a very strict teacher. The stuff she teaches is amazing. But she makes it as a chore to be in that class. I got sick of her within the first month. If you want a passable gen ed STAY AWAY. Did all the extra credit opportunities and still failed.

Prof. Ros is a great instructor. She is funny and very passionate about what she teaches. You must attend lectures because that is where you will get the bulk of information. Do not rely on the posted PPTs or study guides at face value. Doing well on her tests and quizzes relies heavily on what you remember about each artifact or site.

Requires so much memorization for tests which is unreasonable if you plan to take full schedule. If you miss a single class, you are screwed for the weekly quizzes. She runs through the slides and posts them half blank so that if you do miss something, you have to ask someone or just hope its not on the test.

Quizzes every week and lecture heavy. Dont pack up early or talk in her class or she will yell at you LOL. Besides that, shes a nice lady and a good teacher, to be successful in this class u need to attend all the lectures and take good notes. Study hard, tests aren't unreasonable and only cover stuff she goes over. Overall, class requires studying

Dr. Ros gives great lectures and makes the material interesting. However, her assessments require way too much commitment to memory. Also, she has a strict attendance policy. If you don't show up, you miss the material. Missing material makes you less likely to do well on her exams and quizzes.

I have had Dr. Ros for several classes at this point and she is great. You have to attend the lectures though as all of her tests are based on what she tells you in the lectures. She also grades attendance but if you participate in class she is usually good about you missing more than the 2 that she says you get in the syllabus.

I've never met a more straightforward professor than Dr Ros. Took her for Roman art & history and her lectures were very interesting and she showed passionate for her field. Quizzes every week but they're easy to study for. Three papers that are also simple to write up. Exams can be difficult if you're not prepared. Overall a great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved this class and the lectures along with it.  I highly recommend this class if you love ancient history and creative writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof Ros was a good lecturer with a clear syllabus. The class itself is difficult and I ended up putting in more work for this class. There are quizzes every week and tests every 3-4 weeks. Be prepared to take lots of notes because class is not recorded. She is very accessible and was ready to drop a test because a huge portion of the class failed.

I wouldn't take this class lolz or her. You have to remember the names, dates, cultures, and like 4-6 different things about a statue/artwork AND HAVE TO SPELL EVERYTHING CORRECTLY and have to remember 12-16 of these per tests!! its too much. she gives me a weird strict vibe. So study hard and be prepared cause that first test is a huge surprise.

You must attend class and take good notes. There are no surprises on tests or assignments. they're mostly one-paragraph essays or comparisons on objects we covered in class. Multiple choice questions come from fill-in-the-blanks on the slide decks. One of the highlights of a tough semester were the memes she posted at the beginning of PowerPoints.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Make sure to study hard for tests
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: You must attend lectures in order to get information for the powerpoints since they are all fill in the blanks. I love Greek and Egyptian history which was why I chose this class for my gen-ed. I got an F on the first exam, but got A's and B's on the following exams. The study guides cover everything on the test, so there are no surprises. Study!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You have to attend lecture to fill in the powerpoints and because she takes attendance. Everything on the tests are from her study guides (no surprises!) and she always has extra credit questions on quizzes/tests. Study guides can get kind of long so do the questions on them after every lecture. Making Quizlets from the study guides helps a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've had. Introduction to Classical and Mediterranean Archaeology, was one of the most interesting classes I've ever taken. Yeah the powerpoints are all fill in the blank based on her lectures in class, so just come to class and stop being lazy. The tests are challenging, but they're doable. She's also really funny too.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Roman Civ was an easy A. No textbook, she makes fill in the blank powerpoints. Only a few tests and 3 short writing assignment during the semester, every now and then she gives a quiz to prep for the upcoming test. Decently interesting class, great to knock out a gen ed
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Four tests (last one optional), no hw, but you have to attend to fill in the notes for her powerpoints. Her tests are based off the study guide/notes so fill it out. One easy 5-6 page paper based off of the Art Institute exhibit. Oh, and 10 pt pop quizzes that she announces ahead of time. Nice lady, but reading off the powerpoints is super boring.

Lectures are mandatory, attendance is taken and the info from lectures may not be easily found elsewhere. Other than that, the assignments are fun, the content is interesting, and the exams aren't too difficult (straight memorization for the most part). Be sure to take notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She's a really caring person, but SO boring. The lectures are so boring and long & you have to be alert and taking notes the whole time or you'll fail on the exams. She does "pop" quizzes but usually announces them before. There's 4 exams including final, and one paper. She takes attendance!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She's one of the most genuine professors here. Her lectures can be boring but you need to go to get notes for the test. She really does help out if you go to office hours. You can tell she cares about the students who participate and show up. Multiple extra credit opportunities. Gives study guides, fair tests.

Worst class I've taken. Does not know how to lecture for her life or use blackboard. She hated all the students in my lecture and didn't allow any technology or food. Her tests are extremely hard and she is stingy with giving out points

We read several books/plays. She goes over the stuff you will need to know (topics and concepts) in class. There are two papers assigned with 3 topics to chose from for each. She will give you good feedback on the papers if you turn them in early and then make corrections. At the end, whoever had an A did not need to take the final.

Her lectures are the most boring thing I've ever had to sit through. Makes it difficult to take notes, so you have to pay attention and make sure your notes are detailed! She's always yelling about phones and food in her lectures. Kicks people out frequently. Very nitpicky grader on exams and essays. This class is impossible!

All the exams are essay formatted and she is extremely picky and specific with what she's looking for. There are too many terms that you need to know for each exam and she only picks 5-7 out of the 20. The lectures are just way too boring but attendance is mandatory. No phones or food in the lectures. Take tons of detailed notes.
What can't she learn to use blackboard?  Pro a nice lady in real life, but I think she is a snob.  She grades too tough.  Would not take again ever.

She's an awesome professor and everything from the exams are on the powerpoints. Make sure to go to class because she will say some things that are not on the slides and put that on the exams. She makes the class interesting and it's an easy A!

She has a rude attitude and she covers materials as if there is no tomorrow. She flies by materials and does not know when to slow down. On the other hand, she does give you a chance to not take the final if you are happy with your grade.

The last exam is not required. She tells you the last day of class so you don't skip the last 2 weeks. I had a 78. She offers Exam 4. I did better on that than all before, I ended with a 79. She did nothing to help me. I went to get help often, did all extra credit, did everything I could. Harsh graders. Takes points for joy. Did not care whatsoeve

Easy A. Don't think you can just skim the power points though. She makes exams tricky by picking specific dates or details so pay attention to what you're reading. Do study guide and prepare essays and you'll be fine. Attendance mandatory to fill out power points and roll call. No book used. Quizzes are too easy. One 3-6pg. paper also.
Easy A. Only had to write one paper between 3-6 pages long. Tests are easy if you study a decent amount. Quizzes also easy.

Although I earned an A in the course, you might wanna think twice about takig her. She never answered questions and always had a rude attitude. Have to study atleast 6 hours for exam, not mult choice. Grades extremly hard. Will be reluctant to move an exam for you. Did a good deed by exempting students who had A from the final exam.

Great teacher, awkwardly funny, well prepared. 4 tests, book is necessary. Tests are kind of hard because you need to remember about 18-20 notecards packed with info about the artwork. Got a 90 when I studied for 2 days, a 97 when i studied for 4 days.
Great teacher and interesting material! Definetly take her, easy A and she is entertaining

Class is easy. Powerpoints are online but with blanks so you come to class and fill them in. Attendance is mandatory. No book. 4 tests no final. Each test is T/F, Multiple Choice, and 1 essay question that she gives tells u before the test. If you come to class and fill out the powerpoints you'll get an A. Class is B or A.

Great professor! Made me love reading again and sparked an interest in greek tragedy novels! Highly recommended professor! Go to class and take notes and you should be good with an A or B in the class as long as you go to class and read.
One of the best professors at uic.  She makes the class ineresting.  Easy A.  Very organized and very clear on what is expected from students.

Dr. Ros is a wonderful professor. She is very honest about her expectations, friendly toward individual students, and always prepared for class. Gives out helpful study guides. Definitely consider taking her classes if you are at all interested in Greek or Roman art and archaeology.

Take lots of notes on the slides she shows in class, look at the study guide, make flashcards to memorize slides and you'll definitely get an A.  This class isn't difficult but it requires 3-4 hours before the test to memorize all the information needed.
Really good professor. I'm not an art/history major but she made this class easy and interesting. very clear on what she wants, also very organized. One of the best professors I've had.
Take this class, if you want a teacher who favoritizes extroversion, graded on a few items, late items are always zero even if syllabus says differently.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Moon comes off welcoming in the beginning, but if you are going to class just to learn and be given clear direction she is probably one of the worst teachers for that. Insanely disorganized, unclear on instructions, and will add extra work the day a huge assignment is due. Can also be extremely condescending and rude to you, watch out.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very disorganized, contradicting herself often, not the worst professor you could take, but also not the best one. Grading criteria is unclear but she will sit down with you and give you feedback so I if you utilize that you should be fine for this class.
She seems nice at first but can be very condescending. She gives bad explanations and she often contradicts herself. Everyone is always confused in her class.

Kim lectured maybe six times all semester. Grades are based on three assignments with unclear, subjective standards. The Blackboard page is outdated and disorganized, with assignments from a previous term still posted. Her rubrics are confusing and contradictory. If you want to learn about advertising, avoid her class.
Very warm professor. A bit monotone, but super chill. Tests and homework are very easy, just be specific in your writing. Lots of watching youtube videos! Attendance is taken but not for credit.

She is an easy class to take, but please be wary that she is absolutely unorganized. I have never meet a professor with such poor organizational skills. You'll be graded on 4 assignments and attendance/participation (5 total grads).

Professor Moon is good overall. She cares about the students and she makes sure that students do well. However, I feel that the wording of her exams is confusing. Sometimes the multiple choice options are typed in a way that makes you get confused about the correct answer.

I mean she's alright. I definitely learned a lot in this class. Would I take her again, no. She is kind of a tough grader. Also, her assignments directions are never explained well.
