For 270, make sure you prepare well for the midterm and final. Study off the PowerPoints and !!practice exams!!. For 371, theres 5 exams and a final, so make sure you study regularly.

John Sparks communicates business statistics in an effective and understandable manner, and he doesn't ghost you outside of class. He's entertaining, work-oriented, generous, and respectable. It's pretty rare to find a professor in the information science department that possesses all these qualities, especially an encouragement for students.
Reads directly from the slides. Homework, quiz, lab assignments, computer assignments, were only 25% of the grade. Midterm 30% and final 45%. Avoid at all cost!!!

IDS570: Mountains of online homework, many typos. No redos. Tests were easy after studying homework questions. He posts all lectures online and is inaccessible outside of class. You will get sassy replies to earnest questions, get used to it. Focus on concepts not math procedures. Not an online class. But that didn't stop him from making it one..

The worst professor I have ever had, does not know how to communicate, be sympathetic, or care enough to listen to his students. Was rude and very aggressive at times. Hated this class and would not recommend to anyone who is looking for a professor with any sense of humanity in him.

Horrible professor. Took hIm 3x and failed. bought the book, went to tutoring, got A's in all assignment on homeworks and quizzes yet nope. This prof grades like he's trying to purposefully fail people. He triggered my depression in college & coursed killed my gpa. the 2 exams are 75% of your grade so any other work you do  irrelevant. HORRIBLE!
He doesn't know how to explain the material. It is like he's reading everything on the board (anyone can do that!) His ta did way better than him on explaining/teaching. Avoid at all cost.
Paid tuition fees to watch his old recorded videos. Worthless! and waste of time. Could take a coursera course or other MOOC classes instead of this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I only paid attn to this class during midterm and final review. Lots of easy online assignments due every week. I only went to lab if there was a written assignment we had to turn in. Don't slack on studying for the tests bc you will really hurt yourself. The material is challenging but if you study a lot do the practice tests you'll be good.

Great professor! Funny and smart about everything statistics. He is very strict about talking when he lectures and strict on test day but I found his class enjoyable. He uploads a video of every class session which is a bonus bc he doesnt require attendance! Take him you wont regret it!

He isn't great at teaching the material but not bad either, I actually learned better by not going to class & instead listening to his lectures through online lecture capture video. The second exam on Regression is brutal - to do well your main focus should be how to interpret data from graphs. Online hw, quizzes, and computer assignments are easy.

Definitely the toughest and pickiest grader for the memos. The web videos are mandatory to watch. They do help. But going to his office hours will be the biggest payoff when you're re-doing your memo. Definitely record him on audio when you're getting feedback on the memos or else you'll forget how he wants you to do state your analysis.

He gives you everything you need to earn an A. The content is challenging until you study and practice. Exams are 75% of your grade. Study hard for them. He also has an irrational fear of roaches. Never ask him about that. Don't talk in class. He will stop the lecture and yell at you if you do. I love you, Professor Sparks!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Sparks is the best professor I've had so far at UIC. He makes the material extremely easy to understand, and is very helpful outside of class. His final makes up 45% of the final grade, but this doesn't bother me as a. he reviews a LOT before it and b. the class is all about application, which makes sense for a statistics class. Take him!

Professor Sparks is my favorite professor at UIC. He is knowledgeable on his material, and he teaches the material in a way that everyone can understand with some jokes. I have taken him for both IDS270 and IDS371. He is been extremely helpful, and I have learned a lot. Take Sparks you wont regret it.

Currently taking him during the summer. Funny and sarcastic guy. Class is graded by  2 exams worth 75% of the total grade and the other 25% is homework, labs, etc. Overall excellent professor, my only complaint is that exams make or break your grade, luckily his reviews are very precise and helpful. Course load not heavy, but material is hard.
take him, trust me

Just go to class and you will get an A, the actual exam is almost identical to the practice. Whoever said this class is difficult must be SKIPPING classes a lot. Cool and funny guy, willing to take it again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: 2 tests make up 80% of your grade! Lots of homework, computer assignments, and labs which only make up a total of 20%. Although it seems like a lot of work, the first test is nearly identical to the practice test but the final is significantly harder. I studied for 2 days before the final and managed to get an A on it. Make sure to Ace the tests!!!
Definitely take him. He makes the topic easy to understand lowkey. He's a cool guy too. As long as you put in the work in and out of class, you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Cool professor. I appreciate the fact that he records all of his lectures because I work full time and couldn't always make it to class, although he did give homework hints to those who attended class. He is great at reviewing for the exams, drills for a week straight. Online homework and quizzes. Would take him again.

Sparks is a great guy. If i could take him for every class, I would. He gives you everything necessary to do well in his class. If you need help, he's very helpful during office hours and will even stay late to make sure you understand it. He's hilarious too. Overall, great guy and he made stats a lot easier. Take him you won't regret it
Amazing Person! Hilarious and You'll learn a lot with him.

Sparks try's his best to make the lectures entertaining. There was 2 tests worth 75% of your grade. The midterm review is almost identical to the midterm itself. He goes over the final for around 2 weeks. Easy to reach and contact. Just study intensely for the tests and you will be good.  He is an all around good guy.
Study the practice test along with doing the HW and you will get an A
Pretty average.  Kind of funny.  Final was worth a whole lot but he prepared you for it.

He is a good professor, but its a hard class too. Lots of homework, lab, and computer assignments. Dont slack on any of them, even though they are worth only  5 percent. Midterm is VERY similar to study guide. However, the final exam is harder and not as similar to study guide. Make sure to go all the review sessions and follow up on the echo also

Best professor in the IDS department currently. He is very, very good at explaining the material and the exams are faithful to the material he covers. He is also funny and cracks a lot of jokes. Go to every class and pay attention to the lectures, it really pays off. Don't slack on the hw or comp assignments and you'll be good.
Get ready for autonomous study. :(
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I highly recommend taking his classes. His lectures are not boring and easy to follow. The review section is really helpful and you do not need the textbook for this class.

Anyone who says that his exams are impossible must not go to class very often.  He literally reviews and states everything that is going to be on the exam.  Have only NOT gotten a 100% with this guy on the regression exam in 371.  Bottom line: go to class, don't talk during class, listen when he says "this will be on the exam", and you'll get an A.

Sparks screamed in my face when I went in to office hours. His exams are impossible. I studied for 20 hours for the first exam. I was confident that I got an A. I added every point I got right and wrong while I was taking the exam and I got a C. Many people take this class 2-3 times. Good luck.

He's probably the best professor for IDS 371, The class is long, but it is not that boring  at all. Class attendance is not mandatory but recommended.  The class material is not that bad, and if you attend every single class, you should be able to get an A with no problem.  Highly recommended.

Lowkey... I NEVER went to class but i kept up on the lectures through online slides and by doing the homework and everything! I am passing.. don't doubt me ;) lol. I did attend lecture when he reviewed for the tests and to take exams. The exams are not hard if you attend review but you should definitely study!! He's pretty funny and knows his stuff

Fun professor that makes a dry subject bearable. There's no reason to fail this class unless you're being lazy. Everything's posted online including the lectures and ppt slides. His reviews cover 90%+ of what will be on the exam, it's up to you to study it. It's very easy to fall behind, though, when the concepts get harder.

Favorite Professor, Ive taken him twice. The course (IDS270) isnt easy but he provides you with all the information you need to succeed. If you get a bad grade, it means you didnt try hard enough. Literally drills for weeks before the final. Lets you re-do anything you bomb. Highly recommend, its not like any professor makes stats super interesting

He was of my favorite professor. The class is hard, but he gives examples to help you understand. Yes the exams was hard, but the practice exam is extremely help. He's lectures are boring, but he tries to crack a joke here and there.

I found the professor's videos highly valuable and they allowed me to refresh the  understanding of concepts before my job interviews.  I should say that his lessons and projects had a significant role in me securing a   job!

My first review here because he is great. Statistics is a challenge no matter what professor you have. Sparks gives you all you need for the mid-term and final. He will help you as much as legally possible to understand the class. Optional attendance, but it'll be your responsibility to put in 2-3 nights of hard work come exam time to get the A

Sparks chooses to go over concepts that he knows will help us in our future careers. Therefore, every topic covered makes you feel satisfied to achieve and has you looking forward to the next. He is very helpful and always willing to clarify. Study for weekly quizzes, be attentive to homework assignments, and a good grade should be yours to keep.

Put in the effort every college course deserves and you will get the A. Sparks is quite straightforward and helpful. Go to class, study, practice the problems he tells you to go over in class, and the A is yours. Very organized and is lenient with due dates. He can make any difficult topic seem easy, only a great Professor can do that.

I wouldn't consider taking this class with you have 4 or more other classes. His online lectures are long and time-consuming. He will give you a zero for small mistakes give you back your assignment and have you do it again. I didn't learn much despite working so hard to pass.

Going to class is not necessary, but make sure you keep up with the class. If you don't keep up with the class, at least make sure you know everything in the practice midterm and finals. Practice midterm is almost the same as the actual midterm. If you go to class and keep up with his lectures, you should get an A easily.

Worst class. He acts like this is the only class you're taking. I learned nothing about coding in SAS, then he makes you write memos like if he's an English teacher. He tries to make it up by letting you "re-do" your work but he finds errors every time, for example: "must use 2 carriage returns", one mistake like that, and you get a 0.
He mumbles a lot. Wasn't horrible but wasn't the best either.
Great Professor. Very clear and his reviews/drills cover everything on the test. Attendance isn't mandatory and you can watch his classes online if you don't feel like going. Absolutely recommend.

Really hard to keep up in class and they only way to learn something is to work as if it was the only course you were taking in the whole semester. He has a uncaring attitude to what the students learn and the surface is skimmed on various topics including more than one programming language (SAS and R). Hard to keep up with him, waste of time

Nice guy, BUT his exams were difficult. There is a LOT of material crammed for the second exam so be prepared- do the practice exams way ahead of time. The first exam is prty identical to the practice. I think everyone bombed the last exam :/

He grades very hard & isnt that helpful. I showed up to every class and answered questions everyday. He knew my name. When I asked for a grade explanation at the end of the semester I did not receive a response. He doesnt care about his students, just there for the money/research. Goes through material too fast & doesnt explain.

The best professor that I had this semester! The tests and exams were really easy if you show up to class everyday. Really helpful if you have any questions. I would definitely take another class with this professor.

Undoubtedly, the most helpful professor ever. Makes sure that every topic is covered and well explained. Willing to repeat himself until absolutely everyone gets it. Even though everything is on Blackboard, attending lectures is your key to success. Moreover, you wouldn't want to miss his funny jokes. Highly recommended!

I was terribly disappointed with this class. We didn't really learn SAS coding which is what I had hoped to learn. We actually learned how to write papers on statistical analysis. Prof. has a horrible attitude when you ask him a question. He definitely gives you the are you stupid type of look. Overall there are better IDS electives to take. AVOID!
Easy going guy, over complicates things. TAs are useless, so you better buy the book and keep up in the class.
Very confusing class. Lost interest as an IDS major taking this class. Way too much work and he over-complicates things.

Funny professor! Sparks puts everything on blackboard I mean everything. He keeps a boring class pretty entertaining.  You don't have to go to class, because he puts his lectures online, but you should go because its easy to fall behind. The only downside to his class is that it's at 4.

Funny, interesting, awesome prof. Prof Sparks puts videos , ppts, textbook pages on Bb, and he really tries to help every student. He would stay after class to go over questions with the students. He is really good at explaining the super confusing math. Loved that class! You don't have to go to class but you should. The class is enjoyable.
Take this class at Harold Washington w/ Jeff Swigart. He is more enthusiastic of this class. Sparks class is BORING and at 4pm. Learned more at HW than I did at UIC
Good Professor. Very helpful. The best teacher for IDS 270!

Very clear professor! He explains very well. He is willing to repeat his explanations if anyone has any questions. All the material in his exams is covered in class.No surprises. For midterm  and final: STUDY THE PRACTICE EXAMS & learn how to do those kinds of problems!Great professor... I would definitely recommend taking IDS 270 with him!
He provides so much review material that is impossible not to do well in the class. Good quality.

This class is pretty easy if you study last year's old exam 2 weeks before he reviews for midterm/exam. Asian ta(s) are the best because they basically tell you the answer to homework/lab. If you can not get the answers to homework or quiz, just google it.

Take his class! He is very clear in his presentations and is very helpful. He will stay back after class to help anyone that needs it. Tries to be funny during his lectures from time to time. All of his power point are on Blackboard so you didn't need to attend lectures. His homework and quizzes are fairly easy if you try.Overall, good professor!

Extremely clear and helpful. I just wish the class was offered for more than just one time slot. The class was at 4pm and that gave me 6hr gap that really did nothing but make me want to skip, which I did more than I am proud up. Hmwk is online as are quizzes and they're not all bad. Test and final were discussed in class with tons of practice.
He gives you everything you need to succeed. His test are moderately challenging,but if you attend class regularly you can get an A..

The guy sets you up for success. The material can be tricky if you hate stats but he gives you A TON of review material and tools to help you learn. He gives all the answers to quizzes and hw, so try to attend class and you should have no problem getting a good grade.
Took this class online (statistics for management)  A lot of work, but I felt I learned statistics. He was also very responsive to email questions and a fair grader. Good class to take online.

His lectures are boring and useless just about until the last 3 weeks when he reviews all the material for the final exam. Only like 20 of 300 showed up to lecture everyday and those that did were just playing Angry Birds on their phones (to which he noticed and would comment on frequently). He is very jittery in class and always wired up on Coke.

Awesome professor. He gives out the answer for homework during lecture and he can even "check" your quiz before you submitted online. Not 100% easy but if you do follow his practice sets and homework, there are only 5% on the exams that is not "greatly reminded" in class (but that 5 % is still easy if you read his powerpoint).

I took John Sparks over summer 2011, IDS 270 course.  Excellent teacher. He really knows his stuff. If you want an easy A than take another professor. If you want to learn statistics take "Mr. Sparks" class. Made the class interesting. He even answered my email and pointed me in the right direction pertaining to my career goals. Highly recommended

Do hw,quizs,computer assignments that is 40 percent of the class. Midterm is exactly like his Midterm practice exam which is 20 percent..so doing that is an easy 60 percent of the class..Make sure to pay attention to the final three chapters which is the final. Be on top of your stuff after the midterm
GREAT class, because you never have to go! All the notes are online, and tests are manageable if you study for a couple hours.

He is a cool guy if you get start up a conversation with him.  Homework from book is useless and so is lab, especially when you can't understand your TA.  Real meat of the course comes in the second half when you actually start applying formulas to problems.  Overall I liked him, studied hard for the final and got an A.

He's a nice person but an awful teacher. HW from book is so tedious and worth way too much points. Midterm exam is really easy, but final was somewhat difficult. With some effort, it is possible to get an A. No curve. Labs teach you nothing that you didn't learn in IDS 200.

He knows his stuff but is very monotone and dry. He can help you if you ask but he will not go out of his way to make sure students grasp the material. Hard to pay attention and learn, bare with it and go to class he cover the stuff but its boring. Midterm/final are very hard, show work, no curve. so study hard for those.

the teacher doesn't take the time to engage the students with the material.  he just talks and he will need to curve because most students will do bad on tests.thanks to his bad explaining. overall, he an okay teacher. just pay attention.

Professor Sparks was a very helpful teacher, answers questions to the best of his ability. There are multiple homework assignments and quizzes; but there are only two exams. Exams are similar to practice problems and for the final he lets you use a cheat sheet. Lectures & discussion aren't mandatory, but I highly recommend attending them.

The lectures are kind of worthless, don't need to attend except on days when he goes over the Practice Exams or Homework. There are two tests, the final is harder but he gives you a cheat sheet with formulas. He's awesome cuz he goes over homework in lecture, and in lab you go over quizzes.Cool guy, he doesn't like talking in class btw.Pretty easy

He's hard to hear sometimes since he mumbles and is boring, but I recommend you sit near the front. He will go over how to do the homework assignments in class and will prep you for exams to the best of his ability. His practice exams are extremely similar to his real exams. Read the book if you can't understand his lectures. I'd say an easy A

He's a cool guy, only 2 tests, don't really need to ever show up for class since everything is on blackboard. Only attend days where he goes over the homework, cuz some stuff might not be on blackboard. Also go on practice exam days. Both exams are pretty easy, and if you play your cards right you can still get an A and rarely if ever go to class.

very knowledgable, a gentelman with all what the word means,highly recommend taking his classes, extremely helpful and dedicated to stats & students success, need to keep track of homeworks & practise exams (tough a little bit) but he is always there for help& advice and you'll get the A

lovely personality, patient, understanding to students' differences, stats concepts become more applied and real to use ! HMWRKs & EXAMS kind of tough but his guidance always there;  certainely you'll leave this course with strong basics successfully

Very long ppt slides... however very helpful prof and always think of ways to make students' lives easier. Tests are from study guides and hw's so do them seriuosly. Overall an easy class and great prof!
Very good, knowledgeable professor. Lots of material for the final, but three sample exams help a lot. Grades tests pretty good.
Made a boring subject somewhat interesting... somewhat
great teacher!! easy class!!!
Very good Prof! A lot of patience and VERY good teaching skills. Highly recommend.
Really nice guy, just pay attention and do the homework and lab assignments and your guaranteed a good grade!
He gives good explanations and examples beyond the slides. Prep tests actually prepare you for the exam and he's hot.

He goes beyond the slides and text to make the class understand the subject. Grades and tests are very reasonable. His test preparations will give you a very good idea of what will be tested on. It is easy to get an A or B in his class. Took his class on summer, and class could drag on though.
The class was very easy, not too many assignments. Not hard to prepare for the exams. Totally recommend.
Very caring and understands that life happens, just communicate to her. Make sure to do homework and practice questions outside of class and you'll be fine! Attend class to ask more questions!!

Prof Schroeder is a good professor who genuinely wants her students to succeed! She offers so many different ways to get points in the class incase you don't do the best on exams. With that being said attendance is important because the class uses iClicker for in class points. Overall she's a great professor and would definitely recommend!

She was a really nice teacher. She did her best to make sure we understood everything though her teaching methods kind of long and the way that she describes things. She's always an email away and she is available sometimes at the math and science learning center I think our homework assignments were rather fair.

Professor schroeder does an amazing job. Make sure your catching up with the material. the profesor is very understandable and nice and she does an amazing job going over problems and explaining in lectures. attendance is mandatory and i will say i clickers are a good amount of your grade. its not too complicated if u study and review!

Dr. Schroeder is an incredible professor. She is fair and kind in my experience. There is an expectation that you will put the work in to succeed in her course. She is available to her students in the MSLC, during office hours, and via zoom appointments. Be prepared to study! I enjoyed this course a lot.

The best chem 101 professor at UIC. I do think she could improve her ability to help students feel safe in being wrong, as it's part of the learning process. Most people mispronounce her name, but she never seems to judge them for it. It's "Shray-der," not "Shroh-der." Learn your polyatomic ions, don't confuse P for K, practice, and you'll do fine.

Professor Schroeder was the best chemistry professor I have had. She was kind, cared about helping people, and she has her class structured perfectly. She also takes great notes which she posts after class.
The only way I passed this class was with the help of ASAP tutoring because personally I couldn't understand the way that she taught.

Absolutely loved my time in her class. She's an amazing person who cares about her students' understanding. She gives you everything you need to succeed through the slides she uses to teach.  Be sure to attend the lectures, as iClickers will be available for participation points.

I feel this class is too overwhelming for what is being taught. The topics themselves aren't difficult, however the professor adds in steps that are unecessary and just confuse you. It feels as if the way the class is formatted and the way she teaches you, like you're a child. Be prepared to take out an unecessary amount of time for this class.

I used to hope someone would mug me while walking to class so I wouldn't have to go, but that's just because I'm overdramatic. She does give you all the resources you need to pass; you just have to study. 100% prefer her compared to the other Chem 101 profs.

Schroeder is a very good professor. I don't understand why she is rated so low. You can tell she cares, and her lecture are easy to follow. I will say sometimes she is a bit passive aggressive, but it was deserved. If you have to take CHEM101 she is 100% the best option.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
she writes on the lecture slides to help guide us to understand the material better and I think it really helps. for word problems, she goes through it step by step. occasionally she would walk around the classroom to answer questions when she gives us time to work on word problems. she's overall really great

iclicker is used btw

During her lectures she writes down things on the slides and does the problems with us which helps a lot because it gives a visual. Before exams and quizzes she gives us a topic guide to study and it's very accurate, she's honestly the best Chem 101 teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: normal class not as hard as people make it out to be just take notes

I took this class in Spring 2025, and it was extremely draining. Despite my effort, I never missed class and went to office hours, but it was never enough. The TA had no chemistry background, and Professor Schroeder was unfair, helping only certain students during exams. Save yourself the stress and choose a different professor.

I loved Lianne Schroeder and this class so much. I hated chemistry in high school but I found out I love chemistry overall through this class. The assignments and quizzes set you up for success. The lectures can move fast but if you pay attention for the 50 minutes, finish the online assignments, and study, you will receive a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Awesome Love it

It really takes time to warm up to her. If you show up to the MSLC and prove that you are trying, she WILL find ways to help you. Lectures are very important to pay attention to, or else you will be confused. Most grades come from ALEKS, so make sure those are always done. Exams are fairly hard, but if you study, I promise you will be okay.
Be prepared to study quite a bit for this course; lots of things to study and remember. Exams fit perfectly with in-class assignments, and lectures are interesting.

Schroeder can be passive aggressive and dismissive towards struggling students. It can be hard to connect with her as a student and feel comfortable asking questions. When students ask her questions, sometimes she'd respond in a pretty condescending way rather than supportive---which can be very discouraging.

There were quite a bit of things to do every week for this class but it was doable. The content can be hard at times but if you dedicate time to it you'll do well. She genuinely wants you to learn and grow as a student.

Chem is hard. She broke it down amazing for us, she went through lectures quickly and would even finish class early some times. Never shoved lectures at you, she was fun. Didn't expect you to learn everything on the 1st try. She didn't like when people spoke over her. But she was really nice and very helpful. I recommend her A LOT.

She is the WORST. Quiz and exam averages are AWFUL like 50%-60% range and she refuses to believe that it is her fault that everyone is doing bad. She does not explain the material in a way that is easy to understand. She also formats questions different on exams than what is learned in class. Aleks is your best friend. DO NOT TAKE. SAVE YOURSELF

Schroeder is more on the chill side. Usually treats us with respect but does get annoyed whenever people talk over her. Yes, her lectures are long and does go through them quickly. But does give you the slides to download in advance. I will agree that the amount of work is exhausting on Aleks, but they do a good job of making you learn more.

Schroeder is great.She helped me when the chemistry department couldn't on an issue.During her lectures she can go quickly, the slides are posted and you can refer back. You have to buy Aleks. I think that if you do Aleks without help and do the review problems on Aleks for each chapter in the etextbook, then you'll do good in class.

I don't understand why people giving her bad reviews. She was one of my favorite professors of all time. She was really clear with lectures, homeworks. She made her lectures very interesting and easy to cope with. However, her class required lots of homework done within a span of one week. Unfortunately, tests are heavy, but ALEKS helps a lot!
Great prof

Hard class and a bad professor. Every time we took a test, the class average was around a 50% because the tests were insanely hard and she just expected you to know everything she threw up on the board during lectures. Unclear grading criteria and TAs were terrible, I could barely understand what they were saying.

Very bad class. This professor just expects you to understand everything no matter what. She is not understanding to personal matters. And her tests are insanely difficult, the classe's average scores were always around 50%. Grading criteria is not clear at all.

Dr. Schroeder's lectures can get boring and it's difficult at most times to stay focused on her teaching, there's also just a lot of material in this class so you're going to have to do a decent amount of work outside of class to keep up. The exams are also designed to trip you up and the chem department grades tough, so you really have to focus.

I had her as a co-teacher for NATS 106 alongside Michael Muller. She is ok. She is very passive-aggressive...and does not seem happy when asked questions. She gives actual scary stares at people during lectures. Her lecture slides are honestly confusing. She does not explain things well and speeds through slides. Don't really like her, but not bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Awesome professor. She goes through slides a little fast but the pace was just right for me. She is very well spoken and is very clear throughout her lectures. Overall an easy and fun class.

I hate chem, but her teaching style was very helpful. Her use of clickers forces you to apply what you just learned (if you don't read the online textbook (i didn't)), so that kinda sucked. For the most part, the work was manageable. You have Aleks lessons & hw weekly, which count for a few points. The tests make up the majority of your grade, tho
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's a great professor. She explains things very thoroughly and provides visuals during her lectures. Homework is weekly and on ALEKS (you have to pay for it). Review her slides after class because she can sometimes gloss over important material since she wants to cover other bigger topics. Heavy on the Iclickers, which is understandable.

terrribleeeee, i would skip her unless you have no choice. i dread everyday I have class. exams worth so much, flunk one time or do bad and game over. this class has a bad average exam score, stayyy awayyyyy. this class is worse than calculus I, doing better in that class than CHEM 101😂 ICLICKer ruins ur whole grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: When I took this class, I couldn't focus for the life of me. She's a nice professor but I can't understand the things she was teaching. I learned more in Professor Stec's lecture than this one. She's not bad but I guess it's based off preference.

She is a great teacher. I previously had issues with learning chemistry but in her class, it was so easy. Her lectures are very organized and have a great pace. As long as you listen to the in class lectures and do all the practice/hw on aleks, you should be good. I was able to get 100% on multiple tests when in high school I'd get 70's.

ALEKS teaches you more than she ever will. Do go to lectures and complete IClickers because they are part of your grade. Exams are a good portion of your overall grade. reviews.comment: She acts as if we don't have lives of our own and gives a huge amount of homework and reading. By all means find another teacher!!!!!

reviews.comment: She was a good professor. Very sassy though. Had to do a lot of presentations. I really miss that class though. Take the class because it teaches great communication skills and now I'm not as shy presenting!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She's really nice and her lectures aren't boring. Just make sure to read the rubrics for each speech. She grades you based on the rubrics and how much you've improved after each speech. The textbook is mandatory and homework is usually due every other week but the answers are usually in the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This is easily one of the greatest professors I've ever had at any school I've been to, and she's an even better person; one of the most understanding and also very energetic... she actually makes you want to come to this class. She opened up her classroom as a safe space and allows you to be a vulnerable individual without judgement!
She is a great professor and makes the class so much fun, engage and enjoy, I loved it

The easiest 5 stars I can give! She made this class so enjoyable for everyone! Very engaging activities and takes the time to build relationships with her students. She's so kind and sweet, there's a reason all of her reviews are 5 stars. If you're able to have Morgan Lord as your professor, take her course please! Very easy and little/no homework.
Absolutely love this professor! Easy A, attendance matters, and it's a very interactive class so get ready to play some childhood games and mini discussions. There is homework but no exam/quiz.

This woman is an angel sent from heaven. Her class is extremely interactive but wow it truly brought me out of my comfort zone. This is the best class I have taken at UIC and she makes it 100x better. She is someone you can build a bond with.
Love Professor Lord! She makes class very entertaining and engaging! Makes class super comfortable even tho it can get awkward at times. Def recommend her!!
Amazing, kind professor that made the class as painless as possible. Very enthusiastic and was able to motivate the class easily.

Professor Lord is nice and cares about her students feeling safe in her class. You have to participate a lot. However, Professor Lord creates a welcoming atmosphere. Most assignments are reflection-type assignments. You'll enjoy the class if you have a good attitude and are willing to participate.
Amazing human being and professor. Made the class feel like therapy while getting useful work done. Would take classes with her again.
One of the best professors ever. Very understanding and she accepted late work up until the last second possible. No test and no quizzes. Take her.
No Test, No quizzes, 1 Homework per week, Great Professor!!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Lord is such a fun and bubbly prof. They want to support many students and is an utter inspiration. This class really focused on the mental health aspect of business which I now understand is a crucial part of this industry. I am glad this course in mandatory for my major!
Professor Lord is super kind and caring. You can tell that she cares about your success in class. Great lectures and advice. 10/10!
Your loss if you don't take her. She is amazing. UIC needs more passionate and caring professors like her.

She is so outgoing and I genuinely looked forward coming into class every week. She does implement a little participation during class with speaking and moving around but that's what made class enjoyable. She offers many opportunities to revise homework and offers great feedback on homework assignments, resume related work, and personal experiences

Lord is the best BA200 professor at UIC for a reason. She goes over the top at helping her students become better professionals for the real world after college. Her classes are super discussion based, ultimately improving your speaking and communication skills. She is always helping her students w/ their overall professional presence.

Sweetest professor! light work that is actually helpful for you in the future. Attendance is part of your grade but she gives you 2 days off that won't affect your grade but overall she is very understandable about a situation.
She was one of the best professors I've taken. Although the improv games remind me of preschool, I had fun!

Morgan was such a great professor. Sine it's professional presence, showing up is very important. The classes were so entertaining though and the professor really helps everyone get comfortable with each other to the point where the class felt more like a hang out with friends rather than an actual class while still learning so so much!

Lord is the sweetest professor ever. Since it is a Business Administration class you have to be some type of outgoing. But if you're not that's okay because she makes you more comfortable with your peers by playing a lot of interaction games. Highly recommend her!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Lord was a really good teacher.  The class isnt tough, you just need to show up and do your work.  It was fun.

She is very well informed woman dont get me wrong but her class was difficult to do. Shes very lecture and test heavy and also the project could make or break your grade. Her teaching style is very one sided and difficult to understand to view if you have a open mind. dont take her if u just wanna pass the class
Disgraceful professor never seen someone like this before. At least it's her last semester at UIC so no one else would have to suffer what we went through.

This teacher expects so much work out of you. She expected at least 15 hours of homework per week outside of class, but it was crazy. She also gives out a lot of quizzes and has so many things to do for the class.  Also, her exams were super hard. On top of that, she gave us a research project which was horrible and with random groups.

Even though I have a B it's the worst class at UIC that I have taken. All the professor cares is to program your brain with her opinions. Almost all of her teachings are designed to brainwash you into being a leftist. I've stopped paying attention because her lectures are so bias and full of bs. Do not take her class at all avoid avoid avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Would not recommend this professor for this class. Whenever someone would ask a question, she would answer in a very condescending and passive aggressive way. She is very strict on grading, attendance is graded and she is strict on that too, even if you're 5-10 mins late she will take points off. By far worst experience I have had with a professor.

This was the most frustrating class I've taken at UIC. Instead of focusing on management, the professor frequently shifted discussions toward liberal political views, often presenting them as unquestionable facts. It felt more like a political seminar than a professional course. There was little room for open discussion or differing opinions.
Horrible professor, worst professor I've ever had; she does not care about you. If you write a lot, she claims it's ChatGPT. DO NOT TAKE AT ANY COST.
She yaps too much during class and is quick to give you a zero on reflections if you write more than a sentence, claiming it's ChatGPT. Not a great experience overall.
All she cares about is pushing her agenda. Has no interest in teaching actually things related to management. If you can avoid this class

Her class felt more like a platform for pushing a one-sided liberal agenda rather than encouraging open discussion. She insists on her own narrow perspective and shows videos that only push one side. Her grading is obsessively detailed to the point where it makes no logical sense. Steer clear of professors like her.

The worst professor I've ever had at my time at UIC. The class is supposed to be about management but instead has turned all political. She is pushing her communist marxist agenda on everyone in the class. She doesn't care about other viewpoints just her own. Avoid this class at all costs Do not make the same mistake I've made by picking her class.

When going into the class, I heard mixed reviews to be honest. Don't listen to the reviews, she's a great teacher. Her style of teaching actually makes you learn the material, and you can tell that she's passionate about the subject she's teaching. She's a very underrated professor, and you will learn a great deal in her class.

I barely did work outside of class and ended with a B. Her class is easy but if you want to get an A then you're going to have to put like 2 hours a week to do well. I did most of the assignments last minute and never studied and somehow got a B. She has a lot of extra credit so that probably helped. 4 quizzes & 1 test. She's a chill professor tbh
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her class is based off of the slides so make sure you take notes on that. Also do the readings before class because it makes your life much easier. Quizzes were very hard but she drops the lowest one which is nice. There is 1 exam and it was much easier than the quizzes. She gives out a ton of extra credit and is super nice so talk to her!

Professor Leitzinger was pretty good. Sometimes, she would click through the slides too fast or give confusing directions, but she cares so much about her students that that doesn't matter. The quizzes are pretty difficult; make sure you have good notes. There's only one exam, and it's easy. She also gives a lot of extra credit opportunities.

I read some reviews of people saying they fail the first quiz and yes I did as well. She drops one of them and gives TONS of extra credit for you to do well in the class. I failed the first quiz, got a 60% on the second and still ended with an A. She wants you to succeed and you can easily talk to her outside of class to figure out how to do better

Very engaging lectures. Make sure you take notes in class because the slides don't cover everything. Quizzes were hard but she does drop one of them. Exam was alright and actually easier than the quizzes. Few group projects so make sure you find some good people to work with. Her class wasn't hard at all, you'll need to spend some time to get an A.
If you expect to get an A without putting in the effort, don't take her. She expects you to participate. Quizzes are hard. The exam was not so bad. She has clear grading criteria.
I like the way she lectures, I just don't find the content interesting. Assignments are fairly easy if you read the book and pay attention to her class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I personally enjoyed her class a lot. Her lectures were engaging and interesting. The quizzes are open book but hard. A few group projects. You get four free absences but she expects you to participate when you're there. Also take notes in class because her lecture slides she posts don't have all the info!

Has a clear grading rubric. You either do it or you don't. Quizzes are hard, she lets you drop 1 so try to look out for how she questions you. You really have to understand the material if you want to do good. She's a nice teacher. Attendance is mandatory which sucks. She does let you miss 4 days tho. Overall not too bad just do the work!

4 quizzes, drops 1, 1 exam thats a midterm, if class participates then she doesn't make you take a final exam. Not sure why people think her class is hard. If you do the work then you'll get the grade you want. People who get anything lower than a B put in 0 effort. She offers lots of extra credit. Gives you 4 days to miss class without question.

Finished class today and I have to say she is one of the nicest professors at UIC. Mandatory attendance but lets you miss 4 days without any reason. If you participate in class it is free points. Her quizzes are tough but if you go to her office hours she will give you pointers on how to do better. There are a few group projects which are EASY!

Not a good class. Topics that are not interesting are hard to learn. Teacher warns students that failing quizs/ tests is ok. Personally believe that she should prepare students to do better and not tell the students that with an F on this quiz/ test that you could still get an A in the class. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great Professor who challenges students to learn! If you're expecting to get an A in the class for doing nothing, don't take it. If you care to learn about something and put in SOME effort, you'll at least get a B and up. Has multiple extra credit opportunities and is really great if you ask her for help during office hours. Actually speak to her!

Prof. Leitzinger is great, she is very caring and actually wants everyone to succeed. So, try your best, it won't go unnoticed. One exam, no final, 4 online quizzes (hard, do study guides, read lectures). Ask for quiz taking tips. PARTICIPATE!!! The lectures are interesting and engaging, with no book. This class is fun and 100% recommend.

I had a lot of things going on in my life and Professor Leitzinger was so nice about giving me extensions for assignments. She really cares for her students and just wants people to actually learn something. The majority of people who give her bad reviews are people who never show up to class and expect A's on everything. That is not how it works!

Probably one of the kindest teachers I have ever had throughout all of college. Really cares for you to learn. Has online quizzes and drops the lowest grade, gives out a ton of extra credit, lots of opportunity to do well in the class. Just make sure you go to class and attend lectures. Not sure why she has bad ratings but I would def recommend her

As a class/prof. Quizzes are very hard and there is a lot of material to complete outside class. Professor is very passive aggressive and only her opinion is correct. Quizzes and assignments do not reflect what you learn. The class is more of an environmentalist/social movement class rather than a business class. Be prepared. Extra Credit helped.

Professor Leitzinger is a real sweetheart.  She really cares about the students and wants you to learn about current social issues.  The class is really fun if you engage yourself.  There is a ton of materials to cover and it could get over overwhelming.  She does give a ton of extra credit and her office hours are open to student who needs help.

Very passive aggressive. The exams are terribly hard no matter how much you pay attention in class. Avoid this class if you can. She expects you to read articles upon articles in your free time and you still won't be able to pass the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: I fully understand all the concepts in this class and can apply it to outside of class but still got an F in the first quiz, like a lot of other people. The problem is she does not teach. She expects us to do so many of the readings before class and she discusses very few from it, but does not teach valuable concepts in class.
the first quiz was so difficult that I got f even though I paid attention in class and attended lecture during snow.

She is very passive aggressive. The material its self is not hard but she assigns too much hw and makes the class harder than it should be. She is very unclear and expects things she didn't ask for and she'll say "I thought it was obvious ". She does a group project that is worth 25% of your grade and is a waste of time. Worst class I've taken

PLEASE BE CAUTIOUS WHEN TAKING THIS PROF. There is a HEAVY workload on top of the group project. You're expected to keep up with the readings, homework and group assignments simultaneously. The material is interesting & you will learn a lot. She can be passive aggressive, but she does care about your mental health.

Nothing good to say about her. Very rude. don't listen to the recent ratings giving her 5's. that's not accurate at all. she's so mean. very hard quizzes. long readings every week. doesn't give any extra credit and has such a temper issue and constantly threatens to fail her students. read the older reviews for a more accurate assessment. BEWARE!

Honestly I really loved the class because the material discussed are topics i think everyone of every major should learn and understand. I don't understand why she has so many bad ratings, she really cares about the students & wants you to get an A. She gives out a lot of extra credit so if you get a low grade its your fault for not even trying

Great prof. The kids that gave her a bad review are the ones that don't listen and do the assignments. Overall a great class. Work needs to be done like all classes. This isn't a class you can breeze by. Just try a little and she will notice. Easy B if you give it effort.

She is obviously very well educated and has tons of knowledge. She requires you to understand the material and to be able to apply the concepts learned in class. Her exams are pretty hard and unless you have a very good understanding of the class, you won't do good.

Amazing professor. She curves a lot and gives a lot of extra credit opportunities. She also delays deadlines for you and is very accommodating. She also taught us how to do activism, which is very useful to know about. Lectures are very fun. She eliminated books and other things to reduce costs for students, so a "free" class. Participate in class!

I don't understand why so many people give her a bad rating. She is good. Do your part and ask questions and you will be fine. Some assignments are long but it's college... get used to it. She is awesome too outside of class. Very down to earth. Would take her again for other classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The professor is very intelligent and has designed the curriculum to encourage students to think at a higher level. Every class is interesting and loaded with information. I have taken away so much knowledge that I can apply to all my business courses.

The information taught in class was interesting, just the way that it is taught ruins the class experience. She goes the full period and just goes over the slides. She has some serious passive aggression and i personally did not enjoy going to this class at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is not really bad at all. She is really motivated by teaching her class. I love that. I learned a lot about the good and bad side of the actual businesses. You do not need to read the book. You have to take notes, attend classes and read the power points and you will be fine. If you wanna learn how ethical businesses are success go for it.

Professor Leitzinger is actually good. Lectures were somewhat interesting, compared to Management 340. The textbook was somewhat pointless though and I believe she shouldve made the group projects due 2 weeks before finals. Overall this is a relatively easy and interesting class. Study for the tests though, as they may be a bit tough if you dont

Her lectures are very organized and interesting. You have to participate either by speaking in class or posting online. Open note quizzes and cheat sheet allowed for exams. The group project takes some time however there is no other homework for the class.

This class isn't as bad as everyone makes it out to be, Its one of the easier classes you will take. The professor is new, but she's an easy grader and curves, their are readings but you can pass without reading as she lectures it in detail. The topics are entertaining and not stale. No homework, just group work once in a while. Easy & Fun class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Leitzinger has a ton of knowledge in the field and truly loves the material that she lectures. Class is extremely based on lectures and she wants you to be engaged to make it more fun, which I really enjoyed. She is a modern professor that focuses on CURRENT problems and issues which is really refreshing. Would definitely take again!

To be honest, she is not a bad teacher. Only thing is she is kind of vague when doing the final project. The course is not that bad, quizzes are online, and there is no homework other than readings. If confused in some areas, you can ask her and she will clear the confusion. Overall, i learned a lot from her class and would recommend you take her.
Horrible professor. Too many readings and the midterms are super hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: WORST professor at UIC. Avoid this class if you can. Lectures heavy, tons of reading material, assigned seating, and an unnecessary workload. Take this class with someone else if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Soooo much reading, you had to do a huge group project as well as a final exam. this class was one of the most stressful classes ever. It's like she thinks that youre only taking her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you're looking for a class to balance a tough schedule avoid any class taught by her. She doesn't understand that students juggle multiple responsibilities. She gave us assigned seating and doesn't listen to your concerns. She makes her own exams, each multiple choice question is a paragraph long FOR NO REASON. Horrible professor sorry.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: AVOID. She made us buy a book that costs almost $100 and mid-semester she realized how much of a mistake it was because we aren't even tested on the book material. She told us there's nothing she can do and we have to suck it up. She overcomplicates the simplest things and does not value your opinion. Class is run how she wants it only.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She makes a class that is supposed to be easy extremely hard. There is a 20 page group project + presentation at the end of the semester. Exams and quizzes have nothing to do with what we learned in class.
Avoid if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Clearly she's a new professor because she takes attendance based on where you sit and it's annoying. Her lectures are extremely long and she uses the whole class time, so don't expect to leave early. Doesn't let you use your laptop in class, she wants you to take actual notes, but she wants to "save trees". She's extra, annoying and boring!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is a new professor and it shows. Very unorganized and reads straight from powerpoint, doesn't have much input from there. She makes a seating chart for attendance. Gives you 4 articles and sections of the textbook to read in between lectures. Doesn't believe in laptops in class, but exams/quizzes are online. VERY SLOW grader
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Lyles is an incredible professor, and his lectures are informative, interactive, and enjoyable. His classes are not passive lecture classes; you need to stay engaged and prepared. He is heavily respected by his students and colleagues. Lyles is a very rare type of professor/mentor; make your time with him count!
such entertaining discussions from pol 354, i really wish i payed attention more it was a really great class lol. rigor is just like any other hs AP class, dw.

Like the person before me said, not having the lectures accessible outside of class, skipping over slides, but then still testing on it. Too focused on not running out of time, while simultaneously rambling or trying to have heated discussions rather than giving examples of the cases. I like his personality and he is nice, but very unorganized.

not sure if I will be taking him again.  he has an idea on how to set a tone for the class in order for us to succeed, but focus is more on rushing through materials so we can keep up to pace. He doesn't care much on how we apply cases, as he withholds material such as class slides, which makes it hard for us to prep for  tests.  a complete riddle
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: If you're genuinely passionate about political science, take all of Lyles's classes. He is extremely knowledgeable and you will, without fail, walk out a changed person. Lot's of reading but for good reason. Many extra credit opportunities as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Lyles is the best professor I have ever had. Would highly recommend Pols 356 + 358. I have learned so much from Professor Lyles and his passion for the coursework permeates throughout the class. If you are looking for an easy A, Lyles is not your guy. But if you are truly here to learn, take every course he offers.

Graduating this semester but had to rate Prof Lyles before I go. Quite literally the best professor in the PoliSci department. His classes require work and aren't an easy A, but this man truly inspires confidence in students and wants to help you grow. Every debate in that class made me learn something new and I always felt like my voice was heard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: My all time favorite professor for sure. The midterms and final are definitely not easy but with all the extra credit he offers an A is definitely possible. As long as you're engaged in class you will be okay!

This is my third time taking a class with Dr. Lyles, and I can't praise the man enough. Yes, there is a lot of homework- but really his lectures are what you should be paying the most attention to. Read the cases, understand the basic significance, comment on WP, and you should be good. Bonus- do the EC. Genuinely the best professor I've ever had.
The class can be a little intimidating, because he has no problem calling on you but he's extremely thorough in his lectures and I learned a lot from him!
He's a funny professor and all but attendance is 30% of your grade and his tests are a bit confusing.

I've taken Professor Lyles for 3 classes. He's an amazing Professor that jokes with his students yet remains respectful. There are no papers due. Grades are based off participation, midterm, and final. You have to post comments on ever case he assigns which is no big deal. I learned so much about our country's history during his lectures.

If you miss two days of readings its gonna be an uphill battle. He offers a lot of extra credit that can save you from the tough final/midterm. It is tough to reach him via email. The material is extremely interesting. I do not recommend taking his courses if you have more than one other tough class, because this one takes a lot of time and effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The absolute worst professor any student can take. This professor set the entire class up for failure during the last few weeks of class. I am sick to my stomach writing this review as Professor Lyles made it his personal agenda to disregard the needs of his students. From not replying to emails, to failing to input grades, this professors trash.

Incredible professor. I took four of his classes, and I couldn't be happier. The topics were very interesting and they inspired me to pursue a law path. I'm going to law school next semester, and I cannot thank him enough for that. Just fantastic.

Professor Lyels was one of the best teachers Ive had in my life. He keeps his class engaged by doing a hybrid of lecture and Socratic seminar teaching. He allows his students to voice their opinion while also clarifying if that student gets something incorrect. He gives a lot of work but you learn so much in his classes. Highly recommend.

After 4 semesters and many classes, I've realized I've only had a few memorable professors. Lyles is the one I remember the most because of the way he teaches. He keeps you engaged with the material and doesn't hold your hand so it forces you to think critically about what happened with cases and why things are the way they are and were.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He's a really great instructor! Really engaging. Lots of work, but once you fall in the rhythm it's manageable. Teaches you a ton of really fascinating things that are applicable outside of a constitutional law focus. Really enjoyed the class! There are DOZENS of extra credit opportunities that help pad your grade for the exams.
Fantastic professor. He is extremely funny and knowleable in the field.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awesome, awesome, awesome professor. I love this class and Lyles is an excellent professor.
Professor Lyles is an excellent professor. He is funny and I learned a lot in his class. In fact, I'm going to take him next semester as well, and possibly more in the future.
Helped me learn how to break down a case and required me to be prepared. Took this class a while back but lessons he taught still hold true today.
This one of the greatest and most intellectual professors I ever had the opportunity to have. Be prepared to learn some very useful and life changing material.

Professor Lyles is one of the most intellectually advanced and student-oriented teachers on the campus of UIC. I took POLS 354, 356, and 358 with him and although they are constututional law classes, I learned so much more than legal history. These classes are meant for anyone interested about the history of each subject.

If you aren't pre-law, understand that 353, 354,356, and 358 are Constitutional LAW classes. Lyles is thoughtful enough to use the Socratic method, have case briefs as assignments, and unleash on the heavy reading--all things common in grad level law classes. The point in heavy reading is to help you decipher challenging material accurately

Took 4 course with this professor (POLS 353, 354, 356, and 358). Each course offered something new and they were the most beneficial classes I have taken at UIC. You have to show up to class to keep up and must put in work daily to pass with an A. 100% my favorite professor I had at UIC.

We spent the lecture before our 2nd exam, discussing our "feelings" on the election, instead of reviewing for the exam, and we spent the lecture before our 3rd exam discussing whether or not we believed taking the class was "worth it." Dude never mentioned that the constitution is a "contract" which "the people" are beneficiaries of; which is basic

Take his class if you plan to go to law school! His lectures are interesting yet confusing... falls off track and blabs most of the time. He slides through his powerpoint so fast that you can't even write one thing down. His tests are hard. Offers extra credit but the requirements are intensive; they're long papers. NOT a blow off class.

He means well. However, the material is long to read, difficult to understand on your own and yet he quizzes you on it. The wiki is confusing, his lectures are all over the place and difficult to follow. His teaching style is not the best.  Oh and his PP slides are copied and pasted from sites you can find on Google. I would avoid him.

There are a lot of case briefs. By the end of the course, it becomes a good skill to have. The tests won't be easy if the material isn't studied. The wiki is used for this course and it's confusing at first, but you should get used to it. The lectures are fun and interesting and there are opportunities for extra credit. Professor is fair.
Very good teacher

Took this class over Spring everyone kept saying how hard it was. Not difficult at all. Just copy the Powerpoint slides,listen in class and you don't even need to read his textbook which is actually really well written. Fun class, no stress, I definitely recommend it! Easy class.

You absolutely have to do the readings to stand a chance in this class. With that out of the way, Lyles is one of the best (if not THE best) profs I've had in college. He's motivated, articulate and has a command of information like none other. If you're looking for a blow-off class keep looking, but otherwise it's well worth your time.
Lyles is one of the best Professors at this school. He knows how to teach, and how to make it sound important.

I loved POLS354 because you actually get better by the end of the semester. Lyles is awesome and has a good sense of humor that serves the purpose of learning. Attendance is def. mandatory to do well. He gives many chances to improve your grade & is super approachable/nice.Lots of material but you will easily get used to it.Two words: Study groups!

AMAZING professor. Funny. Interesting. Hands down, I had my mind opened up to so many things! I will never look at the laws of the nation the same way again. I don't like law, but I LOVED this class. Attendance is mandatory to do well, as well as taking detailed notes. Phenomenal teacher/person and Phenomenal class!

Professor Lyles is awesome! he makes each class interesting pushing you to think harder about constitutional questions and reasons for court decisions. He is very smart and tries his best to make sure you understand the material. You can tell he enjoys teaching. Attendance is a must if you want to do well in this class.

Professor Lyles is, hands down, the best professor in the Political Science department at UIC.  His class is challenging, and attendance is a MUST. Nevertheless, the material is interesting and he really inspires critical thinking!

It was a very interesting class especially if your interested in constitutional law.  Have to attend lecture to understand the class.  Lyles is a very good professor but his course can be difficult if you don't attend class.

vague rants that surely had a point at least when he begins speaking. the most scatter brained syllabus and endless readings, most of which are labeled as recommended to optional, but then are also fair game for the mid-term! the gws component is really more like a footnote to this class, rather than it's joining half

As long as you read the required material and take good notes, you will do just fine in this class. the midterm and final were online and they are open note. he also gives out xtra credit assignments too. the lectures were a bit dry, but daily attendance with benefit you greatly!

I enjoyed this class and I learned a lot. Professor Lyles works hard 2 make sure tht his students are grasping the material. He does assign tons of reading material (most of which is useless, unless you just njoy reading). Skip the "recommended" readings and focus on the required ones. Midterm is hard, but passable if you prepare/organize ur notes.
He grades tough and requires A LOT, but is a great professor.  Huge setback=does not respond timely to emails.

I personally loved his class. Very engaging and knowledgeable. Very enjoyable class. He usually pretty fun. There is a bit a reading to do. Make sure you do your briefs. They really help around exam time. He combined 251 & 252 together so it did move alot faster. Take his class!!
It's crucial to attend class, but every minute is worth it.  Lyles makes the discrepancies in law come to law and really shows how they affect us.  great classes.
This guy is cool...he looks exactly like Uncle Phil from Fresh Prince of Bel-Air...however very hard tests and ALOT to read...be careful...would not recommend!

He is a great professor, but getting an appointment to meet after class (which is the only way he rolls) is damn near impossible.  Expect to wait a couple weeks, especially after midterms.  GO TO CLASS and take notes.  He's a nice guy and makes things interesting, but most of the BB things are unneeded, except the chapters.
Rather than waste my life typing away, I agree with every comment...highly recommend this guy

Prof. Lyles is amazing! He is clear, concise, and he really cares about the subject and makes sure that the students understand it. DO YOUR WORK! It's very important. Above all, have fun--he does! He makes constitutional law hilarious sometimes. Also, be prepared to defend your reasoning--he won't just listen to your answer and move on.

Prof. Lyles is an awesome teacher. His exams are straight from lectures, make sure you take good notes. Although, his exams are fairly tricky, but once you learn his style, its easy. He really enjoys teaching and the subject matter is interesting, overall great class.
nice professor.  very helpful.

A genuinely good professor.  His lectures are very interesting and what you learn actually is useful.  His tests are difficult and require a lot of logical thinking, but it's a good preparation for law school.
The most respectable and intriguing professor ever!!! So nice and understanding as well!

Excellent professor, excellent class. Lyles uses the Socratic method in a way that keeps all students involved. You must keep up with the work to succeed in this class, but the effort is well worth it.  Highly recommend!!

Pff, I never did a single case review, never read the book, wrote far fewer notes than everyone else seemed to, and didn't study until the night before the test for a few hours (from class notes), and I got an A. The class was a lot easier than people dramatically have made it out to be. Just make sure you learn from your midterm mistakes.

Excellent professor, excellent class.  Lyles uses the Socratic method in a way that keeps all students involved.  You must keep up with the work to succeed in this class, but the effort is well worth it.  Fabulous preparation for law school.  Highly recommend!!
No Comments

I don't agree that he employs the "Socratic method to its finest," but I also don't agree that he's a terrible teacher. I liked him a lot, but I do think he picks "favorites" in the class, and I also didn't like how a lot of the time, if he was running behind, he wouldn't call on you if you raised your hand with a question. Still, take his class!

I thought he was terrible- told me I was too "dumb for law school" I went anyway and did great -what a terrible teacher- go be a law professor if that's what you want BUT constitutional law can be interesting and informative but when you spent five weeks on marbury  v madison -i undertand now that you have no clue

The Socratic method at its finest, to this day his politics are unknown to me.His teaching style will give a heads up on what law school is about.Expect to earn your A, do lots of case briefs, & study up on quotes he uses in class for the exam.

Well, my biggest complaint is the testing done in the class.  Seems to focus on extranious details a bit, and is the same test he gives every semester.  Plus you have to read his book and give a critique, which is a little odd.

Amazing teacher.  Very well informed, and it showed in his manner of teaching.  Do not expect an easy A, but if you truly are interested in political science, and willing to work for an A, definitely take his classes.

Took this course online in summer. The lectures are time consuming but contain all the information you need for exams. Exams themselves usually focus on the easier topics within the unit and are easy to score well on and carry the most weight. HW is nearly identical to quiz material. Textbook readings are assigned but you can get away without them.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing professor! There were plenty of extra credit opportunities and fun group activities. Definitely study for those exams tho! Microbiology ended up being my favorite class, and Professor Mills played a big role in that.

exams were worth 70% and the average scores were about 60% each time, Mills had content he often did not fully cover or mention in lecture, textbook as not much of a help either. Like most other bio courses it's a ton of memorization, lectures were basically pointless.

The course can be taken online during the summer. Which is probably for those that failed the class in the regular semester. Practice exams, quiz, and homework don't match up with the actual exam. I wrote 28 pages of notes based on lectures and most of it doesn't show up on the exam. He doesn't answer emails, go in-person
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Read off slides and explained very little, exams were nothing like the practice quizzes and very few questions worth so many points. topics came up on the exams that was never covered, briefly mentioned or wasn't included in the exam review sheets.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super organized blackboard page made it so easy to stay on top of the class and really understand material. He's a great guy and is really good at presenting and explaining the material.
take him trust
great prof
He will just read off of slides during lecture. Exams would be nothing like the "study guides".

Very effective communicator. Lectures were very well organized. We would have review sessions in class before the exams during the following lecture time which mirrored the exam questions. Gave me a lot of good advice for graduate school. Professor's got jokes too! This class helped me understand the biological side of medicinal chemistry.

Class was not bad as long as you watched the lecture videos before exams. He also has the exam topics from each lecture and gives out lots of extra credit, so make sure you go to class! Very nice person overall. Highly recommend!

Professor is caring but overall structure of class is very confusing. Tests get difficult as the semester progresses and are NOT open note. Many quizzes and homework assignments. Case studies felt like a waste of time. Extra credit could be earned through review days but not super clear. Overall grades are not made available until finals week.
This professor is very understanding about your situation, and the class is really easy, would recommend if Bios 350 is needed. The exams are understandable just pay attention in class.
Prof. Mills is cool. Lectures were easy to follow and tests weren't bad as long as you pay attention. I also appreciated the extra credit opportunities he gives.

Syllabus changes every semester, entire course depends on when you take it. Extra credit is so complicated. Must attend review days & only get points if ur team wins. 53 exam questions in 50 minutes. Impossible if english isn't ur 1st language. My notes are 28+ pgs. Too strict for a 300 lvl. All my other 300 profs are lenient & NEVER have 50+ q's.

the case studies sucked because the TA's took grading them so personal. each homework is EC if you get a 100% (unlimited tries). attendance is EC if you go on days he takes it. there is an exam or quiz every week basically and exams are only open 9am-3pm so leave time for them.

Not only does he have a very confusing syllabus, but he also doesn't make grades visible until week of finals. He is also very strict when it comes to grade rounding, even if it is less than half of a percent. He also never responds to emails, and he acknowledges that his average grade for each exam drops (per semester), but does nothing about it.

Exams are HARD. However, he provides LOTS of resources to help you succeed. Do the interactive textbook and TAKE NOTES because all the exams are open note. Make sure you understand the pathways. He's super nice and chill and willing to help in any way that he can. Lectures can get really boring because he's hard to hear so sit in the front.

Homework is ec, quizzes are closed notes and very easy points. Although Exams are open notes but be prepared before you take them. Attendance is not mandatory but attending a class gives you ec too. there is alot of ec chances in this class to boost your grade to an A. Case studies, find a good group to work with and you'll easy ace them.

He is very nice to his students. Homework is ec, quizzes are open notes and very easy points. Exams are closed notes but manageable. Attendance is not mandatory although attending a class gives you ec too. there is alot of ec chances in this class to boost your grade to an A.
