reviews.comment: Theys has been teaching 261 for twenty years, and it shows. He's perfected a style of teaching that works if you follow his directions: read. Reading the textbook *and* understanding is the key to success in this course. Read, show up to lecture, and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This is a difficult class since is all new material, however Prof. Theys is very approachable and would help you to succeed, use his office hours. TAs are also very hopeful during labs and office hours
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He's a good lecturer, the slices are well-made, things are all planned out. Gives interactive lecture with examples and clicker questions. The labs are hard but they do help you understand, or at least know what you don't understand about the materials. Definitely better than your average professors. homework and exams are all fare games.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Theys is a very smart professor who will challenge you dramatically but will also make sure that you leave the class knowing what is going on. He can seem a little abrasive at first but he means nothing but the best for his students and this is clear in his lectures. He is always ready to re-explain something or clarify any questions.

My only complaint is the amount of homework, some weeks we would have multiple different assignments going on at once. He's a great lecturer and knows what he's talking about. I didn't read much, failed most of the reading quizzes but I still ended with an A. Exams were almost the same thing as the practice exam so study those hard. Would recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: zyante for hw, 9 labs, final group project, midterm and a final. great lecturer.

Professor Theys is a really fair and approachable guy, don't hesitate to ask questions in class cause many people don't, or go to him for help. The book was definitely a must-have for my success in the class. If you find yourself struggling, make sure to do the readings and they will get you far for exams. Overall, I would recommend taking him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: This class was very difficult, but I also didn't read any of the book. There's a good chance that I'll pass with a B if I do ok on the final, so it's definitely achievable. I actually enjoyed his lectures. I don't really have any complaints about the class since I made it hard on myself by not reading. (Definitely Read, the few times i did helped)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: pretty lenient grading on exams and projects. Really good at the material he is teaching
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Good professor, his midterms are exact like old midterms so get yourselfs a copy of previous semester one way or another. The projects can be time consuming but office hours r a blessing and google

Really good professor. Make sure to show up to class, do the homework, and read the book. As long as you do that you're pretty much guaranteed to get an A on the midterms. His midterms are pretty similar from semester to semester, only changing 1-2 questions. The final could vary a lot more, so be aware of that. Projects aren't too bad either.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: His lectures are straightforward, and if you take the time to read the book thoroughly, you should be able to get at least a B. A lot of people struggle in this class because they refuse to read the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lectures are a bit boring. Lots of iclickers. Labs are based on material he hasn't gone over yet. Weekly schedule is a bit weird but overall not a terrible experience. Very knowledgeable and explains things well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Knows his stuff, but the class is difficult and the way he teaches it makes things worse. Wrongly assumes that people understand the material after reading the book. This can make labs and reading quizzes guessing games. His exams are very similar to the practice which can save your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very literal prof... #1 thing i took from his class is how to answer silly questions. If you're the type of student who comes to lecture expecting to be taught you will not have a good time. If you're the type of student who comes to lecture wishing for new doors to be discovered, you will be challenged appropriately.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: The living embodiment of "weed out class". Only the strong survive.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: cool guy and hair
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Do not miss ANY ZyBooks hw assignments as they are weighted somewhat heavily. If you have no experience with C, get ready for a long semester. ASK QUESTIONS, LOTS OF THEM, as he moves forward if nobody asks questions. Written exams aren't that bad but inlab finals are challenging. CS lounge will be your home away from home! Avoid him if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: A great lecturer, but throws you off the deep end a lot. MAKE SURE TO READ YOUR TEXTBOOK BEFOREHAND.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: The professor is intelligent, but he is a mediocre professor. Clarity and purpose is lacking in his lectures. You will buy an online book that helps teach programming in easy steps. All he does is repeat what you read. He does not teach you anything that the book did not tell you already. Lectures are only for participation points. BOOK > PROFESSOR
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Lectures are more like discussions. Uses a program called Zybook that serves as the "textbook", but its very interactive, easy to use, and well-understood. CS 107 is a very flexible class, so if you're ahead, you don't have to wait for others. Sarcasm for the most part is on point.
Class is setup so that you do most of the work on your own and lectures are an opportunity for questions, so you have to be a little self motivated.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Watch out, he knows some things that make's him dangerous.

Love his sarcasm. Challenging class but good for you. Fair grader and in general. Consistent due dates. Up-to-date grades. Questions? then ask and you shall receive. Expect to read and use of iclickers. Somewhat fast pace (good & bad). Amazing professor.

Pretty hard class, and you need to put in a lot of work. If you put in the work this class is super easy. I never used the book and struggled pretty hard, but I think I'm pretty smart so keep up with the class and do the homework. Also he is very sarcastic which is both good and bad. He knows what he's talking about and fun to listen to.

GoTo class and ask tons of questions. He moves on if no one asks questions because he expects you to have done the reading. He provides previous semesters exams and changes around some of the values in the problem. So if you're confused you can work out the problems and figure things out that way. Very nice guy. Loved having him for both 261 & 362

You need to ask questions in class. If you do not, he'll assume you understand and move on. Don't be afraid or embarrassed to ask questions; a good majority of the class is probably just as confused. Labs and homework are difficult, especially if you don't read the book! I didn't and learned the hard way. He does clicker quizzes almost every class
He's the best professor in UIC. Tests are fair. Wants us to learn the material, more importantly understand it. Overall very interesting class. Glad to have theys in 261 and 362.

Do the homework, ask questions in class, and spend some time independently researching the material and you'll do fine. Don't expect a free ride: Professor Theys doesn't curve the hell out of his class, unlike many professors I've had. If you're willing to learn, he's willing to teach, you just have to work for it. One of the best at UIC.
If you come to class, and do the HW, you WILL pass, if not, you wont.

WANTS his students to learn and WILL teach his students. Nope, the latter doesn't exist in his dictionary. He basically wants YOU to learn (somehow with magic) without his help. If you can learn yourself from book, CS-261 is a great class to understand the fundamental architect. I hope if he understand students PAY to learn from him.
Really wants students to learn the material.

The class covers several topics: logic gates, muxdecoder, sequential circuits, control words, processor, USB packets, RAM cells, and virtual memory. Arduino labs and a project are also expected. The exams are easy after going over HW's and previous exams, which he posts on Piazza. For me, his lectures and notes are not great, I relied on the book.

There is a quiz here and there with clickers. Tests are a little hard, but completely fair. Lots of reading involved. One of the best professors at UIC. Really cares about the fact that you understand the material and you're not just passing by. Expects questions from people and will help you as long as you ask.

cs 362 is more laid back than 261.  Focuses more on the arduino and some more hardware side of cs.  the class itself I'd say is a bit easier than 261.  Did below average on both midterm and final and still ended up with a high B.  Most of the work is from the final project (not hard), labs, and homework.  Cracks a joke here and there.

He uses the book a lot. Be sure to read and skim before for each week. If you don't understand anything make sure you ask him because he will explain it real well. Test can be tough make sure to study. Any doubts ask him that is the key. Class is on the harder side but its manageable if you stay on top of things. Classes are entertaining and fun.

Theys' classes are really easy if you keep up with the material and constantly ask questions in class. If no one has any questions on a topic, he's just going to move onto the next one. Exams were basically copypaste of the practice exams he provides. Projects were relatively easy although some have unclear instructions. Clicker quizes in class.

There is no book bc its expensive enough to buy an arduino kit, 150$. He offers supplementary texts from where he gets his lecture info from, buy one 35$. Hw is challenging but doable. Labs are easy to moderate but daunting at first read.  You design a final project based on arduino. There is still a final exam and  a midterm but they aren't hard.

Theys is a good, clear lecturer with a good sense of humor.  He also has a good sense of how his class can foster an all around skill set for a professional (challenging homework, group interactions, writing, and presentations).  I've taken 3 courses with him and would take more if I could.
Great professor! One of the better ones that the CS department at uic has to offer! The book is mandatory for this class so make sure you keep up on the chapters or you will get lost easily!
Great Professor, His projects are challenging and exams are very theory based. His grading is very tough!!!

Overall excellent professor. Challenges his students. Brings sarcasm and sense of humor. He knows the material. For the most part he teaches it well. Sometimes he changes his techniques and they are not as productive. He will not spoon feed you. You may get lost. If you ask for help he may bring you back up to speed. I recommend reading the book!

Great professor. He is really helpful when students ask for help. He really wants his students to learn the material. Sure the class was really hard, it's a combination of two courses which was recently split in two, but the professor only made it easier. Did a great job at teaching CS201.

Class is hard but because of the material. It'd be difficult regardless of who was teaching. Explanations were well done, you ask questions and you get answers, fair grader. If you put in effort for his class (and trust me, it needs a lot) and consistently keep up with the material, you'll be fine. Definitely not an easy A, but is anything?

Theys seemed to be a very mediocre professor. I had him for both 201 and 266 the same semester, and the main problem with his classes is that there is too much material to cover, and he knows it! Doesn't care that his class averages are in the 50's, and he doesn't curve so grades are poor. The project was extremely difficult. I don't recommend him!

Very good teacher. Demanding, unmerciful, mocking but definitely teaches well and provides enough tools for everyone to succeed and exceed. Doesn't care about student's grades, just that they get what's going on.
Never take him if he is teaching CS.

Grades too difficult, moves too fast, this includes my having spoken personally to him, my having taken thorough class notes, and my having managed to pull A's in college computer and coding classes. Workload too heavy, I felt like I needed to quit work and move back in with my parents to keep up. Worst classroom experience ever. Very disappointed.

Lots of work but if you enjoy programming the projects are all easy, you don't need to buy the book it is just for reference, but you can use google to help instead.  You only need to show up for labs and tests, he posts all assignments and notes online.

Brains and ability to be good, but doesn't respect students.  Smug, sarcastic, and egotistical. Has a who-cares attitude, he-knows-the-stuff-lets-see if-you-can-follow-along... I'd rather spend my money on someone who knows less, but has a better sense of the learning process and less of an ego.  Notes are useless, lab/project guidance worse...

I have never had so much homework in my life. He piled on a program, lab, test, codelab, and quiz all in the same week. This is not unusual for him. He is a fine teacher but gave way to much homework. He's also not very helpful in class when students asked questions. I can't believe how much work I did and then end up with a B.

somehow assumed that we know everything already and dont need to be taught. lecture is useless. outside of class, he's a nice guy. he also seems like a pretty smart man. however, he did not succeed in passing down his knowledge of programming to us nubins too well. sorry theys..

Professor Theys is absolutely AWESOME! He genuinely cares about your grade in the class and notices the effort that you put in. He doesn't "curve" and people tend to think that's bad but he actually does a mean shift which helped me a lot and got me an A in the class ^_^. DEFINITELY recommend any class that he might be teaching.
Professor Theys is cool :)

One of the best CS professors at UIC. Knows the material well. Class is not very easy, but if you go to every lecture and read the pertinent sections in the book (preferably before lecture), the material won't be very hard to understand. He posts lecture notes from every lecture online, which is very helpful.

VERY fair grader; Notes always available online, so you can concentrate on participating in the class. Exams are VERY fun too. He pulls questions right out of "Professor Layton and the Curious Village." It's a good choice too, the game really helps put you in the right mindset for problem solving skills you'll need in this class. Totally take him!
Very good teacher.  Speaks clearly.  At times can get boring.  When he asks a question in class he won't continue until somebody answers the question.

The material was very fast paced, but he was more than willing to help the students through whatever problems they had with it. He was easy to understand and encouraged class attendance and participation.  He recommended a particular book, but was open to students using whatever text they felt comfortable with.

Theys is one of the better teachers in the dept. Most profs are obsessed with research and you can tell teaching a class gets in the way of their work, not here. Prof. Theys is very knowledgeable, and is quite easy to get along with. His courses tend to be a bit more work than others, but the knowing the material is worth it. Grading is fair.

He's a very funny professor, which made the class really enjoyable. I was afraid that this might be another english class, which I hate, but it wasn't, it was really fun and I wish every professor was like him.

Cool and funny guy, he is very laid back. Just one assignment per week and 4 projects. Load is definetly manageable even if you are taking other CS courses. Exams are medium difficulty, but if you go to lecture and study a little before you will be alright. I think hes professor's troy's younger brother.

Excellent professor, very funny, very friendly. I enjoyed the class very much, and I hope he teaches again, so other students can benefit. It has a lot of writing assignments, but they are more about what you think about this (issue). I highly recommend you to take this class if he's teaching it.

really good and fun teacher, he's not easy but if you come to class and do some studying before exams you'll be fine. Projects not bad, they take time but are not that difficult, again read examples and book and you will be able finish them before due date.

Goes to fast during the course. Projects are assigned weeks before he even goes over the material you need for the projects. Spends to much time on things that does not matter and to little on things that do. Exams are straight forward though, study hard and go to lecture everyday and you should be OK.

He is good at answering questions, and the concepts he teaches are very straight forward. If you read the book you'll be fine. His projects are nice and not too bad, but challenging enough so you're not bored. Just understand the concepts in the book and you should get an A.
You have to read the textbook and learn by yourself
Professor Theys sucks at teaching , he uses Powerpoint slides a lot. The slides put you to sleep in class. Good at grading and the tests are pretty straight forward.

Prof. Theys is a very good teacher.  He will make you work, there is no question.  However, I fell that I know my material from CS 266 so well, that I can understand the concepts I'm learning now in CS 366 much better than I otherwise would.

I have never met a teacher who cares so much about the future of her students and what they get out of her class. She is very articulate and helps her students think critically, even if they have less experience with public speaking and literature. She pushes her students to apply for scholarships and become the best version of themselves.

I took her class on masterworks in Polish literature, and she has an amazing breadth of historical and literary knowledge. I am an English major and I learned more about how to analyze texts just in her class than in all of my English major courses. Her lectures might be disorganized at times, but if you pay close attention you'll do fine.

Dr. Underhill is one of the best professors I had at UIC. She is very kind and passionate about the material she teaches. She takes an interest in her students and her office hours are always open! I feel like I learn a lot in her classes. The readings are very interesting! She also inspired me to pursue a Polish major.

Dr. Underhill is far and away the most enthusiastic, helpful, and inspiring professor I have had the pleasure of meeting at UIC. She genuinely cares about her students and goes to great lengths to see them succeed both inside and outside the classroom. She is truly passionate about what she teaches and her enthusiasm comes through in every class.

For a gen ed, this class was fairly difficult. The professor was amazing but it's the material that made the class pretty tough. Movies were usually over an hour long, one of them even 3 hours long. Quizzes every week on the movie you watched and hw every other weekend. Coming into the class knowing nothing about cinema, it was hard to keep up.

Professor Underhill was one of the best professors I had at UIC. She is very enthusiastic about teaching students new content. She is very kind and respectful. Taking POL 150 was a great experience. I learned a lot throughout this course and I cannot be more happy that I registered for this class. It was really fun.

I had Professor Underhill for my POLS 150 class this spring semester of 2021. Honestly, I do not regret taking her class, as she was very understanding about anything that may arise when dealing with online classes. Very passionate, gives great feedback, and overall helps to the best of her ability to make you succeed in her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Karen is one of the most vivacious, engaging, and knowledgable professors I have ever had - she takes a personal interest in every student and is invested in seeing them succeed. Her enthusiasm is infectious and makes you want to put in extra effort, even if she is a generous grader. If I could take all of her classes, I would.

Professor Underhill is the most passionate teacher I've ever met. She truly cares about the topic of the class and cares even more about her students. You need to read in order to understand what's going, and although some readings were confusing, they were all mostly enjoyable. I would love to have her again as a professor.

Very fun class. Learn not only about movies, but the time periods they were made and gain a deeper understanding of historical and political movements that contributedaffected a certain style in the way a director filmed a particular movie. Very engaging and informative class, met once a week for almost 3 hrs. Become familiar with PL's movie stars. Professor very helpful and informative, approachable. Fantastic teacher!!!!

Wonderful, down to earth, and approachable professor who genuinely cares about her students and their interest and understanding in the subject matter. Excellent lectures, information-filled, inspiring, open discussion and opinion interaction between instructor and student. Most of reading material uploaded to BB which is a plus. Expect to participate in discussion and weekly HW. Put in good effort and get a good grade!!!!!

Karen is an amazing professor. She is very ready to meet outside of class to discuss any issues you might have had with the reading or any further interest you have in the topic. She is a very generous grader and is constantly looking for ways to help you improve. She can occasionally be a bit scatter-brained but overall she is on of the best!

She knows her Polish history and loves Polish literatureart.  you will read a few stories in English and then interpret their meaning. Not hard! She explains everything and if you want to participate she gives you a chance. I would take any class with her, shes very enthusiastic

Professor Underhill defines the definition of a great and caring professor. After every class I left her lecture with an appreciation and genuine interest for the topic(s) discussed. She shows genuine interest and dedication to each student and provides great feedback and fair grading. Her exams cover exactly what is clearly presented in class.

Professor Underhill is one of the best at UIC. She is knowledgeable and intensely passionate about her field. I took this class as a gen-ed but emerged greatly interested in Polish literature. There is a decent amount of writing but she is a more lenient grader and provides excellent feedback.

This teacher is really funny.  She expects a lot from you, and a lot of writing.  This class was fun but you do have hw almost every week and I recommend going to class.  Really nice and enthusiastic and generous grader.
Comprehensive, caring, detail-focused.
Great prof, knows his stuff and explains material well. Felt safe asking questions and grading was fair. Will take him again if there is an opportunity. Thanks

Great prof. Knows his stuff. Book was optional and free. 8 homeworks and 8 quizzes plus a final exam, pretty straightforward grading no surprises on the assignments. I had to take this class since I didn't pass pre req for Phys 141.

Hands down, the best professor I had in LAS. The grading was straightforward, and there were lots of examples during lectures. Although the homework assignments were challenging, they proved immensely valuable in reinforcing my understanding. I highly recommend him for PHYS 131/132 without a doubt.

Vlad is the most incredible physics professor. He cared about about students and  was always available for questions over email. I felt safe to ask questions and never felt judged. He made the subject come alive and fueled our enthusiasm. I'd take him again for PHYS 131/132

Do not take this course with this professor unless he is the only one teaching it then good luck. Most of the problems he does aren't what the homework is about. Sloppy handwriting so taking notes was hard. Would show a problem & then would turn off mic & camera for the entire class period. Doesn't even offer textbooks. Don't take this professor.

SUCH A GOOD PROFESSOR. The discussion we would have in class were great and she was also very helpful when it came to questions about assignments or feedback. I recommend everyone take one of her Latino/a literature classes because of well she teaches the rich history of Latin America through stories.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: LOVE THIS WOMAN!! I reccommend this class 100%, if you're good at writing this class is an easy A. She is the coolest teacher, totally laid back and easy going and so helpful too. Great professor!
Awesome! Very helpful!
she is one of the best professor's! She is pretty cool and laid back. the class isn't hard at all as long as your papers aren't crappy. i really enjoyed going to this class!
she was great and really helpful her grading is ambiguous she gives A/B for example but it worked for me in the end but you have to come to every class to get a good grade

Papers were graded harder than expected, but overall she wants her students to do well. Go to class even if the material isn't that interesting. Also, try to take advantage of her help- she's always willing to spend extra time outside of class.

I took her for an american fiction class as an elective in spring 08. I felt like i was failing the whole time but i ended up with an A for my final paper really helped me out. I ended up talking to her mid-way about how I was struggling and asked for clear guidlines on what to do, after that it was smooth sailing

Ullibari enjoys teaching and is very chill about it. Course wasn't too hard, as long as you don't write papers like a 2nd grader, and read the articles she gives you'll be fine. Only homework were the four mandatory papers, daily journal, and reading. She's an interesting and laid back teacher that is easy to talk to.

Students will struggle with understanding the accent, but he really does try and puts in effort to help students understand material. Tests are just like the notes. Always relaxed on deadlines. Best chem professor at SIU.
The chemistry professor I would've asked for.
He is a good teacher technically, but he's practically impossible to get a word in from and moves on too quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's very good at explaining concepts. Don't blame the teacher because chemistry is a hard subject. His tests are exactly what's on his lecture slides. He references the book because the book does a good job of explaining things but I'm sure you can google the same concepts and get similar results. Extra credit is given but don't rely on it.

Oh Upul. To put it short, a group of 12 of us taught each other Chemistry. He was a great resource to bounce off of but if it wasn't for I clickers, most of us would have never gone to class. PPTs were put online (and often riddled with mistakes we would have to find). With Upul, when in doubt... ASK HIM. He is AMAZING that way! Get him to know you

I had Upul for 114 in Spring '15. Basically, he's a nice guy but I had a really hard time understanding his accent and soft voice. The tests he gave us were too long and hard to finish so he promised extra credit. Each time, he either didn't give extra credit or only gave a few points back. His methods of teaching are overly-complicated.

You really need to review the material several times before the exam. There are iClickers, which is the only motivation to go to class because he barely writes anything and posts his slides online. Not much learning goes on in the classroom, you are basically on your own.

People say that at UIC taking orgo will make you reconsider becoming a health care professional. This class had the same effect on me. If I could, I would give this guy zero in everything. He was disorganized, made mistakes, and lied to you about what was on the test. I got a C in the class and I am confident I could have done a better job teaching

I had trouble sleeping before exams because I knew how tragic it would be. Exams are a combination of concepts and calculator questions. Sapling is not to bad. He made mistakes on his power points, test, and quizzes. He would make mistakes on his study guide. The only bright side is that he will be nice with grading because everyone does terrible.
Is there for his students, if something's not clear he wants to know so he can clarify. Good guy.

Upul is disorganized in his Powerpoints, and I often look at them to clarify what he's saying. And he has a strong accent. It bothered me. But try to listen carefully. He hints on what will be on the exams. And the exams themselves expands on what he tells you in lecture. He does mean well, but I wouldn't take him because.. He seemed like a mess.
You can't understand him much.  Exam grading is pretty harsh, overall not the best professor.  Don't recommend unless you have to.

It takes a couple classes to get used to his accent. If you pay attention you'll understand what he is explaining. He posts review worksheets before quizzes and exams, which help a lot to understand what is going to be asked on the exam. Sometimes he pulls questions directly from lecture notes (which he posts) and worksheets for the exam.

Ill keep it short and sweet. Cons: Lectures  waste of time because they are straight from the book and he has iClicker questions all along with a thick accent. Pros: 1 on 1 he's a very good teacher will help you understand if you go to his office hours. Overall, read the book, ask for help, do problems, and get an A.

Thick accent, tough to understand. Lectures go on and on and make you want to cry because you feel dumb. Terrible grader. He will help if you go to office hours, but will laugh at your mistakes and make you  feel even more dumb. Made me hate Chemistry.
New Professor. Cant understand lectures. Willing to help.

At first it was hard to understand him, but you get used to him. He's a great professor, explains things very clear and simple as possible. He will answer any of your questions. I would recommend him.

Very nice professor. TA for class was also very nice. Professor goes out of his way to help students and makes excellent practice exams, which are very helpful. Great at explaining things. Very nice person and professor in general. Too bad he was only teaching temporarily in place of someone else. Class is curved.

He's a new professor so a little slack is needed, at first he was hard to understand and wasn't very clear. However as the semester went on he got better. Be careful the class seems to be very easy at first then gets much more difficult. Even though it hurts Show up to class, he gives hints for tests. Heavy curve beat the average and you get an A.

Professor ugo is one of the best professors. 

He is knowledgeable and explains stuff well during class and in oh, he has the best slides too his quote is "there's no stupid questions"

He is also a really caring, funny and nice person, however dont take his classes if you're a bum, you will fail the exams, its literally to write code on paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Good professor, really passionate about teaching, the lectures are good and you can learn a lot from him. I would say though that the course is too exam heavy, you have two exams worth 55 percent of your grade. I am not a fan of CS exams for programming courses, because you will never be in a position where you cant look up docuementation.

Didnt have a CS background so I struggled quite a bit with the course assignments. But the prof's lectures were really good and he takes a lot of time to make sure you understand. 5 quizzes, 4 projects and 1 HW. Fair warning getting an A requires effort since the course is also taken by students with workex.

Professor Buy covers Ruby for 5 weeks and C++ for 8 weeks. The lectures were interesting and went in-depth about oop, especially in C++. However, projects 1 and 3 were a bit too simple since they were introduction projects. However, I don't think they are needed at the 400 level and would've preferred projects more related to oop, also fair exams.
He seems to care a lot about his students and if we are actually learning! He is smart and seems to enjoy teaching!

CS 378 with Professor Buy was ok. The projects were fairly straightforward, although it would have been nice to have them be slightly more in-depth or increase the number of them so that the exams were worth less in the course. Professor Buy was also very active on Piazza which was quite useful. I would recommend.

I took CS 474 with Dr. Buy in fall 2022. He knows what he teaches and makes sure that every student understand the topic before going to next slide. The mantra of the class is "There is no stupid question". Many of student showed appreciation during the lectures and end of the semester on Piazza. 

RECOMMEND Dr. Buy.

I took 474 and 478 together, same prof and sem. If you can, do that. It is cool seeing the theory and the application side by side. 5 projects, 5 quizzes, 2 exams is everything you are graded on. Quizzes are based of slides, open note. Professor answers piazza questions thoroughly. Start project early, complex but simple to understand.

I took CS 540 under prof. Ugo Buy. Everyone has to present 2 research papers from a list of 25. The most annoying part was to frame 3 questions about every one of those papers before every class. You can't write a question that's already been answered in the paper. Also, you need to write 1 survey paper at the end that sums up everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: The Flutter class functions like the Android class. We had 4 projects and 7 open note quizzes. It was a pretty straightforward software dev class. He's also very laidback and his lectures are engaging. He answers every question in class and provides tons of sample code. Overall, no complaints.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Buy is one of the best professors I have come across at UIC. I have learnt a lot from his lectures. He is really passionate about what he teaches. The more questions you ask, the more you learn. The quizzes and projects are a bit tricky and you need to attend all his lectures to do well at them. Overall a great class!

He did a fantastic job communicating course details and would ask for input from the class and was accommodating. Course workload was not unnecessarily heavy like many other electives. You actually learn something because you have time to digest a topic. He put so much effort into making sure students at home and in person got the same experience.

I think professor Buy has adapted over time, as I see past reviews. Uses Ruby/C++ which covers good concepts w/ lectures/projects/quizzes. 1 Final. He is very knowledgeable and will help you till you understand anything if you ask. Projects aren't bad at all and easy to get an A if you put in decent work. Top 5 UIC CS profs. Also does curves now.

His Android course if very good. The projects could be a bit tough, but nothing undoable. Quizzes are open notes. The final exam was a bit hard. He explains things well and gives a lot of sample code.
There were some technical difficulties in the beginning of the semester but the course progressed well.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Absolutely terrible. Can't seem to ever get his machine working. Avoid this professor if at all possible.

Professor Buy made the Android class really enjoyable. He spent the lectures going over the material and went over the code for the apps. He posts all of the example apps on Blackboard and allows you to use whatever bits of code from there you might need. Projects were kind of tricky and took a while to figure out small details. Great Professor.

This course is for experienced programmers. Don't take this course if you are a beginner. Class is full of people with many years of experience (getting an A will be very difficult). Lectures are amazing, got to learn a lot. Projects are very time consuming

Course is tough, material might be outdated, but concepts don't outdate, and professor's main goal is not to teach how to program, but to teach concepts, which is excellent. Be ready to spend a lot of time on projects
Simple and clear course structure. Gives the best understanding of programming.

A relic of the past. Grads and Ugrads are graded together without a curve, so if you are an Ugrad, i would not recommend whatsoever. I think you are better off doing your own side projects to learn OO instead of going through this course. Learning smalltalk is a big hassle and has low benefits. You can learn exact same things in java, c++, c#, etc
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: A huge timesink if you're an undergrad. Would not recommend. Grading's pretty strict too so leave all hope behind. Honestly don't see why he's rated so high aside from his occasional meme personality.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Low quality class taught by a low quality professor. Reads off slides that were made in 2004. Like all professors, I am sure he is a good person, but that's nothing to brag - his teaching style is terrible. He uses smalltalk to each OOP instead of Java/C#; which is godawful and outdated (just like his slides!). No curve either. Say gg to your life.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Grades on a Straight line. He's a tough grader. DO not take his class if you're cs concepts aren't that strong. His projects are very time consuming. You would not have time to do anything else. You would not have time to study other subjects.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Amazing Professor who is very approachable. He has in-depth knowledge of android.

Prof Buy is world-class. My fav aspect is his proclivity to engage when the material gets hairy. Many professors tends to gloss over dense material and are relatively lazy in expounding important core/difficult parts. He can sense when the class needs this clarification, and uses his engaging personality to drill in and help.
Amazing professor. You will learn a lot and he is funny sometimes.
Amazing course!w
This is a solid foundational class, full of lectures. I learned a  lot about programming languages.

Best CS professor I have encountered thus far at UIC. He's a traditional lecturer, and doesn't waste time with this newfangled "peer instruction" nonsense that so many other professors have adopted. Lectures are clear and concise, exams are straightforward and reflect the material taught - no tricks or surprises. He also has a great sense of humor.

Took it first time this class was offered. 2 quizzes, 1 midterm, 1 final. Testsquizzes are usually about design patterns and writing small apps from scratch, coding questions usually 40-50% of the points make sure you can write an app in your sleep if you want to get 100 on your exams. Lectures based on powerpoint slides, can be boring sometimes.

Very detailed powerpoint notes. Good lecturer. Few homeworkprojects compared to other courses. Exams are relatively easy if you go over his powerpoint notes. Reading the chapters of books was over doing it, but helps you fully understand other concepts.

I loved taking this professor; in fact, I'm taking him again next semester. Great, organized ppt lectures. Encourages people to ask questions and explains it till everyone gets it. I wish more professors were like him!
If you are not a CS student, skip this class. Never take this course if you are a not a CS student!

Professor Buy is the best teacher I have had yet at UIC. He definitely knows his OO and won't hold back from teaching in a strictly academic fashion. For 474, my advice is to study the slides with some regularity. Cramming before midterms and finals is only so effective... Also, when learning Smalltalk, start early and really apply yourself!
Hands down one of UIC's best professors. Cares about his students, workload is not too heavy, extremely knowledgeable. Drop whatever course conflicts with his.
Awesome professor.
You can't avoid paying attention. His class is so engaging.

He does use powerpoint slides but uses the white board 75% of the time to explain them. He covers smalltalk & C++ mostly but mainly focuses on Object-Oriented concepts. Can be boring some times but I've seen worst. He does hint as to what might be on quizzes/exams so going to class helps. Projects aren't that bad, just time consuming. Getting an A.

Boring power point slides. Exam questions are not covered in class. Projects are confusing, he says something then after you have done it he changes things around. Comes to class unprepared all the time. Doesn't know how to use blackboard.
Taught well and made jokes during the class. He'll explain something if you are confused. Followed ppt slides for the most part so just bring them to class and make notes on them when needed.
Tests are hard and on topics he does not cover or covers very quickly.  Projects are difficult and ambiguous.  Never has time for his students.  Always seems to busy to help.

He is a good guy overall. I think in some ways he is too smart to be able to translate the material in a digestible way, but if you ask him more specific questions he can get you to comprehend it all. If you show up and ask questions then you will be fine.

The content of the class is more difficult than the professor. He is malleable to a students questions and needs, the material without real work or application outside of class is what makes it difficult. YOU WILL UNDERSTAND IF YOU COMMUNICATE. Otherwise, you're gonna be hella confused. Also, read the textbook.

Professor was energetic and can be awkward at times, but he's human. Lectures can be a bit heavy if you aren't keeping up with the syllabus/texts so missing a class can be hard to catch up. Good at communicating office hours and is flexible, overall a good professor.

Class was complicated. If you miss one or two classes, you will NOT catch up. For a Gen ED, this was the worst and most difficult for no reason. Gets too complicated. Try to get any other class for a Gen ED.

Really enjoyed his class. He's very understanding that sometimes things happen and you need more time to work on an assignment. His lectures were great because he makes an effort to try to explain the material clearly. He's also a bit funny and though he can be a bit awkward at times, I found it to be endearing. Highly recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Hard to Understand, Late to class, No slides, Short explanations

Mr. Metlushko clearly cares about the subject in a way that the majority of the class didn't, but perhaps due to the consequence of 8 am classes, his lectures were prone to making me sleepy. However, he presents the topics in a clear way and it is generally easy to follow him if you manage to stay awake, and he really does want the class to succeed

Vitali is a great professor but he is definitely more suited for the higher level ECE classes, his lectures and notes were detailed but overall the lectures were pretty uninteresting. His notes allowed for the class to be very easy, even without attending. The TAs did not do much to help during the labs and all the prelabs were by other professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Amazing person, not so great teacher. For 115 it is very difficult to follow him. His voice sounds like a lullaby & his handwriting may be difficult to read, and u probably will need to self study. However hes a great person and has amazing motivational speeches when things get tough. He just cant teach an entry level course because he's too smart.

He is an amazing professor.If I have to place him in my top 3 professors at uic ,I'll put him first place tied with professor Vahe . His lecturing style is not for everyone but if you have taken ECE 346 with professor McGinn you will be good with this class .He gives lots of extra credits , hw's are easy, exam questions are straight from lecture.
Very partial at times and not good at explaining things. Does not go into detail on how are things suppose to work.
i personally found him very entertaining

He awards bonus points on the midterm for just trying to answer his questions during the lectures. His labs are challenging, but you will learn a lot from them. In the end, he has everyone do a research project which is an incredible benefit.

The professor mumbles a lot which makes it difficult to take notes, not to mention he speeds through the slides. The class is not difficult but knowing what to learn is the problem because the homeworks provided do not cover all the material. Study hard for exams or you will pay dearly. additionally, he does not grade exams by method but by answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: In the ECE Department at UIC, Professor Vitali Metlushko has been difficult to learn from due to his "Teaching Style" I can tell you that there are more difficult Courses than ECE 340. Still, the difference is "teaching Style" if you are good with memorization, this class will be easy because, more than that, you will not learn.

The material/exams are easier than 340 (since you know how he make exams) but the labs are longer. Since the equipment at UIC like transistor or chips work 50% of the time, labs take longer and you might not finish. I highly recommend recording lab and getting as much points as you can. It will really help for exams.

Those who gave him a good rating is fake news. By far the worst professor in terms of teaching. Rambles and reads from the slides with no environment for note taking. Also gave an unfair amount of "extra credit points" to those who participates, while the rest of the class has to work for their grade. Nice guy otherwise. But I would avoid him.

This semester he would speed through slide. Only one example per topic (shows the answer and points at it, doesn't write it down from beginning) and the midterm cover way to much material. He give two exams, midterm and final. He gives points to people who participate or pretty much the 10 smart people in class and its pretty unfair. Labs were bad

There were three tests and a final. The final was technically worth 50% of your overall grade although I'm pretty sure he will give you an A in the class if you get an A on the final. Don't get bogged down in the details, just focus on understanding the concepts, and you should be fine. The labs are dreadful though. The class is really 340 round 2.

One of my favorite professors at UIC! If you go to his lectures and put effort into homework assignments, the tests are more straightforward. He is really accessible outside of class, and is very engaging during lectures. Would definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I am a CE student, and not that much interested in electronics. I was not spending enough time for this class, but I'm sure if I did I could have received an easy A. If you follow his lectures you can learn, but I was never excited to go in his lectures since they were power points. The labs are outdated, the tests are random uneven choice.
Great professor, knows what he is talking about. Gives extra credit in class like no tomorrow for exams for just answering questions. But a hard grader on exams. Can be 5% off for small things

He is really passionate about what he teaches and cares a lot about us succeeding. For me, I did have to put effort into paying attention in lecture because I didn't understand anything otherwise. But once I did, it made me enjoy the class so much more because Metlushko is such a great professor and he goes over concepts several times.
Prof. Vitali is the bast, his lecture is amazing,do not miss his class.
Smart professor, cares about his students and their up-to-dateness with the Electrical Engineering industry. Structures the class in a way for you to do well.

what an eminent professor @uic! This professor is VERY passionate and cognizant of what he teaches. I encourage you to attend his lectures, he will beat the information into you head each lecture! the best way to understand his lectures is to participate, you'll learn a lot and he will appreciate your participation!

He definitely cares about students succeeding and encourages reading beyond the scope of the course.  Lectures leave a little something to be desired as he can jump around and moves along fast.  Very lenient in grading.  Come to class and do the homework and you'll do fine.

Hands down the best professor in the ECE department. His passion for existing and upcoming technology drives the entire class. He takes tough topics and breaks them down to simple concepts to help students understand better.

One of the best  professors at UIC!  He has a great personality and encourages his students to do well and makes it fun to participate in class. Don't be discouraged if in the beginning it seems that he moves fast through the material, he reviews the material numerous times to prepare you for the exams.

Professor Metlushko cares about his students.  He truly wants you do well.  He gets the big picture across, and tells you the details he wants you to learn. Just study what he suggests that you study, and you can easily get an A!

Nice, genuine guy. Really cares for students not just in the classroom, but also in their real-world endeavors. Material is very straightforward, and exams are based on material he goes over in class. 4-5 tests, but most of the class is weighted on the final exam. OVerall, would highly recommend taking a course with him.

Great professor. Obvious that he cares about his students learning the most important and APPLICABLE parts of the material. Work-load outside of the exams are minimal. He is one of the best professors I've had.
Unmistakably the best professor ever! His experience in the fabrication facility, his knowledge, and his teaching technique make him the best of the best! I would take ANY ece course with him!

Best professor ever! Clear and straightforward lectures! He is always going to be there to help you! He just wants you to succeed and guarantee yourself a good future! He also discusses job opportunities and gives us advice in class

One of the best professors at UIC if not THE BEST! He is always there for you and wants his students to pass with flying colors! His lectures are super clear! He also cares for his students' well being in the future! He always gives us advice about our future jobs! Will definitely recommend him for ANY course!!
Very helpful, clear, on point.

This GUY is a legend, Best professor at UIC by far, he teaches clearly and is super respectful for your needs. If something bad happens he will really show concern for you. Really inspires people to learn. AMAZING PROFESSOR
Professor Metlushko is an outstanding professor. He is clear and concise and makes learning enjoyable. He knows his stuff!

This man knows his stuff! He's my favorite professor at UIC and sadly I only took 342 with him. His lectures are thorough and he moves through material quickly.  He posts all his lectures on blackboard, so keep them safe!  You will come out of this class learning more than any other course.  He's always in good spirits and makes lectures enjoyable.

Great guy. Very nice. Very animated. Plus he's got a huge mustache.   Lectures moves at a super fast pace, but that's kinda good because he only expects you to know the general idea of the topics, not the specifics.  5 exams and 1 final. Exams are 5 questions, short-response.

One of the easiest professors in the entire department. You can get an A in the class without really doing any work. However, he is also good at explaining and you can definitely understand his stuff if you chose to.
show him you want to succeed and you'll get an A. Exams based exactly on homework.
Love him! he's the nicest professor in entire ECE department, and his lectures are funny and educational!
:] I love him!

I was put off by him at first when he left class to go for a conference for two weeks.  But he is the funnest and coolest professor you will ever have.  Not so much focused on mathematics as concepts.  He goes at a fast pace but he really drills it into you and you will know what to expect on his tests.  His notes are excellent, keep them for life.
Take this prof. you won't regret it!!! You will see after taking his tests!

Had a great time in his class. While there is a lot of HW and it requires a lot of self-discipline and studying, it is worth it as you will actually learn and be able to explain the concepts. In addition, he provides students with more than enough support through study sessions, videos, and practice exam questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Yes he makes u teach urself but there is plenty of videos that prepare you. exams are hard , but dude they are literally a copy of the C3s. if u can do C3s in class u can score A on exam. nothing to complain about if u dont understand something, plenty of practice problems and videos explaining like i said.  didnt seem like a weedout class to me.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If I wanted to teach myself, I'd take an online course. He expects you to master the chapter before class and runs quizzes in EVERY CLASS like a CPA exam. Most time is spent talking about WSJ articles, with little teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Take. Another. Professor. He does the “flipped classroom” thing, so he gets paid for you teaching yourself everything, yup YOU are responsible for teaching yourself everything before class. Partner quizzes every day. Insane expectations for students and an ineffective professor. Also ends late every day, so you're late for your next class.

Most organized and charismatic professor I've ever had. Learn the material before you go to class, as it's not a lecture.There are plenty of practice problems and videos of him going through them on blackboard and extra study sessions. He really cares about his students learning the material, you just have to put in the effort.

Professor Raval's teaching method is a bit unconventional, where you have to learn the material before coming to class, but he does a good job of explaining everything during class. There are Content checks every class, and as long as you do the homework, the course will be a breeze.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class has lots of homework and can get overwhelming with some taking hours. There are quizzes each class, however it's worth a small part of your grade. Exams are built around the worksheets posted alongside the quizzes and are pretty much a framework of what to expect, so there's no surprises. If you put in the work, you will get a good grade.

Literally got me traumatized! Easier to change major or even college. Quiz every class without actually teaching, blaming it on you for not putting in enough effort and time (ignoring some homework takes more than 5 hours to finish (and still not 100%), which he assigns due before every class).

Poor structure and unrealistic demands. Lectures didn't match the textbook. Quizzes every class session, confusing explanations, errors during lectures made learning stressful. He is a polite and nice person, his 'sink or swim' approach and emphasis on 'hard work' over effective teaching methods made class unsupportive and discouraging.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is professional, polite and knowledgeable. I have learned a lot with him, especially critical thinking. Take him if you would want to improve critical and analytical thinking. I enjoyed his last lecture at the end of the semester!
In-class assignments and over complicated teaching

I heard this course will be heavily curved at the end. If multiple students end up with failing grades, but end up being saved by the curve, then why not just teach better and not use a curve to make up for it? The material is not impossible to learn, but the teaching method is ineffective.

He doesn't explain anything in class, he just posts videos where he solves a couple of problems without explaining what he's doing. And he overcomplicate problems that aren't even hard. There's quiz every class which is nothing like the problems in the videos. He's a nice person, but I don't think he can teach. I'd never take his class again.

Class is difficult; will make you reconsider majoring in accounting if you have not been serious. Most of your learning will be at home, and you will be expected to know the content in class because of frequent graded assessments. Teaches by asking students for answers to a question, and working through them - can be all over the place sometimes.

If you like to teach yourself, then this is the perfect class for you.
Horrible teaching. Covers one simple problem, then gives a tough quiz. Explanations make no sense, handwriting is illegible, and excessive abbreviations make it worse, even after complaints. Spends most of class off-topic then solves problems in the most confusing way possible.

The instructor unnecessarily complicates the course, making it more challenging than it should be. I would recommend waiting to take the class with a different faculty member. The preparation and learning process feels more difficult due to excessive complexity and confusion. Additionally, the course requires a mandatory, expensive book for Connect
Professor Raval is great! It's definitely a tough class, but if you put in the work, it's not bad. Be ready for quizzes every class though lol.

Professor Raval is one of the few professors i've had in my college life that actually cares that you take the knowledge with you. This is your career and he does a great job emphasizing that. He also does all he can to make the lecture interesting, you have to realize that this class is very hard in itself, Raval will help you get through it.

best prof for ACTG 315!! class is challenging but he doesn't have a traditional teaching style where you listen to lectures but quizzes in every class which helps you learn a lot and is concerned for the success of his students knows each one of them and makes his class pretty engaging and entertaining

Overall, he is a solid professor. He is test heavy (1st exam 18%, 2nd exam 25%, 3rd exam 30%) There is a quiz each class session (usually in groups). His lectures don't teach the material, but rather explain the past homework assignments and whats going on in the "accounting world". It is a difficult class but he made it bearable.
Dr. Raval is amazing. He explains in detail and understandable manner. Ask him questions, he will answer them nicely

Professor Raval was a fantastic professor. This class, in a way, determines if you will be pursuing Accounting for your degree due to its high difficulty. However, Raval made learning easy through lecture videos on his extra handouts. There were quizzes every class day to test your recent homework knowledge, so review because you will be challenged
Awesome Sauce

Mr.Raval is great dude overall- I wish his strutuce was better. If you're a employed student and require time to understand the material, THIS will be a challenge. I don't think his teaching style is effective for all students. You'll need to juggle between tons of homework then study for quiz for each session. You learn more at home than in class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I took him last fall but after another semester of classes I realize how much better he was at teaching than the other professors I have taken. The class is very tough but as long as you do the work and study and try hard on the quizzes you will do fine. He is a very kind and helpful professor and tries hard to help you if you just ask.

Hands down my favorite professor EVER. The guy is a blast. Never a dull moment in class. You study the material before class. Every class, there is a 15min quiz. as soon as you turn in the quiz, he goes over the problems in class. This method literally FORCED everyone in his class to actually learn the concepts. NOT easy, but worth it!!

Literally one the best professors I've ever had. This is a hybrid class where you do most of the learning outside of class simply because there is too much to cover in class. Sometimes the videos are long and the work is tedious, but if you actually follow along, you will get a B or higher, easily.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Raval is amazing! The class is very straightforward, easy to follow, and its easy to get a good grade if you study the material provided. Hes a great professor, very respectful and kind to students. This was one of the best classes ive taken at UIC. People say his exams are super tough but theyre rly not. Just study and youll do good.

I took professor Raval for this class and turned out to be the best class I ever took. He is very helpful. Just follow his videos and do the handouts and homework before every class you will be fine. This class is hard like real hard but he made it fun and try to explain real world stuff, quiz every class and exams are heavy but follow the notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: First thing is that you must know ACTG 315 is NOT an easy class. But see, all depends on how the teach does the work. This teach KNOWS how to do it. Raval will not only motivate you but you also see the results if you follow his words. He is a good teacher. He will make you love accounting ! Be cause of Raval i can tell you a lot about lifo liquid
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Raval is a nice guy, he seems to care about students. However, his teaching style is NOT effective. Quizzes every class, they're ok if you practice handouts. The exams are absolutely ridiculous, he makes them almost impossible. Everyone fails, 30-40% range. He curves, but it sucks to see those scores. Penalty for wrong answers, not even the CPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I loved this class. As an Accounting major, it is important to really learn the material and be prepared to future classes. I think Raval's class is perfect for that. This class was the most difficult class I've ever taken, but it is intended to be difficult. If you can do well in this class, you can do well in any ACTG class. Quizzes every class!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Raval is an kind and optimistic person who is open to any criticism. During class, we would do a lot of practice problems to help solidify our understanding of the material. I would say his tests are difficult but he will offer a curve. This class is meant to be very difficult so be prepared to practice the problems until you understand.

Dr. Raval was truly an incredible professor. It was not an easy class at all, but it definitely will prepare you for future accounting classes and, ultimately, the CPA exam. This class requires lots of studying, and I highly recommend studying in groups.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He's a cool guy, I liked his class. The material is very challenging so be sure to keep up with the readings and online hw assignments. The exam questions are a lot more difficult than the in-class handouts/hw. I highly recommend him tho.

Very fair in Professor. Even though hes young, hes probably one of the best teacher out there. Made an extremely hard class bareable. You can tell he cares about his students. I would take his class anytime, as he seem like an experience person in life and in class. Show up in class and you will do well in the exams and he curves big time!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Probably the hardest class you will ever have to take and Raval makes it even harder to pass. Quizzes every class that he doesn't go over before can be annoying and the tests are massive and he doesn't give partial credit. There is a HUGE curve on everything but shouldn't you actually know that stuff? His teaching style is not effective at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He spends a bit at the beginning of class talking about real life topics related to the material. I personally enjoyed the class even though it is very tough yet he is nice. The exams are tough but he doesn't utilize time well teaching material. Just wish he did more problems. Quizzes every class are annoying but class has a massive curve.
He is ok teacher, trying to amuse you when you feel miserable. Class is hard as any accounting class. He is a good teacher.

Love this professor! He made a really difficult class seem possible. He was very helpful and always willing to go over more complicated subjects during his office hours. There were pop quizzes almost every class, but they were helpful when studying for the tests.  He definitely cares about his students and wants them to succeed!
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Hes was great teacher but good luck on tests as it is written response and impossible to complete on time, the material is hard as hell and in-depth
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Best professor I have ever had, cares about teaching his students, his class is difficult but he makes you care for it. I would always retake this professor if I could.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: One of THE BEST Professors I've ever taken. Every question is a good question in his eyes, his lectures are interactive, informative, and I can say I learned a great deal from this class. He has taken an intimidating course and made it a challenging, thought-provoking and rewarding experience. So thankful I had him for 315.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: THE MOST PROFESSOR U CAN EVER HAVE IN UIC. Though 315 is challenging, he really cares about students. He will for sure provide any help if you need. Really chill and laid back. LOVE him! Highly recommend!

Great professor! Challenging class, online HW assignments are long but you can check if correct as you go (really cool), great lectures, he gives handouts to freely work on (with answers posted online) and gives many pop quizzes (not hard) and EVERYTHING is curved. Would definitely recommend for 315, or any class for that matter.
Didn't show up to class once except for projects do your work and assignments and do good in presentations and this class is an easy A

For MCS 472, not really teaching anything. The concepts of this class are usefull but boring teaching, bad grading. Just reading off slides, grades mainly came from projects. Not really recommending this professor.

Very willing to allow you to learn for yourself and look into different topics for your presentations and will always answer your questions with enthusiasm. Always allows for the Final presentation to take the grade of your Final exam and cares more about you learning something you're interested in than sticking strictly to the coursework.

Class is pretty interesting, but not a lot of people take it (~4 people this semester). Professor was very accommodating, and pushed deadlines when we needed it. All his lectures are posted on YT, but i still showed most of the time so I could ask questions right then and there. Definitely not a harsh grader, just ask questions and you'll be solid

Doesn't actually teach and thus gives no actual new insight into the topics covered in class. Only regurgitates old content. Expects the student to teach themselves based on old content. Avoid this professor. Your time is best spent learning from a better teacher that actually does their job.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He does not provide 100% on any project, even if you do it correctly. Supposedly, there is always "a better way." 50% of his exams have absolutely nothing to do with Data Structures. Expect to memorize previous exams. The questions will not be the same but you may get half points for writing giberish. He will only give a handful of A's overall.
One of the more caring and easily accessible teachers I've had thus far and goes out of his way to make accommodations for people where necessary.

I can only explain Jan as a powerPoint presenter. Dont expect examples on a white erase board because you won't get any to follow along to with the slides unlike any of my other professors prior to CS401. Things to expect: 1. Overly saturated slides 2. Boring lectures with little enthusiasm 3. Explain every single little micro detail on homework

One of the best professors at UIC. If you enjoy Math and Programming this is an amazing and challenging class. The entire class is very interesting and there is a lot to learn from this professor. It's worth showing up to class. The projects are quite difficult, but he is always willing to help with lots of office hours offered.

This was a fantastic class. The professor is very challenging and he really pushes the limits as to what you can learn (which is a lot!). The exams are quite hard as well as the quizzes, the projects are very useful, and the lectures introduce many new ways of thinking. He is generous with extra credit, and he seems to curve at the end.
Exams are not open book and the lectures were confusing. Offers extra credit through homework but its difficult. Tough grader for projects as well.

A great professor indeed.  He makes sure everyone understands the material before proceeding. Quizzes are hard, but points can be made up by doing optional homework assignments.  Exams are open book.  Nothing bad can be said about this professor.
A genuine professor. Creates a distinguished example of how classes should run.
He is a very good professor. Very smart and knows his stuff. Tests are open book. He is very fair with grades and programs. Nothing is rushed. He definitely knows how to run a class.
I did not mind his lectures, and the content itself was interesting to me. However, the quizzes were graded strict and there were not many assignments.

Makes a 100level class more difficult than it needs to be. For the first weeks of class he just rambled on about nothing and then gave a quiz on what he 'taught' that day. There isn't any way to prepare for the quizzes so TAs have to explain what will be on it 10 minutes before we take it. Be prepared for a lot of stress with assignments and grades

Very nice and genuinely passionate professor. His homework has a very heavy weightage over your grade but they aren't too harsh on the grading. The quizzes aren't hard but sometimes feel like you don't know what to answer. Feedback was good. ALWAYS MAKE SURE YOU EMAIL if you feel stuck on HW.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Was extremely stressed almost always while taking this class. Homework assignments are harder than the classes teaches you to handle, quizzes are difficult to study for or understand the concepts of, and grading is harsh. The entire class after about a third of the way through just became so impossible to follow.

I took Dr. Wang for 3 of my classes, BME 339, BME 333 and BME 205. He is a great professor, understanding and helpful. His classes are not that hard if you pay attention and do good on the HWs. He does random attendance but is pretty flexible with it. I would take more classes with him if that was an option.

I can see he is passionate, but at the 100 level, he just isn't considerate or helpful. The material explained in class was always significantly different and more difficult on the homework assignments and quizzes. If you struggle, you get no consideration or second chances. When I asked for help, I felt judged and embarrassed most of the time.

He's understanding when it comes to circumstances that could happen with students' lives, he provides extensions whenever needed and even offers review sessions that are the most helpful study materials for exams. With regards to lectures, it can be disorganized and feels like an info-dump, so retention of the topics is really hard to study for.

Dr. Wang is a great professor. He gives great feedback and focuses on content that will be on the exams. His accent might be hard to understand at times but he truly understands the different concepts and conveys it well.

I think He's a great professor. Yes, his lectures are heavy, but they have a lot of examples in them that would help you understand the topics. The homework is long but if you can do the homework successfully, you can pass the midterm and final exams with flying colors
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great Professor. Lectures are light but can get overwhelming so you must do some studying afterwards. Easy grading and partial credit. Do you work/participate and attend classes and you will be fine.
Content aside, I think this professor shows a great deal of professionalism, He understands students have obligations outside of school and teaches the course very well.

I had to take this guy for 2 different courses. You might not get a good grade from taking this guy, but at least you won't learn anything from him either. Disorganized. Poorly communicates ideas and topics. Unclear on terminology, nomenclature, variables, and vocabulary. The class itself is not terribly hard, but this guy is a terrible lectuer.
His teaching style is very lecture heavy and just missing 1 lecture could leave you confused. I found him very reasonable and understanding. He likes to assign group projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Highly recommended. He gives a lot of homework and the exam grades can be intimidating, but there is likely a curve (would've gotten a B instead). Be ready to. do homework because it is 70% of the grade. Ready to help out on piazza but would not give the answer straight up, he would give you examples and reference to figure out.

This professor is horrible at teaching students, he is going to be your BioE 205, BioE 339, and BioE 431 professor. So be ready and adapt to his teaching style, it's unclear and horribly organized. Read the book! Expect very little to none accommodation for extensions. There is a heavy accent that also makes it harder to understand. Good luck
Its a hard class, and he makes even more miserable. Make sure you do as many as problems before exams. The HW are group based so make sure you contribute.

reviews.comment: I have no idea how this guy can be a professor! I hope you will not deal with him, but if you have to, I would take advantage of the lecture examples.
He is a good person but not professor. He seems to be knowledgeable but he doesn't know how to teach! The tests aren't bad but the HW are crazy hard.

reviews.comment: He's absolutely a harsh grader. The HW are non sense. He teaches like you are all in grad school. Avoid him at all cost if possible, if not, good luck!
It's a hard class in general. Do as much as problems as you can. Pay attention to the professor during the lectures. HW worth 50% of the final grade. So make sure you do them on time and correctly.
