reviews.comment: Textbook example of a professor who truly wants his students to succeed. He provides plenty of resources for students to explore the subject in homework and optional readings, and exams only test the minimum of what you're expected to know. Caring and understanding, but not in a lazy "give everyone an A" type of way. Lectures are meh but it's okay.

I have to give this man credit, he's not the greatest teacher, but he is so understanding and actually cares about his students. His teaching isn't the best and his powerpoints are hardly understandable, but the homework is worth 50%, so just work with your friends, put in a bit of effort, and you'll learn the material and get an A. For 205 and 339

Such a nice and caring professor. Super accessible outside of class, and answers emails promptly. Truly cares for his students' success and is very understanding. Not the best lecturer, but gives clear guidelines as to what to expect on exams. Do the homework and a B is pretty manageable.
Final can feel overwhelming. A majority of the course feels like smooth sailing until it is time to start working on the final
Exams are easy and open notes. There are three group presentations and most assignments are done with your group.

BORING lecture and likes to talk about himself or ppl he knows, 4 presentations the last one is 20-25 min. his grading is unfair. Exams, notes allowed.IMO the grading on the presentations are unfair

reviews.comment: Overall lecture is boring/long and covers very basic material, his group projects are the worst because at the end, you will need to do a 20 minute presentation as long as a 20-25 page paper on a company,
He just was not an interesting professor. The speeches were crammed and they were long. They weren't hard but it was just a long 16 weeks.

Run. The lectures in the beginning of the semester will put you to sleep. Class feels long. There is a group project consisting of 3 presentations and a 20 page paper. He is a tough grader when presenting and it gets annoying that half of the time he can't explain his thoughts. He is also not familiar with business concepts.

I wouldn't say that he's the worst professor I ever had, but definitely not the greatest, has a little bit of a god complex, but just ignore it. He doesn't really let you know that a quiz is due soon and he's not going to help you out or give you the benefit of a doubt if you miss a quiz. So make sure you are on top of it. There's a lot of homework

reviews.comment: This class was not good

reviews.comment: To start with, he isn't even in the business field. He stated he was learning with us as we go as well...I understand that but a teacher should have prior knowledge on a topic before teaching it. His faces while we presented really put the cherry on top, idk if he knows that his thoughts are conveyed on his face but let me tell you it was scary.

He had no idea what he was doing. Whenever he received feedback from students he would shut them down and belittle them while also being smug, and displaying narcissistic traits. He very rarely gives clear grading criteria. He didn't provide rubrics for class and constantly went off on tangents that had nothing to do with the material. Do not take.

There is a lot of work for a 100 class. This is also a speech class so if you dont like speaking in front of people dont take this class. There is online homework that you have to do every week as well as do research for your speeches. Overall he was a cool professor and very helpful for brainstorming the speeches.

I took his class for professional writing... He's bad at explaining what he wants/ what he's looking for when grading. My groupmates and I all have anxiety about our papers, wondering if the smallest things are incorrect. There's no rubric for assignments, just examples you follow. And even if you follow the example, he'll find something wrong
For a class that was level 100, he expected way too much. He gave us a lot of homework. I was drowning in all the work this class required.

While his lectures are clear, his grading is not. No explanations are given for why points are taken off in certain places. He makes faces at his students while they are presenting, which I find to be disrespectful. Would not take a course with him again.

Has high standards for presentations that I dont think even he lives up to. Demeanor is rude & blunt - especially in verbal feedback. Scowls at students presenting. Not sure if he is aware of this. The instructions are often overly convuluted and contradictory.

Grading is fair and the material is manageable. Take someone else if possible

Prof. S was a great professor. He is always ready to help with work outside of class and gives great suggestions. Deadlines are an important factor in the class as staying on top of your work and submitting it on time is important. He is an easy grader and very helpful. He uniquely explains ideas and concepts as well. Overall, great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Does not really help when you ask questions, and has no lack on the schedule.

Good professor. Readings were very long. Speech assignments get increasingly difficult but nothing that can't be managed. Outlines were a pain to do; they had to be in a specific format or else no credit for it. 
Around 1 HW assignment/week + 1 speech/month. Office hours were very useful.

reviews.comment: I personally love having bill as my professor, as he has always been extremely fair and interesting to me. Within every assignment he gives clear ways to improve as a student, simply asking for help and attending office hours guarantees immediate improvement in his class. He is a very personable man and someone that I admire and respect immensely

While he was a good professor for the lectures, he had incredibly high expectations for this to be a 100 level class. He was a bit too strict with outlines and although I felt that his feedback was somewhat useful, I found that if he clarified a bit more what he wanted to say he would've been a better instructor. I would not take this course again.

Mr. Schraufnagel's course schedule is very easy to follow. He is very easily accessible, may it be after class, over email, or in a one-on-one session. reviews.comment: He is a really nice professor, and his class is kinda easy as long as you did everything you should get a good grade in his class. All the work that you have to do are list on the syllabus so it's pretty easy to follow all the work.

reviews.comment: Amazingly chill professor, Professor Schraufnagel is a very intelligent person and very reasonable. Make sure you try to meet all criteria in the rubrics for each assignment and he will make sure you get a good grade when grading your speech work.

reviews.comment: His personality is somewhat bland, and he overall does not make the course necessarily memorable. The course was pretty easy but the grading and the deadlines for assignments were very confusing. On top of this, this assignment has a significant amount of work but still pretty manageable.
Just take it with mohr. That's all.
I highly recommend you take organic chemistry at another school. Save yourself. Don't have hope like I did.

The material you are expected to use for help on the exams dont match what is actually on the exams. Her lecture notes aren't clear or helpful although they are thorough but you WILL get lost in the material. Use other professors material if you want to pass.

yermolina is an actual good prof, she is intimidating and will be blunt with you but you get used to it. she helps immensely during office hours and is honestly a pretty funny prof. she cares abt her students and knows this material is not easy at all.
she literally scares me. but like aside from that she zooms through the lecs like theres no tmr. "this is a fast paced class" how is that my problem like plan better idc

Emailed her multiple times, never responded. Acts like we've known the subject our entire lives like her. Shows the bare minimum during lectures then makes exams hard. She literally uses AI to write her emails. Definitely don't take unless you have the time to eat, sleep, breathe the subject and live in her office.

Emailed her multiple times, never responded. Acts like we've known the subject our entire lives like her. Shows the bare minimum during lectures then makes exams hard. She literally uses AI to write her emails. Wish I never took the course with her.

I took Ochem 1 and 2, and from ochem 1, Mohr is the better professor. Yermolina goes too quickly through lectures, The class heavily relies on outside source material, and to pass relies on having relatively high test/quiz scores. The averages for exams are low, which is professors fault. Practice sets don't have all reactions, also quite demeaning

Prof. Yermolina is def sassy and has a wonderful attitude, but organic chemistry is genuinely a difficult course and her lectures while would be a little difficult to follow were very concise and helpful. If you email her about any questions or go to her office hours she's a very sweet person and will not let you leave until you understand.

She does not teach so get ready to teach yourself. Can barely keep up with notes because you can never read them and by the time you can she's already moved on. She teaches lectures as if you already know the information and treats it as a review. Berates students randomly during class for no reason.

350 words isn't enough to describe Professor Yermolina. One of the most kind, funny, caring professors you'll ever have if you actually put 5% effort. All the bad comments about her are people who are a bit too sensitive. I look forward to seeing her everyday and she makes uic more enjoyable. She really cares about her students if u show effort.
Great professor, If you put in the work you'll do fine. Many people find her difficult but I dont think there is an easy way to teach organic chemistry.

Professor Yermolina, is one of the better organic chemistry and chemistry professors here at UIC. She's very accessible during office hours and is willing to help you understand the context, but she will be harsh when she gives you feedback so prepare for that. Please go to office hours and do the problem sets because they will be on the exam!!!

You will have to watch online lectures and come to class to do iclickers the whole time. If you are someone who cannot succeed with this format take this class literally anywhere else. This professor is only kind if you are already succeeding, if you are someone who struggles in chemistry prepare to have a horrible time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Yermolina is one of the kindest professors you'll meet at UIC. It may take some time to adjust to her, as she can seem strict at first. However, once you get to know her and she gets to know you, you'll realize that she's a truly caring teacher who genuinely cares about your well-being. I highly recommend attending her office hours!

Bad professor. We had online review sessions and she would have an irritated tone answering students questions. She also teaches as if we are supposed to know everything that she's talking about. She explains things, but it's unfair to have an attitude if a student doesn't understand something fully and proceeds with more questions.

As a student who took 232, 233, and 234 with Dr. Yermolina, she was hands-down my favorite professor at UIC. While it may take some time to adjust to her teaching style, she demonstrated genuine care for the wellbeing and success of students who took the time to embrace the material. Her interest in organic chemistry helped foster my own interest.
She is very accessible when you need help and makes sure you understand the concepts thoroughly. The class is definitely tough, but she wants you to do well.

Took her for both lecture and lab, hated her in both. Absolutely useless slides, rude, there is a reason both the lecture and lab receive big curves. It is truly a shame that a university such as UIC can hire such horrific professors for their chemistry department.

Very rude and unprofessional. She makes snarky and insensitive comments to students. Guilty of malpractice in labs (misuse of fume hoods, carcinogens, no lab coats). We have to learn everything ourselves in Chem 233. Her slides have incorrect mechanisms & her syllabus is a mess. All of her classes require 10+% curving b/c everyone fails. HORRIBLE!

Very disorganized and a rude person. I recommend going to TA office hours, because she is an awful lecturer and person. Class was disorganized, unstructured and we didn't know our grade for the whole semester until the final grade. She also lost people's finals and failed them. Couldn't pay me to take her class ever again.

Professor Yermolina is the best and most memorable professor I've had in a long time. Even though it was extremely packed 8 weeks of chemistry, she made the workload bearable, and I would 100% take her again if I needed to take more chemistry.

Dr. Y can come off a little tough, fair enough, but these are high expectations that she holds for every student. Office hours help a lot and she's explains things clearly. Orgo lab had LOTS of work, exams were VERY specific. The class is a LOT, seriously! Don't hesitate to visit her. She cares and wants you to succeed. She IS orgo chem! 10/10 💅🏾

Thank god my labs were high and I had a good TA, awful exams, she purposely makes your makeup exams harder bc its more "work" for her(she said this in class btw). Rude professor and enjoys humiliating people, extremely unapproachable. my friend got yelled by her during a 1:1 office hour for asking a couple questions lol. she also thinks she's funny

If you want to enjoy her class and get on her good side, you have to go to her office hours and suck up a bit—she favors the students who do. A lot of my classmates and I thought she was just plain rude. She can be unprofessional in 1:1 settings and gets openly hostile if you ask her questions. Very low class average and massive curve

233 is a lot of work as you really have to understand everything you do in lab. The pre-lab quizzes are very pedantic and the exams are very difficult as "none of the above" is commonly the answer to MC questions. However, the practical's pretty straightforward if you prepare well. She can also be quite condescending if you ask her questions.

Yea so the person that said the people who complain lack discipline and accountability is completely wrong. Yes there's good things, but the attitude of the professor is the main thing. Be aware with your grade too because you still have to perform decent on the exams to pass. She can be pretty rude and condescending.

Orgo Lab was not easy. You had to put in time each week to conceptually understand everything you'd be focusing on in your experiments. My advice would be to invest a lot of time in doing well on your reports, the midterm, and the practical, because the final exam will bring you down. The final is very poor and people do awful on it.

Most negative recent reviews you'll encounter here are from students who lack discipline and accountability. There is so much filler work, it's ridiculous. You can bomb every test and still obtain a B. I know students who learned nothing and pulled away with a C. If you are self-sufficient and don't procrastinate, this class is easy.

Horrendous outline for Orgo I, almost seems as if she's trying to do the opposite and make you learn how not to understand Orgo. TA's are absolute bullies and pick on everyone (unless they like you or you kiss up to them) and make the atmosphere so tense to learn. Am I here to learn or get disrespected because I want a better life? 0/10 Yermolinda
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: i had a nice ta who graded us super lax, nearly A's on everything. did bad on the exams b/c half the answers are "none of the above" and her study guide is so unhelpful and im ending w a C. curve didnt exist this semester and we didnt know until finals what it would be

class is based off your ta (get a good one) and you dont really know the curve until the end of the semester (its different for each ta based off grading). 233 was a lot easier than 232 imo, just be extremely PREPARED for lab!! its a lot of work for 2 credits!! plan to spend lots of time on pre lab, preparing for lab, and post lab

If you weren't religious before, pick a religion and start praying. 

The class overall is extremely exam/quiz heavy, so if you're having life problems... think again. If you put in a lot of effort, you'll be fine, but if you're taking any other core classes, have a job, or aren't a good test taker? You'll be fighting for that B or C. 

Good luck.

reviews.comment: Great lecturer and good with answering questions. You're expected to have watched the lecture in advance, which is mostly beneficial for the clickers, so if you're willing to lose some points on that, then don't worry about taking notes before the lecture. Orgo 2 is more about the memorization of reactions, similar to the second half of orgo 1.

The provided videos you need to watch before class were outdated and cover stuff you don't need. Learned more on my own outside of class than in class. Reviews had content that wasn't even in the exam. People DO put in effort but the professor likes throwing curveballs for no reason. Organic chem is not hard at all. Professors make it hard.

Extremely rude and condescending behavior whenever you ask her a question. Unapproachable. Avoid orgo lab at uic if you can. She hasn't changed lab flow lab report questions. Midterms are nothing like the pre-lab slides. Videos of her demonstrating the lab is nothing like what you actually do in lab. Yells at the TAs in front of the students.

reviews.comment: I got an A.Not a hard class if you study and aren't lazy. Don't blame the professor because she won't give you an A just for showing up.

Took Chem 232 after Chem 122/123. HEAVILY SELF-TAUGHT. It feels like if you are not ahead in the class, you're behind.

Yermolina does not teach, but quizzes you on the material. Do not rely on her to learn information! You must go to class because there are iClickers every class. Horrible professor but (somewhat) nice person.
She doesn't really teach in lectures just “reviews” but never explains what she's doing. You practically teach yourself the entire subject.

Awful professor with an awful ego. Only really cares about her own research project and is constantly rude to students across the board. Barely replies to emails, if youre taking this class prepare to self teach.

Yermolina gets a bad rep from people not willing to put in even the bare minimum. For Orgo 1 a B was around a 60%. Roughly 30% of the grade came from homework's and videos which are free points! You could bomb every test and still get an B if you tried and cared. People who failed just gave up.

reviews.comment: Orgo Chem with Yermolina is no easy feat, but using resources like unstuck AI alongside the textbook and TA help can make a big difference. The labs are a lot of work, but the exams are manageable if you stay on top of the material.

Orgo 1 was by far way easier than expected. An 80 is an A and I think a 60 smtg is a B. Many easy points include WileyPlus, Iclicker/bacon, and video assignments. If you do the problem sets and go to tutoring/office hours there is no reason you should fail. The kids complaining just don't try and defer to crying and blaming Professor Yermolina
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

I never watched lectures. Yermolina over Mohr any day.
The worst professor ever to have existed. She is mean and not helpful at all, she thrives on making life harder for her student. Just dont.

she isn't the worst teacher for orgo but near it. her classes were just clickers, you had to watch the lectures online before the actual lectures? she has a crazy attitude problem that was funny at first and then become mean. protip fr: watch youtube videos and do problem sets.

Lab sections depend a lot on your TA, but Yermolina is a great prof. Go to office hours! She wants to help you!

Any class as difficult as Orgo will suppress a prof's reviews. The truth is Dr. Yermolina is a fantastic professor. GO TO OFFICE HOURS. You need the repetition.

she does 3000000 iclickers every lecture. shes a great teacher. it wouldve been nice if she at least recorded lectures. however, she is genuinely so so so unkind to students. just rude to be rude. laughing at someone for asking a question that she thinks is stupid. she was rude to someone with an accent like girl you have an accent too.

First off, she's reporting bad reviews to get them taken off! That should tell you all you need to know as far as her character and values go. She is condescending, rude, and acts as if she knows it all even when corrected on her course's own subject by her students. Avoid at all costs, and try to spread the word. And I got an A, enough said.

reviews.comment: Dr Yermolina is a very generous and good-hearted person. I think the racist review that is two posts below me is uncalled for and is a reflection of how evil the hearts of many have become... Keep in mind that UIC has a large body of students so it's important to put ourselves in her shoes when rating her. Her salary deserves to be triply increased
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Yermolina graded a student's makeup lab exam for full points even though the student continued to write in her exam book past the allowed test taking time limit. I saw the student fight three TAs saying she was just transferring her answers but it clearly was not the case. I assumed she would get an automatic 0 but Maria still graded for full point
No just no

I have had many professors during the past 3 years in college, and Dr. Yermolina is definitely one of my favorite. Her style of teaching is writing reactions and mechanisms in a very organized way in which when studying for exams you are able to locate reactions and make logical connections for mechanisms (highly suggest doing practice sets)!

Organic Chem is notoriously hard. I think a lot of students blame their difficulty with the subject on the professor. Yermrolina graded our work extremely fast. Was slow to upload our assignments making the class difficult to stay a head in. Besides that I think she is knowledgeable in the material. Didn't have set office hours.

Prof Yermo is awesome tbh & shes very underpaid! Look, Orgo 2 is hard, its a lot of material to remember and it takes a lot of studying to do well. But she knows what shes doing, answers emails, questions, etc. Exam & quiz heavy, but very homework light. The course is very curved (I think a 40 is a C). I would def take her again.

Huge curve for every Orgo class. The tests are just like the problem sets just easier. If you actually got to class, she will literally tell you exactly what will be on the test which makes studying for the exams easier. People who did poorly in this class are those who fell behind early and weren't able to catch up. Yermo is great just do the work
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Orgo lecture (both 1 and 2) was horrible with her. The lab was surprisingly easy simply because the exams are multiple-choice and have no mechanisms. Labs themselves are a lot of work and prep but it's a 4 hour lab class, so it's fair. Never expected to get an A but here we are. Never had to contact her or see her cause my TA was pure gold.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Made orgo fun the exams where like the reviews and problem sets. She also was great at teaching content in the short class sessions that we did have when it came to specific problems.

She's nice in class and says to always ask her if we need help but when you ask for help she's rude and doesn't help. No one ever knows what's going on, the only way to learn is to ask TAs and sometimes they don't know. Take this at a community college if you want any chance of learning chemistry, you won't get it here.
Amazing professor, cares about her students and helps us as much as she can. Definitely recommend her. If u study everyday you should be fine

She is a nightmare. Clearly not all there because I have no clue what leads her to act the way she does. She ridicules students for genuine questions. She ignores emails till the end of the class. She scribbles in terrible cursive on her iPad the whole time and calls it a "Lecture." I aced this course through sheer grit, I can only imagine others!

Unreasonable amount of writing. Description of lab reports says one conclusion paragraph but Labflow makes you write anywhere from 2-12 paragraphs, plus the rest of the report. You can't see how many until after the lab is done so you have only one week to write. The course itself was so sloppily slapped together. There is no help, she is awful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: The most poorly structured class available at UIC. You have no idea what your grade is until the last week of the semester, if your lucky. I've emailed Yermolina about 8 times, haven't got a single response the whole semester. If your premed, take this class at community college, you will save enough time to improve your app in other ways.

Yermolina is possibly the only fantastic prof in the entire UIC chem department. Orgo lab is HARD, but going to Yermolina's office hours saved my grade. She is hilarious and she cares so much about her students! You can't do well in the class if you don't put in the effort, but she will help you in any way she can. I wish I had her for orgo 1.

Worst professor I have ever had. Utterly shocked by the quality of the course. She recycles old materials so that nothing is up to date or accurate. Never had a question about chemistry that she was able to answer because she refuses to actually listen to the question and gives an unrelated answer. Her having a PhD shows how low the standards are.
Idk even know what to say. The class in general is so bad and she sure dosent do a good job teaching it.

Dr. Yermolina is a phenomenal professor and is the reason why I am continuing with my degree program. She is incredibly enthusiastic about organic chemistry and is always willing to answer questions. Organic chemistry is very difficult, but she makes the material clear to understand. As a word of caution, a lot of effort is required for the course.

orgo chem at uic needs to be restructured. You basically teach yourself watching 3.5 hour videos each week and then come to lecture to do iclickers and watch her draw on her ipad. To pass this class, i suggest actually working on problem sets b/c the exam and quizzes are the exact same. Use orgo chem youtube channels to better help you.

Never again in my life. So happy that I survived her. Worst professor in my life. Be ready to just sit there and watch her just write on her ipad. She does ask students questions but her method of teaching is horrible. I am so sorry if she's your only option.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The structure of orgo lab is HORRIBLE. She's the only prof available this semester, which sucks. Every time she came into our lab, my entire body was trembling bc why is she so intimidating. Choosing a good TA is rly important because most of my labs weren't graded until after the final like what??? Make sure you have a smart lab partner!!

Worst nightmare ever. I got an A in orgo I lecture, and going into lab, I thought this class was going to be good. pre lab quizzes were fine but the midterm and final are nothing like the labs. She makes you feel stupid. my whole semester was ruined just because of this two credit hour lab. if you want to take orgo lab, don't take it with her.

She's funny but a little intimidating. Quiz every week, exams every 3 weeks or so. Watch lectures before class because class is time for problem-solving/examples. Actual learning happens in discussions if your TA is good. If you go to her office hours, she will cold call you which is awkward. But she's pretty nice about it.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: 0/5 Avoid. You won't know what grade you have until the midterm. You don't interact with her because the lab is run by TAs, but AVOID even going to office hours as she will make you feel useless and stupid. Never seen a teacher treat a student like this. Also, the midterm has nothing to do with the labs. You'll feel happy if you pass this class.

She may have an interest in chemistry, but certainly has no passion for teaching it. Perhaps it's due to cultural differences, but her demeanor in lectures comes off as rude, controlling, arrogant, unhelpful, and unsympathetic to her students. Prepare to learn everything on your own. The textbook is infinitely more helpful and interesting than her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: If you want a high grade you should prioritize the problem sets and attend office hours.Some questions from problem sets are on exams. Organic chemistry is hard everywhere, but I really enjoyed her lectures and felt that the exams were relative to what we went over. She is always willing to help, just actually put in effort on your end.

The best chemistry professor I have ever had. Lectures were not required. However, it was beneficial to make yourself known to her as she is willing to work with you and help you succeed. Has a great sense of humor and though lectures are extremely fast paced, she always made sure to make them fun and interactive.

Dr. Yermolina truly cares about her students and is one of the best professor's you will encounter. She will always be open to helping you and explaining something to you as many times as you need it. Go to her office hours. Lecture attendance isn't mandatory but I highly recommend going because it makes a difference.

You don't interact with Dr. Yermolina during chem 233 as it is mainly TA taught. That being said she does hold office hours but they are more helpful during exam season. There is a lab report due every week and 2 tests, but I recommend reaching out to your TA for specific requirements as they do the grading.

Organic chemistry is a very tough course and requires a lot of effort on your part to do well. I took lecture and lab together and would definitely not recommend. The org curriculum at UIC could use some restructuring, but Dr. Yermolina does her best to try and make the content understandable for students. Getting a good grade is possible

really wanted to like her cause shes so silly in person, but the class needs a serious overhaul. they're errors in the lab manual that don't reflect what were actually doing in lab. the sheer amount of work needed to be done for a two-hour class is insane. unknown grade cutoffs, poor communication. make sure you get a good TA, ask around 2 find out

Trash professor who is rude and gives lots of unnecessary busy work. No passion for teaching and second rate human being in my opinion. The midterm and final had nothing to do with the rest of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Yermolina is a VERY rude person and talks badly about her undergraduate students to her colleagues.  It's obvious that she does not have the passion for teaching and does not have the time of day for students struggling in orgo chem. She has a great way of making you feel less of a person. Prepare for a horrible semester with her.

In Orgo 2, you have to spend a lot of time studying in order to get an A in this class. Many people said she was difficult, yes but for Orgo 1 Lab (CHEM 233), but not really in Orgo 2. Don't expect to get an A when you do not spend time practicing Problem Sets because Orgo 2 has a lot of mechanisms to remember. She's funny and passionate, goodluck!
Prof Yermolina is great. She is motivated to help students and shes very approachable. Her teaching style is great and she is able to explain difficult concepts in simple terms.

Professor is very fast paced. She goes through the problem set pretty fast. Also the practice exams are nothing like the actual exam which affected my grade a lot. She very light hearted and makes jokes and calls you out during class which can make you feel a little intimated especially if you don't really understand the material.

I am happy I picked her as my professor. Super funny. However, I do not enjoy this class. Lectures are asynch and are not helpful. During "lectures", we go over the problem set packets which could be helpful depending on the person.

This class is wildly known for being hard. A 55 percent for fall 2022 was a C but that goes to show how many students would have failed if it was a normal grading system. The curved basically saved a lot of people but this class JUST depends on your TA. If you get a hard grader then good luck.

This class is totally dependent on your TA. I know many students who ended with a C in this class But fortunately what I think worked for me was that I went to my TA's office hours before submitting my lab reports.

This lab course is done by the TA. You have to attend in person lab every other week and the other weeks are done online. Try to grab all the max points you can on lab reports and post labs. This course is intense for a 2 hours credit course. The class is curved at the end of the semester. For this semester a 60% and up was a passed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: When you talk to Yermolina in person she seems to be respectful but the coursework she assigns is a bit outrageous considering this is a 2-hour class. The exams and quizzes seem to be very unrelated to the reading preparation. Some questions will be related but the majority of the questions will have you asking yourself "Where did this come from".
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Beware of this class guys. Late grades so you don't know how you are doing. Exam is extremely difficult and contains problems you will not be taught how to do. She will NOT answer your emails unless she feels she has to. The lab procedures are combined with lab videos, manual, and textbook and they do not tell you this. Take Orgo at a CC. Good luck
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Yermolina was probably the worst professor I've dealt with in my entire life. I've taken hard classes like this before but nothing comes close to this one. This class is supposed to be a 2 hour class but I found myself working about ten or more hours a week and I am not joking. Yermolina doesn't respond to emails and the grading is very harsh.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I know a lot of people are giving bad ratings, but she is actually a really good teacher. In chem 233 you do not see her a lot because TAs do most of the work but if you got to office hours, she is super helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Yermolina is awesome! Definitely take her for your organic chemistry courses because she is very knowledgeable and has a great ability to teach!

Professor was alright. She did not teach, just held office hours during "class time" and made us watch pre recorded lectures that added up to more time than the class itself. Nothing bad to say, just don't expect tons of attention. Test reflects HW.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Overall, Prof. Yermolina really cares about the material. However, because the class is very content-heavy, make sure to not fall behind because she moves pretty fast through the material. Miss one topic and then it sets you really behind. Sometimes she doesn't communicate well so just be cautious as sometimes she has a temper.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Chem 234 is a very difficult class with so much information to memorize, but Dr. Yermolina makes this class managable. She is accessible during her office hours and by email, and she replies very fast (also very straightforward), but she made the class enjoyable! I enjoyed learning with her, and the orgo 2 experience is WAY better than orgo lab. GL

This class is a lot but the material is not difficult, just time-consuming. Yermo is available during office hours if you need help. Quizzes are based on the slides and the exams won't include any information that you do not have available to you. The lab reports make up a large chunk of your grade so focus primarily on those.

Good professor but Orgo 2 is just intense. Get ready to PRACTICE. The amount of material learned is about 5 times that of Orgo 1. The lectures are fair and you are provided with everything you need to succeed. Yermo has office hours several times a week so go to her for help. Grades consist of i-clickers, quizzes, and exams. Do the problem sets!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: For 2 credits this class makes you WORK. The content itself isn't impossible, but the structure of the course and discrepancies across different sources make it unnecessarily confusing. Ultimately, your TA will make or break your experience. Start the weekly work well ahead of time, and begin reviewing for the midterm/final WEEKS beforehand.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: TA was great, but the issue with this course is structure. There are 9 reports, weekly quizzes, a midterm, and a practical for 2 credit hours. What makes it even worse is that details matter even more than concepts. Spent most of my time working through contradictions and collecting information from the many scattered sources she gives us.

One of the best professors at UIC, HANDS DOWN. She is a super tough grader and it's super tough to get an A, but you will actually learn with her. She's amazing and if you have any issues, she's the first to try and help. Honestly I would have given her a 5 instead of a 4 because she deserves it but I feel like she can make Orgo 1 Lab better. GL!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Yermolina is the best professor for both Organic Chemistry 2 and Organic Chemistry Lab. Her lecture notes are comprehensive and organized. She is clear with what she expects and cares about her students. She is also accessible outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Pre-lab quizzes that are taken on respondus. At first, the quizzes were hard but became easier once she noticed the course average was absolutely terrible. reviews.comment: The issues with the entirety of CHEM233 lie in the fact that students do not receive feedback on lab reports in a timely manner. By the time that I had submitted my 4th lab report, I was finally getting feedback for the first three.. meaning I had failed my first three lab reports. The professor is a nice woman, but needs to change class structure.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The required digital lab manual that cost over fifty dollars was a book that she wrote. TAs lead the class and determine grades. There were no in-person labs, yet we had to write 2000+ word lab reports. The experiments were fascinating, but we did not practice science at all; we just twiddled our thumbs and did busywork. Nice lady, terrible class

Hardest class at uic (so far). Its all run by TAs and so if your TA is bad, goodluck surviving the semester. Lab reports and prelabs will take up one full day so make sure you set aside one day of the week to do them and make sure you know what you are writing about because it will show up on the exam in some way.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Workload required for this class is insane considering it is only 2 credits. Exams are difficult and you will NOT pass without studying! The TAs were more approachable than Prof. Yermolina. With online classes, it is difficult to judge her teaching but overall she seemed uninvolved as the TAs were the ones to review lectures and provide feedback.

I had her for chem 233(lab), and even though i was in another professor's class for orgo2, I switched to her lectures (online) and started doing twice better in class. I love how she repeats things many times because it helps you memorize. Has helpful tricks and her lectures are not boring. One of the best chem teachers I had, also seems very kind.

Yermolina knows her chem, but I think she forgets that this is the first time seeing this material for her students. Had her in-person for orgo lab (also tough) but got so much feedback from office hours. When I had her online for orgo II, things suddenly got 100x harder and I couldn't get help like before. You basically have to master it for an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: CHEM 233 is very hard, however Dr. Yermolina is great. The TAs are also super helpful. The labs are difficult and you will have to spend a lot of time comprehending them and writing lab reports, however they are very interesting. Exams are difficult, however questions are fair. Read lab manual!!!! Textbook also helpful.

The exams test your ability to memorize and to solve problems fast. The class is online though. So what does Yermolina do? She gives exams that are exponentially harder to compensate, for the integrity of the course. She couldve restructured her exams to make them more comprehension based. Out of touch, cold, and boring

I just began taking her this semester, BUT, as a matter of precaution, I will give her a low rating in advance. Tough labs, tough teacher, tough everything. Avoid her like the plague. She needs to learn what it means to be a human being, and not a cold hearted robot. We are in a pandemic for crying out loud. Be nice!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: In UIC there is no option in an organic chemistry lab, and most likely you will take her. She is definitely the worst professor in UIC. Get ready to write 10 pages lab reports, and get shocked every exam how confusing exam can be. She is very unorganized, yes she posts old exams, but don't expect anything even similar, it going to be much harder.

She's rude, unapproachable, inconsiderate, condescending, + disorganized. Her exams are ridiculously difficult and have errors on them. The class should be worth more credits cuz of the workload. She lacks clear communication. Not much normalization/curve + no EC which can hurt some grades. She lacks the resources to help us succeed, too.

For a student who loved chemistry, this professor ruined my love for chemistry in 3 short months. Such an uninspiring and rude professor. No one likes online courses and its upsetting that during a global pandemic, this professor has decided to give exams exponentially harder than semesters in-person. STAY AWAY from this professor at all costs!

Orgo II and orgo lab are the most draining classes I have ever had. TA's just grade orgo lab, and they are very inconsistent. The exams she gives for orgo lab are the most draining, defeating, alcoholic-inducing exams I have ever taken in my adult life, especially being online. If you don't have all your time to focus on this, you'll be screwed.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The professor discourages students and is very rude to them during office hours. Occasionally refusing to answer questions and instead commenting how the student should have studied better. She demeans many students, but it accessible outside of class. Communication through emails works better and will often help out if students have online issues.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prof. Yermolina is an amazing prof. She is very interested in chemistry, and her passion for the course is evident. There is no easy A's in his class. However, studying and hard work pays off because tells exactly how to get that A if you want to. Exams may seem hard, but if you study, there is no surprises. By far the best orgo prof here.

It was unfair how the department handled the transition to online learning for CHEM 234 as exams and quizzes became noticeably more difficult without a sufficient upgrade in teaching or PSet quality. There were often contradictions between peer leader teaching, instructor lectures, and TA grading. That said, she's an effective, informed lecturer.

I guess there is no other choice but to take it since this is the only organic lab, and I hope they put another one, but they should with a different teacher, this class requires work as if it is a 4 credit but it is just 2 and it is hilarious how you are required to do work as if it is 4 cred. This class is not fair.

There is stereotype about Yermolina that she is terrible solely based on her image outside of class. Try going to her office hours and you'll realize how much she cares about your learning. The earlier you start going to office hours, the more sympathetic she will be towards you and the more you will be rewarded. Don't believe everything you hear.

Okay, so the CHEM 233 lab is run by TAs, not Yermolina. It is hard, it will make you cry, but it is not her doing that. If you visit her for office hours you will realize she is the sweetest person ever, and cares about your learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Yermolina is one of the best professors i have ever had. she makes lecture interesting and places an emphasis on not just memorizing but knowing why a reaction occurs. overall i found her way of teaching very helpful by not just reading off a slide but actively writing out the notes with the class

Dr. Yermolina is the best professor I have ever taken. I took her 232,233, and currently taking her 234 class and must say she is hilarious, professional, and carrying professor. Yes, organic chemistry is hard, and yes you need to work REALLY HARD FOR IT, but if YOU put effort in this subject, it will worth everything at the end. RECOMMEND HER!!!

Terrible. Class is only 2 credits but she literally sets her students up for failure. The only lab professor so ur stuck. Midterm was ridiculously hard, didn't reflect ANY of the labs. Final was hard too. Nothing connects to labs. Reports have to be 9-12 pgs, detailed. She tells TAs to grade rly hard, if avg too high she makes them bring it down.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: The amount of stress and doubt you have over a 2 hour class rly isn't worth it. DO NOT take lab if you have no reason to. Average on the midterm was a 50%. Lab reports are graded harshly and if they are being graded leniently, TA's will be told to grade harsher. This class is meant to set you up for a C. Don't count on a curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Biggest issue is the lack of material covered in the lab manual and textbook not being present in the exams. Class is certainly not 2 credit hour workload. To give a perspective, I got an A in organic chemistry but a C.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Worst teacher at UIC. Does not care about you at all. If you want an A in this 2 credit hour class, forget about it. Prepare to spend at least 15 hours a week just for lab. Midterm and final are insanely hard, and are on a bunch of random sh!t. She does not care about her students. Unfortunately she is the only lab teacher... so good luck...
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Organic chem will never be an easy cheesy class whoever professor you plan to take, but Dr. Yermolina just made that time more enjoyable for me. She has a very unique humor, come to her class and you know what I mean. She is caring and easy to talk to. Her class was small so the interaction between her and the students was amazing.

She is the WORST professor ever. I took her for 232 and 233 since I didnt have another option. I had to start going to other lectures to understand what was going on. Her tests are insanely hard and her way to explain the reactions is not clear at all. She is so confusing and it seems like she doesnt know whats going on herself. Do not take her!

Class is very test heavy, and the exams are super hard. Averages for tests 2 and 3 were about 50-70 out of 125 and there is not even 1 point of extra credit offered. Lectures way too quickly for you to process any information and then gives you only 30 seconds to answer clicker questions. Textbook hardly helps bc it's so basic compared to her ?'s
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Yermolina was one of the best professors I've ever had. She is kind, compassionate, and dedicated to her students. Even though our class was large, Dr. Yermolina made it a point to know as many students names as possible. She is always available (and helpful) during her office hours. I would absolutely recommend Dr. Y to anyone taking orgo!

Dr Yermolina is an angel that we do not deserve. She is the most caring, funny, and engaging prof. who really cares for her students. However, you have to do your part as well. Orgo is not easy but her doors are always open for OH and consultations, and it definitely makes it less painful. She is a professor I will truly miss and please, take her!

Orgo I is hard no matter who your professor is. Dr. Yermolina was great at staying on topic and only teaching us the important concepts for each topics. She was low key funny too. Sit towards the front if you can, she has a pretty quiet voice so it's hard to hear when the mic doesn't work.

As I near towards graduation from the University of Illinois at Chicago with my Biological Sciences Bachelors Degree I have come across many amazing classes but non as good as Orgo Lab. The class is indescribable and unimaginably amazing. Throughout my time I have not experienced a more enjoyable feeling taking this class.

She's a funny and a down to earth professor, also makes her lectures not too boring. It's a lot of new material so that makes her class tough. Something that could've helped me earlier in the semester is not relying on her to teach, while she goes over the material. The lectures are packed, so actually go over the material and read!
One of the worst classes I ever took. High averages on lab reports dont mean anything when the exams are so difficult they bring your grade down. Ill take my D grade and never look back.

I had academically-sanctioned travel and a family medical emergency come up during the semester, and Dr. Yermolina was so difficult to communicate with and so unreasonable about make ups that my grade (and GPA) suffered as a result. Her pedagogy also sucks. Many chem profs don't really like to teach/share knowledge, and she is one of them.

I was very intimidated by Dr. Yermolina coming into the class because of complaints I had heard beforehand, but her first lecture immediately changed my mind about her. She is amazing, plain and simple. Her sense of humor can catch some students off guard, but she has never been rude or mean. I really wish I could take another class with her.
pretty smile. very stylish and great professor

Dr. Yermolina was a fantastic, helpful professor. People had issues with her but the content can be difficult. If you don't seek out help, it can be too much. That's just the nature of orgo. Most of the people who complained were the people who never asked questions or went to office hours. I know because I was always the only one at office hours.

She is amazing. One of the best teachers that i have ever had. Her skill in teaching is remarkable. She is willing to help, and she wants you to improve. I f i have to take her class 100 times, i will. I highly recommend her class guys. If you work hard, ask for her help and do the problem set, your A is guaranteed.
Shes amazing. If your ta in orgolab is giving you a tough time, just talk to her. Shes also very attractive

She was terrible she had things on her syllabus that she just blatantly ignored. She made me hate organic chemistry. She is not helpful, is sarcastic and rude. I did everything to avoid having to take her for organic chem 2. She just doesn't care about the success of her students. Said exams would be normalized and then last second decided not to.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Yermolina is extremely knowledge in Chemistry although, her class can be difficult she will work with you during and after class to get you up to speed.

Dr. Yermolina was a great professor. She is very helpful during office hours and is very engaged with her students.   The class is very difficult. If you put enough effort you can do good. The key is to do good during the entire semester, so that since the curve is so big, you can get away with doing bad on the final and still get an A

She taught the Basic chemistry class as if everyone knew chemistry already.  Her lectures are just slideshows that she reads out loud, doesn't explain, and moves on too quick for you to take notes. She is rude to the students, and makes asking questions scary bc of how she responds, like you are stupid. Really hard class and she made it 100x harder

Dr. Yermolina is a professor that really cares and wants to see her students succeed.  She responds to emails promptly with answers to questions regarding homework.  She even met with students for study group for review right before finals.  This was a very hard class for me however, she was supportive and helped her students however she could!

It was Dr yermolina's first sem teaching and in the beginning, it was tough adjusting to her style of teaching. She's always there for you if you need help and she puts in the extra effort to make you understand the material. Office hours or not, she's there for you. Tests we tough and she expected you to know a lot. Take her class!

She is a great teacher and has helped me tremendously this year. If you want to learn chemistry as easy as ABC's then I recommend her class. Not only is she knowledgeable about the subject but she also adheres to each students individual needs.
Most people won't leave a review if it's not a positive one. This professor has been teaching for 13 years and has 40 reviews

Nice guy but never responded to a single email I sent. The class itself felt like more of a chore rather than interesting so I never felt too in depth in the material. Also felt like no matter what I did I couldn't get high grades on the exams or papers and gave up towards the end. I still got the same grade that I did on papers where I didn't try.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof Whipple is such a respectful & kind professor & has an amazing sense of humor. He never differentiates to anyone & never discourages anyone even if they are wrong & if someone doesn't want to participate he never forces anyone to. He is very intelligent & hears everyone's opinions equally! He encourages us to think! you will learn a lot!!!

PHIL 101 with Prof. Whipple was easy and pretty simple to keep up with. Super lecture heavy which made it difficult to focus sometimes because he can explain things weirdly. He has an odd way of responding to students' questions or answers to his questions although he encourages us to participate. Work load was light

Professor Whipple is a very nice and kind guy, which I respect. His lectures are boring, as many students are on their phones or computers. He has a strange kind of humor, so if you don't have a good sense of humor, you might take or find offense. Has a strange way of responding to students after they add in their own comments/ask questions

Super easy class. I do have to agree that he will humour wrong ideas and it is infuriating a bit. As a women, I also felt as though he never took my answers seriously where when a guy would repeat my idea, would be praised. He is a bit disconnected outside of class and there is daily homework, but lax deadlines and easy work.

Really easy class, hard not to get an A. Professor Whipple is cool. He does this annoying thing where when a student will try to answer a question and get it wrong he will humor them and be like "ok... I guess you can say that." just say they are wrong. The class has some real characters in it and he does a pretty good job dealing with them.

Do NOT recommend course for elective/for fun, which was my mistake. Thankfully, Whipple is a genuinely kind guy and did his best to make sure I had some semblance of an understanding throughout the semester. 

cons: horrible with technology, doesn't respond to emails.
can be a bit unclear/confusing in that way really smart people often are

One of the most wonderful professors I had the chance to meet at UIC. His lectures are well-elaborated and he doesn't just read off the slides. He likes his class to be involved during class but doesn't force anyone to participate. He is a very intelligent person who will be more than glad to help you succeed if you do the work and pay attention.

Great professor but be prepared to learn and not skate by. Descartes is a hard philosopher to study and he does his best to make it understandable. The papers are small but dense. Overall a fun professor and cares about students but the actual content of the course is hard to begin with.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: It was a fun and easy class. Exams and essays were super easy, and the professor knew precisely how to pique interest from students while in class.
Gives time and goes over material for the material being tested on, is understanding, and gives material and lectures that help students on the GRE and LSAT
He is there to help you out if needed, but most of the class is just small amounts of homework that can be done in 20 min at the longest. There are only 4 one page papers and then one 3 page paper.

The professor is very educated on the subjects discussed in class, whenever there was confusion, he made sure that everything was clarified. The class is pretty straight forward; if you do the work, then you will pass the class.

I really enjoyed the topics that we read and the fact we were able to discuss them and voice our views in class. It was nice to be able to express how we felt about the papers and hear how others might agree or disagree.
I took him for Philosophy 101. For a 101 class, it was necessarily hard. The grading for the paper's you have to write is harsh, especially for a class where an English class is not a pre-req.
He's all right: somewhat boring really. If he were to vary his intonations or be more animated or theatrical about the course material, I probably would have enjoyed and learned more.

This class consists of writing clear, concise, and accurate essays about the material - no exams. Don't take this class if you only have casual interest. Short reading responses are often given to incentivize attendance. Since the material is difficult and the lectures are most often insightful, you'll actually find yourself wanting to be in class.

If you have only mild curiosity for philosophy, this course isn't suited for you. I highly recommend this course for philosophy majors and minors, since Descartes and Locke are a very important component of the western philosophical tradition.

The only reason Professor Whipple is challenging  is because of the content of the material. He challenges his students to engage in a dialect with the text and think critically.  We had ONE question quizzes every now and then. And for his paper assignments he is very specific about what he expects. Definitely recommend, very personable.

Being a freshman I took philosophy 101 for the hell of it last semester thinking it would just be easy as its a 101 class (not the case for all classes). Class was pretty easy, P Whipple is very clear on what he expects and his lectures are all interesting for the most part. Attendance isn't "mandatory" but there's usually a hw assignment due

I liked the readings & thought the content was interesting. Fun class conversation, when people participate. You have to do the readings but they're short. Nice guy, sense of humor. Thought he was easy to understand and easily approachable. Wouldn't say it was an "easy" A, but ur fine if you do the readings. Got an A, Would take his class again.
Great professor. Very funny and always willing to help those that show interest and care.
So humble and intelligent, I completely enjoyed his class (but the lectures did get dry and boring a FEW times) but i learned sooo much in his class. Awesome :)

Excellent professor! Organized, intelligent, returns homework in a timely manner, personable, and clearly explicates difficult readings/philosophies. However, his classes are not easy. Keep up on reading assignments, come to class prepared to discuss, and be able to translate your understanding into well-organized papers. Highly recommend!!
Knows his stuff. Takes long pauses. Answer every prompt for essays and Go to office hrs if need help.

I've been a student for nearly 7 years now. In my experience, professors are seldom as thorough as P. Whipple. His lectures are both nuanced and concise; better yet, he's funny, accommodating, and insightful. Students, however, shouldn't anicipate high marks without hard work. Meaning, you will really learn in this class. Highly recommended.

I enjoyed learning from Professor Whipple. His lectures helped unpack some difficult readings. He expects students to come to class having read the assigned material so as to participate in discussions. Essay assignments/expectations were spelled out for us. I appreciated his organized, methodical approach to teaching and his approachable demeanor.

Honestly, I think he is the worst professor I have ever had at UIC. He tries to insult people's intelligence in a "nice but nasty" way, he grades too hard for it to be a 200-level course, and he does not respond well to emails! Taking this course was the worst decision I have ever made.
He's awesome. Really knows his stuff and is very helpful as long as you ask for help. You have to read to understand what's going on in class. There are reading assignments and usually 3 papers.

Great professor, very polite and respectful of everyone's opinions.  He sometimes gets a bit dry, especially when it is hot and humid inside the class, and he has a tendency to make long pauses between sentences.   Makes you fall asleep sometimes, but at other times he is very stimulating.  Overall, Professor Whipple gets A- from me.

He is an awesome teacher. He loves teaching the students and will do anything to help the students, and he's fair. The TA, on the other hand, are hard graders, so if you don't understand a concept or something, ask the TA, b/c he or she is the one that grades your work. It wouldn't hurt to ask what the TA wants, b/c again, the TA grades your work.
He treats us like we are in Harvard...The material gets worse and worse...and the work keeps increasing...Unless this is your only class... DONT TAKE IT!

He does want you to understand, no doubt about that.  But... Discussions are Boring and Useless....! He is good but the Grading is Hard (done by the TA's)!...this isn't a good class if your a CBA student!
He is ok, but his TA, are unhelpful and unclear on what they expect. Since his TA do the grading your grade is what basically suffers

Excellent teacher, and extremely knowledgeable. No question is too dumb. He thoroughly and clearly explains some tough philosophical concepts. If one is willing to put in the effort there should be no reason to do poorly in his classes.
He is ok...His TA's are Useless!

He is very understanding and helpful. The lectures weren't very clear to me but he give such detailed and helpful comments back on my essays which really helped. He's definitely willing to help anyone who needs it.

This class requires a lot of reading and thinking, but if you put in the time and attend class, it's not hard.  I completely disagree with the last comment posted.  Prof. Whipple makes his points very clear and is very willing to help, as are the TAs.
He acts like he is easy, but he really is not!...His TA's and him do not communicate what so ever. Basically your grade suffers, and really nobody cares!

Ehh. Could be worse, one thing is not being clear on how she grades participation. She's just winging it and releases it at the end of the semester... it wasn't fair b/c she doesn't hear students out, just thinks she's 101% right.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I've took prof. wahlgren for two classes at UIC, and while she's a great professor and has amazing lectures, she is a TOUGH grader. I would still recommend her, but don't think that A will be easy.
Just a few assignments, 2 exams and the final project. Make sure to pick a great group to do the project.

She's nice, though she can be a tough grader at times. I agree with some other reviews that her rubrics and instructions are broad and somewhat vague but I actually appreciated that about this class. While she has clear expectations about what needs to be accomplished, she gives you the creative freedom to execute the assignments in your own way.

FOR MKTG570
Started off excited for the class, but inconsistent project instructions and unclear expectations made things frustrating. It was hard to ask questions without feeling dismissed by the professor. She was curt with responses and open communication was almost frowned upon. 
Would not recommend her to anyone.

The class is good and helpful, but professor makes it harder for you to get A. There is no easy A if you take this class with her. My suggestion is try to follow the rubric and the guidelines as close as you can and just try to not miss anything. You could get 0 on different sections of the project if you don't meet her expectations

She is a tough grader, but if you choose a good group and actually participate in getting you work done on time, you will highly enjoy this class. Pay attention to her grading rubrics prior to submitting and take notes. I struggled with her first few assignments but the group project brought my grade out at an A.

She is nice but she really is a tough grader. I have always gotten high scores on assignments but as a senior taking her course she gives 50% on assignments if you miss like one to two things on the assignment.  The class is easy but the few assignments can make or break you even when you do what she wants.

(ME328) The best part of this class was his recorded lectures. Even tho I went 90% of the time and took notes, it made it super easy to look back at the lecture and have him "re-explain" a concept which helped out on the HW a lot. The tests are also very representative of the HW and lecture examples which makes it easy to focus on what to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Genuinely a great professor in this major, if you learn from the HW and material through out the semester it will help pass this class. He follows what he preaches and loves this subject the most. His HW will guide you to success on exams. Would take him again

Great professor, great homework problems, exams not too hard.
I re did homework problems to study and it worked out very well finished with a 99.7%

Professor Xu made this class a walk in the park. He creates his own exams (which are easy) and allows you to bring cheat sheets. The lab/lab reports drag, but those are not under his control. He makes the course material easy to digest and he is overall a funny guy. Attendance isn't mandatory and he posts the lecture notes on Black Board.

Xu is a gem. He genuinely cares about his students. We had an exam where the avg was <40%, so he instilled a percent error of nearly 20%, boosting everyone's grade by at least 20 points. His rational was that he would rather us focus on learning exam 2 material without the stress of exam 1. I love this man. He is also very helpful by email!
Xu is a very good professor. He really knows his stuff for ME 341. Lectures are very interesting as well. He is very helpful outside his office hours and truly cares about his students.

Basically just an easy going guy, open note tests that are fairly simple and to the point. He posts his notes on blackboard do you don't HAVE to show up to class all the time. Just do the homework and organize your notes.
He is very nice

He explained Fluid Mechanics in a very conceptual way, but also brought in some fluids history too. Which is something you don't usually see in an engineering class. I would definitely recommend Xu to anyone trying to take Fluid Mechanics. Great guy, awesome teacher, and curves generously on final grades. what more do you want..

Very supportive and want the students to succeed. The class itself is hard so you are expected to learn the stuff but he made the class very enjoyable and offer a lot of extra credit opportunities. The quizzes are open book and you are allowed to use computer to look at the code and your notes to take the quiz. You have to know what you are doing.

I highly recommend this professor's course if you're interested in learning about operating systems. He strikes a great balance between ensuring students learn and score well. The assignments are demanding, so start them early.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He gives a lot of extra credit opportunities that I think you do them because it will help you understand more about how OS work, at least in the context on xv6. Overall goated asf, definitely one of the best profs here at UIC, highly recommend taking classes taught by him. 11/10 would invite him to try out Hollow Knights. HEGALE. SHAAAAAAAAAW!!!!!

Professor Wang is amazing for Operating Systems! He puts a lot of effort into being fair for everyone and is very accommodating and understanding. The topics in OS are difficult, but he focuses on making sure that students enjoy the topics and want to learn more, rather than focusing on their grades. One of my favorite professors at UIC hands-down!

Both CS487 & CS561 the class is very hands-on with a couple of key assignments where you are required to follow steps and observe rather than discover and implement. The final project is loose on guidelines allowing for a lot of creative freedom

If you're fortunate enough to take any class with this professor go for it
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Has a very interactive class and tries to engage students. Lectures were hard to understand at first but revisited his slides and lecture recordings made the concepts clear. Practical course.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I loved the hands-on CTF tasks and homework assignments. They are challenging but interesting.

Truly one of the most heartless people I have ever encountered in academia. She openly calls things names and seems to have no sensitivity for topics. She is not accommodating at all, and she is the most discouraging educator I've ever had. Very tough grader and unrealistic assignment expectations. Don't recommend ever taking one of her courses
Gives a lot of work and is a tough grader. When you ask her a question she gets annoyed easily and is very rude!

This is for LALS 105.  She's very rude and lacks basic manners. Interrupts and embarrasses her students in front of the whole class. Assigns lots of reading and gets mad when we can't do it all. Lectures are confusing and she goes off topic a lot. Encourages questions then belittles us if its not the answer she wanted. LOTS of presentations. :/
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: She doesnt use lecture slides when she talks about most of the content,so a lot of the notes are expected to be taken by just listening to her talk. She talks about random stuff too. She talks fast and can fall behind on scheduling and it will all be confusing. I do not recommend whatsoever because her teaching style is not the best.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: She tends to speak off topic subjects we had to read during the week. We had to read weekly two articles and write a reading review. She hardly did any grading or interaction with students. TA did all the work. Final project at the end either 10 min. video, 10 page book review.

The worst professor i ever had! so rude, mean and intimidating! if you tried to participate and you got the answer wrong she would make you look stupid! Her exams are hard but i was lucky i had an awesome t.a (Jessica Gutierrez) the readings are really heavy and hard to understand, like 80 pgs+ a week. Hardest A i ever worked for in my life!

Look, she's a good teacher. She makes you think and forces you to read the readings (which are a bit long). There's a required video or 10-page paper at the end. As long as you do your weekly assignments, the paper, and attend class then you have a sure A and don't have to take the final. I do wish she'd use powerpoints though.

Xochitl is a good professor. She's understanding, helpful and available whenever someone needs help. Also, she really knows and cares about what she's teaching. Although the readings she gives are long, if you read them and participate in class, then you will do just fine in her class.

She's a good professor, its just the way she schedules the class which was boring. The whole semester was basically about student presentations (literally). However, if you work hard you'll get a good grade. She is NOT a GPA killer, you'll get what you studied for. She also seems to have a genuine interest in the topic.

i got an A in the class but you have to do the papers for the discussions along with really studying for the midterm and the final exam. Participate in class for points which helps I never did but i really read all the readings and studied my ass off.takes alot of time and work.

The worst teacher i even came across at UIC. She is not HELPFUL AT ALL. DO NOT TAKE HER, SERIOUSLY YOU ARE BEING WARNED. if you wanna fail and see your GPA get dropped, go head take her, if thats what you want.

The worst professor I have taken at UIC. She is very hard to understand while she is lecturing. Sitting through her lecutres was no fun and very boring. She gives out a lot of reading. I aced my final and had a grade of a C on the midterm ended up with a grade that i didnt deserve... dont take her

Most of the class was based on attendance everything else was a presentation listening to presentations and a midterm. Final was a video. Even if you aced everything U could get a C due to attendance (that was me) She doesn't teach the class teaches from presentations. Just be ready to sleep in class for the last half because there won't be a final
If you show up and do the work you are fine. You have to write tests are essay but alot is your research and perception . Not hard grader.

Dr W is a really good professor, and she's super passionate about what she teaches. Exams were fair and often had questions taken directly from the slides. You also get to make a cheat sheet for exams. The only thing that bugged me was that she hated it when we made any type of noise during class, but she was rly nice when I went to office hours.

She was an amazing professor! The exams themselves were not very difficult, but the cheat sheets still helped a lot. She came off as very strict at the beginning of the semester, but she is actually very sweet and does want her students to do well. Lectures are recorded. She gave basically free points with 4 in-person drawings + HW assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Attendance required to keep up even though recorded. it is a lot of material. I started out with a D and she and TA met me in drop in hours to help me with my cheat sheet=Test scores went up. There is 100 points of assignments and drawing in class really upped grade. Class is on a scale. She said she would curve if exam had low mean (they didn't).

only good thing about this class was that attendance was not mandatory. there were 4 drawings that gave you points, 4 exams, and 4 written assignments. the drawings and assignments were easy points, but the exams were hard and a cheat sheet did not even help. class is curved though

Her slides are clear and easy, but exams are tough even with a cheat sheet because time is tight. She talks a lot and constantly reminds everyone to stay quiet; she doesn't want to hear you move, which gets annoying. Grading is fair, with four easy assignments and drawing activities listed in the syllabus. No attendance.

as a professor she was okay, lectures aren't too hard to understand (records them) exams can be troubling but she lyk what may be on it. on the other hand, every lecture was an interruption like every 10 mins which was very annoying even during exams. her organization for exams are not the best,not enough time(40mins) & always talking thru it
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As a person she is very slow. Likes to talk too much about her family. Has the hearing of dolphin. Not understanding at all. She doesn't really teach. She says that certain topics wouldn't be on the exam, but end up being very heavy on the exam. Exams are 80% of your grade. I did well in the class, but not because of her.

Summer class is accelerated. It was over 8 weeks and like being in Marines but tests were open notes. She had a lot of meeting hours. There was a TA so help available because it is a lot for 8 weeks but glad I took it.

her lectures are so hard to get through genuinely cannot stand the sound of her voice. I heard that other professors have easier exams but she gives you a cheat sheet though there's no time during the exam to even look at it because you only have 40 minutes. she also talks so much during the exam. rather swallow bleach than to take this class again
