I hated this class because of how annoyingly disruptive students were.  That being said, the professor is great.  Clear and helpful.  Just go to class, take notes, and you'll generally be fine.

The BEST Math professor you'll find at UIC! Extremely helpful and exams are totally from his lectures! Final can become difficult because the other professor for the course is also involved in final-exam problems! Overall THE BEST!!

He's a great professor and very understanding. He's really funny which made me look forward to coming to class despite the fact I hate math. It was a challenging course but he made it understandable and if you needed help/further explanation you could have always asked him after class or came to his office hours.

Very good professor!Explains everything in a good manner and is very clear. He gives PLENTY of examples and trust me they will help you a lot. He's fair game. Whatever he goes over in class WILL be on the exam. Excellent review sessions and excellent teaching. Hands down nicest, sweetest, kindest, and great professor!He cares about his students! :)

Really nice professor. Does lot of examples in class so we understand the topic really well. Very straight forward in his quizzes and exams. I'm taking him for math 310. I highly recommend taking him.
Definitely a good instructor, knows his stuff and makes the class easier by just telling you what you need to know, very helpful and tries to help you as much as possible!

Overall he is ok, but he was really slow at times doing problems on the board and end up doing one problem in class. He made his MD's easy so had to study for the Final alot more to be prepared. The TA was alot more help than he was. I suggest doing the problems in the book and that will tell you if you understand b/c he's not reliable enough
Decent TA. Always seems a bit nervous, but he really does want to help you, and most of the time he does. Have had better, and definitely had worse TA's before!

Great guy, I recently had him for MATH 180 and some students had difficulties with him, but he explains problems during discussion. Quizzes are really easy, and you do homework in class if you didn't understand it. Also, holds study groups before tests. OVERALL, great TA
Easy quizzes! Not a good teacher; he's very confused when we ask questions, but he's a cool guy ad does the homework for us.
Quizzes were easy, but they were really the only reason I showed up. He had us do our homework in class, which I think is a waste of time.
I had him as a calc TA.  The quizzes are REALLY easy and he really tries to help fi you have questions.  He's a really cool guy too and actually wants everyone to do well.

He was my TA for precalc...smart person but he was a little confuse with a few concepts and he didnt get along well with the professor.  He tries to help us a lot by giving us extremely easy quizzes to boost our grades up because we were all failing the class.  He was very helpful because the lectures were just useless.

Amazing teacher. I had his freshman year, first semester and he took away all my fears of college. So accepting and respectful to students. Papers were spread out throughout the course in an expected manner given this is a college level english class. He is slow on grading but if you shoot him an email or visit his office, he'll update you.
Very Lazy! Doesn't show you your grade until the last day of class. You could get screwed because of it.

This class is easy! He is a really nice person. He edits your papers great. All his feedback is very helpful. If you do all your work, you will do fine. This is unfortunately his last year at UIC, but he was an amazing teacher! Wish all teachers were like him; school would be enjoyable!

Okay teacher, tough grader, willing to help. Doesn't take a lot of attendance and you need to read everything for homework. You do around 4 essays and 1 project and they demand a lot of work. Could find better teacher.
This class is easy! He is a really nice person. He edits your papers great. All his feedback is very helpful. If you do all your work, you will do fine.
This class was great and Mr. Finley made it both funny and interesting.  DEFINITELY take his class!!!
he is funny and easy teacher. if you do all your reading and assignment you will get easy A in his class.

This was Aaron's first attempt at teaching, but I thought it was a good one. He's very helpful both in and outside of class, and he's a good writer that can teach you a thing or two if writing isn't your strong point. He's a pretty funny guy and somehow kept a class based on the topic of death interesting. You'll do fine if you put forth the effort

He's a mixed bag. If you have >70% (I think) attendance you can submit your exams for regrade and recoup 50% of lost points, which is cool. I lost a great deal of respect for him when he said verbatim that our generation "lacks attention to detail," when this is the most mistakes I have ever seen on course documents in a class, ever. Seriously.

Professor is a man of few words; he's a great person when you get to know him, but be prepared for long sessions of silence. This is fine, since the class is mostly groupwork. The professor is very busy, so don't be surprised if you don't get your grade back until the end of the semester. TAs are really nice and will be your best resource in class.

Patronizing whenever you asked questions and terribly handled personal dilemmas. His feedback is very vague and it isn't really feedback, its more like he's reprimanding you for not getting it the first time The TA's are very inconsistent with their feedback with one TA approving of your work and another TA saying that it's completely wrong.

Claims attendance isn't mandatory, yet it is needed in order to revise midterms. Announcements in class are also not emailed so you need to be there. I am currently writing this in April and yet still have ungraded projects and even quizzes from February .I didn't even know my current grade in this class until the last day to drop classes for a W.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Patronizing whenever you asked questions or even showed incentive in the class. Was very insensitive to personal dilemmas. And, his lecturing was only slightly better than Manafzadeh's. Not a good professor in the ME department. Would recommend avoiding at all costs.

nice guy, but not a great teacher, he spends the entire class reading off his lectures and literally doesn't connect with his exams at all, he gives a cheat sheet and its so useless because what he teaches in class isn't even on the exam. Almost the entire class failed the first exam and he blamed us??? 3 exam, 1 final, and 2 in class projects

Professor Abiade, while (rarely) helpful in some instances, was consistently quite vague during lectures and when students asked questions in class. And in the moment when a student would ask a question, he would give a response that feels somewhat patronizing, as if you were being ridiculed for being confused in class.

Not a good Professor, Jeremiah constantly pushes the start dates for assignments but not the due dates which means that in his class you're either in a state of having no idea what to do because you and your team has finished everything that could be finished or rushing to barely make the deadline. Very condescending and vague when asked for input.

Professor Abiade has a huge emphasis on group projects as this was a project-based class. I felt that the activities we did connected to a greater purpose in projects and the professional world. He is a respected professor and as long as you do the work and communicate with him and your teammates, it's an easy A

I took his 380 class during the spring 2021 semester. His lectures are powerpoints that he got either from the book publisher or online. They are not helpful. He has missed many lectures but still gives in class assignments for them even though there was no lectures. He takes a month to grade exams. He says he will post lectures online but doesnt

Professor Abiade gives very straightforward exams and quizzes. You're allowed to use a 1 sided cheat sheet so that's pretty helpful.  His exams and quizzes are totally based on his lectures. If you read through his powerpoints, u won't need the book to study for exams. You do need book for homework though. Gives enough time to work on group project

3 exams and about 10 quizzes, this class has definitely the most reading. Only 2% curve in the end, and if you really study hard and make a good cheat sheet (1 cheat sheet is allowed per exam, but only 1 side). Moreover, he is a good guy, if you talk to him you might argue some pts back

His lectures are boring and are not involving. He was very vague on the project assignment and his exams multiple choice questions, atleast a part of it. But they are based on textbooks, which he wont use in class.

Material that is covered is very boring and staring at powerpoints doesn't make it any better. Professor has some awful TA's for the course so you constantly have to get your grades adjusted. Abiade also does not believe in curving which makes it challenging to receive an A.

This guy looks and acts nice but is the hrdest grader. Loves the book and will pull anything out of it and expects you to know it. Attendance isnt madatory and its hard to sit through bc its so boring and he gives pop quizzes when he sees the class is empty.

Uses the book BEYOND heavily.Make sure you take CME261 before you take this course. He is a materials science guy, and that stuff is very important to him. He's a good guy, but a tough tester. Make sure you read the book before class. You will not pass his tests without reading the book very thoroughly. They are super hard, but Abiade is a good guy

This class is super paper-heavy, but the instructor is very helpful. He can be a harsh grader and hard to follow sometimes, but overall, a decent professor who genuinely wants his students to succeed. Would definitely recommend him, especially to anyone taking ENGL 161 as a requirement.
Professor is friendly, engaged, and very helpful and flexible. The class is paper heavy but its not bad. Easy gen ed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
what a professor! knowledgeable ab his field, lectures developed our understanding of readings v well n his assignments were a blast! i only wish i took advantage of my time in his class a bit more... :,) 

i also had trouble completing the final assignment which he was super understanding ab! legend behavior.

Aaron Krall is a very welcoming and friendly teacher. Class is usually discussion heavy so bring energy and thoughts! There are discussion boards but 99% of the time there Is no reply requirement. You're required to read a play every week and complete a quiz on it so if you don't like to read do NOT register!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I genuinely enjoyed going to class. Dr. Krall is a sweet and genuine individual who clearly cares about his students. The overall class outline is clear and doable, and Dr. Krall is very accommodating to student needs. 100% recommend!

He's a very friendly professor, and he is still willing to keep in touch with you after you finish his course. He is easy on grading, and if I have the chance, I will definitely take his course again.

Dr. Krall is awesome! He is super kind and fun to talk to. The class was pretty easy; we read a play a week and three projects through the semester. There's no midterm, and the final is straightforward and shouldn't be difficult if you read the plays. I definitely recommend taking a class he teaches!

Interesting and entertaining class. Get ready to read 1 play a week, although they are fairly interesting. Quizzes are due on BB every week, per every 1 play read. Encourages participation, is an empathetic teacher, and is very supportive of his students' needs. Will accept late work, and dives into the complexities of dramatic literature.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor was cool. Content for the class was kind of boring though, makes us present a play, felt it was a bit too much for a Gen ED no one cared too much about. An okay course if you need credits.

Aaron was a very likeable person, the content of the class isn't horribly exciting however he was always eager to teach us. Expect to almost always have something to work on in the course, as whenever you are working on a writing project he expects there to be work done between every class period. Of the many ENGL 161 profs, Aaron is a good choice

Prof. Krall was great. I really enjoyed this course and the readings he picked out, there were quizzes every week but they are super easy, and you can get by just googling if you have to. He tries really hard to engage people in discussion, he's kinda funny in a dorky way, and you can tell he cares about what he teaches.
Prof Krall was amazing ! Hes very understanding and makes lectures fun and interactive, but there is not an excessive amount of presenting. I would highly recommend taking his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I enjoyed his class throughout the semester. He is very understanding and caring, he excused me for not submitting an assignment on time. Though this is a hard class, he makes it so easy for you. Gives clear instructions on what he is expecting from you. Great guy. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The professor is really clear about what he wants and wants you to learn. The amount of work assigned per week isn't overwhelming or anything like that. Just be prepared to work and participate, and he gives pretty solid feedback. 5 excused absences and 4 writing projects
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This teacher was honestly one of my favorites. He made sure to check up on us and wasn't too hard on you if you didn't complete the homework. I passed with little effort but enjoyed him so much I'm taking a class again next semester. Highly recommend.

Professor Krall is a great teacher and will give you all the feedback you need on your paper to get an A. He genuinely wants people to write their best paper and constantly gives people second chances if they do not turn in their paper on time. I highly recommend him and would take his class again.

We arent graded on a lot of things and hes a nice man. Hes feedback is alright but its best to see him one on one. I dont like English in general which is why i would take it again but hes a good professor to take the course with. He also doesnt put in grades unless its midterms or finals
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super easy class. Some of the essays you have to write you really have to bs them because he makes the requirements way too long for the context you are talking about. You also have to go see a UIC play. Overall he is super chill, but you need to at least sparknote the plays, he gives pop quizzes.

Good for those w/ interest in theater. Dry personality. Knowledgable but dull in class. Little feedback on projects. Final grade is on 6 projects (60%) quizzes (10%) and final (20). If attendance (allow 5 excused absences) weren't mandatory you could just read the text and pass the class. Smart guy just not my main interest and I found class boring
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This class was fantastic. Very easy, although at first the readings were quite dull. Even if no one comments or tries to have a discussion, he will keep the conversation going. Easy grader, relatable and nice, makes class a good time. You will absolutely have a good time as the semester moves along because of the fluidity of his assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: We had to read a play every week because there were quizzes on Monday. Overall, not a bad class. 2 critical essays, group presentations on one of the plays you read, and 1 play review. Got A's on all the papers. Some effort, and this class is an easy A.

Professor Krall was an amazing professor. He is very clear on what he wants from you, gives great feedback, and wants the best for his students. The readings were a bit boring but they weren't long. I got A's on all my essays.
i would take him again although the readings are kinda boring. he does not require us to buy a book so thats awesome.
He is a good teacher. his class requires work but he is very helpful in his instructions. He gives very helpful feed back on rough drafts. He is chill and approachable.
Very Helpful! But the class was very repetitive and gives way too much work. As if we didn't have other classes. He gave 5 papers, fairly easy. Overall, he's an ok professor at best.

One of the best professor I have ever had. Very approachable guy always available during office hours. Just be sure to talk to him and clarify any doubts you have because the book is too hard and at the same time his topic "English with accent" is fun to study, show him that you are actually working on revising your drafts and you'll get an A.

Krall chose one of the hardest books for my class to read and it was difficult to break down. Lectures were sometimes dull. The workload was heavy, mainly papers and reading assignments. He's very nice and approachable, but can give much better, thorough feedback on papers (one of the reasons why I received a B in this class).

Dr. Krall is a complicated professor. I sometimes can't understand the purpose of the class then to just write papers. He's not passionate, he's more concerned with the syllabus and timeline. Seriously prevent him. His topic on language was a waste of time unless your going to be a linguist major. HARDGRADER.

Krall is actually a really boring teacher. He's SUPER nice and a little too accommodating, but he literally talks the entire time (no joke). He'll ramble on about whatever or keep asking questions until time's up. Other than that, he gives too much homework and reading, and he doesn't really comment/criticize/give explanations for papers.
Very easy if the work is done thoroughly, very helpful, and very understanding if you get behind.

He's a great professor. I took him for 160, and got an A on every single one of my essays. He's very chill and approachable. I seriously HATED english and it was my weakest subject before I took this class. Krall is so nice and very helpful. Best prof. at UIC! Definately take him!!

Good Teacher. The lessons can get boring because its basically a circle discussing the novel read. However if nobody reads it... it is boring as hell! Never calls on people is a plus. Helpful and understanding on late homework and papers. Considerate is the word.

Easy and fun class! Great teacher! Super nice and very very smart. He never calls on you so it's no pressure to be prepared for class but because of this discussions drag sometimes. Overall great teacher!!

He is not hot. Anyways his subject is mostly about wickerpark in bohemia and its drags on pretty much (so boring ):) . Just do the journals he asks for. Nice and easy to talk to. You have to work to earn your grade, but basically I wrote the exact same thing for all 6 essays (including my final paper).
Really cool teacher, will help you with anything you want. Lectures go by fast and most of the times are interesting. Write those essays and do journal work once in a while and its a guarantee pass.
Awesome teacher.  Took 160 with him, all you have to do is attend class and sit there, write the papers, and do an occasional writing journal thing.  And you'll get a A/B

Three exams worth 90% of the grade. Review sessions are ambiguous so you have to cram numerous lecture slides into your head which can really suck the life out of you. If you're really bad at memorizing, this class is not for you. I was hoping I get more hands on learning with networking. Literally feels like a high school class. I barely got a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class was very interesting, I could even say one of the best among the undergrad courses.
The pop quizzes are purely bonus points for the actual “exams”. I only ever bombed an exam because I did absolutely zero studying for it. Minimum effort guarantees at least a 75.

Lectures are boring and not interactive. The topic is easy, so it feels unchallenging. He gives out quiz questions in advance, which makes it easy to do well, but overall the class is pretty dull and you'll get bored quickly.

he make topics so easy to understand and class is exam heavy however tells you what to expect exactly on them; no surprises.Course content is on the easier side so you can get an A easily if you studied well for the exams.

Great professor, always has a review session for upcoming quizzes. You have quizzes that are about 70% of your total grade, however, has them clearly noted on the syllabus (organized class structure). If you make sure to at least attend the review sessions he always emails you he is having, you are guaranteed a A-B.
He is truly passionate about communication networks. His lecture slides were very helpful in preparing for the exams and his projects helped me learn Python.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: 3 exams worth 30% each and a group project for the remainder. His review lectures can be difficult to follow due to how he covers numerous topics but only 5-6 questions on the exams. If your not great at memorizing, you will have a hard time with the exams. Extra credit in class is at an all or nothing basis so it pays to see the slides in advance.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Salah was so lenient and understanding all semester. All his questions from his exams came from practice problems we actually did. Nothing on the test came to surprise me and he is a very easy grader. Overall, I would say take this class because you learn a lot and it's a very easy course to succeed in.

Loay is passionate about the field of computer networking. Powerpoint lectures are posted online, but you get much more from being in class. Labs and projects are straightforward and can be completed ahead of time. One of easiest classes in the ECE curriculum.
Very Good Professor and an Easy course. Highly Recommended for those looking for good grades.

By far one of the best professors I've had so far. His lectures are clear, well-structured, and easy to follow, and you can tell he's genuinely passionate about the material. The class is very manageable as long as you keep up with the coursework. The exams are challenging in terms of content, but are graded fairly.
10/10 Professor

Extremely good professor, lectures are great in person. I guarantee anyone who does the homework without cheating will easily get an A in the class. I didn't try on any of the assignments and still got a B. Labs lowkey suck though, good luck.

One of the best CME professors, lectures make topics easy to understand, very educated on all topics, and quite friendly.  Attendance is not mandatory and quizzes are online.  Also allows for extra credit opportunities throughout the semester.

Extremely nice guy. He is so easy to talk to and is very good at explaining how to do all the problems. The exams are either take home or in class but open note/computer. DO NOT BE FOOLED they are hard, half concepts and the other half actual problems but they are far more difficult than the homework assignments.
Professor Ahmed is one of my favorite professor at UIC very easy to understand and gives great feedback
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Abokifa class was mainly based on his lectures and the platform Wiley plus for homework. There is a lot of concepts and equations needed for this class but the homework helps understand it better. His midterms and final were difficult but there were online so notes can be utilized from lectures.

My favorite professor at UIC! Really great at teaching. People complained he didn't do enough examples, but the class just has soo much material to cover that you cant finish solving a whole problem in class, so dont complain lol, read the book and go to office hours. He explains the steps in general terms to solving every problem which helps a lot

Cme 211 is a hard class in general. Theres a lot of concepts that you need to know. Abokifa was lenient and gave out extra credit. I wish he would go in depth with some examples and actually solve the whole problem using numbers instead of verbally explaining it. The homework was a little bit hard since it was online.

Hes an decent teacher. Weekly hw assignments 2 midterms labs and a final. Hw was 25% labs 25% midterms 25% and final 25%. He is very lenient and did give us extra credit and also let is redo labs where we did bad on. He also did curve the midterm as well. He is very knowledgeable but this is a pretty hard class. Lots of concepts you gotta know.
kindkindkindkindkindkindkindkindkind

Professor is very kind & understanding as long as you communicate. Fun class and interesting material. Quizzes should be easy as long as you read/watch the material beforehand. Recommend him for other ARAB classes as well.
Best professor ever!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: great, super super kind, and very helpful- highly suggest taking him

One of my favorite professors at UIC. Extremely kind and really cares to get to know you and make sure you're doing okay. Assigned so much homework but was so good at taking feedback about it and at the end of the semester dropped a lot of assignments. Also learned a lot from him! Such an amazing professor!!!!

reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He is a topnotch professor. Very caring and funny. As long as you try your best you'll do good. He teaches it pretty well and I learned a lot and my arabic is way better now after this class. Ghassan is truly one of the best professors i have ever had at UIC. Soft spoken and down to earth guy.
I've never had a professor respond so quickly to emails, and the feedback is still very thoughtful.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Truly one of my favorite professors I've had at UIC. He is an excellent educator who honestly cares for his students, I highly recommend any of his offered classes.
Great professor, he really is passionate about what he is teaching and cares for his students.

Was and still is my favorite professor as of writing. Bit of a tough grader, but absolutely loved the lectures and the feedback he gave on assignments. If you have the opportunity to take one of his classes, please take it.

Great professor and lectures! There is a good amount of writing assignments, however if you look through the notes/material you'll be all good. He also provides a lot of information when it comes to midterms as well as finals.

It is so obvious he cares about and genuinely enjoys teaching European history. I would totally take a class with him again. Clear grading criteria for each of the writing assignments. A lot of reading homework, but you could honestly get away with skimming the readings before class and just taking notes in lecture on what the sources had said.

took this course async, worth it, wrote all my response papers without a worry, did not need to show up to class, all material is given on blackboard, easy to understand, make sure to turn thing on time or they will not be graded, did it in 8 weeks so it is easy to lose focus, he will email you about deadlines.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class taught me that, history requires lots of writing, reading, and even critical thinking. This class was challenging because there is response papers, that requires you to read/watch textbook, class lectures, and document readers. Although, the class was stressful and challenging, it made me become a better writer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: The exams are painfully long. While they are given to you in advance, all three averaged me around 6-8 hours in order to get 90%'s or higher. The class is not meant to be taught online and he believes in providing way too much work for a 100 level class. If you are going for an easy and fun class, this is not the right one.

It's an online class, so getting an A is pretty easy, but please be aware of the long papers!! He and his TA graders are very hard, especially since this is an entry-level gen ed that people are using for a GPA boost. It's unreal how hard they grade. They only try hard and enjoy this class, to be honest. I do more Engl work here then my Engl class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Abbott is great. Tough grader, but great.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: this dude is so awesome. literally just made an account to be able to rate him 5 stars. this is the third class i've taken from him and his lecture style rocks. anyone that is deeply interested in history will THOROUGHLY enjoy this class. shoutout professor abbott i hope both sides of your pillow are always freezing

Every lecture and class with Professor Abbott is enjoyable and the professor really cares about his students participating and drilling in the lessons from history into their heads. Don't be afraid to challenge his ideas because he enjoys discussions and alternative viewpoints. He's anything but stubborn and is glad to change his mind.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: You're graded by a few things, and there's no rubric for anything, so it's kind of frustrating thinking you're giving him everything he wants just to dock points for whatever reason. He's a good man, though, and he has much to impart to young historians.

Professor Abbott cares about what he does: and he does this tremendously well. I feel smart being able to simply understand what he says. He does response papers where you synthesize historical info and your thoughts. Catch up on work, ask the TA for help if needed, and study for those exams! You'll do fine.

This was one of the most boring classes I've taken. He only reads off the slides and talks the whole 50 min. No engagement and attendance is required. He grades so harshly and does not tell you what needs improvement. He also speaks way too complex and the class is overall too confusing and complicated for a 100's class. I would not take it again.
I hated this class so much. If you do not like history, then do not take it. Its all long papers and quizzes that were hard. The lectures were so boringggggggggggg.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Very nice man. But, his vocabulary is too high for any normal college student to pay attention to. He also reads straight from lecture slides, which is boring. His lecture slides are enough to prepare for the 3 total tests. Find an easier elective unless you LOVE READING. TAs grade moderately hard on response papers. Kind of regret taking class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Funny guy. His way of speaking can be hard to follow at times and he can be rambly but his lectures are enjoyable. He wasn't that hard on coursework or grading.

Professor Abbott was a phenomenal professor. He is such an eloquent speaking, is super knowledgeable, and clearly enjoys what he teaches. He loves to engage with the class and enjoys hearing other students thoughts about the material. His class does require a bit of reading though. Nonetheless, i would absolutely to him again and recommend him!

Very kind and laidback teacher and patient with those who need extensions.  However, don't take his kindness for granted as he will call you out. The instructions he writes tend to be a little confusing but assignments are usually very straight forward. By spending a little bit of time doing the work, it's an easy class.

Prof Abbott was cool and although lectures were boring at times, he was laidback. Ask for an extension and it's granted, if you forgot to do a quiz, email him and he opens it up for you. Even if you miss a lecture, you can check the slides and recordings for help, they really helped me pass considering I was asleep for most of his class lol.

Professor Abbott was a very cool professor. My class was fully online and you do not have to go to the morning lectures as theyre all posted online as well as the slides. You do have to attend all the discussions, though. I once forgot to do a quiz and emailed him and he was patient with me to the extent that he opened it back up for me! Thanks!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Abbot was wonderful, his lectures were always in depth and engaging and the readings he selected for us, particularly the (many, but all reasonably short) primary sources, really enhanced every aspect of the course and fostered great in class discussion. Will absolutely take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Abbott is just great! He tends to talk in metaphor but he has great lectures . He is also very supportive and understanding of his students. Provides great feedback and is always so kind. Definitely work hard on your papers. Overall, great professor and great class,

Professor Abbott is dedicated and wants you to succeed. He accommodates and gives extensions if you need them. His lectures are dry but still very thorough engaging. His exams aren't overly difficult, and neither are his weekly response papers. He doesn't ask you to follow any actual structure with your writing; simply show what you know.

Professor Abbott is an exceptional professor. He shares his knowledge and perspectives easily during lectures. Although each class is lecture heavy, you really learn a lot. I fell behind due to personal things going onand professor Abbott was understanding, encouraging and really worked with me closely to finish the class w/ success. 100% recommend

I have taken 2 classes with Professor Abbott and both were nothing less than enjoyable. When it comes to European History, Professor Abbott has knowledge second to none about its people and events. While lectures can get a bit stale at some points, his greatest desire is that the student understands the material and will go above and beyond to help

John Abbott is one of my favorite professors. His classes were consistently my favorite and I always found myself excited for his lectures. He has harbored a great love of history in me and if I didn't graduate I would continue to take him again and again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very straightforward, at least for HIST101. Content is taught rather thoroughly, and there are no "gotchas" when it comes to grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is a very nice professor and truly loves the material taught. However, all of his lectures are very very dry. The class is extremely slow moving in the sense that its dull with minor details. Thus only take him with this class if you truly love history and its your passion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He was a good professor, the class includes lots of reading and 1-2 page paper every week. The essay portion of the test is directly from the study guide, but the MCQ you have to dig into the lecture presentation to actually find. overall, he was a helpful teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Abbott is a decent teacher. But he gets off topic very easily and MY GOD he is quiet. The classroom was 3 rows deep and we could barely hare him in the back, even a mic didn't help. You will learn a lot in class but there is a lot of homework/readings. it may not sound like it, Abbott does want you to learn and if you talk to him he wil try to help
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The professor assigns hefty loads of reading. I dont want to discuss readings. I come to class to learn. He is a great guy and funny. I just think he should lecture more and not get iff topic at times.

His lectures can be a little confusing (he kinda draws a mind map on the board when he doesn't have a powerpoint), but he speaks well and knows what he's talking about. He treats questions with respect and explains concepts well. Cool dude.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof. Abbot is one of the best lecturers I have had at UIC.

So far I have taken 2 classes with Professor abbot, both 213 and 214. Class is lecture heavy because he has ALOT of knowledge about the subject. he is soft spoken though. There are 2 papers which require reading from the books that he assigns (books are cheap) and 2 exams (essays). he gives study guides which is basically the exam itself! Easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's a really nice person! But his class was not structured correctly. It was his first time teaching an honors course so I'll give him that but it was very lecture heavy. It was a TR course so he'd talk the entire 1h15m. Which is great if you're a history fanatic but for the average jo, I do believe his content could be simplified a bit.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Respectable figure. I took an honors class with him. Though I respect him very much, his class was a bit dry, and the paper at the end was very stressful considering we didn't work towards it during the first half of the semester at all until two weeks before the proposal was. Overall, genuine teacher, but lectures did not add up to the term paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: If you're a history fanatic, then you will thoroughly enjoy the lectures and class- albeit the occasional dryness in the lectures. However, Abbott  is very passionate about teaching and a very respectable figure. As far as exams go, study his lecture slides and religiously read from the book and you'll be fine.  Personally, I loved his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Abbott's class is really interesting, but there are a lot of readings. He is very specific about how he wants his essays done, and gives good feedback on how to improve for the next one. Dr. Abbott loves to have discussions about the readings, so please be sure to read thoroughly and participate.
Great lecturer and welcoming during office hours. Go and meet with him outside of class and you'll understand the coursework better and appreciate his teaching style more
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: 3 tests throughout the year, otherwise just weekly 2 page review papers every week. Great professor with great lectures.

Tests are based off of his powerpoint lectures and notes. He gives you a study guide about a week before the test that is literally just like the test. No homework except for a 1.5 page paper based off of a reading he gives you every week. Not really worthwhile to read textbook. Attendance counts as part of your grade.

Abbot was an awesome professor. He knows his stuff well and I found his lectures to be really interesting. He ties together all of the events well and shows a logical progression. Paper topics are good and he is usually an easy grader. If you have any questions he's easy to talk to and will give you valuable feedback.

You only take 2 tests during semester plus finals. He literally tells you EXACTLY what will be on the test like a week advance, it's up to you to learn the material. The tests demand a lot but only because he introduces you to what the test will be on a week prior. Great guy, look over powerpoint slides before test and you'll pass. EASY grader

His lectures can be a little dry, but hes a thorough professor who follows his syllabus very well. His tests are fairly easy if you know the subject matter, read, or go to lecture. The papers he requires you to write can be somewhat lengthy and time consuming but not more than average. Overall a very good professor.

If you've taken European History, this class should be really easy. However, it is a lot of reading, and you have to write a 2 page paper due every Friday. If you hate history, then don't take this class unless you absolutely have to.

This class was a let-down compared to what I was expecting. Dr. Abbott is a nice guy, but lectures are extremely boring. 2 exams with decent study guides, 2 papers, and a few quizzes. Grading seems to be the same on both papers. If you get a 70 on the first, the second will likely be similar even if your writing improved. Wouldn't recommend.

There is a paper to write every week and the TAs are tough graders at least mine was. She graded too rough for a 100 level class. Teacher is nice and gives helpful study guides. This class should be easier than it actually is. Requires studying. Exams aren't too bad but response papers are a hassle.
Very intelligent and he knows his stuff.  I love history and learned a lot. Would take him again.
Mr. Abbott is an awesome professor, his lecture are simple and straight to the point. Show up and do your weekly page and half essay on the weeks study and you'll pass easily!

Good professor. The workload is manageable. Lecture is interesting. You have to buy 1 book: "Sources of Western Tradition" by Perry to complete the weekly homework assignments. I recommend this course.

His field is different from what he teaches, Western history, so he does not go over the interesting bits, just a broad take on some of the important ideas. Not a very knowledgeable historian. A boring yet one of the easy classes. If you can write well, take this class for an easy A. Required attendance, weekly response papers, and three exams.

Abbott is great! He is soft spoken, but sitting in the front makes sure you hear everything. I learned so much from him and my TA, Adam, was honestly the best. If you read, do the response papers, and study for the exams, you will get an A. I don't understand how some people don't try. An A is definitely manageable.

easy class you dont even have to pay attention. DONT BUY THE BOOK I havent read it once! Just do the weekly discussion papers and study the guidelines before the test and you will be fine. Also, the TA Tim is super nice and funny.
phew! He has papers due every week or so, and exams that are difficult, if you care about you gpa take this class another semester with sack, he is a solid professor and easy.

Very smart and interesting. Class was not too challenging but not a blow off either. As usual with UIC the TA grades the paper, so it depends on how they grade but most people in my class did pretty well. I recommend him especially if you love history and actually want to learn.

Easy class. Didn't do the readings, because before each test there were studyguides with everything that would be on the test. Only hassle is weekly response papers. TA's graded reasonably hard for those. Tests aren't bad. 1 essay, multiple choice, and some definitions. Attendance is taken at each lecture.

His class was interesting. The assignments were basically to answer a few questions about a book and turn it into a paper. Tests were based around power points and if you study a little you'll do fine. He is extremely knowledgeable and professional.

Professor Abbott, while sometimes incoherent, is an excellent professor. I had the luxury of being in a class of 40 people and he was entirely audible. His grading seems to be relative to prior grades, but is still quite fair. His reviews were sub-par, but he shined in lecture. Straight-forward power-point guided lecture.
He is soft spoken but nice and really smart. The assignments weren't bad, just a couple papers. Overall he's a good teacher and it was a good class

I thought he was wonderful. I am interested in history although not a major. He was incredibly knowledgeable and would answer questions as completely as possible. I will take another history class and I will take it with him. The homework and papers are easy and usually the TA grades them, so I people don't like their grades its not his fault.

He is very quiet in class and it is sometimes very difficult to hear him in the huge lecture halls. He literally gave me an 81 on every single assignment, and I know I deserved higher on some and lower on others. Not that great.

its true he is is VERY soft spoken and as a result its difficult to pay attention. as long as you read the book and readings which is about 30-40 pages per week plus the weekly reaction papers, you will do fine. i got a b and rarely read the textbook. just read and you will ace it.

He's hard to understand because his voice will frequently get really quiet. He is all over the place in lecture and always goes on totally random tangents. Midterm, final, 3 essays. Midterm is basically an in class essay. He assigns 2 books to read, but you don't really HAVE to read them to get a good grade. He also never shuts up about Napoleon.

Easy but frustrating. Really hard to focus in class because he's soft spoken. MC questions were worth only 10 percent on each test, but picks some ridiculous questions. Overall, if you don't like writing, you're not gonna like this class

The professor was a nice guy, but the class isn't that interesting. You have a two page paper due every week on the readings you are assigned. Overall it's a pretty easy class if you study for the test and do all your papers.

Good professor, loves what he teaches. Class is lecture, can be difficult to follow and sometimes boring. Read book if you can't follow lecture. Tests are essay; he gives you the questions in advance. Weekly discussion sessions  with a TA and with response papers due almost every week 2 pgs double spaced. Attendence in discussion counts for grade

Terrible professor. This should be called "English History". As his test are basically 3 essay tests on stupid questions that you have to "argue" or "persuade" about history. Never attended a lecture still got a B. You have weekly 1 in half page assignments turned in, on mostly dry, sometimes interesting history of western civ. pretty useless class

This class was fairly easy.  He posted the slides online so if you did not go to class you could still see exactly what he went over.  He can be really boring sometimes but overall the class is easy (if you do the weekly readings+ short -2page) response papers.

Takes his time with teaching each algorithm and shows you how each of them are developed from scratch rather just skipping through slides of pseudocode. This lets you build a strong foundation for understanding these algorithms and applying them which I appreciated. I recommend attending majority of the lectures though if you want to get an A.

Professor is unhelpful, heavy accent, and his tests are history exams. They have so little to do with actual, testable material, and rather just how good you are at memorizing trivia-like questions. He made a traditionally rewarding, easy class into a class I came to recommend my friends NOT take, since it was so underwhelming and useless.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Midterm and final each make up 1/3 of the overall grade. The other 1/3 is the average for the homework. The homework is difficult, but there are resources to help do it. Midterm and final were not too bad if you understand how the algorithms work and know the pseudocode. There were lots of ec if you came to class. Lectures were hard at times
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His teaching style is very boring and it feels like he doesn't care about the course or his students.

Lectures are very disorganized; he jumps from topic to topic without a clear structure. Teaching style is not intuitive at all, you have to try real hard to understand what he's trying to teach you because he always uses mathematical symbols and variables that just makes everything more confusing to read.
This guy cannot teach.

I took CS 516 (Algorithmic Fairness) with him. The course was research-oriented; the lectures and the project helped me to learn various aspects of the topic. The paper presentations were less beneficial, but overall, it was a very good class.

Was excited to take CS480 under him after reading all the positive reviews but I absolutely did not like his teaching style, it was rather slow and repetitive and also was not value-adding. The material he covered was only partially relevant to what he asked in the exams and his grading criteria completely depended on the TAs which was unfair.

Professor Abolfazl Asudeh left me deeply dissatisfied. Grades were assigned haphazardly, without due consideration for the quality of work. This disregard for careful examination diminishes the educational experience and raises questions about grading integrity.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Asudeh is one of the best professors at UIC.
Best Professor at UIC!!
Very caring and effective instructor!
Awesome professor, very considerable for students. HW sometimes tough.
Professor is very considerate towards the students. Class notes are enough. Very helpful if you reach out to him during OA.

Professor Asudeh is definitely the best professor I have had at UIC. 
He really cares about the fact that students learn from his course and always tries to help students who are struggling. The course is definitely not simple, but he makes even the most complex topics clear.

I would definitely recommend him and his courses.
The lectures were great and covered a lot of interesting topics. Easy to follow notes and fair grading.
He's great Professor, only 2 assignments, and exams were slightly harder, however, if you read his notes thoroughly it should be easier.

The topics are a bit more complex than other courses, but the professor is very clear, and the exam is not difficult. The lecture notes are also well organized and easy to understand.
Participation in presence is highly recommended (also for some extra credit).
He is very friendly and cares for the student.
He clearly loves the course topics.

I took Prof. Abolfazl Asudeh class CS 501 this semester. The professor very patiently explained all the intricate concepts very easily and cleared all the doubts in the class. Initially, I was scared to take advanced algorithms but the professor made the concepts easy to understand and provided his notes that helped in exams a lot.

Not exactly the most remote-friendly professor, but if you attend in-person, you will likely receive an A. I give him a 5.0 because I find that he is a better option than most of the other 401 professors, not because he's necessarily great. The exams were mostly fair, and easier than what other professors gave for this semester.

Professor Abol is a very caring person and knowledgeable. The lectures were fun and the professor used his tablet to walk through different algorithms. Easily accessible after class and fast in grading. The class is tough but if you pay full attention to lectures you will get an A. my only issue was the lack of visual aid for some algorithms.

Took this class during Fall of 2020, COVID was going pretty strong. I got COVID and could barely function. I emailed this professor to ask for an extension since I was sick and even sent him a screenshot of my positive test results. He never responded to my email, instead he sent one of his many announcements complaining about something pointless.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Jonathan Abarbanel is by far the worst professor I have ever had in my life. He does absolutely nothing about class discussion, just lectures for an hour and fifteen minutes and says goodbye. He doesn't allow for success in his class and grades things however he sees fit. Do not take him, he is not empathetic at all for his horrible course set up.

Worst professor I've had in my four years at UIC. This is a 103 class and he treats it as if its a 500+ class. Quizzes are way too specific and he's VERY rude to students. Save yourself and choose another professor. This is not worth it.

Do not take this class there are so many better options. I put in more effort into this class than my math/CS classes. There is no way you are getting through without taking extensive notes, as weekly quiz questions are very detailed. A paper turned in at around week 3 was graded during finals week and he was rude in every single email.
Terrible professor, too much drama.

Get ready to watch 4 or more hours worth of videos per week. Content on the quizzes may be found in two seconds out of the hours of content. Answers found in lecture TRANSCRIPTS still will not result in a high grade. Not a great class to take during a pandemic; isnt forgiving of three plus missing assignments, which lowers your grade by a letter.

Took this class, was not expecting to put in all of this unnecessary work for a gen ed. He does everything in his power to stop people from cheating, which is fine, but it makes the class annoying and tedious for everyone else. Quiz questions are based off the most miniscule things. Things that he mentions once in his 10 part video segments.

awful!! He has an attitude. I took the class bc I needed 3 credit hours and didn't wanna go to campus for it, but def not worth it. He only uploads LONG videos to watch, and doesn't upload any slides which is a pain if you don't have time to watch the videos. not worth wasting your time when there are better choices for online classes tbh.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I guess it depends on the person, but for me Prof. Abarbanel's class was quite hard. I've taken two courses w/ him and it's hard to know what you're expected to know without slides/more guided lectures. He goes off subject and does tend to use caps in emails. Nice guy, but it also feels like he wants to make the course hard/yell at you sometimes.

Rude, annoying and doesn't respond to emails. If u take this class be prepared to spend at the very least 3-5 hours a week watching lectures and taking notes on the lectures. Tests are oc and unreasonably hard. The final is cumulative. If you've been told that this class was easy- they lied. if u choose to take it anyway you WILL regret it.

Professor Abarbanel is mediocre at best. He does not reply to e-mails but somehow sends out 23895102 e-mails a week. This class is a fat joke so I guess it's okay. There are 3 papers, 10 short quizzes, 4 long quizzes, and one cumulative final exam. Don't worry, it's an easy class

He can be very rude and drags on for too long about unnecessary things, he is also not a very fair grader. He is very set in his ways and will ramble on about things as simple as a staple in your paper for 10-15 minutes of lecture. This class genuinely made me loose interest in theater.

I highly suggest u don't take this class. u watch hours of lectures and take good notes only to get to the tests and have no idea what the correct answer is. This class is very stressful and requires a lot of time. I would only suggest if you were a theater major or had very light classes. This class is a easy c/d. Good luck

Jonathan was very rough through the semester. Always seemed to be in a bad mood. Reaching him wasn't easy at all. He was very adamant on being right, His way or highway for everything. Even though the class was relatively easy. He made sure to make it feel hard. Some professors really lack empathy, he was one. Just keep up with the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The teacher's nice it's a simple class it's just a quiz every week and three papers. The class isn't hard some of the papers instructions are super vague but it's an easy A.

Quizzes every week (some short, some long), 2 short papers, 1 long paper, and a final. He takes his time grading the papers so don't expect a grade right away. Make sure to take the online class and you definitely have an easy A to boost up that GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This was an online class, all you had to do was complete an easy 5-10 quiz every week , that's it and few tests and 3 half page essays
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: His online course is very easy. Take notes on weekly lectures and you will be fine. 2 mini papers, 1 big paper (must see a theatre play), and 1 final exam (cumulative). That is it. Simple and easy A.
He is rude!!! If you this class isn't mandatory don't take it . You need to read plays, which were boring to me. I had no interest in theater
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very lecture heavy, but interesting lecture because it's all picture and video. Going and seeing a couple plays and writing a paper on them is the only grade besides some lecture quizzes and quizzes on the plays. Because this was a musical class we had to "Do A Number" but you can show one off youtube too.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: If you have absolutely no interest in theatre, dont take this theatre history class .bc its all about theatre. But if you like it then def take. Hes entertaining (even if the material isnt) and didnt have to buy books. Saw 2 plays wrote a 3 page paper got a B.

Prof. Abarbanel is VERY knowledgeable in his field and he makes sure you're aware of it. This dramatic little man loves: A)pop quizzes B) People who read the monstrous plays assigned religiously C) People who follow his VERY THOROUGH instructions. The study guide he gives out is life and attending class is the only way to score certain test Q's.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: He's pretty funny. You can tell he's passionate about theatre and the class isn't hard at all. You gotta see two plays and write two papers throughout the semester, but those are the only papers. He does do pop quizzes so try to read the plays. If not, shmoop or sparknotes it. Overall, the class is pretty cool.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: You have to pay good attention in lecture because he doesnt give notes which is difficult. He makes rude comments and is too dramatic. Never know what to take from lecture because he doesnt tell what is important. He isnt friendly and I dont recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: In my college career, professor abarbanel is by far the worst professor I've ever had. Not denying his intelligence nor credibility in his field, but his ego and condescending remarks are awful and discourages you as a student. Do not take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Coming up on 4 weeks in his class and have had a different experience in each one. This is due to his mood fluctuation- you can tell if he is having a bad day, taking it out on his class. Pretty egotistical and sometimes takes jokes too far, borderline inappropriate. I will give him pts for his passion and extensive knowledge surrounding theater.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: If youre not interested in theater and would not want to read 20-40 pg plays (quizzes), dont take this class. The lectures are very detailed oriented and Abarbanel does not use powerpoints or any other method of recording his notes. If you miss a day of class, theres no other way of getting the info you missed. 2 papers, exams, and 6 play quizzes
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Cool dude. Its history- so boring but not unbearable. Show up. Do take some notes. Leave.

Abarbanel knows his theatre well, so the class won't interest you much if you could care less for theatre. He doesn't use powerpoints and all the lectures are pictures of the material and he writes down some terms. I found myself spacing out most of the time because he wasn't very exciting. However, the plays he chose were interesting.

This class is okay. But he expects a lot from you, just a little bit too much, especially if you aren't a theatre major. He really knows what he's talking about. He also enjoys talking to his students, so although he may be intimidating, it's definitely worth it to talk to him. He genuinely cares about all of his students.

just avoid him and this class unless you absolutely have to take it. And if you do take it take it passfail because if you don't this is a difficult class and professor and it will kill your GPA. I thought this was going to be and easy elective and it turned out to be the exact opposite.  Attendance is mandatory because of pop quiz

It's not a bad class, honestly. I love theatre, so I took it, but it's a lot to read, and you canNOT just skim. You have to read it very detailed. Pay attention to details, and go to class, because you never know when youll get a pop quiz on the play. Pop quizzes are five questions, and sometimes difficult, so READ.
Don't bother buying the textbook. It's an easy class. Do the work and you'll be fine. Honestly, most of the people who complain about how hard the class is are idiots

I am an International student, and this class is pretty hard for me. There are lots of information need to remember. You need to go to the class because there will be quiz for almost every class. There are lots of readings too. The class is not easy, but I actually learned things from this class. If you do prepare and review, you will be fine.
Do not take this class unless your a theatre major or interested in theatre!

This class made me appreciate theatre. It was a great class and the professor was perfect for this course. Pop quizzes every week not bad at all if you read the plays. You were to watch I believe two plays and write papers on them. One of my favorite classes throughout my four years at UIC. Easy B I would say

He gives pop quizzes on all the readings. You get ONE LONG paper on one of the two plays you are assigned. The LONG quizzes are pretty difficult but if you take good notes you'll be fine. Overall this class was beyond dull, the professor is rude, and you legit dread his lectures!!! Don't take if you're not a theatre major.
Often gives pop quizzes that are tough! All the long tests you will do well on if you look over your notes and pay attention. He's a funny guy but cannot hear very well so speak up.

"pop" quizzes every week.Make sure to read the plays or at least sparknotes.He was pretty rude sometimes.Very knowledgeable about theater.His long quizzes were almost impossible for me. Take thorough notes, otherwise your screwed. He doesn't use power points.This is definitely not a blowoff class.Seize any extra credit opportunities he might offer.

As long as you read the plays (one for each class) you'll be fine. The small every day quizzes are ensure you've read and attended class. It is the final that is hard bc it's cumulative and you're expected to know things like dates. He's a little arrogant but friendly and approachable. He's really passionate and knows his stuff well. Awesome class.

He could be arrogant sometimes but he knows lots of things and he knows what he's talking about. The class requires lots of reading and the plays sometimes are long and boring. There pop quizzes everyday and they are just tricky. You got to see interesting plays at UIC theater and write a long paper about it. Overall the class is hardcore.

If you are not a theater major, DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!  It will be hard and the plays are really boring.  You are also required to watch a few boring plays. Lectures are like sitting in a classroom and listening to him talk.  And yeah, the professor has attitude!  So only take this class if you are passionate about theater!

If you're not interested in theatre do not take this class I hate this class. His pop quizzes and Long Quizzes are tricky and hard. He bases all his points off of quizzes which i read and never got a 5/5 on so good luck .

Lecture could be boring at times, but not that bad. For the most part its easy. Pop quizzes on the plays you are assigned to read & you are to go to two plays at the UIC theatre & write papers on them. I can actually say I walked out of this class loving theatre!
If you attend lectures, take notes and read the plays, you'll do great. He comes across a bit arrogant, but it's just an act. He's a good teacher and lectures are interesting.

This class is not that bad. It is a lot of reading, but you can sparknote the plays and should be good on the pop quizzes. The tests are kind of hard but he gives extra credit. He himself can be a little stuck up.
Gave a nice curve at the end plus extra credit. Long quizzes are hard as are the daily pop quizzes.  I would not call this class easy, but he is good at lecturing.

BEWARE. If you want to take this class to fill an elective DO NOT take this clas. It's a difficult class that is time consuming and if you're not a THTR major and dont care about plays or THTR you're going to hate this class. The prof is pompous a**, who isn't helpful and a creep. If you dont listen to me and take this class, PLEASE attend lecture.

Although he was rude at times, he showed that he had a strong passion for theater. I recommend students to ATTEND class cause he always has pop quizzes. Read the plays! Long quizzes are HARD. The two papers are long but easy if you pay attention to the play. Overall the class is easy if you do the work. TAKE ADVANTAGE OF THE EXTRA CREDIT!
not an easy class at all. if you plan on taking this for an elective please dont. it is intended only for theater majors only!!
not an easy class, read the plays and dont expect the teacher to help u. He has an attitude and wont help students because he thinks he is better than u (but if u give him attitude he might listen)

Lectures are very informational and directly relate to test.  However, extremely unapproachable and rude. Countless errors in grading, which result in students giving every effort to communicate with a teacher who obviously doesn't care.
Cool and funny
He has a lot of pop quizzes but but otherwise he is very good

I received one of the highest grades in this class, although 20% got an A. I only read the detailed sparknotes, writing down important info for reference later. Even if you read the plays, look at sparknotes because details get lost in translation which are needed info for quizzes. All "Long quizzes" were tricky, you really need to take good notes.

It's a fairly challenging class. He was a cool professor, funny, approachable during lectures, and can come off a bit arrogant at times. Make sure you read the plays (or at least some detailed Spark Notes) before you come to class, or you will pay the price. And dont try to leave early, he will sneak in a quiz at any time

Must read plays to get a good grade. Plays are sometimes long and boring. I asked questions after class and the professor was rude to me. He yelled a lot and was very unorganized. Extra credit helped me get the A and he does know his material, but he was very rude.
He knows his stuff I'll give him that. Reading the plays is a must, but reading is extremely long to obtain all the information. He gives EC and tries to make it easy.

he is not arrogant, he is a nice, funny guy.Attendance is a must, there is always a pop quiz after reading. plays are on sparknotes for lazy people, quizes are multiple choice. papers are graded pretty harshly at times, but there is extra credit offered. pop quizes are on details of the play while long quizes are on his lectures.he knows his stuff!

The class was for the most part easy. I only read about 4 of the plays and used sparknotes for the rest (if that). this being said, i did not do so well on the quizzes but did good on the papers and exams. also, abarbanal has many different graders so it really sucks if you get him as a grader because he grades harder than the rest.

It was his first time teaching at UIC so i dont know if he's still like this. But you must must read the plays to do well on the quizzes and attend lecture or else you're not going to do so well. His lectures were super boring which is why I didnt attend too much and hurt me in the end. Overall, he's an approachable guy.
The class is very boring. It is worth very little points. A lot of pop quizzes, papers are easy. Midterm and final very hard. He is not helpful at all. Grades too hard.

idk why people complain about this guy. sure the class is hard, but overall he is a good teacher. getting a B (missed quizzes but made it up with extra credit). the papers are not difficult to write, i got As or Bs and again i rarely went to class. people just need to try harder.

Not a good prof at all. He's rude and arrogant. He thinks every is a theatre major so he expects all of the papers to be perfect. I went to every class, studied for extra exam, and tried my hardest on the papers and I have a C in the class. I had D's on both papers. Hes a hard grader and his study guides for mid terms dont help at all. RUDE PERSON!
He is tough but go to class and go to office hours and you will do well.
I didnt read any of the plays and got a B in the class, but I took down a lot of notes from his lectures and spark noted some plays. Do well on his papers and you'll do decent in class.
Abarbanel's class will be a breeze if you're good at reading and writing and do the assignments. Cannot stand the professor himself. He knows his theatre but is a pompous jerk.
Great class, He actually likes what he's teaching and makes it fun-funny jokes too. Just pay attention to what he says in class (what he repeats alot) and read the plays.
If you're not interested in theatre keep away from this class. Unbearably redundant!
Super entertaining professor, and makes learning fun! Not only will you learn plenty, but have a good time while doing so.

Seemed arrogant and a bit rude at first, but it's not that bad. I liked the class and he is very informative. Lots of reading but what else do you expect? It's about theatre so reading isn't going to kill you.The plays were fun to watch, but not write about since his papers require much detail and there's limited wording. Still good class to take

Read read read! This guy is funny but he is doesn't play around when he means "this is not an easy class". He is a tough grader and sticks to his point system, if he is nice he will have a slight curve, SLIGHT! take a different humanities course! some plays are BORING!

He is kind of a nut, but its funny. He is serious business when it comes to what you need to know. Read the plays and you will get an A. There are a lot of plays and a lot of them are long and boring though. If you dont wanna read, dont take the class! its one play a week for the whole semester

The professor knows his stuff. This class is not hard at all unless you don't read or don't attend class. The plays arent too difficult to read and he goes over it in class and helps you understand it. I had no prior interest in this, but now I do because I learned a lot. Quizzes and tests are a bit detailed but that's to test if you actually read.

Proffesor Abarbanel is one of the best I've had over my 4 years. He is very clear, funny, grades quickly, and follows the syllabus. He is experienced and gives great info and fun facts about theatre. He has greatly enhanced my love and interest in the subject. Just read the plays and go to class and you should get an A! GREAT class and GREAT prof!

This is a very easy class if you just read the plays and PAY ATTENTION during the lectures.  He tells you what to write down/what not to write down.  SUPER SUPER easy if you read and pay attention you'll get an A

Must know for this teacher: 1.Write down anything thats on the bored(it will be on test)2.He goes over the summary of yesterday everymorning, just highlight what he says(that will be on the test) 3. Tests on play readings will usually be on characters so read a character analysis online it will be worth the time.

he is a hard teacher. His TESTS are so hard BECAUSE they are very detail. there is a lot of reading, so don't take this class if don't have too. the teacher is also an ass. he is not very helpful. PLEASE DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS WITH THIS TEACHER!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
No Comments

Difficult tests and quizes since they go so far in depth of the material. Large amounts of readings throughout the year. He is seriously a harder grader than most English teachers. Don't take unless you have to for your major.

Awesome professor!!! He is one of the best professors I ever had. He is very helpful. He will go out of his way to help you out. To bad he will be gone after the summer 09 semesters. Good luck Achrati!!!
a very good teacher, I value the year I spent under his instruction highly
HE IS AWESOME!!!Great professor and great person!
He is pretty easy, I only missed a couple of classes and got B's on the midterm and final but I ended up with an A in the class because i did the homework and usually showed up.

Pretty easy. His directions are sometimes confusing...pay attention. Don't fall behind if you're not a native speaker. He will slow down during class if you're having trouble. Some people tend to be really disrespectful though. Good class overall. Easy final and midterm! I'm almost sure that everyone got either an A or B..nothing less!!
Pretty easy. Cares about his students learning arabic and slows the pace of the class to make sure everyone gets it. Attendance is mandatory.
He is so Funny and so cool! Just participate and ask questions if you don't get something! Highly Recommended!
Very knowledgeable and passionate, papers were not difficult even though they were in a new style, fair grader.

She was pretty good, she would always be available either in zoom or in person. She gives good detailed feedback as well as great structure in her class. Sometimes she does not give clear feedback in order to not make the same mistake again but other than that, she was a really good professor.

reviews.comment: As some others are saying, this class is for serious students only. It seriously felt like an ivy league course. Prof. Acharya's teaching methods are not common but if you go to class and pay attention he will make sure the concepts are clear to you. Definitely got my $'s worth out of this class.

reviews.comment: Brlliant Teacher/Passionate&GoodIntention. You want an A,do not take this clas. In order to get an A,you must study and prepare for the Exams. That does not happen in this class. Exam 1+2,possible to get both 100%. But for Exam3,impossible. You can't prepare. What is taught is not on Exam3. Will spend 4 days trying 2 find duplicates. Will not find.

I took both of his classes, and got A's.  20% of the time you learn conceptsformulas that are useful for the exams. WARNING: Exams are not easy, but if you go to class and take notes you should be fine. The other 80% of the time, he discusses what no other professors do; the real world and how the markets are set up to be unfair.

He is a good professor, make sure you understand your notes and reference the book when you need to. Also go to his office hours, he is willing to help. The first 2 exams where okay. The 3rd exam was hard.

Really??? He is teaching options and futures??? Really ... Maybe he is well achieved academically , but he cannot teach. He goes around and around and doesn't explain what he is supposed to. If I wanted to learn about this subject , I am better off in buying a book and studying myself than paying UIC for this useless course.

Acharya's class IS difficult, but, some of the reviews are a bit over the top. He enjoys talking about his work & he does have an accent but he is willing to assist you if u are struggling with the material. The book for this course is a grad level book so much of the difficulty comes from the subject.  This course is for SERIOUS students ONLY!

Professor Acharya is amazing. He has taught at NYU, worked at the Fed and published articles warning of the financial crisis (years in advance). His classes are excellent. I took both 415 and 416 this fall and learned a great deal. If you're not a serious and well prepared student, don't take his courses. Otherwise you'll drop and complain here.

I have never expected in my life to actually rate a professor on a website. But I will make this only one exception for God's sake. Horrible professor, perhaps the worst I have encountered. Difficult material without clarity to back it up. Nearly no problems to practice. Let me put it this way, No connection in class will destroy you.

Class was challenging, but I learned a lot. Tests are posted online and due the next day, form study groups because they will take hours to complete. The project wasnt bad. You won't use the book in class but you will need it for the test. He does not spoonfeed you, great learning experience  is you want a challenge

Professor Acharya is a very interesting and smart professor. He gives you the  knowledge&thinking skills for the real world and goes deeply beyond the textbook material. I do not recommend him.
This guys shouldn't be teaching, he needs to be kicked out of the university. Just a terrible professor.
