The final is 200 and worth 33% of your grade. I highly recommend you to make flash cards of the quizzes weekly so that when you take the final you don't need to make flash cards by they are done.

This class had two teachers. McGinley taught the second half, can sometimes become monotone in her lectures, but they are very specific! Her exam questions come directly from the lectures and in the beginning of each lecture she will let you know what you need to know by the end of it
Look if you truly care about finance, this is the guy to take. Akbas truly knows what he's talking about and his teaching will
Never answered my questions or provided proper help for exams.

I normally get A's when it comes to school because I ask a lot of questions and make sure I don't fall behind in class, but any time I asked him a question he always told me to study more rather than answer my question. Even when we started math problems in class we'd never finish them and he'd say that they would be on the exam.

I took both FIN 310/421, and these courses changed my perspective on finance. Despite being challenging, I truly enjoyed attending and learning. The material was highly applicable, helping me secure my internship/job. I highly recommend this professor to anyone wanting a deeper, real-world understanding of finance. Just be ready to put in the work!

Good lecturer. Small % of grade dependent on participation, but attendance not mandatory. However, missing out on lectures will make things confusing. Definitely attend the lectures to understand the material better. His midterm and final exams are difficult but if you show up to class regularly and understand the material, you should do well.

Great professor! He explains tough concepts really well and encourages students to ask questions, no matter how "basic" it is. Attendance isn't graded but if you don't come to class, it'll be hard to pass. Exams are difficult, but he prepares you well for them. Around 5 group projects with people you choose. Good sense of humor too.

10/10 professor but exams are crazy difficult, multiple choice questions are usually selected from the question packets he gives you to prepare after every chapter but FRQ is another story. Sorry but wouldn't take again, exams are too crazy. Get ready to pray for a good score after every exam.

The class wasn't too hard, but is slightly challenging. He does a great job of interacting with students in lectures. He generally covers all of the info need to succeed in the class. Would recommend.

Good professor at UIC and it is not an easy A course.
This is what a good professor does, "he is not helping you he is guiding you through the course. 
better find a good team for sure, hard exam but worthwhile.
By the way, he is also willing to help you with your future career!!!

His passion for finance bleeds through his teaching methodology; he genuinely wants each and every one of us to learn. He dumbs down financial concepts to everyday activities and in multiple different ways which I never thought was possible. I sit through class attentively listening for 50 minutes straight.
Class isn't really difficult. If you show up for every lecture and ask questions then you will do great. The mock exams are also super helpful. He's very funny so that's always a plus.

Professor Akbas is great! He is passionate about what he teaches and always invites students to ask questions if they don't understand something. The course is not an easy A, you'll have to study. But mock exams are helpful. His lectures are great and he's a funny guy too. The 50 minutes goes by pretty quickly.
Worst teacher at UIC, don't take unless you want to be miserable. He doesn't respond to emails, refuses to help you and puts random stuff on the exam that wasn't covered in class

Professor Akbas is a very knowledagble man who does a great job teaching Finance. What differentiates him from others is that he does a great job making sure you understand the concept, not just the calculations. His case studies and exams are a little hard but everything is fair and will help you learn alot about finance.

I highly suggest taking him. When we went from in-person class to online due to the pandemic, he was extremely helpful and understanding. He was always willing to help and his exams were extremely fair based on what he taught in the course. 10/10 would take him again.

If you're a finance major, I would definitely recommend taking him if you want to actually learn something that you can use in the real world. Yes, his exams can be challenging, but it shouldn't be too tough as long as you're paying attention to his lectures and actually solving the case studies. He only teaches in the Spring, so plan accordingly!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: By far the best Finance professor at UIC. Started off by taking him for FIN 310 & I loved his lectures so much that I decided to take his FIN 494 class as well. He really breaks down concepts in a way that everyone can understand. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you can see everyone attends anyway because lectures are amazing! Study for the exams!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Took him last semester and he teaches you concepts beyond finance. He changes the way how you think in terms of business. Class was great - lectures are very interesting and he always makes sure everyone is one the same page. Case studies are super hard, but you learn a lot from them! Exams are ok, but hey.. its college not high school.

I am not sure if he will ever teach FIN494-Business Investment Valuation again, but his class was super useful for business valuation. He makes sure everyone understands the lecture before moving on. He is very accessible after class if you need help. Very nice guy. Lots of tough case analysis, so make sure you pick the right group!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Students complain that FIN310 is hard, with this guy? No. Just focus in class and do the work. Great lectures and you for sure will get at least a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Loved him. He really likes what he does and is very passionate. Graded the case studies very fairly, midterm and final were easy because of the mock exams he gave. He also gives practice questions after every chapter. No book required. Very nice and helpful too. Great guy and enjoyed the class

Quite simply, guys great. Very enthusiastic in teaching and explains topics down to the simplest idea. Will redo topics if one person requests it with no fuss. One of very few professors that tie the class into how the real world is aka "In the real world your boss wants an answer and won't limit you from using a TI-84 calculator". Would take again

Excellent professor!Clear explanations,helpful notes.She's nice and helpful during office hours.Homework is hard but prepares you for the quizzes and exams.The class is very interesting and well-organized!Highly recommend.
poor teaching
She can be nice, her lectures are perfect but exams are HARD, Sorry no partial credit. Study from the book, class problems, and homeworks.
he is bright.
great

He was our Lab Coordinator. He covered for our TA for 4-5 weeks. He was helpful a lot (had handouts and explanations of all kinds). Although he was kind of strict with safety rules, it was all for us, and he knew what he was doing. Anyway, I totally advise him...
very smart and helps a lot.

Definitely was hot on day 1 BUT his good looks were overshadowed by his inability to teach the material! He was all over the place! Very unorganized, which made learning harder for me. He needed to do more examples! He just did proofs and definitions the WHOLE TIME! I wouldnt recommend attending lectures just do the hw and show up for the tests.

Great Teacher.  Loved his 'artistic' drawings.  Just an overall great guy to get to know.  Wished I had done better in that class, but it was my fault for not taking advantage of his helpfulness. He's able to talk to his students like a friend.  Yep, he's a pretty good friend.
Excellent teacher. Very clear, totally knows what he is talking about, encouraging and extremely helpful. One of the most pleasant people in the department.
Best & Nicest Math Teacher Ever. He is very intelligent, explains everything very clearly/concisely and is very cordial. Also looks and sounds exactly like David Boreanaz when he was younger :)
Great teacher, definitely one of my favorites at UIC. Teaches very well. if you go to class everyday and listen, you will do well.

The man knows his stuff, no doubt about it, but at times he seemed to be all over the place. You could tell that he just got done with his PhD as he seemed to be teaching in research mode- jumping from topic to topic. Helpful though and exams were pretty straight-forward too.
Very helpful, great professor. He's very good at helping to see topics from a different/non-traditional angle.
Very helpful, intelligent, clear. He certainly knows what he is doing, and he encourages you to come in for help if you're lost. Take him if you have a chance.

I am so confused by the negative review. He is extremely understanding of personal issues that may get in the way of your ability to perform well. He will help you and be lenient on grading if you express your difficulties. Very very kind and easy to talk to, also doesn't seem to care about attendance much either if you communicate!

Professor Twaddle was the go to professor to reach out to in the studio and he was always there to help. He also was very understanding when accidents happened and would often take it into account when grading. There are group projects at the end, but he let us pick our partners. The class is tiring, but not due to the prof. Everyone stays late.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Alex was a great professor, he's so supportive and gives good feedback. He's also really helpful and assisted me with some problem-solving throughout my projects, and he truly does value the work and effort that is put into not only the final pieces but the whole process. Alex is all around just a positive guy who will always have your back.

My biggest issue with Professor Twaddle is that he does not recognize any work you put in. Two students and I came in 4+ days working on our final project putting in hours outside of class and working very hard, just for him to talk very negative about it in the final critique without saying a single nice thing. No time to finish projects in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Loved Professor Rico. The MOST chill Professor I've ever had. Made long classes really enjoyable and was very easy to talk with and have a good convo. It's almost impossible to do bad in his class and he is more than willing to give extensions if u put the smallest bit of effort as a student. Great dude.
Fun to talk too. Super lenient with deadlines and grading. Probably the most fun I've had in an English class in a while. Definitely recommended.

He is the best English professor/teacher I have ever had. He cares about every student, offering help whenever needed (extremely understanding of LOAs and other accommodations), and gives many extensions. He is a lenient grader as long as you put in the work. He makes every class interesting with his sarcastic humor and tangent class discussions.

Definitely would recommend taking English with Professor Rico. He's very easy-going and flexible with deadlines. Participate in class and keep up with the readings which he provides. He's sarcastic in a funny way so there's never a dull moment. The coursework is relatively straightforward. Just show up to class with an open mind!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Don't take his class, sorry about all the other comments but we're definitely his fav…. Wouldn't recommend taking this class, there are better professors out there than him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof Rico is the best English teacher/prof I have ever had. He is super chill, funny, and understanding. His syllabus is helpful to keep track of dates and deadlines. He is very communicative on email, so if there are any cancellations of class, we will know asap. Prof Rico gives great feedback for each writing assignment and is a lenient grader.

If you have the chance to take Prof. Rico do it ! The coursework was very lenient and maintainable. Attendance is graded, he accepts extensions and overall is one of the best professors I had. There is readings throughout the course but its quite easy to get through. I would definitely retake him if I had the chance.

He was a really easy-going Professor and literally if you show up to class he gives plenty of time to work on any essays or projects. He is really funny and cares about his students. He gives extensions when asked and is very flexible. The work is not hard and he doesn't force you to talk in class, so a really easy A.

Awesome professor! Three writing projects due over the course of 15 weeks. Easy stuff. Was very relaxed when it came to due dates if you needed it and talked with him. No exams or quiz. Just brief posts on blackboard about the news and a few journal posts. Would take him again for a different class if I could!

He is one of the best professors at UIC. He has clear grading criteria and gives extensions easily on 24hr prior notice. He cares about every student individually. If you submit the assignment after the deadline no points are deducted if you keep him informed. He is a real gem!

The best professor in UIC English department. He gave a homework every week but it was ok for me. Also, his grading was not tough so if you participate well in class and submit your paper in time, you can easily get an A.
He is very considering, however, if you do ask for extensions for each assignment he will be strict about them. He is so hilarious. If you listen to what he wants it will be an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He's a great professor. He's understanding of everything as long as you talk to him. Class is also fun and he tries to make the most out of it. Would definitely take him again if I ever get the chance.

Amazing teacher, hilarious fun class I would 10000000% take his class again def the best teacher Ive ever had chill dude understands circumstances 100% recommend taking him. Easy A if you do your work while enjoying the best lectures at UIC
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He's so funny and one of the best teachers I've had. Definite recommend, you'll love the class and his personality.
His class for Understanding Literature was extremely easy and the professor cares about his students a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Al is a great professor. He is understanding and has a passion for what he does.

I liked this guy. I showed up to every lecture and I got below the average on both quizzes. His quizzes were short answer and kind of difficult. I felt like the TAs were the problem with this course when I took it. This professor was very approachable. I earned less than half or around half the points in the course and I still passed, nice curve.

I can't even begin to explain how frustrating his class is. Obviously there is something wrong if the class average is like 40%. Just avoid him if you have to take econ121. Honestly up there as the worst class I've taken at UIC. Nice guy as a person just horrible at teaching.

This guy knows what he is talking about and he explains everything very clearly. He makes sure his students understand the material, instead of memorizing it. He does have an accent just like most people in this country. I haven't had any problems understanding him.

Economy seems to be all common sense, but it is not as easy as one might think. Overall, the professor did his best to explain the material - gave useful examples and was always concerned about the class understanding the subject. I did not have a problem with his accent.  He has a great sense of humor! Good professor.

Spare yourselves, this guy is a joke. He tries but his accent is ridiculous once he gets on a tangent. He does nothing to really engage you either. He knows his stuff but good luck learning anything. Ive been struggling all semester and Im failing. Save your money.
Take this class with him, if only for the jokes. This guy has a career in comedy, if the whole economics thing doesn't work out.

He does have an accent but it is still easy to understand him.  He's really nice and has good examples to help you understand the concepts.  If you go to class and do the homework, it's very easy to get a good grade.

He's really not that bad. Don't go to class, just study the book and the study guide book. Sample exams are NOTHING like actual exams. Hard to pay attention for 2 hours so you'll end up not going but make sure you study the book.

Very difficult course. Only two exams, and required hmwk problems worth very low points. Attendance not mandatory but he counts it towards your grade at the end of the semester. Moderately hard material, but study guides were no where near the actual exams given in class. Okay guy, but tough teacher.

I never went to class because it was 6pm-8:30pm so it's hard to rate him fairly.  But he was almost impossible to understand.  His Belgian accent is ridiculous.  You need the book for homework.  There was a midterm and a final.  He's a nice guy, but I would say try looking around before settling with him.

His accent isn't really that bad, and he's actually pretty funny. He makes an effort to make himself available, but sometimes gets a tad frustrated when students ask question about simpler concepts. You definitely have to go to class and pay attention, but there's an ENORMOUS curve so if you get lower than a B you probably didn't do any work

He is a nice guy, but it is  very hard to pay attention in his class especially with his accent. His way of grabbing students' attention is poor and the TA does not help. You have to go to class and read the book. His sample exams are not too bad compared to the test. If you really like econ take it with him, otherwise switch!!! (ECON 218)
Take notes on the book and read the book. Only way your getting an A

The man knows his stuff but he doesn't use Blackboard, power points, or any form of tech for the class. He relays a lot of information in a short amount of time by drawing graphs. He doesn't give you a bottom line for topics and often didn't make clearly conclusive statements. Advice: read the book, pay attention, and write down EVERYTHING he says.

Please save yourself the trouble and enroll with another professor. It is not for lack of interest; I love economics. I've gotten A's in all of my other econ courses. But this guy gave me the first and only C I've ever received at UIC.

Fairly decent class. His accent isnt as bad as people think it is, hes extremely generous on his curves, and its VERY possible to get an A. Stay on top of your homework, and make sure you always get it in on time, show up to lecture with some redbull and kick back and soak in information and ull be good

I don't know what everyone is talking about but his accent is not that thick at all. His english is very good actually. He is an awesome teacher, very nice, and really funny! If you want an A it is totally possible.

Materials are not easy but he grades with a huge curve. Go to his office and he will help you alot better than in lecture. The text book is a must,exams are mostly based on the book.2 quizes, 2 exams (1 midtern, 1 final), and 4-5 special HW's.If your TA is a good one, the TA will help you with your HW's so be friendly to your TA.lol

Class is very dry and boring. I went to class and I could not understand anything because of his accent. I felt like all he did was draw the same supply and demand graph over and over again the whole semester. The tests were extremely hard even though they were multiple choice. I suggest not taking this class.
Teaches straight out of the book, easy class. Bad accent but if you sit up front he's entirely understandable. Friendly to approach but the class material is dry.

Class was extremely useless. Lectures did not help, as I attended all besides one. Mr. Akarca would only teach supply and demand curves in a strong thick accent. Sturdy the book the book avoid lectures as discussion section was just as useless as Akarcas lectures.

I absolutely regret taking this class. I thought the tests were impossible & this is coming from a person that had prior knowledge of econ. There's 2 tests that constitute your entire grade & a couple homeworks that really have no impact on your grade. Please do not take this teacher. He made this subject so difficult because of his inflexibility.

I've never had such a hard time learning a subject. His voice is monotone, his accent is thick, and he teaches straight out of the book. Reading the book can only take you so far..   On the plus side, his head TA is fantastic, and he's pretty funny.

Look. The guy's funny, smart, and knows economics really well. I just wish he would invest (pun intended) in Rosetta Stone or attend an english-language class. It couldn't hurt. Otherwise, the class is heavily based off of the textbook. Read that and you're golden.

VERY funny guy. Its a simple class once you understand the basic concepts, which his TAs help with a LOT. I would recommend going to class though, otherwise it could get very confusing towards the end of the semester. And yes, he has a turkish accent but it's not hard to understand.
Simple class, listen to professor, he explains everything. Nice guy, and pretty funny.

Good professor, knowledgable man, funny guy. The only problem is that most of the time I couldn't understand a word coming out of his mouth. This caused me to ditch class for the last five weeks, but still managed to get an A because the class is heavily based off the textbook.
Accent...he's kind of funny

He is an awesome teahcer! He gets a little boring. Either read the book or pay attention in lecture. I had no interest in this class and thought it was going to be hard scince its macro and micro in one class  but actually he splits it up. So one semester is micro the next is macro only two exams no final. Seriously awesome curves!

great economics teacher you will learn alot from this guy. his examples are very good so pay attenetion. lol he makes very funny jokes. make sure you show up to lecture becasue he goes over everything that will be on the test. His exams are hard but he gives awesome curves.
Accent isn't even noticable after a while.  Gives monster curves. Knows his stuff

Has an accent but people that can't understand him are seriously stupid. Sit near the front. Most people don't come to lectures but he gives hints about homework and upcoming tests in lecture. A bit boring, though.
Great professor. Has accent but is not difficult to understand. Highly recommend if you want to learn...he has an extensive resume!

Wow this teacher really knows what's up, he inspired me beyond belief and deserves something for his intelligence than just teaching at UIC.  I've never met a professor who was so smart about Economics, it flowed off his tongue like second nature!
Very knowledgeable professor and his jokes are funny. If you take this professor you will definitely learn basics of econ, I had him for 130+218

I had this teacher for both Econ 130 and 218 and while I would recommend him for 130 I would NOT take him for 218. The exams are meant for everyone to fail. You would be happy getting a low C! Nice guy but he should really lay off tricking students on the exams.

I consider myself very interested in economics and theory, but I was v disenchanted  by the style of the class, the patronizing attitude he had with students, and also disagree with one of the class premises with is that the free market is the only answer, and that any constraints have a negative effect.

He is very hard to understand and it is easy to tune him out.  You need to read the book and study to get through this class.  The curve is great.  Two tests are worth 80% of your grade and the hw is the other 20.  I got a 70% on the first test and managed an A due to the curve

Personally I thought the class was VERY interesting & insightful.  The material is somewhat tough, but once you get the hang of it you'll feel great.  The book is used and helpful (at times).  The professor was awesome, I just sat in the front rows to throw off the accent.  He's realy intelligent and I assume helpful as he always offered to student

very thick accent. takes time to get used to what he's actually saying. I had him for econ 130+218, not a completely bad prof just difficult to keep awake during class. If you ask for help, he's more than happy to help you. if you attend class (and stay for 2nd half) he basicly gives away answers for the hmw. GREAT curves.overall,not completely bad
if you really want to learn and take your test with out cheating you will love his class! he is a great prof., he helps and really understandable.

Bad teacher and bad textbook. Both are so hard to understand. The only thing he is good at is the curves cause they are like 8-15% and thats what saves most people. Only take him if you have no other choice.
he is really caring!

This prof. is impossible to understand. curves are okay, but tests are made so you can fail, no matter how much you study. the textbook is even worse to understand. the discussion sections is what helped me pass.  lectures are pointless.

No use going to class, can't understand what hes talking about...just draws a bunch of lines and graphs and goes off in tangents. Tests are REALLY hard, the book is very hard to understand too if no one is really teaching you. Strongly suggest to look for his alternative in this class.
He has a tremendously thick accent.  He often uses confusing analogies.  Best bet is do all the homework and go to discussions.

YES, he has an accent so what? Sit at the very front. Either attend lecture or read the book.  Because everything he teaches is straight out of the book. Do the homework. HUGE curve great guy, just read the book and your are all good.
That horrible Turkish accent.. makes Economics a joke.

I understood about 5% of what he say so I never take notes and always leave at the break. This didn't kill me because I study the book very thoroughly and my TA rocks. I recommend attending classes, but it isn't vital. I've missed 6-7 classes and never sat through an entire lecture and I still have the third highest grade in a class of almost 300.

DO NOT listen to the two obvious  high school dropouts below me. They will probably end up failing this class. You must attend his lectures, read the book, take good notes, and go to the review session in order to pass! I think the guy below me likes Smallville so that may suggest that he is a little "slow" if you catch my drift. STUDY HARD!
Yea i'm with that guy, this professor has a bad accent and tends to repeat the same thing over and over, using the same graph for every problem! read the book and forget about the class.

I went to his class for a two weeks and finally realized i had learned nothing at all. He's nearly impossible to understand, so I read the book and ended up with a hundred times better notes than the one he gives. My advice, ditch the lectures and just read on your own AND TAKE NOTES!!!

Hard class and hard material. He is willing to explain the material, but sometimes he still goes too fast and unclear. Tests are much harder than the practice tests, so be cautious and always do more study. However, he's very nice professor, HUGE CURVE at the end. WORK HARD to get an A or B!!
Very hard class! The guy is nice though but his accent could be difficult to understand.  He gives out some awesome curves!

Akarca definantly knows his stuff.  However this class can be very challanging.  There are only 2 tests and 5 homework assignments for a total of 75.  If You mess one up your grade is affected greatly. Overall, he is a godd professor.

He speaks with a thick accent and is thus impossible to understand. Attending lectures became pointless for me and it's impossible to learn much from the text because it's boring as hell. So it's a lose-lose situation. The class(Spring '07) average was predictably dreadful for the 1st test(which was quite tricky and tough).
never went to class. curves are great, hand in homework and read the book. should get a B or C with ease

Second time with Akarca. He's not helpful, TA review sessions are useless. Tests are hard as hell, make sure to seek tutoring help from business floor. Also, tests are nothing like the sample exam. His handwriting is bad, barely legible. Overall, a tough class to ace but curves are decent.

TOUGH CLASS.  TOUGH EXAMS AND HOMEWORK. YOU SHOULD DEFINETELY TAKE THIS CLASS JUST FOR THE CURVES BECAUSE THEY ARE AWESOME.  IF YOU ARE AN AVERAGE STUDENT YOU SHOULD GET NO LOWER THAN A C.  IF YOU STUDY HARD, NO LOWER THAN A B.  TAKE HIM!!!

Difficult class, because some of the material is kind of 'abstract'. Some of the homework problems are tricky, and he tests more on the 'basic' rather than specifics. Read the book, do the homework, attend the lectures and review sessions...and you should be able to land a B.
he is a teacher. NEED TO READ THE BOOK. Best curves ever, which make u get an A:)
He can simplify the complex topics of economics.  I had a new found interest in economics after his class.  He's a GREAT teacher. Although, he does have an accent, so sit in the front.
professor teaches good and curves are great.... doin't be lazy and go to lecture and read the book and u can get an A in the class

It is not easy to get a good grade in this class. His notes are very messy and illegible. The TAs are not that helpful either. The averages for exams were very low but the curves are decent. No extra credit is given, just be sure to turn in all assignments (there are not that many) and study your butt off for exams.

This professor had a good sense of humor but unless your looking for a laugh I would not take his class. He was SOO difficult to understand, very thick accent. The class in general is not difficult one but he just made it hard to follow. If your already in this class try switching or my best advice is work with the TA and study the book. Good luck
BORING! But I learned there are 137 tiles on the ceiling.
he was a great professor as long as you pay attention in lecture you're set... 2 tests 2 quizzes a few homeworks... huge curves... reveiws for quizzes and tests... pretty easy
Difficult class. Hard to understand proffesor unless you sit close to him while he lectures.  best advice: sit close and go to head ta's review sessions, especially before exams.

His class is pretty hard and are exams are even harder but if you go to classes and do your hw you can get a good grade. His curve is awesome but he expects a lot of his students which is a good thing and no matter how hard the class was i still got an A
U do have to study for that class, his handouts are just the basics (take lot's of notes on them)
No Comments
he does have a slight accent, but unlike some of the TA's and professors at UIC he's easy to understand.  I would highly recomend this class, he explains topics well
Don't take him. Tests are hard, the dude doesn't know what he's talking about.

His tests tend to be fairly tricky so u have to make sure u study. Everything he says in lecture comes straight from the book. Lectures r really boring though. The review sessions are really really helpful before quizzes and exams.

Dr. Akarca speaks broken English, which makes it hard to comprehend the lectures and he has no patience to explain the mateiral for than one time. The exams are hard! He's nice, but not a teacher material, especially at a university.
very good class... kinda hard to understand but you get used to it.... his tests are pretty hard but he curves too... go to the extra reviews... they help a lot
welcoming personality
He was a great professor... he has huge curves: 2 tests two quizes a few homeworks and thats it.. there's a review session the TAz do.. very helpful.. overall easy class
what is the curve in his class????

Can not understand him at all! Going to his lectures are pointless. Tests are hard.  There is no way to improve in the class because there are only 76 possible points.  I failed a homework and the midterm and with the curve I'm getting a C.  The curve is the only good thing about the class.
He is pretty good. Strong accent but understandable. He is also very funny.
I liked this teacher! He cracked funny jokes, during class and explained the material well. He also curves all of his exams. They are hard but its a huge curve. Take him, its worth it.
No Comments

Well, I went to class, read the book and studied, and still managed to fail my midterm!  we'll see about the final.  he's a nice guy, but does a poor job with teaching.  does not expain stuff thoroughly, goes fast, and does not review well for exams.  and since the final and midterm are worth most o

the guy is funny but his teaching is boring and not helpful. he has a turkish accent, u need to paid close attention or u'll be totally lost. alot of graphs, graphs. da good news, he has a  nice curve. i got a "C" by just doing the assignments(5) and going over my notes w/o doing any major reading.

He is a funny guy, but his turkish accent is really thick.  The class definately didn't hold my interest, and I wouldn't take it again.  I only recommend this class for business majors not just a blow off social science.

Don't get me wrong, he's a VERY nice man, but cannot relate the material to students. My bro and I both had him and the experience was negative. He gives like 2 major tests so the pressure is on to do well...no extra credit or anything like that.

Micro & macro in 1 semester is hard. He went thru the class so fast & has illegible notes. He was MEAN, he would make fun of students who asked "stupid ?'s" My TA wasn't helpful. I hated his grading system, 1 wrong answer = 1% off your grade
Proffessor's very funny, helpful, fun class-take it!!!
Very funny. clear, simple explanations.

does not know to teach. toughest class I have ever taken.
Has a bad teaching style. Literally can't understand anything in his class. Don't take the course.
He is THE WORST professor I've ever meet. No way you can understand his lecture. He has a horrible taste of jokes and don't speak loud enough. THE WORST.

There was no point in going to class. I didn't feel like I was learning anything, I felt better about studying on my own than attending class. Homework was very different from what he went over in lecture. The midterm and final were based on the homeworks, so I just studied those. And yes, there was a huge curve at the end.

Literally got nothing out of going to class. Do the homework and study the solutions - midterm and final based off these. Tough grading by him and the TA, so be ready to fight for points. Huge curve at the end!

reviews.comment: He's a good professor, a lot can be learned from him. Be prepared to put in a lot of work.

She was a great professor. The class itself was very hard and had a lot of math, but she did a great job of explaining everything. Gives you two options for grading, one where attendance counts and one where it doesn't. If you're not good at math, go to the lectures

Professor Schuck was fantastic; her lectures were very interesting and engaging. There are two online exams and one paper, which are easy if you take good notes. She cares for and checks in with her students before the lecture starts. If you can take a class with Professor Schuck, do it!
There are many required readings that the test is based on. The lectures can be interesting and it's two tests with a final paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Amie is one of the best professors Ive had. Attendance really doesnt matter (even in discussion sections). Very lax with tests. Allows use of any materials, (even chat gpt) on tests. its a very easy class as long as you simply do the work. I didnt even look at the textbook ever and I passed the class with a B. the only work is tests and discussions

This is for CLJ 101. Easy class, highly recommend, textbook is provided online, attendance is only mandatory for discussions. We had 4 exams which are open note so reading the book helps. Professor Schuck made the class interesting because she has a great sense of humor through the stories she tells.

A funny professor, she understands the struggles of college students, and their "dark parts", as in knowing you jaywalk on campus and making jokes about everyone doing it, and makes the lectures interesting by adding real life stories and jokes. Exams are open note so there's no way you should fail, unless you skip lecture on the wrong day.
Very good professor to take.

Genuinely one of the easiest classes I have ever taken. Professor is funny and makes each lecture interesting.  No homework,no textbooks,no quizzes all you gotta do is show up for attendance. There are only 2 exams in the entire semester and all you gotta do is answer 2 short essay questions which she posts all the materials you need on blackboard.

I love her. Made the attendance optional since she still had all the asynchronous materials available. Only needed to show up for exams. All assignments are there if you wanted extra practice. Tests were open notes and she curved it. She was really encouraging and overall doesn't try to bring you down by throwing hard problems at you.

This was an asynchronous, go at your own pace, class which I didn't mind but definitely did not learn as much as I could or would have, had it been traditionally synchronous. She posted weekly video lectures where you can follow along with the book. 10 quizzes, you can take them as many times as you need, plus 4 worksheets. Pretty straight forward!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of my favorite courses. It was very easy with only a couple lectures and discussion posts. Many notes to take, however they really help with the exams which were also very fair. She made the course very interesting by allowing us to engage and share our opinions.

I think those that are good at stats will do great at it and find it easy but this is an online class for me because of COVID and I've never taken stats so I struggle and she offers no help except for her required lecture slides and mini videos. i don't learn that way so she might not be the worst for some people. I did not like how she handled it!

Professor Schuck's really cool. Originally the class consisted of an attendance grade, a midterm, and a final group video project. The pandemic resulted in an alternate final for my class, but be prepared for a group project if you take this class in-person. She's super helpful, and truly cares about the success of her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: It was an easy A for me because I'm good at statistics, but the class was so boring with mandatory attendance. You have a long time to complete the homework, but its super long to do in one sitting which is about 10 hours long. Her teaching really wasn't that good unless it was 1 on 1, but the textbook did a really good job at explaining everything
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Amie knows that this class can be difficult but she tries to make it easier with her humor and real-life examples. You will definitely need the book, any edition will do. Extra credit opportunities are given. The homework cannot be done last minute. Get it checked with your assigned TA before turning it. Notes can used for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class is a super easy gen ed. Only 3 extremely easy HW assignments, 2 group debates, and some in class work. No tests, no textbook. Everything is a group grade, so if you are not in class you still get credit for the in class work as long as someone in your group is there. She is a super sweet professor and makes the class enjoyable.

If you're go with numbers you'll be fine. She cares about students understanding the material so speak up and she'll gladly help you. Tests are open note, but you need to understand the material before hand. She curves the grade because she understands that it is difficult for students. The easiest A of my college career and made me love math more.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: If you are good at basic algebra, can organize your numbers and work neatly, then you should do very well. Tests and quizzes are open note, understand the concepts and know how to calculate all the statistics. Homework isn't so bad. She is very helpful and willing to answer any questions and wants you to do well. Overall an easy intro stats class.

Lectures can be a bit boring, but the great thing is that she posts the slides online and on top of that she's very helpful and cares a lot about her students. Really study for her exams and you'll do great!
Very nice. Class is hard and boring but she makes it as interesting as possible. I wouldn't have wanted to take it with anyone else.

Professor Schuck unfortunately teaches a couple very boring classes, but it is clear that she is passionate about her work. She was extremely helpful to me when I was trying to get credit for an internship, and is pretty funny as well.

She teaches statistics so the class will probably be difficult for many, as it was for me.  However she is extremely helpful and is always willing to help students understand the material.  She is funny and does her best to keep us awake.

Dr. Schuck tries to make the material clear but sometimes fails at doing so. She seems to forget that statistics is hard and most students do not understand and thus doesn't explain things as thoroughly as she should at first, but she eventually goes back and clarifies. It is a hard class but she wants her students to do well and it shows.

(Same as Soc 231) Teaches as if we are criminologists ourselves, however she is very helpful and very nice. She did say she doesn't normally teach CLJ 220 so I do cut her some slack. Tests are extremely hard and contain so much information. You HAVE to read or you will feel lost. Overall, she's ok.

This teacher gives out extremely hard exams! You can literally study your butt off and all you can hope for is a good grade but it's so hard to get it! I dropped her class. I suggest to take her only if you're majoring in Criminology, other than that, NO WAY! By the way, you NEED the book.
Read the book and attend class! Any question be sure to ask. Dr. Schuck is very helpful and very clear in her presentation of the material.

Stats is a very hard class in general, but she had clear explanations.  However, beware:  Her second test is harder, and having part of the test open book or take-home will not make it easier (i took it twice, unfortunately).
It was a semi difficult class, but she made it fun and intersting.

Incredibly boring lectures. Everything he does is straight from the textbook, and attendance isn't mandatory so you could just use the textbook and be fine. He gives very little partial credit. Exams and quizzes are open book open note, and he does post some notes on blackboard but they're just textbook examples.

Attendance is completely mandatory unless if you have a friend that always shows up to class since he never posts notes. His notes are extremely vital to passing the class since homework problems will be the same or exam problems will be the same. Labs can drag sometimes but the actual labwork and reports are kept easy. Very harsh grader.

Professor Khodadoust was one of my favorites. He is an extremely tough grader, so good luck getting partial credit. The class was open book and open notes so use your resources. Labs are easy, homework straight forward, use your notes from lecture. He did not upload lecture notes either, so attend class.
Attend and take notes and everything is easy

Attendance is important because he only writes his lectures on the board. Notes are very helpful for homework. The quizzes are based off the homework and the tests are based off the quizzes. He lets you used your notes and book during quizzes. You can only use the book during tests but you can make notes throughout the book to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Not as bad as others make him to be. It is a difficult course but he tries his best to make it engaging. If you come to class, take notes and try he will notice the effort and be likable. He is a very knowledgeable Professor and delivers well thought out explanations.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Good luck. He cat fishes on half of his quizzes and his exams are tough. He is very petty with partial credit so good luck getting a decent grade unless you go full Albert Einstein. reviews.comment: Easily the worst teacher in all of uic. His exams and quizzes beyond insane and is nothing compared to the notes and hw. Grades extremely tough so if u get the answer right but not the work you still get the answer wrong. Gives little no to partial credit on quizzes/exams. Hes beyond boring and rants. Thank god in heaven this class is over with.

Boring lectures, but notes are helpful for quizzes. Lab reports are short, but adds up to the grade, make sure you do well. Hard and very long exams, but curves at the end. Unfortunately, there's no other choice for this class, but wouldn't take him again.

He was not that bad. his lecture are boring, but you have to attend otherwise you will get a low score on quizzes. Make you sure you take good notes because most of the quizzes and exam are based on his notes. Make sure u read the book before the exam dont expect an easy exam with an open book . Do well on lab report, it will help you.

He grades really harshly, no partial credit given at all. Also, if you get everything right on a quiz/test you will only get half the points. The other half is for you to go full Isaac Newton on the question. I mean WTH its only 1 more D. its not like if you read this you can run away from the prof. He is the only one that teaches it, change t univ

He has to like you in order to get an A , if he doesnt like you then C will be your grade Make sure you attend all of his class and show interest in the material he is teaching plus pay attention to class His exams is fair compare to the amount of time he spends in class teaching the material ! He is a good professor

Realistically if you take this class and do what you are supposed to do, you will pass with no issues. She just does not respond to emails promptly or without follow up. No grades were in until the final grades were posted so you have no idea how you are doing. No feedback on your work. Take another prof if you can, but you'll be fine if you can't.

The class is basically students lecturing. Attendance on zoom is mandatory, camera needs to be on all the time. She's sweet and she means well for her students. A lot of participation, need to participate almost every class for S credit.

I was on my way to campus, so I didn't turn on my camera until I got there, and I messaged her on Zoom chat about it. Then, she kicked me out of the meeting. When I returned to campus, I logged back into the meeting, but she didn't let me in. She never let me in for the rest of the class. She never responds to emails.

Prof Amiri is a sweet lady, but she's completely incompetent when it comes to technology. She has not set up Blackboard correctly at all, which made finding announcements, information about papers, and articles very hard to find. She can't even set up a submission link for the midterm or final paper. She is also terrible at responding to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I do warn you, he does not respect women designers and puts them down. He is sexist and cares about his self-image. He isn't a designer but rather an artist who cares about his feelings. Feelings are not facts but rather a personal thing. Amir is a great professor! He loves what he does and is ready to share some of his own work. He gives back great feedback and is always helpful. Highly recommend.

Amir is an excellent professor that takes a genuine interest in his students and their design career at UIC. Class critiques can be long, but they are exceptionally thorough and useful. Highly recommended.
Great Professor! She is very nice, gives good feedback, and everything is in the syllabus, very organized as well. Would've taken her class again if I could!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Take any course taught by Dr. Bohne if you get the chance! She is so beyond sweet, funny, and engaging. She genuinely loves the material she teaches and is super great about having group discussion. Assignments are not hard, they're designed around everything taught in class and she gives a lot of freedom in choosing topics. Amazing professor!!!

Super cool, really fun, and one of the best 8 am classes I've ever taken. She is very insightful and made the readings fun even if it was a re-read for you. The material is laid out early in the semester, and she is willing to work with you if you communicate. Thumbs up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: no idea how she doesn't have more reviews! one of the most insightful, engaging, and approachable professors i've ever had. lectures were very free-flowing so conversation came naturally n made for a fantastic learning environment. take advantage of the office hours and lectures, you won't regret it!

She is an amazing professor with an awesome sense of humor. Some of what we read was very difficult and downright boring at times but she always managed to make it interesting and fun to learn about. Her papers aren't too difficult and they keep you in the moment and you'll always feel happy and excited when you enter her classroom!

I love Professor Bohne, she is so caring and kind and is always there when you need her. There are 4 writing assignments and some reading as well as group discussion, but it is fairly easy and you would gain a lot from it. If i could take her again, I would in a heart beat. So I recommend talking her for english 160.
One of the best professors I have ever worked with

Dr. Bohne is a great professor who cares about her students inside the classroom and outside. You have up to four excused absences without an explanation. She always gives great feedback and encourages her students to communicate with her for any help. Hands down an amazing professor and human being.
Sweetest teacher I've ever had. She is very understanding and lenient. If you do your work in time you will receive any easy A. I would definitely take her again if I could.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I would definitely take another class of hers if I had the opportunity. She's taught at other universities before, but its her first time being a professor at UIC. She's really nice and understanding all you have to do is do her work and participate. She is lenient on coming late and tries not to give us a hard time. She loves questions.
Loved her class was very relaxed and fun.

The class was pretty easy...some of the homework can be confusing but Professor Jandek does make it easier if you email her about it. Attendance points are given and make up a good portion of your grade, so do not miss out on easy points.

Professor Jandek is amazing if you want to learn about something deep and insightful regarding to her careers and the kinesiology subject. However her exam are so god damn hard. It's surface level questions with answers that all make sense but is mainly the critical details that make them different. Love her but scared of her as well LOL

Jandek is very knowledgeable with her material given her experience in athletic training and she shares stories that help you tie in the material that is being taught in class. Be ready to participate in class she values class interaction and students sharing their knowledge. Super friendly and funny definitely would take her class again.

I had Jandek for 261 and 331. For 261 it was a bit of s struggle but for 331 it was a different game. She can explain the material better. I was wary about taking her but so glad that I did because I learned so much. She wants her students to succeed. She is REASONABLE and nice to talk to and will help you in any way she can. Take her for lab part

Jandek seemed like an okay clinical instructor, but she really can't teach using lectures. She did a good job teaching stuff with demonstrations but everything else was all over the place. When the class was confused on something, she was too (which didn't really help us understand what's going on). Also she clearly favorited like 4 students.

Jandek is a nice instructor, but her lectures are confusing and all over the place. It seems like she herself doesn't know the material and always questions herself. Her tests only cover one fourth of what you go over in class. My tip for passing the class? Study only the movement analysis, and chain reactions and go over your basic anatomy terms.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Amy is the worst professor I have ever had. She HORRIBLE at giving lectures, when you ask a question she responds with "you tell me" and her tests are impossible. All of her test have "all of the above" and "non of the above" options for almost every answer, and almost everyone i know doesn't get better than a C on the tests. AVOID IF YOU CAN!!

Fantastic teacher.  Kept the class interesting.  Her discussions and passion for the subject made the class discussions fantastic. Very fair easy grader, accepts late papers.  Will definitely be taking any other classes she teaches.

she is so great. she makes class interesting and encourages students' 2 talk in class. everyone is welcome to share opinions and pretty much everything. she is soooo nice. loved her and the class was very interesting
She's a great professor! However, her T.A.'s are misleading, boring, unorganized, inadequate and have obviously never taught anyone before.
Easy class. I got an A without even trying. The bad think about it is that I am still not sure if I learned anything ...

At first I was intimidated by the amount of reading material, but it really wasn't all that bad.  She is an excellent professor.  Take good notes and go to lecture, because the lecture material is what she looks for on the exam.  Just study the study guide given before exams, and you'll definitely get an A.

easy class...go to lecture, learn terms and comprehend the main ideas of the movies she plays in class. The exams are pretty much based on the terms so if you do the study guide the night before and memorize the terms you'll be fine. If you have a laidback TA it helps even more! I never opened the textbook and i got an A...easy blow off class

The class is easy, but she grades really hard.  Going to lecture is 20% of your grade.  I got 92, 95, and 83 on my exams, and 100 on my final paper.  I still got a "C" in the class.  She said it was because I missed most of the lectures.

ONE OF THE BEST AT UIC! SHE IS VERY EASY GOING. 3 EXAMS, NO QUIZ, 1 PROJECT (FINAL). READ THE CHAPTERS BEFORE CLASS, TAKE NOTES DURING LECT, FILL OUT THE STUDY GUILD = A+. VERY INTERESTING CLASS.  WILL TRY TO SIGN UP FOR ANOTHER CLASS WITH HER.
decent but nothing extrodinary.

she was a fun professor.  in order to pass her tests you have to do the readings, but they are not too long. i learned a lot from hr and would recommend her to everyone who is truly interested in LALS.

Aparicio is a good professor; you will learn a lot in her lectures but you must take good notes.  The tests she gives are essays but if you know the material it is doable.  The only thing that wasnt so great was the readings every week but other than that her class is tolerable.
No Comments
cool as hell

Dr. Asmussen was truly one of my favorite professors. His essays may seem overwhelming, but he makes the instructions extremely clear. His lectures were super engaging and interesting, and the texts he chose for us to read were fun! Just stay on top of work. Would totally recommend.

Would not take again. Definitely seems like a nice and interesting person outside of class. A little passive-aggressive and finds it really disrespectful if you don't face him during class. He would assign writing assignments that took various days and then not post the readings until the night before they were due.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Eh. Passive aggressive and considers it very disrespectful if you do anything other than face him with full attention. Interesting course at first but quickly fell off and became repetitive. Strict with deadlines. Will direct you to the syllabus and slides but the two never align so information outside of class is limited and in class unhelpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Great teacher. He breaks down the project into very digestible parts, making it easy to follow. Very understanding of any mistakes, the rubric is clear and concise, so that there is no mistake in grading.

very passive aggressive towards students for "not following directions". he doesn't upload the presentations from the class until that specific assignment is due. don't bother asking questions, he'll just direct you to the syllabus. basically listen to his lectures, take notes, and pray you understand the assignment.
He's pretty chill and the class was fun because you get to pick what you write about. Keep track of your absences!
goated prof ngl

Mr. Asmussen is a good at making it clear what is needed to be done by the students and in giving feedback. He also enforces strict deadlines. There are also only 6 excused absences during the course, after which your grade drops, but I believe it was set on behalf of the English department. His lectures can be boring, but there are only a few.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: honestly i thought he would have a higher rating here because i genuinely think he's a good professor. he makes his expectations and standards very clear from day 1, always willing to answer questions from students, and bonds with students. he does set plenty of tight deadlines for the research paper process but other than that he's decent lol

ENG 161 is a paper-focused class with 4 major writing projects and 6 smaller writing assignments. Each project and assignment had clear expectations and guidelines set. Professor Asmussen gives wonderful feedback for the writing projects and wants you to succeed with your writing. Putting in the work for this class will pay off!

All around good prof. He explains exactly what your task is. He is funny and very helpful when you need it. His papers are intimidating though. Best advice is to just talk to him and he'll help you out.

If you do not go to class you will not pass, you're only allowed a certain amount of absents before your final semester grade drops by a letter. not lenient with attendance. strict on late turn in assignment policy. can be a tough grader.

He prob changed his syllabus a bit because for our semester we only had about 7 really short assignments on top of the 4 major papers we had to do. If you're looking for a blow-off class then you'll have a hard time, take Baez, but if you got stuck with Asmussen it's not that bad, he's really nice and if you ask for help he'll give it to you.

This is an entirely paper based class. Youre only allowed a certain number of unexcused absences before you grade drops by a letter. The class was only the papers and nothing else, but that could be because the class changed teachers a couple of times before we ended with Professor Asmussen. An okay class, just a lot of papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Very enthusiastic about America and Texas. Assigns mountains of reading on American nationalism, then tests you on it. Feels like a high school history curriculum poorly adapted into a composition course. Actually, doesn't feel like a composition course at all.

Mr. Amussen my favorite professor at UIC. He makes learning the material interesting. Although he assigns quite a bit of homework, he gives the class many weeks to complete the assigned readings. Also, he provides great feedback on all papers, therefore he sets all of his students up to receive an A. Overall, he is an excellent professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Does way too much. Acts like he's teaching juniors in college. The content you read is very heavy. One time he expected the class to read 200 pgs in a week to have a 40 multiple choice exam the following week. Youll have something due every class. Makes it seem like ENGL is the only class you're taking. You can only miss 4 days or your grade drops.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: worst English professor I've had.

This was a required class for CLJ and it was honestly really interesting. The information can be dense but professor Muchow is extremely kind and understanding. There are weekly quizzes, 4 main assignments, and one big project at the end. Not bad for a required class!

I took Prof Muchow and I love her! I wish I could take more of her classes. We were graded on weekly online quizzes, 4/5 online assignments, & 1 presentation. She really cares for her students and helps you to understand what you are learning. I love her!

There is a long final paper due at the end of the course but you practically work on it throughout the whole semester. Her lectures were very helpful and informative, and she was open to answering any questions. She is very nice and understanding on just about everything and was a great professor overall. Would take another one of her classes.

Dr. Muchow is an amazing professor. Her class is really easy to keep up with, which I really appreciated considering the class was asynchronous. Every week there is a PowerPoint and a quiz. There are also end-of-unit assignments that but they're easy to understand (she makes each question on a different module). The book is not really needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Because classes were online covid and all, professor muchow was very open and caring for students. She's great at lecture. The material is a lot to comprehend. She doesn't give a lot of homework. We only had 4 assignments and then a mditerm and final. The midterm and final does have a lot of information that requires defining and applying material

The class is not bad, but you do have to understand the material since the midterm exam is kind of tough. Can't really complain since she gave out a lot of extra credit. Only one exam and one big assignment. I struggled on the assignment, but my TA was very lenient when it came to grading it. Overall, my experience was decent. I would recommend.

Two exams and one final paper 7 pages long. No hw besides reading. Textbook required but its free online. Class is out of 1000 points. Exam was very hard and consisted of 7 long chapters so memorize everything only way to pass. The paper is simple but you have to find your research first to make it easier. Offers one extra credit exam online.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class instructions for this class are clear. It is an easy class with occasional hurdles through assignments. Lab attendance is mandatory. Lecture attendance may vary. Make sure to do the homework lab and assignments. She is willing to give advice and help outside of class hours. Overall, great professor.
Very easy class with lots of extra credit opportunities to ensure you get A. If you're taking IDS 200, I strongly recommend you take professor Khan's class.

Professor Khan was very helpful. She wants you to pass the class. The has a lot of work since these classes are very bug but she will always make time for you. She gives you many chances, the work is actually pretty fun to do. I'd take her class every time if I had the chance.

If you're taking IDS 200, definitely take Professor Khan. The class is very straightforward; weekly labs, assignments based on the labs every couple weeks. No midterm or final. Class attendance is mandatory and checked through iClicker. Lab attendance is also mandatory. Very easy to reach through email and has accessible office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Khan is one of the best professors at UIC. She is very understanding and caring. The class is easy because she takes time to walk us through the assignments and provides resources. Countless amount of ex credit. Allows late assignments if you let her know before hand. No exams just lab assignments and other small assignemnts

The absolute best professor I've had here at UIC. IDS 200 is such an easy A if you just do the simple work and labs that are assigned, and go to class. Attendance is a huge part of your grade. Asfia is so knowledgeable and brings in guest speakers very often.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is one of the best professor at UIC. Gives you plenty of extra credits opportunity, caring and plenty of resources on Blackboard for career in MIS.
Great professor for an introductory class. She makes attendance mandatory but gives you plenty of opportunities to make up missed classes. Easy grader.
The best professor during UIC period

heavy on attendance, but plenty of chances to make up missed classes. (you get a few excused absences)
lectures have 0 correlation to lab; lectures are extremely boring. that said if you do your lab, assignments, and discussion boards there's no way you don't secure an A.
