reviews.comment: A very caring and patient teacher. You can tell that she cares about the students' well-being and wants us all to do well. The class can be a bit fast-paced, and she doesn't play when it comes to the Tarea Finales. But again, the challenge is to help you prepare for real-world interactions in class.

This class was relatively easy. A significant portion of the homework you receive can be completed in a matter of minutes for each topic. The main focus is on the partner/group projects, and the rubric and information are provided in advance. The professor is kind, and you pick up on the lectures easily over time. It's not bad, just put in effort.

There's a lot of Weekly assignments but they are pretty manageable. There's a lot of group work and projects and the class is pretty fast paced but very consistent with expected homework and assignments, since you have access to all of them from day 1. One of the few Spanish classes where I actually learned to speak consistently.

During the start of the semester, I didn't buy my Spanish book yet, and I was penalized for it. She deducted points from my attendance and claimed I wasn't there when I was. Attendance brought my grade down, but other than that, the class was alright.

She is a really great professor and love how she talks about philosophy here and really enjoyed it. There are only a couple of assignments but she does grade really late... She doesn't have exams she only has essays and there is only one group project. There is one reading exam but its open notes,
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved this class. I am a double major in Criminology & Sociology, so it was the perfect class for me. She is so engaging and fun to listen to. The papers are so well outlined that it feels so easy and fun to write them. The class is phenomenal, and I really enjoyed it so much!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Loved the lectures she really made them feel personal and made me care about the subjects. This made the essays way easier along w the understanding due dates. She often asked for feedback and made sure everyone was okay with the workload. She was not only accommodating but made the class fun and was encouraging!

I love her!! This is my second time taking a class of hers and wish I could take more. she doesn't have tests in her class just papers. A midterm paper and a final paper. sometimes shell take attendance so make sure to go regularly if you can. the only bad thing is that she is such a slow grader.
despite her not always being an engaing lecturer she tries her best to reel us I'm, I love how she brought guest speakers in to lecture also. She is understanding about due dates .

It's just a quick stop on that college highway journey. That quick stop is pretty informative and pretty easy overall. You have your essays once in a while, but no "exams." Class time passes pretty easily, an attendance is not mandatory at the lecture, although they do give you some extra credit if you do show up.

Although this course wasn't in-person, she did her best to keep students engaged. Grading consisted of 5 essays. The discussions aren't mandatory for attendance but the TA's are a great source to understand lectures and get help with essays.

Dr. Bird provides lectures & readings (long) at the beginning of the week that you will discuss with your TA. The class is in all not that difficult but I recommend that you organize your time! There are only a few assignments to be graded by, which are 2 DBs, Media Analysis, Midterm Paper (4 pages), and the Final Paper (5 pages). TA's do grades

Bird is a great prof. who: -is refreshingly UNBIASED, -teaches well, -has a nice voice and tone, -is familiar with tech., -has nice lectures Honestly, there is no drawbacks with this prof. This course has long readings, but she summarizes them. Beware of anti-cop TAs; I suggest you go with the flow and don't disagree with them.
Professor will post around 3, 10-20 minute lectures at the beginning of the week where she will read directly off the slides, providing no more insight than you would get reading them yourself.

She lectures very well. The content is very clear and she always is willing to chat one on one so you understand it more. Most of the assignments are for the discussion part of the class. There are no exams which is nice but there are two fairly long papers that are not part of the discussion. The papers are 1.5 spacing and that really hurts.

The course itself isn't difficult, but there is an absurd amount of writing you have to do. The first writing assignment was double space, but the remaining writing assignments were 1.5 spacing, which I do not understand why. Overall, I felt like I wrote a PhD thesis during the semester.
It was a very doable class. WE had a reading and two 15-minute lectures every week. We were graded on a midterm and final paper and then whatever your TA assigns you.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Bird is very flexible in the course and will give extensions! We only had 3 discussion boards for discussion class, a media essay, a midterm paper, and final paper. Very easy and doable. She's a great teacher and understand where students are coming from.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Extremely easy class. All lecture slides are on Blackboard. There's a midterm and paper that significantly affects your grade. Crucial to attend lecture for the first 7 weeks. All other assignments are given in discussion. Bird is pretty easy going and a fairly easy grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Great professor, very knowledgeable. This course consisted of a midterm exam, a final paper, and a presentation. There is a lot of readings assigned each week, but if you enjoy reading Aristotle, you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Bird is amazing, her way of teaching is great. She knows what she is doing and makes sure everyone in the class understands what she is teaching. For the most part, it is an easy class. There is no tests, but there Is a midterm paper which is in class and it is very easy, there is also a final paper which is due at the end of the semester.

She is a very good professor and knows a lot about the criminal justice system. Her lectures are filled with important information that is used for the midterm paper (40% of grade) and the final exam in-class paper (30% of grade). Overall, she is very knowledgeable and willing to help you out if you need it.

Amazing professor! Her lectures were enjoyable and they were easy to understand. She uses a lot of issues occurring today in order for us to understand. No book in this class, she makes readings accessible through blackboard. Midterm was a paper, and final was an exam.
Interesting class. Good professor. Hope she sticks around UIC.

This class was super easy but really interesting. Your grade consists of some participation points in your discussion section (like a debate and one easy presentation), a midterm paper which was fairly easy, and a final. As long as you go to her lecture explaining the final, it was easy!!
Class optional which was nice. Went to like 2 classes all semester. Kind of boring, hard to pay attention. No textbook though which was nice

This class seemed difficult at the beginning but its really not. I went to lecture probably 6 times throughout the semeter, however i never missed a discussion section. Grade consist of 2 group projects, a midterm paper, and the final exam. She really helps you on the final exam and lets you know what to focus on. She seemed nice i would recommend

Her lectures could get a bit boring and there isn't good communication between the TA's and Professor Bird. My TA seemed to be on a whole different page than her which was frustrating and made assignments more difficult. Theres no homework so whatever work you do is graded pretty harsh. Effort is necessary.

Bird is an amazing professor. If you're looking to take a CLJ class I would recommend her. My TA Shannon was also amazing!  Very caring and clarified a lot of stuff from lectures. There is a mid-term paper, which is easy once you understand the topic. Final is really easy!! I would no doubt take Prof. Bird and Shannon! Highly recommended!!!

I'm not one to enjoy Criminology, but Professor Bird has really given me an interest in the subject. reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I loved having Prof. Bird as an instructor! She does begin the class immediately but that is the only negative thing to say about her. She was a very good teacher and extremely fair. She gave assignments and readings but they were fairly easy. She does give extra credit at some point and if you talk to her after class she is so nice and supportive.

Prof. Bird is really a great addition to the CLJ dept at UIC. Her class is not one you can pass with minimal effort. The readings can be dense, yes, but if you read and voice your opinion you'll be just fine. At the end of the semester you'll feel a lot more knowledgeable than when you first began, she has so much to offer as an educator!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

Professor Jaki is very kind and compassionate with her students. The course is meant as an introduction to various drugs and facets of pharmacy classes. For this reason, it is not difficult at all. There is only one worksheet assignment per week when I took it in Fall 22.

- lot of theory / definitions. 

- spends a lot of time talking about nonsense 

- a lot of useless rigorous notes 

- maybe did 10-18 examples throughout the WHOLE semester

Calc 3 itself isn't bad, but I had to find ways to see proper examples since there wasn't enough to reference from. He also really cares about attendance and will send an email if you miss a session.

Do not take this professor! I was never able to learn from any of his lectures because he teaches so incredibly slowly, writes unnecessary information, and has basically zero good examples. I had to teach myself this entire course and just tried my best not to fall asleep during this class.

takes up majority of class time writing definitions that are not needed to solve problems. does little to no examples during class and is very passive aggressive when receiving emails. when asking to be excused for an absence that was legitimate, he'll dismiss the reasoning and fight to not give you credit. would not recommend

Birkett does nothing but write definitions the entire lecture. Also, pretty disrespectful if you try to email him. Although calc 3 wasn't that hard, you essentially have to learn everything yourself because he's terrible. Any other professor would be better

Proffesor Betul was honestly a great proffesor. She teaches you exactly what was gonna be on the test. One thing I would say is the homework and lectures are a hit or miss. She's one of the best Professors I've ever had. She teaches really well and helps you grasp the concepts proficiently.
Bilgin cares a lot about her students and is always accessible through office hours. Awesome professor!

Dr. Bilgin strives to make chemical engineering concepts approachable and is an excellent professor to have for introductory courses. She has a great personality and is a respected faculty member of the chemical engineering department.
lectures were unhelpful and spent too much time getting to the meat of the subject
Very nice and understanding, hard to follow initially online, but if you attend office hours and reach out, you will pass

class material is not hard but the lectures are horrible. the class has about 70 students. fewer than 10 show up to lectures. 60% of grades are coming from a midterm and a final. He is very good at his subject. It was a very helpful course.
Interesting subject to study. One of very few 500 level courses at UIC thats worth attending.

Prof. Liu teaching data mining for couple years, his teaching is easily understanding. He always help student a lot. You will learn a lot from his lectures, projects. No pay, No gain of course.
Not helpful, cannot understand, but he does extend the deadlines. Basically nothing to say anything good about, same for Bell and Balasa. Did not prepared me for CS202. More like a waste of time.
I didn't understand his lectures and then I found the class to be rather dull. He didn't seem to make the class very interesting and fun. That's something that I seek in a teacher.

Reading off of a powerpoint which is readily available to us online doesn't help too much and defeats the purpose of having class.
Awful...can't teach cause he can't speak english well.

Go to class and just take notes, drawings are SUPER detailed and will be easy to grasp if you attend class. Will make sure you pass the class and gives so much extra credit for students. Amazing professor, you literally can't fail this class he gives so many make up opportunities.

AMAZING professor, one of my favorites here. So passionate about the subject and KN. Some EC opportunities available by participating in lectures, 10/10!!!

The content is difficult but you don't need to read the book as long as you review all of the tools he provides you w/. This professor is amazing. He clearly breaks down the concepts you learn in lectures and makes sure you get the material. He's easy to talk to and relates to his students. Take this man if you can!!!

This professor is great. Lectures are easy to understand and relatable. They're so good that you don't need to buy the textbook. He offers extra credit opportunities after each exam. He replies to emails very fast (we're talking within 30 minutes). Also does videos about material. Very, very lecture heavy. Amazing guy. PAY ATTENTION TO LECTURES. EZ

He was pretty funny and he would explain the concepts very well, but not use full sentences? so it was hard to write about it bc he didn't give us the language. There is a CRIMINAL amount of reading (100-150 pages per week) and he says it's not all important--after we already read it. The assignments are vague and he's not approachable for Qs

His lectures are informative. In my opinion, he writes hurtful comments on student's papers.

Ialy enjoyed this class. It's real easy to pass. Attendance and text readings are required but it's not too bad. There aren't too many tests/quizzes and barely a lot of homework. He's a real cool guy. The class focuses mostly on the history of music, but if you love that and music it's worth it.

If you need an easy class or are freaking out about writing your History major thesis, take Bledstein.  I honestly don't know why he's still employed, other than tenure.  He's a really nice guy, but I can't say I learned a whole lot - other than what I sought out myself.  Good if you don't need a challenge.

Nice old guy, but his time has passed. Class went off topic every week. It was more of a 3hr rant on the economy, pop culture, etc. I didn't get much of a chance to improve my writing or analytical skills, because the class is all about HIM. All assignments were rushed  into the final 2 weeks of class.  This class is more a test of your patience.
he is a sweet older man that just likes to talk sometimes ramble and talk about his life. He reminds me of Sean Connery. He always brings a gun to class.
Such an adorable old man. He talks a lot but it all helps in the class. He also let's you retake half of the final. Take this class.

If you have to take a history class, I'd definitely say take him. The tests are easy, but only essays. If you go to class though, you can simply regurgitate some of the things you heard in lecture or discussion and get an A. Prof. Bledstein is a cute little old man, his lectures are pretty boring, but not terrible.

I really like Prof. Beldstein. He's a very nice cute old man. His lectures are a little boring.. but they're helpful. I would recommend reading the book because everything he talks about in lecture is from the book. The discussion is very helpful... great TA!!! I like this class even though history is NOT a favorite of mine.
great

Very nice, passionate prof.  He did stray from the topic quite frequently, but it didn't matter much since the text and discussions filled in the blanks.  He'd be very interesting in a political science class.  It's a very easy class, especially if you took AP US in high school.
He's not very helpful when it comes to auditing a class, he was very rude.

let me tell you...this guy can be extremely boring. he rambles on and on and only covers 1/4 of the chapter in lecture. two tests that you are basically on your own with. but as long as you read the chapters...the whole text is covered...and come to lecture you will be fine. got an A in the class...TA was very helpful.overall the class ok. 1 papers

He was okay. Very boring at times, but also a very nice professor. There are 2 tests and one paper. The tests are entirely essay and you will not be given the questions ahead of time, so you really have to pay attention to figure out what topics will be on the tests.
his class is not too hard but a lot of reading assgt.

Old man who is getting senile.  He rambles on about the topic and you are left wondering what he is talking about.  He also goes off on political tangents.  Says he doesn't care about student ratings -- so does he care about the students themselves?  He does give take home tests, so that is the one good thing about him.

Class is on Canvas and she does not accept late work at all. Make sure to be on top of the HW it is ALOT. There is a reading annotations and discussion posts every week. There is also a group presentation. Overall, easy class but sucks she doesnt accept late work.
I had IDS 355. This was probably one of the most difficult classes I have taken. Much harder than MGMT 495 in my opinion. The TAs graded everything, and half the class either had an A or a B.

Very reasonable and fair to all of students. Great professor, great lectures.

One of the worst professors I have ever had. Be prepared to teach yourself because she does not like to go over any examples nor is she clear on what she expects from us. Very difficult to understand during the lectures. Her English isn't that good. She just reads the slides and wont go trough any of the examples in order to better understand the topic. Wont recommend.

reviews.comment: Fun and easy to follow teaching  fair and human-centered management and grading and real respect for every student and different racial backgrounds.

One of the realest professors you'll encounter. His class consists of a few group projects, one of which your group has to present. He does some pop quizzes, but lets you know in advance. He genuinely shows you how behavioral finance is all around us and includes many relevant topics. He cares about all his students. He's honestly really great.
He is a great professor and loves to teach, it does get a little boring at times due to the class being late at night. Best bet is to just show up and you will do well in the class.
Great professor! Definitely my favorite finance class!

Although the class was 2.5 hours in the evening, it was the only course I truly enjoyed my final semester. Lectures were engaging, and the professor was kind, funny, and gave great feedback on projects. Light workload with biweekly group work. Great if you want to learn without feeling overwhelmed.
Such a great guy. You can tell he really cares for his students and is passionate about his job.
Best professor ever

One downside about this class is that it is late at night and that is about it. This is a relatively easy 400-level FIN class. About 5 group projects where you have to find 2 articles that related to the topic of the lectures. Attendance is random and it counts as quizzes and a final exam that is similar to the projects.
This class consists of 4 random attendance quizzes, 5 group projects where you have to present one of them, and 1 Final Exam. Relatively easy, awesome professor. Must take!!

Overall, this was a great course. You learn a lot about financial behavior and perspective. The concepts are meaningful and can be applied in a handful of day to day situations in and out of finance. The class is long, however, the professor has very engaging lectures. Don't hesitate to take this course.

There are 4-5 group projects that are super easy, two pages max. Exam was also easy and the lectures were really interesting. He took attendance randomly a couple of times for credit. I would definitely take him again, the class was great.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awesome professor, lecture heavy but he knows his stuff. Very interactive and chill. Attendance not mandatory, but will have random "pop quizzes" that are pretty much attendance checks so in a way you should still show up. Had a night class but never fell asleep because it was very engaging. One final that is just like the assignments.
One of the best professor i ever had
Professor Bodnaruk is a great soul and is looking to help students is excelling. The class has 3 to 4 group projects and a final exam which is also easy.

He has pop quizzes which are essentially attendance check ins~answering random questions. Around 4 group projects ~ finding 2 financial current events that relate to the class topics of that week. Half a page for each current event. Final exam is the reverse of the project, given an article and you have to answer "what happened", "who caused it"...

Prof. Bodnaruk is a great professor. His lectures can be tedious as usually, he stands up and talks about the presentation. He is not a presentation reader, he knows what he is talking about, but the 2:30 hours are very long for this topic.
He makes a lot of examples, exercises and "experiments" in class to further explain.
Amazing professor! Makes the class interactive and interesting. I think I learned about finance and human behavior here more than any other finance class combined. 100% recommend.

reviews.comment: Professor gives real-life examples in class that will keep student's attention. He also provides lecture notes. Multiple group projects and 1 exam. He is funny, knowledgeable, and a great professor.

Needed to take this class for my last finance minor requirement. Class was super easy and fun. 5 mini group projects, 1 group presentation. 

The professor is super funny and has lots of examples and articles to relate to the topic we are speaking about in class. Class is super laid back and chill. No reading textbooks. Would take him again
I had him for the summer semester so the lectures were long but he was a great instructor. Very straightforward and engages with the class.
Great professor, probably at UIC so far.

I did not wanted to include this in the teacher evaluations because Professor Bodnaruk is truly amazing but, the presentations at the beginning of semester about how we should not send you emails can discourage student communication and are not promoting free speech, if anything students will be scared to reach out.

I think that this Professor is a genuine and amazing professor. He is understanding and aware of situations going on in the real world and the real world application to the content in class is helpful. He is funny and the class for the most part was engaging and I enjoyed going to class. Group projects are majority of the grade but not too diffiucu

He gave out random quizzes in class and youd get credit. Professor was great at explaining and talked about interesting topics. Loved this course!!
Great content!! The professor is also really funny and engaging.

TAKE HIM! Best Finance professor I have taken and wish he taught more classes. He is super nice and respected. Cares about the student and has a good knowledge and is passionate about teaching. Take this class and it is an easy A as long as you put in work. Workload is not bad at all and take this class as an elective.

reviews.comment: Professor Bodnaruk is the best professor at UIC without a doubt. He's very caring, and wants to see his students succeed. Class is not mandatory, but you will want to go. Pay attention in class, do the assignments, and you will be able to pass the exams by just going over the notes he gives in class. If you are in the COB, take this course.

The best finance professor at UIC and frankly the best professor I have had at UIC overall. He is very smart. He gets to know his students and interacts a lot though experiments with the students. The material is very interesting and he manages to make every topic exciting through applicable examples. I wish this guy taught more classes at UIC.

The best professor in the Finance department at UIC. You will learn a lot about behavioral finance from an interesting perspective. He cares for his students and really makes effort to make the lecture as interesting and useful as possible. I wish he taught more classes at UIC. Pay attention in class and you will do good!

Very interesting class that helps you understand how people behave or react over finance topics. You always learn something new, and the class is never boring. You do need to attend class to pass the class.

took his behavioral finance class this summer at UIC. He is really funny, down to earth but also very smart. Professor B really cares that he makes his lectures interesting, with many real life examples of behavioral biases that affect financial markets. It was a really interesting class that I really appreciated!!

Hands down the best professor I have ever taken. Awesome, engaging and funny lectures. Every class is just like a stand-up comedy, absolutely make my day every time. The material gives a great insight on how markets and investors behave backed up by research. 10 out of 10, would take again.

Prof. Bodnaruk was one of the best teachers I've had! He is very intelligent and his lectures were very captivating, funny, and encouraged critical thinking. reviews.comment: This guy is the man!! Great teacher gives you lots of industry knowledge.
Very good Professor

Prof. Bonham is welcoming and laid back, and he'll answer questions if you ask. His teaching style doesn't always match the slides, and the textbook felt unnecessary. I mostly taught myself using slides and mock exams. He allows late work and is easy to understand. Even if accounting isn't your strength, self-studying works well, trust me.

Cool guy. The professor is a very kind and caring person. He will allow late submissions. All u have to do is ask him nicely. His style of teaching was very clear and to the point. Loved the slides he made. Exams were honestly too easy, as most of the stuff followed the review materials.

As a transfer student, Professor Bonham has been the best professor I've had at UIC. He's understanding, engaging, and explains everything clearly. Attendance is mandatory, and perfect attendance earns extra credit. The workload is light, and if you take good notes and stay focused, you'll do great in his class.

Good prof, but doesnt go by the workbook at all. not even sure why we bought it. he isnt good a teaching or explaining things. He also goes by pretty quickly. Hes a nice guy who cares about his students but just cant teach.

Bonham is not a bad person just really bad at teaching. Simply put. I took the final today and it honestly was nothing like what he had taught us exactly in class. That being said I self-studied hoping i passed. He runs through slides, barely explains. But he is super carings and helps if you ask. I would avoid adn taek Patel tho. Hes a better prof

The accounting department is very structured with its exams, slides, and notes and I believe this holds Bonham back who wants to teach in his style. He is a good professor but I had to teach myself a lot of stuff due to inconsistencies. He is very caring and sympathetic to our needs. I would not take a class with him again though.

He's a cool professor and advocates for students. Grades are based on hw, quizzes, group assignments, and exams. It can be a difficult class if you never read or understand the material. He's good at explaining concepts but moves on quick.

Genuinely one of if not the best professors at UIC. He knows how to teach and genuinely wants to see students succeed. If you take him I guarantee you will get a good grade in accounting, take this professor!

Accounting 211 is controlled by the department at UIC, so they make the powerpoint slides and the exams and homework. All he did was read off the slides he was given. Not a bad professor but also not a good one. He's ok. I have an A but that's because you have to teach yourself. It's an ok class and an ok professor.

reviews.comment: Prof Bonham is truly a great professor. This is his first year at UIC and I think he is doing a great job. Accounting is hard but somehow he makes it understandable and easy to follow. There are a lot of lecture slides but he goes over them at a manageable pace. First class I actually looked forward going to! I definitely recommend him!

I am currently taking Professor Bonham's course at UIC. He is a great professor and really cares about his students. Knows what he's talking about and always ready to answer questions. An open note quiz after every unit and 4 total exams. Homework is given with ample time to complete. Exam is difficult if you don't study otherwise you'll be fine.

Prof Jonathan is great! Unsure y other review says otherwise. Accounting is hard no secret there. But he does an amazing job at helping & answering questions. Go to his office hours. He cares about students passing & will curve if necessary. I was scared for this class cuz im not an accounting major. Hes the reason I am passing this class. Take him

To preface, I took Bonham at the UChicago, not UIC. He is the worst lecturer I have ever had the displeasure of learning from. Exams will make or break your grade (~50% of your grade). Even the multiple choice is hard, because he will pick some obscure fact from the slides. Class averages for the 3 exams were 51%, 52%, 41% and the exam practice wasn't helpful. Group projects are ~25% of grade, prepare for terrible teammates. Harsh grading and barely got an A. DO NOT TAKE.
He's very knowledgable and caring. However his exams are very hard and very essential in this class, so make sure you study. He's a nice guy but sorry too crazy exams so probably won't take again..
Don't do it.

reviews.comment: His tests are based on how fast you are at taking tests, not being able to assess and walk through a problem to take a test. Not a great class overall.

He's awesome! Nice guy, very knowledgeable on investing. I learned a lot. I didn't find the class hard, just a lot of material so you have to make sure you pay attention. Any negative reviews didn't even try in the class. He's very organized and has clear expectations. 10/10 recommend!
Good professor, heavy accent but he is understandable. He's a nice guy who knows his stuff about finance so if you want to learn about investments he is a good fit.

There is no reason for you to fail the class if you do all your work and study, he even curves the grade. There are a total of 11 homework, 3 Excel group projects, and 3 midterms. Professor Bondarenko is a top-notch researcher who does great work for CBOE. His lectures can be a little dry, but regardless he does a great job going over the material. Excellent professor, grades on a class rank curve. Very clear as to expectations, exams are succinct, and he draws problems directly from the assigned homework and class examples. The projects assigned are easy and excel based in groups of 4. Overall a nice and helpful guy.

Gives detailed notes and no tricky tests. Very nice and helpful professor although it may be hard to stay focus during the lectures. Grading is generous extra credit is provided (do it because it helps a lot!!). Don't mess around and you should get an A fairly easily.

He's a good teacher.  He explains everything clearly.  He does things step-by-step so you will understand.  3 very fair exams, 2 easy group projects and a 10-point extra credit opportunity. I def. recommend this professor. His classes fill up quick!
He's really helpful and his tests are pretty easy. The projects are easy and you'll get full credit if you follow the instructions.  Just go to class and take notes and you're guaranteed an A.

He's a very good teacher. He really works hard with the students to help them understand. His tests are from his lectures and the HW. SignUp soon coz his classes fill up fast!
Exams are easy.. there are 2 projects but answers would be given.. He is a very nice guy.. easy A..

Awsome professor.Teaching style is awsome.Has his own notes that you can understand instead of the publishers.Easy class if you attend class. very good prof, always gave good critiques and helped us a lot if we were confused or stuck with our writing. attendance required at beginning of semester, by the end you barely have to come. only 4 essays, the last 3 are all part of the same final essay. only thing is she was very disorganized and wouldn't follow syllabus which left us confused.

LOVE HER. Makes expectations very clear and is very caring and understanding.

I love Prof. Boulay! She is so clear with expectations and actually listens to students. She's very kind and gives great & insightful lectures and feedback. I would love to take another class with her if I wasn't transferring schools.

She is a great professor. She may seem intimidating but overtime she is actually really nice. Going to class was important as that is where you will make your paper improvements. She makes you into a better writer.

reviews.comment: Professor Boulay is hands down the best professor I've ever had! She's a very kind professor and she always dismisses class early! Professor Boulay is very laid back, she seemed a little intimidating the first few days but she's actually really down to earth. She's very accessible outside of class and is an easy grader when it comes to papers.

reviews.comment: Best prof! I had health issues and so I was in the hospital for almost a month but she was understanding and didn't require that i do the assignments i missed. Her class is super easy but it didnt feel stupidly easy bc i actually learned things, you watch a movie in class once a week and then discuss it the next day. 100/10.

Must admit I'm a terrible writer but meeting her during her office hours will definitely help you in passing the class. She give great feedback! Get to know her!

reviews.comment: Boulay is a badass I love her so much. Make sure you meet with her outside of class during her Office hours with your paper and she will give you everything you need to get an A. Best professor I had this semester going to miss her
