reviews.comment: best class i took last year

I am not an art major or an art person at all. She made the course extremely enjoyable for me, encouraged opinions and participation. Yes, the exams were a bit rough, but you need to study. Expect an 8 page paper, but you get to pick the artwork you'll research. The class was fun overall if you intent to come to class to learn.

The class itself isn't too bad. But the exams are the absolute worst. And they make up almost all of your grade. We look at so many pieces of artwork. And you would think the ones that she spends the most time talking about in class would be the ones on the exam, but no. The ones she spends 2 seconds on in class are the ones on the exam. Beware!

AVOID!!!  She expects way too much and nothing is ever good enough for her. It's especially irritating if you aren't even an art major and are just taking the class for the creative arts gen. ed. requirement. Definitely go with a better prof who is a little more reasonable and doesn't expect completely unattainable things from students.

Teaches you how to interpret paintings and you learn the differences between different painters and era styles. Go to class and the essay questions on the tests are much easier becaus eyou compare paintings that she already talked about in class. You need to memorize a lot of paintings and their artists and years for the tests, but its not too bad

A lot of these ratings are from people that obviously had her for 111, and didn't care about it. I had her for 111, and she wasn't excellent, but she's GREAT in more specialized classes. Anyone interested in the topic will love her. She REALLY knows her stuff. She comes off cold, but is really just a little awkward; she is actually very kind.

She is awesome. I loved taking this class it was so easy. She does kinda talk monotonously a bit and her voice kinda sounds like Janice from Friends ( a little annoying) but she knows what shes talking about and you can totally get an A with minimal study time. Just study the PDFs she makes and you're good to go
As long as you read the book and pay attention to the slides to know for the exam on BB, this class is not too bad. It was interesting and some of the guest lectures were very fun.

Speaks in monotone and is difficult to listen to. I just put on my ipod and looked up the works on google and learned more from that. Makes an already boring subject excruciating. I just stopped going to the lectures and attended section discussion instead. Why is she presenting in front of 300 students? Munman is way better.
lectures don't facilitate note-taking. not helpful (sometimes even rude) to individual students. interesting material though.

This professor is so boring and speaks in a monotone. She goes through every piece of art and describes them in very boring ways compared to Munman (AH110 teacher). Definitely take AH110 instead if possible. I don't think she has kept my attention in even 1 lecture.

Nina Dubin describes every piece of art we study in a captivating yet easy to understand manner. As long as you attend lecture you will ACE the class. I didn't even buy the book! SOOO easy. At the end of each week, she even makes a list of the MOST important *hint hint* artworks and terms to study for the exams.

Honestly this professor was litterly useless. I would attend lecture day in and day out and I would miss maybe one lecture one day here and there and then the test comes around and the stuff no one cares about is on it. Horrible teacher
Is a kind professor. Make sure you value deadlines as no late work will be accepted and attendance is mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: This teacher has pleasant teaching methods. however, the assignments are so randomly assigned that it can be easy to fall into a super low grade even if you attend classes faithfully, speak fairly fluent Spanish, and participate in class. Very little room for error, grading rubrics are not consistent, and she can be petty if you challenge her.

Teacher has a nice personality, which is the only reason I could give her 2. I've never had a grade as inconsistent as Elementary Spanish II with Duarte. I have received A's in math classes, science classes, work heavy classes. She sets up work/dates in a way that's unclear, and expects a standard which is higher than an elementary level course.

I have taken other Spanish classes and consistently earned A's. I worked hard in this course, but points were deducted on larger projects, even when I made sure to meet all of her criteria. This stood out after comparing my work to peers with similar quality who earned an A. I noticed a discouraging difference in tone in her interactions with me.

Sabra is funny, chatty and reasonable. Spanish courses are hard, but she teaches well. Get ready for most of the lecture to be 100% spanish. Hard learning curve, worth it.

SPAN 101
Guys. Girls. EVERYONE. I havent met a single person that likes this Professor. She is very tough. Doesnt respond to emails. Doesnt provide meaningful feedback. TONS OF HW. Please avoid. GOOD LUCK
Very helpful and always willing to help. Office hours were very valuable, and she is very caring. She made the class very easy, and I learned a lot!
a great professor, and very helpful. easily accesible outside of class, and office hours help a lot. lectures are awesome, and i barely had to study outside of the lectures
Best professor in math in general. Super great teacher with great lectures and always willing to help.
Took her for calc 1 and she was great, responded to emails quick too and explained concepts easily
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Tells you very clearly what is going to be on the exam. Explains things down to the very last detail. If you are taking any math class at UIC, take it with her.

Dr. Hamed was a very good professor who explained subjects clearly, took time to ask students about their day, and tried hard to help us all succeed. Her lectures are clear and she moves through the topics in a timely matter. I would recommend her to everyone and would gladly take another course with her.

A great professor who deserves wonderful recognition as a teacher who can organize thoughtful lectures throughout the semester rather than regurgitating Pearson exercises. Amazing after class and gives thoughtful consideration to achieve a great grade within the course—a diamond in the sea of public school professors.
She was a really good math teacher she tried her best to help as many people as she can, her lectures were refreshing but fun, and she really cared about math and you can tell it a lot

I love Dr. H! I had her for Math180 and she truly gave you a lot of resources to help you succeed. She presented the material in a variety of ways that allowed us to truly understand the topic and help out our groupmates about it. She truly made sure we had a good foundation in one skill before moving onto another.

For STATS 381. Professor Hamed is an awesome professor, she is very caring and charismatic, and wants the best from us. She does talk a bit quick so if you're not paying attention it can be hard to focus, but she makes great notes and explains topics really well. She is also very quick to respond to Piazza posts, and is very helpful.

Dr. Hamed is awesome! (Math 180-Calc) She has a true passion for teaching and connecting with people! She is willing to talk to students before and after class if they have general questions. She helped us understand the concepts behind the math which was refreshing from being forced to memorize things. I would love to take more of her classes!

She is very nice and loves to talk to her students before class. She is caring and going to her office hours really helped with the math material. Math 180 can be very difficult for some students, but if you study hard you can get an A.
Great lecturer and is super sweet. She goes out of her way to talk to students before class starts. Highly recommend taking her.

An amazing lecturer! Take her if you can. Extremely nice and puts in effort every morning to say hi to her students and always has a smile on her face. Her lectures are clear and easy to follow. If you just listen to her and follow her along you will be good to go for the exams. If you ever do get lost, her posted lecture notes are really helpful.
Professor was great! Goes by a new name and pronouns though, Emily Dumas, so use that instead. Class was difficult and material went too fast.

I took him for MCS 275 and I really enjoyed the topics he decided to teach, which were a variety of different programming concepts from data structures to some web dev. He was very easygoing and very good at communicating with his students.

Might be one of the best professors working at UIC. His lectures are clear and concise, and if you listen in lecture, the homework and Projects are a breeze. He is also the most caring professor and understands if things happens. 100/10 would take again. Amazing Professor.

Great programming class straight from the mcs department. If you need to take mcs260 and mcs275 take with Dumas. You will land an internship just after having those two classes. He does live coding which is very helpful. Very helpful during o.h. Supportive and caring.

Had him for MATH 180 and he's a great lecturer who gives great examples and is very thorough. He is extremely organized and makes a minimal amount of mistakes. He's great to take notes off of and he answers your questions in a way you will understand. He got his PhD from Harvard so that should tell you something.

Most lectures consist of practice problems & note-taking. Professor is very smart & understands the subject. He takes the time to answer questions students may have. He is a very good professor but subject itself is hard. Exams are standard for all math 180 classes so it is difficult across the board. Study past exams & notes. work for your grade

Mr. Dumas is a dry teacher, but a good one. He goes over lessons in detail and answers any questions you might have. At UIC all 180 classes take the same test so its not a matter if he is difficult to not. However, he is the hardest test writer, which will affect everyone taking 180, not just you.
Awesome lectures very punctual and organized but also very thorough in explaining
Best Calc 3 professor, made the class pretty easy because his lectures are clear and help you prepare for the test
He cares, and he is a great lecturer. If you really want to learn, take him. And He absolutely hates it when people come in late.

He really doesn't care about the students. Nor does he have the "inspiration" to teach. He just does the "bare minimum" to make it seem like he teaches. His "notes" are confusing and it just mostly what is already written in the textbook in a almost "word for word" format but without plagiarizing. He may know math well but he can't teach. Dont take

Since I already have experience with Calc this class wasn't that difficult, but if I was someone that didn't know much about calc I'd probably cry myself to sleep every night. He's not horrible but you really have to pay attention and sometimes he skips steps and then you get all confused like how did he get that? Oh and get ready for the graphs!

Honestly the best class (I learned the most not the easiest) I have taken at UIC and I graduate next semester. Dumas is well prepared for class and EXTREMELY knowledgeable. An absolute pleasure to study under.

The averages for each exam were well below %50, meaning more than half the class ended up failing.  You'd expect something a bit more fair in a first-year Calc course. Does  NOT curve. Not a very good instructor, you'd be better off trying to learn on your own than gaining anything from lecture. Student beware.

Professor Dumas is perhaps the best professor (or teacher for that matter) of mathematics I have ever had. His lectures are well organized with geometric proofs, examples, and defines terms mathematically as well as "plain English". Highly recommend him. Study the practice exams and haveALL your questions answered. He emails back within 20 minutes.
Excellent Professor, his notes are very organized and clear. It is evident that he is one of the best professors at UIC. I highly recommend taking this professor!

Awesome professor. Clearly explained topics and I had never taken Calculus before. I got an A. Best thing to do is study from practice exams and you should be fine. You should take him no matter what! :)

Professor Dumas was a great teacher! He gives a lot of good notes and tons of examples for each chapter. He made calculus very easy to understand for me because he never rushed any chapters. One of the best math teachers I've had, take him!

He was by far the cutest nerdy professor ever. He is extremely well qualified to teach this class. He is always on top of things. His notes help a lot! He's got his little quirky jokes every once in a while. All my friends would skip their math lecture to come to mine b/c the Professor Dumas was so good at teaching. I HIGHLY RECOMMEND HIM!!!
he is extremely helpful and gives alot of examples. he always has an outline prepared and explains each concept clearly.

pretty cool professor, he's good at relaying the concepts. you always know what you are going to expect since he outlines the class. Really good at keeping you updated with things related to the course makes quirky little comments every once in while, which are funny. Overall a good professor

Lectures are very dry, and his slides are disorganized walls of text that do not flow very well. His explanation of his own slides still doesn't make sense, and would scrutinize you for not understanding. He is not very accessible outside of class, so this is all just self-teaching. He is the only one teaching 566 so good luck to those who take it

Do not take this class. The professor is disorganized and unprofessional. He sends last-minute emails late at night with same-day deadlines. He ignores the syllabus, deadlines, and basic academic policies. The class is chaotic, and he seems proud of running it like a dictatorship. You'll learn nothing but stress.
Even after reading all the reviews below about this professor and you still decide to take him for one of your courses. I would only say that may god give you strength to deal with his courses.

reviews.comment: He seems like he means well although he's too cynical and obnoxious. I'd overlook that if he'd bother to put more effort into presenting the material clearly and intelligibly. Worst professor ever. He just spent most of the time complaining about everything—complaining that students aren't smart enough, UIC isn't good enough, etc. He won't answer your questions either; he'll just think they are too basic.

Always late to class. PPTs too difficult understand, with some slides being handwritten pages and others being a wall of text. You have to study on your own. Very rude, worst professor at UIC.

He is very non-inclusive with his teaching approach. Grades relentlessly hard no matter how hard you try to demonstrate your understanding. He is very rude and does not teach material correctly. During the pandemic he made his courses harder than before. You can understand all the concepts of Digital Systems Design and still fail.

Worst professors at UIC in terms of professionalism. Sighs whenever someone says anything incorrect. Tells us to ask questions and answer questions even if it might be wrong. After taking many courses at UIC, first time I attended a course with good quality. One should put lots of effort to get a good grade. Professor should respect everyone's time though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

He is among remaining 2 or 3 professors at UIC who still maintain good standard in the course content. He is condescending and makes you feel bad about yourself if you answer wrong. Hated being in his class

TL;DR - great course for learning something and working hard. However, instructor is incredibly rude and I WILL NEVER take a class with him again. Pretty much stopped trying to answer anything.

reviews.comment: His lectures are of very high quality. Each class is like in-depth research of something very interesting. I learnt so much from his Parallel Processing course and I saw improved version of myself after this course. I encourage inquisitive students not to miss his courses.

If u r someone who wants to put in a real effort to learn, don't  even think for a minute to take his courses. I missed taking his Digital Systems course by listening to students who just go for grades. In-depth teaching, challenging assignments, then and there feedbacks to learn and grow(weak ones take in a negative way) Best and unique Professor!

Highly encourage people with interest in Digital Design to take his ECE 465 course. His assignments and Projects are non-trivial and requires a lot of thinking but he always gives a hint or a clue just 2-3 days before the deadline. His teaching is good but his notes are very good. You can impress the professor by answering his questions in class

He takes a very different approach in that all work is non trivial which makes the homework and projects VERY time consuming and hard. But they are really fun and worthwhile. I never felt so accomplished. Unfortunately he is a bit stubborn and will hold up class until he gets exactly the answer he wants, so someone just keep trying to answer him!!!

There's a lot that you can learn in this course. The material taught in the class is informative. Assignment problemsproject are non-trivial, so you are forced to think about it. Professor is strict but learning requires discipline!
I believe the course helped me get insight into parallel algorithms and the projects were also a great learning experience. I'm glad I decided to take his course.

Course taken in Fall '12. The topics covered were interesting and taught in-depth. Very smart prof. Learned a lot. He is a bit demanding of excellence, which throws some students off. It will help if he goes easy on that (not everyone is that motivated to excel) without much reducing quality and the challenging nature of the course.
Very rude and one the worst professor I have ever meet.

Vert helpful prof and you will learn a lot in this course. The prof treats students like friends and not like students, so you will enjoy while learning and you will have a desire to excel and learn the materials. Innovation is encouraged greatly and you can do something ur own way and have a chance to impress the prof with it. Highly recommended.
Tough course, but good choice of topics, well-prepared slides, good teaching, learn a lot.

This professor is very rude,non respectful, and won't transfer any knowledge to you. It won't be difficult to have and A for the class but you would have to learn anything by yourself. AVOID ANY DIRECT CONTACT WITH HIM, HE IS EXCESSIVELY RUDE AND GET ANGRY EASILY: probably because he don't understand simple things.
Very mean professor. Yells at students for no apparent reason. Expects everyone to know everything immediately. Horrible english as well.
Do not take his course. He is crude to his students.
Good professor but not an easy class

I think it's easier to watch Mohr's lectures though.

Dr. Wardrop was a great teacher. I've had him for 4 classes now and really appreciated his approach to teaching. If you put the time and effort into this class, you can succeed. Taking the higher-level courses has just proved to me more that he cares for his students and wants them to succeed. In my opinion, he's the nicest prof in the department.

Very good professor. The course has lots of places to obtain points outside of exams so you have a fair shot at an A. Wardrop is VERY helpful during his office hours, make sure you go if you don't understand something. The class is a lot of work but if you stay on top of things you'll be fine. Large curve.

Its ORGO, if your not gonna put in the work you wont get a good grade. However the man is very good at explaining and generally out of all the possible orgo professors he is by far the nicest and his exams aren't unfair. Overall the class is going to be hard, but the professor doesn't make it worse, and helps out students in a lot of small ways

Orgo was the hardest class I've ever taken. Wardrop did not go over any of the problem sets during his lecture and he didn't do any questions that'll be on the exams during his lectures either. The way he explained things and the examples he would go over would make no sense. Quizzes every week brought my grade down even more!! It was terrible!!

Professor Wardrop is very understanding but you must work hard for your grade. Theres lots of lectures so take good notes and do the problem sets! The exams resemble them the most so attend office hours or watch them go over these. If you leave things to last minute you will fall behind fast. Weekly quizzes help you practice as well.

reviews.comment: This class was difficult but it definitely is manageable if you study and work hard. Professor W. gives a bunch of resources which help make this class easier. reviews.comment: I personally liked his classes. I took it online so we had an option to either watch his own lec. or another prof. Three exams total. quiz every week in the live discussion sec with TA. Exams are not that hard if know the basic material, no trick questions. you have an A at 80%. A problem set (key prov.) and Wiley Plus due each week.

Dr. Wardrop is a very very fair and good professor. You must do the problem sets and go to office hours. PRACTICE will get you an A in this course. Wardrop even dropped a quiz and a video assignment for us to ease some stress. I would definitely recommend this course with Wardrop to anyone wanting to take Orgo.

reviews.comment: Wardrop's deep voice intimidates me. That's all I gotta say man. Proceed with caution.

reviews.comment: Wardrop is a great professor. He's very helpful and made Orgo bearable. Orgo is a very difficult class and you won't pass if you don't read the book and do the practice problems. Put in the work and you will do fine.

He his a friendly man and approachable. This is a weed out class so it's suppose to be hard, be prepared to work for the grade you want.
Never paid attention in class went only for iclicker points. I spent all my days locked in my room studying from the textbook.

Dr. Wardrop is a nice guy but easily one of the worst instructors at UIC. He doesn't care about his students and don't even bother going to office hours bc he won't help you out one bit. Be prepared to have a stressful semester if taking this class and with this instructor. Be sure to read the whole book!
He gives students adequate problem sets and answer keys for these problem sets, which allow you to be able to get enough practice and check your work. He is very glad to help students.

Got a B and never really paid attention in lecture, powerpoints are really good, weekly problem sets  (not mandatory) and quizzes keep you caught up w/ material. Grades based on percentile, so kinda hard to tell what grade is but he eventually posts it. Dropped lowest exam grade!

This class will challenge you. It's like The Hunger Games but with Organic Chemistry. There will be a ranking which identifies the different curves and where you stand amongst other students. If you have a Pre-med goal, make sure you read the book, read his lecture slides, and do the problem sets. And don't fall behind, especially before exams.

He outlines everything during the first lecture, and lets students know what to do to get a good grade: READ THE BOOK, DO PROBLEMS, AND RETAKE NOTES.

Everyone seemed confused on his lectures with two of the semester exam averages being around 30%. Never posts any of the quiz or exam answer keys so you will be clueless. Had to use online videos and read the book to learn. Problem set keys were sort of helpful. Stressful semester.

Tests are just like the problem sets but still very hard. Class is hard and you compete against fellow students for your grade. Only went to class for iClickers. Orgo is always hard no matter what so good luck!
Two things:  huge curve and copy-paste exams! Enough said.

OMG!!! Probably one of the normal and easy to understand professor for orgo at UIC!! And yes that's a huge statement for an orgo professor at UIC. Horrible teacher, does not know how to keep students attention. He's very disorganized and teaches irrelevant stuff that's not even on the tests. The only thing cool about him was that there was no HW. Overall, wish I hadn't taken him because now I have to retake the course.

Memorize mechanisms

read the book..

very disorganized. teaches a bunch of extra stuff that is not on the exams. doesn't always return emails, just overall not that helpful.  the quizzes hurt instead of help your grade, they're really tough.  if you don't have to, don't take him

I like him as a prof.I was in 232 for Spring 2010 and he is really helpful if you go to office hours.Unfortunately, he does speak quite softly in class so u must sit in first 2 rows, but he makes up for it by taking the time to talk to you during office hours. I'm sure there r better 232 profs, but I like his style and wish I could take him for 234
One of the worst professors I've ever had. Could barely hear him in lecture and doesn't speak up even though asked to. His slides are somewhat helpful, but you're better off reading the book.
Most useless professor at UIC, don't show up to lecture, just learn on your own. Take Miranda or any other Orgo professor.
This professor is awesome and doesn't give so much homework. You have group projects and you're allowed to us AI.

Best professor I've had at UIC. Grading material was clear from the start and assignments were easy, but you still learn a lot and it's an interesting class. Younger professor so I felt like he related to students better and he clearly has a passion for what he teaches.

hes soooooo boring. just the way he talks OMG so boring. he's so dead. Exams are grades super heavily it's crazy. bio lab is EASY!

never ever ake bio 100 with this professor he acts as if we are a like bio 500 level class and talks in such a monotone voice never learned anything this semester

reviews.comment: terrible, terrible, terrible. take another teacher. hard class and you need to devote all your time to it. He is sarcastic and not much of help. pop quizzes occasionally.

Some people complain that he is monotone, but I enjoyed his dry humor. He says things with the straightest face, not laughing, but he is clearly joking. He really cares about what he does and cares about his students.

He is a very good professor. The class is essentially like Bio 100 but on steroids. Getting an A is doable, but I had to study until my brain was fried.  He isn't the most colorful lecturer, but the material in this course is just dry in and of itself.  With that being said, I enjoyed learning from somebody who had experience with the material.

You cant understand anything he says because he uses way too many scientific words. To make matters worse, he has a super low monotone voice and talks horribly fast.  Tests are HARD so prepare to study 4-5 days prior to the exam. Try to pick someone else for cell bio.

Lecture capture didn't work for the entire semester so if you didn't catch what was said you were out of luck. He speaks in a very low monotone voice so it definitely would have been helpful. The course was great until the last portion of the class. He was not prepared to teach the material and the left the class confused. Went from a solid B to C+

Monotone voice? Who cares? His lectures are very informative. Unlike many professors who download slides from the book's publisher and add their two cents, he brings insightful examples that help to understand the material. The tests are a bit challenging, but it's 200-level bio. Expect to read and study and you'll do fine. Very helpful too!
meh. not a fan of the writing portions of the test. those parts were really really hard.
He's a great speaker, and his lectures are informative. Speak with him after class; he's very well informed about many things.
Decent guy, will help if asked. His tests are kind of difficult. Memorize his analogies from lecture because they will show up on exam.
He has a monotone voice which makes it really hard to pay attention. Overall he is a cool guy you just need to do the readings and look over the study guides and you should be fine.

Dr. Dubreuil is a really great professor! He is extremely knowledgeable in what he teaches, and answers questions from students with ease. People find his voice monotone, but it forces you to work for your grade. Go into office hours; he wants you to succeed in the class. He also has some jokes during lecture, so look forward to them!

Overall, he is a decent professor. Lectures are a bit dry, he could make them more interesting yet doesn't. However, he is a nice guy and you can tell that he genuinely wants you to do well. The material for cell bio is VERY dense... read the book, def memorize the study guides, and record his lectures. I would recommend him!

Dr. Ron is an awesome guy. His lectures are very straightforward. Exams are not hard if you read the book and pay attention in class! I took this class over the summer and received an A (without the curve) so it IS possible!
I had a hard time staying focused in class with such a monotone, low-volume voice. His exams are pretty much exactly what he posts on his study guides, so study them!

The lectures were so boring! He is monotone and not enthusiastic about teaching the material. He can make this difficult material interesting, but doesn't! Attending lecture doesn't help at all. Quizzes are mostly easy, but prepare to teach yourself the material to do well on exams.Focus on understanding info from slides, not so much on book.

Prof. Dubreuil is a great guy. Really helpful in office hours and gives hint about the exam. Must understand and know the study guide inside and out, that is where most of the questions come from. Also have to read the chapter which he draws about 40% of his exam questions. Not very hard.

Teaches first half of cell bio. very helpful guy and knows his stuff. make sure you go to lecture because that's where most of questions come from. STRESS ON THE STUDY GUIDE that he gives before exams because questions show up from the study guide. Read the book but PAY MORE ATTENTION TO HIM TALKING (record lectures) because he talks fast. Take him

I really enjoyed this class. It was co-taught between Drs. Dubreuil and Kay.  Both were splendid. Tests are no joke.  Super confusing if you didn't really study. My secret weapon for getting an A was using the CD that came with the textbook and practicing the sample tests over and over. Attendance is also mandatory for success.
Dr. Ron is one of the most intelligent professor at UIC. He tries to approach the idea by simple ways. Just go to lecture and take notes any you'll be good! He got very funny jokes!!

dr. dubreil was a good professor overall.  he was very knowledgable and taught the material very well. when the class was having difficulty with something he would focus on it until we figured it out.  plus he was a very personable guy which was nice. his tests and quizzes were pretty fair too

I absoulutely LOVE this teacher. He's very helpful and friendly with questions. His slides are generally easy to follow and he posts great supplemental info on slides/topics that were not in the text book. The material is dense, but if you give yourself 3-4 days to study before the exam, you'll be fine.
He is a very straightforward and clear lecturer. Be sure to pay attention in lecture because that's where the tests come from. You should go to class because he says more than is on the slides.
soooooo boring... he reads from the slides ... this class will make u fall asleep!!! just study the slides and u will be fine for the exams

He's a great professor. extremely clear, and an engaging lecturer. i recommend recording lectures and re listening to them.. i didn't really open the book when i studied, i just did that and got a A. Highly recommended.

One of the best language teachers I've had in my educational career, for both 103 and 104. The workload for the class is pretty hefty, as most language classes are, but in-class activities are interesting and inclusive. Teacher is kind, easy to reach, and knowledgeable.

Very kind and understanding professor. Willing to help explain anything harder to understand, just ask her. CHIN200 covers many new Chinese vocab every week. Plenty of homework, lectures full of content, occasional class discussions. Clear instructions for larger assignments. Projects had the option of working with a partner. Accepts late work!

I am a heritage speaker and took this class expecting it to be fairly easy. However, the amount of homework and the difficulty of the assignment and tests made the class hard for me. The worksheets and such she makes you do online have some pretty ridiculous questions that are hard to get right even if you understand all of the languages.

This class was fully online due to COVID-19. Lectures 3 days a week with quizzes every other Friday or so. Important to pay attention in class since she goes over important vocab however you still need to study on your own.  Lots of homework that you need to keep up with but if you do what is necessary of you then you will pass with an A.
She's great. Talks very fast but will def help if you need it
This class burned me out of the Chinese language. I ended up hating my experience and stopped attending.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She's a really nice teacher and person. However, I personally don't care for her teaching style. Sometimes she just goes off explaining things in Chinese pretty quickly, and I have no idea what's going on. And she writes things on board but won't write the English so it's like even if you wanted to take notes if you forget it's not really helpful.

Meng laoshi is an excellent Chinese professor. She takes time to explain class material. This is an integrated language class which means it involves independent study through the use of technology. You must watch all the videos for each lesson if you don't like to read the textbook to understand the content.

Meng Laoshi has been my absolute favorite professor in college. I'm seriously upset that I can't take another class with her! She's extremely easygoing and very patient when you need help. It's pretty easy to get an A. DO ALL OF THE HOMEWORK. There's a lot and they make up the bulk of your grade. Memorize all  of the characters too!

This professor is awesome. I have learnt soo much within the passed months. Although I am a native speaker myself, my mandarin is so-so, but after taking her I don't regret moving further with it. She loves her students and care about them. Meng Lao Shi Zui Hao!

Absolutely love this teacher! She has a great sense of humour. Explanations are clear and helpful. Watch out for the exams. They are fairly challenging and some contain essay questions which I usually struggles with.
Very friendly teacher and willing to help. Just do your homework and study the dialogue and you'll be fine.
Very nice lady. She has a lot of patience, and if you do not understand what is going on in class, she is more than willing to give you extra help. She is also quite humorous. Awesome teacher.
Very easy class. Just do the homework assignments and look over the dialogue a few times before the test. She is very lenient with students.

(I also took CHIN 112 with her) A really nice lady, but it may be hard to understand her if you aren't good with accents. Just do the homework. Exams are typically easy. The only thing I didn't like is that she was really disorganized.
She's an easy going teacher who has a lot of patience. Not a very hard class if you do you homework, which by the way are not too bad.

The Blackboard website was the most difficult aspect of the class, but with the new Canvas platform coming out, maybe that won't be an issue soon. She doesn't play, but she's considerate. No hand-holding, but not a “gotcha” class by any means.
Sharyn Dyer is a lovely professor who always takes her time to explain things to students and always finds a way around unfortunate circumstances. She goes the extra mile for her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Course if not difficult, the prof makes this course super confusing and hard to navigate on blackboard

I understand that every course will have homework and its own deadlines. However, in PUBH100, Dr. Dyer make it like everyone only have her class and gave us a bunch of random things, the worst part is, she put deadlines time and day completely random. Very disorganize, unprofessional and completely high level of ignorance in other people's time.

Class, syllabus, and blackboard were very disorganized. Sharyn doesn't lecture but instead makes you read tons of chapters. It was hard to figure out what was due and what day it was due. Learned nothing from this class even though I received an A. She grades assignments slowly so its hard to tell how youre doing in the class. Would not take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very poor professor. Seems very confused and online lectures are not informative or w
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Dyer was such a caring professor. It was such a pleasure to have her. She genuinely cares for the well being of her students. Her class is simple. If you pay attention and do what she's asking of you, you'll pass. AND she offers help and extra credit. I would definitely have her as my professor again if I could.

This asynchronous, 100 level class (literally the first class in the department), had a semester long group project where they had to meet with their peers, record a presentation together, and are requested to visit the neighborhoods researched for "passive observation". Some of them aren't even safe to visit! And this is a third of our grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Attendance isn't mandatory. Professor Lott will stop the class to call you out if you're talking. Make sure to read the book. Go to lectures because he will put examples on the powerpoints that won't be in the book. These examples will likely be on the exams. Pop quizzes online due on Fridays on the readings.

Straightforward class. Just look at the definitions from textbook and read all assigned readings and you'll do good on the exams. Attendance is not mandatory and I never went to any lectures but did all assignments and took all exams and ended up with a B.  Great for people that don't like lecture but discussion is mandatory!!!

His lectures do suck, he uses incredibly formal language to describe straightforward concepts. I took pictures of the slides on my phone (cuz they're not on BB) & compared main ideas with the ones in the textbook & I did fine. The life project is worth a lot of pts. Use your TAs they're helpful. No cummul. exams. He will call you out so pay attn.

Lott is too good for everyone and unclear in his lectures, he is extremely scripted and does nothing to get the class entertained. He also is very power hungry and will stop the entire class to tell you to shut up. Do not take him if you want an easy class, or a fun one. Not helpful at all, he will direct you to a TA for everything.

Day 1. This guy is a jack-ass. He speaks with great enthusiasm regarding the intellectually rich discussions he wants to invoke, and then talks to the class we are a bunch of morons. How does this coexist? You can't talk down to a group of people and at the same time expect them to be engaged in philosophy. What a dumpy, irresponsible teacher!

don't take this class. this was my hardest class yet and I believe that's because he makes it extremly hard. the lectures really have nothing to do with test really, you have to read the book. I studied for hours and hours and barely got a B, DON'T TAKE. He makes the material hard for no reason and puts all the hard material on the test.
Too good for everyone Not clear in instruction Not helpful at all Turns away students  Hard to get material down
Worst class ever! Boring, tedious, and unclear class so to speak.

the class content was interesting but the exams were horrible. made a mistake taking this class with a new prof. Got B coz there was nothing to bring it A. 3 exams, 1 paper. all were like 80%. Lesson: never take new prof. he might have learned now to teach this class again. who knows?anthro is easy class but he made it extremely hard. lower my gpa!

He was hands down the most boring lecturer I have ever had to sit through during my three years in school. He came off rude and mumbled into the microphone during lecture. His tests made no sense; they did not fairly represent the material covered. Overall, this was my least favorite class I have taken. I do NOT recommend.

hes such a nice professor. I am taking him now and i would totally recoomned him. exams are based on the book terms, lectures, and readings. you can pass with an A easy if you study and put effort. attend lectures and discussion because if you dnt attend discussin they will fail you after 4 absence. loved it!

SO BORING. Dry, long presentations, doesn't give you enough time to take down notes, holds a microphone and stands in one spot. Hard to hear. He WILL call you out if you talk and you are not to pack up until he is done talking or he gives pop quizzes. Last time he didn't give a pop quiz he just slyly added extra questions to the exam.

One of my favorite teachers. I felt comfy being in her class. Really helpful, takes it slow if students don't understand. Projects were fairly easy just took time. Don't stress if your French is rusty. She made Harry Potter examples the rest of the year after I made a reference. Just a little side note for future potterheads and whovians out there.
She is an amazing teacher! Very helpful and is willing to slowly take you through the lesson. Replies to all of your emails quickly and a nice and fun teacher in general.

She's very helpful and tries to be clear as possible. If you dont understand, she is willing to help you. She's a very good teacher and if you pay attention, you will pass her class. She replies to emails really fast and overall is a good teacher.
Clear on directions and helpful with assignments and pronunciation

The course of RUS 150 was very great. Im happy that Ive taken this course this semester. She taught me how to analyze and understand cinematic language. Moreover, the films were very great now I know more about USSR cinema.
The class was so boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Although professor Tetyana can get ahead of herself and talk for way too long during lectures, she is EXTREMELY nice and caring. She will literally give you an A for breathing. Just show up, do the little amount of work she requires, and BRING UP THAT GPAAAAA.

It was one of the easiest classes. This class is an easy A. She didn't give us any quizzes/exams/final/midterms. If you participate or at least come to class you will get A for sure. She tries to give the most important and interesting information that could be useful outside the class. I wish every teacher was like her.

A really great teacher in teaching not only the linguistic and grammatical side of Russian but also the cultural, social, and historical aspect of Russia and how it ties into the language. Very knowledgeable and very helpful. Whatever concern a student has whether in language difficulty or on a project or assignment, she'll be there on the double.

In our Russian language class, the proficiency skills were vastly varied but Tetyana managed to specifically cater to each students level and needs. If you needed more help, you only had to ask for clarification. I feel a new confidence in my speaking abilities. Class was not only traditional learning but included fun popular culture information.

Tetyana is a dedicated professor who spends extra time finding interesting materials for class. She challenged us to speak Russian the entire time, which advanced our language skills greatly. I would say she is also very intuitive and quickly senses students' personalities and learning styles, adjusting her approach accordingly. Amazing person!

Tetyana is one of the most caring and talented professors I have ever had the opportunity of taking. She is incredibly funny, passionate, and inspirational. Whether it was creating hilarious skits or discussing current events, she never failed to engage her students in entertaining educational activities and always encouraged her students.

I took a summer intensive Russian course with Tetyana. She is probably the favorite professor I have ever had. She teaches in a very hands-on way, always including real-life language applications, skits, and my personal favorite: music videos. She was always very caring and gave us breaks when we got tired. My Russian improved SO much thanks to her

Tetyana is a great professor and person. In-class speaking exercises allowed me to more comfortably and accurately speak Russian. No other professor has taught me so much about Russian culture -was introduced to a favorite Russian poet, Balmont. Definitely recommend to any serious Russian student.
It was very interesting. I have learned a lot about the Russian everyday life.
She is simply amazing. She really wants us to learn Russian. She is the best teacher I have ever had.

While she obviously cares greatly for her students and is a kind person, she is not good at teaching the Russian language. She has an over reliance on free online material, and will tell you to look there on your own time to learn extremely complicated Russian grammar instead of teach it during class. More than half the class stopped coming.

I highly recommend Professor Dziadula! I was hesitant to take an economics class but her knowledge + her engaging and enthusiastic style of teaching made it a pleasant and educational experience. She is organized, clear in explanations, cares about her studentsâ?? progress, and makes a big class feel like a small discussion group! A+  instructor.
Great professor! Makes everything crystal clear. I was also impressed how she knew my my name in a lecture hall of 150 students! impressive.

She is one of the best prof Ive had at uic. she is very reasonable with grading and assignments and exams are not too bad (she automatically gives u 15 pts so you can technically get 115% on an exam). She is excellent at teaching and is very funny. If you take this course, make sure you get her!

Amazing Prof. She is great her lectures could be boring at times but the overall class is interesting. Exams are easy I studied the day before for each exam and got B's on all of them. Just keep up with the weekly homework and quiz's and you will do fine. Highly recommend her.

Great professor, interesting class. Tests are easy if you attend lectures and study. Homework is a significant part of the grade, but not difficult. Paper is not graded harshly; lowest grade in class was a B.

Great class and great professor. She's really nice and easy going as long as you aren't being stupid in class. Respect yields respect. You need to pay attention and give effort, but there's plenty of chances for extra-credit. Highly recommend.

Her last name is Dziadula not dziuela. She's really friendly and helpful. Too many people mess up, its not a hard class so long as you attend lectures and keep up with the online assignments. She gives an okay curve too.

She's a very good teacher, she gives powerpoint slides that contain all the information for the exams. Attendance isn't mandatory but I would highly recommend it. She is extremely friendly and willing to help, she replies to all emails asap. There is one research paper which no one gets an F in, no matter how bad it is. I would HIGHLY recommend her
Only complaint is he sometimes goes off on tangents. Was polite and fair and respectful

This is for ACTG 495 - Prof McDonagh truly cares about his students, and gives plenty of opportunities for students to improve their grades. His lectures are extremely interactive, and is one of the nicest professors I've met at UIC. Definitely recommend.
He is a good teacher if you really care about your degree. His lectures are in good pace and easy to understand.
Professor McDonagh is pretty easy going. Lectures can drag, but that's the subject matter and not his fault. I left the class well prepared to take the AUD section of the CPA Exam.

I didnt like the class. Shes really nice but unorganized at times. She really loves her job and is willing to help. Its only 3 papers and a small quiz every other week. Its a pretty easy class but boring at least to me. I would always be confused in lecture but my TA helped a lot during discussion which helped me
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She's extremely passionate about what she talks about, and is an overall nice person. She's a little disorganized and all over the place but it's not too bad. She doesn't take attendance, only in discussion. She assigns readings but I didn't read them, only took notes on when she went over them in class and got an A. No exams, just papers.

Attendance is not checked during lecture but is always taken during discussion with a sign-in sheet. As far as Eaton, she is very passionate about her job and enjoys facilitating discussion during lecture. As far as grading, its not exactly easy, but if you show up to class and take a couple notes you shouldn't have a problem with her assignments.

extremely disorganized. she's tough to understand. her testsquizzespapers don't reflect what she covers in class at all. overall bad professor, which is sad because it was an interesting course topic.

Interesting things to talk about, but never stays on topic. She'll say she's gonna talk about one thing but gets wayyy off topic and carried away and never even touches what we were originally supposed to talk about. Somewhat helpful, readings are kinda difficult. Assignments are somewhat hard, but ta's are there to help. Average teacher.
Nice lady and fair teacher. Material was kind of hard but she will help you when you have questions. She's a bit unorganized and grades tough but I would take another class of hers

I've taken a handful of courses with Prof. Eaton. She's a little scattered but she's passionate about what she teaches. She's very liberal but I wouldn't say she "pushes" anything. Critical thinking skills mandatory. Show up and read the material, or else you'll be really lost.

...This class is a joke. Do not take a class with her unless you are prepared to listen to someone get sidetracked often and go on 15min tangents about politics or gender issues in a class that's supposedly about learning how to write better. Also, I have no idea what my grade is because she hasn't graded papers which we turned in months ago.

She is completely unorganized and seems to make up the syllabus and entire lectures without any prior planning. With 4 weeks left in the semester, no one has received a grade on any papers or homework which we turned in: no one has any idea what their grade is. She constantly shows up late, cancels classes and pushes liberalism and feminism. Avoid!

The topic is very interesting, if you ask questions and participate the class will be much easier. There's only 2 major essays the midterm and final. They're easy if you paid attention during lecture and discussions. If anything doesn't make sense ask questions during lecture, or the TA during discussions. Highly recommend this class.
I thought she was very energetic and she was nice and helpful when i asked her for help. The class isnt hard its just alot of reading. the topic is interesting!
I totally loved this class!!!! It was awesome and was also a good topic. If your lucky you'll get Issac as your TA... He was a great help and understanding the readings. :)

She is very energetic and passionate about what she teaches. If you don't have an even cursory interest in the topic, then don't take the class. Do the reading, talk in class, just don't expet her to agree with you. She can be harsh in grading. But I enjoyed the class overall.

She is very kind, and very energetic. I didn't have any problems with her grading, I thought she was rather flexible. She loves what she teaches. Her "favorites" are simply the students who actually participate, rather than collect cobwebs in the back of the class. Take her, VERY little course work, and very interesting topics :)

Passionate about what she teaches but expects WAY TOO MUCH from her students. grades a 100 level class as if its a graduate course. If you give her exactly what she's looking for, she'll still give you a C. ive taken over 10 philosophy courses at UIC, some 400 level, and this is THE worst grading.
Save yourself! Do not take this professor. She is very rude, has her favorites in class and is extremely strict on attendance. She always talks about herself. Not what I expected at all!

She is too strict with attendancce. We had assigned seats in a crowed lecture hall! The discussion is very "liberal" meaning if you have her veiws you're right if you don't "at least you're consistent." I expected more from this class
There are favorites, so just make sure you're one of them. Attend class and speak up and you'll get at least a B.
Amazing prof and exciting and stimulating lectures!  TAKE HER CLASSES FOR SURE!!!

Shane is a great instructor. I was able to grasp a lot of new concepts this semester; he's very helpful and kind. His classes can be a little boring, but hey, it's a grammar class lol. He incorporates activities and discussions, and a lot of group work, which makes it fun. Honestly, I would take more classes with him; I definitely recommend him!

Profesor Ebert is so nice! I was nervous about taking SPAN 103 because I struggle with Spanish, but he is good at teaching and allows you to make mistakes without penalty. He is really understanding of the fact that learning a foreign language is hard. He is SUCH AN EASY GRADER. Overall, I enjoyed SPAN 103 with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Super chill overall

Professor Ebert is awesome! I am taking his class online due to COVID & it is synchronous. There is a lot of homework assignments but they are not very long and they really help boost your grade. He is a fair grader and is really understanding. SPAN102 material is the same for everyone, so I would suggest taking it with someone who is kind & fair!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: He's a sweet guy and if you stay on your game with assignments and learning the material then you'll do good. Great choice for teacher and for class to take. Class is fun
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The professor is super knowledgeable, but it can be a little difficult understanding the concepts at times. I think he could work on adding even more examples in the lecture, bc ling is based on looking at patterns. Tests are take home, but they are very very long. Weekly hw assignment and 2 excused absences, which I think should at least be 3.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly, his class is extremely boring. There is lots of busy work, but he's a nice guy and if you do the work you'll get an A.
do yourself a favor and do not take 202 with him
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I believe Shane Ebert did a good job discussing the topics. They could get complicated so obviously there was some confusion but he always took time to ask if anyone had questions and would explain in various ways until the student understood the concept. Easy grader and I liked how he didn't just lecture the whole time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: If you are doing the teaching of Spanish program or majoring in Spanish, do not pick Shane for the love of God. He can't teach. Never give the right examples and contradicts himself a lot. I had to really learn outside of class because he is confusing. If you have time to teach yourself after going to class, do it. But if you don't, drop the class.

Do not recommend. I took the Span 202 course for fun and because of the difficulty had to drop out. The tests are very hard and despite everyone getting a C or less, he doesn't curve his tests. The tests make up 60% of your grade, so it will tough to get a good grade. Cool dude outside of class, but I highly recommend any other teacher but Shane.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Shane is a great guy. Attendance is mandatory so you need to go or else you won't pass, but he's an easy grader. Participation really doesn't matter, but try your best and it'll pay off.

Going to the class was more confusing than strictly teaching yourself the Spanish grammar because he didn't know what he was doing, but attendance was necessary. He would explain things incorrectly or make a bunch of errors in examples and we were constantly confused. Meet up with students outside of class and teach yourselves.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's good at explaining everything and making sure everyone understands. His lectures are long are boring af. He is not at all lenient when it comes to grading.

Overall, Spanish 206 was a very challenging, but some of the topics within linguistics are very interesting! I also suggesting studying early for tests, because the tests can be challenging. Shane can be very awkward, but he is easy to talk with after class.  He provides all reading and homework materials for students. The T.A.'s were also useful!
Speaks in english which is great! Fair grader but you really have to exert effort for the A

he can go quickly at times but he gets his point across and gets you prepared for the tests. the tests in 202 are really long so be prepared to work quickly. hes a good one to have! but this class isnt a piece of cake it takes work, unlike the 100 level spanish classes at uic

I took Ebert for Span 202 and the course was moderately tough. There's homework due every week (Sunday 11:59 p) through BB and there were about 3 tests which were also moderately tough (but straight forward). If you visit his office hours, he's nice and helpful. This is not a blow off class, I got a B.
He teaches kinda fast, but his tests are straightforward. He tends to be a push-over so our class did whatever we wanted.
Really nice guy, but cant effectively teach...i had to rely on my high school skills
This class is very interesting....recommended.
I'd been waiting to take 455, and I really enjoyed this class.

I enjoyed the way the class was structured.  It was a lot of work, but I was able to get a lot of out the course by keeping up with the reading material, starting the project early and using the TAs.  It was exciting to gain exposure to so many different areas within of tissue engineering.  I was challenged, but I definitely recommend.

This class is all over the place. Exams and HW are not like what is lectured in class. Lots of group work so good luck if you have someone who doesnt wanna work since youre stuck with them. Pop quizzes were not effective whatsoever and are used as a scare tactic. Best part was guest lectures as I learned the most from those.
This class helped motivate me to apply to graduate school to do research in tissue engineering.
Motivational and exciting introduction to the field!
The exams and HW have nothing to do with the lecture material. Lots of guest lecturers. He doesn't care if the whole class is struggling, but there's a good curve in the end. Good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ebony is a great teacher as he seems to really value balanced lectures as well as students participation in group activities. Ebony teaches humanity!!!
