reviews.comment: Ethan is an excellent instructor, probably the best I've had at UIC. His class is very fair, if you show up and pay attention you will learn a LOT. I landed a SWE internship at a Fortune 500 this upcoming summer and 80 percent of the knowledge I used to pass the interview came from his lectures. He is extremely dedicated to helping his students!

You can tell he loves what he's doing. His lectures are very easy to listen to and understand. He's very knowledgeable, funny, and interactive with students. Would definitely recommend him over other cs251 professors. Hands down my favorite professor on campus.
Great professor! Lectures give you material needed to complete the projects. There's also an army of TA's to help you!
Great prof with a heavily loaded course. 251 is filled with projects, but the lectures cover everything you need for them.

Super knowledgeable and available in office hours even for advice on personal projects. Medium to hard quizzes and satisfyingly tricky projects. Lectures were easy to follow, take notes from, and material was meticulously recorded and organized. Takes comments on learning style to heart and changes explanations for students.

One of the best CS teachers you can find at UIC. Lectures are engaging and the projects are always about what you see in the lectures. There are THOUSANDS of office hours and the prof. is accessible/explains very well. I really enjoyed this class!

Genuinely does not make sense to give us 4 exams that are only 10-12 questions long and make them worth 24% of our grade. Each question you get wrong drops your exam grade a letter grade essentially and there is no partial credit. Should have just had two/three written exams with 50 questions like every single other professor does.

Prof. Ordentlich is an exemplary professor; I regularly went to office hours despite doing really well in the class because I loved seeing how he interacted and helped his students. He offers specific, actionable and concise feedback on any topic you can possibly think of. Head and shoulders above a lot of teaching staff I've taken classes with.

Ethan has a brilliant mind. He's got a really deep understanding of C++ and loves teaching.

He designs projects and quiz questions which test the concepts, but also are highly applicable. Although we didn't always make it through all the slides most of the time, Ethan's lectures are really comprehensive and doesn't leave any question unanswered.

I actually took another course with her, not 421. But anyway, her course organization is fine. But, she is extremely critical and questioning of students and their work. She microanalyzes "flaws" and rarely compliments. Other than that, she seems passionate about teaching.

She is okay and seems to care. But she doesn't seem very knowledgeable and up to date on some topics. She's also extremely straightforward and critical which intimidates students especially when I need to talk to her 1:1 in person.
Good teacher, explains things well and very approachable.

Great professor, interesting homework, exams not too difficult (she asks exactly what is done in class, so one just need to review). The class itself is a good mix of computer science and linguistics.

I took Jakob for 361 in the Spring. He knows his stuff, but his teaching style is extremely hard to follow. He is also very disrespectful toward his students. His exams are worth basically the whole class and participation scores are based off of an iclicker that he made which doesn't work. He has no slides, he just stands and plays in terminal.
Prof. Eriksson is super knowledgeable. Just wished he had more structure in the class - otherwise he is great

Professor Ericsson is very knowledgeable, but at times the material presented was unclear or inaccurate. Really great and knowledgeable professor. A lot of learning is done outside of class via the homeworks but his grading is fair. One of the best professors at UIC.

One of the best professors at UIC. Took his CS 463. The course is on the harder side with 5 tests (4 quarterly and 1 final). Going to his office hours helped with the homework. Is really knowledgeable and passionate.

reviews.comment: The content is difficult but interesting. The professor does do a good job teaching, though I may be biased on this.

Lectures is essentially the whole class browsing and examining source code; extremely interesting and engaging. Course is graded entirely on exams with optional HWs acting as the study material. Every course should be an Eriksson course!
captivating lectures, engaging homeworks, more focus on learning than on grades, exams are tough, difficult to get an A

A very technical professor, you would learn a lot watching him work.

he is a really good professor if you want to take charge of your own learning. lots of hands-on work during lecture. make sure to take notes and do your own assignments. the quizzes and exams are the toughest parts of the class, but just learn the "tricks" to answer his questions and pay close attention to his wording.

reviews.comment: Get ready to WORK. If you think you have the “A” formula, you are incredibly wrong when it comes to this class. Challenging but rewarding course. Professor is knowledgeable and engaging. Highly recommend utilizing resources like the textbook, study sessions, and tools like unstuck study to succeed.

Doesn't work blackboard well, assignments have no feedback, lectures follow no style, considers 50% average good, study guide? whats that? Due to the nature of the course having so many solutions for problems you think there would be a structure around how to use the tools and assignments to test the capabilites of students but nah wing it lectures

Awesome Professor. Class is very difficult, and takes a lot of hard work to understand the material, and dig through the code to finish the homework. The professor is Brilliant, passionate about teaching, and cares about his students.

Whether or not you enjoy a class taught by Professor Eriksson depends entirely on your own learning style. This class is just the professor pulling up some code and running experiments on it with input from students. Expect very difficult exams. If you like his teaching style, it will be a great fun class, but it did not work for me. Nice professor
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The professor is very unique in his way of teaching in a good way ofcourse. I would suggest taking any class with him
Great professor, great course

First of all this course will give you the full understating of kernel, which is going to help you in long run as computer engineer/developer.
Professor is very experienced and have designed the homework, quizes, exam very carefully.
His lectures are well thought and full of core concepts.
He is always open for discussions, inside or outside class.

He's one of my favorite if not my favorite professor at UIC. He emphasizes learning the material throughout the class and grades based on how much you understand. It is a difficult class, but the curves are generous (A - 70%, B - 50%, etc.). He is a very knowledgeable person and an excellent professor. I really learned a lot from this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: An amazing professor. Super knowledge and helpful. He really want's his students to learn and understand the material. His exams are tough, he expects 50% average on his exams, so don't beat yourself up about a bad score. He doesn't make lecture slides, he really dives into the code which I think is valid for an OS class. Always up for discussion.

He's a great teacher that would happy to discuss and explain, though his hw/quiz/exam are super hard, you'll need to spend a lot of time on it.
Even though I didn't do well in class, I'm still like his lecture and would rewatch them again and again to understand the class.

Lack of lecture slides make it harder to prepare for the always difficult 361 exams. Labs and the textbook help, but to a point. 1 cheat sheet per exam is very helpful however. Homeworks are doable but take a lot of time, so prepare beforehand.

A was achievable with some effort. HWs could be done easily if you knew what lecture and lab code were doing. Lectures were very helpful and professor was open to answering all questions, but you had to attend in person. Reading the textbook was a huge help for the exams.

- Exams based on homework
- Labs help directly with homework
- Lectures help directly with homework
- Homework challenges you as a programmer, but in the systems domain
- This semester, if final was better than midterm, then final took place of midterm.
- All labs were extra credit (up to 10% total)
- 10% end-of-semester participation bonus

I learned a lot in this course and have a better understanding of low-level programming than I did in CS 261. It is noted that you should probably take 15 credit hours or less with this professor, but if you are willing to put in the work, you will surely receive a good result. I love the lecturing style even though most people disliked it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I felt like Prof. Erikson cared about how the students did in his class. The lectures consist of him coding live and you need to ask a lot of questions and attend live to get the most out of them. This was an issue with a lot of fellow students, a lot of people didn't attend live (admittedly, I am one of them). Overall I learned a lot in this class
The professor's lecture style is very difficult to comprehend. His assignments are extremely poorly worded and not for the faint of the heart. Be prepared to spend all your time in OH

This class with Eriksson is insanely hard. Avoid taking him at all cost if you do not want to be clueless with weird requirements. He had an extremely high RMP rating when I took it but I should not have based my decision on RMP. The biggest regret of my life.
Do not take him for 361. He is very confusing and unorganized. Don't base the decision on good reviews from 385 and 461. The class has been nothing but struggle.

Jacob is a really good professor, he cares about his students. Though the homework is hard, we got extension for most of the homework. Also, I suggest reading the textbook before coming to the lecture,  if you don't read the textbook, it's definitely hard to follow his lecture. No lecture slides and good exam review, I think he need to improve.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The homeworks are so vague with no clear description. The class is structured poorly. His knowledge of OS is extremely superior but only people in 461 can understand him because of their prior familiarity with 361. With 361, the story changes completely. Would love to take him for 461 but never for 361.

His lectures are helpful for homework (aka mini-projects) which our grade is half based on, but he's had to give extensions to most homework. This just shows the lack of understanding he's able to provide to his students within lectures. I was excited for a teacher with an amazing rating, but this is just very disappointing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: No slides to at least help me learn from. Hard homework that helps us think on our own and research, but he just fiddles around in the terminal during most lectures assuming all his students understand all these commands being used. I'm here to learn but I haven't even been taught all these basics or what all these input combinations mean.

Professor expects you to figure out homework on your own. Lectures is 1.5 hours looking at the terminal of him coding and no slides. No plan when doing lecture, just kind of go with the flow. Labs are very helpful because of the T.A.
He's interesting and chill

The professor is knowledgeable but sometimes moves fast because the material comes easy to him. Homework and exams decide your grade. Doesn't use slides but he codes live which really helps for the HW. The HW is pretty hard but you learn a lot doing the homework and going to labs. No review for exams so what will be on the exam is not specific.

Eriksson is very smart though be warned that if you are hoping for a braindead class where all you have to do to get an A is memorize a bunch of slides and take an exam where all this info is just recycled then this professor is not for you. Deeply thinking about the concepts is a requirement if you want to do well which I very much appreciated.

The biggest problem with the lectures is that there are no slides. For example, he uses a notepad and draws diagrams of what's going on, but doesn't post these anywhere. What would help a lot is if these diagrams were in the form of slides which he simply went through so we can follow and refer to. Slides would make this class substantially easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very clear in presenting lectures, and helpful in answering questions

One of the best and most knowledgeable CS professors at UIC. He is tough but fair. All the relevant material was covered in class with great detail, his lecture style gets criticized but I vastly prefer it to slide reading. His in-class coding shows you how he debugs and uses tools which in turn has helped me become better at C/Rust and Linux.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Dr. Eriksson is the most knowledgeable professor I have ever had at UIC. His lectures are structured in such a way that if you do not take advantage of this fact then will not do well. The reason is because like many have stated his lectures are completely improvised hence you need to ask questions to get the most out of them.

I really enjoyed his lecture style however the lack of slides makes studying for his exams difficult. The lecture style is loosely structured and allows for experimentation. Attending lab sections is optional and you could receive up to 13% EC by attending. His homework assignments are challenging but they help you learn a lot. Starting early helps

His style of winging it shows as there has been multiple times during lectures where he forgets the exact Linux command and then has to look it up on the man pages. Deciding to teach this class with one section in Rust and the other in C made no one show up one time to one of the Rust lectures. How can you learn a language AND systems programing???
he fell off

Has 0 slides, he kind of wings it every lecture, and every lecture is him typing in the terminal thinking we understand what's going on and doesn't truly explain everything. Hasn't taught this class since 2013. Midterm average was a 10/23. No good exam prep. I feel so lost despite knowing people in the class. WORST CLASS out of my 3 years.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was by far the most horribly managed class I have taken. There are no lecture slides and the lectures usually consist of him typing in terminal commands and expecting us to know what's happening.There is no preparation for the exams. We are thrown into the void and it is survival of the fittest.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lectures felt unstructured and improvised, mainly consisting of Eriksson sitting at his computer and coding/debugging Rust for an hour. Lack of proper lecture slides or class notes makes it very difficult to study, and the professor's online attitude is obnoxiously sarcastic and snarky. 361 is a hard class, and Eriksson did not make it easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Attend class, start homework early, study for tests, and take notes. Forget one and may God have mercy on your soul. Enthusiastic enough in lectures to keep my attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: His lectures are horrible and really hard to follow. It's like he goes in circles before saying important information. He doesn't plan anything at all. No slides/notes. You'll basically be teaching yourself. He says that he "improvises" his lectures. The labs are good for the homework. He rudely responds to questions on piazza as if you were dumb.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Eriksson is really nice and knowledgeable! But be prepared that he likes to have a huge curve in the class - so don't feel too bad if you get like 50% on the exam, it will probably be about the average grade. HWs can take a long time (and maybe make you suffer a little), but they are interesting

I took this class for a free elective as a CS major. Professor's lectures are very helpful for homework but it usually requires a little bit extra looking up to do the homeworks. This class is definitely worth taking if you're a CS student, easy to understand concepts and will be useful for learning about different BASH commands. Good class/prof.

CS294 was LINUX/UNIX Bootcamp this semester. Professor Eriksson is a great lecturer and will give you all the info you need for assignments but he goes FAST so you will definitely need to pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Eriksson is extremely experienced on what he teaches, so the live coding you see in lecture teaches you a lot (unlike other professors who are not so nimble live). The lectures contain all of what you'll need to know for this class, so take notes there. To take advantage of the course play with bash and come with questions/challenges.

For the first time teaching Rust, Professor Eriksson gave great lectures and assignments to supplement learning a new language. Graciously offered extensions when needed and checked in to make sure students were understanding the concepts. Not an easy class, but would definitely recommend taking a course with him.

Professor Eriksson is clearly knowledgeable about the subject matter. It was tough at times but you get out what you put in. It was interesting to go through different techniques of tracking a programs performance. Understanding how a program interacts with memory and interpreting it's performance are important skills to have as a programmer.

Professor Eriksson is enthusiastic about the material and you will learn a lot if you keep up with the class. Some of the homework assignments were a ton of work, but if you do them, you will really understand the material. The exams do not require weeks of preparation and memorization, but they do require you to go to class (or watch lectures).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Pros: Great professor and class, lectures and projects teach a lot about networking. Office hours are helpful. Lectures recorded Cons: Very Difficult projects, Need a good grasp of low level programming + networking to complete. No lecture slides Verdict: Take if you're willing to work hard and want to learn about networking, Don't take if not
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: It's not very often you find a class that you can attend, digest knowledge, and not be so stressed out about getting every last detail in a notebook. If you're willing to do a little work, you will get whatever grade you are shooting for.

I took cs461 (OS) last fall under him and took a new class covering performance this semester. Both were the most challenging classes I'd taken up till that point. At the end of the class, I felt like I genuinely learnt something new which changed the direction of my future studies. I would highly recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Enjoyed my time in his class.
Good Professor.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Awesome professor, need to go to class to get the most out of lectures. He records them, though, so all is not lost if you miss. Make sure to keep up.

The best course I took at UIC. The professor has in-depth knowledge of the topics and is passionate about teaching them. The assignments are relatively hard work but very interesting and challenging. Definitely recommended!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The professor has a deep knowledge of the topic and is able to transmit it during lesson and with some challenging homework. Lessons are very practical: usually a new concept or tool is introduced and discussed with some code examples. Highly recommended if interested in performance topic.

Professor Eriksson is one of the most brilliant professor's I've ever had the pleasure of taking a course with. He does live examples and is so knowledgeable about his field. While many professors who are doing research don't focus very hard on the courses they teach, Eriksson does. He even wrote a book to go along with the course! Highly recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's a passionate guy who really enjoys teaching. OS won't be a black box to you after taking this course. It is like taking the red pill (of "The Matrix" movie fame) and staying in the Wonderland, while the Prof. shows you how deep the rabbit hole goes. Definitely a rewarding class. Tip : Don't miss the homeworks and class lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He teaches the course in a way that makes something as arcane as operating systems and kernels approachable. Always up for a great discussion during the office hours and a fun person in general.

Key points of the course: 1. Professor is very knowledgeable and passionate about teaching this course 2. Challenging n exciting homeworks 3. Rather than being another memory test, exams were efficiently designed to test students' understanding of the subject 4. After finishing this course, you will be in a position where you can make your own OS

Operating systems is a difficult topic but Professor Eriksson really strives to make sure you can understand the material. He regularly has office hours where you can ask for help on homework or more explanation on a topic. His lectures are available if you miss a class, but I personally recommend you attend class, then re-watch the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Would take again

reviews.comment: Amazing course structure and very practical approach. Video recordings are a real help.
10/10 would take again.
I have taken Operating Systems course with Prof Eriksson and liked it very much! The course was hard! Professor is very competent, accessible, professional, caring.
385 with Eriksson was one of my favorite classes at UIC.

A great course that will help you get a well rounded understanding of how a basic operating system functions. I would highly recommend everyone to take this course. Although it may be difficult, you will also have other students struggling with you (which means you'll be saved by a curve.) Do every single homework and visit the TA if needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very hard class with a lot of work. If you devote the required time you will pass and you will learn an incredible amount doing so. Eriksson is a great professor and knows his stuff. His lectures are engaging and interesting. He is sometimes condescending to us lowly students but that's understandable given his academic level. Great prof and class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I do not recommend CS 385 with Eriksson if you are not already a pro C/kernel hacker.  No homework/test solutions to study from after turning in work/exams, and no sample exams.  Lectures are recorded, but are not well organized, and the textbook has no relation to what we do in class.  Not set up for a hard-working, non-genius student to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Professor Eriksson was one of the best professors I've had at UIC. Always willing to answer questions in and out of class, enjoyable lectures, and learned a ton. Learned a lot about operating systems in general and picked up some useful Linux skills on the way. Exams were extremely hard, but was a fair grader. Very knowledgeable. Awesome af.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the best and hardest classes that I have taken. He forces you to fully understand what is happening in an operating system to be able to solve the homeworks. Homeworks are usually weekly and make sure that you start them early. I would recommend this class and this professor to any in CS at UIC
Probably one of the best CS professor I ever had. The course is work-load heavy, but the lectures helps a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Probably second hardest class I have ever taken in my 4 year university career. The class revolves around learning important OS concepts by adding features to xv6 (a learning unix-based OS from MIT). Programming all in C and a little in Assembly. HW will take VERY LONG hours learning the code of xv6 and debugging. Recorded lectures. Great prof!

Great class, but requires a lot of work and a lot of understanding of the materials.  He said on the first day that we'd be spending around 15 hoursweek on this class, and he was not wrong.  The weekly projects are tough, but manageable.  Exams are just as tough as the projects, but really are there to show what you've learned throughout the term.
World class teacher and brilliant hacker
Every week, I spent 15 hours on struggling with homework. Exams are too tough.

Great class.  One of my most rewarding CS classes for sure.  I think the prof is too quick to assume a students' questions are trivial, but he'll own up to it when he's wrong.  Lectures are worth re-watching online, and assignments are very valuable learning experiences.

Eriksson is a very passionate professor, but his projects are very straining for the average student. Naturally, the experienced find the class tough but completable, But %85 of the class really has a hard time keeping their head above water. For some the end grades make the over-ambitious set of projects worth-while. But truly less would be more.
Very few professors teach so well that you learn to love what you're studying. Eriksson did that. Definitely the hardest class I've taken so far but also the most beneficial and most worthwile.

One of the hardest classes I've taken at the school, but I don't think you can get through the class and say you haven't learned anything. Well thought-out homeworks that teach you everything you could want to know about low-level programming and more. You should take at least one Eriksson class before you graduate.

Great professor, workload was almost brutal but incredibly rewarding and worthwhile. Definitely a course I learned the most in and was not the bane of my existence. If you get the chance to take a course taught by him, just do it. If a class conflicts with a course taught by him, drop it.

Best professor at UIC. The guy is brilliant yet super helpful and approachable. Extremely engaging lectures consisting of on-screen C hackery and puzzles. Homeworks are original and very applicable in the "real world". Give a solid effort and you will learn a crazy amount. Can't recommend enough.
Extremely knowledgable in all areas covered in class. He codes a lot in class, shows off many useful UNIX and C tricks. If you have an opportunity to take this class with him, just register ASAP.

One of the best courses ever. If you ever want to learn about Comp. Nets in theory and practice, this is the course. A tough course so plan accordingly. Worth the effort you put in. You'll never regret taking this course, be whatever grade you get. I've seen courses where your interest is wrecked by the professor, this is not a place for that.
Awesome Professor, awesome course and interesting homeworks! Glad I took it!
Great professor. You will learn plenty. Interesting topics. Don't think about it, if you can take a class with him do it.

Professor is one of the best professor in UIC Computer Science Department. I had taken CS450 Introduction to Networking when he taught. His Lectures are really interesting. Time just goes and the homeworks/assignments he gives is programminng intensive mostly in C , some ib bash scripting. A lot of learning.

Great Professor. Super helpful during office hours. You will learn a lot in his class. Extremely fair grader, gives you plenty of opportunities to improve your grade. An A is possible if you complete all the assignments and do decent on the exams. I highly recommend this professor and course. Hopefully I get a chance to take more classes with him!
Great professor!

Great class. Homework assignments are challenging(for most), but really help the student develop a deeper understanding of how user applications and operating systems interact. The professor does a good job at explaining difficult concepts and is always open for questions during lectures.

This class seems to have a hype surrounding it as being the most difficult CS class. It was definitely challenging, but always fair. Professor Eriksson gives out more than enough extra points to receive a decent grade. If you put the effort into this class, getting an A won't be difficult.
One of the best professors at UIC. HW assignments are fun and challenging.

Intense C programming. The assignments are refreshingly original compared to CS107/201/202/340 where the focus is on boring games. I loved the discussions we had on Piazza. I think it's important to mention Tim Merrifield (TA) because he was a lifesaver with assisting on homeworks etc etc. Erikssons a pretty cool Professor. Dedicated and Original.

Professor Eriksson is extremely brilliant. He know C like the back of his hand. You will learn a lot from his class. However, the homeworks are punishing, especially if you have a heavy course load. The grades you receive can be disheartening but there is a curve. Even still, you will learn a lot from his class.

I started this class with low confidence, got really less in homeworks, but can't deny how much I learned in it. He is really good. He gives plenty of chances to make up for any lost scores. You may not get good grades, its okay, you will learn a lot and every minute of his lecture is totally worth listening.

His homework/projects are brutal and half the class often gets 0 points on them, but is one of the most brilliant professors I've had at UIC. Became proficient in C in one semester with this guy. The grade you get is not as important as the knowledge you learn in this class, you just need to put in effort.

The course is excellent and the professor is very direct and crisp in class.  If you pay attention and work on the exercises, there is no way you won't learn a ton.  Also, its nice to have a CS professor who isn't afraid of code!
Eriksson's courses are brutally challenging, but are equally rewarding if you put in the effort. I would gladly take any course he teaches.

Extremely challenging class but I learned a lot. Professor Eriksson is one of a kind. His teaching style is very unique but engaging. His class is extremely organized. But his homeworks and exams will be the hardest things you'll do in undergrad.
#ez
Difficult but you learn a lot
.Very fair in grading. Extremely smart teacher,explains everything as clearly as possible. Likes student participation and questions. Is always willing to help people in the class.
My friends and I have a rule, if Eriksson is teaching a class, we have to take it! Yes, his courses are challenging, but it's the challenge that makes learning the material so rewarding.
Excellent course. Has home-works every week, which require good programming skills. Posts video lectures and attendance not mandatory. Possibly, the toughest and most useful course in CS dept. :)
Awesome!! particular about grades. If you want to learn Networks, go to him. He's the man..
Great for programming practice. Not so great to learn conceptual side of the topic. Lectures are not structured very well and some class time gets wasted.
Expect hard studying, lots of programming in c and bash! Must understand the concepts really well to do good in the hws and exams.
a nice way to learn about networking

Took CS385 and CS450 with Eriksson, have to admit it was the best choice I made while at UIC. Eriksson is the GREATEST professor at UIC. Very intelligent guy, definitely knows his stuff and makes class fun. Class is very challenging but you LEARN a lot! If you have a chance of taking a class with Jakob do it!!!!
One of the best prof at UIC. Take this course if you are looking for programming intensive course.

Hands the best CS professor in UIC. Very effective teaching strategies, live coding, use of visuals, C language. He is a very knowledgeable person, I learned a lot in his classes. I wish other professors were like this.
Excellent course

He is THE best professor one could dream of. Makes you work your ass out, true. But in the end, when you look back, you'll feel you've accomplished something. My time in UIC will be remembered the most for Prof.Eriksson.

He is THE best professor one could dream of. Makes you work your ass out, true. But in the end, when you look back, you'll feel you've accomplished something. My time in UIC- will be remembered the most for Prof.Eriksson.
Great prof!
Excellent course !! I learnt a lot from this course and I love learning from the assignments he gives.
awesome
Great course! Awesome professor! Should teach more courses! love coding and he gives lots of it in assignments!
Best teacher I've ever had.  Makes you apply what he teaches and you really LEARN how things work.
Really cool prof who will make you strong in networking basics in just 3 months!
Interesting lectures. Lots of homework though. About one assignment per week
Liked his style of teaching.
His course is challenging, but he helps a lot.
Best professor you can ask for considering super-hard homeworks each week.

All lectures are recorded. Ten homeworks allow to practice in C, scripting and even latex. The professor is very friendly and fun. I would recommend taking even for students not pursuing networking or systems development.
Great class. Challenging/rewarding assignments. Exams are like trying to deactivate a bomb in the movie Speed. Attendance is not mandatory but the professor is great eye candy ;).

This course has weekly programming assignments. They are meant to be challenging, but you're rewarded with hands-on networking experience. Lectures are all recorded online. The professor is very enthusiastic about teaching and does a great job at explaining real-world concepts. He makes the challenging assignments all worth it in the end.

Truly an asset to the computer department at UIC. His assignments, although overwhelming at times, make the best use of your time. The programming assignments are there not only to learn the topics in class, but to exercise your programming skills in order for you to gain the appropriate skills to a be better programming

Prof. Eriksson is excellent: the lectures are fast paced demos and concept mapping, illustrated top-down. Lectures are very current, and entertaining. He expects a little bit of class discussion, which helps with clarity. The homework and tests are difficult. He's not joking about how much of a load this class is. But classes with him are worth it.

Truly a C/Linux Genius that want's to pass his knowledge to all students. A lot of C assignments but it will benefit you in the future. Lectures are online which is a great plus for commuting students, although I will recommend going to his classes.

Very time consuming class, homeworks once a week that take 5+ hours to complete.  Class is extremely hard but very rewarding, was worth every moment.  Great professor recommend any class he teaches, you will learn more with him then any other professor.

Jakob Eriksson is an inspirational professor who 'acts as your tour guide', in his own words; for this top-down course in Computer Networks. Live programming is combined with animated discussions in class, while the home-works give you something to brag about (like intercepting wifi packets or 180 hosts all pinging each other). Admire His passion.
The best professor you could ask for!

Prof. Eriksson is funny, inspiring, and brilliant. Through hard work, you'll quickly learn the importance of each network layer and use a few RFCs to write your own network programs. The competitive nature of his class adds an extra incentive to excel in it. I recommend knowing at least a little C before taking CS 450 with him.

Sounds like a professor usually, but every so often he'll say something like one of your hacker friends (in a good way). He's always prepared and seems to know darn near everything. Tolerates your dumb questions/comments with a smile.  Assigns C and shell scripting for homework.  Take a course with him before he's deemed too good to teach.

He makes subject very interesting by giving hard and practical homeworks. It needs the right idea to hit on to do his assignments or exams. It makes one feel good about themselves once they do the work given. Its a very nice course and students will definitely learn the subject. It'll give motivation to learn beyond the syllabus.
Cool, helpful professor with a good positive attitude. Makes you work for what you get. Interesting lectures.Lots of stuff to learn from him. Wish I could work under him too!

If interested in computer networks&programming, this's definitely a must have class in UIC. Very well prepared lectures, carefully designed homework are among the highest quality in CS depts. The homework are a bit of challenging. However, for those preparing careers in CS, I believe leaving the hard time in school is a better idea. ILoveThisCourse

The course is challenging and involves a lot of programming, so those coming from other universities might want to be well prepared for that. Despite this, Eriksson takes time with his students and if you go to office hours, you will receive the assistance you need. Lectures are entertaining.

Amazing professor. One of the best players in the game. Lectures are very well presented and complimented with helpful demos. Homeworks are plentiful, practical, fun, and force you to learn tools like svn, LaTex, gnuplot, Perl, shell scripting, awk, etc. If you're interested in Networking then make sure to take it with Jakob. He knows his stuff.
Though tough in scoring, he was a motivating professor, whoes grading made one try hard till the last.He gave a nonstop guidance through out the course. On the whole a dedicated professor :)

Most important thing is not that he is a great professor but the important thing is 'he is a great person'. He is equally fair to all students and very gentle in his attitudes. Wish him all the success in his future endeavors.

Jacob is amazing with his teaching esp. the way he create the slides on the go. He is my role model and because of him I am loving networking more than the one when I had before attending his class. Jacob you rock :-)

Amazing guy! Probably the best Prof. I've come across... He is what you get when an uberhacker comes to teach. Wish I could do his homeworks a bit better ... Warning: The course he is teaching at UIC is a misnomer - if you know nothing about networks and C programming - you wont survive the ordeal. But he is THE PROF, wish I could work under him!

He is the toughest CS profs in the department. His exams average to like 30-35%. His homeworks are impossible to do, specially for undergrad. THIS IS A VERY CHALLENGING COURSE NOT FOR UNDERGRAD.One project to do which is IMPOSSIBLE. home work is also impossible. If you ask question in email he just says "google it". Don't even try to take this class, don't even bother, there's absolutely nothing to learn from this class. Di Eugenio is a terrible professor, absolutely terrible!

a HUGE WASTE of my time, the book is horrible, she's the only prof teaching this class. i REALLY REGRET taking this class, ANYTHING IS BETTER. Try anything from troy, troy is good. BUT DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!

Very nice professor, intelligent, smart. You have to read a lot, post postings online, participate in class. If you show him your hardwork you will get an A. Takes attendance, allows you to miss 5 classes max.

I didn't like him as much. He started out ok but his accent makes him a really dull professor. Theres no interesting discussions you can fall asleep and still get an A. You do have to participate once in a while. Basically really dull but an easy A and not too hard except if you hate essays and long articles.

He is a pretty cool teacher but at times he can be very confusing. It's really easy to get an a as long as you do the blackboard postings and the two papers he assigns. You read pretty good novels and short stories in his class.
He is a very cool and laid back teacher.
Very nice and smart teacher just do the postings online and you can get an A
Professor is awesome. He's a little slow but he's nice and relaxed. If you do journals and keep up with class activities you're almost guaranteed an A.

Professor Kang is a very kind person. He is very lenient with homework and grades. It is impossible for to fail his class unless you do not do blackboard posting or miss class too often. Discussions in class are interesting and are based on the reading. If you do not like to read a lot do not take this class!
very helpful and understanding professor.
Very chill, calm, and understanding professor. A little too non-assertive--will accept slacking a bit too much but generally a nice guy and an easy class.

Dude was super chill and laid back, globalization was a some what interesting topic which included a ton of outside work. but overall its an easy A if you attend class and don't completely fail at writing papers.

Great teacher. Very, very blunt though. Don't be offended. His advice is always helpful and will help your writing become. Highly recommended you take if you need to do Advanced Fiction. Very laid back, great conversations.
Wild Man is very down to earth and probably the best English professor at UIC.
Is a bit blunt, but is willing to extend deadlines. Very understanding and accommodating, though.

Not as bad as most would say. He's a nice guy but can be irritating with how much work there is and his grading criteria. Keep track of the due dates or else you're going to stress out. So many group presentations but very little time to work on them. Overall enjoyed the class mostly because it was a small class size and everyone was cool.

Very confusing. Not only with the ever changing assignment list but also with what he says in class. He can't finish a sentence that he starts. Spare yourself the headache and find a different teacher.

If you enjoy typing a lot of pointless papers (Articles, individual paper, chapter questions, team questions) with a professor that can't explain what he wants and learning nothing from the professor since he doesn't teach you the content. This is the class for you!

The professor rambles and completely confuses the entire class. He seems to relish in being unhelpful and this is also reflected in his Blackboard activities. Nothing is organized. It's like a garage sale of online assignments to sort through.

Fregetto's teaching methods don't foster the success of his students. Relevance of the material was not established until the last week of class - when the final project was due along with four other assignments that he forgot to assign during the semester. I have had hard teachers but I have never had this much resentment towards any of them.

As a marketing major, Consumer Behavior is a critical course to take. Sadly, I learned nothing in this class due to Fregetto's teaching style. He should no longer be teaching at UIC, professors like him are the reason the CBA has a bad reputation. I'm now considering changing my major after taking this class. Buyer beware...

This is by far the worst professor and class I have taken at UIC. Do not, under any circumstances, take any course with Professor Fregetto. Seriously - avoid him at all costs!
Do not take him! He is the worst teacher at UIC and simply does not care about his students. He just makes everyones life miserable.

If you can at all avoid it...DO NOT TAKE THIS INSTRUCTOR.  I am a marketing major and this was by far my least favorite class in four years.  He is incomprehensible, assigns a huge course load in a small amount of time, and is just not a nice person.  I think he should be reviewed and removed from this school!!!

Absolutely horrible,  being in the military I have certain obligations to uphold. the final was the most awful thing i've ever taken in my life, the ta gave us a packet that looked like a book that was worth 70% of our grade, there was no amount of studying in the world that would prepare you for the short answer questions

What makes this teacher so frustrating and difficult is the fact he does not follow his own syllabus, does not set space out assignments/tests properly. In my summer school class he had 1 test in the first 6 weeks, and crammed a test/final/presentation into the last 2 weeks. On top of this we had the SPSS, and constant busy work.

It seems like he thinks that students are just students. But most of us have full-time jobs or internships. He has so many homework and he assumes that you know what to do on SPSS even without teaching it properly. I've never been so stressed and exhausted in my entire life. It is too much and I learned so little. DO NOT ENROLL IN ANY OF HIS CLASS.

He gives you this very demanding term project but will never help you figure things out on how to make it. DO NOT ENROLL IN ANY OF HIS CLASSES.

I really don't understand why people are saying so many horrible things about him. Fregetto is a great teacher. I mean what else do you need if you can do that.

This class is ridiculous. He does not help you at all. The only stuff I have learned, I have taught myself. He does not help you with homework. He goes on tangents. Does not help with assignments at all.

Professor Fregetto is a very challenging professor. I have had this guy for Small Business Consulting and Personal Sales.  He should not be allowed to teach.  He has lost his mind in his old age.  Someone help me get this guy out of the university so we can have a respectable entrepreneurship program.

He is a piece of garbage.  He gave us a stack of papers an inch high on the first day of class and said to read them for next week. He wouldn't let me come up to his office even though he was there.  Worst professor I've ever had.  Had to change my major cuz of him.

This guy is a relic. He means well but is 20 years behind the times. I am ashamed to call myself a UIC Entrepreneur major (not only because of this class). Dave Kohler is 100x better, and some of his classes are basically the same as Fregetto's. BUYER BEWARE!

One of the worst classes I've taken so far in college. He never reviews for exams, and he assigned SO MUCH WORK for only a 3 credit course. I changed my major because of this guy! He's not a bad guy, he's just a terrible professor. Avoid him at all costs!!!

All the bad things (and then some) you've ever heard about Eugene Fregetto are true. DO NOT take this course. Avoid it at all costs. This could very well be the worst professor you can find ANYWHERE. He needs to hang it up and stop making student's lives so ABSOLUTELY  miserable.

While mildly annoying and long-winded, I'd say Fregetto is a good professor! I don't know what horrible experiences everybody else has had, but I think he's great. A very incoherent professor. The guy makes things unncessarily difficult. He is not helpful at all. He teaches you one thing, and when you do it, he disregards what he previously taught you.

exams are way too long.  40 multiple choice, 40 T/F, 4-5 short essay questions all done within an hour and 15 minutes.  be prepared to turn in 5 page ESSAYS every 2 weeks of the semester.  IF YOU ARE READING THIS FREGETTO, IT IS ONLY A 3 CREDIT CLASS!!!!!

She was honestly my best professor, super caring down to earth. The workload wasnt as heavy just homework and mcgraw hill assignments due every sunday. Tests were easy she lets you use a cheat sheet one page double sided.

Professor Lord was great! Only used the course pack during lecture, which she'll check before every test, but posts the answers every Friday. She walks around the lecture hall to give help, and she was an amazing professor overall.

Suuuper sweet professor and funny, its easy to follow along in lectures. All we do is the course pack in class, a few homeworks and a few quizzes. Its very clear what will be on exams and she tells you exactly what she expects of you, overall really enjoyable class.

Prof. Eva is a great teacher attendance is not required but if you start to miss class your grade on exams will reflect that. She does course book checks for points but posts the answers on Friday's. 10/10 Would recommend - practice exams were just like the actual exams. Content made sense and honestly was kind of fun as long as you did the homework.
Great Professor, will want you to buy her workbook but its actually well written and makes her class a breeze. She's enthusiastic, logical, and knows her stuff.

Professor Lord was the kindest teacher I had during my fall semester. Her lectures had guided notes, which helped me learn better. Not too much workload. Would recommend.

she's is such an amazing teacher. she teaches very well and goes into immense detail so people don't miss out anything. she does walk around the class to make sure everyone is on the right track and takes attendance. she WILL check outside the classrooms if you try to skip however. overall she's a nice teacher and she tries to help everyone !

Prof. Lord is a great teacher. She was easy to follow and was very clear on deadlines and grading criteria. She was there if you needed help for group/solo problems in class. Great professor and person. Doing the homework on time and showing up to class will earn you a B, and studying before tests and making good cheat sheets will make it an easy A. She was nice and content was easy. All we did was the course pack which we went over problems individually and as a class.

Caring & intelligent!
She is awesome.
Great teacher! She explains things so well and is always willing to help. Was able to use a cheat sheet for 2/3 exams. Weekly hw and reading assignment, easy to follow. One extra credit opportunity.
Very nice professor

This is the type of professor that cares about making sure the students are actually learning the material. She'd walk around while we worked on problems to offer more direct assistant to questions. She seemed passionate at what she does. Although I thought the class would be difficult, her way of teaching helped grasp what the problems were asking

Not a good professor at all!!! Do not take her class i repeat do not. The exams were not similar to the practice exams. She does not know how to teach and on top of that she is not leniant with grading whatsoever. She does not care for her students at all!!! Trust me on this! I was a straight A student and I struggled so much only in her class!

Prof Lord was great. Great at explaining and simplifying accounting basics. She allowed cheat sheets on our last two exams which was very appreciated. If you pay attention and stay engaged, this class is super easy. If you're on your phone or don't bring the accounting workbook, you'll be lost.

Lord is a clear and well spoken professor. You get what you put in. If you're on your phone and skip class you wont survive this class, because it is tricky. I think she has a hard time putting things in layman's terms becuase I think she has a long background as an accountant. If youre unafraid to ask questions you'll be engaged and learn a lot.
ACTG 210 is a difficult class, but she managed to highlight the important things.

I highly recommend Professor Lords. Her lectures are extremely helpful and she very patiently makes you understand the concepts if you don't get it. If you attend her lectures you'll be fine throughout the semester. I highly recommend her.

I had the pleasure of having Eva for both Accounting 210 and 211, both times I have felt that I was given the best teacher for the class. Although her lectures deal with quite a lot of information, I never once felt unfairly taught as she always broke things down to digestible sections throughout the lecture. Utilize study hours and get that A!

This is a professor I would highly recommend. Despite not going to many of her lectures, the times I did attend, she made the lectures very interesting. Clearly explains concepts and uses interesting examples that keep you entertained. For tests, she provides the topics and allows cheat sheets. Overall 10/10, especially for a beginner actg course.

Great lectures and very engaging. Homework thru connect. Test reviews during class time a plus. Was available for office hours. Very caring and was so patient with everyone. Put in the time and effort and you will get an A. Allows cheat sheet for tests -write down your formulas! Journal entries were tricky study those and you will be good to go.
Great person and professor, easy to talk to, helps out alot you just need to ask! One of the best professors at UIC. Highly recommend
She's really great! If you're scared to take accounting take a class with her. She makes it easy to understand concepts and she's very nice.

I am a finishing up my semester with Prof. Lord and have honestly enjoyed taking Accounting 210 with her. The exam averages this semester were honestly really bad but she curves so! Most of this class is exams so be prepared for that. From what I have heard she is by far the best professor for ACTG 210 so take with her!

She is a pretty good professor. The class itself is interactive, which is good for visual learners and those who like  note taking. She makes you buy her own version of a textbook and another online platform, so $$ does add up. She starts off good at pacing her lectures but the last 2 lessons she will run through it because she runs out of time.

She herself was a good professor, she took her time to explain things and would answer any questions HOWEVER her quizzes never matched up to the problems we would do in class. You're allowed to have your notes but even they couldn't help you with those quizzes. She requires you to buy a super heavy book to write all your notes and you NEED it.
boring professor. unclear. half the class was asleep or absent.
My favorite professor this semester!!! Professor Lord was helpful no matter what, and always did what she could to see her students succeed. UIC needs more teachers like this.

Professor Lord was phenomenal. She really cares about her students, she took time to go over exercises with me individually after class. Top notch educator.

Didn't really get to interact with her because of covid but in regards to her online material she was a good teacher. Very accessible when needed and communicates great with students!
