She is a really nice lady. This class is pretty straightforward and logical. The readings actually help a lot and are pretty easy to follow, just do them bit by bit. Weekly HW, quizzes every 2 weeks based on HW, and exams based on quizzes. EC discussion board is easy. Do the readings at your own pace, make a study guide, and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Personally, I am a nonaccounting major, therefore this class was quite difficult for me. I would say this class isn't an easy class, really need extensive studying to fully understand the class, and utilize every resource in class.
This class is like most of the accounting classes, it will be difficult. As long as you pay attention in class, you will be fine.
One of the greatest POLS professors at UIC. Do what is expected of you, and you will be fine :)

Professor McKenzie is very knowledgeable on various topics in political science. This was POLS 259 where we had guest speakers every other week so it was amazing. There were weekly reflections, a midterm, and a final. The midterm was a little difficult as it covered many topics overall an insightful course! Would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --So many papers

reviews.comment: This class was weird because Professor McKenzie's lectures and reading materials were online, and we only met with our TA once a week. Personally, I did not learn much from the lectures, but it may just be because they were long and boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mckezie is an amazing professor.

So much extra credit was offered. The only thing I needed to attend to was the discussion; I had it at 8 am, but my TA was great, so I didn't mind. The final and midterm were the same, multiple choice and essay, both were easy and could be answered by just watching the lectures and doing the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: The online lectures with the in-person discussion really worked for me in this class; my TA was great! The tests are easy if you take notes and pay attention to the lectures, and the book presentations for the discussion sections are interesting if you take the time to read them.

He is a Narcissistic professor who expects all students to be on his level. His lectures are boring and he wants to discourage to go into law. McKenzie said most of you will not get into law school on the first day. He is the toughest grader in the whole poli sci division

Professor McKenzie is a great professor! I took him for POLS 258 and it was extremely informative, he really knows a lot. He cares about his students and wants you to learn the material. If there is any case in the media he will make sure the students understand. 3 essays and 2 tests. That's your grade so just make sure you pay attention!

Professor McKenzie is so insanely knowledgable in this field but that's what makes his lectures amazing. The class is very test heavy but he curves the tests and his lectures are thorough regarding information. You definitely have to work for a good grade in this class but he is supportive and willing to answer any question.

I did not learn much from this course. I had a hard time understanding the lectures as well as the questions on the exam. The class is also very boring mainly because the class is lecture-heavy. Literally, its the same as taking AP GOV
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Mckenzie was okay, but his lectures are very boring, he goes through them very quickly, and they're complex. I did not learn much from the overall course;the midterm and final exams are very difficult. The majority of the class did poorly, he did curve but never puts grades in. The work load isn't too bad, but if you read it's a lot.

The class is overall really interesting, especially if you are planning on going to law school. Prof McKenzie, although gives off an arrogance like attitude, he does care for his students and will make time outside of class if you have any questions on the law school and/or need further clearerfacation on the concepts learned during class.

He is hard but one of the smartest uic has to offer . You cannot half ass his class. He will make you work hard to get a A but it's only  because he  truly wants you to understand the material . If you want to be a lawyer this is the class  you want to take . No other class or teaching style at uic will prepare you for law  more than his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Very smart, and he knows it. He'll speak to you like a child if you ask questions. The most arrogant teacher I've ever had. You'll learn a lot in his class, but you'll also learn to despise this man. Teachers like this motivate me to become a teacher because I see how condescending and destructive some can be.
He was grumpy 1/4 of the semester. If you ask him a question, he would make you feel stupid.
McKenzie is a great professor for POLS 101. He gives his lectures in a clear manner that doesn't make you go to sleep  even though the material may be to some people.

Prof McKenzie made this class super interesting and is extremely passionate. Only tests were the mid-term and final but when they tell you to read the book, TAKE HEED OF THEIR ADVICE. The tests heavily revolve around the books content so simply taking notes during lectures is not enough. Otherwise, only had to write 2 short papers (2-4 pages).

THIS CLASS IS NOT HARD. Just put a little effort and attention to the class and it'll be interesting and easy. He's a clear lecturer and always posts his live lectures online. I personally loved it. Taking his class will really interest you in Poli Sci. I would also recommend taking the Disc. with Eduardo Salinas, he works with students well.

Prof. McKenzie is an amazing educator.  A former D.A. and well-accomplished academic in political science, specially the judicial process and law. His Civil Liberties and Public Law classes are tough, but well worth the effort. You will always learn something and walk away with a greater knowledge of the concepts.

Awesome lecturer & sweet human. Failed my midterm w 65%, still got an A as my final grade. He gives a ton of ex, credit & is really passionate about the content which made the lectures more interesting. Only tests are midterm+final, they're detailed so u need to read the book or powerpoints. If u are struggling talk to him, study, & he will pass u

McKenzie and Balbus are THE BEST. The smartest, (difficult classes but very very interesting) and the most influential teachers. I have taken all my poli sci classes for my degree and these two are the top BY FAR. awesome guy, pushes you to learn but makes it fun and interesting. Taking McKenzie's classes will help you in your degreeminor alot!!
He's a great prof! Genuinely funny, incredibly smart, but tests are a little tough.

I took this class as a 4 week summer course. It was extremely accelerated and a chapter to be read a day. It is essential to read the midterm and final came directly from the book. Furthermore participation is key. He always asks for questions conceding the reading. Do the chapter quizzes at the end they will help you!

His exams are pretty hard. However, his lectures are entertaining. You will understand more if you attended the lectures. I attended all of them so far and received a 76% on my midterm exam. He gives you 16 essay questions and 2 of them are actually on the exam, but you only have to write one of them. Gives a lot of extra credit opportunities!
Worst teacher ever. I was sick on the midterm day to a point that I had fainted twice and he failed me even with a doctors note. He is an inconsiderate human being

Class his actually easy if you pay attention to his lecture, he givers great examples and you should read the textbook a bit as the class is very discussion based. But the class is very enjoyable,had a brief every week and a couple of tests but other than that class is very manageable. And he tells some stories that help you better understand cases

Prof McKenzie is a very good teacher and you should take if you are interested in going to law school.  However, this class is not easy and requires a lot of reading but if very good pre-experience for future law school students and his knowledge in law is very beneficial.

I took this class because I am an undergrad. student looking to go into law, and can honestly say I was genuinely interested in the material. But Professor M quickly ruined this for me. Extremely rude, egotistical, and suffers from a sever napoleonic complex. If you try to talk to him he talks down to you, and if you ask questions you're "stupid"

He is very knowledgeable but knows it and talks down to students, making you feel stupid for asking certain questions. His tests are HARD. Feels like a 400 level class, not 100 level. Also, this is not intro to government, it is 100% ELITE THEORY!

Took his summer course. Nothing to do with the introduction of american government. felt like i was in a 400 level class. didn't know anything about the american government and still know nothing about the american government. thanks.

Worst mistake of my life! Professor M is nice but other than that everything sucks! The class is called intro to Am. govt but is all on freakin Elite theory! Completely misguiding, they should clarify that. I had the worst TA ever, so that didn't help either. He is horrible and just pathetic. They have to realize it's a 100 level class, not phD!

He is my favorite professor at UIC. I absoultly loved his class & his lecture. Lectures are not mandatry, but I wanted to go to all of them because he is so intresting & a great teacher! He is not easy, but he is a fabulous professor! Also, LOTS of extra credit!

McKenzie is very smart and a great lecturer. His tests are hard but he curves at the end of the semester. Lecture attendence is not required but very reccomended. McKenzie makes lectures interesting and they go by fast. Great professor.
Good class. Good professor! Do well on the first test and do all the extra credit.

He is my favorite professor at UIC. He's extremely smart. His exams are HARD and detailed. If you don't understand the concept inside out and backwards then you're not going to do well. You can't half ass this class. He's a nice & approachable. He's very helpful and takes a genuine interest in his students.

I had him to Judicial Review. He is extremely smart and is a practicing lawyer. Very Intelligent. HOWEVER, his is tough. He expects excellence and for everyone to love law. I don't, but my friend said he was amazing so I took him. I learned a lot! However, the test were very hard and detailed.

Very good professor.  Tests are difficult but all questions come from the textbook so be sure to read.  If your interested in law, this professor is a lawyer and will also talk about law school admissions.

This professor is AMAZING! One of the best teachers that I have ever had! He is very approachable and I am not sure what emails people are complaining about but I never had a problem! If you ask a question, he takes the time to answer it and answer it well. VERY good guy!
Very good at explaining the most complicated things to his students. The way he uses his Law degree to help explain things is also very helpful.

Overall this was a very good class. McKenzie expects allot of his students but curves at the end. I didn't read the book except to skim through at the midterm and final. You must go to lecture and discussion and be engaged. Had Lawson as my TA and she was absolutely awesome

Vastly knowledgeable, oft times an entertaining lecturer, but he has better things to do than to assist you. If you need anything, you're better off talking to your TA. He plays petty little games like taking attendance, waiting for people to leave, and then taking attendance again. No personal feedback on iclicker attendance either.

Excellent, knowledgeable professor. Truly knows his stuff. A lawyer, John Marshall Law School Professor, and UIC POLS professor. Takes attendance, allows 4 absences. Tests are difficult and are based from lecture and textbook. Great Pre-Law class. Transferred from U of I Champaign and am getting a better education at UIC thanks to McKenzie.

Terrible lecture presentations. To survive you basically take notes from the book and start memorizing. There are no notes from lecture to help you. He also takes a VERY long time to grade the papers and tests. Class could have been much better.

Good class if you are an underclassmen looking to go to law school. However, McKenzie is not very nice. Supremely egotistical. Don't email him with anything ever because he's says it's for "professional use only". Dude, its your UIC email. Its for students to contact you!!

the tests are hard but he explains things well. he gets annoyed easily from emails so i only talked to my TA - Mike Owens, he is the best TA ever. so make sure you go to class, take good notes and study
For the sake of your GEN ED GPA! TAKE THIS CLASS! Only difficulty is the midterm and finals but review the powerpoints and you will be straight in the class!
Good and interesting professor. Hard tests. Remember to prepare for those.
He's just rude when you ask him a question he doesn't even bother to help I reccommend not to take this class
Great professor.  Very knowledgeable.  Knows how to speak in normal, everyday, even humorous language to discuss topics.  Had him last summer.  You can tell that he has an insider's persepctive!
Good professor, TA's were good during discussion but no feedback on grades. No book, mostly online, independent work. Overall, very easy class.

Thought this class was a little difficult for a 101 course. Tests were very hard and covered a wide range of material. I didn't like the integrated blackboard format with only one lecture. Lectures were interesting and professor knew a lot about his field

McKenzie was recommended to me by a friend and I am not disappointed.  His class is always interesting (sometimes fun).  It's imperative to stay up to date on the readings, but they only make his class more enjoyable.  One of the top 3 professors I've ever had.

Great Professor.  I decided to take the four week course so I could enjoy the rest of the summer and let me tell ya, it was intense.  Not so much so because of the material but because we were doing a week's worth of material per day.  He was extremely helpful and his PowerPoint presentations were on the mark.Do the readings and you should be fine.

A bit too much work for a 3 CH class. However, the class did help me a lot in terms of learning about American politics. Also, the grading was really very leniant by the TA. The professor's ever-willing to answer your questions by e-mail or in-person.

I thought his class was going to be the hardest class I've ever taken, turns out I really enjoyed his class. We did read a lot of cases, however, the workload was manageable. Some concepts were confusing at times, but overall he was really helpful and lenient on grading. Great class and professor to take if you want to go to law school.
GREAT CLASS! The media journal helped me get so much more into politics, and the short assignments are helpful, but not graded too harshly. TAKE THIS CLASS.

This professor does a GREAT job.  He knows soo much, and there is no question I couldn't ask him.  He is very approachable after class, and is helpful to anyone who asks.  I recommend this class to everyone.

This professor does a GREAT job.  He knows soo much, and there is no question I couldn't ask him.  He is very approachable after class, and is helpful to anyone who asks.  I recommend this class to everyone.
i love this guy. i really enjoyed his class. the person who hated him shouldnt be in  college. the class was reasonable and i loved the professors silly jokes. i
too fast and very hard. exams were also very hard, seems like a nice guy, but i dont reccomend the class...

His course is somewhat difficult and he uses blackboard a lot for all of his assignments. He's rude to the students who approach him after class and he does little to help students prepare for the mid-term and final. Overall, he's arrogant but very knowledgeable about his field.

Mckenzie is a good proffesor. He always tries to make lecture interesting and he's just a nice guy in general. There is a lot of reading but the tests aren't really that hard and the course is pretty easy.
he was too fast-paced and his tests were too hard!!!

He does give alot of work in terms of assignmnets, but his class is mostly for individuals who want to prepare for law school. Prof. Mckenzie is tough, but you will learn alot and get a taste of law school.
Class seems very difficult for a 100 level course but the professor is an expert at his field and makes lectures very interesting.
His lectures were very interesting, but the class just kind of got boring after time. His tests are not easy either.
He may not be the easist professor, but he is a nice guy and very very helpful if you ask him. He is very easy to talk to as well.
Still my favorite professor 15 years later. Changed my major cause of him.
Half Lawyer/Half Political Scientist.  One of the best professors I've ever had.
No Comments
One the best professors I've had.

I personally did not really enjoy her teaching style. This is a lecture heavy,highly conceptual class so it was boring to me as it was hard to follow her sometimes. She always helps outside of class and with anything, but I just feel like she makes the class so confusing and hard. Midterms were alright but final was hard

She is a great professor. Yes, the work & materials are hard, however, that's expected at this level and class. Prior to each exam she specifies what to study and look over. Overall, shes a very nice lady who is willing to help. PSA!! DO NO CHEAT IN HER CLASS, she took at least 2 peoples exams during the final.

The material is tough, but that's expected in a field where people really have to know their stuff. She's kind, caring, and explains confusing topics in different ways. If you're willing to work with her, she'll work with you. She gives lots of free points and wants you to succeed. Great professor!
She is a great professor. But the material she teaches in general is just so boring and hard. But she is a good professor that lets you cheat on exams.

This course was FIN414 Financial Plan Development (first semester this course was taught). The class overall was educational, although very lecture heavy. Attendance and participation was mandatory. Homework was all online and there were no tests or quizzes administered throughout the semester. Overall group final project of a financial plan.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Golubeva is a great professor! She gives good feedback, cares about her students, and is very easy to reach outside of class. Pay attention and do the homework. Quizzes and the hedging games are important and will prepare you for the exams. Take advantage of her office hours, she is very kind and will help you!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Tough class nonetheless. Its really one of those classes that you really have to stay on top of your classes and have a passion for futures.  You will learn well. She's really nice. Allows 5 absences.

Tough class but not an impossible one. If options and futures is something you're truly interested in then you likely will not have much of a problem in this class. Go over the lectures as well as the practice exams in detail since exams are a bit tough. Ask questions and study a lot. She's very helpful.

This course is not easy, if you want to learn about Options & Futures Prof. Evgenia is your best option, her syllabus is fair if you keep on top of your other assignments (hw and hedging games) you should be able to get a B even if you don't do that well on the midterms. You should have a firm grasp of most of the concepts if you attend and focus.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: FIN 416 possesses a wealth of information that uncovers the various fundamentals of understanding derivatives and their use cases, pricing, and much more. It is a fascinating class, and Professor Golubeva complements the interesting course material with her passionate teaching. I would highly recommend this class and Professor Golubeva.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This isn't the most awful class you can take, but her accent is super heavy and she doesn't give good feedback on what she grades. Hedging Game is stupid, curves exams, knows the material, but expects you to already understand instead of attempting to learn. Wouldn't recommend to take as a filler, but if you need a Finance class.... I guess.

Professor Golubeva is a prime example of what every professor should strive to be. She not only cares about her students truly understanding the material, but their well-being too. She is a fair grader, funny, clear and is always so happy to receive questions and give feedback. She is the absolute best! I recommend her to anyone and everyone.

Professor Golubeva is the best professor to have if you really want to learn finance. She does an amazing job of explaining the concepts and is always excited to teach the content. Her exams can be a bit challenging so you really need to study and prepare for them, the practice sets she gave were extremely helpful. Exams are open notes as well.
Awesome

Nice professor who enjoys what she's teaching but the class subject itself is really nothing to be excited about making it fairly difficult to keep interest during the entire class. Some homework assignments are easier than others, no actual feedback on them. Exams are pretty difficult if you don't review practice sets and homework extensively.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: For this class 45% of your grade is homeworks and there is 8 homework assignments. The homework follows solved examples that are posted on blackboard. The midterm is 15%, project is 10%, and the final is 30%. You get a formula sheet on the exams. The class is hard just because of the concepts but you will actually learn something.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great/Solid professor. She explains everything to you and if you have questions she will be more than happy to answer it for you. 3 Exams, the first two are solid half MC/Free Response. She picks the best exam you took and counts it twice, and for the final she provides a ten question EC Bonus. Pop quizzes are easy if you pay attention & No hw!

Professor Golubeva is hard, but she is a good. Theres only 3 exams so don't expect to use homework to help your grade. Sometimes it can be hard to follow her but you just have to realllly listen! If you sit there and pay attention, you will get the material. The exams arent hard but like one multiple choice question can be worth 10 points.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's great, really supportive, and stuff. The papers and stuff are alright, getting context was slightly hard, but do the work and it's an easy A. Go to office hours show up and he's good with extensions also as long as you don't ask like 1 hour before the due date. His syllabus says he will give an extension if it makes you submit a better paper.

A lot of your grade in Engl161 will be determined by the 4-ish papers he assigns throughout the year, but if you show up for the lectures and communicate with him they'll be fine. His class was very rewarding and its obvious they care very deeply about their students.
Evan was a good professor and all the feedback was clear and if you follow the feedback you will get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very kind, helpful, and its an easy A honestly just make sure you take the feedback seriously.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Horrible
No explanation for low grades on papers, and no help offered. Seems to have favorites and it's obvious. Seems not matter what you do you cannot please him.

English teachers are the worst. Evan is cool but class sucks. So many papers, im sick if yapping for him in class and on my papers. If your a good writer im sure youll be fine but if you aren't like me then good luck man.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Actually the best professor ever. Hes such a sweet person and very lenient when it comes to anything. As long as you do your work in the class it's really fun and entertaining. The class goes by very quickly since he really engages with the students. Overall I would take this professor again!

My favorite prof by far. They are a very caring person, and the quizzes during the semester were easy as long as you were paying attention to the reviews. They are always ready to help students with papers and make the guidelines very clear for papers. If this is your first class at UIC I highly recommend taking this class.

This professor shows very interest of the students in the classroom. Professor Evan, makes things easy by providing the sample essay how is it structured and how it looks like. he does four quizzes and one extra credit at the end of the class. For this class, attendance really matters because he tells you what to expect would makes it useful.

There are 5 papers due during the semester. He is a very tough grader whatever you do he won't give above a B. There's a quiz due every other week for the first half of the semester. I tried everything to get an A in writing projects but it won't help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Evan Steuber is a great professor! You may ask him any questions, and he will always help you. He even encourages you to ask them! Follow his feedback on papers you write - and you will receive excellent grades. If you spend enough time working on essays, you won't have problems in the course. A lot of group work, and participation is mandatory.

Professor Steuber is by far the best English professor I have ever had. Steuber is super chill, plays good music, is reasonable with turning in assignments considering this is the first time everything has had to be online. The work load is not a huge amount and the writing assignments are kind of fun to do. 20/10 would recommend.

Evan is the best ENG161 teacher at UIC. The class is difficult at the beginning of the semester with numerous reading quizzes, however, if you make an effort to read you'll be fine. The Comedy theme of the class makes it very interesting and easy to follow along. Essays can be tough but Evan is always willing to help so go to office hours.

I loved having Steuber as a teacher. They are easy-going, funny, and a good personality in the classroom. Steuber gives great feedback on papers and is always looking for different opinions on topics. My class with Steuber was full of discussion and a great place for making new friendships.

Steuber is a true gem of the English department. They are so organized, knowledgable and flexible in their lectures. Some people found them to be a tough grader on the papers but you just have to have a solid process and outline beforehand. Initially I didn't find the topic that interesting when I signed up but they made it fun and informative.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Profesor Steuber was honestly one of my favorite professors of all time. He does give a lot of work to do, but it's all easy and interesting. Extremely helpful. You need an English class, might as well make it fun. Definitely take his class.

To be fair, the English department is in control of a lot of what the classes do, so I can't fully put it all on this professor. And at the same time, this class was very difficult. There was a quiz every class day for the first two weeks based on the homework, five papers due in one semester and it was very hard to catch up if you ever slip a bit.

You only get 5 absences, which can be hard with a MWF class. Great professor, very understanding and easy to talk to. Losely structured class, after the drop date it is almost all writing in class for the final research paper. No final.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He's a very interesting Professor, very enjoyable and very easy going at times. I agree the start of his class does come out as sort of difficult just because every reading he assigns, there is going to be a quiz about it and none of them were multiple choice but it does prepare you for the four writing projects you will do throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Amazing professor very clear and gives good feedback just be attentive and you will pass the class easily
reviews.rating_tags: GROUP PROJECTS--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: In Evans class you have 4 major writing projects, basically thats all you do. The class starts off difficult with a few readings to prepare you for the writing project. Honestly, supper fun class to be in, he has a very out going personality!! Pop up quizzes happen, NOT MULTIPLE CHOICE. 10/10 recomend.

He grades very difficult on papers, thinks that his class is your only class so he will overload with readings and homework that is impossible to get done. Attendance is absolutely necessary although some of the days were completely irrelevant.

Evan is a good teacher, I enjoyed his lectures. He took over this class when the first professor fell ill, and he did a really good job. Make sure to participate and attend class, it matters. He is stingy with advice and hints for the exams but if you attend class he goes over pretty much everything you will need to know. Pay attention!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Evan is really funny guy. he truly cares about his students and wants them to succeed. he explains his tasks very clearly and gives second chanced if you really mess up the first time. i really recommend taking his class because it is very interesting

Evan is really helpful and he is very invested in your improvement as a writer. He wants you to redorewrite rough drafts, and think about the bigger picture with the readings he gives you. He is very clear in his lectures, and he encourages group discussion. If you're good at English, I highly recommend him. If not, he can help you out if you try.
Hands down an amazing teacher, he really wants you to better your writing via revisions and what not and is very outgoing. If you need help, ASK! He will gladly assist you. 5/5 A+

He doesn't like giving out A's on certain assignments because he has "high standards" but I passed the class with an A so it's not that bad. He gave decent feedback on drafts and we had journal entries often. He's strict with small stuff like homework and attendance. Otherwise he's pretty chill.

Olga is a very approachable professor. She is very reasonable with her choices/decisions. She responds to emails within the day you send them and overall she's very nice. Attendance is mandatory for this class; you can only miss about 4 days before you get an incomplete grade. If you show up to class and do the work; you're gonna pass the class.

Professor Evdokimov is a great professor, she clearly has a passion for Physics. She's nowhere near as bad as the other reviews make her out to be. She is very approachable and kind. The class is extremely difficult and you MUST attend class, or you will not do well. The labs will be very difficult without in class help from her and the TAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Boring, heavy russian accent. If you dont know coding you will struggle in this class. A 55 is a C, but she grades fairly harsh and its hard to know what she wants since the 1 example report she gives is short and has hardly any math since its an easy problem. Class is fast paced, if you miss one class you will struggle to get a 60 for that week.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: One of the least charismatic instructors I've ever had, and I've been in school for years and years. Listening to her shrill lecture voice is like listening to someone learn to play the trumpet. She has a heavy Russian accent. Her assignments are very difficult and time consuming, but Phys majors at UIC may have no choice but to have her.

This is a class based on computer programming and thus it's very difficult by design; however, Olga works very hard to help everyone in the class succeed. It's sometimes difficult to determine what's expected of you on lab reports, so the grading is tough there. She respond to emails willingly and will always strive to help you do better.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Best physics teacher I had at UIC, very clear, explains well, and makes the subject easy to learn.

Took her for physics workshop alongside Phys142. Shes a nice lady and very enthusiastic but you will get nothing out of this class unless you keep up in Phys142. If you do keep up, she can be very helpful for reinforcing concepts and practice problems.
She was very detailed in her lectures, a tad fast at times but with the amount of material that is expected. overall if you put in the work you'll do fine

If you go to lecture and do the mastering physics assignments, you should be fine. She's a bit unapproachable, but when I needed to miss an exam and I told her ahead of time, she just told me I didn't have to take it.
Smart woman, nice woman, HORRIBLE TEACHER. Do NOT take her or you will regret it.

reviews.comment: Very easy to pass Professor Reynold's class. There are four major papers which he gives you enough time to do. He also gives great feedback on first and second drafts, just make sure you turn in a paper copy.
You'll be straight if you pay attention to lectures, get good quiz grades, and do the homework and projects, pretty light grader and easy work. Very nice professor as well.
He made some mistakes grading projects which is my only issue. Otherwise really good and smart professor.

Professor can be pretty lenient in general. However, homework and project outlines are unclear, inconsistent, and sometimes wrong. The starter code is messy and lacks guidance, so you're left guessing. The grading system is unfair, limiting high scores. Overall, the homework is boring and frustrating, with only some freedom in project design.
Mccarty is the best. If you come to 75% of lectures and study for the quizzes a little you'll be straight. I highly recommend him, he's very knowledgeable too.
The GOAT. The best professor at UIC hands down.

reviews.comment: courseload was very manageable and he gave a lot of chances to bring your grade up through quiz re-takes. he gives students 5 late days total to use on homeworks and projects, DO NOT use them on homeworks if you can help it lol save them for the projects. you shouldn't get below a B in this class if you're taking it with him.

Evan McCarty is one of the best CS professors out there when it comes to explaining Theory and Logic. Every semester I've had him I never had a problem understanding the topics. His HWs can be pretty tough but they do teach you ALOT and YOU WILL be well-prepared for exams. He also give a lot of time to do your assignments and he's a fair grader.

Best possible professor for any logic related class. Class could be structured a bit better (ie. labs do not relate to lectures), but the material was taught  well nether-less. Wished more students cared about computer hardware though, the lectures were always empty.

I took Professor McCarty for CS 151 and now CS 301 and I have always loved his classes. He has clear grading scales, attendance is never mandatory, and if you watch the lectures and take good notes, you'll do well. For the exams, always watch the practice exam that he goes through - it helps tremendously.

ONE OF THE BEST CS PROFESSORS AT UIC, register for a CS class and see his name there, you are guaranteed an awesome professor. Taken him for 151,342,301. Beyond informative for all of them, easy to pay attention and follow along in this lectures because the way he speaks is great

Professor is really good. He gives extra credit also his exams and quizzes are pretty much what u learned during lecture 1:1.  He wants you to pass so he gives many oppurtunies such as extending deadlines. Hes is a very kind and understanding professor. I high reccomend!!

An excellent professor that truly cares about his students. His coursework is somewhat high, but very manageable and flexible. He gives a lot of opportunities to succeed in his courses, and I have learned so much from his lectures.

Prof McCarty is a respectful and caring person. All his exams are not hard. He does an in-class review session, which helps. Also, he doesn't make the exams much different from previous semesters' exams. He is very fair with homework and quizzes. His lectures can be a little boring, but they are still very informative, and everything is recorded.
I have had McCarty for CS 151 and 342. Very chill professor and even rounded my 151 from a B to an A! I would highly recommend choosing him!
He is understanding and gives good lectures. I found his lectures to the point and engaging. Enjoyed his class!
Absolute best at UIC. Have taken 151,301,342 and have worked under him. He is one of the most understanding prof here and has blessed so many students as he Improves any class that he takes up. : )
McCarty is a caring professor. Many projects and work come with the CS 342 class, but they are all helpful and the professor is very kind and considerate to everyone.

Professor McCarty's teaching style includes explaining how programming topics work, then demonstrating them during live programming. Attendance is not required, and lecture materials/recordings are posted online. Projects have defined goals and are a very fair level of difficulty. Professor McCarty is also kind and cares about students learning.

Definitely the best CS teacher in UIC. Had him for 3 different classes (CS151, CS301, and CS342) and I'm having him again next semester. His classes are a little difficult, but he makes them way easier. Attendance always not mandatory.
Mccarty is a great professor. I'm glad I took CS151 with him, he made it very enjoyable.
One of the best professors and so much to the point on what exactly is taught and needs to be learnt.

McCarty makes his expectations for homework, quizzes, and projects very clear and reasonable. The lectures are always engaging and actually useful for learning, rather than busywork. He is definitely a great teacher and passionate about helping his students succeed.

Professor McCarty is one of my favorite professors at UIC. I had him for CS151, 301, 342, and will have him for 362 in the coming semester. His method of explaining complex material is very organized and clear, resulting in a deep understanding and retention of the info. He is very accommodating and helpful and is an overall amazing professor.

I had professor McCarty for CS342, and I must say he's a really great professor and very accomodating for student errors. He makes the class very straight forward in that if you're doing well on quizzes then the final will be fine same goes for the projects themselves. I really enjoyed the class and the projects we had were challenging and fun.

This is my third class with Prof McCarty and he's easily one of the best professors at UIC. His lectures are great and he always assigns a reasonable amount of work. He is very accommodating and will help you out so you can succeed in the course. Highly recommend taking a class with him if you can, you won't regret it.

For his first time teaching 342 he structured his quizzes and final exam a lot like the 151/301 format. homework and quizzes where definitely manageable if you take the time to go over his lecture. Pairs allowed for all projects, last project felt rushed but we had a lot of liberty in what we could do.

reviews.comment: Had McCarty for CS 151, 301, and 342. One of the best professors at UIC and I'm always hyped to take one of his courses.
Goated! You will love him!

This is actually for 342, but I had him in 301 and 151 so Im basically a McCarty expert.  This man is easily one of the best professors at this school.  Lectures are engaging, although 342 was a little thrown together, not really McCarty's fault, I still learned and did a lot in the class.
He is really an amazing professor.  Would definitely take him again for another class
Took him for both 151 and 301, I don't think it's possible for a class to be more organized than Prof. McCarty's classes and for a professor to be more understanding and helpful than him.
dat boy goated

Very knowledgeable. I think he knows almost everything about computers. Very fun guy to talk to before/after classes about any computer related topic. Gave opportunity to fix our homework to get a better grade, and he would give curves too.
Really good professor.
Awesome Professor! Just paying attention to his lecture and slides would suffice to great a good grade.

reviews.comment: the best

Wow, I really do not get what past reviews of McCarty are saying. Great professor. I enjoy the way he teaches, his lectures very loud and clear. Never boring. To get a good grade, attending labs and completing homework are a must. The class was also one of the most organized classes I've had at UIC.
Professor Mccarty makes 151 an easy A for students that put the work in. If you attend class, labs, do the homework and study for midterms and the final.

reviews.comment: Very charismatic, discrete maths (151) has a lot of new/weird concepts but he explained them in ways that made them easier to understand. reviews.comment:
Not really sure about the negative comments, have him for CS151 this semester. He is one of the nicest professors, easy with deadlines and thoughtfully curates the test. Also, the course is not designed to be too heavy on students since it is just a weekly HW every Wednesday with Lab work.

Would definitely take any other class with Prof McCarty.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is great at answering questions during lectures and his slides and examples are relatively easy to follow. The course content is difficult but if you ask him questions it becomes easy. He tells what each type of question on the test will be so it is easy to prepare and you can bring a note sheet. Exams are not bad and lectures are okay.

I've never had an instructor who went to such great lengths to make sure every student's question is answered during lecture. This teacher goes above and beyond to make sure that his students are prepared to succeed on exams, going as far to ask if we feel comfortable with a topic before putting it on an exam. Very light homework load.

Had him for 151, made 301 a lot easier knowing his teaching style. He makes it as easy as he can to get an A. extra credit, and exams are pretty identical to course material. Better than the other 301 profs. Overall, the class helps you think more analytically when approaching coding, but can't imagine it's much more practical beyond that.

I had McCarty for both 151 and 301. He is very active in helping his students understand the material as much as possible. Grading criteria is clear and he is very generous with it. I learned a lot in 301 and he made theoretical computer science fascinating to learn about. I would definitely take another course with McCarty.

reviews.comment: Took McCarty for 301 and his review sessions basically covered what would be on the exam without any trick questions. As long as you go to class/watch lectures this class is very generous with lots of extra credit available(up to 5%, also got 1% for course eval) . Nice change of pace from other CS courses like 251 and 261.
Really good professor. I took CS151 with him online, now I'm taking CS301. 100% recommend taking a theory class with him.
"WOW" Professor

Genuinely a really good professor. However, the coursework and syllabus is definitely not easy, but if you focus on the lectures and practice homeworks well, it will seem way less challenging. In retrospect, the material is pretty easy. However, when we were first learning it he made it seem like the most complex thing in the world as he explains next to nothing. reviews.comment: This man's lectures are so vague and barely go into details. After this, he gives you very difficult homework that has nothing to do with the lectures. Also, he takes far too long to grade all the homework because I suppose he's trying to catch cheaters. The way he teaches the course is like he expects you to be a master at it beforehand. Avoid!!!

He's a really nice professor, and the lectures are really helpful. One thing I loved about the course was professor McCarty implies active learnings, where we get to study and experiment with different kinds of methods for applied level questions while doing the homework, along with great help in office hours.

This guy is really out here giving 20 minute lectures on a full chapter and expecting people to write formal proofs explaining concepts he barely even mentioned. An absolute joke of a class. I've also seen him intentionally giving students the wrong answer in office hours because they're supposed to "figure it out". Avoid at all costs.

He would not respond to my emails all semester. His lectures are super vague and he does not teach them well at all. His teaching style is, he will vaguely review the material so that you would either have to cheat to get it right or rely on a curve. He would usually curve it, however, the class pointless when he does not teach class well.

You'd need to know discrete math PRIOR to this class in order to learn from him. But if you don't cite your knowledge on EACH assignment, you'll be labeled a cheater since another student came up with the same answer you did. And now you've been reported to the dean:) NOT recommended for any 100-level course. He's a smart guy though, technically.

His class is like an emotional rollercoaster. There's highs and lows. The highs are some meme quality lectures at the beginning of the semester.... and the lows are constantly being put under intense panic attacks thinking you might be part of the 1/3 of the class that gets reported as cheaters. Would not ride this rollercoaster again nice guy tho

The communication with this instructor has been the worst experienced I've had thus far in my prior college and here at UIC. I know we are in tough times with everything online currently, but his online lectures have not been great at all. I wish we were on campus.
Useless in the online format

He's a pretty cool professor, relatively understanding of the course load students have. A lot of his lectures tend to be more abstract, so if you aren't good at connecting the dots for concepts, you're going to have a hard time.

Took him in Fall 2019. His lecture was fun and challenging. He answered questions patiently during office hours. There were Q&A sessions before exams which were very helpful. In all, he is a nice guy. My favorite professor at UIC so far.
Lots of Extra Credit opportunity. Not an easy class, but an A is achievable if you put in the work.

One of the best professors i've ever had in a lifetime. reviews.comment: He's a nice guy. Lol to whoever said he "only has an MS degree" (still takes hard work). Evan will hold you to high expectations and want to challenge you so keep that in mind.

He's my favorite CS professor so far. He responds nigh instantaneously to Piazza messages, and his lectures are fun, clear, & easy to understand as long as you show up & pay attention. reviews.comment: Really nice guy, office hours are super helpful. EC opportunity and pretty significant curve. Book was helpful. Material is much more abstract than other CS classes, but if you can wrap your head around a few key concepts then it becomes pretty straightforward.

One of the best professors in uic. The class was hard, but he made it easy. He cares about students and he is very lenient on grading . There are 2 midterms worth 20% each, 1 final worth 30%, 6 homework worth 25%, and 5% clickers. His homework are hard, but his exams are easy because he tells the exam questions to students in advance.

His homework and exams are difficult. TAs aren't great during discussion. This is his first semester teaching at UIC, so I'm giving him a bit of support. Office hours are helpful. The book and labs are optional, but they do help with homework. He at least gives us a choice of what topics we want/don't want on the midterm/final by majority rules.

reviews.comment: CS 301 with Prof McCarty is the perfect definition of riding a bike, but that bike and everything around that bike being on fire. This class was miserable. He doesn't provide with solutions to anything, doesn't help with his impossible home works and he cares more about his TA's than he does for his poor suffering students. Good luck taking him!!!!

CS 301 is by no means an easy class. The material is unlike anything you have done previously. But, if you pay attention in class, go to office hours, and spend time going over the labs, you will do fine. He is very approachable and his office hours are very informative and laid back.

I love her! She cares so much about her students and offers several office hours. If you ask her for help shell definitely help you. Fair teacher. Relatively hard listening exams. 2 tests, both have listening exams where they give you around 30 symphonies/concerts/operas that you have to and you're responsible for up to 8 minutes of each work. Amazing professor, knows what she's talking about. This class was fun. The professor is solid, genuinely engaged, and teaches really useful material. The grading is ok for the projects, progress reporting is so important tho. They are manageable

Solid professor, very clear slides, easy to follow, and the workload is fair. He's flexible if something comes up and quick to respond to emails. Labs are useful, though sometimes he tries to fit too much at once so they can feel a bit rushed if you miss a step. Only thing is I wish he'd shut down side conversations during class more often.

Awesome class. We had some assignments (4 or 5, I don't remember anymore) thorough the whole semester that are very interesting. If you learn from the assignments and pay attention to class, you gonna pass with an A easily

Lecture is not nearly as good as it should be. He lectures the entire class and none is really meaningful. Grades tough and doesn't give good feed back. reviews.comment: Great and kind professor!

Course material is up-to-date and gives an overview of the current tools and techniques used in big data vis. There are two assignments at the beginning weeks to have hands-on experience right away. Afterward, you get to work on an interesting group research project. He is always available to help the students. A genuinely nice human being.
Good and up-to-date material, fun assignments, but almost no class interaction. Professor was available to answer questions outside office hours.

The lectures are not as good as how I would expect. The professor didn't make students participate during lectures and it's really hard to get past his accent. On a bright note, he was able to help people out when they're struggling with the homework assignments.
Easy and interesting class.

The class consisted of short weekly open-note quizzes based on lectures, readings, and videos, as well as group journal assignments. The workload was manageable, and the content was very interesting and informative. She was a great professor!
Take this class if you need one of your gen eds fulfilled. very easy professor, all the work is straight forward and super easy
Very easy class. 1 quiz a week with another assignment every 3 weeks. Best class I've taken
prob the easiest class youre ever going to take at uic. if you need a gpa booster or an easy gen ed this is a def a class you would want to take.
Very easy class! Take it. One quiz per week.
Completely asynchronous and a very easy class. She made it known that we could contact her for academic or personal reasons which I thought was pretty sweet.

The lectures this professor gave were all the answers to the weekly quizzes. The class was easy to pass, weekly quiz and discussion posts. Her lecture videos and readings were always short and easy to understand!

This class is really easy, but super interesting! Even though I took this class to fill up a GenEd, this was honestly my favorite class. Despite being online asynchronous, we still had the opportunity to learn about our classmates via journal entries. Take this class, you won't regret it!

Definitely recommend taking this class for credit. It is an easy A especially if you are in the groupme for it. There are weekly readings and a quiz. Sometimes there is a journal but that is pretty easy. Overall take this class for the easy credit.
I loved taking this class. It was very easy but also very insightful information relating to culture and food. This is an easy A and made my first semester as a grad student very enjoyable.
Very easy A, weekly homework quizzes with a few questions each, and then 5 small/short writing assignments. Would recommend for the GPA boost and easy gen Ed.

reviews.comment: Giamila was an awesome professor, HN202 is an extremely easy course but has really interesting content that makes the class pretty enjoyable. Two papers and weekly quizzes means there isn't much work to be done for the semester. Take the easy GPA boost and take it with Giamila
Easy A and this professor will extend deadlines if a lot of people ask and the class is very easy.
Easy class, 2 simple papers and easy content quizzes every week. Professor Fantuzzi is very lenient with late work. Fantuzzi is easy to reach out to when you need help too!

Class is very straightforward! There are 2 800 word essays but she gives plenty of time to complete them. This class is organized and there are only weekly quizzes besides those essays. Read the papers and watch the videos! Easy A !
weekly quizzes that are super easy, plus 2 written assignments. easy A

reviews.comment: Easy class...the videos were simple and the weekly quizzes were based off the lecture videos and some articles. Professor really kept it simple and is willing to help her students

10/10 recommend

reviews.comment: weekly quizzes that include nine to ten questions and multiple choice. All are taken from the available resources and course slides. 2 simple papers for the midterm and final Overall, the professor is friendly and the class is enjoyable.
This class had many interesting topics and was just weekly multiple choice quizzes and 2 essays
All there is to this class are weekly quizzes that are all multiple choice and a few very easy paper assignments. Good class overall and the topics are very easy and fun to learn from this course.
Fun, interesting course that never stressed me out. Excellent choice for a gen ed. Helps you reflect on your own culture and its food while learning about new ones!

Professor Fantuzzi's HN202 class is amazing. The lectures are super interesting and not too difficult to understand. There is not much required of you except for weekly quizzes (which are easy if you watch the content) and a few short essays. I would definitely recommend this course and professor.

Her class of food and culture has pre recorded videos which are around 20-45 minutes long which you take notes on. Just watching the lectures and actively paying attention you can get an easy A. She is very lenient on late grades too.

Best class ever, these quizes are so easy its hardly a challenge. She's just mandatory on attendance, but trust me the class lectures are very interesting. There's this potato lecture that inspired me to grow my own potatoes. Definitely recommend this class :)
