reviews.comment: HN202 is a really easy and interesting elective. Just 14 quizzes and 3 very short assignments. The material is interesting and you will do well on the quizzes if you review the material. The assignments are also very simple. Great elective if you have a busy schedule!

The professor is phenomenal, she has been one of the best professors I have had the privilege of studying under. The course material was incredibly easy to understand and as long as you watch/read content on Blackboard you will pass. No textbook required, 14 quizzes (one each week), and 3 super easy assignments. She is passionate about the content.

Easiest class ever! No sync lectures, 14 quizzes (1 quiz per week, you get a week to do it, it's 10 questions and timed to 30 min), 3 homework assignments that are super easy (100 word papers and the topics are easy to write about). As long as you read the material posted on Blackboard, you'll do fine on the quizzes. Also professor is super nice!
Super nice. 3 assignments that are pretty easy and 13 quizzes which are 10 questions and 30 minutes :)))

amazing person. very easy and interesting class. 3 exams, 4 homework assignments, and 5 quick activities. all super easy. exam questions and answers are straight from the slides. she uses poll everywhere for attendance point (1 for each day). she's a sweet soul and I completely recommend her and this class!

Shes a nice women, class is easy all she asks is you dont talk & be respectful. She used poll everywhere for attendance/participation. Exam questions are straight from the slides. Really hard not to get an A. Homework is minimal & there were about 4 easy readings. She plays a lot of videos too. Easy gen-ed option.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Keisha is a lovely, caring and understanding person. She is passionate about advocating for the voiceless in our society, and is well respected in the organizing community. She is just not a good professor. 90% of classes were student led, and what lecture she would give would blow through concepts that she herself was not familiar with.

Had her for US 101, and she taught the curriculum really well! She explained urban concepts well, using examples from Chicago to better visualize them. Also had a fun group project for finals where we did a community profile of a neighborhood. I enjoyed it!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Keisha was an amazing professor. A very tough grader, but gave us opportunities to learn and revise for a better grade. I did feel like the class was mostly students teaching each other, however, she always contributed to the dialogue between students and presented a few times on her own. I learned so much in her class!

Wonderful human being, not a great professor. In person class turned into online class because she had "allergies" every day, but more importantly, I'd say more than 80% of teaching was done by other students and not her via power point assignments. She kinda pawned off her job on the class it felt like, which is fine in undergrad but not graduate.

Dr. Kiesha is a great professor. Her lectures are easy to access outside the classroom; they're inspirational and engaging. She's very helpful and kind as well. 10/10, definitely would take her course again.

Kesha is a lovely person and her lectures are always engaging and interesting, but she isn't a very schedule oriented person and can be pretty disorganized. Group presentations get skipped due to lack of time and moved to other days, and class gets randomly cancelled with little notice. Also not very tech savvy, lots of time spent troubleshooting.

Dr. Farmer-Smith is very passionate about the subject of urban studies. She uses a lot of resources to prove her lectures and she is very kind hearted to help a student exceed. Engaging with lectures is important and she enjoys answering questions. She truly cares about her students learning as well as urban studies!
Dr. KiKi is warm, kind and fun! I changed my major after taking her class to urban studies
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Keisha was so kind and caring. Her passion was evident in her lectures and she was super personable. I took the class as my elective and didn't know much about urban studies, but she made the class engaging and easy to understand. I appreciated her positivity and cheerfulness that was felt through the screen.

great personality, definitely knows her stuff about urban planning, yet gets defensive when asked about due dates that are nowhere to be found/ can't make up her mind on her own syllabus. Granted she kinda had a rough semester, but when you contradict yourself... lots of EC opportunities, can be reading heavy at times. participating & projects
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Assigns a lot of reading responses but allows for corrections. Overall, really easy class
Beat class ever!!!!!
Great instructor and I enjoyed the class. Tou will do a lot of reading and reflection writing tho!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Keisha is a true asset to our planning program. She encourages critical thinking about the theories and models that we cover in class. She is also careful to approach planning from and intersectional lens.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Excellent professor- she brings her real life/ work experiences into the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She has a great personality and seems very nice and caring but I don't think she has enough knowledge on Urban Planning. The class is an easy A as long as you do the assignments and a final group research paper.

She cares about her students and what we think. She is almost an urban planning expert and is a great person to aspire to be as an urban planner. There is a lot of reading but she also goes through it during class to make sure everyone has the concept. Super great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Wonderful and dedicated professor.
Great lecturer and a very interesting class.

It's appalling that this professor is still employed. This is the worst academic experience I've ever had, not even sure you can call it academic. She is either grossly incompetent or doesn't care at all about students. Lectures are useless and assignments are labs with vague tasks. I'm not sure what the point of this class is, It's just a waste.

This professor didn't teach well, unorganized, doesn't use blackboard correctly. She doesn't post practice problems for the class. She also does not record her lectures and its very hard to follow her when she's lecturing and seeing where everything connects since she writes on the board.

Very unorganized, poor communicator, can get snappy with students, and greedy w points. Not very accomodating and leaves emails on read. No lecture slides, mostly sloppy handwritten notes. Doesn't work through problems during lectures as often as she should. Too often doesn't post necessary materials in a timely manner if at all. Posts grades late.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: A mess. Lectures are disorganized and she only does handwritten notes (that she doesnt post). Essentially your only resource is a hard to follow textbook written by the professors. Takes weeks/months to respond to emails, cancels class half an hour before its meant to begin. If you absolutely have to take this class, dont take it with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: The content of the course doesn't seem too bad but this prof makes it 100x worse.

BEWARE! Do not take this class if you're taking PHYS 132 with her. Her teaching style is horrible! You have no idea what she's talking about and majority of the course I have to teach myself. The textbook isn't helpful at all! She takes forever to respond to emails. It's not worth it. I don't know why UIC hires bad professors. Don't go through it!
I can teach this class better and i don't even know the material. If i can give her a 0 rating id do that to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Doesn't teach off of ppt slides, simply hand notes. Notes aren't organized and is difficult to know what chapter is being covered. We once had to learn a whole chapter in one lecture the day before the exam. Didn't like her teaching style/notes since they didn't directly reflect the exams which are majority of your grades.
She explains well. She goes a little slow, but she makes sure you really understand.
good professor and good lectures! also, a very kind professor
I really like the way she teaches ;you will really grasp the concept well if you take her class.
She really takes the time to explain the concepts. She will repeat the point more than once so that the concept really get ingrained within you. Would recommend.
Does not turn around to acknowledge that she has a class. Begins immediately and is not open to classroom questions. Thick accent, hard to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: 2 midterms (22% each) and a final (25%), quizzes (19%) plus homework and in-class participation. 2 lowest quizzes dropped and class is curved with 78%A, 63B, 50C, and 38F. Lectures are unclear at times, so prepare to learn from homework. Exams can be hard be but curve makes it possible to get an A.  She is ready to help in office hours.

Really cool and funny guy, but also very unclear and tough on students. I get that it's just the way he talks, but he often comes off as rude and uncaring. If you've ever talked to him about something unrelated to class you'd know he's actually pretty chill, but that doesn't justify mocking students and pushing them too hard (during the field trip)

Fabien is really funny and enjoyable to be around. His demeanor is very stereotypically French, which I think is an acquired taste. I think the reason students have issues with him is that he expects that students reciprocate his passion for rocks, which I can't fault him for. As such, he's a pretty harsh grader and the course was rigorous.

Doesn't put much effort into the class and what I would call a "Powerpoint professor". He just goes slide by slide on the PowerPoint and explains it. There isn't much material to study from except the PowerPoint slides. If you're friendly with him and talk to him, i feel he will grade your paper more leniently than students that don't talk in class

The class wasn't very well structured when I took it. Nearly the entire class bombed the midterm which was very difficult to study for due to lack of materials. Super lecture heavy. Professor Kenig offers good commentary on class topics. Overall not an easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Heavy report.  Fun field work

The course was very interesting and Fabien was a friendly professor. Only downside to Fabien's courses are that exams are very difficult and contain lots of random details one would not expect to appear on exams.

At first I could not understand his accent, but after a couple of weeks I got used to it. For his classes you should know EVERY detail for exams because random things he spends two seconds or less on end up on exams. I also spent time memorizing things that never appeared on exams. Good luck, but there's a small curve.
Both Nagy and Koenig are quite boring.  Prof. Koenig has a weird accent, and pays more attention to ladies in class. Waste of my time.
he is funny ... likes to interact and answer questions... knows his stuff ... loves to teach obviously... makes you want to learn ... grade A+

This class explores the geology of southeast Missouri. Prof Kenig taught the class with Prof Nagy. The up-front class work was interesting and necessary to understand the features in the field. Prof. Kenig is a lot of fun and has a cute french accent! The field trip was the best spring break ever!!The only bad part is writing the report afterwards.

He is a funny teacher sometimes, but lectures can get really boring. This is an ok class, not so hard but it's not easy either. The book is not used at all so do not even bother to buy it; it's just a waste of money. Labs are ok, they can get frustrating. Field trip is a lot of fun. overall it was an ok class, not my favorite but if you like scienc

As long as you attend class and take notes you should be fine.  The key is to understand the concepts and be able to apply them.  You should enjoy his lecture on particulates in the atmosphere, especially soot.
Hard to understand him with his accent, but he's nice enough and knows the material

this guy is funny and has a cool teaching method...class for 101 was way to hard...60% averages on mid term...final 78%...book was used first 4 weeks then nothing...if you attend lectures, labs, and field trip and try with some effort you'll be fine.. got 80s on midterm and 90 on final...very helpful if you seek help..very nice guy and fun, but har

This class have TONS of notes. The avgs for the 2 midterms were around 60%. The exams can be quite difficult because his questions are tricky and he picks specific questions. The final itself wasn't too bad b/c I guess he realized how bad we did on the first two midterms. Doing well on the LABS are a MUST and so is attending the field trip.
the material was difficult, and hard to understand. we never used the book.
No Comments

This overall was a pretty easy class, she made the lectures mandatory the first half of the semester but gave up because she doesn't like tech (which she talks about a lot) overall it is an easy class with only a few papers that are easy to do so I would take this class again.

Eh. The lectures were boring, quite dreadful. She did attendance at beginning of semester since it was mandatory but stopped once she realized barely anyone would start showing up. She cares about her students, it is obvious, but it is quite a boring class to be in. 2 papers, and 1 long essay for final. Discussions mandatory. Wouldnt take again. 🤨
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She's a good professor, but you definitely need to stay on top of the writing assignments and papers. There are three smaller writing assignments and two papers, and one final paper. Attendance is mandatory for lectures and discussion, but you don't necessarily need to take notes. She does talk a lot about phones and technology in her class though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: mr feldman is THAT GUY. Everything is open note. even the final was open note LOL. Free easy points. He's pretty soft spoken so its kind of hard to hear him sometimes but he's a very good teacher and he cares about his students!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! so 1000000000000000000 reccomend

One of the best most chill professors i've ever had. Attendance is only required for discussion, one discussion presentation, and three exams which are all open note (you are allowed to have your laptop and look at the lecture/discussion slides). Would absolutely recommend taking his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The topics covered in the class were very informative and interesting, especially with his input. There are three take home exams which are simple. There are weekly readings which are not too difficult (pls read them!). Besides that, he is pretty funny and a wonderful professor, he only wants the best for his students, definitely enjoyed the class!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easiest gened that you could actually learn something from him
Prof. Feller-Simmons is the best! He's so smart and makes you care about the class. I would take his class again and again!
The paper exams made it difficult to draw the notes. It was a bit tiring to do homework every week, but he is a generous instructor in terms of grades.

He's a very harsh grader. The homework could get very difficult at times and I didn't like the flipped classroom method. I thought his videos were too long and just reading the slides worked better for me. He's incredibly helpful if you go to his office hours and he has a good sense of humor. The extra credit assignments carried me.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Felder grades relatively tough compared to the other BME professors at UIC. However, he does this because he truly cares about teaching students. In BME 310, he releases empty slides that he goes over in class to force you to take notes. He wants students to learn and truly understands the content unlike many other UIC BME professors.
One of the best professors at UIC.
He understands students in this online course, reducing loads of work, and turning two works into extra credit. Also, his jokes in every class were lit.

Not only is he a real teddy bear, is usually always available during class hours and outside of class hours to help you when needed. He is very understanding, having taken out 2 homework assignments to ease the load on us, while giving us extra credit opportunities.

BioE 250 is a group based course. You will be given three BioE problems and you and your team should find a solution for it. Prof. Felder is amazing. Everything is clear, if not, ask him. He's really kind and he will answer immediately.

I enjoyed how Dr. Felder taught this class. His lecture slides are easy to follow and he is always to answer questions if there is any confusion. I think that a lot of the grading for BIOE 101, in particular, is actually done by the TA because if I was in the TA's office he would mention to me whether or not he graded my most recent homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Awsome professor! I can't complain about him. Just attend the lectures and do the homework on time.

If you don't take a class with Dr. Felder, your bachelor's experience is incomplete. He is really passionate about teaching and genuinely cares for his students. He has the best way of speaking that will draw you in. He explains difficult engineering concepts as if he is telling you a bedtime story. You will actually learn in his classes.

He is one of the best professors I have ever had. He truly cares about his students, and he wants every student to succeed. You will not only enjoy the way the class is taught, but you will learn to love the material.

Most down to earth professor I've had in all of my college career. He really cares about the class, is humorous and makes the class fun. Take him for any BioE class whenever possible. You WON'T regret it.

He is the best professor I have taken at school. His class is well paced and planned. He genuinely cares for your success and interest in bioengineering. He is always ready to help. He is pretty straightforward with what he expects.

Hands down my favorite professor. Genuinely cares for each of his students, and fully answer questions. Projects and assignments are explicitly explained. Easy to talk to, and lectures are also interesting to listen to. Would 100% recommend. You will love him as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Avoid at all costs. Nothing matters except for attendance and submitting homework with the correct answers. If you do that, you'll be able to pass the classes. Each semester is the exact same structure, exams, and projects.  The course is set up poorly, but once you get the hang of it, you'll be able to know the best way to pass the class.

Absolutely would not recommend this professor to anyone. She is a tough grader and does not really care for her students. Participation and attendance are her priority. She also assigns homework every other day and it is not just one thing, it's a whole list. Doesn't explain the assignments or projects at all and just expects you to do them.

She was nice and tried to make the class fun and easier but did not prepare us well enough for the exams. The study guides were basically saying "re-read the book" and no actual practice problems. The actual tests were all about explanations while class was more about getting the right answer. I gave it my best and somehow only managed to get a C.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Fernandez is such a good professor! You will have a lot of homework and readings but she is totally a good professor. She explains everything very clearly. Her exams are based on the readings, so if you don't read, you won't get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Claudia is passionate about her subject but this is definitely a "do as I say, not as I do" course on teaching. There are good readings, but a ton of mindless busy work followed by repetitive lectures. Worst is that instructions for almost all major assignments sent out by email a week before due! No respect for students' time or planning. Boo!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: At first she can come off as a little overwhelming, but as long as you simply as for clarification and show some genuine interest, she is more than willing to help. Pay attention and ask questions. She is very understanding and is willing to work with you for the grade you want. She tries to be as practical and accessible as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I didn't learn anything and had to study with outside materials for the exams.

Instead of just doing a "course curve," maybe you should change your lecture presentation style to one that would make sense for the class. If I'm not getting a good grade with the curve, I'm clearly not learning much or anything, which doesn't benefit me whatsoever. The professor just needs to change his teaching style.
It's hard to understand his english because of his accent but the grade wise he is the best professor. He literally curves grades for homework, quizzes and for the exams too.

This was Prof. Klein's first year teaching here, so many of his mistakes were very elementary and talked though when he would make them. That being said, exams (3 of them) are 50% of the final grade, every exam was curved, and not too tough if you did the bare minimum of studying. However, it's very important to understand the basics of each ch.

You won't learn a lot in the lecture, because he seems to get confused and lost himself while teaching. However attendance is mandatory because there is a single pop up question during every single class. He is cute though so going to class wasn't too bad. Exams are hard, and nothing like the material in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures, homework, and discussion sections prepare you perfectly for the exams. If you study, do the homework, take notes, and actually show up to things its an easy enough class. Professor Klein is kind and knowledgeable and answers questions well, and will respond to emails quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Difficult to understand his lecture, as he doesn't explain the topic well, his wording is confusing. The tests are challenging; the questions are confusing. What helps is the way he curves the tests, which is very generous. Just stay on top of homework, complete weekly progress checks during the discussion sections, and be thankful for the curves.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: UGH I feel so bad because he genuinely seems so kind, but MicroEcon 120 is already confusing as is, especially if its ur first Econ class so maybe just wasn't the class for him. He knew what he was talking about and the slides were okay, but the exams were like, above the thinking of what we learned. DO THE HW THO, thats what will help u pass

Dr. Klein is a very kind person, and the course does not have much homework with attendance not required. However the exams were really hard for me but the curves are extremely generous. Just be ready to take notes in class and there will also be weekly discussion sections with 5 question quizzes. Also there are pop up questions which are easy.

I honestly just felt bad for him, he seemed so uncomfortable and confused the entire semester. He started lecture with telling us the professor who was supposed to teach the class suddenly retired, so now he was teaching it. He canceled class one time because his back hurt, that was funny. He curves generously. All in all, solid B tier professor.

He seems like a nice person, but it's hard to pay attention in class as the majority of the work doesn't make sense, and you need to be on top of your homework as you receive a lot, and aren't alerted or told when it's due. You get graded from pop quizes during class, you get review test during dicussions groups, and get warm ups graded.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Boring lectures, Random "pop quizzes", and exams did not really reflect what was shown in class. Never mentions due dates for any homework or assignments, so figure that out yourself.

I dont know why all the reviews hate him, he's a pretty chill guy. Granted, his lectures are a bit slow, but you can zone out while he talks and be fine because he posts his slides and they're straightforward. Come to class just for the pop-up quizzes and study for the text the day before, you'll get an easy A. That's my boy right there

He's a really nice guy, also his first year teaching. Class is hard but you learn a lot more in discussions than in lecture. Homework counts for a lot but it's usually easy. Exams are hard but the final grade is curved a lot (60% is a B for example: this can change depending on the scores of the class though). Lectures aren't that engaging
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: He seems like a nice guy, but is a horrible professor. He seems like he doesn't even know what he is talking about in lecture half the time. Lectures are really boring because he talks so slow. He doesn't show you a lot of example problems that can help you study. Homework doesn't go into hand with lecture. Exams are really hard. Final exams = 20%.

Great guy! Just not a really good teacher. Got bored a lot in class, and almost none of the material is connected to the real world. If you tune him out, the textbook videos/problems will teach everything for you. Lectures are really boring. He's nice both in grading and talking to 1:1! Just does not do a good job as a lecturer.

He's not a bad professor—lectures can be slow, but he explains well. I wish there were better study materials since the textbook questions don't match the exams. Still, if you stay consistent and try your best, the class is very passable.

He seems like a generally nice dude but he's just not good at his job. The lectures are very very boring and only has these things called "Pop ups" as a way of mildly engaging students. They're also how he marks attendance. Main point is, very boring lecture style.

Amazing class! If you want to learn about Balkan history, you are in luck! You will get to spend 5 minutes on Albania and then the next hour on all of the history on Poland! If you love Poland, this is the best class for you. We learn about Poland , Poland and some more Poland. Fantastic class if you love to take exams and 8 page essays. Amazing!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Her grading style was frustrating, as she is an excessively hard grader. Then the attendance policy, which requires students to "clear any absence with her at least one week in advance and write a 3 page critical analysis based on the readings". This policy is unfair, as unexpected situations can prevent students from providing advance notice.

While this was a hybrid course (asynchronous lectures just aren't for me) they were all very well done, and the in-person class sessions were always engaging and interesting. If you're interested in Eastern Europe, take her
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Fidelis is incredibly smart. She is clear with not only what she wants but what will actually make you a stronger writer and academic. Also, she's funny! The readings, though, aren't always the most accessible. Walls of text sort of readings. I enjoyed lectures but the hw usually left me bored and I dreaded the final paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is mean. I asked her for a letter of recommendation. She agreed. Within a week, I got a call from another prof in the department who told me that she is telling everyone that she put in my letter that I am intellectually capable, but not committed. To put a cherry on top she made me sign one of those non-disclosure forms. She cant be trusted

She makes very interesting lectures and chooses good books from which to educate us on. Her and her TA Zukhra did an amazing job this semester. Class was always fun and full of discussions. Just be ready to read otherwise not bad.
Worth taking - had to read quite a bit but overall not bad. Certainly better than other classes I took this year. She knows a lot and is helpful.

Prof. Fidelis is great and is extremely knowledgeable in her field. There are only a few assignments in the course with one big paper. Besides that, there are a few books that she expects you to have read in order to write your paper. Nonetheless, the course was not extremely demanding but it was very interesting and I really enjoyed her lectures.
I enjoyed the class a lot. Not at all difficult if you pay a bit of attention.
Incredible teacher. Discussions were fun!

I like Professor Fidelis so much that I ended up enrolling in several of her courses. Not only is she intelligent and inspirational, she is also very committed to her students - providing great feedback and advice on a variety of assignments. UIC most definitely needs more professors like her! You will not regret signing up for her classes.

I am signing up for another class with Professor Fidelis this year. I took history of Poland with her and I recommend it. The class was interesting and less stressful than other classes for me because all the exams were take homes.

I don't understand all the bad reviews on this website about the professor. She was really nice and actually cared about her students. She provided plenty of extra credit opportunities and made class interesting. She did fire her TA in the beginning so maybe that was the reason grades weren't as great in prior years.

Wonderful teacher! You do have to pay attention and if you do you will realize that what you are learning is actually interested. Prof. Fidelis is so knowlegable and cares about what she is teaching. Great Class. no textbook needed. Polish studies program at UIC is very well established. Wonderful teachers and prof. fidelis is one of them!

WOW, the worst teacher at UIC by far. Horrible. She's mean, not helpful, laughs at your opinions, she requires you to show up to EVERY lecture. SUPER HEAVY ACCENT. UIC's reputation is ruined by teachers like her.  TERRIBLE TERRIBLE TERRIBLE.

I took this class because I wanted to learn about the history of my Native country (Poland, and I dropped this course after only 2 lectures. She is a terrible teacher. She doesn't seem like she even likes what she teaches. She reads straight from her notes. You can't really understand her that well because her accent is so heavy. BEWARE!!!

Honestly, it was BAD!  I think she is way too much into teaching!  She requires her undergrad students to do the amount of work grad students would do!  It is insane!  Lots of reading, lots of essays!  She grades hard too!  Hard to understand and not too helpful!

Speaks with a heavy accent. Hard to understand sometimes. Well organized though. Knows her stuff, but doesn't like to be questioned. Lots of reading. Lots of discussion. Participation and good writing are the must! Willing to comment on paper drafts. I would recommend the class only if you're interested in it! Requires you to study a lot!

she's mean. she discourages questions. i once asked her to slow down because no one could keep up with her (she talks really fast with a thick accent and u have to write as fast and she talks) and she gave me this look like i was an idiot! She does not like helping others with work, and is just not a good teacher.

i don't know how she got those two positive opinions! she wast the worst teacher i ever had including preschool, high school and and 5 years of college. biased, unfair, doesn't know anything about what she's teaching! UIC needs to get rid of her because she ruins its reputation!

terrible. if you dont like to participate alot or are not great at writing essays then do not take. that is your whole grade. plus shes so boring and doesnt talk loud so you cant hear her in the back of the class.

I thought she was great teacher. I learned a lot from her. I earned an A because she was so helpful. You have to read your assignments and participate. She is your textbook!!!!! Great to get to know during office hours and she is wonderful to me.
Very good teacher. Would  definitely recommend one of her classes.

HORRIBLE TEACHER!!!! i agree with other opinions... this teacher ruins uic's reputation! don't take her! i thought i would enjoy this class but it was my most difficult class! i enjoyed chemestry more than this class! worst experience ever! she thinks that you have nothing to do than reading stupid books for her class! she is unfair!

HORRIBLE TEACHER!!! BEWARE!!! SHE FAILED ME AND ACCUSED ME OF PLAGIRISM AND I DID MY PAPER MYSELF!!!  IF YOU DON'T ATTEND CLASS YOU WILL FAIL!! HARD TO UNDERSTAND ALSO!  BY FAR THE WORST TEACHER I HAVE EVER HAD IN MY LIFE!!!

hard as hell. its like taking another language. Material is hard to understand. Grades hard. Lot of essay questions on final. Need to attend class everyday and read all the material. Take good notes or it will hurt u at the end

Passionate about what he taught, it was AH 273. Not sure because of the classroom or him, but kind of a lot of lecture and made me sleepy. Interesting things, but still a lot in one long class. You don't really need to read just pay attention a bit, he tells you exactly what will be on quizzes and exams.

reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

If the app tells him you don't read every page or don't leave quality enough comments/questions on the reading, he docks points. For students who are slow readers or English is their second language, this is entirely unfair.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class was pretty heavy on the workload. There were several assignments due every week, plus longer papers interspersed between. I did well in this class because I love art, if you don't it will be tough because this course will take you to the deep end of the swimming pool. I liked it overall though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: If you have an interest in art and history, but have no intention in majoring it or minoring it in it, take this class. It was like being in a TED talk each lecture. Attendance is only mandatory because he gives out information out in lecture, which makes the powerpoints a bit dispensable. How to pass the test? Just write anything you remember
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The exams are completely based on memorization. The study guide has dozens of pieces, while the exams are only based on a few. The lecture itself is really boring, but he posted each PowerPoint after class so if you miss/skip class you can always catch up later. Finegold is an okay professor but the way he presents is boring. Don't take this class.

Professor Finegold is a great lecturer. The class was interesting and you could tell he was passionate about what he was teaching. The tests were a lot of memorization, but that's what's to be expected in any Art History course. If you go to the lectures, it is much easier to study later on.
I took him and honestly, some images were interesting but how does he expect us to memorize every image? Its absurd. My TA sucked too so it didnt help. Its all about memorizing.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Horrible elective class, based on memorization. If you are bad at memorizing 50 plus images and specifically describing them, do not take this class as an elective.

I took her class for UCWR 100, needless to say she is super sweet and smart, but she's an incredibly harsh grader. She expects perfection in every essay. Too much busy work and is super meticulous about everything. I remember i got docked points because my name was not in the right place on the header.

She is a good professor. I took her for a mandatory class and she understands that English classes aren't for everyone.  She is somewhat of a harsh grader, but if you put in some effort, you'll be fine. I finished the semester with an A, with hardly any effort. Talk in class though, she grades participation.

She's really nice and smart but she grades hard. Don't take her for an easy A. lol. You won't get it. 85 is her favorite grade to give. You'll read some good literature and some pretty boring stuff. Still, I am glad I took the class but it is not very easy.

She is very nice and intelligent, obviously. However, it seems that she expects perfection in assignments/writing, rather than working with the students to make sure they produce their work up to her expectations of certain topics and writing quality. I admire her chutzpah with English, but her expectations aren't consistent with a 100-level course

Julie is very sweet and helpful. On each paper she gave really helpful comments and she even let me re-do some papers if she felt that I could do way better.  Maybe it's just me but I feel like she doesn't know how to keep the class interesting. Also, she is a tough grader. But she is fair and is always up for helping you as much as she can.

She is a ridiculous grader--VERY harsh, and expects you to be perfect at writing. I took a 100 level class with her,and she literally assigned heavy homework EVERY DAY.Completely unnecessary homework too,just busy work.Falls behind on syllabus,WAY too much work,and ridiculous grading scale.She's a sweetheart,but needs to relax with the work.
She explains everything in a step by step process which is quite helpful. I ended the class with a B+, not so much because she is a bad teacher, but because English really isn't my thing.
Great teacher. Took this class during the summer and although it was intense, she made the class great. Highly recommend her. Quizzes are easy. Test are somewhat difficult.
She is the best. Ever.

Professor Fifer is awesome. I can't believe that this was a 200 hundred level class. We watched 3 movies that were really fantastic, we had to write a music blog every weak-which was really easy. Exams are exactly the same as the study guides she gives. She is really nice and helpful. Totally recommend her!!!!

Fifer is a great professor, she is very organized and fair. She emphasizes key points and ideas so it is easy to stay on track as long as you do the reading (which is not that much work). The three small papers are veryy simple and reasonable and she is a nice person! TAKE HER

Fifer is excellent, just come to class and pay attention and the papers will be very easy to write. Workload is reasonable and papers are short! The class is a little repetitive which makes all the concepts so clear, I learned a lot and would recommend her. She is also a very warm and sweet person who I've personally never seen angry
She's a hard grader and she's picky. Attendance and participation required. Read and understand all the readings! She's unpleasant when nobody participates and reads. Wouldn't recommend her.
Good person not the best professor. There wasn't much feedback on work so you don't know why you received that grade,  but he is an easy grader.

he will just say things in class, like certain things won't get points taken off or that attendance ISN'T mandatory, then change his mind mid-semester without telling the class. he's an easy teacher, but it comes at the cost of him not being very clear on things or outright giving you the wrong information. very nice guy tho

He is a good person but not a good professor, he doesn't give any feedback unless you ask and he is super flexible and gives alot of time to do the projects, which is a good and bad thing because the class was behind most of the semester. Dont even attempt to email him. He also only grades your midterm and that is your only grade until the final.

He is a nice and good guy but not a good teacher in my opinion. He hardly reply to student emails, his class is always behind others and he give really unclear idea of what u need to do for your projects.
100% should take this professor, he is really supportive

I've had professor Flemister for 2 semesters now and I can not begin to say how thankful I am to have had him. He is the most caring, funny, flexible teacher I've ever had. He is understanding and has every quality you want in a professor. I'm so grateful for him that I nominated him for teacher of the year. 100% would take a class with him again.

Provided a caring and engaging atmosphere, while also allowing his students to work independently. Frequently lectured with a rambling style that made it feel more conversational. Mostly assigned projects and stuck to the syllabus, but offered flexible deadlines. Provided tailored feedback to each student. Gave professional anecdotes liberally.

I took his class about the history of race in the middle ages and it is hands down the most interesting class I've ever taken. Dr. Fletcher is a great lecturer and I was never bored listening to him talk as he is great at explaining things, while making it interesting and engaging for the class. Workload wasn't bad either. Would highly recommend.

Honestly thought he would be a tough grader but if you actually put in work, do the readings, and try to do the essays properly you have a high chance of ending the class with an A. He is also understanding and he makes sure he can accommodate to anything happening in your life.
Really nice professor but a tough grader. Worked really hard and still ended up with a B. I would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Fletcher was a breath of fresh air during online school. He did not require us to turn our cam/videos on. He was very easy-going and sweet. We had a couple short papers and discussions for grades. He grades fairly fast and gives great feedback. The class was not something I was interested in, but he made the lectures really interesting!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was an online course so it really wasn't too challenging, however there were weekly quizzes, 3 main exams, and 2 written assignments. I do think it was a lot of work but it is worth it for an online gen ed/major requirement.

Professor Floros class (Pols 184) was one of a few classes were I enjoyed going to lecture. They always were always interesting. The class itself was extremely easy, quizzes and tests including the final were online, and other than two easy essays there was no other graded work. Very easy Gen ed, I def recommend it.

The professor herself is okay, nothing negative to say. The discussion section is useless in my opinion and don't add anything to the class even if you participate. Exams are online and two main writing assignments. If you're taking this as a gen ed and don't have much interest in pols, DO NOT TAKE IT!!! Trust just look for a different class.

Holy yap and we have to use iclicker

The class was easy. Exams are online and pretty straightforward. They give good feedback on the writing assignments. Worst professor ever. She also violated the ferpa code

This professor is heavily biased in her teachings and when she starts to lose a political discussion/argument she gets very shallow and petty. doesn't help that her lectures are the most average ones you might attend. this class made me & a huge group of ppl extremely uncomfortable. takes pics of the class. also she released a list of names of students in SJP to an israeli gov official she invited to speak in the class. she also made sure to silence the only palestinian student in the class and sat right next to them during the talk. idk how shes still teaching

Does not care for the well being of her students or their safety, especially Arab students (specifically Palestinian). She seems to have issues any time a student shares an opposing viewpoint to her. Very odd person. Idk why she is a professor. She gave me the creeps. Not normal- who takes a picture of her class. Very bizarre person. I have to say she creeped me out.

On the first day of class she took a picture of our class because she knew students would drop the course during the semester. The class wasn't very engaging in my opinion and the discussions were bland.

Hated every minute of being in her class. She often excuses herself for having ADHD her requirements and assignments were ridiculous. I don't know how UIC still allows her to teach after all the very questionable decisions she's made.

She's your typical far-left liberal UIC teacher that spews her agenda onto you. There's no real substance or critical thinking in this class, just like the overwhelming majority of UIC political science professors and classes.

pretty good semester with this professor, even if the subject wasn't my fave. textbook suggested for class, but showing up to lecture/taking notes will suffice for tests. map quizzes will catch you off-guard, but they're not that bad. discussion activities are relevant, and pretty fun. professor likes to crack jokes and tell quick stories in class

Her lectures made you not want to show up to class. Very hard grader and lacks understanding. Made very questionable choices without caring about her students. The format that she required for the paper was ridiculous just like all the assignments for her class. Don't take her class unless you want to be miserable.

Material isn't hard to comprehend but the professor is close minded towards certain topics. Dosen't let students state their opinon. TA Yasmine does a wonderful job explaining the class, let's students lead discussion with their own points of view of the topic, and actually cares about getting the material right.

Absolutely teaches anti-American sentiment. Very unorganized and not open to opinions she doesnt want to hear. Spent a whole class trying to convince out class that China is not a threat to the United States. If you want to learn minimally this is the professor for you!

Wasn't worth my time. She didn't seem to have a real grasp of the material(at least to the level I would expect) and her lectures were not very engaging. Very biased, hard grader

reviews.comment: She made lecture really interesting. And Amir her TA is really cool too. She shows a real interest in her job and seems to enjoy her job.

Professor Floros is definitely one of the best professors I've ever taken. She's really funny, the lectures are interesting, and she puts a lot of extra credit opportunities. You can tell she knows the material by heart. I really learned a lot. Would recommend.

Professor Floros is amazing! Very knowledgeable, super understanding and caring. Lenient with homework at times if you let her know before hand. Funny yet informational lectures. She's just great. Not just for this class, but any political science classes.

POLS 184. The professor's lectures are interesting. You won't fall asleep. DO NOT BE FOOLED BY HER CURRENT RATING. Floros is extremely childish and she takes any feedback as a personal attack on her character. Does not communicate with her TAs which leads to wrong grades. The diplomatic visits and short papers are great. Easy A if you do the work, great professor!

Prof Floros is really engaging and funny. She makes lecture interesting and easy to pay attention to. No need for a book, just take good lecture notes and you'll be fine. Tests are similar to AP style (application-based, not definition based). 3 major (100pt) papers. 3 tests. map quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: The only college class where Kahoot is a valid form of test review, the discussion sections before exams were fun. I didn't really vibe with the fact that there were such few tests and with the fact that we had map quizzes... didn't know I was taking a geo course. Besides that, Floros is pretty chill, she's very knowledgable in her field.

How much you like this class depends on how much you like the topic. Floros is a decent professor, lectures are sometimes dry but as long as you have the info you're good. Content is not hard, and is really pretty intuitive. Don't take this if you absolutely hate the subject, you won't have a good time. I did like it, however, and did well.

The class itself: 3 exams, multiple map quizzes, 3 current event questionnaires. Attendance is mandatory for both lecture and discussion. Professor? Overrated. Very mundane lectures, takes a lvl 100 class too seriously. Along with TA's, never gave good feedback and is not too interested in the success of her students. Take someone else if you can.

This class was Gen ED requirement for me, professor Floros was always unprepared, very bland and dry, her TAs did not give any insightful feedback and did not let you revise any assignments. Not an easy class unless you like the subject. Discussions were useless and were not related to the actual class. Highly do NOT recommend FLOROS. The Worst.

Shes a great professor and the class is a useful gen ed. As long as you attend lecture class is a pretty easy A. You dont really need a textbook either her lecture notes are extremely thorough. Discussions actually fun for this class.

reviews.comment: I definitely think Floros is a knowledgeable professor, but this class was definitely not an easy A. Although there are no exams, attendance is mandatory. reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Loved this class! Floros has engaging presentations and she's great. Discussion is mandatory, but lectures aren't. But you'll learn a lot by going - less than 2 hours a week for lecture but you'll spend even longer a week trying to catch up so you should go.

Professor Floros is good and passionate about what she teaches however shes lecture heavy and doesnt stop to answer too many questions. The TAs are who youll address most of your questions to and see outside of class and in discussion. 3 exams, 5-6 map quizzes, 3 memos.

reviews.comment: Awesome professor, great lectures. Really breaks down the material for students to easily understand. A bit of work is required, but I would highly recommend her.

reviews.comment: She's funny during class and the information she provides for the class is plentiful. Tests are very easy, since they are based off of her powerpoints. You may need the book only if you are confused with the materials. On the tests, there are extra credits. You need to attend classes since she tells about her personal life, which are extra credit

Dr. Floros is a really cool professor. She may come off as mean sometimes, but if you get on her good side then you'll be fine. She does require you to write A LOT, but the topics are almost completely up to you so she gives you freedom with her essays. I would definitely recommend taking her.

Course would be more enjoyable if you have an interest in the subject. She really knows what she is talking about. Course consists of 3 "memos" & 3 exams. Exams are not hard as long as you pay attention during the lectures (she gives useful study guides). You don't need the book (only if you plan to read on your own.. which you don't need to do).

At the time that I took this course, I was a Political Science major. This course was the most difficult intro level course I have taken at UIC. If this professor doesn't particularly like you, do not expect her to budge on your grade. She is boring in lecture unless you are truly passionate about IR. 0/10 would not recommend

reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Simple enough class. If you come to lecture the exams are pretty easy. The most difficult aspect of this class are the map quizzes, so be sure to study for those. Lecture is interesting and enjoyable. You only really need the book for the case studies.

Passing this class really depends on whether you have common sense or not. Dr Floros was funny, engaging, and informational with her lectures. Her tests  were very easy and to-the-point, right off her slides. Her TAs were some of the nicest and most willing to help you improve. As long as you show up and show some interest, you are good.

Prof. Floros likes what she does and you can tell because her class is not boring. She   is funny and has something to say about almost everything. Her class was very interesting. You don't really need the textbook. There is only 1 paper we have to do and a midterm and a final.

Awesome class. The teacher is funny, her lectures are great and she makes the material very easy to understand. Attendance not mandatory and you don't really need the book. Everything in the powerpoints is what's going to be on the exam, no surprises. Discussion sections are super easy too.
Her exams are tricky - you have to spell terms out, but they are doable. Make sure you study! She is an incredible lecturer and you learn a lot. Read the book and attend class.

Prof. Floros is good lecturer, and knows about the field. 40% three papers (not very hard), 50% exams and 10% quizzes. Exams are multiple choice and definitions. Know the definitions and skim over the book chapter but do well on the papers.

Funny lady. Entertaining lectures. Tests are quite easy if you study the outlines which she gives. Most people don't come to class. She doesn't take attendance. There's almost no homework or reading. I would highly recommend this class.

Very helpful professor. Her lectures are actually interesting even if international relations is not your major. Her study guides basically are outlines of the exams. If you go to lecture you most likely will not even have to open your textbook. Take her!

She is great. Very enthusiastic! Her exams are exactly everything she talks about so you need to go to lecture. There is some busy work the class but it's worth it if you like the subject. I loved her class and I'm taking another one next semester!
She is a very good lecturer and her points are on point and knows what she is talking about. Not too much work and they are not hard either.
**PHIL 201 for review below

PHIL 204-It's def necessary to take notes in class. Otherwise, he can send u the recording if u show up to class. He's also pretty lax on not showing up (as long as u got a good excuse). He can send recordings to u. Grading isn't clear, but that's phil for u. Just get everything down the T and go to office hours. Participate- esp in discussion.

Interesting guy. Needs to be more open to taking questions in class. There is no clear grading criteria in class which makes it confusing. Heavy topics, need to pay a lot of attention. He needs to record his lectures and make them more accessible to his students. He allows people on zoom under some circumstances but needs to be more flexible.

Professor F never disappoints. I have taken 3 courses with him and while he can be a tough grader it is with the intention of improving your abilities. Philosophy can be tough but if you do the readings for his courses you'll be fine. Interesting lectures, a chill prof. and good feedback on papers always. He rounds grades up. Great prof esp for UIC

reviews.comment: Professor is good overall. You do have to buy books that you will read. If you just put your effort into it you'll be fine. Still not so bad. I would recommend.

Professor Fleischacker was an excellent professor.  Though the reading are dense he would explain them, so they were easy to understand. The lectures were very interesting and you can tell he is very knowledgeable on the topic.  As long as you wrote down what he said during the lecture, the essays were easy as was the final.

This was the easiest class yet the stupidest. There was no real grading criteria. The TA checks and grades the paper, And they don't want your thoughts they want what is right. You don't get any points or anything just a grade. This class was ridiculous. No point at all. I worked so hard and got a C. I atleast expected B. Should've been an A

3 Papers throughout the semester that act as exam grades. Weekly summaries and weekly in-class questions are used as a supplement. Not a hard class. He's really engaging and promotes questions and deep thought processes.

Course material is difficult, but Prof F is one of the most helpful professors I've ever had. He's extremely intelligent and knows what he's teaching. He quite often uses the socratic method and challenges students to think critically about the material. I would certainly take another course with him. Grading is rough, but philosophy is not easy.

Engaging, interesting, articulate and a charismatic teacher. If you're in college to learn then take a course offered by him. Breaks down tough material and is quite witty! His academic honesty is something to be respected. Always willing to go over material during office hours.
He's a great teacher.  He's interesting, articulate, and passionate about philosophy.  He's shrewd and sometimes even poetic. He's really just an all-around, good guy.

One of my favorite professors of all time (and I'm a senior, so I went through many of them)!  The nicest guy ever, so reasonable with grading and attendance...I seriously cannot find a negative thing to say about this man.  If you have a chance to take his  class, you will not regret it, I assure you.
So refreshing to have a professor that is so passionate about what they teach and has so much knowledge about the topic.

Class stayed fresh with different topics every few weeks. Professor was very interested to take students philosophical views, and was incredibly understanding. Attendance was pretty much mandatory, but it helped when writing the paper which was the majority of the grade. I'd recommend this prof to others.
If you pay attention and take notes, reading is not even necessary. He has a genuine desire to help students both in his class and in life. Highly recommend a course with him.

THE BEST professor for a class on Religion and Philosophy. His interpretation of the assigned readings is clear and concise. Take lots of notes! It will help with the papers. Remember, he teaches from the perspective of the philosophers covered in the course. He may argue on behalf of them sometimes to help you better understand their thinking.
He is a great teacher. He knows what he's talking about and the T.A. (Tina) really helps explain things further. Getting an A in this class is pretty easy, you just have to think a little.

He makes Philosophy much easier to understand. Such an insightful person! He has put out several interesting reads that can help in your PHIL studies. "A Short History of Distributive Justice" and "A Third Concept of Liberty" just to name a few...
No Comments

may be hard to understand at times, but he's always willing to explain again in office hours if you don't get it. kinda hard to get an A, but B's are fairly easy to get. take him if you want to test yourself a little.

very subjective and inconsistent. seems like he cannot understand people who doesn't agree with him. if you share the same ideas you'll be fine, if you disagree w/ him just run away. or you'll get an unfair grade.
Starts slow, but once you catch on to his style of presentation, it becomes easier to understand. Paying attention when he goes into a monotone is crucial!
awesome and a lot of fun!  yeah philosophy fun
The best teacher I had before I transferred out of UICrap.  I strongly recommend taking his class, and if you have the right mindset you'll find out why.
very knowledgeable. dont hate, he went to yale, and hes smarter than youll probably ever be.
class itself is easy, but he can become unclear. he acts pretty stuck up, and many times wont accept other views students may bring up. class discussions were alright, otherwise.
So arrogant and conservative.  Thinks that he knows everything.
No Comments
Very concise, clear, organized.  Was willing to get into discussions with students about subject matter.

She was amazing. Her analysis of our society in regards to inequality was so mind blowing and interesting. This class was truly life changing and it really makes you think about why our society is set up the way it is. I learned a lot of meaningful information. She was super approachable. Make sure to read the textbook!

I didn't like her as a professor. BORING. Uses iClicker (mandatory attendance). Two non-cumulative exams. One 15-page essay that is split up throughout the semester.
