I recommend him.  His study guides are so comprehensive that going to class is completely unnecessary.  I skipped ~80% of lectures and fell asleep in the ones I went to.  The online homework is simple and the research assignments were all graded generously (though I am good at these in general).  The group project is not something to worry about.

Nice guy, but the content was not very interesting to me (I'm not a computer person) Lectures are optional, no attendance, you can probably make due with just reading the book/ppt slides. Final project is with a group and in most cases group projects suck esp. when you've never met or seen the other ppl. Online hmwk isn't too bad.

Fyfe is a really nice guy... this material is just SO BORING. It's really hard to pay attention in class. I never went and still pulled off a B in the class. There is homework, a couple short papers, and a final project.  There are four tests-as long as you study the key terms he puts in the slides, you'll be fine!

He is such a helpful professor! The TAs aren't that helpful, but Fyfe will sit with you and go through each question and explain what you need to write. As well as the project, if you go to him he will help you soooo much! He is so sweet and helpful go to help for help. If u study for two hours on for each test you will get at least a B! He curves!

She is an incredible prof. She is caring and understanding as long as you communicate. There is a lot of reading but it is pretty interesting. It is participation heavy, and discussion is highly encouraged. I took her GWS/ANTH 248.

Prof is very kind and understanding, her classes do require a lot of readings so there's that, but in my opinion not much assignments, reasonable. Pop quizzes though! She dropped half of ours luckily, overall, great! Attendance is mandatory for discussions, go to lecture more than half of the time at least.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Respected

reviews.comment: Professor Reddy is one the best professors on campus. She makes herself available for students outside of class and talks about the importance of current events. She's very flexible with her student's schedules. She doesn't allow access to her slides out of class so pay attention in class. There are also readings each week, which are quite dense.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: assigns too much reading, exams were hard, and class structure was unorganized. if you want to get an A in the class, you have to work really hard. I barely read any articles but relied on summaries and managed an A. attendance system sucked because you have to wait for a piece of paper to go around the class. don't take this class. TAs don't help

If you have the opportunity to take this course you 100% should. The lectures/discussions/readings are so interesting and extremely relevant to current events and social structures. need to read 2-4 readings/week to understand lectures and discussions (5-9 pages each). Prof and TA's extremely helpful and insightful! Amazing course!!

Take this class! Professor Reddy is by far one of the best instructors I've had at UIC. She genuinely cares for students and wants to see them succeed, and is flexible with deadlines if you communicate that you are struggling. This semester was online which made discussion difficult, but participation is important to get the most out of class

I absolutely adored this class and it taught me so much. I 10/10 would take a class taught by professor Reddy again, she has been so inspirational every week providing us with an email of encouragement.

Professor Reddy was great at making the material understandable and making it engaging for the class. The class overall was very interesting but you must take a lot of notes and pay close attention otherwise you will miss the material completely. There are also a lot of readings that you have to do but they were generally interesting. Great class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Don't recommend this class for people who want to learn something out of it

Literally why, I took this class thinking it was going to be a great lecture but she she a very bad professor. She herself is an amazing person she just doesnt know how to teach and makes the class harder than it should be. I shouldnt be studying more for this class than my biochem class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Constantly reassigned and changed readings, grading criteria was NEVER clear, assignments and grades are NEVER posted onBB, Took for Anthropology 216. Professor teddy is a nice person but a horrible teacher. I would absolutely NEVER retake a class taught by here and do not recommend to my worst enemy. CONSTANT research papers and projects + reading
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The reading for the course is a lot and we have a pop quiz every other week. The class is interesting itself but if you are not willing to read or go to class I would not recommend taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: If youre looking for an easy blow off class, this is not for you. Kinda hard for an elective in my opinion. So many articles to read. So many ppl were failing so she reduced # of articles. 5 quizzes. 2 exams. Tests were ok but if u dont read u will fail!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The professor is amazing. If you are overwhelmed with work she will give you extensions no questions asked. She understands life is life, and she actually wants you to learn about India rather than memorize facts. She is EXTREMELY knowledgeable about all of South Asia and is able to answer even the most inquisitive of questions. The BEST

When you enter the class be ready to do a lot of readings, there is no textbook but if you choose to print the articles you'll use up nearly all of your printing money. If you attend class and do the readings the quizzes and exams are easy. The lecture if generally interesting but can sometimes drag on but overall I enjoyed this class.

No textbook but gives extremely long readings. Doesn't really tie the readings and lectures together very well. Not sure what I am supposed to be getting out of this class. Pop quizzes would be easy if you truly digest the readings and fully understand her lectures. Knowledge of geography helps with quizzes.

I'm a little surprised she doesn't have higher rates. I felt the class was very fair on grading. She mentions that there is a lot of readings but if you pace yourself it should be able to handle. She's very sweet and the topics are pretty interesting.

Interesting class. She assigns a ton of readings which can be overbearing. I'm talking 3-4 articles a week that are 10-27 pages in length. I advise going to discussion, material will be clearer there. Don't really like her note slides.I found her exams to be difficult.The readings are interesting though,and the films!Plenty extra cred opportunities

Straightforward class. Essay exam format. Pretty easy to BS if you ask me. Offers extra credit & encourages classroom discussion. I thought she was a cool professor. Not sure why everyone is complaining, I took harder classes in high school.
Very excellent professor, but the material was extremely difficult. If you are compelled to take the class, take it with her.

Be prepared to read 4 semi-difficult articles a week (15-30 pages each) and then do a writing assignment on each article. Tests in essay format (3-6 pages per question). I found it extremely difficult to keep up with the reading. Also you have to give a 15 minute presentation to the class. Least favorite class this semester.

Very good professor! She is very knowledgeable. Nonetheless, this class is not a blow-off class. No textbook, but you have to read 40-page articles per week. 4 1-page papers throughout the semester. Pop quizzes so you need to attend lecture. She gives good review sheets for midterms too. Overall, I highly recommend this class, I learned a lot.

She's actually a very good teacher, the only problem is that she goes way too fast with her power point slides and talks too fast. My notes were never totally complete. Still, she's a good teacher, I definitely loved this class.
She is a good prof. but she speaks quickly and zooms through slides so you have to be there and you have to pay attention if you don't then you are screwed completely

She has her way of teaching. She used power point slides so you didn't really have to take notes. The movies she showed were very interesting. What killed me were the LONG intense readings she assigned. The weekly papers were easy. The midterm was hard but the final was easy. Her class makes me want to minor in women's studies =)

Hands down one of the best professors at UIC. Incredibly intelligent, holds idiot students accountable (so yeah, read, and try otherwise don't got to college). She's also very fun to talk to after class (witty and a bit cynical). If you are lazy and feel entitled to a good grade no matter what, don't waste her time she deserves better than you.

Such a great professor! It was a one day a week class but she made it engaging & worth the time. There is a lot of reading but if you keep up with it & take part in the discussions (which can get heated & interesting) you'll do well in the class. Definitely one of my favorite professors thus far @ UIC!

This class was pretty intense. We had numerous articles to read every week and they were very hard to understand. We had to analyze numerous news articles and write papers. The tests were pretty difficult. I got an A in this class, but I had to work very hard. Don't expect an easy course.

Vocabulary is unclear in powerpoints. Puts powerpoints up for one day and takes them down immediately. No textbook for class and profs notes are unreliable. Class is an overload of material for a 100-level class. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.

I think I have learned more in this class than in any other class thus far. Don't take this class if you want some easy blow off. The readings are intense but if you do most of them and attend lecture on a semi-regular basis you're gonna learn SO MUCH! I'm gonna minor in GWS thanks to this professor and her awesome class :)

Prof. Reddy is really nice, and will help you if you have questions, but the class is still kinda hard. The issues and topics that we discussed were really interesting and the videos/documentaries we watched were cool too. The tests are easier than the writing assignments (we got to use cheat sheets). The TA's however, are NOT helpful.

I took GWS 102(spring '08). We had to write  2 papers and we had 2 exams(one midterm and one final, 10% 4 pop quiz, & 4 discus.. So if you screw any of this up then you are screwed. She doesn't curve much unless you talk to her about it. I had a bad TA. The professor is fine. Reading/slideshows on BB. Get help if you are stuck. Overall kinda hard.

This section of Gender and Women's studies was particularly boring... she talks a lot and because she doesn't make you write notes, you kind of just wander off. Her TA's treated the class like if it was a 200 level course, and it was completely unnecessary. I didn't like the class much.

Im not sure why everyone has such a problem with her.. she is really helpful when you have problems, and as long as you do the course work, shes pretty good on grading as well. Really really liked her.

Greetings! I think people are being too harsh. I agree  that the load was big, but it wasn't impossible. I'm not an Anthro major & I was able to do just fine. She's not asking for the impossible. Maybe it wasn't as easy as people thought. I love writing so I didn't mind the work. Be nice people!

I didn't think she was too bad, but she was a bit unclear. She just needs to realize that we're students not fellow collegues. I loved the theme of the class, and I had fun with the things I did on my own. You got to love my pamphlet guys!

I was told to comment by a friend, and I agree. I love science and this is related to my field, but I hated this class. Too much work, and too critical. Class felt unmotivated by her, and hurt by her criticism despite the work load. Never again!!!

I have to agree with the comments posted here. She thinks her class is the ONLY class in the world. EVERYONE dreaded coming to class, & doing all the assignments. She just wants you busy, & that's the only thing she cares about. The topic is interesting, but she makes class BORING! She just wants wo

I must say that if you are going to take this class, you must prepare to receive hard looks from this conceited prof. She has favorites, and shows it. A lot of people wont get a word in. Only those who are in the field, and those who kiss ass. She's TOO critical and uptight. Not what a good teacher!

This proffesor thinks everyone is an expert. She demands an enourmous amount of work from students, even though the credits earned from this class are minimal. She is too strict, & has a very aggresive way of promoting participation. Few feel comfortable in this class. NOT A FUN CLASS IN THE LEAST!

Everything is always posted late, it is so disorganized, and he never grades anything. Maybe the worst professor I've had here. You will not learn anything and will just do the same assignment 4 times a week. It's all busy work.

Avoid this professor. He posts content and assignments so late, sometimes not until Saturday, when things are due the following day on Sunday. He will also post the wrong things and then 3 days later say it was a mistake and we didn't need to do it (after half the class already completed it). Plus, he grades like 4 weeks late for everything.

Professor Gawel's disorganization negatively impacts his students in ways he does not realize. Assignments take forever to be graded so u have no clue where u stand. EXCESSIVE amount of BUSY WORK that causes u to focus more on the deadline than the quality/actually retaining information. Extensive expectations for 3-4 points per assignment.

All over the place and clearly not meant to teach. Syllabus was provided weeks into the semester, doesn't grade assignments, and posts lectures 1-4 days late. Lectures are very heavy and heavily rely on textbooks and other video content/lectures. So many assignments which are repetitive and redundant. Did not learn anything.

I'm halfway through an online class with him. Overall, he's a very nice guy! There's a lot of content to go alongside the textbook, which is very helpful. The layout is very organized. I've found him to be very accessible through emails. He is a SLOW grader though and there's quite a bit of homework. Certainly not the worst class I've taken.

Very obvious that he could not keep up with grading alongside his full-time job, midterm was not graded until finals week. Did not have much prepared for the majority of lessons, reused slides and skipped through a lot of them. Unreasonable and unnecessary amount of writing for midterm and final. All of my learning was from the textbook readings.

In other posts, they say he gives out a lot of work, duh, theyre online. I was in person and the work we did in class was exactly what we had to do for homework, so the work was easy since we had references. If you'll think you'll have a problem with the workload, take it in person. Cool guy just a slow grader, gives lots of chances to turn work in

Like others have said, content isn't the difficult part. The difficult part is keeping up with the unbelievable amount of work that is assigned 1-2 days late. You also will not have grades in on time at all, and you have a 6 hour 10+ page midterm to look forward to. I cannot speak on the final as it is finals week with no final exam posted still.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Class is overall easy but wayyyyyy too much work for the level of course it is. Weekly discussions, journals, responses and other assignments each weak and always posts them late. Professor needs to give less work when he himself can't even keep up with his own schedule. Course content is very boring and monotonous.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Overall, I thought the course was ok. As someone who has a background in project management, the course was extremely easy and good practice for future positions in the industry. The grading criteria was very vague and there was minimal feedback throughout the course. Weekly assignments also never came out on time. Professor seemed kind and helpful

This class is easy but he was really bad at responding to emails, was a tough grader w no explanations on why you earned a low score, and graded VERY late. I think people got good scores by the end of the semester because he was 1/2 a semester behind on grading so prob did it in a rush. Overall, not a hard class at all.
She is very kind and caring. Her lectures are interesting and she gives a great feedback. Cares about her students and email them if she is concerned. She has a great interaction with students.

We had a lecture once a week with two assignments due each week. There was a good amount of reading but the assignments were not difficult. The topics were interesting and I enjoyed the class discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: nice professor. very understanding about late work and outside circumstances. lots of reading but you'll get a good grade if you pay attention to the lectures.

Took her class in saic 
lectures are so boring. Too much homework every single week.
never discuss readings that assigned，so i don't know why we were reading so much essays.

Lectures are great and it feels like she really cares about what she's teaching. A decent amount of reading, but they're never super long. As long as you pay attention in lecture and discussions, the exams are relatively easy. She always makes any opinions about the art pieces feel welcome so speaking in her class doesn't ever feel bad.

Very kind and always available for questions. Lectures hardly ever last the full 50 minutes and participation is usually only required for the discussion classes. Incredibly easy class as long as you do the readings and responses beforehand and pay attention to the lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Hannah is very easy going and chill. If your paper or if you are late it, is okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Caring

reviews.comment: Took her class in SAIC. She gave a lot of work EVERY week (1 museum assignment, 2 readings). Her lectures were really mid and there's TOO MUCH in class discussions. Tbh I don't care how other students view a piece. I also don't think she connects different events in art history nicely. Conclusion: mid lectures with lots of hw, should try to avoid.

4 exams; 1 per unit. 2 lectures and 1 discussion each week with 2 readings due whenever there's lecture. i recommend taking notes really useful for the exams. overall, she's really chill i recommend taking her class :]
2 lectures (participation not required) and 1 discussion (participation required) every week. Very easy homework and online exams. Very nice and chill teacher.
If you want to improve your writing take her class! She really took the time to work with me and she cares about her students.

Honestly don't take her, she's sweet at times and is passionate, but the course is a mess and not at all manageable when you have other classes that take priority. She gives so much work (2+ assignments a week), quizzes each week, and does not have solid due dates. The workload compared to other English 161 professors is just overwhelming.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Lots of hw there is something due everyday. Lots of writing in short time. Random quizzes every week. Extremely boring. Bring printouts of readings for extra credit. Also very unorganized and hard to find due dates.

One of the best professors I've had at UIC! Her class really inspired me to think of myself as a professional a writer. I was a hesitant writer going in, but I gained a lot of confidence after this class!

confusing assignments and projects
very boring and long projects
will not learn anything in class
a lot of work and projects
would never take class again
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Very unorganized and dont know whats going on in the class half the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: If you engage, it will be better for you. Interested in the subject of the class and attentive to all students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Many of the assignments had very broad directions, whether it was the topic to write about or the guidelines for what had to be included in the paper beyond the word count. I liked how everyone in my class was able to bond over the fact that we were all very confused and sometimes annoyed about how unstructured the course was.
Loved the professor! She knows her stuff. Would take her again if I could.

Many assignments were only brought up the night before or upon our arrival in class. She said that she didn't know about the due dates and advised us to check the syllabus. Rather than using Blackboard, she opted for a shared Google Docs folder for the entire class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is a great professor. She can guide you at all difficult points and make you understand the content. Go to her office during office hours or have Zoom meetings. Both are significant aspects of communication and aid. She is never tough on you.
She's an amazing professor, really easy going and cares a lot about her students and gives great feedback!

Professor Sibyl is very sweet and her class was pretty fun. She's very kind and down to earth and also can be funny, her grading is fair and the feed back she gives is very useful. I would love to take another one of her classes if I could fit it in my schedule one day.

Great professor! The material/ assignments are based on the concepts of gangster films and the global south. Her class can feel a bit disorganized at times but she does try her best to provide reminders for due dates. She's understanding and provides great feedback. If you pace the assignments and participate, the class is fun.
Great professor who is funny and works hard to engage the class in interesting discussions. She's caring and very accessible. Going to office hours really helped me.
She gets off topic a lot and doesn't fully explain writing assignments.

She is a great professor if you simply put in the time to read these readings she gives the papers are super easy. She gets off topic but that keeps the people engaged cause she's engaging with us rather than monotonously reading off the board. She works hard and always shows up so I think she deserves us to show up too.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Loved taking her course! Yes, she does get off topic, but is a really funny person. Going to office hours really helped me and her feedback is helpful on what to improve on. Definitely cares about her students.

Excellent professor! Her class really improved my writing and helped me better express my ideas. She is a caring professor and willing to go out of her way to help her students. She also uses a lot of photographs and film clips which I liked.
She gets very off topic and doesn't fully explain how assignments should be done but rather just tells you when it is due.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Sibyl is super caring and flexible. She's understanding with you missing class (just cares if your work gets done). Lots of group projects and probably daily homework, but it's mostly just assignments you didn't finish from class. The readings are difficult and she grades pretty hard. She rambles during her lectures and doesn't always make sense.

Great Intro to Rhetoric class. No textbook, the whole class was done through pdf's provided by the instructor, which was great. Readings were expected to be done prior to each class but nothing was too long. All in all a good course.

The class is pretty easy, but attendance matters and participation in group work and class discussions is key. There are mini projects. lot of case studies to read and talk about in class, but they're manageable. There is a coursepack you'll need to buy, but it's inexpensive. The main key to doing well is just staying engaged and participating.

class is easy, attendance matters, graded by participation with group and class discussions. There are a few mini projects but they're not hard. Lots of cases to read and discuss with class, but not difficult. There is a coursepack you have to buy but its cheap. key to doing good is participation!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Grades are based off two things: “contribution” and exams. Seems easy at first but he will not post or update any grade until the end of the semester when they are due leaving no time to access him for grade inquiries. The content itself is not hard to understand however, the lack of grade transparency ruins the entire class.

This professor is VERY lecture heavy with emphasis on group work. Case studies are going to be the number one thing you'll be doing in this class. He DOES NOT put anything into gradebook! I know that sounds really good, but it isn't he will be having you wait until the end of the semester to know where you stand.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Like any graduate level course, you'll receive the grade based upon the effort and time you put into the course. There are a few long case studies you'll have to read in the class, but they were very useful and insightful. I would really recommend this class!! Professor Gal is very understanding if you have to miss a class once in a while.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures were long and monotonous, and it was hard to grasp and retain content since the class was held virtually once a week for 3 hours. Professor didn't turn on his camera once the entire semester and would often interrupt students while they tried to contribute to class discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The best professor at UIC. His lectures in person are such a delight to attend. The fact that he can exemplify everything is such a rare quality in teachers these days. Take his class irrespective of your work/study background. Would rate him 5 stars any given day!

This is completely online and is an easy A. There are quizzes and discussion boards every week but other than that it is a very easy course. I would recommend completing most of the quizzes and discussions at once so you don't have to worry about the class as much during the semester.

*ASYNCHRONOUS* This class is generally easy. There's a weekly quiz due on Friday's but it's only 10 questions. There are 3 exams and they are also due on Friday's but the quiz is still due that day. Also some weeks there are practice tests and discussion posts along with the quiz, so it can seem like a lot of work. She does offer extra credit.

I actually took this professor for two diff classes and both times she was amazing! she sends out a weekly email everyday monday morning with list of things to do for the week and a reminder on friday again. really easy if you keep up with the work and she's extremely clear ab the requirements and what to expect.
This is an easy class to take for a gen ed requirement. There are quizzes and discussion boards due every week but other than that it's easily manageable.

Take the asynchronous class, extremely easy A. Most of the discussion responses are AI generated and I think she recognizes that and doesn't care (I personally put a little effort but I'm a 4.0 GPA student so idk). Weekly Modules that maybe take an hour to complete, 3 exams total and a concert report. Very light and easy credit for core gen eds.

It was an easy elective with straightforward grading criteria, such as online quizzes and discussion boards that she gave a lot of time to complete. Three exams and an 800-word essay about a concert that you attend in the same semester, at the end. Not much to say other than as long as you do the work, you'll be straight.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This class was a breeze to get through, and the professor seemed genuine. Each week's module only took me about 20 mins to complete or less. You also have to attend a live concert and write a brief paper about it. Overall, this class was super easy and enjoyable and would definitely recommend if you need the credit
Probably the best music teacher in UIC. Class was very easy, 1 quiz and 1 discussion every week, 3 online exams, and 1 concert report

I took MUS100 as an asynchronous online course. Dr. Gariazzo really knows her stuff, and her lectures are online modules & videos. There is homework every Friday - quizzes, discussions, & practice exams. Syllabus lists all exams & papers. Prior music knowledge helps, but as long as you stay on top of the modules, you will succeed in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Good Professor

The syllabus is clear, and the weekly assignments are not difficult. The exams are open notes and not too bad. You have to attend a concert during the semester and write about it but it wasn't too bad. Everything is always due on a Friday, but you can complete assignments ahead of time but if you procrastinate like me, it could pile up.
Easiest class I've taken. Just a quiz and discussion board every week and 2 projects. All online.

Class is easy, there's weekly quizzes and dbs which are simple. There's a couple big assignments like a concert report, one project, and 4 exams which the 4th one counts as the final. Her lectures are easy to follow and she includes videos which simply the material. Take if you need the credits

Dr. Gariazzo is a fantastic instructor. She truly cares about her students' success in class. The class is not difficult. You can finish the modules as quickly as you like or at your own pace. I did the latter. There are two papers, a midterm, and a final, but she gives you more than enough time to work on the papers. An awesome class!

The class is set up to be simple, however, the exams are worth 200 points, and you can easily lose points. Some questions are multiple answer, but I will say that the quizzes give you three attempts. It's easy to get an A, but it's also quite easy to get a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: There 3 mini quizzes every week and a discussion and two papers. Overall easy class and you learn a little of music.

The whole class was online and was so easy, she has her own website with all the information and would just have two 5 question quizzes due every Friday, but they were open book so it was so easy. I recommend her if you don't want an online class and need something easy but interesting.
MUS 100 is a great option if you need to fill a gen-ed requirement. Assignments and grading criteria were all very clear. The courseload is very manageable and she responds quickly through email.

This class was not hard at all. If you're looking for an easy gen-ed take this class. I would say she does do pop quizzes if the attendance is low, but they're pretty easy to do. It is literally impossible to get a bad grade in this class. All of the quizzes and exams are open note!!!

This is not a hard class if you know Spanish. She may not be the best professor in the way she expects students to participate, and she will make you feel dumb at times. Just try to learn her "correct" way of understanding the literature and rewrite it in the paper or exams, and you will earn a B or an A. Essentially, your opinion doesn't :/
This class is the reason I stopped looking both ways before crossing the street and on my way to class I hoped I'd get hit by a car just so I wouldn't have to go.

Her classes are really boring ngl but if you show up and say a few things then you'll be fine. She never updates blackboard and comes up with excuses like shes always busy. Just overthink the essays and you'll get an A. its graded on 1 oral presentation and 2 essays and an exam. shes not the worse but shes very far from the best.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: she spends more time talking over students than listening to their points.

Not an easy A. She expects a lot from you. Great for those academics who want to be challenged. She's extremely intelligent but has a hard time creating an inviting learning environment. Great on a one-on-one basis though. Grade based on attendance/participation, group presentation, 4 response papers, final paper, and 2 quizzes (lectures).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I can't stress enough that this is reading heavy class. It's very discussion based. There is no clear criteria when it comes to tests and papers. It's really just based on if she agrees with you or not. You're allowed to miss 3 days. 2 quizzes, 3 reaction papers, and 1 research paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Gajic was not a great professor. I felt like I was never improving in her class. She is a tough grader. She is extremely hard to impress. She wants you to participate in class and when you do, she is very rude about it. She is not great at explaining and she make students feel dumb. She is not a professor I recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

She makes you use critical thinking and has constructive criticism, which can come off a bit harsh sometimes. She could be better organized, but overall she cares about teaching and I learned a lot from her courses.

Good teacher if you really want to learn or are interested in the material. She assigns a lot of reading, which is good or bad depending on what you want out of the class. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class is unnecessarily difficult. She has poor communication skills, doesnt respect your answer during participation and makes it difficult to want to participate at all. reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Expected a lot from you and to know everything in general. She would have a syllabus, but really didn't follow it and would add way too much homework. Made you participate, but really never accepted your response. Overall judgmental and unorganized.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Really made us participate in class but shot down our answers every time. She didn't really seem enthusiastic about teaching, she just liked talking it seems. She was an ok professor, kind of boring. She is rather hard and expects us to know a lot. A lot of people in class were doing bad so she curved our grade a lot
Easy class, mostly memorizing tenses. I did not like her teaching strategies. She makes people participate, which made her annoying.
She is a very helpful teacher, clear at what she expects and organized. Come to class and participate and you will do fine!

.... the only thing i would say is perhaps try and respond to her students with a little more respect, it is understandable that she is a professor but sometimes the way she responds to her students is quite rude, other than that she is quite helpful.
She is hard, which challenges you too try harder. It helps you realize what you need to focus on as far as Spanish composition goes.
Pros: She's a moderately approachable prof, fair grader, and her classes are relatively well organized. Cons: She really needs to work on the way she responds to her students' opinions and questions.

Professor Riera is truly amazing. He's very funny, caring, and intelligent. He's very passionate and knowledgeable about what he teaches, which motivates you to learn more on your own. Personally, I love that he doesn't use PowerPoint and instead speaks directly to the students. His grading is fair, although the exams can be difficult.

Prof. Riera is so sweet and loves what he teaches. The only issue is that if you learn best by looking at Powerpoint slides, then I will not recommend this class. He also speaks very fast so listen to the recorded lectures if not you will be lost. The exams have 2-3 parts and require min 900 max 1000 words. too much for a minor course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: The best professor that the University of Illinois at Chicago has ever had, he really loves what he does!!!

He is a very intelligent and kind professor, though he does expect quite a lot from his students. The class was far more interesting than what I had expected, but at times he can be a bit unclear during lecture.
The most intelligent and profesional profesor i ever had, he cares about his students.
Riera is a great professor. He does expect a lot, but is very funny!!!

He is a very intelligent man...but can be unclear sometimes. Overall his class was interesting. He does expect a lot from you and I feel that sometimes he treats us like if we were graduate students. I admire his intelligence :-)Cute and funny too lol I do recommend him...

He is a very intelligent man...but can be unclear sometimes. Overall his class was interesting. He does expect a lot from you and I feel that sometimes he treats us like if we were graduate students. I admire his intelligence :-)Cute and funny too lol
Genuinely the best professor I've ever had by miles. Probably the best at UIC.

This is one of those classes you take and remember years later positively impacted your educational journey. The instructional method is extremely clear, resourceful and inclusive to all learning styles. The instructor does not impose a standard, rather they engage students meaningfully, even the challenging aspects are fairly curved.

This is one of those classes you take and remember years later positively impacted your educational journey. The instructional method is extremely clear, resourceful and inclusive to all learning styles. The instructor doesn't impose a standard, rather they engage students meaningfully, even the challenging aspects are extremely fair. GOATED

He is the best professor I have taken all 4 years as an engineering student. His lecture are very clear and entertaining, labs are optional but very helpful and serve as extra credit. Homework can be challenging but he offers resubmissions after posting the homework video solutions. Exams are difficult but course def prepares you for them.Take him!

Pretty good professor overall. Lectures give a lot of information but it can be hard to use that information in code as we don't go over full functions of implementation. Lectures are still very good. Interesting homework assignments as well.
Best professor to take 361

Professor Maratos is one of the best professors at UIC. He genuinely cares about his students, explains difficult concepts clearly, and always answers questions with patience and respect. The course is challenging but fair, well-structured, and centered on actual learning. He's a great professor and a truly good person. Highly recommend.

Really great Professor! Has the best explanations and teaching style! Homeworks and Labs are not that bad but study for Midterm and final! Attendance can be also taken at home via quizzes on gradescope!

Awesome professor. His lectures are easy to follow, he speaks very clearly and with a lot of passion. Loves answering questions and interacting with students. The labs were optional but definitely worth taking the time to do, plus you get extra credit if you do them. Generous grader but will still challenge you with the exams and hw. GOAT

Actually a goated king. Gives students every ounce of opportunity to get extra credit. If you forget that one function in a library he will give you a hint on the exam. Labs? Extra opportunity and a chance to get hints at how to do the homework. Goes in-depth about topics and doesn't just content dump.

Probably one of my favorite professors at UIC. I had heard that CS 361 was a tough class and although the concepts were not easy, Maratos made it very easy to succeed in the class. Attending labs were optional and for extra credit and if you got endorsed on piazza you would also get extra credit. He made 361 enjoyable and I learned a lot.

His lectures are very informative but can get boring sometimes, probably due to the nature of the material. One tip is BUY THE BOOK (vol 3, Bryant). Not required and hardly mentioned but a great learning tool (and great book in general) for this class and 261. Overall, he is the best possible prof for systems programming, really knows his stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Maratos will bend over backwards for his students to help them get a good grade in CS361. The class is very clear in what it expects from you, and he offers extensive extra credit on the homeworks, which are 50% of the grade. The only thing that could use improvement is the exam preperation, but I'm willing to forgive that considering all else
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Hands down one of the best professors I have come across. He is very approachable and loves to help out students. I had taken this course in Spring '24 and everything he covers in lecture is plenty to prepare you for the exams. He does make the lecture engaging by asking quite some questions.

I am taking the summer session wich is basically we being experimental rats. 

The class is 3 hours daily, 4 days a week and I still don't feel overwhelmed or bored.

Maratos knows how to keep your attention and how to explain things in a way that it's easy to understand. So far the experiment is going well.

The best professor I've had at UIC. Professor Maratos managed to make CS 361 a fairly easy course. All labs were extra credit but were the best resource for learning material and preparing for the projects which can be extremely difficult if not prepared for. He also gives a ton of supplementary material such as videos and practice exams.
This professor really pulled a Kendrick "Like that" on all the professors at UIC. Goated.

361 is apparently supposed to be the most difficult 300-level class for CS, however Professor Maratos did an excellent job make the material understandable. Although it was challenging at times, he really took the time to break it down and explain. Honestly hope he teaches more classes during my time at UIC.
I love this man. He deserves all the praise in the world. S/O big OG Maratos.
Was nervous to take CS 361 at the beginning of the semester but Maratos made this class not so scary and actually made me enjoy this class. Keep up the good work!

361 is not an easy class by any means but his lectures were very organized and informative. He taught tough concepts well and his idea of giving bonus points for being helpful on piazza actually made piazza an extremely useful resource throughout the semester.  If you have a class withe Maratos or McCarty at UIC you are lucky.

took kidane and felt like dropping out of cs but then I took maratos and remembered what a effective and genuine professor feels like. guy is amazing. no EC and kinda strict on curves but the way he teaches and structures the class you won't need it. Class is def hard but manageable because of him. legend is the dasgupta of 361
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Definitely a very tough class, but he makes it manageable with his hw policies. Sometimes he lectures can get boring or confusing but the fact that not all of them are like that is impressive enough when teaching a class like 361. He always answers questions during class. And for HWs he provides an intro video to help you get ready for the hw!!
THIS MF GOATED

The class itself is project (called homework) heavy, and they are hard but if you're willing to go to lab it alleviates a lot of the issues. His style, video formats, it really feels like he wants to make sure you get the best grade possible but the projects I wish were structured better.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best CS teacher at UIC.  This was supposed to be the hardest class you take in CS, and he made it so organized and simple that it wasn't bad at all. Yes, the content is hard but do everything early and you will pass just fine. He is a great guy and lenient when things come up in life. Wish all my professors were like him.

I wish he taught all of my CS classes. 

My favorite class at UIC.

Labs are set up to be extra credit added to the projects, and they also explicitly help with the skills needed for the projects which is amazing. Lecture attendance is mandatory, but there's an async option to get credit with an online quiz after the fact. He's clearly very excited about what he's teaching, and gives lots of help on piazza.

He is a professor who clearly cares about teaching the material well and it shows. His lectures are great and the workload of the class is very reasonable. There are a lot of opportunities for bonus points and resubmissions that allow for everyone in the class to do well if they put in the effort. I would 100% recommend taking this class with him.
Very good professor, amazing lectures which are optional, but I tend to enjoy them so I attended all anyways
Best professor not even close, Maratos clears. UIC is lucky they have him.
Good professor; however, gives very little partial credit on the exams.

Overall phenomenal professor I attended all my lectures because every single one was actually useful and informative. The labs were extra credit when I took the class. The labs help extensively with the projects that are assigned, so if you are to take this class I couldn't recommend more that you attend lab.

I think he is THE best CS professor at UIC. I was nervous in the beginning as I struggled badly with 261. But now I'm finishing up this course in a day and thinking if I should try 461 because Prof. Maratos made this course interactive and interesting. He 100% wants his students to succeed. Course schedule posted was followed from A to Z.

Everything was fine but the project announcements were delayed a few times(Though, he extended the deadline whenever that happened.) Answered questions on piazza even on weekends. But I think he should wear something else than the check shirts that automatically tell other that he is a computer scientist. That's the only thing I can complain about
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It was his first time teaching 141 but I have to say I really enjoyed his lectures. He explains coding in a way anyone can understand, using analogies that made the material accessible and engaging. He is very helpful during office hours and extremely patient, just don't expect him to directly give you the answer to your problem. Very encouraging.
Worst class ever. Don't expect him to grade your homework or answer your email

As Maratos's first time teaching, I think Maratos did pretty well! I took 141 with him, and I think that the projects where manageable, just start early and you will be fine. Also, try to think more of how to solve a problem instead of gunning straight for the coding solution. He is also very passionate, which made attending lectures fun.

Cs 141 is a workload but Maratos lecture slides are good and have example for labs and studying for the exams. Very patient when explain concepts/reviewing for exams in office hours and allowed for brain storming for projects in class. Don't expect him to give you answers to projects, instead ask how to approach bc hes genuine when trying to help.

He is a very good professor. Even though this was his first cs141 class, his lecture was very clear. Since cs is my minor and I am not really good at coding stuff. I often felt the pressure of the code. He would patiently answer my questions and give me good insight.
way too difficult and a very tough grader for a 100 class. the TA was really amazing and I learned much more from her than the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This professor was very lecture and grading heavy wasn't clear/ concise with the material. You also have to email your assignments. Which is very frustrating because you don't know when they'll be graded.
Tough to get through lectures. Grading criteria not always clear.
Very soft spoken, lectures were slow and kinda boring, hard to follow tbh
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I don't know why she's such a tough grader when it's not an upper level course and not a requirement for most majors. Like doesn't she know most of us just take her class for credit or as a requirement, she needs to chill on her grading criteria. It's a joke at this point, very subjective to HER point of view and makes no sense

If I could put "no grading criteria" and "how is this level 100 class this difficult," I would. other reviews are absurd. I had a great time with this professor, gave many examples when showing topics. You can tell she cares about what she's teaching. Just wish her class involved more discussion or interaction among other students.

This is the worst class I have taken so far, we were graded based on one paper and one exam. The paper was graded 2 months later, five days before the final. reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

She can't separate her own experiences from 50+ years ago and uses them to diminish valuable points you make, regarding the human rights issues of today. All of the feedback I got was ridiculous and when I made corrections as she said to, she then corrected those. Stay away!

Avoid this professor if you can. This class would have been so easy if not for her unnecessarily harsh and nitpicky feedback. Basically impossible to reach outside of class. Most of her feedback makes no sense and isn't clear AT ALL with what expectations for assignments are.

Very hard professor. She just expects you to know everything. Doesn't keep up with deadlines and rushes you to finish papers. Lets you pick topics but gets nitpicky if you pick the "wrong" topic. Her feedback is very confusing and she critiques your personal opinion and what/how she would write a paper that is 'opinionated' Avoid taking her!

super vague in the paper prompts but is really tough when grading, even though her expectations weren't clear. If you keep it simple, easy A. If you try to offer a different stance, automatic C. I cant tell if she's close-minded or just really dense, but shes not the best person to be teaching philosophy. She dislikes when ppl think outside the box
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: one paper and two tests. Professor Sinkler does not give quizzes. Lecture attendance is not mandatory, but it is better to attend for notes because she does not post materials on blackboard. Overall it was an easy A.

She was really quiet in lectures and wrote really small on the board. Lectures are so boring, but must pay attention since most of the test material comes from lectures. Really strict with grading. TA's weren't helpful at all.

Dislike. Whenever someone gave an opinion or questioned something she would always just say, "I don't know what you're getting at" every time. She was an extremely hard grader and *really* nit-picky on stuff like wording and would take tons of points off giving some extremely confusing explanation as to why.  Also textbook was the worst ever

I'm not sure why the last reviews were so harsh. I enjoyed the class even though the material wasn't my favorite. She has high expectations but it was a 400 level class and she seemed genuinely interested in helping students succeed. She is a great lecturer and you will leave the class having learned a lot of valuable information.

Take this class only if you belong to a certain "group." Take that as you will.. She doesn't explain what she wants you to write for ANY assignment. If you ask her to clarify anything, she'll just get mad and make up some BS. She's VERY opinionated and unwilling to consider opposing ideas, which is pathetic. I can't believe she is allowed to teach.

One of the worst professors in the philosophy department at UIC. She is unorganized and doesn't explain her grading system at all. It seems that there was no clear grading rubric for her essays and papers. Good luck asking her to explain why she grades the way she does; she'll just get defense and then mark you off even more on future assignments.

Ms. Sinkler is an easy teacher, she gives study guides before the test only had 2 exams, 1 paper, 1 Homework assignment. tons of readings, but you're not graded on them so you don't have to read all of them.... All in all easy A
Teaches the class as if she was teaching a kinder garden class. However, this class is an easy A.

This professor could be seen as boring or difficult, but if you are interested in the topic, take advantage of the fact that Prf Sinkler is brilliant and knowledgeable, if somewhat eccentric. Pay careful attention to lectures and don't be discouraged if she shoots down your ideas, she is a stickler for you clearly expressing your ideas.
BORING!!!!!! Stay away

Worst teacher ever.  Absolutely stay away from her.  She makes everything boring and dull and is the toughest grader even though the material is not too bad.  She is horrible and I would never ever take her again.  If you value your grades even the slightest bit, STAY AWAY FROM HER!!!

Yes, this class was quite boring. BUT its an easy A imo if you copy all her notes on the board. Easy paper topic. Easy exams and quizzes. Straightforward. Nothing against the teacher, but I won't be taking another philosophy class.

At first she looks like a nice old lady, harmless. BUT BEWARE- she is so DRY, and BORING, and so SUBJECTIVE, that she will shoot your ideas and opinions down, even though the class is about a subject like GOD. She is  mean, hard grader, and looks at you like you're stupid or something. I HAD TO DROP even though I LOVE PHILOSOPHY!!!!

Going into this class I was interested in learning about philosophy and took it for a gen ed. I'm not sure if I got anything out of it. I learned some facts but not anything really interesting. Must go to lecture for the notes, or just borrow someone else's. 2 exams and a couple quizzes in discussion-easy. One easy paper.

She's very funny. She does use some rather jaw-dropping examples though. One involving Arnold Schwarzenegger running in to the classroom, sticking a gun in her hand, and pulling the trigger on a student actually. Oh, and she referenced blowing up the Daley library. A large part of your grade in this class is participation in discussion. So TALK.

If you go to lecture and take notes, you will be fine. However, the key is to actually study those notes haha. The TA is the one who grades everything and he is a little harsh. Basically, this class should have been an easy A, and I ended up with a high B.

I think this teacher is extremely accomodating when it comes to office hours.  Although she doesn't believe in technology such as email or blackboard, she still makes herself accessible.  Listen to her lectures, copy what she writes on the board, and look over them once before the exam.  Not a lot of effort is needed in this class. 2 exams, 1 paper
A little stubborn, and acts like what you're saying doesn't make sense. Two tests and a paper, so easy stuff, but hard grader.

It would be almost impossible to find a teacher as boring as she is, and plus she gives these really messed up tests which almost no other philosophy teacher does.  Avoid her unless you like being bored.
OMG this class is so boring! The TA's also suck. Stay away from this class!
good professor, material is a little dry, but the class is interesting. it makes you think. if you cant think dont take the class, losers.

This professor seemed nice and enthusiastic however the enthusiam was lost on the class. She does not give out a syllabus which made it very difficult to prepare for test and papers.  The material is dry and class participation is not encouraged.  Work load was light 2 test & 1 paper

Ohh yeah the class is super easy, but it is the most boring class in the world. It is basically a waste of time, but if you can endure the mindless rambling, it is an easy class to fill your requirement
This is the most boring and waste of time class ever. I learn more from my foreigner TA with huge accent than from this perfect english speaking idiot. Definitely avoid
This professor discourages any expounding on the material by students. Because of her, I dropped my philosophy minor. Avoid her.
Great teacher. very easy to follow and clear.
No Comments
She was a challenging teacher, but awesome in her approach to the subject ... don't understand the complaints by the student above me... I got an A, and didn't even work all that hard!
You will not get an A in any of her courses. Turn in a five page paper and you'll get back seven pages of notes on what you did wrong.

He is extremely smart and knowledgeable. He has like 5 favorite kids in the class, and the rest of us are just there. Exams are really hard. No study guide, just PowerPoint presentations and concepts you have to know.
You don't need to pay for any textbooks, which is great. He's easy with attendance. 4 exams are not cumulative. Exams are pretty hard, though.

Prof Scully gives great lectures, and he makes the class very engaging. Participation is not mandatory, but it is encouraged. Attendance is not mandatory, but the course is very information-loaded, and if you miss the class, it is your loss. The grade is dependent on 4 exams, and there is no extra credit. His exams are tough, and all are MCQs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very good lecturer, uses lots of personal real life experiences to explain tough topics.

While many disagree with this, Scully is actually one of the best professors you can have in either ethics or law. He doesn't beat around the bush and makes sure you understand the subject to the best you can. Hard class, exams were the only grade per usual but best elective i've ever taken
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great lecturer, great professor. Class isn't too hard, grade based on only 3 tests with some small attendance penalty. You can take the last test, the AICPA exam, early and as soon as you have all tests completed, you can stop showing up, generally about 12 weeks in. Would highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Professor Scully is a great lecturer. He uses real-time examples that go along with what he is teaching. Very reachable outside of the classroom.
The material is difficult. There are four exams and one optional comprehensive final, the highest of the two will be your final grade. Expect to take very detailed notes & attend every lecture.
I don't like the way professor Scully lectures. But as long as you read the book and study you'll get A. The grade is based on the 3 exams

I love Scully for being passionate about what he teaches. I think people overlook his lectures. For ACTG 470, he makes you take AICPA for the final. He tells people to start on it months ahead because it is time consuming. It's not hard, just time consuming. Understand his notes, and you should be fine. He is slightly passive aggressive at times.

I have never encountered someone as hateful and have ZERO empathy for students. He will make a fool of you if you don't know the answer. His class only has exams, and they are all very hard. He will not respond to most emails because he does not feel like it. He has severe anger issues and yells at students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I hated the class because the preparation materials he provided were not much help and there's too many exams in this class. So here's a piece of advice, try and do as many application practice questions as possible because those are a significant portion of the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The material can be hard and you're graded only on exams (and a bit of attendance), but overall his lectures are great and engaging. Very fun and knowledgeable. No homework, so make sure you read the textbook to fully understand the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His exams are hard, specially the last one AICPA is very hard, I did not enjoy class that much. He is not that good professor, also doesnt provide material for exams. His exams are hard.

Read the book and pay attention in lecture. The first exam was pretty easy if you pay attention to the lecture but the second exam is challenging and confusing so make sure you study for it. The final is a guaranteed A but you will have to put the work in. You need to get a 90 to pass it. But there's no limit on attempts so you will pass eventually
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed having Scully as my professor, class met 3 times a week and at first he made people sign in in socrative to mark attendance but after a while he stopped caring. Class is graded by 3 exams and the exams are difficult.

Prof. Scully is great. He calls on people and uses them in scenarios, don't be afraid to speak up and give your opinion. Lectures are very entertaining and don't seem to be forced, so you learn a lot just by listening and paying attention. There are only 3 grades - 3 exams. READ THE BOOK!!! A lot of test questions are based on the book.

This guy is horrible highly don't recommend him. This class had no HW all based on exams. during lectures he has a very short temper, and he calls you out if no one participates. He treats the class like a law school level course. You have to read the book, come to class, and read the outlines to get a passing grade in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is the worst professor at UIC with boring classes, unpredictable temper, and inexplicable stubbornness. He can also be very disrespectful to some students. All in all, I lost my interest in accounting because of the professor's behavior. Run!

Honestly, I think he is one of the worst professors at UIC. He uses lectures that are 8 years old and does not care to do major updates to them. The tests are based on the book, not the lectures he gives. If you are willing to spend an hour after each class reading then take him. I stopped going to class and read the book and ended with a B

Straight forward class but not easy. You must read and understand the material to do well. graded on 4 tests, or an optional comprehensive final. highest of the 2 will be your course grade. Test questions are difficult if you did not spend a good amount of time studying the reading AND the examples. teacher is very interesting and animated.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ethics 470, in general, is an easy class. the readings are not long and very simple. Attendance was supposedly mandatory but after 3 weeks he stopped caring. Only 3 tests to determine your grade so give yourself time to study for the exams and you'll do well. He's also a really interesting professor (and NO he's not racist. from a black guy =).

Loved this professor and he was very engaging in lecture. Exams are a little tough and cover a few things that were only in the book. Really enjoyed the professor just wish the tests were a little bit more reflective of lectures sometimes because reading wasn't required and wasn't talked about much. Grade based on exams and attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Exams are not strictly correlated to lectures. The basic idea but can be hard to apply them on the exam. Great professor with many goods stories a lawyer and a judge. Very knowledgable

Prof. Scully was nice but the material was really hard for me. You'll definitely need to read the textbook. Make sure you know the chapter summaries for exams. I got an A but even when I felt ready for the exam I was nervous because the multiple choice answers confused me every time and made me question my initial answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Entire course grade is based on three exams. Each exam is worth 1/3 of your grade. If you miss more than 6 classes, he deducts 1% of your grade for every additional class missed. Exams are easy. Final exam is a guaranteed A, and it's online. He's very politically opinionated and will try to win you over to his way of thinking.

Scully is fantastic at taking a class like accounting ethics that can be less interesting and uses great examples to make it relatable and easy to get an A. He goes out of his way to bombard you with opportunities to get internships and jobs. Go to class participate and make sure he knows your name and you will be in for an easier ride.

He is a tough professor. You need to show up to class, read the book, and participate in discussions. There are only 4 tests and the final is online take-home exam. Make sure you read the book AND PowerPoints.

class is tough but you get the grade you deserve and the grade that reflects the effort you put in. Scully goes over and beyond to make sure the material is understood. He is one of the best professors at UIC.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: My advice is to go to the study groups and show interest in the subject and you will get an A without studying so hard. One of my classmates got a final B even though we had the same score ( I got an A, by the way). She studied hard but she didnt go to the office, study groups and etc. The class is 4 tests only. He is a good teacher.

good prof!!!
Very nice, young professor. his office hours are very  helpful, and he is always willing to help.
Gives hard exam, but curves it such that most people gets a B.  Nice teacher in general.  Great explanations.
Great professor, very helpful, but exams are hard

Picks and chooses his favorites. Rude professor. Has potential to be great. Your typical ego manic architecture professor where he likes tricking his students in order to learn. It's his way or no way.
In a weird way, he's a great professor.

Great professor, tough class

Karras is one of the coolest and best professors I ever had. I love this men. He is lenient with grading and he loves when you ask questions. I recommend him, if you want an A, do the homework and spend one or two hrs studying for the test and is completely possible.

I really enjoyed his class. He's best professor @ UIC.
