reviews.comment: Instead of using I-clickers, we used our computers to answer questions during lectures. No more power point lectures anymore, READ the topic in the textbook. There's a ton of homework and quizzes online. Try to get at least an "A" or a "B" in all of them. She has worksheets to help for the test and very approach if you have questions.

The course was difficult! Reading the book is a must if you want to get a good grade on the test. Exam 2 is the most difficult- all the others are OK. Going to lecture is also a must since points are given for learning catalytics. I highly recommend to go to class and do all hw assignments. Points for hw make a big difference at the end.

This class was not as easy as everyone below described it. Biology is my passion, but this class was very challenging. 4 exams with questions from mastering & learning catalytics. With effort, you can easily get a B.  I worked hard, but the style of the class is not easy for me. You use learning catalytics and studying must be done on ur own time.
Easy class as long as you go to class and pay attention.
In lecture everything seems really straight forward but on the tests the way she makes you apply it is really difficult. you must thoroughly study for the exams   any questions

She uses learning catalytics and as said before, you're expected to read before coming to class so that she can reinforce what you've learned. Exam 2 is HARD! The rest are okay, and it's possible to get an A if you work for it. I was taking KN 252 along with it, and I felt like I learned more in that class when learning the same material.

Professor Gibbons uses Learning Catalytics, you need to learn material independently and reinforce what you learned during class, there is no traditional lecture. If you keep up and take advantage of the class format, this class is not difficult. Mastering hw and postlectures are free points and the exams are fair. With effort, you should get an A.

She changed  course grading strategy, which now includes in-class participation and online homework. No traditional lecturing, but you can still use the powerpoints that she posts online. Exams were fair and easy, except Exam 2.  Make sure to review all homework and assignments questions before exams. Expect similar questions on exams. No curve!!

Professor Gibbons is great, exams consists of 50 multiple choice and lectures are not really lectures, but learning catalytics (like iClickers), 7-8 questions per day. You're expected to read before class and online HW is easy. Exams were straightforward, with no tricks or strings attached. I never did the guided readings and still got an A.

Use the book for guided reading assignment. Some people uses her slides but she doesn't lecture on them. The learning is outside of class and participation is in the class by using learning catalytics. Read the whole chapter and take notes because the tests uses questions from learning Catalytics and mastering. 4 tests. 2nd test is HARD. NO CURVE!

She changed the way she lectures. She prefers to do the learning outside of class by assigning guided readings for the book. Then there is participation in class by using learning Catalytics, sort like iclicker. The reading needs to be completed before learning Catalytics and mastering assignments. There is no curve. A 89.9 is a flat B+.

This prof has a knack for teaching and understands her students. Extra credit was given and a couple HW that really is there to boost your grade. Test were basically from the slides. Lectures were really well written and she explains everything so effectively while genuinely keeping  my interest.

If you're the type that reads the textbook before lecture with the expectation that the lecturer will expound on the intricacies of the material (because heshe expects that you've read the textbook before lecture), Gibbons is not foryou However, if you just want to be given powerpoints summarizing the textbook, take 100 with her. She's an easy A.

Sandra Gibbons is a great professor and lecturer. She explains the concepts very very clearly and is good at explaining the material in the class. She practically spoon feeds you the material. If you do bad in this class, then you either didn't try or should change your major.
Professor Gibbons simplifies complex biological concepts and basically what she teaches in lectures are on the exams, which are super easy if you go to class, do the homework, and read the textbook.

She basically dumbed-down the material so even an elementary school kid could understand it, which was helpful even though the material wasn't difficult. Her multiple choice test questions are easy and straight-forward.  It's definitely possible to get an A in this class with all the homework and extra credit assignments.
make sure you go to lecture. her tests are easier than malchow's. if you want clear and concise. she does use iclicker in every class, so attendance is mandatory. study from past exams.

Have to do a joke of service project. She is a very good teacher, but erroneously adds clicker points at the end so make sure you show up or have a friend in the class to rack them up. Tests are basically off the slides and make sure you are prepared for ALL the short answer questions provided. A lot of A's were blown because of short answer.

The class was overall very interesting. She gave excellent lectures which were essential to understanding the material. Most of the exam questions came right from her slides. Make sure you study what she writes on them. The only bad thing about this class is the strict grading scale. 90-100 A 80-89 B etc... So make sure you aren't borderline.

Gibbons was a great professor. She explained everything well and repeated things several times if they were important. She is nice, helpful during office hours, and just a great professor in general. She has definitely increased my interest in the topic.

For those that don't go to lecture you better take her afternoon class because if you take her morning class and not more than half the class shows up she won't put up a lecture capture of the materials you missed. For homework, read the powerpoint then answer question and you'll get most of it right. For exams read the other post here.

Amazing professor.She records her lectures so if you miss it you can basically watch and listen to it from home. Her tests are based off the lecture notes which are based off the book and she gives you the essay questions that are going to be on the tests beforehand so its not that hard to study for it. She also gives extra credit. TAKE HER!!!!

Awesome professor! The exams can be a bit challenging but it is a 300 level class. Really easy to get a B in this class and you have to work a bit harder for an A. Homework is very easy and helps boost up your grade. She's sweet, helpful, and makes the course very interesting. Highly recommended course for bio majors.

Professor Gibbons is awesome. She made me appreciate more about the health care field and biology. There is a lot of materials.. listen to her lectures! and book for specific details. Come to her office hours if you have "Any Questions!" haha. She is so helpful and so expert at the subject :)

I recommend not buying the book b/c there's an online book. Write down everything she says, attend class, and do challenge questions ahead of time. She's nice and helpful during office hours and after class. Interesting class, I gained a sense of appreciation for biology through this class.

Exceptional. She really wants to help her students succeed. It seems like she gets angry if you don't ask her for help. But the tests aren't bad. Most ?'s came from the online HW. She gives you the short answer questions beforehand. Her HW is also easy, but time consuming. Downside is that she talks a little fast. Overall, take her.

this is an interesting class but not an easy A. you do have to either go to lecture or watch lecture captures. homework is easy. exams were somewhat difficult but the essay portion is pretty much given to you ahead of time, you just have to memorize the answers. shes REALLLy helpful if you go to office hours. textbook is just there for help.

Interesting class. Not boring and one of the best Bios classes at UIC. HW is easy. Service learning units easy. Scientific American is easy but time consuming. EXAMS are what determine your grade. Written portion is freebie. Multiple Choice is tough, but NOT TRICKY. TAKE HER CLASS IF YOU CAN. You won't regret it.

Book is not needed for this class, a lot of homework but is easy to do...overall class was interesting and i learned a lot from  her. Nonetheless her teaching was superb!! I wish she taught different type of classes.

Don't listen to anyone who says this class was hard! They are clearly not the sharpest crayons in the box. I skipped every lecture. All you need to do is watch lecture capture and note what she writes in RED on her slides. This is very important! The questions on her exams refer directly to these RED markings. Do all assignments. Easy A.

This class was VERY interesting! There are three exams which are no bad if you studied hard. She gives a good amount of extra credit and the masteringmicrobiology points make a difference. You learn a lot in this class and its worth taking. I got an A! :) Lecture capture was helpful because she is a fast speaker.

she talks really fast so i suggest using lecture capture & really understanding everything b/c the tests are really hard. homework is easy except aren't really worth much. shes a nice lady i just think her class is really difficult due to the fact that her exams are really tricky and you REALLY have to know your material and it is a lot of material

Very straightforward class. I didn't end up using the book at all. If you're going to ditch class, watch the lecture capture. If you only go off the slides you will be in trouble. Online homework is easy and comes word for word from the book. Tests can be tricky. Overall one of the easier biology classes I have taken at UIC.
very nice lady! cool class learned a lot of interesting things. definitely a must take

She is a very good professor. To get an A or B in the class, go to lecture, listen to lecture capture, do the questions of the day, and do the homework (obviously). The exams are based off of what she says in lecture so don't waste your time reading the textbook. The book is only useful when it comes to doing  the online homework.

Lots of extra credit, so don't worry too much.  As long as do all assignments, and get high B's on exams, will get an A in class.  Go to her office hours- very helpful for exam hints etc. Turn in assignment to BB early bc if there's a glitch, too bad so sad. Memorize slides, especially the stuff she says in lecture. Don't need to read book.
Amazing teacher. Study the slides and you will be fine. There are homework assignments but they're not bad and masteringmicrobio doesn't count for much in the end anyway.
Great teacher! A lot of homework, a lot of extra credit. If you do everything one time and attend classes you should be fine. You mostly need to study notes from class.

Good teacher. Unnecessary homework, but it is easy. Exams are tricky memorize the slides and attend class and watch it again. Do all the questions of the day. Never used the book except for homework. Get all the extra credit. She will not bump you up even if you are .1 point off from the next grade.

She's a pretty good professor. She restructured her class and it's awful, with pointless online homework that's due before you ever cover the material. As a teacher though, she's fairly knowledgeable, a very nice lady, and a pretty competent teacher. I hated the class, especially with the ridiculous grading now, but I do like her. Good lady.
She very very good. Very helpful and friendly. Makes sure we understand befor moving on and encourages questions. Super easy to get  B if you want an A, you'll have to be in time.

She is one of the best professors i've had at UIC. She is really great at explaining what you need to know and is open to answering all questions. Her exams required a lot of studying and some oustide work is required for homework. It is not a blow off class at all, but it is a very interesting class.

Probably the best professor I've ever had at UIC. She really cares about her students and their understanding of the material. Because she explains everything so well, exams aren't horrible. You must study, but she has a list of things to know for each unit (objectives).There are online quizzes and articles you answer questions on, but they're easy

workload for the class wasn't bad. tests were difficult, you have to really know the concepts well. tests were not cummulative and there was no final. come in to office hours because she is more than happy to help.

From the first class she said to STUDY THE DETAILS and yes, she requires a lot of details on the exams but the slides she posts on blackboard are very helpful. I would recomment to record her in class and listen to the lectures later to do detailed notes( there is no way to write she says in class). $ online quizes and book club assignments.

She is a great prof and is extremely helpful. Just because she has great ratings does not mean she will go easy on the exams. They were difficult and requires lots of time to study. Do not take this class as a blow off class. If you go in for help, she is willing to help at any cost. Homework for this class was great and easy full credit.

An A is easy if you study for the first few exams. Exams are mostly based off the slides. Nonetheless, she did make exams increasingly difficult, because more people were getting As in the class than she could allow. Homework was bogus (most students I talked to thought so), and it's as if you're not allowed to get full credit.

Super hard! The material is very difficult to understand already,still her exams questions are often misleading.  She does give extra credit points though.  Also, she's very helpful when you stop by her office hours. BUT STILL--study a week before the exam if you're not keeping up with the material, read the book and DO read her questions carefully

She is a superb lecturer but the class is harddddd you have to keep up. Go to class and take excellent notes, record lectures if u can and reading the book also helps for clearification. She goes really fast and always behind on the schedule. also every figure in lectures is important, know them in &out.

Go to class, write down everything she says on the printed lecture slides, and fill out the objectives asap. This will all show up on the exam. You don't need the big textbook, but you do need the story book for hw. She's a nice lady and very understanding. She will help you understand certain concepts if you don't. 310 points in the class with e/c

I love her!!! she is THE best professor at UIC! feels good to have a professor who is so sweet and caring and loves to explain and have students understand!! but you have to attend all lectures because most of the test is from what she says in lecture and not in the book or powerpoints but who cares..she is AWESOME!

If you have had cell biology, the class will be so easy.  If you haven't, this class I hear can be hard.  Don't buy text book because all exam problems are from lecture slides.  You however need to borrow it for doing 5 online assignments, which took me about 6 hours.  The exams are straightforward DIRECTLY from lecture slides. Attendance is a must

She's an awesome professor. You should go to class because she explains EVERYTHING in her lectures-which is good because the book is BORING. The tests are hard but its a 300 level class so should be expected. She also gives extra credit to help your grade. She's the best bio professor I've ever had!

Its a 300 level class so be prepared. No final, just 5 tests  and hmwk. You need the book to do tutorials, but otherwise her slides contain everything you need to study for. This class is very hard especially since Biology isn't my strong point! IF it wasn't for the homework and tutorials, I wouldn't have passed.

She is a great instructor and always eager to explain things, and class is also great. The thing with that class is that is not curved but there's no cumulative exam which is good since it's a lot of material.

Interesting class, but if you screw up in the beginning your messed up for the whole semester. Shes a cool teacher, everything on the test is on the slide lectures. But sometimes she puts whack questions that aren't on the slides so yea watch out for that.

She's nice and helpful with most of the material. Her powerpoint slides contain most of the material on the tests. But the tests are near impossible to getting an A, but its a 300 level class so be prepared. Don't expect to enjoy the class if Biology is not your strong point. No final but there are 5 exams and hmwk is easy but the grading is tough.

She is one of the nicest teachers I have had at UIC.  She really cares about the students and has a true interest in whether or not the students are learning the material.  I wouldn't say it's a must to attend her lectures since she puts everything online, but it's definitely a plus.  She makes the material interesting and explains in more detail.
very nice

i liked her lectures very much. made the material VERY interesting! her exams are tough but it's a 300 level course so expect it to get hard. Know every detail, go to office hours for help, show interest, and enjoy the course and you should be fine. You do have to expect to put a lot of time into it though.

Does not care how her class is doing.  She claims curves are rewards for bad grades, what the hell! The people taking this class are not just in it to slack off.  When everyone fails the first two tests SOMETHING IS WRONG WITH YOU.  I have NEVER studied so hard in my life!  You have to memorize the tinest details to do well on her tests!

She's a great teacher, very clear and powerpoints notes are very helpful. She almost never finishes the material and tests you, but she helps out by posting notes online before the test. Easy if you go to class and study.

good professor, but I HATED HER PERSONALITY! Never go to her for anything but learning the material. I got dropped from the class, and althought it was the school's mistake, I never got credit for the class even though I took almost all of the exams. She was of absolutely NO help. She's not like other caring UIC professors

Even though the professor is very nice, and is willing to offer a great deal of help, do not take the class during the summer. You only have 3 exams, and you can lose your chance to get an A as of the first exam. Exams are very detailed, and you have to memorize all of the minute details, so study ahead of time!!! Answer all of the objectives too!!
Not the best teacher

She's very clear on what you're suppose to know for the exam.  She gives out a TON of extra credit points.  The papers are easy A's that boost up your grade.  The exams are straight out of the lecture slides (kind of a lot) but it's so do-able.  She's nice and easy going.
I had this class at 8:00 am so I almost never attended the lectures. For the tests I read the slides and went over her review sheets and a got a B in the class. In my opinion this is an easy class.

Her test averages were below 60% for the first two exams and the Final. I would NEVER take her again or the other teacher at UIC. They both never finish the lecture material, but test you on it anyways. There is not enough homework assigned to help make up for subpar test performance. How can you have half your class fail the first two tests?

extremely nice lady who helps you out, just come to her office hours or if youre afraid, you can post a question online. her test is pure memorization for 35 questions and the other 15 questions are critical thinking. take her instead of witmer, since she gives extra credit and her lectures are far more interesting ;)

She's the best prof. I've had. She made me feel really comfortable and was ALWAYS willing to help out. I stress that you get help and ask q's. There is a LOT of material, but keep up with it, and you will do fine. Make sure you study the lecture notes and her study guide/questions.  Those are really helpful.

i was actually scared of this class, the material isn't as hard if you go to lecture and go for help! she is one of the nicest professor that will actually HELP YOU if you just come and ask. very easy going and nice personality. as for the class material, it is tough but as long as you stay on top of things... easy class.

I took this class last spring.  It is very easy to get a B in her class.  She gives extra credit, and she also gives e.c. if only a certain number (6) of cell phone calls go off during the semester.  The material and the way she teaches is very straight foward and simple.

Very helpful, provided as much help to anyone who asked for it.  Was not even close to as difficult as people say.  Studying was necessary, but other than she made every attempt to help the students do well in the class

Tough to get an A. 250 points total/ 5*50 point mc exams. You'll end up with 8-10 bonus points at the end of the year.  The grading scale is not curved(90A,80B,70C).  Lectures aren't essential to go to unless you pay really good attention.  The book is a good way to figure out the lecture slides. Do not take this during summer!only fall and spring
Worst professor at UIC I have had experience with

Tough class, though if you read the textbook, you ace the class. 100% average on 10 HW Assignments = 50% of grade. 15% Midterm which got a B, but got A on the Final. He also curves big. 60% basically an A. Ignore the other reviews, but you got work hard in the class. It's AI. It's difficult. Textbook heavy though--buy the book. Enjoyed this class.

A coding assignment every week. Exams are based on what the prof teaches in classes (not recorded) and involve rote learning algorithms and definitions. Like it's an alright AI intro course made necessarily harder due to logistics. A project or some conceptual challenges would've been better. Great curve but there are far easier ways to get an A.

Terrible professor, lectures are him just rambling on about slides that are not really important to what he will test you on, do not take this course you will not learn anything from him. Just read the book, do the homework assignments and pray you do okay on the exams, he will curve the course so much because no one really knows what is going on.

No care about the success of students in this class. No lecture recordings, no slides, rarely any announcements, and no physical OH. During lectures, he only cares about making himself understand what he is saying, so there's nothing valuable to gain. He also refuses to listen to students' POV, only wanting to protect his flawed point.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: A prime example of who shouldn't be a lecturer. Lectures are incomprehensible, with no recordings. He only teaches for himself to understand instead of explaining clearly so that students understand him. Exams are okay if you take notes, but he grades extremely harshly. He only cares about defending his point instead of helping students during OH.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He might be a bit inscrutable in his teaching style, but you will understand it while reading the book. Yes, get ready to read the book and TAKE NOTES. He expects you to read chapter before the lecture, but he jumps between chapters making it difficult to predict what will come next. Exams are moderately tough with 1 or 2 really tough questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He was late to class almost half of the days. Get ready to be destroyed in exams. Curve is insane. Be ready for loads of homework. Getting an A is very easy in this class. Just do the assignments and attempt all of the questions in the exams and you'll be fine. Classes are boring. Book is huge. Don't recommend this professor if you want to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Course had alot of Assignments (Theory and/or Coding). The Coding assignments are hard implementations of abstract algorithms from the Text Book (so start early). Lectures arent recorded. Prof does give pointers to what questions/algorithms will be asked in the midterm and finals in classes so attendance is highly recommended.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Nothing good to say about him. He is always late, no study guides for midterms, does not record lectures for students to review later, no clear directions of what to do on the assignments and what to expect on the final. Overall, just a bad professor that just doesn't put in effort to make sure his students succeed.

In my experience taking CS411,

The professor gives hints on what will be on the exam during class but be prepared to be humbled in the exams. They were completely out of my league.

There's an extremely large curve so just get the homeworks done and you'll be fine. There's an autograder to test your algorithms.

The professor has a very strong understanding of the subject and teaches it very well. The assignments can be a bit challenging but very manageable. Note: CS 411 by Prof. Piotr Gmytrasiewicz is a difficult 400 series course. But it is a very important course if you want to learn the basics of AI.

The workload is okay, but the online lectures are not worth going to, as the professor just reads and shows stuff right out of the textbook and he also doesn't require any form of participation by the students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor was not bad, but the course material is very dated to the point where students with new laptops had to install virtual machines to access older versions of software. Would like to see a better balance between explaining concepts and modern implementation so students can more freely advertise their new found "applied" skills.

Overall, I would consider this professor ineffective in his teaching methods and course, as well as, inconsiderate of his students. I would NOT take a course with this professor again, and would recommend any other professor over Gmytrasiewicz. Note: His teaching method consists of reading the textbook word for word.
Low grade
Good class
Simple course with 5 projects which are peer graded and a final exam
The only good aspect about his classes is that he curves like a mad man.

Always late to class (5-15 min), but if you're more than 5 minutes late to turn in your homework at the beginning of class, you get deducted. His lectures we very confusing and did NOT help me understand the material. Was interested in AI, but won't take it from him.

Uselessboring lectures. Teaches concepts by reading off a pdf.  Lack intuition of material and therefore have poor portrayal of examples. Rely heavily on self-learning from  the book to pass. Grading scale: 50% HW, 10% Midterm, 40% Final. Homeworks  look at book example, now do the problems. Finals reflected extremely poorly on class material.

I had him in AI I during the Fall 2012 semester. He would show up to class maybe only half of the semester and leave the other classes to be taught by a doctoral student, Alexandro. Alexandro really knew his stuff though. Read the chapters he assigns and try to memorize how all of the algorithms he presents work in general. Crazy curve at the end.

I like him. His style of teaching is really good. He can put most complex stuff clear. I could not afford to miss his classes else I will be lost. Exams are tough(very tricky). Ah he will be late to the class. But really smart and funny. One of my favs.

Always ~6 minutes late.  Used slides from previous edition of book for lectures, seemingly picking at random which topics to discuss in depth, without regard to bigger picture or course goals.  For tests you need to know which topics covered in lectures, but you're better off learning them from the book than lectures.
Too bad he is always late explanations are incomprehensible projects are terrible not clear final contents
This professor is always late and I feel that is taking my time and money

I have to say that I was very interested in artificial intelligence prior to attending the class.  Now I sure don't want anything to do with it.  Prof. Piotr G. is funny and makes the class go by quick. Although I didn't like the class and had a hard time with it I managed to pass with a C.  His CURVE IS HUGE. I would take another class with him.
He can make the subject matter interesting, but when asked more detailed questions, often does not know the answer. His tests are difficult. Expect weekly homework.
The class was extremely hard for me but the curve in the class was hugeee..I went from about 38% to a C thanks to it. If you stay on top of your stuff though I think you can do good in the class.
his class is impossible to sit through and the TA's are horrible

This class was a lot of fun. We had the intelligent agents olympic games, only in the end we don't know who won. A lot of assignments, but doable. Grading in the end was good. If you want to take this class, do it with him.

Artificial Intelligence II. Piotr is extremely knowledgeable, but he sometimes has difficulty teaching. He's usually late to class. He gives little input to your performance via grades. He throws lectures together on the fly, sometimes it works sometimes it doesn't Very entertaining and vibrant, you won't fall asleep.
You will not fall asleep in these lectures!  The programming assignments were fun.

There's a huge curve in the end, and while he knows his stuff, if the topic at hand has nothing to do with AI, you can forget him really caring. He sort of just lectures from the book and answers questions with things like "just because it is". He is very nice though, and funny, and smart. I'd take him for an AI class, but not really anything else.

CS 107 with Piotr is fairly difficult. His lectures are useless so you just need to come for the exams. The projects are too difficult (except the last one) if you have some previous experiance with writing programs. I know that the students with no programming experiance had a really hard time in the class. The TA(Matt) is really helpful.

This professor is incredibly understanding, accommodating, and friendly. They take the time to explain concepts thoroughly and are always open to discussions. Lectures are concise and helpful, leaving plenty of class time to work on assignments. Attending class and participating is the key

Professor Goldbach is amazing! He really makes you feel comfortable sharing your ideas in class, and he makes his course extremely flexible for you. He lets you write about topics you are interested in, and overall, it's not a class you should worry about.

This instructor is amazing and makes the class enjoyable. The course is not heavy and is an easy A if you stay on track. Writing projects are clearly explained in the syllabus and are manageable. Attendance is required, but some absences are allowed. Due dates are flexible, and there is not a lot of homework besides major writing projects.
had so many nice conversations outside of class. top tier professor who will help you develop critical thinking, very kind and understanding.

He's is a great professor who genuinely wants to see his students succeed. He's really clear with his expectations in class and is very flexible with students. The course itself is a typical english course but he still manages to engage with students and allow them to feel comfortable sharing their ideas in class. He also provides useful feedback.

I took his 160 class and it's so fun. He gives us so much time to work on our projects but he makes sure we are all caught up. If I could take him every semester I would. As long as you do your work, you get an easy A!

Professor John is a really helpful person. I had him for English 160. You have 4 writing projects, he doesn't grade the drafts, and gives you good feedback before the final draft is due. There is no final for this class; he wants everyone to do well

I loved this class, the professor is very open-minded, so you are able to speak your mind as he creates a safe space for everyone. We talk about real-world issues in the context of the subject, which makes it a lot more interactive and appealing to learn.
John Goldbach is kind and genuine and wants everyone to succeed. Has pushed back project dates to give everyone ample time to complete projects. Cool and chill guy, take his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Only keeps you in class if you need to be there which is nice. Easy to attend office hours. Helps workshop ideas well and gives good feedback. You do have to show up to know when things are due but if you fall behind he's willing to work with you
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is very laid back and his class was fun. Gives good feedback on papers and wants you to succeed. Not much homework besides a couple of readings and articles.
Very good professor the class was good

He's very interesting, layed back and a great person in general! Though sometimes class can be a bit dragging as long as you do the work it's very very easy. He gives great instructions and feedback too, very helpful!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Goldbach was super kind and made the class fun to come back and collaborate with. Not a tough grader but he makes sure you understand the material and how to become a better writer through his workshop class. Made me feel welcome as an incoming uic student and would love to have another conversation with professor Goldbach!

Professor Goldbach is an amazing person; his lectures were very understandable and easily accessible to students if they want to go back to them. Really cares about his students and ensures that everyone is doing well. Gives clear feedback, is easily approachable and understanding of everyone's situations. Very flexible and will give extensions.

Mr. Goldbach is amazing. I highly recommend taking his class. He is super understanding and very lenient when it comes to due dates. He is also very helpful when it comes writing essays and discussing topic ideas. He is very flexible and you will not regret taking his class.

John is such a nice guy and really cares for his students. He wants to make sure everyone understands the material without confusion, and always lets his students speak their minds. He picks great stories to read and is up for recommendations if students have a preference.

The sweetest most nicest professor, genuinely wants his students to succeed, very easy grader. Easy A class, there's a few discussion posts and group project (which he grades very easily on). Lectures can be long and boring, but can be interesting. Attendance counts, but because of the easy assignments you can afford to miss a few. TAKE HIS CLASS!

This class made me take a step back and really think deeply about things. He is a really sweet professor that cares for his students. The lectures are sometimes interesting with informative articles that discuss culture all the way back from ancient ages. There is a group presentation and a short reflection at the end of the semester.
As everyone else says, maybe easiest A in biology! You read papers and talk about them. Not a bad class, but I also didnt feel like I learned a lot.

Easy A for an easy class. Seems to give A's to almost everyone? Nice guy! The lectures felt a little disorganized. I think he knows his stuff, but it would be good if hours per week showed up more in me learning new and harder things. There are regular questions about readings and a final group project. Overall, pretty OK.

This professor is hands down theeee best prof you can take at UIC. Not only is he super fair in his grading, but he also replies to emails quick, and will ensure that u finish the class with an A as long as u do the work and attend lectures. IF UR CONSIDERING TAKING THIS CLASS, THIS IS UR SIGN TO DO IT AND GET THAT A. HES AN AMAZING PROF!!

literally the most precious and understanding professor. Easily my favorite class and he is so sweet. He is genuinely interested in the work he is teaching, you could tell he is passionate. No final. Presentation at end worth 60% of grade.

Environmental Change and Human Culture was a great class run by Prof Meler. He gave us some weeks off to do async work and you just had to do discussion posts every week. The lectures are interesting and the group presentations are fun. The content was really interesting and I'm glad I took this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Took him for topics in tropical ecology. Honestly an easy class if you find the subject interesting. Expect to read articles and write discussions/talk about them. Super smart prof, makes connections you never knew were possible and makes you want to be an ecologist full time!

If you have any prior knowledge of higher level biology, the course is quite easy, almost at times a bit dull. He is knowledgeable about his field and has thought provoking ideas, but it felt hard to stay engaged in his lectures. Coursework is centered mainly around discussion board questions about readings, as well as a final group project.

Manages to make science relate to real social structures in an engaging way. You learn by going through packets with your table, with more writing you'll ever do in any science class. Even though he's got a great sense of humor, he does tend to go on tangents and from there my mind tends to blank. The final project was fun as well. Very distinct.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Great professor, very chill. The content was very dry (for me, at least). If you enjoy environmental science and the like, then this class is for you. There was no exam, but a final group project, and weekly reflections. If you show up to class and do the work, you should be fine.
He made me think. Connecting influences of environment on human culture was not something I thought about before.
Great class. would take again

Great professor, really cares about his students. He makes the subject easy for you if you go to his office hours. There can be some language issues on the test since his portion is usually free response type, so make sure you ask him if you understood the question correctly. Be ready for complex thinking for his part of the exam.
best teacher at UIC I ever had. with his help went from a C to an A

Professor Meler is extremely knowledgeable on the subject he teaches. He also sends out some exercises from the next test on the email 2 days before the test. However, his tests are the hardest I have ever taken. Nothing straight from readings or anything, you have to  critically analyzed the question to then answer. average on his tests is 50% .

Great guy, really intrested in the material, no quizes or tests, just one presentation and a short weekly writing assignment.  If you go to class and have him review your presentation before you give it he will give you an A. Best prof at UIC thus far.

Don't waste money buying textbook.  You won't even have time to read it.  Instead visit his office hours (and Malchow's) daily.  Refresh concepts and clarify things that were touched on in lecture. Gonzalez-Meler is super funny and nice and willing to help anybody out.  Brilliant guy and knows his stuff.  Class act all the way.

Extremely nice professor.  Will help students out as much as he can.  Go to his office hours and introduce yourself to him.  He's very good with names so he'll remember you.  He will explain concepts pretty thoroughly and will test you on general concepts rather than minute details about things.  Still, he forces you to think on exams.

Gonzalez-Meler is one of the nicest professors at UIC. He met with me on multiple occasions to help me understand the material. If you are struggling, talk to him! He is VERY willing to help. His powerpoints are very wordy. A lot of the information is not necessary. Ask him what is important and he will tell you. Really cares about his students!

The plant portion that he teaches is hard, probably because most people are used to learning about animal cells,behavior,etc. You REALLY need to study. Go see him during office hours though!He is a good lecturer and helps you understand the material well! Exam questions are tricky at times(especially his essay questions), but there is a huge curve.

Don't buy the book for this class. His powerpoints are really good & does a good job teaching his portion of the class. Sadly, his part of class is not very interesting, but he does a great job still because he keeps us paying attention by saying jokes. His test questions are REALLY hard! Make sure you know charts and graphs. Nice when approached.
No quizzes or exams. Participation is a huge part, though, so show up to class and say something. Just one final project(15min presentation). Overall, easy and cool guy.

Professor Meller teaches the plant portion of BIOS 240. This is by far the least interesting section. He keeps the class interesting with funny stories. The material, however, is difficult to study if you have no interest in plants. He is very approachable, and has a spanish lisp, so relatively clear. Also, curves at the end. Like most bio at uic
Topics and exams are not easy, but he adjusts for that at the end with curved grades. He cares about making connections and integrating and is a painful process byt very rewarding at the end.
Miguel is my guy! Without him bios 240 would suck... unlike other professors at UIC he wants  to help his students do well in the course. A quality that very few science professors here have....
Best professor ever!!!! he is very nice and chill take him for HONORS 134!!
He explains the material very well and has good powerpoints. His exams are tough and he does not speak particulary loud.

Don't buy the book, never had to use it. He seems to know what he is talking about but you have to listen intently to try to understand what the main point is. Lectures are not very coherent so watching lecture captures often helps. His tests are pretty hard even though you may understand the topics. One good thing is that there is a huge curve.

He explains things very very well. The key to doing well in his class is to listen very carefully to his explanations and always ask questions. Use a recorder if the lectures aren't video captured. He is very conceptual on the exams. He expects you to think deeply and make connections. Not easy, but rewarding.

Class is NOT as hard as you think.  The teacher is Very Very Very Helpful, at the first of the semester he tells you that you do not need to buy a text book.  Very TRUE, you do not need it.  If you go to his office hours he will be more than happy to assist in helping you. And he is very good at explaining it.

this class is not as bad as everyone seems to think. the material seems challenging at times and can be a load, but if you just put in the effort to go to class, ask questions, study on your own time, the exams are very fair. the professors give you 25% of your test to do at home and they curve very well so your grades are better than you think.

A little hard to understand the material, but EXTREMELY helpful at office hours. All I had to do was ask and I went from failing to a B. If he sees that you understand the material and can explain it to him, you should be fine. Don't be afraid to ask him for help! No books/hw/quizzes so be sure to go to office hours and be prepared to STUDY HARD!
he gives good guidance if you ask for it. the material is hard, but makes it accessible
excellent overall

The class itself is hard...but the majority of your grade depends on the final exam- youll pretty much get that grade in the class.  Before the final I was worried about passing...but somehow I managed to get a B.  The notes are all powerpoints, and are generally easy to follow.  Overall, not that bad looking back on the semester.
very confusing and hard to follow.

Talks too fast and not clear at all.  All the lecture notes are powerpoint pictures so you need to take good notes.  How can you take good notes when you don't even understand him!  It's a hard class, but if you study it's possible to survive.
Not very clear - has a very weird american-spanish accent - funny - helful - average tests - all notes are online - class curved in the end

Many professors lack the ability to teach but professor Goncharoff is an expert at teaching. His lectures are very informative and cares about his students and their careers. Homework's are simple as they reflect the lecture material. Exams are fair since they're from the quiz questions. Projects are fun but get a good group since that helps a lot.

He's been teaching the class for decades and it shows. Everything is well planned and explained clearly. Labs were surprisingly fun for me but a lot of people took a long time on them if they didn't fully understand the material.

Goncharoff is a fantastic professor for ECE 341, he is very clear on the content and gives you extended time in order to complete quizzes which reflect exactly what will be on the exam. Projects can be difficult as they are long and require coding in matlab that I was unsure of before. Office hours become very important for homework and projects.
He cares about his students and is very friendly. He arranges his time well so that students have enough time to complete their homework

I would say his lectures are very easy. Additionally, he records the lectures so you can watch it if you miss anything. Labs require more detailed explanation. Three exams in total. Midterm 1,2 and final. Just study his notes and Practice problems and you should be fine.

Pro Tip:
Start working on labs ahead of time.
Revise notes(exams has mcq's)
He truly cares about his students and always gives helpful career guidance.

The class is clear if you follow lectures and quiz study guides. We used ZyBooks for reading assignments and had weekly quizzes, no exams. The lectures are helpful w/tips for quizzes. They're recorded. If you take good notes and try to understand the topics, you'll be fine. He is also nice and is accessible outside of class.
Very understanding and easy-going, and his lectures are useful. Approachable too and willing to help. cool professor!!!
cool guy
One of the best ECE professors. Knowledgeable, understanding, helpful. Labs can be tricky so come prepared, but you will learn a lot from this course
Let me say first the quizzes are very hard and you really need to know the material to do well, but the project are really easy. Going to his office hours really helped.

Another great class with this professor, one of the best at UIC. This class was really easy if you pay attention to his lectures. The homework for this class sometime is a bit confusing but going to his office hours really helped. He doesn't trick you on exam. Straight forward class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Honestly the best professor I ever had. I took his synch online course this semester and enjoyed every bit of it. He is easily accessible outside of class, great at explaining students' questions, and he's super caring. You can just tell he loves what he teaches. Oh, and a bonus, he's pretty funny too. Would definitely take again if I could.

I found the class to be easier as it goes on. I wish he taught us the topic we need for the exam because some question on the exam were not taught until the end of the class for the final. I wish he would do a better job of explaining the labs as they were vague and hard to begin. Overall he is a good professor.

Professor Goncharoff is very willing to help with the difficult homework assignments if you come to office hours for this class. Don't bother with the textbook; exam/homework information is from the lectures, which is why I struggled.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: online quizzes
He gives you homework to practice. He responds to e-mails promptly.  He really cares about your success.  I would love to take him again!

Lectures, homework, and tests were generally pretty clear. He posts all his lectures online so it's very easy to go back if you miss something.  Very favorable in grading with lots of extra credit.    My only complaint is that the class is lacking in practical problems.  So you get an understanding of concepts, but not when or how to use them.

This guy is a genius,  he knows everything and can teach anything to anyone. Very fair exams,  if you do the homework you should get an A in this class exams  are based off the hw.  He is one of the best professor ECE department has if you have a chance to take this any ece class with him TAKE IT!!! you wont regret it (unless you dont go to class).
Goncharoff Is one of the absolute best professors UIC has to offer! You could learn anything from this man. As well his dedication to his students is tremendous. 1010 would take for every ECE class.
He's a great prof, very helpful and obviously knows his stuff.  You should always attend his lectures if possible!
Knows his stuff. Great teacher. Very clear notes. Do the practice exams he gives and you'll do great.

Let me tell you this, this man knows his electrical and computer engineering. He is a great teacher and it is a pleasure that UIC has him as a professor. I really enjoyed every lecture in ECE 115. It was great and I look forward to taking courses from Professor Goncharoff in the future. Thank you for a great semester.

I had him for his first semester teaching 115, he usually teaches higher level classes. He was somewhat unorganized because it was his first time doing 115 but an amazing teacher none the less. Very lenient, very helpful, if you ever need help see him in his office, he has office hours every day. My favorite teacher by at UIC by far.

Bad teacher.  While he presents impressive material in an impressive manner, his lectures are just too boring, too unfocused, and go off on too many tangents.  Labs also barely have any connection to what is being thought in class and thus in turn don't really help out for lecture material.

Comes highly recommended. Extremely informative, & topics are explained crystal clear. Having said that you can't afford to miss his lecture which comes in pretty handy for doing assignments and quizzes. Gives enough opportunities to get an A in the class. Undoubtedly so far the best instructor I had at UIC.

So far the best professor I ever had for an ECE course at UIC. Following from what others have said here, all I can add is that you will get an A if you don't miss any of his lectures, since his homework assignments are tied to the lectures, which in turn are tied to the quizzes and the finals. If you do your part, then its a walk in the park.

At first I thought that he was too hard because i was struggling.  But, that was on me, I had to step it up.  At the end of the semester I thought that so far he  is the best professor I had at uic.  Willing to take summer cource ece 341 because he is going to be the instructor.
Fantastic teacher. Very nice and funny guy. Knows the material inside and out and backwards. Do yourself a favor and take whatever class he's teaching!

BY FAR THE BEST PROFF @ UIC. IF HE IS TEACHING A CLASS THAT YOU'RE INTERESTED IN TAKING, LOOK NO FURTHER. HE IS AN EXCELLENT INSTRUCTOR AND AN AMAZING PERSON IN GENERAL. TAKE THE CLASS WITH HIM! TRUST ME.

I HAD HIM FOR SIGNAL PROCESSING AND LET ME TELL YOU HE IS AN AMAZING DOWN TO EARTH, WELL VERSED PROFESSOR IN HIS FIELD. HIS LECTURES ARE VERY INTUITIVE & CLEAR.  HE IS ALWAYS THERE TO HELP YOU, AND HE IS THE ONLY PROFESSOR THAT I EVER WOULD LIKE TO TAKE A CLASS WITH AGAIN AT UNIV. OF IL @ CHI I HE GAVE ME GRADE OF B BUT I WOULD GIVE GRADE HIM AN A+
Class is useless, teacher plays youtube videos, and then gives 10 page programming assignments.
This guy is amazing, just take him and u won't regret.
Great instructor! You have to work very hard to get an A.
The class average on his final is a D. This professor cares more about meeting ABET standards than anything else. I would not take this instructor again.

Dr. Goncharoff is one of the most difficult professors I ever had throughout my education. He grades very tough and expects a lot from the students. If you take this class, make sure you aren't taking too many other difficult ones at the same time. The programs that he assigns are VERY time consuming and sometimes are impossible to finish on time.
Prof. Goncharoff is clearly one of the best professors at UIC. His lectures are a lot fun and actually interesting. If you need to take 267 you better take in NOW while he is still teaching it.

Prof Goncharoff is a very good professor. He explains the material very well and his exams/quizzes/homework assignments are pretty easy. For some assignments he will basically give you the answer. As long as you study the review material he gives in class, you will get a good grade on the exam. Going to class is very important.
Mr. Goncharoff is one of my favorite teachers. He explains everything very well, and is a really nice guy.

He is the best proff that I have had to date. You have to pay attention in his class, slacking is not an option. His tests and exams are ok and you learn a great deal. his class is fun too. great professor. I highly recommend him for 267.
He's great. He strikes a perfect  balance in all aspects of his teaching. Try to get all of your classes with Goncharoff.
All you need to do is pay attention during lectures and you can get a B in the class. Getting an A requires you to make little mistakes in his easy tests.
This professor is one of my favorites. I took ECE 265, ECE 341, ECE 367, and ECE 398. He was friendly, helpful, and I love his methodologies of teaching.
Professor Goncharoff was one of my favorites. I would suggest taking a class with him if you can. You will learn a lot, and you will walk away knowing that an EECS professor is on YOUR side.
Exellent teacher, geat person!
Best ECE teacher at UIC for any ECE class. Cant get a better professor anywhere else.
BEST ECE Teacher at UIC.  Lays everything out very nicely.  Easy to understand & very helpful if you need help.
No Comments
He's the best ECE professor at UIC! At the end of the semester you will understand the material and have an A.
No Comments

Dr. Goelz is a great professor. It is clear from taking her class that she is passionate about what she teaches, and this makes learning in her classroom fun. There are plenty of resources to help you succeed in the course, such as UTA led exam prep workshops, practice questions with detailed feedback, and kahoot reviews. 

You'll love KN 372!

Dense with content and course pace is quite quick but the class is overall very interesting and applicable to health careers. Professor Goelz is amazing and always there to help if you are struggling with any concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's an amazing professor. Took her class last semester with little to no knowledge about the course. Kn 372 was a difficult class and even though attendance is not mandatory, attending lecture helps so much. She offers additional help after class so I highly suggest going to her office hours or UTA's exam reviews.

I am writing this review after many years! Let me tell you I still remember so much of material Dr.goelz taught. It has helped me so much in many of my class during PT  program. She is an amazing teacher and you will retain the material even years after!! She truly is a gem to kinesiology program

Professor Goelz is an excellent professor. If you come to class it is 100% possible to get at least a B. She offers many resources to better understand topics you're not certain in. She's very jumpy and definitely knows what she is teaching and it helps a lot! She great you won't regret taking her in this class.

Definitely take Professor Goelz. She offers many extra credit opportunities and it's easy to get a good grade in her class if you come to the lectures and study. She's very fair with grading and she's also super caring about your learning. The best!

Love the teaching style always super energetic and going out of her way to make sure students understand material. If you go to class theres lots of extra credit opportunities, but be prepared to review lots of terms and memorize.

She talks extremely fast. For someone that is bilingual, it is hard to grab the concept of what she is trying to say. She is extremely hard and her exams are super tricky. She tricks you on purpose so you get the material-her exact words. I liked her personality and teaching but the exams were tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Goelz is energetic and fun. Her class is not difficult, make sure to go to class to fully understand the material. She is easy to talk to.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I came in intimidated by my first neuroscience class but Dr. Goelz made the material very fluid and incremental. She has a very energetic teaching style which helps in remembering processes/pathways, not to mention she repeats long explanations repeatedly so students are able to fully grasp it. Definitely a professor who truly knows their field.
Dr. Goelz is awesome. She is very approachable. For this class, definteley need the book. Read ahead if you want to get that A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Her classes are not easy and how you do in KN 372 or 472 depend on the effort you put in her classes. Grades are based entirely on quizzes and exams so keep up with studying. She is very energetic and approachable and she genuinely wants you to learn and succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is very energetic and interactive. Highly recommend going to class, she offers extra credit quizzes. Don't have to buy the book but pay very close attention in class and take good notes. It's doable to get an A but you cant slack off either. Tests are multiple choice and short answer.

I love how excited and encouraging Professor Goelz is- not just about the material, but about students' input in class discussion.  She has incredible energy so it's really easy to stay engaged during lecture. I never used the book, everything you need to know is on lecture slides.  I learned a lot, she's awesome.

She's probably the best professor one could ask for. She cares for your learning more rather than your grade. She make sure you understand the information and it CAN be a lot of information but she's so clear and concise and approachable that even the more abstract ideas are understandable.

Dr. Chin is PERFECT! Her lectures are fast paced but not too difficult to grasp if you're paying attention. She values your opinion as a student and is very understanding in any situation. The material she teaches is definitely valuable. I would and I am taking her class again. (She teaches KN472).
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--CARES ABOUT STUDENTS--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Chin was a pretty cool professor. She had a lot of enthusiasm and upbeat energy in the class which was very nice to see. Attendance was not mandatory, but she gave out easy random pop quizzes that were worth 1 extra credit each, and even if you got all of them wrong she would see that you attended most lectures and would round up your grade.

The way they grade is frustrating. They say there's no wrong answers in philosophy until you're taking the in class writing assignment, and all of a sudden you didn't answer correctly. The class is boring, wouldn't take it if it was required. She makes the concepts more difficult than they need to be. Never liked philosophy and this made it worse.

The way Professor Goodman chooses to run this class is frustrating. The class consists of 4 in-class, handwritten essays and a final of the same nature, which feels unnecessary and dated. The lectures were a little redundant, and I didn't understand concepts until the discussion section. I don't recommend taking this class unless it's required.

She says "um" a lot - like A LOT. It makes it kinda hard to follow what she's saying.
Overall, just started this course. Not entirely sure what to think. My TA is pretty great though, so I'm still hopeful.

You're graded on 3 argument summaries and 2 argumentative papers. The class is a breeze because there are no quizzes or tests. That being said, no technology is allowed in class. Attendance is mandatory. She's overly confrontational when someone's talking. Grading is left up to TAs so she can't help you. Answers lots of questions in lecture though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
There was nothing good about this class. The class is HEAVILY based on essays, essays are the only thing that factor into your grade (aside from attendance). It is next to impossible to get an A on a singular essay.

Attending office hours for the TA's is also useless. They say your paper is good, but give you a bad grade.

Professor Goodman was an amazing professor. If someone brought up an idea, she would rephrase to make sure it's clarified to not only the class but herself as well so she could understand and help with issues or questions you had. She's also engaging in class as she tries to get students to talk about their own ideas!

She's a brilliant instructor who manages to get across course content in an engaging and interesting way (though the TA for the class was... not my favorite). If philosophy is new to you, be sure to do the reading and sit up front and engage with her often, she loves to talk about the subject with students. She's also very accommodating.

Professor Goodman is very good at making sure you understand the content. Every time someone has an idea or question she rewords it to make sure everybody understands, and her lectures are pretty concise. Sometimes she does go a bit fast through the lectures, but overall she is pretty good. She's also Australian which is pretty fun.

He's a great professor & guy overall, but the assignments he gives can take a really long time to do, even the smaller ones. One small assignment that was related to my final took 5 hours to complete, but I do like his deadlines because all of the assignments were due a 1/2 hour right before class.

He was nice and very helpful and generous, especially if you email him about something. The class just had a lot of tedious work and if you are taking a ton of other hard classes its a bit tough. Sometimes he would make jokes or talk a lot and I didn't really understand (or care...) so it was a bit annoying. Also prepared to be randomly called on
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: very interesting person

what a delight! imbues old english texts w/ humor and spunk that makes them engaging 2 learn ab. some creative activities as well! u can tell he rlly cares ab the subject n his students' understanding of it. 

lack of flexibility w/ due dates was def a struggle tho. and bring ur textbook!

This review is for ENGL 154. Prof. Gore seems personable on the surface, but if you test his very limited goodwill, he gets an attitude for the rest of the semester. Cares more about his rules than his students; he violated ADA guidelines when I burned through his allotted skip days and didn't apologize even after he was reported and corrected.

Professor Gore is so funny & nice. However, be prepared to read the material because he takes class participation as a leading tool for his classes. he will  call on people and ask questions/thoughts on the readings. If you have unexpected situations arise in your private life, he will give you opportunities to make up for missing assignments.10/10

Lovee professor Gore. He's so spunky and fun and you'll never leave his class without laughing! Can tend to have many assignments but theyre very doable and relevant to class. Many readings too that you cant skip because he WILL call on you, trust! and if hes not satisfied with your answer he will keep probing until he is lol

10/10 would recommend

Professor Gore is a great professor. HON 121 often fills with STEM majors who are not well-suited to an English course: for those people, take a different course to fill your creative arts requirement. For those in the humanities, this is a great course to take. Lectures are a little rambly but always has a point. Definitely read the material!

We had assigned readings every meeting (over 30 pages), then we would discuss them in class but not the entire book. He had us write 2 essays with topics that were vague, and a final project that's basically an essay with real world examples using texts. Just make sure you really enjoy what you see in the course description before registering.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Class is what you expect out of a reading/writing english class, LOTS of reading, and he randomly calls on people to speak. You don't really have to do the readings, as you can use sparknotes for everything and still get the main ideas. Essays were alright, gives a decent amount of time to write them. Not bad, but not amazing either.

Intro to Shakespeare with Dr. Gore was a great class! His teaching style is a little different, but it works very well for me, personally. He calls on people randomly to participate but is more than willing to work through things that the class hasn't comprehended.

He is certainly passionated about what the content he's teaching. He is understanding if you can't attend class, and he is lenient on late papers (if you have a reason). He is a typical college professor; he assigns readings, expects participation, and cares about students. He may teach in an unusual manner, but he knows it will better the students

I loved his class but it might not be for everyone. He makes you participate A LOT. He will call on you randomly & have you go up to the board so pay attention and READ. The readings are relatively short but dense so sometimes you'll have to read them over again to complete the hw. The essays were fun to write. He's really silly and nice overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Jeffery Gore is a great professor, Hes extremely passionate about what he teaches and is incredibly helpful and makes class actually enjoyable. But there are consistently long readings paired with boring journals. On top of this participation is forced upon you at times, and the essays are somewhat long
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I loved his class. He's a great professor. Very passionate. There are plenty of opportunities to meet outside of class if you want feedback on an essay or other major assignment. You'll learn a lot from this course. That said, journals may seem like a lot, but they aren't graded harshly. Attendance is mandatory, you cant miss more than five classes

Prof Gore is an extremely enjoyable prof. He is super enthusiastic about what he does. Be prepared to read many novels and participate in class- a lot. He is super helpful in helping you write papers and is willing to assist at any time. His cheerful and light attitude always made class enjoyable and full of laughter. Be prepared for daily hw.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I took a grammar class with him and the content wasn't hard. He teaches it well and we relied on the book A LOT. The quizzes and hw aren't hard at all either. HOWEVER, he's very keen on participation and makes you read your answers out loud. So, if going up to the board or talking out loud in class aren't your thing, you'll have a hard time /:
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He talks way too much about things that have nothing to do with the class. He seems to be quite narcissistic. He is so nick picky about everything, sarcastic, talks at you, attitude problems. Taking this class during the pandemic is tough, I wouldnt recommend. He is too emotional to teach this class. The guy has issues and is kind of rude.

Awesome professor, loved getting feedback on my essays. Three papers and a final exam. Lots of reading but the novels are interesting, and there are journals due based on the readings. Overall enjoyed the class, but you need to put lots of time in outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He was an amazing professor. My favorite one this semester. He has daily hw, 2 papers, 5 quizzes. midterm, and final. He is hilarious and is open to going to his office hours. Definitely recommend

He can come off a bit condescending at times. Daily book exercises, 2 essays, midterm and final. Fair warning-he grades major assignments kind of slow.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: My most FAVORITE professor yet. He is interesting to talk to and listen to, keeps us engaged in class, super accessible outside of class. Got A's on all my papers because he prepared us so well beforehand plus he meets with us as many times outside of class to go over it. Makes class fun and gives good advice. Def take him, you won't regret it!!

Dr. Gore was my favorite professor of the semester. He is engaging and enthusiastic about the material, and every class brought interesting discussion. You have to do your homework to participate in discussions, but it is not that difficult (and rarely checked). You will most likely enjoy this class, but at the very least you wont dread going.

Dr. Gore is charmingly hilarious. He will try to do his best to make you you understand the material. He can come off as rude sometimes, but overall, he's a nice guy and class is really fun most of the time.

Heres the lowdown hoedown. Jeffrey Gore rose from the depths of hell to terrorize students and their GPAs. If you love hearing a white old man ranting about other white old men for 45 minutes to an hour, take this class. If you want 80 pages of reading/night and random 45 minute tangents on old 1400s white dudes this is the class for you! NO. NO.

reviews.comment: Super caring, genuinely wants students to pass with comprehension. Makes the dullest of topics fun and understandable.

Gore was personable with his students while being highly professional. His syllabus is followed to a "T" in this class, and each of his assignments' instructions are included in the syllabus. Gore really cares about his students, and he is excited and motivated to teach grammar. He is supportive and you can't do badly if you do your work and study.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Prof. Gore's class was great! The nature of grammar makes the class lecture heavy, but he really enjoys getting the class involved in work and making it accessible to everyone. He can be a little eccentric, but he really knows his stuff and cares that his students understand the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Lots of unnecessary group work, going up to the whiteboard, and nitpicky quizzes. The sarcastic attitude he got when he unknowingly went over his lecture time and people started packing wasn't appreciated either. The material is VERY dull, and the fact that we had to meet up three days a week for it made things even more tedious. Not recommended.

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed taking his class. He's a funny guy and very understanding. You can't miss more than 4 of his classes to pass; however, if you talk to him and work out something he will work with you. I recommend him.

Class with Dr. Gore was a very awesome experience. He is a genuinely nice guy, very fair with his grading, very clear and concise with his expectations, and very approachable and accesible outside of class. I would honestly recommend any class he teaches. The front half to 2/3 of the class are homework heavy, and theres two papers, but overall easy
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Professor Gore was a great teacher! He was really enthusiastic and had great teaching methods. Maybe it was because I took his grammar class, but it was pretty straightforward and easy. Lots of chances for extra credit, such as doing additional exercises. Overall, good experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He is a nice guy but I was not a fan at all. U can only miss 4 classes and after that each class u miss ur grade is dropped a letter grade. Im the one who went to class everyday and turned everything in but for some reason he gave me aa B. AVOID

Dr. Gore is a very sincere , goofy and genuine guy. He's an easier grader on essays, and they make up a big percentage of your grade. If you show up to class, put time and effort into every draft for each paper, the class should be a pretty easy A. You don't really need to do your journal entries before each class, just do them b4 he checks them.

He was overall a good professor. He's a tough grader. I was upset with my grade so I'm letting yall know that you should visit him during office hours. I am highly recommending that because if you're borderline at the end of the semester he won't round you up.

He is one of the most wonderful professors at UIC. A beautiful weirdo. He deeply cares about his students and in his own little way, he wants to push you hard to succeed and think in different creative avenues. You will get the most help if you attend his office hours. I absolutely recommend anyone taking him whenever he offers English classes.

Dr. Gore is a super friendly person. He is indeed very motivated to have his students learn more about Global Issues that affect our daily lives and does so in an exciting manner. As long as you participate in his class, getting an A shouldn't be difficult! Join his GLC program!

Professor Gore is very eccentric, funny, sarcastic, dorky, and intelligent. Provides helpful analogies to help students understand texts, many of which are quite dense. REALLY cares about his students. Is extremely enthusiastic to dedicate time to helping students with both class and personal issues. Can be a tough grader, but the class was great.

Really goofy and enthusiastic about what he teaches. He's really helpful and insightful and makes sure you understand the material. Sometimes it's hard for him to stay on topic and he is all over the place when he writes notes on the board but good teacher overall.

He is super funny. Does this Grover impression from Sesame Street from time-to-time. He's kinda weird but he's cool. Sometimes unclear but if you try and ask for help, should be an easy class. Just have to try hard and actually think about what you are doing and writing.
HILARIOUS teacher.  Really wanted the students to learn and is really passionate about what he teaches.  His class is very interesting and he is by far the best teacher I've ever had.

Professor Gore disproves the notion that one cannot excel in mediocrity. Not bad, but nothing memorable or interesting. Talks at you; does not draw out the interesting aspects of Shakespeare; makes the greatest English writer sometimes feel a bit dull. Still a nice guy, but nothing remarkable. At all.

It's true he doess go off on tangents, and he does act very sarcastic as well as being a little bit of an egonamic. However, he is a brilliant person and is willing to help you if you need it. Just don't take him too seriously.

It is very hard for him to stay on one topic. If you say one thing that may relate to something else he will go of on a total tangent. Doesn't explain essay assignments extremely well and then expects you to go to him when he should have explained it clearly in the first place. Too sarcastic for me and can be a  ass if u take things too seriously.
No Comments
Nice, easy lecturer. He explains things very clearly, and is always willing to help. The only problem with him was that he gave a lot of work at the last minute. Nonetheless, a cool guy.

Lectures are secondary to readings. To do well, focus entirely on analyzing the texts, writing, and start reading early. Prioritize progress and annotations. The online layout needs some navigation, but the workload is manageable enough to succeed in class.

reviews.comment: Mr G. isn't difficult. The curriculum could be more on task; however, it's incredibly easy. He's understanding and gives great feedback, but his way of organization is... unique. If I could rate him out of ten, I'd give him a -10000/10. He is so unorganized and wastes your time every class period. Gives you attitude and judges you for everything too, so come prepared. He also grades based on "effort", meaning how much you talk to him, no matter if Shakespeare wrote it, he'd fail it. Take him if it's your VERY last resort!!!

reviews.comment: His blackboard site could be organized a bit better, but I nonetheless enjoyed the more 'laid back' and non-lecture-heavy approach to his class. Scott is a solid professor to say the least. Although he isn't the brightest in communication and might be boring, he does care about you and your grade in the class. reviews.comment: I was a student in Mr.G's class frpm 2012-2013. He is a wonderful professor, mentor and friend. reviews.comment: Very helpful and caring professor One of the best I have ever worked under

Professor Grunow is probably the best English Professor I've had at UIC, to the point where I'm considering minoring in English with how helpful him and this course were to my writing. He is very strict with readings and assignments but will consider opportunities to make up work if he sees effort in the class. A very valuable instructor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Grunow is very strict and insensitive, and if you aren't a well developed writer, you may want to reconsider.
