Portfolio Management is by far the toughest finance class you can take at UIC but very doable if you pay attention. I liked Prof Chen - one of those too smart to teach profs.. so you need be PRESENT in class, not just show up to pass. Homework (30%) is team-based, so choose wisely bc the exams (midterm & final - 70%) are exactly like the HWs.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Great class if you looking to work for portfolio management firm or analyze funds performance. 50% interesting lectures 50% math and finance heavy lectures. Tests are basically homework problems, make sure you know how to do them by yourself. All homework are done in excel, make sure to brush up your excel skills. Exams are open notes.

Chen is one of the smartest Finance professors I had the pleasure of knowing at UIC. The class is VERY challenging though. Tests are based on the homework, but that does not make them any easier. The homework takes a lot of time to complete so get ready to spend long hours working through them. Work hard and get rewarded. Slack and you won't pass.

Professor Chen is truly a smart guy. He is awesome because he knows everyone's name and is helpful.. But damn, this class is extremely hard. Basically, the homework is your key. The hw is based on the lectures, and the exams are like the hw. The problem is, you have to build the hw alone in excel. Useful class, but I can't keep up.

Guys, take it from someone who's been through hell and back in this class. DO NOT TAKE IT. You'll hate yourself, your life and your mom for bringing you to this world and having the opportunity to take it.
just read the book prior the lecture and you'll be fine! Really loved the project, open book exams!

took his portfolio analysis course this semester. this guy is a nice guy but it doesnt seem like he knows how to teach. he expected everyone to be an excel expert, which wasnt in the course description. the exam question were based on hw, but he didnt really give the answers to the hw problems in class. Expect lots of office visits for an A.

He was extremely difficult to understand. When students asked questions sometimes he would get frustrated. The most frustrating part, was he really didn't follow the syllabus. We would find out when we were having an exam the week prior. We also had a group project due, but never really gave any type of direction or what to expect.I don't recommend

This professor is horrible, Do not take this course if you do not know how to use excel for stat and finance functions.Has an accent, whole class relies on smart students to do the homework, tests are similar to HW's He definitely a smart guy no doubt good class but needs some tutoring to teach. Waste of time and money I dropped it no hope to pass.

he is the best teacher I ever see in UIC. he know what he talking about and let student to work on the project themself and present it and he will guide you through the work if you dont't understand the work. His test is real simple if you understand your hw. His test is just same as the hw only few number different.

The professor is a really nice guy and definitely knows his stuff, but that doesn't mean that he is the best teacher for this course. His accent makes it very difficult to understand him and he rushes through the lessons (which you have to be an ADVANCED excel user to have a chance to keep up with). The test are hard and the averages were under 40%

Really difficult class...Sometimes hard to understand Prof's accent...Assumes we are experts in statistics/excel prior to course which none of us were...Vague explanations in class...Prof. Chen definitely knows his stuff when it comes to investments/portfolios but he really isn't that good at teaching...Work hard and hope for a C at best... :/

This class was quite good.  I think it is funny that the person who posted first said that this was not an easy A.  ITS PORTFOLIO MANAGEMENT FOR GOD SAKES.  Chen was a good instructor, humorous, and helpful.  Bust your butt and get an A or B.

I would say that if you don't have a decent understanding of stats and finance prior to taking this class,it will be challenging. This is a 400 level class, so he has to assume you know something. Otherwise, this is an excellent class, proffesor is experienced and helps a lot with the homework. You have to attend to do well, and pay attention.

This class is very difficult. This is not for those who want an easy A and requires reading and understanding things on your own. He does not show how to do h/w and the test are really hard. Take this class only if your really interested in this subject and willing to give effort toward learning.

I have seen many bad teachers but someone with a behavioural problem this bad has never been seen before. All others make sense except for her. She would make random groups and will ask you to stick to them. Ending up only 1 person doing the work. Provides no material for exams that comes out Entirely different from what was taught.

This professor has absolutely 0 empathy for students. She is super unclear about everything in the course and is blatantly rude towards her students. It is almost impossible to know what is going on for exams. She also schedules things for outside of class time and says "Oh well" if you are not able to attend.

Definitely a tough grader so make sure to leave no stone unturned in the homeworks. Do every assignment and ask questions about the in class. Lectures are heavily based on theory and questions can be hard to understand. Be ready to do extra reading to pass this class. Final exam was also hard despite being open book.

I would never suggest to anyone to take this course!! A lot of homework and grade were horrible !!!!very tough grader and exams are not relevant to her lecture. Topics are not used as hot topics. If you want to waste your time and get C, you can take it!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Nice teacher, good classes. But she graded exams EXTREMELY harsh. 2 group pojects and 1 presentation, hws every week(hard copy) You would thought the class wasn't too hard, but the homeworks would be much harder, 3 exams MUCH MORE harder. Average grades would be in the 20s, every little mistake in your solution could result in 70% points deduction.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Her class was amazing. Everything was well organized, and the homeworks were not bad at all. It is an easy gen ed and you learn a lot.

Very, very easy class but I still feel like I gained knowledge for taking it. Only met once every other week. Lots of group work in and outside of class, but she's a very sweet professor and definitely cares about her profession and students.

I love her! She is extremely kind and genuine! She truly cares for her students. If you ever need help do not hesitate to reach out to her! She is truly one of the kindest instructor's I have ever had. Her workload is manageable and easy. She gives out a lot of extensions. Very soft spoken which made the classroom a very good place to learn!
Super approachable professor, super caring. Her insight to the material was great and she was always clear on the things she expected out of you assignment-wise.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Hughes is super kind and understanding. The workload is not bad at all and the assignments are pretty easy to complete.

He's a funny guy if you're listening. Best part about him though is that he doesn't try to break your balls, he knows his class in the grand scheme of things isn't very important. Other professors who assign a ton of work just to make their class seem important could learn a thing or two from him. He also is a prof who genuinely cares.

Professor Huerta is an amazing professor. He is very kind and has interesting lectures. He is a very funny and cool guy. Class was generally very easy but could be a lot of reading at times. If you show up to class you should get an easy A.

Huerta is very knowledgeable and passionate about the readings he assigns. He has a diverse range of readings and truly delves into them. He loves having class discussions so keeping up with the readings is crucial to getting a good grade. He is very understanding and funny, so he is very approachable.

I really liked this teacher, It was a basic class but he did a good job teaching. You only need to pass this class by understanding the lectures and GOING to discussion session. I would recommend this teacher, nothing special but he does his job well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Huerta is enthusiastic about his work, you can tell he really tries his best to interact with the class and provide a safe environment.  His presentations are very entertaining and is great at creating conversations with students when the students choose to participate, he likes to make sure everyone gets heard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: I took this class as a requirement. This was a fairly easy class, the professor is so chill and although my class was dead asl, the lectures were interesting to me. The class was graded by discussion posts, a couple quizzes, and few papers. All of the answers were in the texts provided, if you just do what is asked, you'll pass with an A fr.

He is a caring prof but his lectures are very boring and I found no reason to go because the discussion sections were nothing related to what he talked about. There were weekly discussion board, weekly readings, and a couple of projects here and there. This class is not hard. Just participate in discussion and do most of the readings.

Took him online during Covid. Chill guy. Classes are mainly covering powerpoints but they're mainly for learning new things and nothing was tested on. Had some bigger essays and one group project but it's nothing worth losing sleep over. If you're interested in the topic, you'll learn some new things if you pay attention.

Huerta was cool and his class was not difficult. Probably my only criticism is that the powerpoints and lectures he would do for class did not tie at all with the readings he would assign for class, so when it came to the exam and we were tested on the info it was kind of like ??? why didn't we talk about this during class? Still a great professor.

He is a really funny professor with true personal stories that really help understand the topics. The course material was extremely interesting and fun to learn about, and there was minimal reading for the book needed for the class. Even discussions were easy.

Huerta is very generous and understanding of students. Quizzes were content based, so if you read the readings it was an easy grade. One group presentation, a few papers. No final exam for my section, we just had a final 5-7 page paper.
There was a group project and you had to use the books for some assignments. Overall it wasn't a bad class it was pretty decent. The lecture was a bit boring but nothing hard to handle.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very informative lectures, Prof. Huerta clearly knows his stuff and often mixes in video clips to keep things interesting. Attendance is mandatory, but you can survive from the online notes as they have most lectures covered. He gives out the readings that NEED to be studied before giving a test so as long as you read by the test date you're set.

He is awesome! I dont see why so many people complain about his lectures. Hes very straight to the point and hes also very passionate about what he talks about. Hes super funny and sweet. Take him! Easy class not much work just readings but nothing you cant handle. Hes also very understanding and just a great guy!
Super easy class, attendance is mandatory. Coursework is very light, focused on three books (short novels) and west side story. At the end there is a group project

His lectures were so boring although they were interesting. Don't even bother taking notes, all of his powerpoints are online. You can skip lecture but definitely go to discussion. The TA is super cool and makes it clear what you have to do to get a good grade. So much reading! esp 15+ page articles. Other than that, it's not hard to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Professor Huerta loves what he teaches and taught many interesting topics about Latino culture. His lectures did get dull at times and had many readings (both books and articles). His class assignments were not difficult but were time consuming. Had a cool TA (Laura Nieves) who was tough, yet understanding. Final and Midterm were ehh on difficulty.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The class is interesting. Yet, the lectures do feel longer than they should. He does crack a joke here and there. You do have to read some things for discussion. There is work to be completed and at my time I did get a group project. Still not a bad class. Just go to lecture, and take notes. You should do well.

There's a lot of assignments but not too many exams. He's really chill, flexible, and funny. His lectures can drag but overall in you put in a reasonable amount of effort you can get an A. Occasional pop quiz in discussion

Professor Huerta is very funny and wise.  He just has a great attitude about people and diversity.  There's a lot of reading, but it's all enjoyable stuff, nothing difficult.  He knows how to lead a discussion on literature.  If you don't read or pay attentionstudy the powerpoints, you won't do well on the tests or in the course.

Lectures can get boring at times. He seems to have a passion for classic rock. His powerpoints were kind of irrelevant. There's two group projects. He is very funny and has a passion for his Mexican culture.

He is a smart and nice guy, but the course is EXTREMELY boring and his lectures seemed very irrelevant (hard to follow) I honestly read 4 of the 30 discussion articles, 0 of the 4 chapter books. I can't tell you for a minute straight what I learned in his class. And I got a B. A few papers, (3?) no final exam, but overall this class is not worth it
Good professor and really cares about the students. His lectures can get boring at times but he is really nice. A lot of work but it is pretty easy. You wont be disappointed taking his class.
Good professor, he is knowledgeable and readily available to help when needed. He can be a little dry sometimes, but he's a nice guy and does have his humor.

This is a pretty easy class although it cane be a bit boring at times. There's quite a bit of work required (2 readings each week, 1 mid-term, a research paper, a few random assignments, and a couple pop quizzes) but none of it is rocket science. If you actually put a little effort into the class you should have no problem getting an A.

It's a kind of boring class, but if you do the (there's reading every week so it takes a bit of effort) readings you should be okay. The class probably focuses on the most boring parts of Latino culture one could find. I never did the readings but I'm still passing. But do the readings and you should get an A. For more fun, take a different course.
Lecture is kind of boring but he's not a bad teacher. There is a lot of reading involved though but if you read everything the class will be easy.
Cool teacher. Do the work an read the assignments. Ended up with an A
He is a great professor even though there are some boring parts; he is very nice! there's 1 midterm, No final, 3 papers, little assignments here and there, takes attendance. Overall, easy class!

Whoever wrote the previous comment is crazy.  Professor Huerta is one of the best professors I've had.  Very interesting and insightful and always changes things up.  I think he is great, and you will too!
Very bad. Loves Texas too much. Doesn't teach Latin Cultures.. just useless things like San Antonio and soccer. Rambles a lot about NOTHING (tries to make it sound educated)

I had just recently posted a review, but I had done great injustice. I mistakenly selected the 4/5 rating for difficulty, which is very misleading; I had meant to select the 1/5, because he explains everything very well!

Very inspirational and certainly a genius! He will notice if you are not understanding a concept, and he will make sure that you get it! Man how much I respect him! Yes, he is English; studied at Oxford; and speaks the language fluently... but dare you not learn English from him :)) UNLESS you weren't his student, you will understand what I mean...
Very kind and encourages students to engage with the material.

Very kind and patient. Class attendance is mandatory and class grade is mostly based on short essays, attendance, and the final. Assigned readings are important and discusses them heavily in class. Do the readings, attend lecture and attend office hours. You are guaranteed an A. His TA Sam B was amazing. Best class I've ever taken!

He was an awesome teacher. He was avid, knowledgeable, and patient.  He responded promptly to emails and seemed to look out for all of us.  He and Professor Fleishacker were the best teachers I've had so far.

He's patient, knowledgeable, and seems to take an interest in his students.  He's one of the better teachers I've had in college, so far.  I think that he and Fleishacker are at the best Philosophy professors. His logic class was pretty hard, though, and not for the insincere.
A really great teacher and a great person. He's so patient, if you don't get something he really cares that you understand. He loves physics, so if you don't you may not enjoy it.

very dry teaching style, class is easy at first but if you start to slack off towards the middle of the semester it will come back to haunt you because it becomes impossible.your grade also depends on the TA you get. avoid david potts if you can as a TA, hes absolutely awful, offers no support never explains anything. take this class pass/fail
Good professor. A little hard to understand material if you are not paying close attention, but he is very helpful and responds to e-mails fast.

BEWARE!!!!!!!  hate this class....  teacher not reliable. TA understand the problem but are not clear with their own explanations. I made a HUGE MISTAKE takin this class..  STAY AWAY!!!!!!! this brings ur GPA DOWN

Alright, so... I hated this guy at first, but it turns out he's not as malicious as he makes himself out to be the first week of class. He explained the material clearly enough for me, but I noticed that he wasn't very good at answering questions, so you better get lucky...
A somewhat interesting class. His teaching style is a little dry and long winded. Lectures are boring but when it comes down to it, his class was pretty easy.

the material is hard to grasp.  I think he's really into it but hasn't fine tuned his art of teaching.  While I was taking the class I thought the material was sort of pointless, however, two years later it comes up a lot, and I think I learned some very valuable things.
Study hard and you'll be fine.
Seemed stuck on himself. Class was harder than it needed to be.
anyone who doesn't like his teaching is probably just not interested in philosophy. i loved the class!

Hated this class! In the beginning the professor seemed nice. Then he goes crazy. He even yelled at people trying to leave early!! Did not understand one thing, just barely passed cuz of the TA. DO not take this class with him!

You need to have a hard interest in the subject matter, otherwise everything will go over your head.  He takes attendance even in the lecture by means of a sign-in sheet that goes around during class.  I needed to keep pinching myself just to stay awake, and focusing was normally impossible.
He was not very helpgful in the class- if it wasn't for the TA I would have failed!
No Comments

I was not sure if Prof H was teaching a hard or easy course until just lately. He cares about teaching I think! My feelings towards him mirror my grasping of the material.  Seemed too easy, then too hard/boring.  Now I get it.  Too bad I didn't get it earlier, I could've learned a lot more.
What is that man talking about.
Teaches well, keeps you awake.
If it wasn't for my TA I probably would have failed this damn course.
No Comments
No Comments
Easily one of the best prof's I've ever had. Expects a lot, but he gives a lot. He loves the subject he teaches, and it shows.
No Comments

79/100 - What I got on my final paper. How petty do you have to be. After that, I checked my overall grade, it was a B. Final grade ended up being a C because she doesn't want you to succeed. Completion of assignments doesn't matter unless it's exactly what she wants; the person who has studied this for years. Will contradict herself and is rude.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor has a clear agenda and set beliefs that you will be punished for deviating from. The workload is large and the mandatory theme is uncompelling. Do not take this professor if you enjoy the freedom to write topics which interest you, or if you plan on deviating from her espoused political or historical beliefs.
nice professor, but workload is ridiculous for a gen Ed course. Requires a TON of reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: The complaints about this prof seem to be from 200-level classes. Long papers and a heavy workload are par for the course in 400 level classes like this, however. Very attentive, frequent check-ins to keep you on track, group discussions where participation is expected- so doing the readings is important! Helps prepare you for the museum field.

I would totally recommend this class to a history or anthro major, but to those looking for an easy gen ed. Heavy workload, but the topic is extremely interesting. Prof. Hudson cares a lot and is always willing to workshop papers or spitball ideas-- she wants to help you succeed! The papers and exams are pretty demanding, however.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: I do not recommend. Totally agree with the previous reviews. Unless you can keep up with no structural slides and only her talking, dont take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I also agree that she is a nice person and all but her teaching method is definitely not for me. Ive never had a professor like this. It is EXTREMELY difficult to follow her lectures. Its literally just pictures and she talks really fast and jumps around a lot. She is also TOUGH grader, unclear about her expectations and contradicts it in the end

I think she's really fun but as for the structure of the class, it really didn't work well. There was a large paper due in the fourth week that required having read an entire book and then part of another, I wasn't even able to get the book until the end of the second week. I also agree that the lecture slides were not helpful at all, just pictures
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: I had a very difficult time keeping up with notes in class. Her slides consisted of only pictures and she spoke really fast and was jumping all over the place. She is a nice person overall but her teaching methods are not it for me.

Professor Hudson is a gem! If only more professors were like her. She cares so much about her students. Always is willing to help you work through your paper ideas and issues, she is an amazing resource for all things history. Any class you take with her will leave you better off in both the short term and long run. Highly recommend.

I loved Prof. Hudson's class. She is hilarious and super knowledgeable and works hard to engage the class. She assigns a moderate amount of work, so if you don't want to read or write a few, shorter papers, don't take her class. I really looked forward to this class and enjoyed her teaching style so much I took class with her the next semester!

The online lectures have terrible audio and video. I strongly recommend buying the textbooks, you are better off with those than watching the lectures or learning online. Also, be prepared to write a "required" paper, do NOT put it off. Lastly, if you do not have any prior music background, you will struggle.

The recorded videos he provides as the lecture material are unbearable to watch, the audio quality and video quality are horrid. Spent my time watching random music theory YouTube videos instead of his garbage recordings.

Sure, this is the easiest A you'll ever get, but if you're remotely interested in music theory, DO NOT TAKE HIS ONLINE COURSE.

Prof. Huang is nice and respectful. However, the class is a bit weird considering there are no proper resources to read or study from besides the lecture videos which are very old with terrible audio and video. It's difficult to learn anything from watching them. If you have any formal music education, you should do fine. Workload is pretty light.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I went in looking for an easy A, and this is not that! You will be learning about musical notes, and how to read music basically. However, he is a good professor, I just am lazy. He cares, and if you put in the work you will do well. Hard class if you are not good at music though.

Hai Tao Huang is one of my favourite professors as an incoming freshman. The class is very textbook heavy so it is easy to follow along despite his accent. Participating in class will lead to a better relationship with him. I can tell that he wants to see me succeed and having his support is very uplifting and is pushing me to succeed.

I had Mr. Huang during an online semester. His lectures were unbearable to watch really, due to his very thick accent and poor video quality. So I basically taught myself using the workbook that was recommended. The homework was easy enough, but I dont think this class would have been doable without the workbook and self teaching.

Professor Huang is very wholesome in his lectures and theyre pleasant to watch. You will need to do homework weekly as well as watch two one hour lectures a week plus an exam about once a month. This class is great for people who dont like to participate. Its heavy in terms of reading the textbook, but its doable! Good luck music boys!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Huang is really sweet and caring as a professor, but his soft voice and heavy accent combined with poor use of technology sometimes makes his lectures hard to understand. He attempts to cover a lot of theory in one semester and that makes the class heavy, but he gives many resources and easy assignments to be able to pass with an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: If you're a beginner don't take this class. I choose this class thinking it'll be more interactive but the class is only slides based. I really appreciate the work he does and he's really sweet but if you're looking for a good music experience I'll recommend you to search a different class.

Professor Hai Tao Huang is a great professor! He is very knowledgeable about music theory. I had prior music experience on the piano before taking this class. I would say if you at least know the foundation of musical notes, you'll catch on really quick to the rest of the material. It's not too hard of a class I promise! He's great!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's a cool guy. I basically lived at his office hours but mostly to chat. Accent, yes, but I had no trouble. The class is kind of hard after the 2nd exam if you don't have music experience. He does move a bit fast but you can review what you missed with videos. You don't technically need the book because he'll give you the hw & it's $80+. Hi Hai!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: This class is hard. You have to really really pay attention, focus, study and memorize. He is a very sweet man and will genuinely help you. He seems to curve test grades and offers lots of extra credit. He does teach kind of quickly though and is hard to understand but is very nice. Definitely not an easy A to get if you dont have musical knowledge
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is literally the best professor I've ever had. He's very caring and always willing to help students. He makes everything simple and easy to understand. He has an accent, but it's not difficult to understand him. If you play an instrument, this class is an easy A. If you don't, just pay attention in class and you'll pass with at least a B.

He's helpful if you want to do well in the class! Just read the book or ask him if you don't understand. You can borrow the book from library. If you haven't learnt any music instruments before, I won't recommend you to take this class because you may feel hard to follow. Homework helps study. Expect that class will be difficult after Exam1.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's helpful if you want to do well in the class! Just read the book or ask him if you don't understand. You can borrow the book from library. If you haven't learnt any music instruments before, I won't recommend you to take this class because you may feel hard to follow. Homework helps study. Expect that class will be difficult after Exam1.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I loved the class but there was a language barrier a bit tough to understand sometimes. There is a textbook that he says you should get but I was fine without it. Keep in mind, I already know a lot of music myself so this class was not that hard. For a beginner, it would be a new learning experience, just show up and you'll be fine.

Go to class and attend lectures. It's really a simple class and he follows the book. The person who recommended this class to me was a complete idiot and somehow managed to get a B just by reading the book and showing up for exams. I know for sure he didn't go to class because he would be sleeping on my couch. Highly recommend taking this class.

He's a really nice guy, can be funny at times too. There's a bit of a language barrier, but if you have trouble with it you can either read the book if you got it or watch videos of the topic on youtube. Easy A.

It is easy class, but not easy A.  Still must study ,and do your work! I would take it with friends to understand the concepts better. I think I would have had hard time if I didn't knew someone with better understanding of music theory.
Impossible to fail this class if you go and listen to his lectures... if you at least look at what is on the board you can pass with an A.

Professor Huang is one of the most helpful professors i've come across UIC. If you have no musical experience like me, come to his office hours whenever you can! He is willing to help. I struggled a bit in his class but if you make the effort, he will do whatever he can to make ends meet. This professor is great. TAKE HIM!

If you play an instrument, this class is probably going to be a joke to you. If you have absolutely no musical experience like me you should steer clear if you want an easy A.you'll probably be putting in more effort than you should have to considering his accent is very thick and so following him can be hard. Got a B, but gpa booster? Not so much.

EASY A, especially if you've played an instrument before. Didn't buy the textbook and still got an A. He gives you a copy of the hw so you really don't need it. I failed most of the ear-training quizzes but got 100 on all of my exams because they're super easy if you understand the concept (plus a little bit of memorization).

If you miss high school, take this class. If you play an instrument, you are guaranteed an A. B = didn't try hard enough. C = okay what are you doing in college? D = slap in the face F = okay withdraw from UIC
go to class, take notes. read the book. get an A.

very caring professor. he will guide you in the right direction if you aren't doing well in the class, even if it means he has to help you on exams. didn't have a music background so it was harder for me but still doable. doesn't require extensive time to prepare for exams. my friends with music backgrounds barely studied for the class.
Easy A, just study day before exams
YAY FOR GPA
GPA BOOSTER!
free B easy A. if you get a C you shouldnt be in college.
"so easy a caveman can do it"

Hai-Tao is awesome. He wants everyone to pass! I got a 75% of an exam and he made me stay after class and asked me why I did so poorly! Because everyone should get an A or at least a B. I play the piano and guitar which is helpful. It is true he has an accent but material is easy if you put in some work.  You're in college not kindergarten

Easiest class hands down! Take this class! I'm not smart and I dont play no instrument and im a psych  major and i easily got A in this class. take this class to boost your gpa. funny professor with einstien hair. just hearing him talk is entertaining.
Easiest class I've taken at UIC. I play an instrument which is helpful.

This is an easy gen ed for creative arts. He has heavy accent but this class is SO EASY for a gen ed. He is very helpful and wants his students to pass. This class will be even easier if you played an instrument before (almost like your reviewing). Take him... if you don't like his teacher you can still pass his tests by reading the book.
He is a nice guy and the class is super easy. I got an A without buying the textbook. He give quiz every week but that is pretty easy if you take note in class.

If you play an instrument... Music 107 with this professor will be the easiest gen. ed for you at UIC. This teacher is awesome and funny! He's chill and he will help you if he see's you are struggling. The first day of class...he said NO ONE should get a C in his class.

He's a nice guy but it's hard to understand him not only because of his accent, but he mumbles a lot. The subject isn't as easy as I'd like it to be and can be quite confusing at times. Some things are difficult to grasp and remember. He's a good guy but idk if I would recommend him

Very nice professor! His class is a easy one if you pay enough attention during the class then there is no challenging. If you have any question, don't be late to solve it! Just go and ask his help! Again, He is a very nice professor!!!

He is the worst professor I've had this semester! He is a sweet man and willing to help you with the work anytime, but he is INCOMPREHENSIBLE! He speaks with a heavy accent and you can never understand what he is saying! You're better off using the workbooks for class if you want to pass.

He is the worst professor I've had this semester! He is a sweet man and willing to help you with the work anytime, but he is INCOMPREHENSIBLE! He speaks with a heavy accent and you can never understand what he is saying! You're better off using the workbooks for class if you want to pass.

i don't know what all these people are talking about, but this was def not an easy class. i got a c in it. idk, he's very hard to understand. i thought i would have gotten an A or a B, but when i saw my final grade it said a C. i took it as a creative arts course and i'm really regretting that i took this class. i should have taken theater 109
Still an easy class, dunno what the rest of these people are talking about. (As of Spring 09, I just finished)
awesome class. awesome teacher. just go and you'll be fine
EASIEST class I've EVER taken at UIC. Take his class if you can! I use to study for the exams an hr beforehand and passed them with flying colors.
someone would actually have to TRY to get less than an A in this class. easiest class and he was the BEST professor ever.

He is honestly one of the best teachers I've had at UIC so far. He's VERY nice and cares about your grades and your money that he chooses to use the cheapest music book for his class. This class isn't that hard, but it helps if you have some music background.
Easy class. Don't even need to buy the book as long as you attend all the lectures and take notes. Do a half hour of studying the morning of the exam and you will be fine.
very easy class. As long as you take notes, and study a little before the exam you'll be fine. It's hard to understand him sometimes tho, but he's a good guy. He wants you to get an A.

There's a reason Hai Tao's Music 107 sections fill up so fast: he's the best. His exams and quizzes are not difficult if you study, and he's always willing to answer questions. He's also very understanding and willing to help out. Take Hai Tao's Mus 107 for humanities credit. It requires minimal studying and one very easy paper.
he's teh BESTESTESTEST of all teachers. no matter how crappy your papers are.. he'll give u an A. Ask him a question during an exam and he'll tell u the answer. take it
This is a pretty easy class. the professor is very understanding/laid back. you only have to study one hour tops before each test.
No class will ever fill up as fast as his because he gives A's accross the board.

He is a pretty good teacher. The material is not the easiest to do, but I thought he did a good job of presenting it. The book in my opinion just confuses people. Tests were fair although I never finished early. He sets barely enough time. Has a pretty big curve so getting an A shouldn't be too hard.

The material is not as much hard as it is time consuming, I think if everyone is willing to make the commitment I think they'll do well. That being said I barely did anything because I found the reading dry but problems fun, then it became kind of tedious and boring. He's ok,doesnt really explain well, but easy pass/fail class.Lil effort thats it.
This class was very difficult. The professor is highly intelligent and I think he forgets that not everyone is that smart while he's teaching.
class was interesting but hard. Materials were a bit hard to interpret and he was confusing in his explanations.
He is very enthusiastic and wants the students to participate. However, he has a hard time explaining things so that they are sufficiently understood.

I don't even know why people will think this class is hard as long as you try to do the homework and then attend the discussion section and the TA's will explain how to solve the problems.  Just follow the rules and get A in that class.  Big curve because alot of people get low grades on tests which I don't understand why.

People who think his class is hard probably didn't read the book. You can skip lecture, but it is absolutely essential that you READ THE TEXTBOOK. Its written in a way that makes it easy to learn. Other logic classes use a different book, and it's 10x harder. Understanding Symbolic Logic by Klenk is the one we had. It gets real hard the last unit.

Hardest class ever!!! I looked up what people had to say about him before I enrolled but I took it anyway...please don't.  Finals are next week and he still doesnt know how big of a curve is going to be.  The average score on tests is a low D.  He tries his best at the material but teaches it too fast.  Homework was graded very harshly.

On the first day he makes it clear that you have to KEEP UP! and its so true. Its a hard class and its essential to read the textbook. Make sure you have the current one too because I had the older one and some hw questions were different. The TA's do take off for EVERYTHING... I had Kamron... he was OK.

Try to avoid Hylton's class his TA's are such hard graders most of the time you don't get any partial credit for your work. I wish I took this class pass/fail. If you think that you know everything for an A, on exams you will get B or C
i loved this class. follow the book go to lecture and discussions when you need clearing up from the book

Ridiculously easy class.  Got an A and attended class less than 1/3 of the time.  Homeword every week, but it doesn't take long.  If you don't attend class much, watch out for quizzes given in section on occasion.
I thought Hylton was really cool.  The material is difficult, but he does his best to explain things.  The exams represent exactly what he teachesin class.
this guy totally made me love logic. he even conducts study groups before tests, so helpful. and when you get something right, he says "brilliant" or "elegant" in his british accent! haha.

The class is hard, but the professor is very much interested in helping his students succeed. Unfortunately, several of my classmates seem to want to talk in class and ignore the instructor and then get bent out of shape if asked to be quiet and pay attention...not a blow-off class.

Very hard class, and even harder material.  But sincerely doesn't want to fail anyone, I practically did, talked to him and he is giving me an incomplete, instead of an F, most teacher's aren't as generous.
He knows the material, and getting useful feedback is a matter of knowing what you want to ask and being clear about it. The class IS hard, but some of these ratings just sound like sour grapes...
Sometimes difficult to understand what he's trying to get across, but he does seem to try and truly wants students to succeed.
he teaches himself- not to the class and makes people who ask questions feel like complete idiots.  Not a very nice man at all.

While passionate, Professor Kennedy is not a good stats teacher. They spend way too much time on the most basic things such as mean, median, and mean while when it comes to heavier topics they rush through. They are not a clear explainer, yet give a test once a week. The class is  reading from slides with very little actual examples and support.
Thanks to my TA, the labs were great and very short, and I could understand the class material well. I dreaded the lectures, they started extremely easy to understand, and rapidly took a turn south.

The lectures were fine but most of my knowledge came from the TA-run labs. As a matter of fact, the TAs really carried this class for me. No shade to the professor I just feel as if their presentations were hard to pay attention to and we didn't have much of a personal connection despite being a relatively small class. Still easy and kind! Take it!

Pretty easy stats class as long as you attend class and lab. I feel like I learn better in Lab, but that's probably because I do not like stats and hearing about it in a lecture setting is boring to me. Theres a quiz every week, if you make sure to understand the material before class you will be fine in the class.
Ian was very supportive and made sure we understood by using outside perspectives.

OMG I LOVED THIS PROFESSOR. I hate statistics, but he did such an amazing job at teaching SOC 201. In hs I always failed with statistics, but with him I passed the class with a B which was amazing. Just DO THE HOMEWORK, it is the same as the tests, it will help you sooooo much.
solid prof, easy going, and straight forward. Prolly da easiest A tech elective fr fr. shoutout Kash-Moneyyy
he's alright I guess
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The grading is criteria is built clearly, but  everything else including the lectures have no substance. He has a severe stutter and frequently goes on tangents. The assignments and lectures are hardly related, you'll have to learn everything from books or Youtube.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easy A class. No exams, graded based on 5 quizzes and weekly HW assignments. Workload is reasonable, straightforward path to getting a good grade, but programming assignments can be difficult. Extra credit is given through doing grad assignments if undergrad.
Easy A class

Professor Kash is chill and the lectures are interesting and pertain to real life economic problems in tech. The grading is fair and forgiving. There are no tests except the final which you don't have to take if you are happy with your grade.

Note that this class is not about building trading algo's, it's about auction theory, equilibrium, etc.
(for CS 411) Chill professor. Homework isn't always related to content in lecture, lectures are also super ambiguous.
Assignments were super ambiguous. Mostly unrelated to lectures and hard to verify. Vague grading criteria

I took Economics and computation with him. Very interesting topics throughout the course, but his way of teaching is just not for me. His lectures are confusing and he explains as if the students already know everything. Very few examples throughout the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Really thorough professor but was not a stickler. He was extremely knowledgeable and made the class interesting. Somewhat monotone but overall a really nice guy who often gave students second chances. Saw potential in everyone even if they were in a crummy situation. Definitely would recommend him!

Prof Tobasco teaches this class like a higher level math class, trying to 'prove' all the equations which eats up time and confuses the class. I appreciate the sentiment of understanding over application, but for the amount of material in the class, we don't have the time for a deep dive on everything. Please just outline theory then do examples.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Good professor that very obviously knows what he is doing. HW is group based and heavy on the proofs, so pay attention in class. Tests were given as an oral exam through Zoom due to CoViD, they were based on our understanding of the material, i.e. proving how a concept in class works mathematically. Study and attend class, and you will be fine.

I took his course Spring 2020. If you go to class, follow his slides, and start early you will be fine. Do not be afraid to ask for help. Bad reviews are by those who do not try. Put in effort and he will help. He actually saw 2 major bugs in 2 seconds when I went to him and laughed saying he loves compilers for this reason. Rewards good students.

reviews.comment: TOXIC CLASS, UNREALISTIC PROJ
Ruthless and uncaring

reviews.comment: Professor Hummel is the best prof at UIC. He is tough for sure. In his class, you need to do a lot of homework and project. But, you can learn well from that material. If you just want to pass class, do not choose him. If you want to learn, He is the best choice. He will let you know what is in pain and happy
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: He's obviously a very smart guy and a good teacher. I think with him, he's done with the students ****. There are a lot of lazy people and it seems like he deals with a lot of them. The material is very interesting and the projects are very fun actually. The exams are pretty hard but fair. There is a whole project worth of extra credit (4-5% ish).

Professor Hummel, though some criticize his sometimes-scathing message board answers, is a fantastic lecturer. The two courses I've taken under him, 141 and 251, were difficult, outright extreme at times, but always manageable for the most part. His lectures are extremely helpful in teaching the required material and actually helping me grow in CS.
How can someone like this can be a professor he should be in army

He gives you a hammer and expects you to build a house with it. You have to learn everything yourself and probably ask for help when debugging your crap code. This is the first weed out class for those who want to do Computer Science. The next one is CS 251 good luck!

I recommend future cs students to never take his class even if you have to wait a semester. He is rude arrogant, and Ive never said that for a professor. He will humiliate you for asking a question and it feels like forcing him to do his job. I learn a lot more from other resources than I have from him and have seen better professors.

A lot of people say Prof. Hummel is mean and uncaring, but I think it's more of a 'tough love'. Some of the work can get hard because CS 141 is a weed-out class, but it isn't the teacher's fault. This is just what Computer Science looks like. If CS is your thing, then this class shouldn't be a problem for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: BEWARE!!! This is a weed-out class. If you decide to take this professor for whatever reason, get ready to lose sleep, patience, and motivation. His teaching style is similar to the phrase, "Here is a hammer, go build a house". Currently working on a project where only 15% of the 250 students submitted something, and most of them were below 60%.

Good professional in software engineering field but bad Teaching Professor. Demands a lot from students while provides almost to none. Be prepared to spend all your time on projects and get 0 for efforts. Best of luck

Never take any class with this Prof. Hes extremely rude and doesnt know how to teach. If you have to take him, get ready to quit your work, kids and dont have any social life. Hes grading policies are rough, either 100 or 0. No partial credit. Projects, hw, labs takes days to finish. Only feed back you will get is that you are wrong and stupid.
Never listens to any reason and is very bad while talking and understanding things

reviews.comment: No way see this professor again

Great professor, terrible person. He won't try to understand your problems or reasons why you didn't do anything. He behaves like hysterical, disrespectful person. The way he answers your questions is awful. Well-structured lectures, interesting projects but would never take him again. Working experience with J.H was disgusting. Bad personality.

easy to follow lectures, project heavy you definitely need to start those as soon as you can. really active piazza page but i hated how rude he can be when answering questions, makes you feel stupid for asking them. just bc content comes easy for some, doesnt mean it comes easily to all. overall he was okay, work for your grade

Rule 1 for Hummel: don't Chegg (or cheat) it. He cares about his students; if you complete ALL labs, Zybooks, & projects, his tough tests won't destroy your grade (so don't freak out). Utilize all his resources & you WILL pass - an A IS possible. (PS: he can be hilariously blunt and unfiltered in responses: expect honesty before sympathy.)

This class was one of my favorites this semester. People say the projects are hard and while it's true, the professor gives a generous deadline. There is however, a lot of work involved. Early in the semester there will be Zybooks readings along with homework and projects are due biweekly. You can get an A but you're going to hae to work for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The class structure is:biweekly projects followed by exams(1 week exam/1 week projects). The exams are fair(except MC because MC makes brain to brrrr) and the projects are all doable if you manage time well. I feel that his deadlines are very generous as well. Note that this class is very project heavy and you need to work decently hard to get an A
Good luck guys
Worst professor, doesn't know how to teach or explain. He doesn't know how to teach or how to explain to the students. You have to be too genius.
To be honest, be prepared, class really hard and he gives u a lot of things to do.
Great professor. The class is easy to manage if you stay on top of lectures, go to OH, and start the projects super early.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: I thought he would be great since he's some Head of the CS department. The worst time I had. I learned nothing in class. It was just completing projects and no learning whatsoever. He is way overrated.

Really good professor made it easy to understand data structures. Was helpful in office hours and would go over many ways in class to solve his coding projects. People who are mad were just lazy and asking questions gone over lecture. Wish we did not have the pandemic would have gotten a week on heaps.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Easy A. Data structure is supposed to be a hard class, but his material is too easy. I have to study by myself in summer to learn useful things. Also, he is strict and weird, you have to do whatever he says. He also can get mad easily.
This class should be renamed to Data Structure. All we did was trees. Expects you to know CS301 things beforehand.

Hummel  code god. If you can stay on top of your work and start projects early, this class is manageable. The projects are indeed hard as is the class as a whole, but if you put in the work you will succeed. This class will not be a weed out if you are actually putting in the work to get a passing grade. Don't let the other reviews fool you.

Great teacher, knows his concepts very well and is always on piazza to help. Literally if you pay attention and do the homework and projects, you can be guaranteed at least B in the class. Also teacher gives extra credit and tries to help confused students
It's his way or the highway. And he always seems to get mad at students who ask questions he doesn't like.

He knows the material well, but good do a better job of teaching it. Loves trees so much that he kept talking about it for weeks so we didn't spend much time on graphs, and basically rushed through minheaps. Projects are not that hard if you start relatively on time. Exams are a bit hard, requires writing code on paper. May take him again.
Just cuz he reduced the syllabus and removed the mathematics from it doesn't imply that it makes him a great teacher. Exploiting his power as head of CS. Avoid him at all costs...

Great professor. He explains the concepts very simply and clearly. I learned a lot from his projects and assignments. The only downside might be that he spent a lot of time on trees, and the last week we ended up rushing through minheap. Everything else was great.
wants everything his way. inhibits creative thinking and is not regular with his own work; projects, labs and homeworks are released pretty late.

Very knowledgable in Data Structures and offers many in class examples to help us with the projects. Exams on the other hand are very difficult and is a very hard grader if he doesn't like your approach. If you've done Data Structures before you may handle it well other than that, be prepared for an excruciating class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: he sorta simplifies things in class which can help y'all get an easy A and it could ruin the most career-defining class for y'all. it was the latter for me as i did not learn anything that should've been taught in an academic setting.

this review is for cs 251, In the data structure field he is the best the UIC can offer right now, i wish that he teachers 341 and 342 in spring 2020. by far the best prof and dale reed for 141 is also good.
He is a very nice professor, lectures are amazing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Hummel is probably the best 102 teacher at UIUC. He makes the transition from high school chem to college chem very smooth. He curves every test, and is accessible outside class. CHEM 102 will be a lot easier if you have Hummel.

He does MWF classes, with small coding assignments throughout the week. This worked great for me; revisiting the material so frequently kept it fresh in my head. If you do the small coding assignments, the projects become very feasible. It's an easy class, and you gain exposure to different programming languages. Lastly, he's super-friendly.
Though ticky Tom might be intimidating, his lectures are great since it addresses chemistry concepts very clearly and he's very helpful whenever I email him asking for questions.

Professor Hummel has got to be the best CS professor I've had so far. He is extremely active on Piazza and will respond to every single post. There are projects that are somewhat challenging but he probably went over techniques during the lecture which can help you derive solutions to the projects. He made the entire course practical and enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Even though I'm not a CS major, I had to take his class to fulfill my engineering requirements, I can tell that it was A LOT OF WORK. Hw due EVERY Monday and Wednesday, and Projects and Labs due EVERY WEEK. Only take this class if it's utterly necessary.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Honestly wanted to say something bad about him since I'm not exactly happy with my grade, but there is nothing. He is an amazing professor if you want to learn. Will answer questions at 3 am. Lots of assignments, but all very doable. Exams can be hard if you don't pay attention.
This man is hilarious and is very good at what he does.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: A very great and knowledgeable professor. He is direct to the point, which may put some people off but he only means to help the student understand the subject. A lot of work but it's doable and helps you understand the material. Despite some allegations of him being arrogant, I found him very approachable. Definitely recommend to anyone taking CS.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He gives amazing lectures and there's clickers in class. You have to put in a lot of effort into his projects because they're actually a bit tough and worth a big percentage of the grade. Exams are hard if you do not take the projects seriously and stay on top of the material. Overall, he is extremely helpful and wants his students to do good.
Very knowledgeable---wouldn't take his class again,, very respected-)

One of the best professors Ive ever had! Hes NOT arrogant, hes just cutthroat because a lot of students are unwilling to think and dont read the handouts he posts which explain in detail. A lot of projects, but interesting and hes upfront that there is a project every week. Didnt make us go to lab after the first month. Hes really engaging
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The best professor! Highly recommended, he can explain difficult stuff in the most easy way! I would take all classes with him if I could. I've learnt a ton in his classes and increased my love to computer science thanks to him. Lectures are well organized and prepared. Answers in a quickest way.

Proffessor Hummel is a very good teacher, but his tests are hard. He is known by students as "Tricky Tom" because he likes to test the exceptions of common chemistry rules. Funny guy, very approachable. If you are willing to put in the work you should do fine in his class. He prepares you well if you need to take more than one semester of chem.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: A god among professors. Gives challenging yet doable assignments. You will learn a lot from lectures, and he makes sure to answer every question on Piazza. Truly cares about his students, and is a very fair grader. Highly recommended.
Even if you know nothing about programming going  into this class you will be fine.

About as good as it gets when it comes to professors. Sometimes up until 2am answering emails with homework questions, always willing to help students, goes above and beyond. Course is tough, if you dont study and work for it you wont get a good grade. DO NOT FALL BEHIND as class moves fast and will be very difficult to catch up. Would take again.
As far as professors go, he's as good as it gets. He's very helpful and available at all times. The class itself is also very easy. Do all the homework and reviews and you'll get an A.
If you actually do every assignment and the reviews should be a pretty easy A

Great guy. About the best you'll get. *very* organized. No ambiguity. Lectures are very on point, engaging and helpful. Grading is very fair and not based on ridiculous things. Grading is also spread out among many assignments.

Very good professor. Lectures are clear and concise. He hands out printouts of the lecture slides so there is very little need to take notes. Tests were straightforward.  Final project felt like a waste of time, though, and the presentations occupied the final week of class, which was time that would have been better spent as final exam review.

Had him for 341 and 301.  301 is more theory side of cs but none of the less Hummel  broke down tough concepts and made it easier to learn.  Lectures were never boring.  Recommend him for any class he teaches.
The tests are very difficult but he grades with a curve

Hummel is by far the best professor ever. His lectures are helpful, the homework is challenging, but engaging. He dedicates so much time to helping his students. He'd be online at 3 am answering students' questions. I hated programming going into this, and now I'm majoring in it. The class is a great intro to programming and it's actually kinda fun
Programming seems very difficult but the professor really makes the course interesting. Plus if you get a good TA, then life is good.

Short and sweet powerpoint notes makes for easy to follow lectures. More time spent listening. Great lecturer, interesting topics. Uses clickers for class participation (required). Plentiful homework, quizzes, tests which are meant to help you learn things you will need in your future career, NOT to make your life harder. Hoping he teaches more.

Professor Hummel is probably one of the best the Prof's I've had at UIC. His lectures are clear concise and very engaging. His projects aren't hard and tests and quizzes are pretty easy. As long as you do everything in a timely manner you should be fine.

One of the best in the dept. I learned more from him than I did from any other professor in CS. Knows how to get students pumped to learn a topic bc he includes real life application to his lecture and HW. Clicker quizzes in class. Prints his lecture slides for the whole class. Interesting projects F#,C#,C++11,SQL,LINQ. Brought snacks  for class !
Very great lecturer.  The way he teaches is not traditional, the students actually participates but i learned more from it.  Homework is do-able and not hard.

will try to humiliate you in class if you ask for help or simple questions. not helpful. will try to avoid you if you are trying to contact him. had three friends take him at different schools all had the same experience. He does not like teaching. Gives really annoying and tedious projects. DO NOT TAKE HIM.

This guy is hands down the best professor I've ever had. He not only is one hell of a presenter/lecturer, but he makes it so easy for you to learn. He prints out his slides, no need to take notes, just listen to the man teach. Extremely organized and definitely is one of UIC's best! Brings positivity to the classroom which is underappreciated.

Just like any other (CS) professor at UIC. Teaches what is relevant to his research. Has a condescending, "better-than-you" attitude. Grading isn't consistent. YMMV. Plus side: lecture slide handouts, lecture content is relevant to assignments. Quizzes are fair. Definitely attend lecture.
Great Teacher, very clear in explanation. Really cares about the students and does what he can to help you out. Does a great job explaining programming concepts to those new to programing.

Lecture is always engaging and entertaining. Learned programming paradigms and how theyre implemented in different programming languages and why. Great speaker. Final exam was to pick a topic you enjoy that we havent discussed and demo it. Only about 12 people had the chance to present and if you put in reasonable effort, you got a 100.

Professor Hummel explains very well and I was easily able to learn C++/C and MATLAB without much problem. His homework and quizzes were relevant to what we were learning and really helped us to understand what we went over in lecture. One of the best professors I've ever had

Aside from being very knowledgeable in his field, Hummel is a very experienced lecturer, making his lectures crystal clear and very easy to follow. I learned a lot from his class and he is one of the best professors I have ever had.

Great professor. He was very clear to understand in lecture and made an effort to be sure everyone was following. Sometimes the pace seemed a bit slow.. but based on some of the Q's from the class, it was probably necessary. Assignments were engaging and the final project was fun.

I can go on to say that Prof. Hummel went too far in making programming easy. I can only recall one homework that demanded some brain effort, but two good afternoon sessions were good to completely solve the homework. But you do your work, on time, and you will learn. No question about it.

Great Professor. This class is all theory. Allowed us to choose between a program in C++/Java or take the final exam. The course is an extremely easy course at the beginning. It starts to get hard after the 2nd midterm though. If you attend every lecture/discussion, you'll be fine.

The material is tough but he is very helpful and makes it a bit easier. HW is tough just make sure you dont wait till last minute to due it.( you wont finish). 2 Midterm both fair. No final, instead theres a final project and that was really easy. Great Professor overall.

Best professor I've had at UIC. Truly knows how to teach, and makes a difficult subject like computer science easy to learn and appreciate. Really cares about students, and is very clear in his lectures. Lenient grader as well. Most of the grade consists of programming homework assignments, as well as minor quizzes and two exams. Overall great man.
He teaches well and the HW is helpful for learning C++ and MATLAB.  The final is a project that was not too hard and kinda fun.  He knows what he's talking about, which is nice.

Very enthusiastic n very helpful during his office hours.C++ is hard but he makes it a lot easier.Online HW(codelabs)were very helpful in understanding the basics of C++.Quizzes weren't bad,mostly on the covered stuff from HW.Exams were fair,but programming assignments were kind of tough,but you can always ask for help.No final exam,just a project.

Prof Hummel is an Awesome professor. He really cares for his students and really tries to help you all he can. He has quizes daily which helped me understand C++ alot better and kept me focused in class. Programming excercises are a bit difficult and take some time though but if you work with a friend you will be fine. Take him!! Final is Project!

Very easy class!!! The only assignments that he has you do is 4 page papers every two weeks. You also have disscusions post after every class so you do have to pay attention. But the papers are creative writing so you can write anything you please.

Can get a little boring since it's 2.5 hrs but he does a good job of discussing various fascinating topics & keeping you engaged. You'll do well if you actually find the material interesting. Articles assigned can be lengthy. 4 pg double spaced journal entries every 2 weeks, but he allows a lot of freedom & creativity. Ask q's during lecture!!

Took his class Freshman year and found it to be pretty interesting. He's extremely knowledgeable and has a lot of experience in the field. BUT he does not use power points during his lectures, so if you don't prefer to take notes in class or do not pay attention in general, you can't expect to pass the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Ibarra was great. His lectures were always interesting. You have to take notes for this class.  He doesn't actually write notes down, so as he's speaking you have to write your own notes which I know isn't easy for everyone.  The tests were fairly easy and the review sessions were always helpful.

Lectures off his own notes based on assigned readings. Lectures were boring, but the material was important to note as it would be on two short answer exams. Final paper was 8-10 pages. TA could be a tough grader on exams and final paper. Grading was not fair as it was only two exams and a final paper. Expect a C on average in this class.
He honestly is a good professor, he is very proper and obviously if you are not raising your hand he does not know what you are thinking. he did very good at teaching, i loved going to his class

Tough but fair professor for sure. Attend all lectures and take notes on his lectures! 2 exams and one paper, but very interesting topics. If you tend to not go to class absolutely do not take this class, no notes online! If you enjoy the topic, it is a must take!

i honestly do not know what to think yet.... i am about to go take his midterm and we barely had any class notes and the study guide is so general... all we have to study from is 2 readings... ill try to come back and comment again after the test and tell you how i feel about this guy....
he is one of those instructors that you want to stay away from, he tests on the things not covered in class, he mumbles during class, highly not recommended
good class for CLJ majors and people interested in issues that permeate society

he tests you on things that are barely even talked about and the tests are worded funny. he goes off on useless tangents and the review for midterms (2) doesnt help much. books are "mandatory" but they are barely even talked about it. dont take him if you dont have to.

Not sure what the other recent comment is about. It is well-written, but it's just off.  "Modern day applications towards race and ethnicity" are meaningless and hard to understand without knowing the history. And regarding "professors that are more experienced," this is just uninformed.  A class covering eye-opening material, a must take for all!

He has a poor attitude, is unable to relate to students in a manner that is conducive to their learning the material, and is generally out of touch with modern day applications towards race and ethnicity. I would recommend taking alternative courses similar in nature with professors that are more experienced and better adapted to the classroom.

Tough but fair professor. attendance is 10% of the final grade. 3 exams including final. all multiple choice exam and one 30% research paper. If he offers extra credit, I suggest that you do it. The extra credit helped me get one higher grade. Overall, fair professor.
Far too fast paced with extraneous work that did not increase knowledge or comprehension
Love her. Amazing lectures and very laid back when it comes to deadlines and grading.
Best marketing professor I've had. Super nice!

Very nice and caring professor. She communicates well and explains things in detail. She makes sure everyone does well in her class by providing multiple extra credits. No tests, just online quizzes. A lot of hands on simulations that will help you gain real life marketing experience. Take any class she offers, she is amazing.

Such a caring professor. There are no tests, just a few quizzes, which are online during class. We did some group work and some online simulations, which were actually fun. Easy grader too. The class is pretty hands on and she is always accessible outside of class. She cares about the students and appreciates class participation. Def recommend her!
Great professor!A very complex topic. A lot of interaction during her class.
Lots of Hands on Activities.. Really learns in class. All topics are very relevant in the current field and useful for future
Professor Ibrahim provided many career oriented in-class activities that were very hands-on that helped me get a certification.
Very knowledgeable on the subject.. Interesting hands on activities in class. Training on digital tools which are key to future careers.
Hands on activities in class. Not lecture heavy. We really learn by doing..
Helps apply in practice all what we learn. Gives emphasis on hands on practice and enables to achieve Industry certifications

tons of homework, lots of reading, very stick on grading criteria, deep down everything, heavy project and too many assignments. You must take at least than 2-3 hours for each assignment, the maximum like a hold day for one assignment!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Focuses on Class Participation. We do real time projects. Enables us to get industry specific certifications as assignments. This is extremely helpful in job market.

Very hard to understand sometimes. Assignment instructions are very unclear. Quizzes are on blackboard, but during class and the questions are very specific. Group projects. She loves in-class participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Grades too strictly, taking account most of what we focus on in class isn't even on test. Had a hard time distinguishing from a literature class and a history of Spain class. Boring, save yourself trouble and take another professor.

Her pace is TOO FAST and her grading too strict.  You'd be better off teaching it to yourself.  She needs to understand quality, not quantity.  Flying through pages strict grading is not on the 101 level.  I wish I could take a different teacher;  I feel overwhelmed.

Grades everything super difficult. Actually takes off punctuality points if you're nut fully prepared but she can arrive 5 minutes late half the time. Class is never entertaining. So if you want a teacher that grades very hard then by all means sign up.

I feel that she forgets that this class is for non-native speakers. I did very well in class yet she picks on me and ignores my e-mails asking for help. She's not as helpful as she should be and personally she makes me not want to go to class because of her. I honestly learn better on my own than how she teaches. Take someone else
I Liked Idoia, she was Helpful and pretty clear, sometimes classes were rushed but she was always available for tutoring help and emailed back within 24 hours. Close to an A but gave me a B :(

I took 103 over the summer and while the 8-week class was rather rushed, I'm sure not too many people got A's in the class because only three exams were given that all averaged in the 70% range, well below what would have been received should I have taken it during the fall/spring. I was so close to an A yet she gave me a B. I doubt many got an A.
Professor Martinez-del Mozo is laid back and very helpful
Although I do not like spanish as a class, Idoia made it tolerable. She is very approachable and will try to help you if you ask for it. I enjoyed her lax teaching style!

THIS CLASS IS PRETTY LAID BACK. AND EVEN THOUGH SHE IS A COOL TEACHER, SHE DOES GRADE QUITE HARD ON ROUGH DRAFTS. HOWEVER, MAKE CORRECTIONS SHE HAS RECOMMENDED AND YOUR FINAL DRAFT GRADE WILL BE SIGNIFICANTLY HIGHER. I EXPECTED A C AND GOT A B.GOOD TEACHER.

Wow, I did HORRIBLE on the exams and still got a C. That just shows you how nice she is, and how important hw & attendance are because that's what saved me from a D lol. I was actually able to learn alot from this course unlike my other span courses. She's an awesome Spanish prof. Extremely helpful/nice, and she's pretty attractive too hehe.

I had her over the summer semester and she was very helpful in increasing my interest as well as my knowledge of spanish. I think she was a great teacher that was on task and easy to talk to for help. She is willing to help you understand spanish. I was a little worried about the course because of the writing, she helped me improve it and my gramma
I was completely lost in this class. I felt as if she expected us to already know it. She didn't make sure we understand what was going on. Not helpful at all~

He's a funny guy and super smart. He loves theory and explains a lot of background of math problems. He does write ALOT but compared to all the math 180 teachers, he is one of the best. The math department is super competitive and you really need to know your stuff to get a good grade. That means a lot of out of class work is required to do well.
- Knows math real good, but horrible job presenting and explaining basic simple concepts.   Overall, most of the time the textbook does a better job explaining than he does.

He is a smart guy but doesn't teach very well.  He is all about theory and not about practice and examples.  He'll write a novel worth of information on the board, but it's worthless when it comes to the test.  He rarely does examples, and when he does, he doesn't finish them because he says the math is trivial. Stay away from him.

Try to avoid if possible. Very smart man, but does not have the slightest idea how to teach. He literally makes you write paragraphs as notes. Not enough examples. If you have to take him, make sure you know how to teach yourself.
Iddo is a smart man who knows his stuff. If you put in the effort it's a good class, but he does not do enough examples so be prepared to do A LOT of outside work to get a good grade.

First of all he isn't completely a professor yet. He is a Advanced graduate student! All he does his copy and pastes quotes on power points and that's how he teaches! He is pompous, and arrogant! What he says goes, that's his motto! I despise this class! Be warned if you take this "professor". If I could go back I would of dropped this class!

slides are text copied and pasted, NOT helpful, especially since they are not on blackboard. if u take him, buy a recorder.the paper writing process will make u feel like ur 2 and not capable of writing a good paper w/ ur own style/judgement. asks for honesty (like if you finished readings)only 2 hold it against you. entertaining, but it gets old.

You definitely have to keep up on the readings with him. And also be able to differentiate between what the textbook says and what he believes because he will test you over both. Nice to look at too :)

His pedagogic skills are low. His exams are ambiguous and his classes are a waste of time, although mandatory.  Better of study with the TA?s who are more helpful and much nicer. Don?t take his class because you will regret it.
don't take his class. you'll regret!

Material was interesting. He encouraged student participation and critical analysis of material. Seemed interested in students viewpoints, but some times dismissed student comments as unimportant.
