reviews.comment: He is an alright TA. If you participate often and do your homework you'll pass.  It's an easy discussion class just sit near the front to hear better. He does mumble a little and sometimes he seems nervous to teach but he is interested in the topic and wants everyone to participate. Come to class as much as you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I had Patrick as my TA for this class. He was very helpful and clarified assigned readings that we had. I never needed to read the assignments because he went over them so thoroughly. TA sessions were mandatory unless you want to drop down a letter grade after missing 3 classes.

He does not normally teach this course, he took over for another professor. That being said he is a very fair grader, and we had only a few assignments. No exams, and no textbooks all readings were online. This was a discussion course, he barely lectured. Attendance is worth 40% and is mandatory. Easy A

He is boring. Attendance is crucial because everything that is on the exams he has gone over in lecture. Definitely did not increase my interest in this course. I've had a better Anthropology professor than him. I guess he's okay. Exams are tricky so review your notes carefully and attend EVERY lecture.

Lots of reading for this class. If you skim through the book, articles, and read ALL of the notes, you will get a B at least. Most don't buy the Peoples book and get Cs or Ds on exams (class average: 78%). Project was not as difficult as it's made out to be. Professor Knight rambles on quite often; he does not give much time to type out the notes.
He's a pretty nice guy and going to his discussion sections help when writing the response sets :) Sometimes though I must admit the class can be boring, but that's when no one talks.
best ever.
Take HIM. AMAZING CLASS, I learned so much about cultural anthropology, made me almost consider being an anthro major:. I really enjoyed this class. Very good professor.

Class is fairly easy. Papers are not a challenge, and pop quizzes are easy as long as you do the weekly readings. Be sure to take notes and read the textbook for tests and you'll be fine. The life story interview is incredibly time consuming, but pretty easy overall; just be sure you don't wait until the last minute to do it.

This class is super easy. Knight is a cool guy but he mumbles a lot, sit in the front if you want to hear him. 2 tests, a couple 5 question quizzes during discussion, 2 papers. Life story interview is time-consuming but that's the hardest thing. Take this if you want an easy gen-ed.

go to lecture, take notes on his slides and pay attention to what he says that's not on the notes, and you will do well! he's very good at responding to e-mails if you need help and he's kinda a funny guy! major interest in this subject now, he knows his stuff.

I took anthropology 101 with Knight. He is obviously very passionate about what he does, which is nice. But he mumbles quite a lot and most people don't really know what he's saying. The class is SUPER EASY though. Only 2 tests, 2 papers, and one big project. Tests are pretty much common sense- I didn't even crack open my book and got an 86.

Professor Knight provides a very well planned lecture with good, easy to follow Powerpoints. Go to class, listen and take notes of the Power Points, (I wish he would have posted them on BB) and you'll do good on the exams. He provided a study guide before the exams that helped a good deal. The Life Story Interview is long, but very rewarding to do.

Took the same course over the summer...must say I was pleasantly surprised.  The teacher and TA are passionate about anthropology and are good at sharing it with others. My guess is that the other reviewer didn't attend lecture/discussion or was looking for a super-easy course (it's about average).

I took this class over the summer. It is the worst class I've ever taken. It's so boring and both him and the TA like to talk a lot. It's a lot of reading, but not that many assignments. The project is really long though. He also tends to mumble a lot
Very interesting lectures.

I took the course two semesters ago. Professor Knight responded quickly to my emails and was very helpful.  The course was tough at times but if you keep up with the readings, attend lecture, and do the work you should be fine. Also, it's clear he curved the course that semester, so he's fair.  I have a more interest in anthropology now.
This class is pretty simple. Lectures aren't mandatory but they do help even though he mumbles quite a lot.
I took his class last fall and let me just say I'm glad I took it pass/fail. Too much work for 100 level class and the guy's lectures are boring and confusing.

I had an interest in Anthropology until I took this class.  Mr. Knight's lectures did nothing but confuse me.  He really seems to like the sound of his own voice and I'm sure his lectures make sense to himself--but not to the rest of us who thought we we taking a 101 course.  Also, the work load is way too much.  Don't take this class.

This class requires that you put a lot of effort into it. You should really show up for his lectures and try to absorb as much as possible and take very good notes. It was a very challenging yet interesting class that will definitely not appeal to slackers or those looking for an easy A. Also, he is HOTT HOTT HOTT
Don't take this class if you don't have to. I'm glad I took it pass/fail because it's too much work and whenever I asked for his help, his explanations left me confused even more.

First of all, he is not a professor; he's a grad student. Second, he made this semester notoriously difficult. He probably came on here and read the comments saying he's easy. There were 4 papers and the topics were not only ambiguous but sometimes irrelevant. The directions for the project were unclear. This class is not an easy A. And he's hot.

Do not take this class unless it is a requirement.  This fall semester he gave out 4 2pg papers, quizzes on multiple readings, Mid-term and Final exams, and an interview project.  Take something else for your cultural diversity requirement .  He made a topic even more boring than it already is.

This has been the most interesting class I have taken in my college career thus far. Professor Knight's lectures are extremely thought provoking and challenge you to think outside the box. I disagree with all of the negative comments posted and think that most of you are afraid to be challeneged to think in different ways.

he was a great teacher, granted he had this monotone voice during lectures, but i've never seen a teacher so excited to teach about a subject before. i loved his enthusiasm about the topic, it's what made me do so well. the class isn't hard; go to lecture, take notes, pay attention and you'll do well.

Professor Knight was an amazing professor! He makes anthropology interesting! You just have to attend lecture and read the book and you will do fine on the exams! ..plus it doesn't hurt that he's good to look at!

I really dislike this guy. He's kind of pompous and acts like we 're all ignorant. He says "once again" every few seconds and it's really obnoxious. That being said the class is pretty easy. I liked most of the readings, and my TA (Meierhoff) was really awesome. But if you aren't interested in this, take something else for cultural diversity.

He does have a monotone voice. His tests can be difficult if you dont go to lecture.  the bad things about him is that he doesnt give out any sort of review before a test. the project was pretty easy. However, this class is NOT a blow off class

Nice guy Easy class exams can be tricky but are not hard compared to most other classes. There is some reading but it is kind of interesting. Just keep up with the reading its not alot but it tends to accumulate because you really dont have to studdy until a few days before the exam
Definitely an interesting/weird/quirky person. Young, too, so he's able to bring up some interesting examples. Overall I really enjoyed this professor.
good class. paul bick was an AWESOME TA

Great professor! Lecs are kinda dull yet interesting and sometimes funny. Easy A if u work for it (only 2 exams,2 papers,and 4 quizs). His lecs notes are important. U dont have to read very word from the book; just understand the main points. His TAs are easy on the papers. Prof/TAs were really nice and helpful. Learned alot from this great class!!

go to lecture and discussion super easy A.  use your braing and a little sense and you got yourself a great class.  lecture is a bit dry, but helpful.  gives great base for further education.  keep it up.

His lecutres are boring!  You dont need to go, just read the book chapters, you only have 2 projects and they are not hard.  The midterm was hard (but I didnt study, and I only go to lecture on Tuesday).  I emalied him and he helped me, but Paul Bick is an awesome TA, make sure you get him.

This class is sooo boring. The prof. does not know how to teach. The stutters and really does not know how to handle his class. He will not help you if you have a question. He does not answer questions that students may have. Even if he sends an email through blackboard he will tell the students not to reply to the email but to ask the TA. Dont tak

If you go to class and take notes you should be fine. Look over main points in the book to help you study for tests. Discussion section attendance is a must, there are several easy quizzes to boost your grade. I feel he needs to have a better handle of his class to keep the lecture hall quiet. Try not to get lost in his eyes...
He's a rock star in my book!
he is generally a good professor. make sure to go to lectures and study for tests. not exactly an easy A, but if you work hard, you can definitally get that A. oh and he is hot. really hot.
Love her.  She's passionate about writing in her personal life, and it shows in the classroom.
No Comments

she's a great teacher and explains what she wants really shows that she cares about students if your lost. not too difficult but theres A LOT of reading and writing, but we never did essays, just responses and one research paper. reasonable grader and nice lady...take her!!!

she's a pretty good teacher. assigns a lot of hw so be prepared to do a lot between class sessions. the class's theme i could care less about, however she is very nice and grades decently if you have any idea what you're doing. do the hw and turn assignments in on time and its an A class.
Kneplers one of the best professors I've had. She's not a pedant,easy-going, & actually cares about students. Just go to class & do the readings..you'll get an easy A.

She's a very good teacher. She explains the material very well. Homework is somewhat easy. just a lot of reading. If you listen to her discussions and follow her criteria you'll be fine. She's a really nice teacher. interacts with students. i'd recommend her.

The music topic was enough to make me happy, but Knabb as a professor was pretty cool too.  He seems pretty laid back, but one thing I got from him is that he knows his stuff and is pretty smart.  I actually had to think more critically in this class, he asks a lot of thought provoking questions that require some critical thinking but I recommend

He was absent about 33% of the semester with "headaches" (hangovers probably).  He canceled some assignments due to many missed classes.  Some assignments were unclear.  His doesn't grade papers carefully, just skims through them.  Overall, I'd say, this guy doesn't care if you learn anything, makes no effort.  But you can still get a decent grade.

Topic was really cool and for your final paper you write about your favorite music artist. I actually enjoyed doing the work in this class. He also gives very interesting lectures. Just make sure to participate you can lose a lot of points if you don't talk.
Hes really chill. Cancels class alot! VERY easy grader. Guaranteed A because each paper is reviewed 3 times before you get a final grade. Really cool guy

Class is really easy. Just go to class, take notes and its that simple. The final project we have to interview a person two generations older than us, it took a lot of work but wasn't hard to get an A. Anthropology isn't interesting so this class was whatever, I just took it as a gen ed. The professor is ok, not annoying but he's not amazing either

Interesting subject (music). Cancels class A LOT though sometimes its annoying when he does. Had to squeeze in our papers in the last month but it wasn't too hard. He also dropped one of our papers. Overall the class was super chill and easy to get through. Totally recommend if you don't care about following the syllabus.

I took this class a couple years ago but by far he has been my favorite teacher at UIC. He is so personable and if you ask him he will help you get through the class. At least for me it was a life changing class and I wish he taught other courses. Definitely recommend him to everyone. Also he wrote me a letter of recommendation.
One of the better topics. Cancels class a lot. Papers are easy.
Class topic is cool
the best professor i ever had. enough said.

Probably one of the best professors I had at UIC.In order to get a good grade in his class, you will have to be WILLING to improve your writing skills and learn. Be very mindful of his comments on your papers as improving your wr skills is imperative. He is a cool teacher and his class improved my writing exponentially with his comments and advice.

He is a pretty chill teacher and people that like music like his class. I didn't really kiss up to him and because of that class was much harder for me, also I think he doesn't like kids that come to his office hours too much.

He's really funny, class is fun. Most of the time he cancels class. He is very unclear though, and he expects you to write papers without him explaining the guidelines. The class was still fun though!

terrible teacher, he needs to make himself clear, and stop acting like he knows everything in the world!.. Go to class, and  meet new people that is all i did when i had him. Oh and of course turn in your work. Gives good feed back, but not specific. All around an ok teacher
He's a good teacher overall. Funny, and charismatic. The topic was by far the best for 161, so it'll at least keep you interested.

I have such mixed feelings about this class. On one hand, I loved going because the topic is awesome- Popular Music. On the other hand, no papers were graded until the end of the semester, assignments were confusing, and it just seemed like Knabb didn't care about teaching the class. It's the best English class to be in though.
He was great as showing us a new prespective on writing not just the old dry boring writings of dead white guys. Fun teacher.

Best Professor.. Loved the way he teaches.. He's never mad and has a great sense of humor. Many times lets students out early.. Easy A in the class.. Never thought I'd get all A's on my essays.. easy going.. Best class!

BEST PROFESSOR EVER!! This guy will rock your world. He is hilarious as hell, and gives great feedback on your writing. His class topic is "Songs of Love & Hate: An Examination of Taste Through Popular American Music." I HIGHLY recommend it, I can assure you it will become the highlight of your day.
Eh he is ok. Makes class kinda funny. But the homework is graded hard and he has an insane amount of power point slides per chapter and wont make a study guide. So be ready to spend hours studying.
I think this is the most interesting Psych teacher you can find at UIC, and if you so choose to go top class he will actually help you to stay awake with his teaching.

Omg terrible teacher. He talks about his wife like the whole time. When we do a chapter he never finishes it and you have to read the rest in the book. The homework is also graded rough, so make sure you are thurough and don't copy straight out of the book.
I loved 209 with her! She is truly brilliant and I learned so much. Definitely an emphasis on material analysis which was really great. Read the books and take notes!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Meh she's smart. But that's it. Wouldn't recommend her class to anybody. One of those many smart professors who don't know how to teach at all. Plus, she doesn't know that she is pretty rude to her students occasionally.

Kornbluh is very smart. She dresses nicely? But that is it though. A lot of reading and she rambles all the time. Definitely not the worst (or awful) but would not recommend taking a class with her unless you have to. She knows her stuff and might be a great writer but she is one of those writers who are not capable of teaching at school.

She wasn't great, but she wasn't awful. I never had any personal conversations with her, but she seemed nice in lectures. The lectures do drag, though, and it makes it incredibly hard to follow what's happening. I'd stop paying attention very quickly. A lot of reading, but that's just how the class is. More engaging lectures would help immensely.

This professor is the worst that I have experienced with my time at UIC. She has super long rambles during class and her presentations are not beneficial. She treats students needing help like nuisances and is pretty rude. I would not recommend her to anyone wanting to study English.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I am not sure what to say about Kornbluh. She is clearly intelligent, on-the-go and a rising star in academia. Her class is simply a mess, though. No one likes it and people really come with high hopes disappointed.
Kornblu is really really smart, but she is the best example of the research-teaching paradox of the liberal arts university offerings. Sorry 2/10 no recommend for me.

Lectures are mandatory, and boring. They drag, and half of the class is just doing other things on their computers anyway. She sometimes gives out pop quizzes, too. (Almost ) every Friday there's a reflection paper due, which isn't terrible. She kind of expects a lot of reading to be done for each class.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: this class sucked the joy out of my spring semester. there are ways to teach material on controversial subjects without boring everyone to death and overanalyzing titles and single sentences. kornbluh's psuedo-woke lectures are miserable. take this class with anybody else if you can.

Anna is the kind of teacher that graded us all the same based on her mood that day or night, no matter how much effort you put into your paper. She told us we would be having quizzes each week, but we only ended up having one in the beginning of the semester. She avoided telling us our grades and didn't give us enough time to read long excerpts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Kornbluh is really nice and understanding, stays within allotted time, likes for students to engage in her class, is really good with answering questions, and is accessible outside of class. The only bad thing was that her powerpoints are not really helpful, some pictures, a couple definitions, but nothing to take good notes off.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I took Professor Kornbluh for English 240 and liked her so much I decided to take her for 242 as well.  She's a great lecturer, extremely intelligent, engaging with students, and gives you all the information you need to be successful in the class (contrary to other reviews).  Show up, pay attention, read, take good notes, ask questions. Love her!
She fits right in with the bulk of UIC's English professors. Make of that what you will.

Class was not too bad. Have to keep up with readings and class attendance is mandatory. Her lectures did not help me out on the tests. She mainly talked about the history of the material in lecture but that is not what what on the test. Class made me hate English!

gives lots of information in lecture, but easy to keep up with. if you get the general ideas of the readings, you'll do fine on exams. she's totally invested in students, she's easy to talk to and will elaborate and explain anything. take her class. guys will like her, she's great looking

This class is not too hard if you read, come to lecture and pay attention. She keeps you involved as well as offer extra-credit opportunities to raise your grade.If you need to take English 242, Professor Kornbluh will help you really understand the history behind the books you read. You will become more knowledgable of the field.

She's amazing. Her lectures are so engaging, she's super available, her expectations are high, yet always within reason. I was so excited by this class-- she did a wonderful job with everything from lectures to syllabus organization. If you have the opportunity to take her class, do it. She also has really cute clothes!
Her lectures can be a bit fast-paced, but she really knows her material. Brilliant. Helpful when you need it most. I also agree that is both cute and gorgeous.
She is gorgeous

Dr Kostadinova is very knowledgeable, you can see she a LOT of research experience. You will learn a lot of interesting material, and ask her questions - she is happy to discuss stuff with students. Not a tough grader at all. However, book her office hours in advance-there's a chance she will be busy with other students and not take you.

I took her class on the European Union. Since she is from Eastern Europe she offered a unique perspective. She only graded based on a weekly news story you can pull from a reputable website, as well as a paper at the end of the semester. Her lecture slides weren't very detailed so you had to pay attention to the lectures if you wanted to learn.

This was a 1 credit hour Honors seminar class. You have to submit the weekly news alert and show up to class for attendance point. If you did all of that, you will get enough points in order to avoid writing a 10-page paper, and still pass the class (it was a pass/fail class). Though her classes were interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She's great

Very nice and understandable professor. When I asked her for an extension for a writing assignment, she kindly said 'sure.' However, there are a few writing assignments you must do, and they weren't very short. I felt like I wrote a Ph.D. thesis paper in this class.

Professor Kostadinova is nice and generous. Her powerpoints are excellent. Her exams are relatively tricky though. You have to read the books since there are questions that is from the book. For our class, she has made curves and adjustments to our exams. I got an A because of it. Do well on map quizzes and the essay. Always attend class

Dr. Kostadinova is really nice and smart! She gives you good notes to take during her lectures, and there is nothing complex about her class. Just make sure you read the books, as there are very detailed questions on her exams that you'll only find from the book. Overall, she is an awesome professor and I would definitely recommend her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: grade consisted of attendance, 3 exams (including final), 1 paper/presentation, map quizzes. textbook information is on the powerpoints, so study those aggressively.  exams arent too hard as long as you study them and pay attention in class. very sweet and well educated
Easy Class most of the exam was based off her power points which she uploads to blackboard.

Personally I loved this class. But if you're not interested in international politics than I wouldn't take it. This class is easy and fun if you show up to lectures & discussions. Part of your final grade is one a project that you do one your own & it's on a certain chapter, which is a 5 page paper & an oralPP presentation. She's specific & clear.

This professor was great. She had lectures that covered the material we studied. The presentations we had to do were fun and gave each student a chance to become more familiar with topics we studied. Study guides are provided so there is no reason why anyone should not get an A in the course. Everything is covered, all it takes individual effort.
Great lectures, do textbook problems (even the ones he doesn't assign) and you'll do well. Tough grader but curve is generous too. He's available outside of class always and generally really nice!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Awesome Professor. Exams are similar to textbook. The textbook is good to reference to understand what he's doing in class. Live Laugh Cylinders
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: CHE 312: kind, caring, smart, accessible. He is helpful, math savvy & it's very obvious that he tries. The class is tough, his exams/quiz/HW are too so be ready. He's changed a lot and gotten so good!!! Though his math notation is funny but valid and he takes a lot of math shortcuts, but he'll slow down for you if needed
His class made me realize I want to work with reactors atleast for some time in industry.  Incredibly smart guy, is always there if you have questions.

Dr Torabi is an amazing professor.  He is incredibly smart, and will always be there for you if you need help.  Transport is a tough class and I had many questions, all would be answered by him.  Toughest part was his notation for the math. I suggest turning to BSL if youre ever confused, and also reach out.
He does a good job explaining things but is a harsh grader and does not care about students succeeding. He fails people every semester.

He is an ok lecturer but can go off on tangents that aren't very helpful. It's very difficult to tell what to prepare for exactly on exams or quizzes and the homework takes an insane amount of time. He lacks empathy in regards to student's grades and won't hesitate to fail even though failing 311 can set a student back 2 entire semesters.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: CHE 311 and CHE 312 are very difficult classes. This professor makes both subjects even harder. His lectures tend to be irrelevant to homework/quizzes/exams. The homework can genuinely take 10+ hours to do. It seems he loves to fail students in this course. Looking at the history of 311/312 he is the only professor who consistently fails many.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is caring. His exams & quizzes are pretty random & different from the HW+quizzes, thankfully they are from the book so be paranoid and read all answer keys that you can. Krista was so amazing! The class itself was not hard if you're actually on top of your work. Krista is super understanding and will give you extra time to finish an assignment when needed. reviews.comment: Fav professor at UIC, he is so fun and caring. Very easy class with a couple of short assignments.

This Professor is awesome! The class is not difficult at all just participate and read the book/slides and you will pass! He gives so many extra credit opportunities as well. 1 easy paper, 2 in class tests, and one black board final. Highly recommend!
Real Estate Principals 250*  SUCH A WARM AND FUN PROFESSOR! All you need to do is interact with his class

Kris was an honest man throughout the whole semester however he must love ruining someone's day. He grades like if this class was a 300 level course. reviews.comment: she's really nice, and you need to be prepared for exams...they aren't TOO difficult, but you do need to do a little more preparing than you probably think

I clicker and Growth Gauther are a good amount of your grade.
Self-study class that has a bunch of assignments. If you like studying by yourself, it is fine, but the actual lectures don't really help.

She was very nice and willing to sit down during office hours to give specific feedback to improve exams. Exams never felt unfair. Her response, saying I should only compare myself to myself, felt dismissive and made me uncomfortable asking questions. Overall, I did not feel supported and would not recommend this class.

She gives out a lot of extra credit and instead of weekly quizzes she has problems you can work as a group for review during discussion. Mostly used slides to learn and the internet to clear up any confusion concepts. Her structure of the class is light and as long as you review you will be fine. Great professor and is super kind.

Genetics is one of those classes where you really have to put in the time and effort to do well. I highly recommend keeping up with the textbook readings and regularly going over the learning objectives to make sure you understand the material. The professor is also very caring and understanding if you take the time to talk to her.

The class can be challenging if you do not put in enough time, but the material itself is not very difficult, theres just a lot of content. As long as you understand the lecture slides, you will be fine. Exams are long and detailed, so knowing mitosis, meiosis, and PCR well is important. Dr. Kukday is genuine and always willing to help if you ask.

reviews.comment: Took Fall 2025. Very time-consuming class. You will be expected to complete weekly assignments, even ahead of the actual content schedule. Get ready to rely on the textbook, basically. Exams somewhat reflect lecture slides, but are always 10x more in depth.

Lectures were kinda boring, but the class was okay. I definetely learned alot but on my own by reviewing slides and skimming through the text. My TA was also super awesome and did a better job teaching than the prof.

Overall a pretty average teacher. Lectures can be a little heavy with a lot of content but if you pay full attention it is definitely manageable. 

Tests reflect the lectures, extra credit is provided, and as of fall 25, 1 midterm test and some assignments with the lowest scores are dropped.

But the TA you take the class with is more important.

This professor was very unapproachable. When I asked her the average grade for my class for OLA 1, she laughed and said "the only person you should be comparing yourself to is you." The class itself was not too difficult and definitely manageable, but I would recommend taking it with a different professor.

awful. if you want to keep your sanity, do NOT take her. lecture slides are nothing like the exam which are god awful btw. she takes off points for turning in an exam ONE minute late after asking for an exception and being told yes. will accuse you of cheating. answers on the exam marked wrong even tho they were right and nothing gets done about it

Great projects, appreciate that the class isn't heavily structured. WGSL is pretty hard, but he does good job explaining. Tests also aren't hard.

Professor Sidharth is one of those chill professors whose teaching style shows he wants you to learn. He explains in great detail, this class made learning sql great. The group project at the end is something i'm actually proud of. The professor is very responsive made students feel welcome to ask questions

Nice but unmotivated and uninspiring prof. He never seems like he wants to be teaching. He has unnecessary weekly quizzes, which is ridiculous for the little amount of material learned. Lecture is him literally reading the slides out loud, and scribbling SQL queries on the slide as well as the occasional YT that does his job of teaching us for him

He's like a 3.5. He made things sound harder than they were but once I understood it the class was a breeze. I wouldn't say he's a bad teacher and he definitely knows his stuff but at the same time his way of teaching goes in circles and confuses the topic. Very nice and genuine so he's worth taking. As long as you do the work you should get an A.

Loved the course and the explanations were great!
Lots of extra credit up for grabs. Course mainly covers SQL. Frequent in class quizzes. Takes a lot of questions during the lecture and tries to keep the class interactive.

He is a cool person I like him personally I had a few chats with him outside of class unrelated to school by chance but I have to be fair his teaching is not it. Taking a course with Professor Kupchek is not for the faint of heart. The workload was significant, the midterm and final project were challenging. The class required lots of discipline and critical thinking to be successful. In the end it was one of the hardest but most rewarding classes I took.

Awesome professor! Always willing to explain thoroughly and provide extra help. Responds quickly to emails and makes sure that students don't fall behind on material. The material itself is not easy but if one attends classes and labs and seeks help if needed, he/she should do well.

His first semester at UIC. He is a good professor, knowledgeable, easy grader, and cares that his students learn the subject (Java). He slows down the pace of the class if he sees most are struggling. Just do all labs/homework and do practice exams before exams and you should get an A.

A very intelligent professor. His lectures were broken down into sections, which made it easy to complete the assignments. He was always available for extra help, and would give you multiple opportunities to correct assignments for full credit. He was extremely responsive with any questions. I had a great experience!

I had Goran for a class at DePaul, he was extremely helpful, always willing to meet up outside of class and making sure you understand things. We did have group activities every class, but it wasn't too bad. Overall, he's very relaxed and interesting, I would recommend him and his class!

Professor Kuljanin makes all of the topics understandable, relatable, and applicable through in-class small group activities and exercises. The assignments are manageable. The tests are fair. Group projects increase understanding of topics at a deeper (corporate) level. I would work towards a PhD with Professor Kuljanin if possible.

TAKE HIS CLASS! I wasn't too thrilled about taking stats, but he explained stuff so thoroughly that it all made sense. Psychlab is optional and the book is helpful, but not necessary. The EC opportunities are very helpful and he tells you exactly what to expect on exams from the in class review. Sort of on a tangent...he looks like Omer Asik! =)

Prof. Kuljanin has been by far the most helpful professor I've had at UIC. He's available even during non-office hours, he will sit with you one on one and help you get the material. Plus, you have opportunities for E.C and exam reviews. HIGHLY recommended.

Kuljanin is the best instructor that I've ever had in UIC. He is very helpful and very good at teaching the material. always available to student lots of office hours lots of Extra credit. I also suggest that you don't buy the book because I have never used it for this course. he post the lectures on BB no need for the book.

Professor Goran is a remarkable teacher. Although there is a lot of materials covered, he makes the class interesting. Plus, tons of extra credit opportunities. If you do the HW,  you could seriously get an A. My interest in this subject has increased after taking his course.

Dr. Kuljanin was very knowledge about the topics we covered. He managed to make some rather dry material interesting and relevant.  I'm definitely interested in learning more about i/o after taking his course!!
He is very detailed when it comes to what will come up on the tests. Lectures are great. Amazing Convos. He teaches in a way in which he makes sure you understand the content

Seemed like a nice professor, it's hard to say in an online formatted class. Was always very transparent in what was due, when it was due, and what needed to be done in order to succeed in the class. Amazingly useless class full of time filler unrelated readings (100s of pages) and free work for random small companies in the Chicago land area. The discussions have nothing to do with anything. Feels like I was just used for free labor and my tuition money was stolen from me.

Her class isnt HORRIBLE but its definitely not the best eithe

I have taken Prof. Inoue for three classes.  She is very tough--but that is what college is about.  Your LEARN in her classes.  If you want an easy grade and do not want to learn, choose someone else.  She is a great teacher, so if you are smart and willing to work, take her!  You'll learn.

Although she seemed nice, as the semester wore on, she became turbo-teacher.  expected everyone to understand everything and felt no need to explain more than the book did, but did mention many times that she didn't think the book was the best out there.
Professor Inoue is out of touch with students.  She gives students very little work that she grades and bases the grade on the final exam.  The final exam is completely unintelligable.

Basically told me to leave the major and focus on anything but my dreams/future. Told me one thing and then changed her statement a few months later to make herself seem better. Very unsupportive and condescending lady.

reviews.comment: This class was required for all freshman and transfer engineering students, and met once a week. Without Chris, I might not have enjoyed it as much as I did. She was genuinely enthusiastic about the course and was always available to students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Engineering 100 takes the cake as one of the most mind-numbingly tedious classes required at UIC. Prepare to be utterly bored for your entire semester until the hands-on project at the end, for rigid regard of speakers is enforced through prowling TAs and frequent chiding of all students. You can only skip one week of class - choose wisely.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Not a real class just go in for information on how to put your engineering degree to good use when you graduate or cheat your way through engineering school. Engineering Orientation is a MUST for graduating and she is your only choice weather you are transferring or starting at UIC. Take it as early in your years there as possible.

I can understand why students like this teacher. She does assign minimal work for a  1 credit hour class. However, she does tend to have favorites like most teachers. I have been to her office hours a few times where she has just given me attitude and then tries to act nice when other people are around.

She really cares about her students. If you have any trouble at all, go to her immediately. SHE WILL HELP YOU! This class is only needed for graduation, and don't really do anything besides show up and listen.

It is mind blowing that so many students love Kuypers. She has given me nothing but horrible advice, while being extremely condescending. It seems any time I've asked her for advice (or rather general questions) she's tried to lead me to the direction that would prolong my time at UIC as long as possible.

The class is boring, and doesn't help that you have a limit of only one absence.  Even so, the class also gives some useful information.  As for Chris, she's really helpful if you ever meet up with her in office hours.  As for in class...........................it was boring, so her being there didn't change anything.
Chris = Awesome. Nuff Said.
This class is easy, and Chris is a fantastic professor to have for it. She's always there to help her students even if she's busy at the time. You couldn't ask for a better, more dedicated teacher.

If you can't pass this class... Find a new major. This is by far the easiest class you'll have in your engineering career. Just attend for 11 out of the 12 weeks (shorter than the typical 16 week schedule), submit a resume, and submit a society evaluation form (attend an ENGINEERING club at UIC and evaluate it).

It's a required course for engineers and she's the only instructor. But I wish she stays as the instructor forever! It's the best way to get to know Engineering at UIC, to discover how passionate are you about your major, to know what to do and what not to do in your undergraduate carrer, to start polishing your resume, etc. I had a blast!

This is such a blow off class for engineering majors. Just go to class for points and you just have to turn in a resume and this sheet for a Engineering society meeting. Super simple and Chris is really nice.

Chris is very enthusiastic about helping students transition into the engineering department and is very approachable if you have any problems. Attendance is mandatory, but you're allowed 1 absence (and a coffee if you're late).

She is one of the best professor! She is very nice and she will guide you to success. Don't be late for class unless  you bought her some good coffee.If you fail this class you should not go to engineering school.
Let's face it, this class is a joke and 12 weeks too long.

This class was a blowoff class. It will be really informative to you if u did not pay attention during orientation. You only meet once a week, write one easy 2 page paper. If you do not pass this class then ur a complete idiot or was too lazy to come to class, becuase u only get one absence. o yea chris, SHE's cool.

Chris is terrific. Her class is full of really useful info about how to excel in the college of engineering. The class may seem trivial, but Chris has a good idea of what's important and conveys it enthusiastically. She's super knowledgeable about the engineering dept, and she went out of her way to help me find which major is right for me. Thanks!

Chris' Intro to Engineering course may have been the best class I had in my career at UIC.  She helps guide you through the labyrinthine process of determining which discipline is right for you, how to navigate the school bureaucracy, and actually makes students excited about the years ahead.

Excellent. This class was really helpful, and it really pushed me to the right direction. I thought it was going to be useless, but it was really helpful. Better than getting absolutely no advice in LAS and being lost.
She is very good. Very clear and wants you to succeed. She is there for you whenever you want as an engineering student. I highly recommend her.

Wonderful and  Magnificent... It's an informational class and she makes sure you get the info you need.  Class is fun, as well. Chris has a lot of energy and really care about her students success. I was actually sad when class ended.  It's pass or fail- show up, turn in the three assignments (which are REALLY easy) and you pass!!
She likes to embarrass the students. Its uncalled for and very unprofessional AND disrespectful from her part.

I don't know what that other kid was talking about. The class wasn't a waste of time. I learned a lot about UIC and the College of Engineering, and Engr in general. Chris is a really cool professor who knows EVERYTHING about the school and is really open to helping students. Attendance is required and we had to do 3 assignments. No books 2 buy!
The class is a joke and it is easy as hell. Seriously, you cant fail this class.

She is the awesomest teacher ever. Extremely down-to-earth. Good sense of humor, fun to mess around with unless she has alot of **** to go over... HAND IN YOUR 3 ASSIGNMENTS AND U WILL GET AN "S"... oh and dont miss a class (only once a week)

Chris is probably the coolest and most down to earth professor you'll meet at UIC.  She can help you with whatever problems you're having with classes and shes a great person to go to for advice! I recommend visiting her in her office and getting to really know her...you'll regret it if you dont!

Best class ever, the things we learned actually helped a little, especially if you take it as a freshman which I strongly suggest you do.  I mean we watched the last samurai because we have the WARRIOR SPIRIT :-P
No Comments
she's cool. the class is easy. just turn ur**** in on time and she'll love you.

In the course she's very helpful, but be careful whenever you ask for her help with something.  She has a nasty tendency to ask you to volunteer for stuff...this is the biggest reason that I eventually stopped going to her for help with anything.
Shes energetic so its easy to stay awake, and shes definatly very helpful.

A Very nice person. She will help you with anything. Always energetic! She has a lot of connections and treats you like your buddy. I had engineering 100 with her, so it was a breeze. On Helpfullness and Easiness, out of 5, I would give her a 6!

His lectures consisted of him reading off slides that he didn't write, and he often seemed confused by the material, making basic mistakes in his lectures. The class consists mainly of memorizing material and not actually learning biochem. That said, the class was pretty easy and didn't require much effort to get a good grade.

I honestly think Dr. Miller is excellent! I enjoy his dry humor and how he said "god" when he was struggling with a PowerPoint slide once! When he said that, I honestly felt his struggle on a personal level. I appreciate him as my Professor. He's definitely a real one!! Would absolutely take his course again! 10/10

Professor is regularly not prepared for class, regularly makes mistakes in lectures, not a clear lecturer at all. My biggest complaint is that learning the concepts and succeeding in the class are not the same - he doesn't teach core concepts in class, so you have to read, but the exams are basically all trivia so you have to go to lecture to pass

The lab has to be the most oddly organized I have taken in any of UIC. That being said, you're mostly writing reports, the TAs are quite light with grading. The quizzes were online, and the short answer questions were just brutal, I rarely ever got even partial credit! Had no idea what the curve was till the last second.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers

reviews.comment: His lectures are not so clear. But take notes when he says anything outside of the lectures. I did not like him in the beginning. But went to his office hours and he explained everything better during his office. Make use of his office hours. Its so worth it.
Horrible. Worst professor I've had at UIC. Doesn't seem to know the material. Reads directly from the slide.

Very poor quality professor. Comes through the door acting like he doesn't want to be there. Reads right off of his powerpoint slides, which he consistently gets turned around in. Testing is largely based on memorizing and not actually learning. Grading is a lot of all or nothing.  Take it with someone else if you can.
Horrible Teacher, Avoid him

For a 400-level class, the class is really easy. He doesn't really know much about biochemistry and wouldn't know anything about it w/o his lecture notes. Study the practice exams and you should be fine.
Class isn't bad. Make sure to completely understand the practice exams.
He's not a good profesor he was constanly turned around in his notes and lectures and most annoyingly his structure drawing.  Be prepared to teach yourself he stinks. He does make it easy to pass

I took Biochem with Miller and I have to say, for a 400-level class it WAS NOT that bad. Exams weren't horrible and there were HUGE curves. The only annoying thing is that he's REALLY particular about your answers. Dont add an extra hydrogen on your structures or your screwed. Other than that, great class!
I dont think he is that bad of a teacher He curves slightly in the end. He passes out handouts in the class so go to lectures. It is a lot of memorization but I found it interesting

teacher seemed like he was thrown into teaching this class. Very unprepared. Knows his stuff but just not how to explain it. Somewhat inconsistant with what he expects you to know in class and on tests. Not as hard of a class as i thought though.

Great teacher, always made the lectures enjoyable and clearly explained the material. She gives a lot of extra credit, and her exams aren't very difficult, but attendance matters quite a bit. Definitely recommend taking her!

Dr. Lam is a very kind woman. I would definitely recommend her class to anyone. You can tell she wants everyone to succeed. Definitely go to lecture because tells you exactly what will be on the exam!

She was amazing. There was only one weekly assignment and one essay, which she gave you 3 months to do. Her lectures are always interesting, and she tells you what will be on the exam. She records her lectures so you can always go back and listen to them when you need. The exams are multiple-choice and include two short-answer questions.
she chill fo real

Overall Great human who is easy to connect to on a human level. She was a great professor I learned a lot, and she was always very clear about what you needed to know or do to get a good grade. Lots of resources and extra credit opportunities. First prof. I felt connected to at UIC, looking forward to taking her again!
The lectures could get boring but she's a very sweet person and the content is pretty easy to understand.

very nice professor who is understanding about life circumstances. she gives a few extra credit opportunities out but overall the class is 5 exams worth 50 pts each, attendance, online assignments and one essay.

She is really nice. She will read straight from the slides. She has this professional tone in her voice. She isn't strictly business. She is very understanding. Homework assignments are all online. Five online exams that contain about 40 questions each. She makes you come in to class to take the exams for some reason. A lot of people would cheat.

reviews.comment: great teacher, very pretty.

If you want to do well in the class, you do have to attend lectures and do the online homework. All her lectures are PowerPoint, you can print them off before lecture. Homework is done through homework manager (which is all fill in and multiple choice). When you go to her for help, she acts like you should know the material already.

She gets confused pretty easily a times but I'm pretty sure its just because of her language barrier.  Overall she was pretty good, I should have done a lot better then I did.  Make sure you use all the powerpoints and practice problems on Blackboard
Excellent professor, I wish she could teach 315 in Spring 2010 semester!!!

wow, confusing.  Out of every ten words she says, you will only understand two. material is super hard with really bad explanations.  I hated those in class quizzes. Really boring, it was a waste of my time going to her class, take accounting at a community college, you'll be better off.

Very unorganized. Powerpoints for lectures are always revised and it's not a minor revision sometimes the whole thing.You end up printing another set. When answering problems in-class,she does not have the presence of mind. Beware of "where did I get that number?" a question she always asks herself. Confuses students. Does not update grade online.
i enjoyed her teaching. learned a lot from her. outstanding.
great prof.
i took accounting 315 with this teacher! got a C and was really happy with it. 315 is the hardest class for the accounting majors!

I took this course fall 2008. I already rated her before. But I just took 315 (got an A), and I am so thankful I took her for 210, because it was everything she taught and I felt like I really learned all the concepts from her. So if you plan to become an ACTG major, I highly recommend taking Prof Kim. She intelligent and approachable!
great. knows her stuff. challenging but helps students.
Very good prof. Knows her stuff.
If you actually want to learn financial accounting then this is the porf. Had to work for my A.

everyone that gives her negative reviews and says it's hard are more likely the slackers. I thought it was pretty easy, never read the book, just went to lectures. just treat it as any other class at UIC

ATG 210 She knows her stuff, But very hard though. Popup quizzes, and very hard grading on tests. If you have any bit interest then you'll do good, otherwise you are screwed. Grading should be eased up on, this is opening Accounting class.

Helpful teacher! Understands all problems you are having, but you need to show her that you actually know something before coming in. Test are ok...Read the book (every chapter), powerpoint slides, and her handouts. Be prepared for every class because you might have a quiz. Got an A in her class!

She is very HARD! I agree with others, avoid this class or take it at a community colleges. The tests were very hard and her lectures are definitely boring. Her syllabus says no make-up quizzes but she allowed a student to make up 1 while I was with the TA and denied this opp. to another student.

I just took the class during the fall 08 semester and it was definitely my hardest class. She has 7 unannounced  quizzes and the test were nearly impossible. The only thing that probably gave me a passing grade is the online homework. The pace of the class is very fast and her English is not the best. LOTS of handouts and notes. Avoid if possible.
Her exams were joke: either too hard or too easy just to pass students that got low scores on the first exam.
She knows her stuff, but doesn't know how to teach it. I suggest avoiding her class if possible.

I am in the same class as those who posted below me. . . I think that they just don't study. She is very helpful when you seek for help, and very nice as well. The class is very fast pace but doable. Getting an A in the class as of now.

This professor is one of the worst professors i have ever had. She barely speaks english, her tests are a far cry from what she teaches in lecture and she is unwilling to help students. I know that she is the only person teaching actg 210 at uic, but seriously, unless you are an accounting major, try and take this at community college over the sum.

VERY DIFFICULT CLASS. The two midterms and final exam are difficult(my class averages 60%). She did not tell us what would be on the exams and there are a good amount of trick questions that require very in depth understanding of topics. 7 pop quizzes given to insure attendance. Boring lectures. Homework is easy but is a small amount of your grade.
knows her stuff. and hot too. :)
I found this professor very helpful.  She was always available for help!  There is no doubts that this class is HARD…but if u do all the extra problems, and homework like three time you will be fine!

well it's not her fault that 315 is a class from hell, tests are very hard and the average is usually around 60%, you def need to go over the extra problems she gives in class, homeworks and quizes are pretty easy, overall she's a nice teacher
DIFFICULT

Horrible teacher. How can you tech accounting with power point? Then brings a bunch of printed out problems and just fills few numbers - you left lost. Never writes examples, just uses hand wavings trying to explain accounting. The worst actg teacher at UIC!

Her exams are hard. 10+ MC and 5-7 problems in 2 and a half hours. problems are consisting of several knowledge points. She makes problems very complicated. You really have to understand the materials to solve her problems. She gave some examples in class, redo these problems after every class twice if you want to do well in this class.

Hard teacher, Hard Class.. but grading is fair.. ONLY if you SHOW ALOT OF work on Exams.. just dun rite the answer... She gives alot of partial credit and there is about a 5% curve at the end of the class ....

Decent teacher. Tests are very difficult, because of the nature of the material and time constraints. Managed to earn a high 'B' with 10+ hrs/week of studying. No curves. Average test grades 62-68% for each of te three tests. She gives you plenty of extra examples in class and on BB. If you didn't master the basics in 110/111, you will not do well.
She's great.  Very helpful in class.

I would recommend her, class is hard but she will tell you what will be on exams. Basically mini samples exams, based on homework that she will tell you to know. Take her, other financial accounting prof are much, much harder graders. Difficult Class
Hard Class, be prepared to study ALOT. Material is hard, but she is very fair tells you what will be on the exams. I would recommend her, lectures boring, but it it an accoubting lecture!

Pretty hard class, extremely tough midterms and finals. Quiet, monotonous voice makes you fall asleep during the lectures. Not the best teacher, but a good person, will answer all the questions you have about the class material.

Lauren is a great professor! She is really chill and funny.  She's a tough grader but as time goes on you will understand that her feedback really matters and helps you become a better designer. Attendance wasn't mandatory she took it once in a while, but go to class and participate. She will notice you and your work.

Lauren is the most friendly and supportive professor! If you're looking for an easy A her class isn't it but you get 3 tries on every project so you can get there if you really want to and she really wants to help you get there too. The semester is over today, I wish she taught more classes next year.

She is strict on attendance; if you are a minute late, you get marked as late. She is super opinionated, passive-aggressive, and rude. Her feedback is not detailed; she just says, "Doesn't work, here's some inspiration to help." When trying to improve a past assignment, she walked up to me with a smile on her face, saying she lowered my grade...
She is caring, funny and smart. What else do you need to know? Take her class, you'll work hard and become a better designer.

Lauren is everything you want in a design styled classroom as a professor. The only thing is starting my first college semester off with her kicking things off in such a tough environment was eye-opening, but well learned from. She helps anyone who asks for it and tries to go around critiquing students work to help them for the better.
If you are even 1 minute late for class, you will be marked absent. Her grading is really strange, you need to understand her mindset. If you manage to do this, this lesson will be very easy for you.

She has been an amazing professor to work with since day one, very knowledgeable and down to earth. I actually view design differently after taking this class, it opened my eyes to type and composition. And it's nice that all the work is done in class so no homework. Her feedback and support give me confidence that I'm in the right place.

Peer feedback? essentially nonexistent. The only time we'd be "encouraged" to give our feedback she'd quickly get impatient and talk anyways. Her feedback was incredibly vague, just "___ was successful, here's some inspo for the next phase". Combined w/ the fact that she's sassy, she was imo unapproachable. Most confusing and discouraging class oml

Lauren is one of the better professors at UIC. Although her grading is tough, there is ample opportunity to improve your work and grade. Photography is subjective, but she provides clear and understandable feedback for how to successfully capture a moment. She is tough on you to push you to unlock better skills. Nice person and great class energy.

She has a clear knowledge in photography and isn't afraid to tell students if their picture isn't the best. If she says your photos are good, be proud of yourself! She will go above and beyond to help if it is needed. Very passionate in what she does, would highly recommend her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: My all-time favorite teacher. Lauren Nichols is really supportive and inspirational, plus she has this magical ability to give advice that immediately makes things work 100xs better.

Professor Nichols is passionate about design and helping each student improve, bringing such positive energy to the classroom and laughter to the constructive critiques. The workload was heavy but it forced a constant awareness of composition. And the high expectations in craftsmanship pushed me to produce strong solutions that I'm really proud of.

Lauren has knowledge on photography, but is a complicated professor. Not the best teacher in my opinion, but also not the worst. She admits to being "moody"-- she'll say she likes a photo one day, then says she doesn't another day. Nevertheless I would take one of her classes again, she can just be annoying with her teaching strategies.
She is by far the best teacher I have ever seen, she is always there for me when I need help. And she really wants us to learn in her class!

Lauren is a very funny person and she is not afraid to give good feedback on your work. I thoroughly enjoy her class and I think the pictures we have to take are very interesting and get you thinking more about the world and light around you.
Very nice and fun to be around. Although her grading standards are very tough, revisions are allowed to improve your grade.

This instructor kept the class fun and was very easygoing, loved being in her class. She's also kind of a tough grader, but will always allow you to improve your grade with revisions while giving you feedback on anything you show her. She'll always willing to stay after class and talk about your assignment until you understand it.
Easily everyone's favorite and very laid back about attendance (as long as you let her know things). Also very understanding of students and their schedules.

the material is presented primarily by reading from the slides. It would be very helpful for the class if you could provide more real-world examples or deeper explanations beyond the text on the screen. Additionally, more frequent communication regarding our questions and course updates would significantly help us stay on track with the curriculum.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Omar was very nice and understanding. If you actually pay attention in lecture and make an effort to study you'll be good. Attendance is mandatory and there are worksheets you need to complete during lecture but you get 6 of them dropped at the end of the semester. He also allows exam corrections and provides lots of resources to prepare.

He just reads off lecture slides, does not explain things well enough, and expects you to be a genius. TA's are also not very helpful and this course is exam heavy and problem set heavy. He doesn't do a good enough job at making sure his students are okay and doing well enough. Just watch youtube videos to help with the exams.
To be success in this class, Do Problem Set. Study more than exam practice for exam. Cheat on zyBook is fine. Go to class.
A very polite professor with very little acknowledgement of how his student understands the material. As a student in this class, you are expected to be a genius to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor's teaching is unclear and disorganized. Lectures lack structure, explanations are rushed, and key concepts aren't broken down properly, making the material hard to understand. The class feels low-energy and unengaging. Exams are much harder than the instruction provided, making it a frustrating experience.
