reviews.comment: Class was taught well. Main issue is the problem set assignments which are worth 20% of your grade were graded like exams and they refused to help you at all with mandatory problems.

You honestly just need to pay attention and study notes, it's an algorithms class so spending time reading is important. He also grades fairly, there's alot of opportunities to get points. Encourages partnerships and will spend time explaining

Great course structure and way of lecturing (nice ratio of lecturing : practice examples : try this on your own). Took 301, and now 401 with Ibrahim. Would say that if you attend/watch lectures and actively pay attention, homework, labs, and exam material, it will make sense. edit: makes good cookies.

Cares about students but lecture slides were a bit bland and not a lot of study material. Practice exam questions answers were posted the day before the exam so it was hard to study and know which questions you got right or wrong in time for the exam.
Just take bello.
Good professor. although lectures can feel slow but welcome to theory classes that's how it be. Exams and homework pertained to the content learned in class.
Do not listen to other reviews, he is a great professor IF YOU GO TO LECTURE.

He's a good professor for 301, exams were reasonable along with HW. Lectures can be boring but it's a theroy class so that's to be expected. Material can be difficult at first but the labs help a lot with the learning. Overall I learned a lot from him and would say he is on par with McCarty. Don't skip lecture though, it is easy to fall behind.

Prof. Ibrahim is a nice guy, but not the best professor. His lectures are bland but informative, and they lack enough examples for students to really understand the material. Homework and tests are graded extremely generously, and the labs are the only places to do exercises, which are only graded for effort.

Course level doesn't even matter, if it did matter, MATH 310 would be just as difficult as CS 301. Omar is simply a bad instructor. He doesn't provide answer keys to homework and literally the only thing he gives us to study for exams are past exams; which aren't even helpful to begin with.

This was the hardest CS class in uic that i took, The content in itself wasnt very hard but we had very few sources to study from and the professor made the exams really hard. He kept telling that the class would curve but there was no curve altho more than half of the class had very bad grades. The mean on the midterm was 68 percent.

Everyone writing terrible reviews were truly just upset about their midterm grades since they didn't put effort into a 300 level course. Omar is a really caring professor  and is genuinely passionate about his students learning. I recommend taking if you want a professor who cares about your learning, and you're actually willing to put in effort!

Omar appears to be kind, although he was very below average. The lack of resources, keys, and examples made it difficult to learn. TAs were told not to directly assist students to the ability that they should in order for students to learn. Terrible instructor- truly a shame. NO XC or curve which is not normal for 301- last 20 years had one. ):
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Don't be deceived by the midterm reviews; Omar is a down to earth, professional professor who explains new material clearly and answers any and all questions you may have for him. Although attendance was 100% optional, SHOW UP TO LECTURES, it is the key to success (would've helped those who left a bad midterm review). They are the ideal professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I do not agree with every low-rating here for Omar. Lectures are optional, all posted online, homework is graded *to give students at many points as possible*, responds fast, has easy extra credit. He also is really young, and just genuinely cares. Everyone rating him low simply did not put the work in to get an A, and are salty. Great professor.

Genuinely one of the worst professors at UIC. Dude does not know how to teach at all, he makes everything so unnecessarily complicated and hard, and nobody knows what's going on half the time in lecture. The class structure and grading system is also horrible, considering like 80% of the class averages below a C on both exams and hws. Smh

The course was very easy but our instructor made it very difficult. There was no room for improving your grade. The marking scheme was also very difficult and he would try to deduct marks to the best of his ability. It is like he does not want students to pass this course. He should not be allowed to teach any class.

Please do not consider any reviews made around Feb 20th, 2024. That's the week exam 1 grades got released, which shows how much people have a grudge against him bc they don't study.

I do not attend any lectures as it does not count towards your grade, but if you watch the recordings and attend lab and do homework, you'll do fine in this course.
Not enough examples in class. HW and exam grade too hard.

Learning is more of an excuse for him not being able to teach his students well. The entire class has a low grade point average. Is this just a problem with the students? Think about how dubious his teaching style is. When students asked for more examples, they said no.
People will hate because the class average on the exam was low when the test was very similar to the practice exams given. Stop crying. Skill issue. Start studying more

No idea how to teach a class at all. Just talk about useless definitions. the questions on the exams, labs and homework are completely different difficulty levels. Waste of time to talk about topics that are beyond the syllabus. He will deduct your whole mark for one small mistake. You will feel that your efforts are totally useless.
NEVER take a class with him again
Easiest class I ever took. All you have to do is show up and barely take notes. The labs were almost too easy and just exemplified the bare bones of the lecture. Fun and stress free class!
Lectures were interesting but content-heavy. Labs were engaging, but I wish the TAs had explained more. Overall, it is an easy class for general requirements.

you get out of it what you put in you can easily pass the class if you want to, even by not showing up, so it's an easy gen ed. but if you are genuinely interested in archaelogy and anthropology, lamotta is incredibly good at lecturing and keeping you invested. very knowledgeable but able to explain things to people who know nothing about the field

This professor was magnificent. His class was very interesting and could tell he actually is experienced in his field while also caring for other students lives. The lab is fast-paced but manageable because it is fun, along with not-so-stressful graded assignments during class. I would suggest to anyone who needs this, especially when life is hard.
I never went to a lecture and still got an A. just do your work in the discussion section and do the tests and bang easy A.
Amazing professor!! Highly recommend. I brought cupcakes for my birthday and he sang happy birthday to me with the whole class. He even did a small cute dance.

Labs are pretty easy, depending on the TA. Lectures are super interesting, and he actually covers all of the information that will be on the exams. Try to go to the Zoom meeting study session he holds because it is super useful for the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
lectures werent heavy n u cld tell he was passionate ab the subject which made it much more engaging (esp 4 a field i was unfamiliar with)! labs were fun n u rlly got the sense u were learning more thru them

also HAVE 2 give this diva a shoutout 4 pausing mid-lecture 2 glare everytime this 1 group wld talk n distract us until they shut up. ICON.
amazing professor

Extremely fun class despite how the title "Ceramic Analysis" may sound like to people. The professor really enjoyed teaching it and made every lecture very enjoyable with his own personal stories and tips. If you're going to take any class with Professor LaMotta, ask him about the giant crab that attacked him.

I stopped going to his lectures after the first two-three weeks. I only went to lab as attendance is required and it was a lot more interesting than lectures. I used the study guides mostly and I was completely fine on the exams.

I typically got really sleepy in lectures because of his tone, as it is a little monotonous and calm. Other than that, he is archaeology itself. I'm 99% sure he eats, sleeps, and breathes archaeological research and information from how detailed his lectures were. I never looked at the textbook/study guides and I only went to lecture + lab. Easy A.

Great professor who is passionate. no homework. labs are mandatory and all work is due at the end of the lab. technically the lecture is mandatory but no attendance is taken. honestly a super easy class as long as you review the slides and do the study guides. we have a textbook, but I haven't read it and currently have a 95% in the class.

Anthropology king! Very interesting and passionate about what he is lecturing about. Attendance is optional at lectures, but recommended, attendance is mandatory at weekly labs. The labs were interesting, especially with a good lab table, and more lab work is due every Sunday, usually taking 1-2 hours of work. Interesting class overall, easy A.

LaMotta is an amazing professor, extremely understanding and is truly interested in the content that he's teaching. He gives many opportunities for you to boost your grade and is a great person. I highly recommend him for this class!!

If you procrastinate, you will fall behind in reading the textbook. I recommend going to the lectures because it's easier to understand the course when he explains. The labs are mandatory to go to but are interesting. Try to keep a strict schedule for reading the textbook and doing the online labs. Schedule labs (earlier days) to get homework done.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Lamotta genuinely cares about his students. The lecture isn't mandatory, but the lab is. Overall, the class is pretty easy but the lectures are quite heavy. He is very organized and has a lot of resources for his students to help them succeed. I 100% recommend taking this class with Professor Lamotta.

Professor LaMotta was very informative and very knowledgeable. He actually cares about his students and encourages them to take advantage of office hours so he can help you. Labs are mandatory to show up to. Just your basic college class.

He's so nice! definitely one of the best teachers in the Anthropolgy department. He's so helpful, and while he gets carried away sometimes, if you speak up he will always go a little slower. I took SW Archaeology, ; be ready to read if youre taking that course, but it was pretty interesting and you can probably get by with skimming it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: He is so sweetie. The labs are super easy and depending on your TA, they will let you out if you complete early. It is a good amount of time and can create long days but it is super easy. The lecture slides are posts and the tests are based purely on them, no need for book. A few extra credit opportunities too.

This class was incredibly easy and the labs were quite interesting. This class made me switch my major, so if you're into anthropology would highly recommend it. Labs are easy and tests are online. Lots of extra credit as well.

Professor Lamotta is very passionate about anthropology, which is what makes his lectures more interesting. ANTH 102 is easy as long as you show up to lectures and labs. There is a textbook, but you will be just fine without it. Tests are easy as long as you pay attention in lecture.
Another great semester with Prof. LaMotta! He is super passionate about his field and delivers very informative lectures. If you're interested in archaeology, he's your guy.

Absolutely love LaMotta as a prof- went to him for advice on majoring in anthropology and he was super helpful. Had his ANTH 102 class and while it's super lecture heavy, the lectures are easy to understand. Definitely cannot skip this class often though or you'll miss everything. Only had 3 tests the whole sem.

This class is unnecessary and if you are looking for a science gened i recommend anth 105 instead. The class set up is ridiculous: 3 hours lecture weekly + 2 hour lab section (you can't leave early and you don't work on the actual lab packet)+readings+exams+lab packets+lab videos. I'm an anthro major AND I got a 98 in the class so... not worth it.
A great professor that is very knowledgeable, has a lot of consideration for his students, and will make sure that you can achieve the highest grade possible.

He is literally the best professor I have ever had, I take classes I am not super interested in just to get to be in his classes. He is clearly passionate about what he teaches and is super understanding of things you may be going through. Definitely the best lab based class you can take for your gen ed.

I was actually pleasantly surprised by this class. Although his lectures are a little boring, he is actually a really kind person who genuinely cares about what he teaches. I met with him once or twice about minoring in anthropology, and he was super supportive. I only had 3 lectures per week and a lab with online work., a
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took the course in the asynchronous format. His lecture videos are very long. Each one is damn near an hour + long, and you'll be assigned 2-4 every week. An upside is that they can be sped up. Exams aren't difficult but are based on the lecture videos. It's imperative that you stay on top of those videos or you'll be unpleasantly cramming.

I have taken 4 courses with this professor and he is amazing! He is also super assessable to talk with and has plenty of useful information. Because of him I picked anthropology as a major. The courses are heavy but they were entertaining and fun. Every class I got an A expect for Anth 223. I highly recommend him.

guys do not take this class if you are not an anthropology major. if you are doing this class as a gen ed, don't do it. There are so many other easy gen eds. So much work given for this class for no reason. Mean professor. Awful class. Labs are about 2 hours and you do nothing. Waste of time.

Extremely knowledgable and articulate. He is very supportive, responsive w/ email and wants students to succeed. Lectures are EXTREMELY long in duration. Graded hard on some labs. Take the class in person vs. online. If you tend to procrastinate, as I do, you may be in store for 4 hr. lecture marathons (material that tests are primarily structured)

I had Professor LaMotta in my first semester at UIC and I just want to say he was one of the BEST professors Ive ever had. I took his class as a Gen Ed requirement I had no interest in Anthropology what so ever but he made class fun and interesting. Great personality and very detailed/organized.

Took him during the Fall 2021 semester and the lectures are all online. Lab attendance is mandatory for a grade, but the labs themselves are sometimes just time-consuming but not difficult. There are 3 exams plus all 12 labs as the total grade. I watched 10 hours' worth of lecture videos for 2/3 exams and got a 95+ grade. Take good notes on videos.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Some might change for the Spring semester but for the Fall semester, we have to these recorded lectures which some can be really long (60 minutes). Lab packets are pretty easy if you pay attention and read the instruction. Not a lot of work for me personally, lab packet might be hard to grasp at first but you will understand as you go
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Heavy Lectures, each recorded lecture is at least 60-80 minutes. In addition, you have weekly labs that are enormous, at least 20 pages each. If you are not an archaeology major, I would recommend DO NOT TAKE IT! You need to spend some solid time of the week to do the labs, plus there are participation points, and attendance is mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor! He gives you so many opportunities to earn extra credit to boost your grade. I took him during an asynchronous COVID semester and he could not have been more accommodating. 50% of students in my class got an A. Only reason I didn't is cause I would turn labs in late and not read the textbook. Even still I got an 88%.

Very time consuming class with long lectures and labs, but Professor Lamotta spaces everything out giving you enough time to complete the work. 3 tests overall which were fairly easy if you study. Overall he is very kind and understanding.

Prof. LaMotta has handled the transition to online classes during COVID better than any other professor I've had. He is compassionate and genuinely wants you to succeed. The material is relatively easy, and he gives lots of insight during lectures. Tbh, it's difficult to do poorly in this class as long as you do the labs (which are genuinely fun!)
professor lamotta is an amazing professor and an amazing person. he genuinely cares about his students success. very passionate about anthropology.
I really enjoyed the asynchronous lecture segments and Dr. LaMotta's insights as an archaeologist

2nd class with Professor LaMotta. Enjoyed both experiences. Very well-spoken /articulate, has deep knowledge of the topics. Realistic expectations for HW and exams- always gives study guides. HW usually easy, just might be lengthy. Very kind, extends deadlines without asking. (Dont recommend getting textbooks, just take good notes on lectures)

Prof. LaMotta has been very considerate this semester given the COVID-19 situation. He even shortened our last exam to lift some stress/ease anxiety. Weekly labs (but they're so easy & sometimes fun) - attendance is mandatory but my TA was cool. As long as you watch his lecture videos (asynchronous) & take notes, you're all set for (3) exams!

The lectures can get tedious at times, but Prof. Lamotta shows genuine interest in the course material and eloquently presents it to students in an organized manner. Few exams but worth a lot of points and largely determine your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor LaMotta is an extremely caring professor who put students mental well-being first. Make sure to attend or watch the lectures because he covers all testing materials on his lectures. Lectures can be lengthy but he does a great job at keeping them interesting!

The class was a bit tedious. I studied 300 terms for the final exam. However, I got a 97% after going over those terms for 2 days. His tests are designed so that you can rule out answers very easily-- provided you've been paying attention and have a wide knowledge of everything learned. It's rewarding to feel like studying really pays off.

Professor LaMotta is the best professor I have ever had at UIC. He is extremely caring and makes the lectures interesting. He does not post slides online, so it is best that you come to class. He posts a study guide for each exam that helps greatly! On the study guide he includes 30 questions that WILL be on the exam and there's extra credit!
Vincent is pretty easy going and understanding. Attendance isn't mandatory, but if you miss the lectures, you miss a big chunk of information that's vital for the 3 exams throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: To my surprise i really enjoyed Dr. LaMotta's class. He is very passionate about the field of Archaeology/Anthropology.I actually learned a lot. His lectures contains a lot of info and that info is reflected in his test. So make sure if you have to miss class you can get the notes. Only three test and this includes the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took the class as a gen ed. I followed all his lecture outlines, studied a bit the night before exams, and ended up with an A. Not super hard, but also not an easy A. The final was the hardest and consisted of 50 questions "old content" and 50 points "new content" so don't slack off at the end. Lab portion of the class was tough

He's honestly such an amazing person, as long as you show you actually care about the course! He's extremely lenient as well and overall a pretty good lecturer; lecture outlines are bad though so just take normal notes! The class was easy as long as you go to lecture here and there. Labs are pretty easy too but the TAs are very picky!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lecture is very dry, but you should attend to understand the material. Exams are hard if you do not look a the study guide. Labs are different from what you learn in lecture. If you take this class just know if you do not put in work you will fail. This class is more of a GPA dropper than boosting. You have to work for the grade you want.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Loved this class. The lectures were interesting and well structured, and you can find the outlines online. I attended most lectures but missed a fair few and still did well in the class by following the study guide provided and reviewing concepts before the exams. He's a really nice guy and was very good to talk to outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Such an amazing professor, his lectures are interesting and he is very passionate about archeology. Pay attention in class, attend all the labs, do the study guide and it should be an easy A. Overall I would highly recommend it!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Classes aren't mandatory because theres almost 400 people, just get a good TA and you'll be fine. Tests are lecture based. His lectures cna be a little dry, but they're pretty funny at some points.

He makes quite a few dad jokes while providing significant information for the topics at hand. The lectures are a lot of information but if you pay attention and take notes from the powerpoints you should be good. The exams are difficult and contains a LOT of information so be prepared to study hard! Overall a good class.

ANTH 102 This class is the epitome of what lecture based classes should be. Everything he talks about in lecture will be on the exam. The study guides are comprehensive and tells you what exactly will be on the exam. If you at the very least, attend lecture, take notes, and pass lab you will pass. It's straight forward and the content is enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: I took ANTH 102 as a requirement, but I enjoyed the class and that was due to Professor LaMotta. He's very passionate about this field and it shows in his lectures. There are moments where you catch yourself dozing off in class, but the class is not hard at all. Labs were straightforward and there's opportunities for extra credit.

He is a very smart and intelligent professor who takes Anthropology very passionately and seriously. His lectures can drag at times, however all the information he gives you during lecture matters and you can expect to see them on the exams. He also is really funny at times. Just take good notes, and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY--Would take again

reviews.comment: Dr. LaMotta was an amazing lecturer. Sometimes the lectures can get a little dull but for the most part they are very interesting. The exams were very easy but ONLY if you come prepared yet they are not tricky at all. You also get a study guide. Labs are very fun if you have the right group but the TAs, although helpful, grade very harshly.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I'm a poli sci major, I just took this class as a gen ed and I wasn't looking forward to it. This class turned out to be one of my favorites, He is so passionate about Archaeology that it makes you excited too. Make sure you start studying for the exam as soon as the study guides come out. He gives you 30 of the 50 questions on the exam early.
Dr. LaMotta is one of the best professors at UIC. He's cool and his lectures are very interesting. I would definitely recommend his classes for elective credit or just to take for fun.

Dr. LaMotta was one of my favorite professors I ever had. He knows his stuff very well. If you are interested in SW archaeology I know of no one better. His presentation style is very clear and professional. There is absolutely no reason to do poor in any of his classes.
His classes cover interesting material and are very enjoyable.
Cool and helpful professor. If you go to class, attend every lab and actually try, you will get an A.

This was an interesting class and pretty easy if you use the study guides he gives. The questions are usually from the lectures and study guide is pretty complete. As long as you do moderate effort and use the study guide you'll get an A.
The most BORING lectures I have ever had. His grading scale doesn't even make sense and there is too much material for a 200 level course. I regret taking this class.

My TA graded the labs very harshly. This is honestly one of the hardest 100 level classes at UIC. A lot of information for every test (3 of them) that is overwhelming to register. You have to work really hard.
Several quizzes on lecture material, two exams, and one project. The American southwest is his field of study, so it's pretty interesting.
Exams are tough but there are only two (midterm, final). Annotated bibliography is easy. Would recommend for Anthro majors. He also really likes Star Wars.

I admit, his lectures are very dry, but the subject matter is very interesting, so it kind of evens out! Tests are taken DIRECTLY from lecture, so you better go. If you study from lecture notes, you'll have no problem on the tests. Labs are easy, but sometimes they're a little long. In the end, I wouldn't mind taking a class with him again.

HE is a very BORING LECTURER. You get sleepy real fast because he dims the lights. His lectures really don't line up with the exams! LAB was extremely easy. I had an A for the average in lab and a C average for exams and still got a C in the class. He didn't curve either, even though the exam averages were low (always a D average).

I took this class because it was required for gen ed's. It actually was not that bad. & The TA's were helpful, and knowledgeable. If you come to class, do the readings you will do okay. This class isn't an easy A, but it was a very interesting class. I definitely prefer this class over a chemistry or physics class any day.

the TA's grade all the labs extremely hard. The test are almost inmpossible, you have to attend lecture you have to read the book. Don't take this class unless you want to work extremely hard for a B in the class. It is way to much information for a 100 level course. Don't take this Anthro class unless your an Anthro major

Genuinely nice guy.Some "pop" quizzes but very simple & he really does warn you ahead of time in a not so subtle way.He really just wants you to learn and enjoy & Im actually going 2 take him again!He may be dry 4 some & if thats the case print the online notes and zone off a bit in class but Do pay attention and attend lectures! Taking notes help

Very smart man.  His delivery can be dry, but I learned so much from this course; I usually have a hard time with the sciences (as an English major, I was required to take a lab, so I chose the least "science-y" one, Intro to Archaeology), but this class/subject is more interdisciplinary which was great.  I would highly recommend Prof. LaMotta.

I tried so hard for nothing. He wants you to know theory, but his tests are all about specific details. He wants to help you, but he struggles relating to undergraduates. He's not comfortable talking to people with less than a PhD. It's UIC. Most of us are brain dead. Break things down for us, in little words. Please.

Excellent professor, gives very thorough powerpoints in class. Attendance is mandatory, but with his powerpoints, you'll want to go. Reading of book is unnecessary. I took two of his classes and got easy As!

Very nice guy. Responded very quickly to emails. Homework due each week but you can do it in groups so that's nice l. We just had quizzes and then one exam at the end. It wasn't too bad of a class at all.
Terrible. Non accommodating & if there is a technical issue your grade will suffer. He would not let me rejoins quiz after my laptop died.

One of the top 3 worst professors I've had. The biggest issue was his inflexibility. Every other Thursday we had a 30 question quiz (length of an exam) that was only available from 3:30-7pm. So, if you work, commute, or do literally anything else during that time, you're screwed. Asked for an extension/new time for the quiz and was rudely denied.

Class entirely online and graded on bi-weekly tests and homeworks. He uploads the book PDF so you save money, but half of the test answers are not in the book and you need to think the way he does to answer them, which is difficult when you don't know his train of thought. Heavy curve though which is a plus but most people still get a C or below.

reviews.comment: This guy seriously doesn't know how to teach. He went over the slides very fast and wrapped up everything so you are so easy to get confused. He will give curve but even with that the average of the class still ended up getting a low C. TRY TO AVOID HIM IF YOU CAN!!!

reviews.comment: He says everything is "really simple", yet his tests are everything you don't need to know, and most likely won't know. He has big curves, and utilized them for 27 years.. This guy does not know how to teach. His tests are complete bs and try to trick you more than testing what you need to know. They're way harder than they need to be. He just reads off his slides. Very difficult class that requires a heavy curve. The curve is not very clear, it isn't specifically disclosed until the very end. This professor was hands down one of the worst professors I have ever had.  His teaching methods were awful and extremely hard to follow.  He was very fair when it came to exams, but it was hard to learn anything in the class if you did not teach yourself.  I would not recommend taking a class from this professor.

THE WORST PROFESSOR I HAVE EVER HAD! If the midterm average is a "D", its time to change your teaching techniques Lee. 60% of the students in the class dropped the course because you have NO clue what your grade is until the end of the course. The material is actually really interesting, but you are better off teaching yourself at home.

The shocking thing is I acutally liked this material. He still uses an overhead projector and his tests usually have a twist to the question that was not in the homework. If you are a math major, you won't have a problem. Get material online from other programs from other schools. Same info but much easier to understand.
He is hard to understand.

Very difficult to understand; classroom attendance was useless, - his lectures made the otherwise easy material more confusing.  Nice guy, but very poor teacher.  Curve is generous but not sufficient to compensate for poor instruction and availability of help outside the class.
Very boring class. He's very hard and most the class don't do good.  He is however a fair man and has really great curves which will help u suceed in the course.

Memorize how he does problems. He tells you exactly what problems will be on the test w/samples. Dont miss class. Once a date is set for exam-HW, that's it. He will cancel the lab session and make himself avail during then. Hard material, but is not impossible.My last semester and they are taking IDS450 out of requirements for the major.UIC Sucks.

The material is easy, but the teacher confuses you so much you are ought to fail it. He makes fun of students, mocks them. You can't talk back because he'll put you on his**** list instantly.  Worst teacher I ever had.
just awful

Best Professor for IDS450(hahaha...) There's no other professor like Lee, one of his kind, nothing to say but the best.  Keep up the good work prof. Some friendly advise:don't miss class at all(even if you need to go to the emergency room), copy everything he writes, and memorize all the ex. he solves in class. That's it, you should b able to pass.

Unfortunately, people who are in the IDS program at UIC have to take the class for the major. He is the only one who teaches this class.  He mocks his students and intimidates students during the tests.  People are doing bad but he does nothing to change the way he teaches the class.

If you take ids 450, it is likely that you will fail and have to take it again. The only advice I can give you is memorize everything. Don't try to understand the material because it'll only make the memorizing harder
I hate him more than any prof I've ever had. He's extremely unreasonably all the while pretending to be helpful. He will also mock you.
Everything is "no problem" but I never understand what he's talking about
No Comments

She is a very caring professor who genuinely wants her students to succeed. 100% take her class because she explains things clearly and makes the class a great experience. The group projects were very fun.

Professor Trujillo is a very caring professor who genuinely wants her students to succeed. 100% take her class because she explains things clearly and makes the class a great experience. The group projects were fun.
Professor Trujillo is a very caring professor who genuinely wants her students to succeed. 100% take her class because she explains things clearly and makes the class a great experience.

TAKE this professor, you won't regret it. She is very caring and inspirational and really tries her best to help everyone. The assignments are not hard if you pay attention, which makes sense to me. She is AMAZING!

100% take this professor for MKTG 469. The class is interesting enough that you'll want to actually learn and come to class, and it's easy enough where you can get an A if you're the type who doesn't really care about the content. We even had a fieldtrip to Chinatown!!!
So disorganized it is a mess to follow the material sometimes. It is very easy to get an A if you finish the assignments on time. She is caring but the lectures are boring

She is a nice person, but not the best proffessor. She will tell you to pick the BEST answer when several are correct. Context? doesn't matter. Nuance? nope. Be prepared to get things wrong and not understand why.

Professor Torres is a great professor, a very caring, and understanding lady! Her lectures are engaging, and as long as you pay attention, and do the work you will get an easy A. Her group project assignments were really intresting, and somehing I enjoyed doing. I learned a lot about markering, and looked forward coming to her class every week!

Professor Torres is very sweet, and I enjoyed her class! It wasn't very work-heavy; you only needed to keep up with discussion posts and work on two group presentations. She is also very lenient on grading and provides good feedback. Opt for her if you can!

Honestly, she is one of the best professors ever, I would take her for all my marketing classes if I could. She is very lenient and understanding, the definition of "as long as you do your assignment, you will get an A." She is not a harsh grader at all and gives amazing feedback on presentations. Take her classes if you can!
One the best professors at UIC. Very easy A!

Global Marketing with her was enjoyable. Easy grader, easy assignments, almost all groupwork. 2 Midterms, No Final, Team Projects include paper and presentation for: Midterm, Final and Case study. Lectures are for points and she does her best to make it interesting. Discussion posts are only for the first half of the yr.

"Extensions are reserved for significant situations such as a death in the immediate family or a student being hospitalized". Although I can understand the importance of fairness, but it dismisses a student's reason for an extension. If fairness is what is aimed for, we need to learn about equity (which is a core nursing belief, by the way).

Unwilling to work with students. Stubborn (her way is the only way). She is a harsh grader not just a hard grader. Avoid if you can. Take the class with a different professor or even in another semester if need be.

Had her for 332 and 397.  In 332 she was horrible.  Very strict.  397, she seemed a lot better. Still tough grader, and any mistakes were seen as "med errors." Everything has to be current, but her examples and literature were from 10+ years ago.  She made the program horrible for me.  Don't ask questions, you won't get a clear answer.  Good luck!

I don't understand why her reviews are so horrible. She's a quick and fair grader and not very nitpicky. The class was fairly easy. Just follow the rubrics and assignment instructions and you will pass.

Dr. Vega is a tough grader and expects a lot from students. It took me awhile to understand her "harshness," but I realized it was due her form of getting students ready for the final class to earn your Bachelor's of Science in Nursing. She expects you to learn from your mistakes and find ways to improve on yourself.

reviews.comment: Professor Vega isrude for someone that works in the nursing field. She nitpicks everything, yet on multiple occasions, I have noted grammatical errors in her instruction She expects you to be 100% accurate or it is seen as a "medical error", yet the same is not required from her. Unfortunately, she is the only instructor teaching NUR 397.

Does not communicate well. Extremely harsh grader. No leniency whatsoever. Deducts points if you blink the wrong way. I had her multiple times and every time it was like living an educational nightmare. She really made my experience at UIC miserable.

Professor Leta Vega has a condescending attitude towards students; she expects them to be 100% accurate and even deducts points for minor issues, yet in the same tone, her materials are outdated and often contain numerous errors. Her instructions are vague, and when you ask for clarification, she refers you back to the exact unclear instructions.

Does not give clear instructions and will deduct major points without allowing you to defend your answer. When you ask a question, it is rare to get a helpful response. If you miss both places to turn in your assignment, she will not grade it and will deduct 50% off the assignment automatically. No liency and does not care about the students

Nothing positive to say about this instructor. I can't believe UIC hired such an awful instructor to lead aspiring nursing students. This professor really knows how to suck the life out of you and ruin your experience in this online program. Avoid crossing this instructors path at all cost.

Extremely harsh grading with unclear instructions. she was almost hunting for any deductible mistakes (which are bound to happen with unclear instructions) and would take off 20-30 points for minute errors. Completely unapproachable and has no concept of work/life/school balance whatsoever. Made the class unbearable. Good luck !

EVERYTHING that has been said about this professor is true.  She teaching Nurse Caring Theory, yet she is not caring at all.  Don't ask any questions, because you won't get an answer that helps.  She just reiterates what the instructions say.  I could go on and on about how bad of a professor she is.  And she surely should NOT be teaching CARING!

Using old material but expects you to use up-to-date within 3 year articles/studies/journals. Grades awful even if you miss a partial instruction. Has no leniency even though this is an online class and people work full time and have lives outside of nursing school. Many not working links in the class and many hiccups but expect us to be lenient.

she doesn't clarify her assignments' instructions. She does not understand work/school balance, and she emails you regarding other students dropping out of her class that were in your group. Be prepared to do a lot. tough grader in general

Tried to fail me for not knowing how to change keynote to PowerPoint when if you have a Mac it will automatically download something as keynote (had to learn this the hard way). Do not recommend.

She used redundant learning materials over and over in the weeks in both classes I took with her.  She is overly strict on APA and doesn't explain things well.  She states in her syllabus she considers something that is submitted to the wrong spot will be docked because she considers it the equivalent of a medication error.  Are you kidding me?
She teaches caring theory while uncaring students. Instruction is not clear. Grading is inconsistent. Lack of constructive feedback.

Everything everyone else has said is accurate. She does not care about students and thinks too highly of herself and her course. She is not helpful when you reach out to her & is demeaning with her responses. It's ironic because what she teaches students about being a caring nurse is the opposite of her conduct toward others.

reviews.comment: Avoid her if possible, she is your typical nursing professor who goes on about their accolades but is the worst communicator. She will go in circles when you ask for any further detail or explanation, "As per my instructions..." "Please read the resources provided..." REALLY annoying especially when you are simply asking for clarification.
Unrealistic and too high expectations from students. Tough grader and was not quick to get back with an explanation when I reached to clarify her HW
Very unprofessional. Encourages students to ask questions but whenever asked always has a smart remark and no clear or definite answer.

I took this class without any prior knowledge of the professor or of the course, purely out of interest in the subject. You will fail this class if you don't attend lectures (only about 15/40 students consistently attended). Prof. Reyzin is a fantastic teacher who is extremely passionate about what he teaches, take advantage and, GO TO CLASS!

THE WORST

I've seen grades for previous semesters, and it's always like this! He doesn't curve or provide feedback for your homework. If you have him as your professor, just drop the class. It isn't worth it!

Don't take the class with him! There are many professors who are better than him.
I regret taking the class with him!
Take him if no other options. He knows his stuff but can't explain well. Attend office hours and you will be fine!

Lectures are interesting. Need to attend lectures to get clarity of concepts. Homework is graded based on effort not correctness. Professor is clear on the difficulty of exams and what he expects of the students. Overall a great class.

No matter the partice questions or the exams, there is no commonality at all. There is no clear enough solution mode, and all topics rely on narration and on-the-spot play.
