The tests were a bit in depth so reading the book and going to lecture was important even though he did not take attendance. Lecture was also a plus when it was really cold out side or really nice because he then gave extra credit for showing up to class.

He is an awesome teacher for Comm 103. As long as u go to class and take notes, you're totally fine. Comm 200, however, is a different story! He talks really fast in lecture & its hard to get down exactly what he says sometimes. And his tests are like 30 questions, short answer & very hard! The best grade on our mid-term was a C before the curve

If you want to pass his test go to class. His lectures are not always out the book. He talks pretty fast so if you want to catch everything buy a recorder. Overall pretty reasonable class. 3exams, 3quizzes, a group presentation, a media log and a number of chanced to recieve extra credit.
No Comments
Professor Omar was very informative and took time to engage the class participants and ensure that the topic was correctly understood.

I don't go to lecture because I work but I still did good overall and got a B. The exams are not hard but not easy either. I would recommend students at UIC to take this professor but sadly this is his last semester at UIC :(

Extra Credit questions on exams, easy journal assignments, and 1 extra credit journal at the end. Do read the powerpoints and look at specific details carefully, however, since he does like to put statistics and other small details on his exam. He does do a slight curve though. If enough of class gets certain questions wrong,he adds pts to everyone

Professor Jamil is a good professor, his lectures are straight to the point, his exams are from his notes and book, weekly homework was easy, and he gives extra-credit which is very helpful. I would take him again.

P. Jamil is a great professor! His class is really easy if you attend and take good notes! Make sure you pay attention to his examples because they are used on exams. Weekly hw is really easy. Exams are based off lecture notes. I got 95% on all 3 exams by reading the book, covering his slides, & attending class+ taking notes! 4 e.c. ? on his exams

One of the easiest classes I have ever taken. Just take good notes, or review the lectures he posts online and that is basically what the exams consist of. Do weekly journals, easiest points to earn. They help a lot in determining final grade. Overall super easy A class if you do avg on exams and get full Journal points.

Loved taking community psychology with Professor Jamil(highly recommend)! Attend class and pay attention for minimal use of textbook. Weekly 2 page journal assignments worth 3 points each (really easy). Multiple choice exams, non cumulative final. Lots of extra credit opportunities!

His class is pretty easy if you put in the effort. It's better to come to class since he emphasizes certain parts from the text, but you'll survive if you only read the book. There are weekly journals, which help boost your grade and 3 exams (non-cumulative) with 4 extra credit questions in each.

Easy class. Attend lectures and take good notes. Then go through book and take notes on what he didn't speak of in class. Study all that and you're set! Extra Credit is offered in every exam, so that really helps!
Really wish he would review before his exams. They are hard, especially if you don't know the information in the book well. Journals due every week that helps your grade.

Prof Jamil is nice and helpful; however his lectures are a bit dry. Class is not mandatory however I would suggest to go prior to exams to figure out key things that will be on them.  Weekly journals (easy), 3 (non-cumulative exams), overall very easy class!

Weekly journals (2 pagers minimum) and 3 exams (non-cumulative final). That's pretty much it. I found that attendance isn't mandatory because the exams are all based off of the book, but he clarifies and highlights parts during lecture that can be helpful. He's cool. Course, overall, is a bit boring.

He likes to say "you know" which really bothers me. I think textbook is helpful because I cannot pay attention in his class. His class is really boring. I never take notes. I study textbook for exams.

Nice teacher. VERY Boring class. Exams are a bit hard. Textbook is not highly recommended. Shows a lot of clips on class, that was the only fun part. Very robotic voice. Doesn't seem so interested in class.

Weekly HW helps boost your grade. Otherwise there are just tests. Final is non cumulative. Prof shows videos in class and does some activities that include talking to neighbors. Never really use the book. Study and youll do fine. Prof Jamil is great

He's an interesting guy, uses a lot of video clips for supplementals. Class is an easy A, exam and midterm are straight from the notes, lectures aren't necessary, but definitely worth going interest wise. Quizzes are online, and there were 5 very easily graded hw assignments. Take him if you can get him.
Very easy class with lots of extra credit options.

Very laid back class. All the material on the exams was given in the lecture. The book isn't really required but I found it helpful at some points (like writing the 5 papers and taking the 5 quizzes). It's an easy A if you read the notes.

One of the best classes and best teachers at UIC. The class was super easy I barely attended and never bought the book and I got an A in the class. Homework and quizzes were easy. I totally recommend this class with this teacher. Amazing teacher. Completely recommend him.

Great Professor, class is interesting and very easy.  The material is mostly from his lecture outlines.  The material on exams is very easy.  The extra credit is a little ridiculous (can increase grade by 4%).  Bottom line: If you do not get an A in his class think about dropping out of college.

Sarah was so kind and understanding, she knew that most of us in the class hadn't taken math in a while so she was very considerate to that. I would reccomend asking her all of your questions and having clear communication, it makes the class easier.

WOW seriouslyyyy,,,the best TA i have ever had at UIC..she is amazing...i wish i have her for all my classes. She is really nice, helpful, and really help you to learn the material. Had a bad prof, but she helped me alot. Sarah is totally the besttttt...TAKE HER if you can...i guarantee you will like her too ^.^

Best TA EVER! She wants you to do well and asks everyone if they understand numerous times. I almost didn't pass because of my own study habits but she helped me pass and not only by teaching well. SUPER nice and can never get mad at anyone. I 100% recommend her and if i could take her again, i would.
She is the best TA in whole math department.  She is extremely helpful and she knows the material very well, so she can explain you good way.  She is really easy grader.  She is beautiful.

Amazing TA!!! She will never get mad at the class or yell at anyone. She is pretty laid back and helps anyone during class and office hours! She is really really nice and will not treat you like your stupid. I had her for 2 semesters and I loved her. It was better than my heavily-accented math professors... At least I could understand her!
Sarah is the best TA ever! She is very helpful and gives tons of out of class help.  She even got us a pizza party! Take Sarah for sure...she's the best!
No Comments

I took Prof.Harmansah's AH 110 course in the fall. It was very difficult, even with 12 credit hours. If you must take this class, please take thorough notes on the video lectures. They made the exams easier. The course content was interesting. The professor himself is sweet, though he barely pops up. Manage your time!!

It's really hard to like this class since it's not worth so much tedious lecture watching and notetaking for a 100 level course. Your grades completely ride on the 3 exams and museum essay, because doing bad on any will tank you a letter grade. The textbook is not even necessary, its just an extra cash grab by the professor. Do not buy it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class has a crazy workload for a 100 level class. If you don't need it for your major don't take it. That being said, it's not the worst AH course I've taken. You rarely see Omur in person but when you do he's very pleasant and sweet and you can tell he has a lot of passion for AH. However, the online lectures are lengthy ~4-7 hrs a week.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Harmansah himself had incredibly detailed, passionate lecture videos… though they were a tad outdated and really long. He does care a lot about his students. But for a 100 level class this was definitely so much more work heavy than it needed to be and expectations on assignments weren't always clear. He is so sweet though.
Horrible class

Dr. Omurshah is a very kind man, and his class was easy for me. While it is true that the tests (2 mid terms and one final) are all free response only, they are a little bit stressful, they are also open note where you are given a study guide which contains all of the artworks that may potentially appear on the test. Video lectures best at speed 2x

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. The tests are free-response only, and each question is timed. You get 5 minutes to hand-write 150-200 words comparing two art pieces FOR EACH QUESTION. At the end of the test, there is a section where you must write 700-800 words within 15 minutes. In other words, this class requires too much pressure for a 100-level class.

Long lecture videos, sometimes up to 4 hours but you can watch them at 1.25/1.5 since he speaks pretty slow. Weekly quizzes on lecture videso but theyre pretty easy as long as you pay attention and take some notes. Study guides for exams are pretty straighforward and very useful. Never actually read the textbook, only read readings for discussion.
He is quite inconsiderate and rude. His class is definitely not a beginners introduction.

I 100% agree with every negative review for this course that has been left. This class took a toll on my mental health and often made me feel incredibly stressed and confused. The amount of work is obscene for a 100 level beginner course, and it felt like I walked away not really learning much. Avoid this class at all costs I'm begging you.

Passionate, but he has no regard for student mental health and well-being: weekly quizzes that have no weight on our grades, hours of lengthy video lectures that clash with the textbook, 3 hours to complete exams that require more time. He can have an attitude when emailed so I stopped. He believes his class should be at the pinnacle of your life.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: 3+ hrs of lecture videos + multiple chapters of textbook per week. Talks extensively about history (only basics required to know for tests). Did not help students develop art/historical analysis skills (TA had to). Does not show up to in person class (TA does). Puts content from guest lectures on study guides then does not use it on tests.

The professor himself is sweet, but the sheer amount of work is insane. Each week we get assigned around 10 lecture videos each around 15-30min long along with 30 or so pages to read from a textbook. That's just half of it and this class is supposed to be the least of my worries. At least the content was somewhat interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: So many long lectures weekly… lolHe seems like a nice professor but unfortunately I find it difficult to keep up with this class even though it's a gen ed. Idk i took it thinking it would be interesting but tbh it's not what u think it's gonna be at all. Quizzes every week as well and the midterm reviews they give do not help at all! Pointless tbh.

Weekly 3+ hours of online lectures, weekly quizzes, memorizing countless artifacts/architectures, annotating extensive articles before every weekly discussion, and timed midterm essays. Most exhausting class I've ever taken. You'll also need to bring a plethora of notes to participate in discussion, otherwise pray your TA doesn't cold call on you.

This class is really not that hard; it's just time consuming and requires effort. There's a quiz on the pre-recorded 2-3 hours of lecture per week but it's not hard if you pay attention and take notes. The 2 midterms and a paper is like, not great, but he does seem to take feedback as he increased the time limit to 3 hours and seems passionate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: An absolutely bogus class that doesn't adapt to any valid, reasonable, student feedback and/or critique. This class is required for art majors and I have NEVER met someone who enjoyed this class at all. It is an obscene amount of work- nobody I know has time to sit through his 50 weekly mind-numbing lectures and uninteresting reading assignments.
Can be petty if you disagree with certain timing, even if the TA's and other classes agree. TA's made it livable.
I had to start going to therapy because of this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: praying for anybody that takes this class because I swear for an art level 100 class, there's nothing easy about this course. this was a hybrid class where class was only on Friday while you're required to watch about 10+ video lectures that are half an hour long on top of the 3 midterms that majority of the class didn't understand. terrible class!
if you have to take this course? Thoughts and prayers.

Wouldn't recommend for those who have no interest in art & are only looking for an easy elective. Homework heavy (tests, lectures, readings, and 2 essays) but definitely doable if you are only taking 12 credits for the semester like I did. If you want to pass, manage your time well. Professor is definitely very passionate & wants you to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Interesting and thorough lectures although very lengthy. If you put the work in and are transparent with TA's you can get a good grade in the class. Open note tests included being able to identify up to 60 ancient artifacts and write about them. If you have no interest in anything Art History related dont take the class. caring and passionate prof

This is a very tough workload and unreasonable for a 100 level class. constant lecture+notes then quizzes with intense essays. if you must take this class, clear your schedule and get ready for a lot of information. Very,very hard to focus through the lengthy lectures. Brace yourself and don't fall behind. You need a very strong will. I didn't.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: It is difficult to stay focused on all the pre recorded video lectures given each week. Especially remembering each detail for the discussion because it usually only goes one direction.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: this is my 4th year at uic, so I have a lot of experience with other levels of classes. I took this bc I have an interest for art and wanted something easy. I was so wrong. 2 midterms, a final, two papers. The professor and TA expect you to know things like you have a PhD in art history. Work load makes 0 sense for a 100 level class.

RUN! JUST RUN AND IF YOU HAVE TO TAKE THIS CLASS THEN PRAY YOU PASS! This class has been nothing more than stress, tears, panic, and frustration. 
 You will be learning by 2-3hr of recorded long lectures that is more history and archeology than actual art history. 2 midterms, one final, two papers that you would have to take in this course. RUN
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The professor is knowledgeable and the information is interesting but the class is an absolute nightmare. I have a 4.0 gpa this 110 level art history class has been the most annoying thing I've dealt with in school. Do Not Take It.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Omur. has been my biggest nightmare since freshman year.I failed his ART 110 class back in 2018, and I took it again in 2021 thinking that he'd be better. What an absolute mistake! Tough grader, awful at communicating, and worst of all the exams. The "study guides" that he provides you, are images, and are left to research 100+ artifacts. AHHH
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Omur did no work in regards to helping students. He assigned way too many papers for a 110 level class. Not to mention for the final paper he seemed to have graded it with the expectations we are all art historians, which is obviously not the case. He also seems very pompous and doesn't offer any feedback for grades, just makes you feel stupid.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Don't take this class. It's the hardest class I have ever taken in my life. You are graded by few things and they don't update your grade till the very end. Many papers to write. I appreciate his passion but his assignments are not specific enough and you're left to figure it out on your own. It's so much work and reading to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: To put it nicely, this class made me want to be unalive. I took this as a random elective class, and that was a huge mistake. Lectures are LONG. Sometimes 3+ hours worth of lectures a week. There are MANY long writing assignments and you take 2 midterms for some reason. It is an exhausting class and if you don't have to take it, absolutely do not.

This class is the most work intensive class I've ever taken. I feel like Dr. Harmansah sets his students up to fail. The lectures are extremely dense and required, but have most of the same info as the readings but the textbook has more info. I hate this class with all of my being. If its a requirement, find a way to waive it. hes nice tho
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: In the beginning, I felt like h was a good teacher and he knew about art but he is more of an archaeologist than an art historian. I'm sorry but he doesn't know much about art. Otherwise, he's ok.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: There's nothing to retain or learn because he does not explain the readings at all when they're immensely dense, don't understand how he's a teacher. He lets PhD students dominate the conversation and ignores others who comment. States he has favorites. Shouldn't be listed as an anthro or art history class--nothing in the content deals with either.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you talk to Omur after class, he will let you know what you have to do. AH110 is very lecture heavy and the exams are a workload. If you study, the exams are fairly easy. The lectures start becoming more interesting after the first few weeks, but the first few weeks drag and are boring. Omur is a caring professor but you do need to work.

A very interesting class. The readings are a repetition of what goes on in lecture. Overall, i loved the class. Although the tests are a bit difficult, they are manageable as long as you study. He also cracks jokes here and there to keep his audience awake, which works! Although the content may seem dull he makes it seem fun and interesting.

I took two of his art history classes. They were more history (and archaeology) than art but they were very good. He assigns lots of readings and expects a lot from students but his classes have stayed with me and impacted me in ways that few other classes have so they're definitely worth taking. My favorite was his urbanism class.

Prof Harmansah is extremely kind and does want you to pass as other people have said here. However, the size of the class is perhaps not suitable for the style of teaching he seems to want to  have. It seems that he isn't that tough of a grader, but when it comes down to the exam, it's a whole different ballgame.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: While certainly a nice man, he seemed fundamentally unable to grab the attention of the students. He seemed to get so lost in many of his presentations that it often seemed like he was talking to himself. He was so boring that in my class so many people weren't coming to lecture that he had to make attendance mandatory, and people still didn't come

The lectures were interesting but readings were extremely long, although fortunately in the form of PDF.  The exams were hard because you both have to memorize a ton of art object details and the history.  If you put in the effort, which you absolutely have to and I didn't , you could pass. It just was not for me though.

Professor Omur is brilliant and knows what he's talking about all the time. He encourages you to ask questions and is very kind. The biggest thing is that he wants you to do well in his class and it requires a lot of work on your behalf. Make sure you do your readings and get your papers revised by him.
Smart lecturer, definitely not a teacher to take a "blow-off" class with.

Professor Opacich is absolutely horrible as a teacher. Shes inconsiderate and she grades harshly for papers as if were English majors. She talks a lot, and shes very selfish about the issues of students. Most professors are understanding but Opacich acts like a dictator, as if the voices and opinions of students doesnt matter.
This professor loves to hear herself talk. Not very understanding and realistic about this issues students has. The program needs work but shes not very receptive to that. I

Literally in the middle of a pandemic acted as if her class was the only one that was being taken. On the papers if you didn't explicitly state that this is that and such you got points off. You would have to write as if you were talking to a toddler. very irritating and in my opinion not a good teacher at all. BEWARE!

Decent and interesting class. Graded by a few things so it's easy to mess up, take advantage of extra credit. You can find the textbook online. Group project at the end but take my advice and start early, with this being online it Is difficult to get a hold of your group. Use the writing center for your essays and you'll get a good score.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: I took PUBH 100 as an elective. Worse decision I made. The class is graded by a very few one point assignments and exams and essays. The workload is extremely heavy for a 100 level class. Wouldn't recommend taking if you had an option.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: During the course, you were required to write a shot paper about an issue pertaining to young adults. Mine was binge drinking in college students. Within this essay, you had to write about your campaign, and provide scientific evidence from multiple sources and state partners that may help you to acknowledge this issue. Karen graded very harshly.

If you have to take this class be super hard on yourself there's so little room to make a mistake. The main big assignments are out of max 20 points, and she's a super harsh grader to the point of being unreasonable. The class itself is barely interesting, and she sucks at making tests. Take another public health class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class was really informative. I ended up getting a pretty in-depth, comprehensive overview of public health. Having speakers come in was fun. You watch a couple documentaries in class (some are hit or miss). Was assigned readings from the book, so I'd say the book is necessary. Easy read though. Keep in mind, I took this class in the summer.

Professor Opacich was nice and understanding.  There were 1 exam, 2 papers, and a group presentation.  She gave 5% of extra credit in the class. The group presentation was very important (25%). So students needed to spend time to do it. Take her if you can. Attendance was not mandatory but it would affect the grade.
Took her class for an elective and I learned some interesting things. I really liked Opacich. She was really nice and fair. She was also encouraging and helpful. Easy A.

She did not teach us at all. She would have us watch movies all the time. We had major assignments that we did not learn anything about. She was a hard grader, and everything is worth like 1,5, or 10 points. So if you mess up on one assignment you're screwed. I was very excited for this class, unfortunately taught nothing.
Hard grader
Absolutely awful.  Never taught us anything yet expected us to do well on exams that were short answer with no study guide? We watched movies everyday and knew nothing.  Very hard grader.

Professor Orit is passionate about her teaching and very flexible with assignments if you communicate with her. AHS 330 was not a difficult class; the material was engaging and informative. I plan to take another class with her next semester.

Ill never have anything but good words about her. I took two classes of hers this semester and it was my best decision. She has helped me so much. And she is by far the most knowledgable and experienced rehab professional out there, shes dipped her toes in everything. Take her class, you will pass if you just show up and try.

She is the best professor i've had in all my 3 years at UIC.

100% the most passionate and knowledgeable teacher ive met. She even helped me get a job in rehab by being one of my recommendations. She is an amazing tool to keep in your back pocket and she is so happy to help her students be successful. Just do your best on attendance really.

Prof Schwartz is an amazing prof at uic. Her lectures are very interesting and provide so much information. The conditions are a huge part of mid-terms and finals. Studying is required to pass as long as you put in the work there is no reason why you should not pass. She is a very caring a nice prof and works with her students.

Pay attention to class and you will do great! The final and midterm were based on the medical conditions. The final is the material covered after the midterm.

We had a group presentation as another major grade but she graded fairly and let you use your notes.
She is such a wonderful person and professor. I took AHS 325 as well and got an A
I love Professor Orit, she is so kind and understanding. Her grading is not tough but is fair. As long as you try, you will do great.

Theres a good amount of assignments, but as long as you review her discussion slides and the few papers she assigns as reading, you'll definitely pass. She gives feedback on all assignments so that you can improve on the next. There's also a good amount of reading a good 7-8 pg. rarely. She's understanding, just communicate with her beforehand.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I loved Labor Econ! This class requires consistent effort but it never felt overwhelming. Professor Ost's goal is to help you become a better writer, and he provides you with great feedback on a few short 2-page writing assignments. One final 5-page project. Very manageable. No traditional MC exams or quizzes. Engaging, fun lectures.

Professor Ost is an amazing teacher, period. He seriously made me consider getting my PhD in economics because he is so intelligent and has such a precise, clear way of explaining things. Most econ classes are hella boring but he has such an engaging teaching style where it doesn't feel like he's lecturing you. I cant rec him enough

Really nice guy, passionate about his expertise. You NEED to attend class and keep up with the homework-- that's it. There are no surprises. Just keep tabs on your assignments and go to class and you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great professor. Make sure to take notes and pay attention in class, lectures arent hard to follow. Doesnt post notes or powerpoints. Helps guide students to the correct answer. Assignments arent difficult but due every class. If you dont understand something hell help you find the answer yourself and is direct.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Mainly writing
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Great professor. The only one I have had at UIC that encouraged students to have a sit down at the beginning of the semester to learn about each other. His lectures are clear and he uses examples that require thought. There are no tests, but an assignment is due almost every class. Take him and at the very least you will become a better writer.

Super smart guy, one of the best econ classes I've had.  The class is structured in a way that requires continuous effort, but assignments aren't overwhelming.  Very approachable and goes out of his way to ensure students succeed.  Wish he taught more undergrad classes, would take him again for sure.  Attendance/punctuality mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: He's a revolutionary educator.

Professor Ost is not an easy A, but his lectures are incredible and well organized. Go to class and take notes, work hard on all the assignments, and study for the quizzes. Apply a steady amount of time during the entire semester and you will do well. Ost is definitely not a subjective grader so writing must be substantial.

It's an easy class. The book wasn't helpful, and his notes are the hw and quizzes. He never posts the notes on Blackboard, so write down EVERYTHING. I didn't and lost a lot of points. Most annoying thing was required attendance, and he gave clicker quizzes right at the beginning. To be fair, it does get boring, but not difficult. Didn't learn much.

Awesome Professor and great class! He is the most innovative Professor I've ever had. There are no tests but a lot of homework which teaches you everything you need to know in the class. Lectures are very interesting and fun. The clicker quizzes make you pay attention and come to class on time. He is helpful and his grading is fair.

Professor Ost is a great professor. Lays out all grading criteria and sticks to it. No tests just homework and easy 2 page papers. Definitely take him for the necessary writing course. Show up to class and you'll get at least a B.

Really hard class but Professor Ost is a smart dude. Take this if you enjoy Economics and want to be challenged. Spend some time on concepts, then focus on topics. We read so many articles and he uses a lot of of research during his lectures. Ex. does college make you smarter, or do patient people go to college? Should we raise the min. wage?

He has a dry sense of humor so we've had some good laughs during class. He is very tough however. Make sure you turn in all your stuff on time and keep up. No exams, but difficult hw due almost every class. Does scheduled clicker and written quizzes occasionally. Learned a lot though. Be on time, write decent notes (notes -- HW). Learn by doing.
I ended up with a B, which is OK but he never responds to emails did not tell me my grades on my two papers or my two tests.  So, it was a mystery grade.
Overall, he is a great professor. Even though exams are harder than expected, he is really into Jazz and teaches you a lot of stuff about Jazz, so if you really do like Jazz, take him for sure!

Prof. Davis is a great professor, and can provide huge insight into the jazz world. He does have his opinions and goes off on tangents and rants a lot, but he never fails anyone, and as along as you show up and aren't a screwball you will probably get an A, great teacher overall.

The class was pretty dull... He went off into rants about jazz, and I mean, it's great that he's passionate, but he doesn't need to push his views on others... The final was ridiculously hard and caused my grade to drop from an A+ to a B... and I did study for it for several hours...  I recommend you bring your computer for entertainment.

Mr. Davis is absolutely worthless. There's no point in going to lecture. He jumps around way to much, is very disorganized, has no notes, and because of that does a very poor job of lecturing. This is by far the worst "professor" I have had UIC.

Very opinionated class; he thinks jazz is better than classical music, btw classical musical existed way longer jazz. He is extremely disorganized and his notes are everywhere. Hard to distinguish between his opinion and fact.

His notes are everywhere, meaning it's really messy, however, if you study the notes you've taken from class and know people and their history easy A. have to write 2 papers, fairly easy. This professor is not bad at all

Jazz class fills up with reg. very fast. During class 1/2 student are absent. Lectures are notso organized. Plays lot of music =fun. "i don't like giving F's and D's". Gave out ~40 extra credit. 2 easy papers - easy grading. 2 exams (midterm and final) - all multiple choice. In review, he READS off the exam, keep that in mind - even he admitted it!

i really enjoyed this class. yes he's very passionate about jazz, but hello, thats a good thing! if you keep an open mind and open ear, he can really get you into jazz. hes a fun guy and this class was one of my favs, even though im not a big jazz fan. if you study and go to class, and actually pay attention in class, you should be fine.

reviews.comment: This professor's teaching style promotes independent learning, with YouTube as a helpful supplement. His lectures are concise, emphasizing core concepts. Though his direct approach can be challenging, it encourages student accountability. When difficulties arise, he underscores the importance of personal effort and understanding.
Difficult professor to work with. Professor / student connection is not there at all. Get ready to learn everything by yourself. Effort alone is not enough.

reviews.comment: Great class! Take again!

He will write the first half of an undergraduate analysis text book on the board during the semester. Will have to know a lot of the proofs he does, but gives review sheet. All of his proofs are impressively  easy to understand, and they all build off of each other so you don't get lost. Curves generously. Does review sessions. Nice guy.

Not sure what everyone is talking about. He is the single most amazing professor I've had in my college career. His notes are priceless and have proven to be more useful than any book. Detailed, clear and to the point, and he actually CARES about the students. His door is always open and he is always more than willing to help. Wants you to learn!!

he's not clear at all when he explains his exmaples/theorems. He's a genius, i'll give him that. But he doesn't know how to explain to young adults, like us, who are trying to grab the concept. his lectures seems as if he's speaking to other professors in the math department, rather than young students. His curves are pretty good, thats about it

His class is pointless.All he expects you to do is memorize his proofs.His test consists of rewriting the same proofs he did in class.He never responds to emails and he's not very sociable in class.I wouldn't recommend him.
I do not have enough space here to explain precisely why he is bad, but... just take my word and do NOT take class with him!

She's freaking hilarious and beautiful… it's hard to concentrate in her class! 
Very tough and demanding.

She's knowledgeable about a tough subject, which is impressive for her age. She's demanding, yet caring and fair. Be prepared for tough tests and group projects. She does give tons of extra credit opportunities though.

Her beauty and humor can be a distraction and somewhat a disadvantage to her.

Professor Pham can be quite witty. The course is very lecture-heavy and one of the most challenging courses in the CUPPA program I have experienced so far. High grading and high expectations, especially with the group project. Be mentally prepared to put a lot of time and effort. To do well, study with fellow students and work with Professor Pham.

I dreaded having to show up to her class. Her class gave me insane amounts of anxiety. It was hard to keep up, the content it's very difficult and she lacks compassion and understanding. It was difficult getting through this class. Good luck to all you CUPPA students. She is not as "cool" as she tries so hard to be like.

I loved this professor. He is so understanding and so engaging and encourages everyone to pick topics that specifically interest them as an individual. He helped me improve my writing a lot, and if you put in the work for this class it is an easy A. He is so personable and overall made class a great experience. Pretty easy class overall.

This is the best professor in the entire school. I took him two semesters in a row and I'm very sad I won't be able to anymore. He is extremely inspiring in the lectures he gives, and he ONLY wants you to succeed. Extremely down to earth, what more could you ask.

His lectures were boring, but the assignments were easy and he's easy on grading. During my class, he talks about nuclear weapons all the time, and that's the only topic we focused on. So unless you're interested in making up stories and interested in politics, it'll be hard for you to have many ideas about nuclear weapons.
He is a wonderful lecturer!
super nice and easy

Had professor Hayek for 2 courses now and he's been nothing but amazing. He has some books for reading but does his best to find online versions for his students. The coursework is clearly outlined in his syllabus but will go out of his way to clarify and further help students by giving them feedback and small 1 on 1 talk about the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Although I didn't like the topic nor the textbook,professor Phil was such an amazing,caring person. He helped and supported me during every essay we had. No strict deadlines but  you have to turn something in to earn points. He's an easy grader and gives feedback on drafts.He tries to make the class enjoyable with funny jokes, I would recommend him

Amazing professor! He's funny, and very down to earth. He always kept class interesting, especially with current events. He gives a lot of great feedback + full credit on assignments. I definitely recommend taking him!
He is very chill, gives full credit but still critiques/gives a lot of feedback.

Took him for 383 and 384. Pretty chill professor that connects with students and is a funny younger guy but don't mistake that for an easy A. One of the few UIC ENGL professors that actually has you do rough drafts and gives edit suggestions. Seriously take him, he's one of the best professors at UIC.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very kind and fun professor, very casual class. An easy A if you participate and attend class. The rhetoric studies can be difficult but Philip is dedicated to workshopping and communicating with you. Highly recommend!
One of the best teachers Ive ever had. Super chill and really funny. Ridiculously easy grader as long as you do the assignments,and made the class really enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Phil is an amazing professor! He connects with his students and wants to make sure everyone knows what to do in order to get the best grade. He gives great feedback and really makes the class enjoyable and fun!

Really easy class. We don't do that much in class so really you can just chill. $ writing assignments and portfolio at the end. Take his suggestions with each assignment and it will increase grade for sure.

He's funny and fair! The assignments he gives are not easy or hard, I'd say as long as you read the instructions and criteria, and take his feedback you'll do good. He cares about his students without being overbearing, he's also understanding and is there to help you in any way he can.I WISH he taught my other English classes :')
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Phil is an overall great professor. Easy to talk to The classroom setting is very laid back and always an open conversation. He is always open to different opinions and perspectives. When you, ask he gives good/specific feedback. This class had 5 projects with various readings throughout the semester but he is not too strict if you miss a reading.

This class was harder than I expected it to be, but it was informational and I did learn a lot of new material. Classroom is light and fun atmosphere, outside work is very technical and has to be done in a specific way. Phil is very accessible outside of class through email or office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Phil is such a great guy, class with him is an open-ended discussion and all his classes are real life based, so it just feels like you're having a talk about regular stuff, but you're actually learning. He starts every class off asking for jokes, and is so easy to talk to.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Phil is amazing. Hes super understanding and open with his students. He genuinely wants to get to know his students. Hes great about extensions and setting reasonable expectations. His classes made my day. You will genuinely enjoy Phil, both as a professor and as a person.

Phil is the greatest professor on the planet. Not only do you learn but he makes class so much fun. He connects with his students and makes sure everyone is comfortable in his class. He is extremely funny and knows his stuff. I would take his class over and over again. Highly recommend.

The best professor i have had at UIC. Very knowledgeable, and approachable. He always comes in with a smile. He is a humble guy even though he is incredibly accomplished and well respected in his field. 10/10
The guy knows econ like the back of his hand

If you like US history, this is the class for you. There are two essays, a midterm, final, and a group debate that determine your final grade. Material is dense so keeping up with it from day one is a must. Professor is fairly lenient and encourages participation. Clearly knows Econ like the back of his hand and you'll learn a lot. Take him
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Such a nice and knowledgeable professor, but lectures are dry and the powerpoints lack information. HW is math heavy, but lecture isn't so it's difficult. Exams require alot of studying . The good thing is that if you fail the midterm and are doing bad, he'll change your grade to whatever you receive on the final.

Professor Pesky was a highlight during my time at UIC. The depth of his knowledge with regards to economics and it's history is something I feel fortunate to have experienced. The class is dense(it could be 3 classes), but if you want to know something you didn't know previously, this class is a must.
Persky is just a good man. I have had him for 3 classes. NOT ONE TIME have I seen him in a bad mood. The lecture material can be dry. But you can tell he really loves it. Smart as hell.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable and enthusiastic prof! You can really learn a lot. One midterm, material heavy but the study guide was extremely helpful and helped to prepare well. Uses i-clicker for attendance- easy points. There's a 10-15pg paper- topic of your choice so it can be a fun activity. Overall enjoyed the class and changed my perspective on history

Persky is such an amazing professor, I don't think I've ever seen him in a bad mood. Material can be a little dry but how crazy can you get with economic history? All his notes are posted on blackboard so the book isn't really necessary. There is a midterm, final, and 12-15 page paper plus i clickers every lecture. Fair class for the most part.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: One of the best professors at UIC. His lectures can get a little dense and obscure, but he is always willing to help if you ask. He really knows his stuff and really cares about his students. Tests are tough but nothing you can't handle. He is the sweetest man.

Genius. Knows everything, very helpful. He really cares about the material and helping you learn it. The homeworks are ridiculous and pretty much unrelated to the tests. Tests are tough but fair. Hard  class but an A is achievable with effort. Read the book. Very handsome.
Awesome professor. I got an A in the class. Just team up with someone to do the weekly homework.

Professor Persky is a very good instructor. He may be confusing at times but does know his stuff. He's extremely helpful and pays attention to how well the class is doing and curves accordingly. If you show up and pay attention you will get an A!
He drives me crazy. Horrible with his scheduling and won't reply e-mails. I don't even know if the final is cumulative or not. Doesn't open homework up until day before exam. HORRIBLE.
Professor Persky is one of the brightest teachers in the econ department. Show up to class and you'll get at least a B.

Professor Persky is one of the most adorable professors I've ever met. His lecture can be very long and tiring, but if you put a bit of effort to listen, it is interesting and will help you get prepared for his exams.
He was a cool dude. Easy class. Just study.
The class was boring but Persky was fun and helpful.
all around great professor
One of the best professors I have ever had hands down...he is very knowledgeable, helpful and friendly

Great prof. Patient and willing to explain in great detail. Recommended for the serious econ student. Pair up with a buddy in the beginning of the semester, that way you can ace the weekly blackboard quizzes.
Kind of a boring class, but its not bad. Just go to the lectures and do the on-line homework.

Prof. Persky is an excellent economics teacher. However, plan on going to his lectures if you want to pass the class, he covers topics outside of the book. His notes are also a little crazy but as long as you keep up you should be all set. He is very friendly and is always willing to help you if you need it.
Great teacher with lots of patience.  Go to his class and you will learn a lot.
Read the book, and do the online HW. Ok class just that the theory makes it boring. (required for econ majors)
He loves class participation.  Take his class if you like to participate in class.

A very seasoned, knowledgeable, solid professor. Not particularly easy, but I managed to get an A by going to office hours a few times. He was always available and friendly, and has a good sense of humor. Sometimes class got a little dull, but hey, that's macroeconomics for you. Highly recommended for the serious student.
Never again! If there are other professors take it.
Had him before he became a professor. As a TA he was amazing. He mad calculus easy and fun. I did very well in his class.
Difficult to understand at times (due to his thick accent), but he explained the material really well, gave good examples, and cracked a joke every now and then. Decent T.A., overall.

Great professor and human! Then again, I was surprised to discover that Canadians named Philip don't have hinge heads, so maybe take my anonymous internet evaluation with a grain of salt. (No hate; it's a South Park reference.)

I enjoyed his class. It's very lecture heavy though but it's clear that he knows his stuff really well. He's extremely passionate about maps and cartography and really knows his stuff. The workload isn't too bad, with only a few major assignments and midterms. I would definitely recommend taking this class as an elective.

Attendance is not important for this class, all the lectures can be found on BlackBoard. Make sure you read and take notes since you are going to be using all that information for 2 small papers, a midterm and a final 10 page research paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: He's really great! One for the books. Community Development is lucky to have him.
The best Canadian professor at uic
Hes so hot and so smart

I took him for an elective, he made the class very laid back and his weekly lectures were pretty intriguing. Gives good feedback on HW. Everything was very structured and straight-forward from syllabus so the class knew what to expect each week. It was my last class after an exhausting day, and his good looks managed to keep my attention each time!

She gave lots of extra credit. The final exam is online, which is great. She did curve the grade at the end of the semester. Being respectful to the professor and talking to her nicely if you need help or have questions. That will help the conversation to go well.

Prof is Respected & amazing lectures, lecture heavy, conveyed material to undrstnding.Exms were hard graded toughly, no formulas provided no cheat sheet. This class should be an easy intro to stats but she made it super hard for us Average on tests was usually like 50% No notes or formulas on tests and very bad lectures and discussions Would frequently cancel class right before Both her and the TA were rude Hw was graded extremely harshly with no explanation after yet claimed to care about learning
Just do your homework online and you'll do fine. The class is really easy especially if you have a background in Spanish from high school this class will be a breeze.
Funny, sarcastic, loves peanut butter, great stage performer, overall great professor. Show up and just do the homework online and you'll pass.

This class is not hard. Yet his teaching style was not helpful, the class was not engaging. You go to class, he tells you to goes over the activities in the book, gives us time to do it, goes over it and thats it. Everything we did in class I could have done by myself at home because his teaching methods were not beneficial to my learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Rhea is a very approachable teacher. I like that she includes examples from different cultures. If you ever want to distract her a little, ask her a question about cuisine. She's goofy, but is passionate about teaching.

Provides easier notes on grammar than textbook. Speaks very clearly w/ no accent. Provides great info on spanish speaking countries which make the class really interesting. Take her! Fun class. Even gave us candy when we played games sometimes! :)

Its spanish, so obviously you have to follow what the department tells you, but Rhea makes the grammar concepts make sense. There is no reason anyone should not pass this class, just show up to class, do decent on the Tests and you should be fine. Rhea makes spanish a lot easier to understand. Definetly take her if you have the chance.
Rhea is the best! She's very articulate and makes sure we understand before she goes on. Super laid back and communicates well with the students. Has a great sense of humor. I highly recommend her!
Rhea is the greatest. She's really laid back and is easy to communicate with, and she's also very funny. I really like her as an instructor. I highly recommend her.
Rhea is the greatest. She's really laid back and is easy to communicate with, and she's also very funny. I really like her as an instructor. I can't recommend her enough!
She's a nice lady, one who's willing to help out students if they get stuck. Great class! I would recommend her.
Ms.Phillips could teach any language successfully with her teaching technique. She explains language's structure at a much deeper level than what's just on the surface.

NURS 419 (her married name is Schwind now): W prof!!! Her lectures are so engaging that you're always surprised to see 2 hours have gone by. You can tell she knows her stuff. The key to doing well in this class is taking good notes during lecture and having ChatGPT make you practice exams. Lots of ppl underestimate the 1st exam, so y'know, don't
She is a wonderful teacher
No Comments

Mr. Pieper was honestly a solid teacher. His class was definitely interesting and his lectures would lowkey get off topic here and there. As long as you attend the lectures and discussions, you should be good. If you're good at self studying, you can still get an A. That's how I got mine (wouldn't recommend it though).

reviews.comment: easy to ask question

He's a very old-school professor, but he tries very hard and is always willing to answer questions. I went to office hours for extra help and took a lot of notes during lectures. The class is mostly exam based, and if you skip class you are screwed, but grades are curved and the material isn't too difficult with practice.
He's not a good professor. he doesn't provide exam prep sheets and although he's nice an understanding, he is a tough grader. Your grade is mainly based off exams.

Prof. Pieper gave interesting lectures and the content from the exams and homework matched the class discussion. As long as you attend lecture and take notes on examples/concepts, you won't need the textbook and will understand the material much better. He posts all of the notes online, but you can fall behind if you don't come to class. 80% : A
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: There is a lot of important history about economics in this class.  I learned a lot about the FED, interest rates, and different schools of thought for the macro economy.  In addition, there are also a lot of good resources for economic data given in this class.

This professor did a horrible job of preparing you for any of the tests. None of even came close to helping you prepare for what was on the tests. You have to completely learn the material on your own to have any chance to succeed in this class. Avoid the professor if possible.

I'm not joking when I say this, he sent me to therapy. His lectures only teach you about the basics for the exams and homework. You are better off taking a grad-level class than takingthis class. Please, do not take him. I think he got a good rating from other people because his content was fair back then. But they are 100% outdated.

Professor does not explain material well. Paul speaks as if he does not know what he is talking about so you will have to read book to make sure he knows what he is talking about. Paul really does not give in depth response when you ask for help. Study Guides for exams are not remotely close to what the exam is going to be.

Really bad class. Can't tell you how many of the homeworks I failed even though I watched the lectures several times in order to complete them. Exams were ridiculous, didn't even get a 50% on them. 60% is a C which is good, but it didn't make up for it. Please do not take this course online, you'll be dodging a bullet.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: His lectures only explain the very basic of what you need to do for the hw. The hw are extremely hard and unclear. the quizzes are insanely hard. And good luck on the exams, the study guide does not help at all. Honestly, if you take this class, you will rethink your major. DO NOT TAKE HIM
Do not take this Professor he is awful. You have will be doing a bunch of pointless homework to fail your exams. DO NOT TAKE HIM

This class, was hands down the worst class ever; the TA doesn't know anything about the class, and the professor takes 2-3 days to respond to emails. The exams and quizzes are extremely hard and the lectures and textbook barely help. Honestly, if you take this class you will BARELY pass if you're lucky

Sometimes it was difficult to pay attention during lectures. Nevertheless, he is caring and understanding. He is genuinely excited when someone asks a question or the class engages with him. He may be a little old-fashioned when it comes to his teaching style, but I looked forward to his class. Fair grading and extra credit opportunities.

I love Pieper. As long as you attend class most of the time and take good notes you wont even need a textbook. The homework really helps you prepare for the exams, so if you put in a good effort to learn the material in class you shouldn't have to put in much time outside of class. Lots of extra credit offered, and 80% is an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This is a tough class. He adjusts the grading scale because it is difficult. Be prepared to spend time doing the homework and visiting office hours if you want to pass. Not an easy A, interesting class though. The lectures are boring though. He only assigns a week for his homework assignments that are double-sided.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Hes a good guy and very approachable, but his lectures are boring and its difficult to pay attention. However, read the book, pay attention (as best as you can), find a good study group, go to class, and you should pass fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Must attend class or you won't past. Exams are hard! He will surprise you with hard multiple choices. Must read the book to understand and memorize all the concept well. Must know all his notes inside out and how to do all the problems. Boring lecturer. You will not pass the class if not put full effort in this class. No study guides.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: His lectures are very boring, where he talks like he hasn't slept for days. There are 4 quizzes and a final test (basically just 5 quizzes). He makes up the quizes and homeworks, and the exams are usually filled with mistakes. Usually someone spots out the errors. I doubt he actually double checks before giving it to us. He gives a lot of E.C.

He does not give any practice tests and practice problems in the book do not help with his quizzes. No tests, but 5 quizzes throughout the semester. Most people do very poorly. Nice professor, but very unorganized. Would not take him again.

Professor Pieper is a great guy. I was surprised to learn that he knew my name considering I never went to office hours. The lectures are pretty clear, although not always thrilling. He's definitely willing to help, especially with the homework. Be ready for that first quiz, the homework really helps you understand the concepts.
Follows book and notes word for word. You could skip and still do well. He is very approachable and knowledgable of macroecon. Can be dry at times but otherwise a great professor.
Great lectures, he knows what he is talking about.
Great professor! The summer session was a little intense and attendance was mandatory but it was all worth it in the end. Reasonable grading scale. Very interesting class overall.

Summer 4-week Macro was easy. 2 quizzes, 2 Tests, and 6 HW assignments. I enjoyed the class. Professor Pieper is pretty knowledgeable when it comes to macroeconomics. Would have liked to get into deeper material but you can only do so much in 4 weeks. I recommend this class. If you attend class and do the HW you will get at least a B.

I learned a lot from this professor. He is so sweet and very knowledgeable. The way he asks questions on the exams really show that his lectures are VERY important. If you actually show your interest in class, you will go great! He is very considerable when you make a mistake on the exam or quiz that you knew .

Overall pretty good professor. Lecture's are from the book and his own notes, make sure you go to class because his notes make the class easier. Exams can be hard if you don't study the material. Some MP questions from lectures will be on the exam. He tends to curve a lot for exams and drops one of the homework so that helps your grade.

Great Professor. Tests are difficult so make sure you do the homework and study guides. Goes directly off the book, but pay attention in class and take good notes, it makes the material so much simpler. Huge curve, and he is willing to help you at any time. Read, go to class, do the work, and ask for help when needed. You'll get at least a B.

Very dull. Doesn't seem like he ever has anything prepared. Always uses the book on the overhead and goes off of that for the lecture. You can just skip class and read the book on your own time. Never on top of emails, hardly replies back. From what I've seen, the class might not be his main focus.

I love Prof. Pieper! Expect off the wall questions on tests and homework. Otherwise he's always there to help and doesn't seem to care if it's his office hour or not. Make sure your lecture notes are good and compare with others, sometimes he erases things and re-writes over them.
Very clear explanation.  Great Professor.

He didn't even show up to his own midterm, made his TAs do it. Taught absolutely nothing in class that would be used in the homework/labs. Extremely unclear grading criteria/expectation for the final project. It was a bullet point list, no rubric. Difficult to understand just because of how soft spoken he is. Id avoid this professor at all costs.

The lectures have poor attendance or participation because they scarcely teach the material you will actually be graded on which is R code. On a positive note, you are free to answer the questions any way you like, so you have freedom to use newer libraries rather than the old, convoluted, hard-to-read R code he demonstrates during lectures.

The professor is nice, but like others said, it doesn't cut it in this difficult course. The topics are advanced, and the lectures are no help. The labs and homework descriptions would often be long and disorganized. Only 1 exam. The course has some really cool topics, and the professor seems knowledgeable, but does not come across effectively.

His lectures are very difficult to follow along with because he is all over the place. The homework is very difficult, and the only exam we had was also very difficult. Instructions for the final group project are vague. He is very nice, however.

Overall, this course is extremely all over the place. Homework takes a lot of time and is difficult to understand. The exam was extremely difficult and questions were phrased poorly. The course project is vague and a lot of work. The professor is nice and available outside of class, but lectures are impossible to follow. Get ready to teach yourself

The instructions are hard to follow. Homework is hard to comprehend. Lectures are definitely all over the place. It's tough to understand, he does ask if we have any questions, but it's like what are we even learning to make a question? Project was a pain, and the midterm exam was given on Week 12. That's not even a midterm. Go for a passing grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolutely the worst professor I have had. I usually doubt the ratings here, but this time was definitely true. His lectures are really hard to understand, and the assignments are really hard to follow for instructions. He seems like a nice guy, but it doesn't cut it for how hard the class is to understand. If you can, avoid the class.

Worst class I've ever been apart of. You will understand 10% of what the class is offering. I won't go into detail because the other reviews paint a good picture but be aware, you'll hate it. If you're not in your final semester, I would wait until a different professor teaches the class.

I don't have a single positive thing to say. His lectures are the worst I've ever seen in my entire academic career. They don't prepare you at all for the overly difficult homework he assigns. He hand waves through all the math and even when he does try to explain it's so horribly unfocused you can't even decipher what he's trying to show you.

His lecture style feels somewhat all over the place. He told us many times that we didn't really need to understand the theory behind the ML methods being taught, but then he'd spend 2 or 3 full lectures teaching the theory. Homeworks more or less followed the labs we did in class, but the one exam we took was incredibly difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: A very knowledgable and caring professor, but the material is difficult. It's a lot to take in and learn, but you can manage to pass since he curves. HW is due almost every other week, and it's hard BUT he's very helpful outside of class. Exam seemed impossible and the final project requires ALOT of work, but all the tools learned are essential.

I like the format of the course and he's always willing to answer emails and help with the material and is a nice guy. Unfortunately, he just doesn't present the material in an understandable, enlightening way. I left the class not really knowing the subject well. Some quizzes and tests are easy some not so much but he gives partial credit a lot.

Most disorganized professor at UIC. He keeps lecturing us on topics not listed on his syllabus/course description but his tests are on topics we haven't covered. He also does not realize his class is 50 Minutes long and continues to lecture. I got an A but I will not take this professor if I were you.

Truly the best professor I have ever had! Carrie cares so much for her students and their well-being. Her lectures are engaging and have valuable information that helps so much. Homework assignments and tests are straightforward and class notes help with those assignments. Highly recommend!

I think everyone wants a life partner to love them as much as Professor Pichan apparently loves teaching phonetics. Potentially the most fun class I've ever taken (and this is my fourth year). Knows her stuff, great at conveying material in a fun way and answering questions, goes out of her way to help, contagious enthusiasm. Take her classes!

i absolutely loved carrie! she made her lectures interesting and was not a boring professor. she clearly loved what she was teaching and she cared for all the students. frequent readings but the content is interesting. definitely recommend carrie as a professor!
She is lenient with dates, and helps everybody understand Italian!

Professor Carrie is very sweet and caring of her students! Despite being online, she still kept a positive attitude for 9ams. If you want to do well in the class, you should keep up with the readings and review lectures/notes everyday to retain the language.

Shes very sweet and always willing to help even after you did bad on a exam or quiz. If you are struggling sit down with her get the help you need. Italian 102 is rough with all the grammar you have to learn so get help as soon as you find an issue in your writing or grammar.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Carrie is such a gem at UIC. This woman never has a bad day. Even tho I was not the best at Italian, all she wants to see is that you are trying. She calls on you to participate (which usually gives me anxiety) but you soon realize even if you get something wrong she doesn't care she just wants to see you trying! U can tell she adores her students!

Hands down best spanish professor at UIC. Take her if you get the chance. She is always very nice and always willing to help if you are confused about something. She wants everyone to succeed and makes learning the language fun and not stressful.

She is so nice and caring. She makes learning Spanish fun and easy. She is willing to help you understand the material and the classroom environment is so opening. By far the best Spanish teacher I have had at UIC.
Great professor. She tries very hard to make sure students understand the material and engage in class. Very supportive, and very fun classroom environment.

Professor Pichan makes sure that all her students are doing well in her class. It is very important to engage in class so you know how to do the homework. It's like she never has a bad day, she always walks in the classroom with a big smile on her face ready to teach. I hope she continues to teach at UIC for a long time.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I really value how he gave a lot of attention to rough drafts while the grade on them would not sink you. He made me think about how language matters well beyond what I anticipated. Plus he was fun. Excellent professor!

He wasn't horrible, but he was the only English teacher at the time who graded rough drafts harshly. I did not like how he graded them so hard, especially since they are very rough. Also, there was a point when he did not like my research topic, and discussed it out loud to the entire class in order to get a laugh. Hard grader, and a bit strict
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Jenks taught me so much about critical thinking, writing, and the topics. I found the classes to be engaging and he knows how to challenge students. Awesome.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Jenks is an amazing professor, and he genuinely cares about the success of his students. His feedback on essays is very detailed and individualized, and because he grades the rough drafts the toughest but also makes them worth the least number of points, there is room for improvement and you can end with a good grade.

He is an easy grader and allows 6 absences before grade deduction. If you follow the syllabus, the class is an easy A. I personally got 99% in his class. There are numerous extra credit opportunities. He's fairly liberal. He talked about communism is a positive sense, but if you can tolerate liberal rants, take him for an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Jenks is an extremely talented individual who actually cares about both writing and his students while also maintaining a tendency to roast students and critique capitalism in the same class. Attendance is the ENGL 161 policy (5 absences) and his late grading is fairly harsh (30% off) but his comments are VERY useful and class is discussion-based.

Topic was Race/Class/Gender, which is so broad you could basically write about whatever you wanted. Class was mostly discussion based. Lenient grader, great class. Any problem you could probably work out with him. Dont use phones in class (unless it's for reading/research) because it pisses him off.
Super nice professor, so glad I took him. Go to his office hours and you will be fine. If you put in a bit effort, the class is easy.
so glad i took him for 161. super nice, caring, and understanding. just do the work on time and you will get a good grade

He's an extremely nice guy and very approachable.  Will help you out whenever you need it.  If you put the effort into his class you'll get an A.  Only bad thing about him is he's VERY liberal, to an annoying extent, can barely make it through a class without pushing liberal ideologies.  Overall good professor though.

He was the bombdotcom. He genuinely cares about the topics and student he teaches. If you keep with the curriculum,  an A is easily accessible. We also take cool field trips, FOR EXTRA CREDIT. He is awesome.

He's intense, funny, and even makes composition fun. His race, class, and gender class challenged me and helped me more than I knew. I'm seeing now how much I learned from him. Also, he cares about each student. I recommend his class.

I took Jenks's class my first semester when the subject was "Animal Cruelty". It was honestly the most memorable class I have taken at UIC. He has so much passion for the topic and goes out of his way to find something to do or show that helps connect the readings to real life. He gives you plenty of time, great feedback and meets with you to help!

Professor Jenks is a really nice guy. He has some issues in teaching (he veers off on tangents a lot), so the class time seems like a waste. BUT you have to option of taking the class where you want. He is very open to discuss almost anything. In terms of work--easy grader, not too much work, and very helpful.

Jenks is an awesome professor. I barely spoke in class, but  I went to his office hours and talked to him there. He's so understanding, and he's legitimately a realist. He's changed the syllabus like 20 times and extended due dates for big assignments. You need to put forth effort, but he helps you along the way. His feedback is awesome on essays!

I had Dr. Jenks my first semester of college and LOVED his class! He's a wonderful, caring and very smart professor. Go to his office hours. He's genuinely interested in learning about YOU and helping you develop a writing style that caters to you. He's funny, too. Down-to-earth dude; knows mistakes happen. Engage in class and read! Be original.
He seems tough, but things ease up. I like the feedback and help I get on each draft. Also, he does inspire. Probably because he cares!
He's tough, but things ease up. I like the feedback and grades I get on each draft. Also, he does inspire. Probably because he cares!

This professor in general is boring. He's a tough grader and I really mean it. He will grade your rough drafts which I find it outrageous because you know drafts are meant to be for mistakes but he taking it serious like if he was grading final drafts. If I was you, I would take someone else. His lectures are pointless and a lot of reading, A LOT.

Dr. Jenks is an outstanding professor! As long as you're willing to put the effort and come to class I guarantee you will do great. He is enthusiastic about his class and knows how to get everyone on that same level. If you have any trouble go to his office hours and he will help you and answer any questions. He seeks student success.Take him!
He helps a lot! Also he is different from many teachers because he actually teachers you in more than one way, such as movies, field trips, lectures, and peer reviews.
Take him! You will not regret it!!!!!!

He's super helpful, great to talk to, and good to work with. Doesn't change assignments, but does remind people. Is not overly demanding. Textbook use, normal for college as far as I can tell. Requires evidence connecting to claims in a very well designed course.  isn't teaching opinions.

Jenks is an amazinggggg professor! He really strives to help his students understand writing and analyzing texts! He also is so funny and great to be around in class and out of class if you need extra help. At the end of the semester you actually feel like you learned something. Great guy, good heart, dont piss him off!

He is a decent teacher. I don't really think I learned much from him mostly due to my lack of interest in the subject, but the information given is very sufficient in order to pass the class. His syllabus is very well written and thorough. Word of caution though, if you ask him questions that you could have figured out by yourself, he will yell.

One of the most interesting professors on the UIC Campus. He made a boring topic fun, he made class worthwhile with his sarcasm. I enjoyed his class very much even though I HATE English. It isn't an easy A though, but worth the challenge!

He actually cares about his students. Although he does give a lot of work, they all fit into the course topic. His humor always attract our attention like when he claim the noise from the ceiling to be "cold evil" which was the name of an article/essay we read. Just make sure you "always" fix your grammar because he grades heavy on it.  Good Luck
Jenks is a pretty cool dude. At times there is a large amount of work, but the class is generally relaxed.

Get to know him. He's gone through a lot of stuff so if you are struggling in any way GO TALK TO HIM. About life, about school, about anything in general. He wants to be a friend and know you on a personal level. Participate; he wants to know what you have to say. Hard class, but you will learn SO MUCH. He da bomb.

Great Professor. You will def. need to make sure you read the readings and take time to write your papers, BUT if you clearly put in the work on paper and in class, the your final grade will be in your favor. PARTICIPATE IN CLASS. Readings will provide useful information, you may even learn something new!

Definitely helpful and enthusiastic about his work. This guy is a genius. He's very down to earth, makes him that much more approachable. Super caring about his students. He wants you to succeed and will help you in any way possible. I never thought animal rights would be so much fun and such a great learning experience. Easy if you apply yourself.

He is going to make you work. Also known as learning. I felt I understood material better when going to class and discussing them. Assignments and reading are clear. He also cares about students, which is what I find attractive. Some don't pay attention and do nothing, expecting an A. That's not how it goes either. Show up and do the work.
Do not take him for an easy A. He is very picky and not clear. He is very moody. He will refer you to books instead of helping you. HE IS NOT HOT!!!
This guy is a genius. Jenks makes class fun. I realize now how much I learned from him. I wish there were more classes with him. He's also hot and highly intelligent.

Jenks knows his stuff and that made the class great. I can't belive I took a writing class where I learned about animal rights and about myself. He is very clear about his expectations so there's no way to do poorly. Still, some students do. The load is heavy in the begining but it's worth it. Take this guy! You'll get an A!
Docta Jenks is the bomb. hes funny, hot, and helpful. go D.J.!
Amazing. There is hope for this university after all. Most profs suck here. he is fun and tough but in a good way. perfect? well, pretty close!

He is a great professor that really cares about the students. He does not only talk about animal rights, and he has you read interesting yet challenging pieces that he goes over in class. Participate in his class and go to his office hours, he always has interesting stories/things to say!

Dr. Jenks issues a challenge. He encouraged us to make the best class ever. Balancing humor and dead seriousness, grammar/form and critical thinking, and an interesting topic made for a great class. It's the best one I've had yet.
