He is very fair and challenging. It's all about claims being supported by evidence. He doesn't care if you agree with him - if anything perhaps he finds the suck-ups to be transparent. Compassionate. Actually cares about each student.

He is an excellent professor, and the course theme is more interesting than some of the alternatives. He is a hard grader on drafts, but is overall very fair in terms of grading, as long as you back up your arguments with strong evidence. He is very critical if your views do not match his own, so be sure to agree with him as much as possible!

Jenks is a beautiful human being. He is a professor that genuinely cares for his students, and he is always open to help students with their papers if they have questions. There are open discussions, and he's pretty cool making the readings (some of which are very dense)  understandable. Students should definitely take him if they have a chance.

I think he was a great professor. He showed patient with a batch of students that was dull. Despite challenges, he brought in great speakers from syllabus and was enthusiastic. I can't wait to take another course with Jenks. highly recommend.
Considerate, intelligent, responsive to student needs. He is pretty flexible, but values participation. I felt comfortable in his class and recommend it. Cool guy. Plus he's hot in his own way ;)

He is a nice professor who actually cares about the students.His class gets boring at times but you can miss few classes so it's OK.His feedback was very helpful and I feel like my writing has improved thanks to him.Overall,he is a decent prof and is a very fair grader.
Excellent teacher. Made English a fun class to go to. Highly recommend trying to get Professor Jenks as a teacher.

Philip is the most understanding and helpful professor I've had at UIC. He really cares about the students and does him best to help out in any way he can. Class was nice, dry at times but I enjoyed it! I recommend this class, he's awesome

he is very funny and helps a lot at the same time. Knows when to be serious too. He spends a lot of time with feedback. That got me more interested in responding and writing.  I'm actually not into writing but it was great to have him. He held my interest in doing better.
Amazing! A lot of fun, chill.

He makes you work, but he is extremely helpful and an amazing teacher. He definitely improved my writing and taught me to think in ways I never did before. He is very fair. He makes you work hard and grades hard at some points, but he does give breaks and a change to take a breath during the course. One of my favorite professors...

He's funny and nice. He made boring stuff cool. And i thought it was real tough for a while but in the end I thought he learning become easy. Now I know how to write a solid research paper. Plus he cares about his students. Organized from summary to research. I didn't want to stop coming to class. Chic academe.

I like this teacher. He is tough and just at the right times flexible. I feel better prepared in all my classes because of this class. I never felt shut down. He will challenge you to support your claims. Also, a fair grader.

I didnt know anything about the topic or the teacher when I came in. I really think he is the best teacher I've ever had. He is supportive and fair. He challenged me to think and provided counters to my opinions, but that was done in a helpful way. I don't agree with everything we read, but I am doing well on the papers.
Jenks is very helpful, but he doesnt let you voice your opinion. if you dont agree with him he'll make you feel horrible, and it will also effect you when he grades your papers
I am so glad I took this. I didn't know at first, but he is so helpful and puts 100% into assisting us in our writing. And, he made me feel comfortable at UIC.

Expects you to read the textbook to learn much of what he grades for.  Also very opinionated.  It seemed to me like his biases got the better of him sometimes and he graded some of us down for disagreeing with him but hey, this is coming from quite literally the only conservative in his ultra-liberal class about animal rights.....

He is really caring and understanding. He loves his job and loves to help. I failed the class because I  was late everyday so I dropped it mid-semester. But I did like the class. The readings he gives are thought provoking. He is big on participation so if you don't like to talk then skip his class. A lot of reading! But its all interesting.
Great teacher! Highly recommended
Awesome teacher!!

I just took this class because it fit my schedule but it is so good I want to take his English 101! he is caring and always gets me thinking of new stuff. He really helped on the assignment three. His feedback is the best I have ever got.

Definitely, the teacher with the most amount of work i've ever done yet he has a vast amount of knowledge. His class opened me to many new things and changed the way I feel and think about our society. I definitely recommend his class it was a great experience.

Definitely one of my favorite professors. The final paper was supposed to be around 20 pgs long and it definitely made future papers in other classes seem like a breeze. Very helpful and caring. If you talk to him on a personal level, he's an awesome guy with amazing taste in music ;) Definitely got me into some awesome stuff.

Jenks is really easy going and very passionate in reading and writing. That passion carries over well into his teaching methods. I enjoyed being in his class. At times I actually looked forward to going to it.

A very understanding teacher but be prepared to get docked a lot of points if you don't follow minute details. MLA is like his religion and he will take points off if you don't staple. Seriously. I would recommend his class.

His class was definitely the most rigorous class I've ever taken. However, he was extremely understanding when I was having trouble and truly cared about each and every student in his class. He didn't stick to the syllubus at all and he was consistently late for class but he made up for it by leading interesting discussions and grading fairly

When people write dismissive junk like "I hated going to his class. Rude at times" you always know they are the actual culprits to their own lack of imagination. Great class. Great professor. Passionate. Smart. People who don't appreciate his class, probably complain about most of the teachers who actually challenge them to think.
I hated going to his class. Rude at times.

I had the honor of taking one of his classes my freshman year, and even though it was college required and the participation was dry at times, he made the best of it. I enjoyed my time so well in 160, that I proceeded to take 161, and 101 with him in the following semesters. He's a very interesting professor, very understanding, and always helpful.
If at the end of a class, I want to no if a teacher is teaching any more classes I figure that says something. He's great in this class. I imagine him as good or better in an advanced class.

He handled a really hard class. One student was especially difficult. If you do your work and participate, you do well I think.he is not easy but he is fair and interesting. Glad to be done glad I took this clss
I thought I was going to take another college class. Instead, this teacher expanded my understanding of the subject matter and he improved my writing skills. Plus, I think he made it all fun.

He brought me and others to a new level of understanding. I am in that class too. Most of us are doing well in that class. Most of us did not drop. And that's because he listens and works with students. Expect to be treated like you are in college, an adult. Respected.
I didn't think I liked Literature, certainly didn't think I liked poetry but the way he teaches it is different. He understood us and he showed me meaning

The class is tough, no doubt, but it's a good thing. Go to class, participate, write all your assignments and journals to length, and it's an easy A.  His methods aren't always orthodox, but play along and use the concepts he preaches in your writing.  He'll notice it.  Also, the smallest things count-READ THE SYLLABUS!
I didn't know how much I would learn when I signed up for this course. Now that I'm done, I feel completely prepared for my future classes. And inspired.
Hard grader but wants perfection from his students. Tries to be nice.
He is a very good and very hard teacher. He is also nice. I'm glad I took his English 161! Best English class ever!
I didn't know MLA and now I could cite this entry if I needed to. He taught us both grammar and the difficult material and I feel prepared for my other classes.
this guy taught me so much. I know MLA. that matters and it was hell. but he is very cool and we learned so much.
I am learning about all things apocalypse in this class. He is considerate and dedicated to teaching.
I am getting so much more out of this idea of daring truths than I imagined. His class is both fun and educational, serious but not cruel.
good guy, horrible teacher.
This is a very fun and challenging and educational course. We owe that to the work that he puts in, his amazing knowledge, support, and enthusiasm.

I didn't get a great grade from this course but that doesn't mean i didn't enjoy being in it. I deserved the grades that i got because i didnt do anything. But he still gave me a grade that didnt really harm me too badly. I greatly respect him and he has a lot of great insight. "Who would Jesus bomb?"
He is really helpful and dare I say O so hot!
This is a very tough class! He is also helping a lot and we are learning a lot.
The class was interesting, the teacher is fair. Sometimes the readings and work are heavy, but he balances it out.
I'm glad this professor is teaching a class I can take next semester. That should sum up what I think of how well he did this semester.

I think it was a few weeks in when I realized that this guy blew my mind. I find it challenging and fun. He gives a range of assignments, different readings, something for everyone - especially those who appreciate genius.

He is very considerate and helpful. He goes the extra mile and puts students first. His classes make us think. I think he managed to educate us, get me interested, and be clear about expectations. Then the class "feels" easy. The course is well-organized. My guess is that some students are lazy (and can't spell, see below) and blame him.
really good teacher, he grades easy, but id have to agree hes pretty unorganized..though he gives lengthy articles to read

He is a very nice guy. Willing to help and wants to help. Not very organized though. Fairly easy grader. I liked him, but I do not think I could handle another semester that is this unorganized. He likes discussion. If you like to talk in class, you should definately take his class.
I hope I can take more classes from...the best teacher ever.
I think he is really great. Anyone who is complaining probably isn't doing the assigned work and maybe theyre to blame
He is very good at working with students; each and every one gets attention. He puts a lot of comments on papers and they are helpful. We have a great teacher and a great class too.
No Comments
Pinar is one of the rare people you can face in the academia. She is funny, cool, and bright. She cares about students only. Seriously! If I had the chance, I would take her class like 100 times!

Such a great lady. She is really funny and cute and just loves what she does. The class isn't that hard, she understands if you cannot make the museum visits, and the final project is so much fun and insightful. I literally go an 100% in this class and if you get anything below and A its your own fault.

I LOVED Pinar, she is so sweet and funny. She was really understanding and her teaching method was great. I really enjoyed the projects and concepts and was passionate about the work that I did. She loves this subject and it is her living so it shows. I would definitely take her class again.
Her class is interesting because she links the discussion to everyday subjects and keeps your attention high. She is also very helpful and very understanding.
She's full of information on curating! She is helpful, friendly, and fun. Her class is never boring and the discussions are engaging.

Prof was great. Outlined clearly what we needed to get the A. Do the lab, study slides for exams, do extra credit. He honestly made me interested in paleontology and piqued my curiosity in the subject. Exams were not tricky and straightforward. Labs were also straightforward although tedious and easy.

Good class, straight forward. Key is to literally memorize lecture slides. Go to lecture so it's easier to remember the material and there are iclicker questions. Tests have more detailed things from slides that I did not expect. Labs very easy.

The class isn't hard, everything from the tests comes exactly from the slides. There are however a lot (and I do mean a lot) of slides. I used the book for the first few weeks of class, but then realized that as long as you study the slides there is no need to read as well. He is quite a character. I always got a kick out of him.

Roy is a very friendly guy, but he is not a good teacher at all.  His powerpoints look as if they have not been updated in years and are full of errors.  He expects everyone to have an exceptional math background when it isn't even required to have taken basic statistics for the course.  The two tests given in the course comprise 85% of your grade.

Nice guy. Horrible teacher. Just goes over power points, no study guides and then expects you to know everything on the exam from the power points and book. Final exam is apprently not cummalitive but he gave questions from the entire semester. Expects you to know info on a million slides with nothing to base studying off of. avoid..

Pretty interesting guy to listen to during lectures, well at least, in comparison to other professors. However, exams are very hard and they ask the most obscure of questions. No study guides or anything like that, so make you sure you study your slides pretty well.

Easy going guy. Everything he goes over in the lectures is online (powerpoint) and it seems kind of pointless to actually keep going to class but you have to because of the "Clicker Questions". Its an easy class if you attend the lectures and study every now and then. The labs are easy, and the TA's are pretty cool too.

He just lectures from slides which were also all we had to study from.  There were about 800 of them to study from overall which is ridiculous.  Field trip is easy, labs are easy, and exams aren't too bad.   Didn't use textbook.

Pretty nice guy that knows his stuff. Lecture is somewhat boring. He posts the notes on blackboard but will take them off if no one goes to class. Easier to get an A if you attend lecture and actually pay attention. There is a required field trip that is not that bad. Labs are not extremely hard. There are three exams and a final.

A "funny bird" is exactly how I would describe Plotnick. He is pretty enthusiastic about the material, yet lectures are still really boring- power points. I would recommend this class to someone who HAS to take a lab course and doesn't want to take chem or bio... But otherwise, no.

I knew what to expect since I took EAES 102 before this class. Lecture is pretty bland if earth science is not your thing. Labs are pretty tough because the math can seem confusing. If you do not pass labs, you fail the class basically. Which is why you should always ask questions during lab, The TA's are extremely helpful and usually give the answ

A lot of note-taking. There were 2 exams and each exam had 30 something questions over 20 pages of notes. We also had to write a 10-14 pg research paper. It was kind of a hard class. I would not take another class with him again.

Plotnick is a funny bird.  He is very enthusiastic about the material... he also thinks his students are, which is not the case.  Too much material. Needs to be presented in a more cohesive manner.  He's a good guy though.
Plotick knows his stuff and is helpful if you are willing to take the time to go see him. He is a very relaxed teacher and its apparent from his appearance.
Plotnick is from another world.  He has poor social skills, hardly can dress himself decently, and fails to relate to other humans.

Please do not take this class, Thermo is already hard enough and she does not help. 70% of the grade is just the exams and the practice problems she gives do not prepare you for the exam. The subject matter is very confusing and she doesn't explain well enough. Please if you have any other options I strongly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Her lectures are so fast that it is very difficult to keep up with, but she has clear handwriting. She rarely gives examples of the concepts we are learning: she focuses on the theory. When I asked her questions, she would repeat verbatim what she already said. It didn't matter much because I just watched the course coordinator's posted lectures.

Professor Pourarian is a great professor to have if you pay attention to lectures and do all the required homework. There were guided lecture sheets to follow along with during the lectures, which were great for going over exams. She makes the material clear and concise.

She was a good professor. Went a bit fast at times but if you ask her to slow down she will. She answers questions and is really nice. The class was super simple, I would say it is an easy B. Attendance is taken throughout the class period so if you are late it will not matter.

So, haven had Shokouh for Calc 3, I can say that as a calculus teacher she is pretty okay. She does expect some level of participation, so if you are actually lost, then she does carry some level of judgement if you are simply not getting the material. However, she is overall nice outside when she expects participation. Decent professor.
Lectures were extremely rushed and could get hard to understand. Made the class much harder than it needed to be.

she was really fast and got through 2 lessons in one lecture. Her handwriting is so neat which is very easy to take notes from and she even answers 3 question in one lecture with keeping the same speed. The most things i am using in Math121, I learned from her not McNamara. she is way too slow!
Lectures are helpful but can feel rushed. Highly recommend attending lectures and completing ALL of the optional written homework to exceed in exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Her lectures were pretty helpful because she gave a lot of examples and has really good notes but she doesn't post them online so you have to go to class. Attendance is mandatory and there's a pop quiz every week. but it's open notes. She's very nice and approachable, go to her office hours and she'll work on the written hw with you.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She doesn't put any lecture notes online, and there is no lecture capture. The professor simply writes a bunch of notes on a whiteboard, which becomes unorganized and hard to follow...
As long as you are on time with the material, you will find the lecture very interesting with the way she teaches.

Make sure to sit in front of the class because she writes everything down on a white board with hardly any ink left in her markers. Accent is heavy but does not make it impossible to understand her. MyMathLab saved me from this class and her lectures became completely useless to me by the end of the second midterm.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Overcomplicates, focuses too much on theory and not enough on problem solving.
Calc 3 is not hard, but she always makes things way more complicated. TBH, good at math doesn't mean you are good at teaching math.
Showed every problem nicely and paced the course well. She was bad af too

It was very hard to understand her and I would definitely not recommend taking her. All she makes you do in discussions are the online worksheets. Literally no one would show up to her discussion or lectures. Good luck learning everything on your own.

Ms. Pourarian was unfriendly and seemed like she never wanted to be teaching us. Her English is not very good which makes it hard to understand her while she is teaching. In the discussion section, she would sometimes not say a word during the entire class. Her complete lack of care or enthusiasm made it hard to care at all about her class.

Professor Plott is the best. He has a ton of knowledge about economics and helps you really understand things with good examples. Tests and homework are difficult but as long as you have a decent understanding of the material, show up to class, and demonstrate you are trying he will make sure you improve and pass. ECON 303

I was lucky enough to be in a class where all the tests were take home. The tests were still very difficult! However, he is very straightforward on what he expects. He's very intelligent and will help you out if you are willing to put in the work. Be forewarned to not use Google on the homework, he'll catch it and fail you.
The class is hard, but he is willing to answer your questions and help you succeed.

Probably one of my favorite professors. Do the study guides and actively listen during lecture. There are few surprises on the test and he gives extra credit and curves the exams by +/-10pts. Make regular appearances to office hours, he notices that. Ask questions and actually try and give a rat's a$$ about the topic and you'll succeed.

Initially I was eager to wreck Dennis' reviews, but I thought I'd wait until the end of the semester. Now I have a very positive opinion of him. The class isn't easy, but the issue was at first I didn't think to go in and ask questions when feeling clueless about the problem sets. Go to office hours- he's very knowledgable and will help you out.

Dennis is GREAT! He is an excellent instructor and works really hard for his students. I've never had a professor invest so much time into my work and it really paid off. Go into his office hours and get to know him. Show him that you're interested and he will help you. Take good notes and study hard. Def not a blow off class, but well worth it.
Excellent explanations, thorough in lectures, but you need to listen and go to class. Learning is actually rewarding with Dennis, knowing how to model an ARIMA function has never been easier.
Very interesting to say the least.

Awesome professor. Not going to lie, it is a tough class, but if you go to class, take notes, and go to office hours, you will do well. It's obvious that he really cares about Economics, and this will make you care as well. Take his class!
It was a tough class, but if you put sometime and effort in it then you can prolly do good. Not given but errthing is earned.

I was the student who rarely went to class and rarely took notes...Biggest regret of my college career. Honestly a great professor and a great instructor. Actually cares about students understanding the subject and will help. If you do the work and attend class you can do well, he doesn't baby anyone and gives you what you deserve, how it should be

I recommend taking him if you want to be challenged. It was a rather hard class but you learn a lot. If you’re an ECON major pursuing further ECON studies I highly recommend because he does build you a great foundation for more advanced classes. Don’t miss one class because he covers a lot of notes that the book doesn’t clarify. UNDERSTAND GRAPHS!

This class will definitely push you. If you expect econ to be easy, then you need to rethink your major. Dennis is a great instructor and whoever said that he is "worst instructor at UIC by far in every possible way" probably never went to class. He cares about each student's needs and dedicates his time in explaining unclear topics.

He won't just give you an A. He might not even be nice to you. He will probably be the one to tell you Santa doesn't exist. But the homework and the tests are fair and beyond thought out. He puts a lot of effort in this class and wants you to show him the same. Go to class, take notes, understand graphs and you're set. Nothing will be a surprise.
Bottom line - listen in class and study. He is challenging but I find that to be a good thing. His tests are fair.
He is terrible! He is very confusing and his tests are the hardest. Only take him and his classes IF you want to receive a C after working hard in the class.

A very challenging class to say the least.  Plan on attending all classes, and utilize his office hours if you get hung up on subject materials.  Fantastic real world applications, that spill over to the exam materials.  Stay in the textbook, and follow the graphs that Mr. Plott presents in class.

He is a very good teacher tests are hard and no homework is given. This is not a "blow off" class, you WILL work for your grade! But if you show up and show interest he will be more than happy to help you out! This was not an easy course but hands down learned more in this course than any course I have thus far taken at UIC.

Great instructor, very knowledgable. The material its self is difficult, however he explains things very well. Closest thing to real world applications i've experienced so far. No extra credit or homework, but the "adjustments" on the exams are more than fair. If you enjoy Econ take him, if you want a "blow off" class, steer clear.

I had Professor Plott for Econ 221. It was a tremendously challenging course because he wants you to learn. Students must work diligently to achieve good grades and an understanding of the material. Professor Plott is extremely helpful and  and if he knows you are putting in the work, he will effectively help you out. Take the class.
He is very helpful teacher. Its an easy a if you attend the class. He offers extra credit options in all his exams. His classes are very helpful

This dude sucks as a teacher. He will make a great economist but sucks at teaching. Way too many graphs to memorize. I will not lie he offers easy extra credit opportunities and if you read the textbook you will do decent. It is the graphs man.
Dennis is a really good professor. If you put in the work and show up to class every day and understand the concepts you should do well.

TAKE HIM! He actually cares about his students and will take the extra time after class and during office hours to explain concepts to you until you get them. You will actually learn in this class and be able to apply it to real life! His humor makes the class quite interesting.
Class is hard but you leave there actually knowing the subject rather than memorizing. Studying is key

Dr. Poretsky repeatedly mocked me in her office hours and insulted my intelligence. Her exact words were "I think you know a lot but don't understand anything." My interactions with her in office hours made her classes miserable, I am halfway through the semester and wish I had never signed up for this course. Be Cautious.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She is so nice
Dr. Poretsky is clearly passionate about the material she teaches. The class is challenging but really interesting. I learned a lot.

Claims to be teaching this course for 10 years, but there is no wayyyy. How can one be this disorganized, have no structure to a class, etc. AFTER 10 YEARSSS. I'm pretty sure the 5's on here were written by her cuz she don't know how to lead a class even after 10 YEARSSS of teaching it. Don't get me started on pretending to be welcoming.

Super unorganized. Little to no structure to the class. 
Claims to be "welcoming", but is not at all. She mocks students when they ask a question, makes you feel dumb, grunts when you ask for further clarification. 
Lectures are one big RANT session that are rushed EVERYTIME.
Takes points for not answering questions in her head on exams. 
DON'T!!

As others have mentioned before her organization and presentation could really use some work. Sometimes just mean to students. So random. Anyhoo, not really a hard class, and the co-professor was helpful, but there are other professors in biology and other departments that teach similar computing classes. IMO better to google/youtube your way.
Disorganizing material
Kinda rude in class, she called out a classmate for using the bathroom during class and does not seem approachable.

Great professor full of knowledge and actually currently doing research in her field. Not your standard fair dry-lecturing-slow-talking old guy. Very easy to listen to and very approachable. Class was very quiz heavy and she definitely expects you to actually understand the content, but not unreasonably difficult. Reading the book would be helpful.

She co-taught a biology themed computer science class. She doesn't explain concepts and ideas well. But boy will she talk your head off. This woman just rambles on and on sometimes. She comes off as a know-it-all in her office hours and shows frustrations when students were having trouble. She's rude and I would avoid her if possible.

She's terrible. AVOID this class. This class is a part of Sloan's research(college students at such a big university aren't rats). She tries to act nice but her cruelness just shows more when she does so. If you ask her more than a few questions she'll start yelling at you. Very disrespectful. Way too difficult as the first CS class for CS majors.
She is very respectful and an easy person to talk to. She has a very good understanding of Python Programming.

Professor Podrazik is very knowledgeable about the world of digital media and all things pop culture. He's very easy to talk to and often brings up topics for the sake of conversation. His class is based on blog posts, a few essays, and 2 presentations. Class is lecture-heavy and often contains class participation and conversations.

Professor Podrazik is great! He has a huge amount of knowledge regarding television. Unfortunately, the class is extremely heavy on lectures and it can be hard to pay attention. The workload is reasonable. The individual and group projects are actually pretty fun. Overall, an enjoyable class and a great professor!

One of the best professors, his life story and experience is truly fascinating. Grade will be based on 5 Blogs,10 Annotated Articles and Essay with presentation. The class is interesting and motivating, didn't regret taking this class even for second, pure joy from educational process.

The class is based off of 10 blog posts, 2 papers, 20 online quzzes, 1 big group project, and no exams. It was really easy and he is very lenient about everything. He takes points away if you miss class.

HE GIVES A's!! I had Professor Walter as my instructor for 2 courses and I got an A as my final grade for both courses. Without a doubt one of the best Professors I have had in my college experience. His grading criteria is clear and he loves enjoys talking with his students. I will truly miss him.

He is extremely straightforward about his grading criteria--no surprises. He teaches with enthusiasm and also allows for a lot of creativity in the written assignments, which is the best part of the entire class. Participation matters so make sure to share your thoughts here and there. It was an enjoyable class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Loves what he teaches. Doing papers sometimes is tricky because he doesn't really give you a step by step guide of what he wants so you feel like you're doing it wrong the whole time but do the paper and you'll get a B and paper topics are fun to write! no tests just online quizzes. He rambles a lot but such an understanding, loving teacher.

He clearly knows a lot about the subject, but is a weird grader. Like previously said your paper has to be astounding to get an A, his grading gravitates to mid-Bs. Class only consists of a few papers/presentations tho, both of which are mostly opinion-based though since there is no right or wrong predictions about the Future of TV. No exams!! (:

He babbles so much. He's passionate about what he teaches but finds a way to turn interesting subjects into dull crap. He refuses to give As on essays bc he claims unless he feels the urge to publish it, he does not believe it's A worthy. If students' writing is at a professional level, then why are we in school instead of getting paid to write?
Really good professor, passionate about his work and really gives you an insight to what the outside world is really like.

Condescending and treats students as if they're beneath her. She talks down to students making weird jokes like "do you guys still know how to read?" The exams are ridiculous one exam requires memorizing six dense readings, 19 terms, 24 artists, and 70 works of art/ the dates.
She is a tough professor but taking her class was a lot of fun/insightful. I believe she is genuine and critical in an effective way.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Yes she is a very difficult professor, however she knows her material backwards and forwards.  And she expects her students to come prepared. If you are prepared for class everyday you have nothing to worry about. If you want a challenging class take it.

If you are not an art major student, I recommend you DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS! She pulled up a lot of readings for every class meeting and her pronunciations would make you fall asleep!  She is a tough grader, even though the exams are short essay questions and some definitions, you need to prepare almost one hundred pictures and memorize everything

Worst class i have taken at UIC. The professor is very unclear in what she wants and is obsessed with the material. Exams consist of memorization of over One Hundred Images and few definitions. I am in her class right now and i find this course extremely challenging for a 200 level . Do not skip class, she will punish you severely, even when sick
Should have gone here first. Very unprofessional and rude when asking for feedback and help, did not have concrete guidelines, unwilling to work with me. Find another elective.
She might be a well educated one but she has no communication skills. she's difficult and obsessed. Not to mention too complicated and unclear.

Josh is honestly one of the best professors i've ever had. He is big on participation, but only because he really cares about his students opinions. He will walk around the classroom to talk to each student and really try to get to know them. He definitely cares about each one of his students and will guide you in whatever you need

He is a very caring professor, very kind and easy to talk to. Overall easy class, its mostly common sense. Group project, mid term and final. Graded in class assignments. He is very easy to reach and gives good feedback.
One of the best professors! Take him if you can! He typically teaches this class only in the fall. Very friendly, and his TAs are amazing!
he's amazing

One of my favorite professors in the School of Public Health undergraduate program! It is clear he is passionate about teaching and the public health field. He inspires his students every day to challenge the education system we are in and to open our minds to what is going on in the rest of the world.

Professor Prudowsky made this class unique. I learned many of the fundamentals of public health and how public health directly affects individuals and their communities. He made all of our lessons engaging and interactive, focusing on individual and group learning. It has been my favorite class this semester.

Goated prof. The class was super fun and engaging, and the lectures weren't boring; they were fun. The TAs were awesome and very helpful. The grade is mainly based on quizzes and in-class assignments; attendance doesn't matter. You allowed notes on the quizzes, midterms, & finals. Class inspired me to switch majors. So so fun take the class
I absolutely love that this class is a mixture of lecture and interactions. It really allows all students to actively listen.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
My favorite part of this class was also the most beneficial, and it was how engaging the professor was. It was a unique experience for me
to feel like class was like a conversation between me and the professor. I also feel like the professors personal attitude made it easy to pay
attention to this class by being extroverted and fun in other words.

I really enjoyed all the participation activities in this class. Many or most of my other professors lecture a long time,
but this is one of the classes when the professor takes time to come up with fun and engaging activities that are not only fun, but very
educational and informative for the course material.
lots of group work and a really cool guy, would take again
DON'T RECOMMEND THIS CLASS, WITH THIS PROFESSOR!
Good lectures and lots of group work
Great class. Makes me think in different ways
She's not as bad as everyone says. She's brilliant and a has a lot of knowledge. She just has high expectations.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Condescending, unclear grading criteria. Not a lot of room for any opinion that isn't shared with Pollack. Take at your own risk.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Condescending and treats students as if they're beneath her. She talks down to students making weird jokes like "do you guys still know how to read?" The exams are ridiculous one exam requires memorizing six dense readings, 19 terms, 24 artists, and 70 works of art/ the dates.

This class is graded on one essay at the beginning of the semester, and three exams. It is all memorization-based, and answering each question on the exam is timed in very short increments. Pollak also has a bit of a condescending attitude at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you are not major in art history don't take it as an elective. Your grade is ONLY based on exams. This class is heavy based on memorizing course material. Not easy to communicate with.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If you enjoy art history, especially Italian art and architecture definitely take this class. Take notes, and participate and you can get an A in this class, but she is kind of strict. She doesn't give busy work, but instead, you really have to pay attention in lectures. I really enjoyed the class and her lectures but it is not for everyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class is fine as far as an Art History class. She is not a tough grader as long as you know what you are talking about. Very few assignments. Probably could get away with not doing the readings since she will talk about the subject in the lectures. Names, Patrons, and dates are very important. Mid-term and final are worth a lot, 35% each.

Professor is sharp with her words, just respect her and she'll respect you. There are very few assignments so unless you get an A on each you're failing the whole class. Notes and tests are remembering names and dates. Papers and tests are graded as if you're a architecture and English major. Cool content but the assignments and grade not worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ok lecture isn't really necessary and reading the text isn't necessary but it helps ALOT. For lecture she is a little difficult to understand and her voice is almost like a lullaby you will want to fall asleep but push through it and right vigorous notes! For tests MEMORIZE art dates. Hard class but interesting.
What an incredible teacher. Never before have I learned so much from one course. Great lecturer, poised and highly informative. She's funny and sharp as a tack.
She is so passionate about her art history and architecture. she has an adorable sense of humor and is fun to listen to during lectures if you give  her a chance, very nice.

Don't get on this professor's bad side, even by accident. She can be vindictive. Thin skinned. Has power and knows how to use it. If you are a favorite, you'll be fine. Knows some of the material very well. Other, one gets the feeling she reads up on it the night before class. Rather insecure-- challenge her with care and at your peril.

Highly intelligent, knowledgeable, makes herself available to advise outside of office hours & over weekends. Though we had the freedom to pick final ppr topics, she has specific parameters & contradicting ideas about the end product. Can lack tact, plays favorites; she's the boss & she'll let you know it. Regardless, learned a lot &  worth taking.

Frustrating! Can be demeaning & treats adults like they are in HS. Threw fits if you came 5 mins.late or spoke to your neighbor. pay attention and take notes, you'll be fine. 75% of readings were on reserve at the library and each reading could be up to 50 pages. It was ridiculous trying to share these readings with 35 people making copies of them

Lectures are long, boring and full of needed information (if you can stay awake or not playing internet games). Passing the class is not hard, but passing with a B or better is. Class is 60% memorization and 40% luck. Take good notes and go to discussion. Don't be afraid to switch TA's to find one you like, they will make a difference.

EXCELLENT professor, with a little getting used-to. Pollak is a wealth of information and is very enthusiastic toward her topic. I took Art History 111, and the class was challenging but Pollak's personality made up for it. If you have any interest in Art History whatsoever, take her class!

Way too much to read...most of it is on reserve at the library.  About 80% of the class did not read the reserves, but just went off the information at the lectures.  SHE IS REALLY STRICT WITH HER INFO!  So if you are not 100% commited in class...just don't take it!

I took 2 classes with her and enjoyed both very much. Definitely learned a lot.  She comes across as distant but is helpful and clearly very knowledgable. If you like a bit of a challenge and like reading, I recommend taking her class.

Took 4 classes w/Martha & an oversees trip. Very articulate, very knowledgeable. Responds well to your ideas & rewards good work. She can come off as aloof, but if you approach her with respect & intelligence she's gracious and helpful. Always responds to email and returns phone calls. Trust me, she's a good person to have on your side!
way to soft spoken, unfair amount of reading, u buy a book but never read it, u only read books that she put on reserve in the library
She speaks too softly you can't understand half of what she says and she doesn't respond good to any questions you have.
she couldn't speak clearly and she made me fall asleep.
Very worldly and well spoken, rewards attentive students, very fair grader

I believe he does not teach the material as clear as it should be, especially when it comes to an introductory course. He teaches as if you already know the material, so it is a bit hard to catch up when he says unknown words or concepts. He, however, is very helpful when it comes to feedback on projects.

He's a very kind and funny professor. Sometimes the assignments were confusing, but he and the other professors were there to help during studio. You kind of just have to do your own thing, sometimes, the professors seemed like they were unsure of what was happening/had different answers for questions.  Just attend class and do your best

I actually connected well with Paul; he understood and encouraged my concepts, often telling me what to include in my designs when I didn't have ideas. He very much did his job as a professor and he was very lenient. He was the perfect teacher for first-year undergrads.
He saved my dying dog's life, through CPR; I owe him my life and am forever indebted to him :))

Preissner is the worst professor I have ever studied under and that's saying alot. He shows up late every single day, completely changes projects halfway through, and just genuinely doesn't put forth any sort of effort in his class. At the end of the semester he just gave everyone the same grade. Do everything to avoid his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took her 159 class and enjoyed it. It's a little homework heavy if you already have a lot going on, with a short paper due per week. But she's very helpful and kind. I would take a class with her again and recommend her to others.

The most helpful Professor I've come across so far understands your problems outside of the University and helps you and works with you prolongs deadlines if there is a genuine problem. Instant email replies and very understanding and caring. She is truly a gem of a person and would definitely recommend you to take her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Absolutely loved her class! Really cares about students and was very helpful with papers.

Grade Consists of 4 exams, 1 3 page paper, 7 short papers, Blackboard assignments, and Attendance/Participation. The class isn't from the 4 rating isn't hard, theres just a lot of homework. The exams were exactly like the study guides. A lot of Short papers and assignments but they were easy. Overall she's a cool/caring teacher but lots of hw.

She's a very good teacher. Very understanding if you need an extension. Course was easy to take. You can learn a lot on speaking formally in Spanish with her. She's not strict and she's very easy going.

She barely teaches at all. it the same thing over and over again, come to class, take attendance, review last nights homework, puts you in groups 2-3 times every class and doesnt even remind you or tell you or upcoming homework on blackboard but gives you pointless homework. Horrible, disorganized and low quality teacher. would never recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She's a very tough grader and talks bad about students when not in the room. She says "great speech!" but then gives you a C on it or lower. Even if you follow the rubric, if she doesn't favor you then you will not get an A in the class.
Evie was honestly one of the best teachers I've come across at UIC. Didn't dread her 9am one bit, I had fun, even.  If you get the choice, take her. It'll be such a rewarding  experience.
Amazing! Does not waste your time. Do the work, turn in on time, follow the syllabus and guidelines also, make sure you incorporate what SHE recommends into your speeches  and she's happy!

EVIE IS AMAZING. As simple as that. I've dreaded taking a COMM class since I knew I had to take it. But Evie changed that. Her enthusiasm and energy is what kept me going. She gives amazing feedback and is definitely there for you. TAKE HER!! Thanks EVIE!!

Evie was an amazing lecturer.  Honestly I couldn't have asked for a more motivating teacher to guide me through a speech class.  Her enthusiasm, friendliness, and respect all account for how great she is towards her students.  Although the communications department sets up the syllabus, she does a great job of making this course enjoyable.

There is a much bigger focus on reading poetry than writing, however the readings really do help understand the technical skills that poetry requires. The assignments are clear, but they are basic and don't feel as if they're challenging as a writer. However, she is very approachable and so understanding. She prefers the classics for sure.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Pugh is an accomplished poet and it shows. Sometimes it's hard to meet with her but she always does her best, and the class is easy if you care. Sometimes lectures were a bit boring but what can you do? It's college not a circus. Really helped me develop a greater understanding of poetry.

Professor Pugh is amazing. Each day we learned something new about poetry, different terms and styles, etc. she is very thorough in her explanation as well. She provided the tools for us as developing writers to create great work, and was enthusiastic about everyone's work. Take this class with her if you are a serious poet!

Prof. Pugh is awesome, especially if you like to discuss literature. The papers are not difficult and I found what we read interesting. Yes, you have to discuss. It's much better if you actually have classmates who care instead of those who are just trying to get by. Don't be one of those lame people.

This faculty member is a serious problem. You can't avoid her if you want to study poetry at UIC, though she will avoid you (generally unavailable for meetings, unhelpful feedback on work, hardly on campus).

Prof Pugh is sounds very intelligent but extremely boring. Nice teacher and knows her material, but I find the class extremely difficult to sit through. Makes you buy a course reader that you use every day so buy it. Papers are assigned pretty quickly after the previous was due but they're all easy to get a good grade. Not a challenging class.

This class is definitely for those who wish to learn and don't mind putting in the work to be successful.  Prof. Pugh is extremely concise and clear in all of her instruction, and extremely nurturing to your individual understanding and growth.  If you like poetry, I highly reccommend taking this class with her.

lots of reading to do. she makes you buy a huge expensive course reader, but you actually use it. the papers were easy if you've taken any college classes. lots of "discussion" though so you have to hear the mindless thoughts of your classmates.

He is a fantastic educator—but only if you are an "ideal" student. If you show up to class, read the textbook, and do the homework, you'll be fine for any of his classes. But if you are someone who has any disabilities/accommodations, I sincerely insist you pursue/wait for other professors to teach the class. He's funny, but he lacks understanding.

His level of teaching was so hard to understand for me if you ask him questions about it, he makes you feel dumb. I felt discouraged to reach out to him because of it. I took this class with a better prof and was able to get a b and somewhat enjoy Pchem for once

Prof Snee is incredibly knowledgeable in his field & others. He wrote his textbook & its free which I appreciated. At first he might seem intimidating, but once you get to know him hes actually a great prof and a great guy in general. He responds to emails very quickly & his exams are fair. You'll always know whats on exams, never surprised.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Mister Presty Doctor Snee is an amazing professor, and my best friend as well. Quantum chem is impossible to understand for some people (me). I am glad that he was always welcoming during his office hours and helped everyone without a doubt. Kinda sad that he won't be teaching this class anymore. For his other classes - just go to office hours!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He thinks he's funny but he's so cringe. I will have him for 346 next semester because he's the only one who teaches pchem. People say he's 100 times better than the previous professor for this class. Be ready to do 10 written problems every week cause they will somehow prepare you for exam. ChemE students found it easy. Im a chem major, i suffered
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Really great professor, he's extremely knowledgeable and accessible for help outside of class. You will be fine as long as you do the problem sets and read the book. He's kind of intimidating at office hours initially, but he will make sure you end up getting the concept. One of the best chem professors I've had.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Decent
Very rude during office hours and with emails.
he is really rude professor, his email is like I do not care, dah, he is funny in class, but in email and drop-in hour, he changes to be the monster of rudeness

Quite an entertaining class, professor Snee keeps you engaged with the lecture, he is clearly passionate in teaching with humor. His lecture videos are all you'll need. Homeworks are mostly math heavy, and the exams are easier and more conceptual. If you can take good notes and review them before the exam, you're golden. Made quantum bearable.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's honestly the best professor I've had, and he's right up there with my Anatomy professor. He's funny and knows the subject really well and can teach it in a way that makes it fun and interesting at the same time. He does recaps every class for 10minutes, and also gives background info on the scientists that derived the equations. Super smart!

Professor Snee is one of the few good professors at UIC. His energy and passion makes the class interesting and fun. He's designed the course to help every student to succeed, so it should be very easy to secure a good grade in this class.
AMAZING professor!!! So passionate about teaching and cares that the students understand the material. Also wrote his own textbook so you can read about something if you don't understand it in class.
Rude and disrespectful

He's a great professor! Actually he was the best professor I has through out my entire undergrad! He makes you love the subject! He makes sure you understand what's going on with the class and if you didn't, you can go to his office hour! The class is not easy, but it's fun at the same time!

Amazing, smart,  and one of the most caring professors at UIC.  Made physical  chemistry an intesting  class. Easy A, and resonable  exams if you do the  homework  sets. Also take advantage  of  office hours where  not only  you  can ask the professor  but also can  meet  up with  your  classmates, form study groups, and make  friends.  :)

I think Professor Snee is the best professor at UIC. The class is actually really fun to go to and not difficult. You'd expect Physical Chemistry to be the really challenging sequence of courses in Chemistry major, but Snee makes it really it simple. I would recommend any one looking to enroll in this class to brush up on their algebra though.

He ran the class very similarly as last semester: problem sets, exams, and final exam all contribute to your final grade, except for PCHEM II he made the homework worth a third of the points, so we had a huuuuuge grade buffer, so to speak. So the final exam, midterm exams and homework each were a third of the grade. In other words, he makes it easy
The best professor I've ever had!!

really cool professor who actually knows his stuff... make sure you show him that you want to do well in his class and show up to class because he notices if you ditch.. he always gave candy during exams and actually wants you to do well, which isnt too common

Dr. Snee is the best chemistry prof. I've ever had. He connects physical chemistry processes to real life examples into the point that he makes you imagine gas molecules around you!! He's funny and he's always helpful during his office hours... expect homework due every week, it's not hard as long as you don't cram lectures into one day

When I first took this class, I really had a different impression from what most say on rate my professor. He does keep you awake in class and he seemed like an approachable person ; however, when the time came to see him during office hours, his attitude changed. I was disappointed in a sense.

Dr. Snee aka Dr. Chicken jokes around in lecture a lot, which makes it pass by quickly. He however does not joke about the course content.I thoroughly enjoyed learning the material with Dr. Snee and was suprised how much I retained. He was also very genuine and wants all his students to succeed. My favorite teacher of all time... Of all time.

Snee is easily one of the best professor's I've ever had at UIC. He made a tough class seem like a piece of cake. Just don't miss lectures and DO THE PROBLEMS SETS!! Exams are just like the problem sets and it's an easy A if you put in some work. Also he brings chocolates to exams!

This one of the best professors I had at UIC because he really tries his best to help the students in knowing the material. The exams are based off the problem sets which really helps in knowing whether or not you understand the material. Attending class is very important, but he records his lectures which helps if you miss class.

A funny and nice teacher, he is very clear on what you have to know and basically teaches you how to ace his tests. I feel like I learned a lot because the homework is very similar to the test. The class isn't a blow off and requires effort but is very manageable, he posts videos on his own dime which allow for self study, Very good professor!
He's a good professor. In all honesty, if Snee isn't teaching the class, you may want to consider waiting until he does.

Awesome professor! He cares about your understanding and makes sure you are ready for the exam by assigning very similar homework. He has review sessions before every exam to help you focus your studying. He records the lectures manually because he doesn't have lecture notes. He lectures old style by writing on the board. Easy A if you work for it.

Snee is the man. A man's man. He can be confusing and he makes mistakes but at the end of the day he knows his stuff. And he sure as hell makes sure you know it too. Or you fail. Don't bother getting the book unless you genuinely are interested in the material. He gives plenty during lecture for you to ace the course.

Honestly one of the best teachers I've had in my undergrad.  He's very clear in how he teaches the material, fair in grading and testing, and can approach the material from different angles if necessary.  He legit tries to make the class as interesting and doable as possible, which is saying something for Phys Chem.

Do not buy the book, he even says it's useless. His problem sets are similar to the exams so if you understand those (they are difficult to understand at first), you will do fine on the exams. He hand writes on the board for all his lectures but tends to be all over the place so it can be irritating. He makes a lot of mistakes too, very annoying.
snee rocks- end of story. his lectures are interesting to attend, and he has a great attitude. i think his homework is great prep for his exams- he sets you up for success if you put in the effort.

The book is very hard to understand, but his lecture is more interested. I was able to clarified when going to his lectures. He explained to make sure that I know learly when I came to his office hours. Very nice professor!!! I will suggest take him in the chem course.

Snee's the bee's knees. Very smart (makes "nanocrystals" in his lab research) yet practical. Material presented is interesting and useful. He frames topics as "how nature works" which is a cool way to think. Exams are difficult because example problems aren't similar to hw, but not too bad. Don't bother buying the text. Loved his illustrated book.

Fantastic professor. Very smart, great personality, lectures are interesting and informative, and he has sufficient background knowledge to explain almost anything you may have a question on. Not arrogant at all, and he doesn't put on a show. No memorization, just comprehension. This is what education should be like. Kudos, Dr. Chicken!

He's a great prof, but the class is disorganized and a mess. some of the TAs under him are incompetent, so good luck w/ that. over all, not too bad, but the lack of organization and supplies, and TA incompetency will make you want to fall on a broad sword just to end it all.

Off the bat a very unique character( depends on your taste) I did not mind. Very energetic in lecture and really wants everybody to understand the material. Passionate about his work and chemistry in general thats a plus in my book. Take the guy overall he is like an 85/100. There was a high average in class but thats the students fault.
He's ok? The curve kind of sucked most 300 level courses should have a wider curve. Hes sorta weird and into beastiality
Great teacher!!!! Very interesting to listen to him!!!

Dr. Snee is AWESOME! He is so funny, it's almost impossible to fall asleep. On top of that he is a great professor who makes the class very do-able, and he is always willing to help during office hours. I don't even have the textbook, and I'm doing great.
No Comments

However this 3  cred class feels like 5 creds.

This was CS 251 in summer 2023. Dr.Reckinger made the class as easy as possible given the short 8 weeks of instruction. The exams were exactly on what we learned and were similar to the practice exams. We are given everything we need to know for the 5 projects.

This was CS 251 but RMP doesn't have that option, his lectures occasionally he would struggle on topics and couldn't explain it but he made 2.5 hour lectures go by fast and made accessing the materials really easy, the tests are the best example of learning from a study guide and projects are planned out and give time to complete.
He's very kind but it's so much work

Do not take this man. In just the last week, a hard homework assignment due Tuesday, we have the 3rd assessment on Wednesday, a take home exam that is coding heavy due Sunday, and then the Final exam that is due the next morning. He reads off the slides and is extremely unaccommodating and unhelpful. Exams are difficult. Worst professor at UIC.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Avoid him

Be prepared to spend your entire weekend for working on his homeworks  and quizzes. The class is heavily dependent on lectures, but all he does is read the slides. He doesn't care about feedback from students and laughs it off. Never replies to emails.

Can't believe I'm struggling in a class which is supposed to be very easy. The amount of work he assign is ridiculous. IDK what's going through his mind.  Like, this is the only class we are taking and we should care of?

NEVER, I repeat NEVER take IE 342 with Scott. He is just trying to makes student's lives hard. His homeworks are lengthy asf ( as if this is the only class we are taking). Very annoying that he expects a lot from the students.

what is going through this mans mind. His homework is so long you'll be spending the rest of your week working on his homework. I get it, its a online class & a 300 level class but to horde us with this much amount of busy work is crazy at that point I'm not learning anything I'm just trying to finish the homework to get it done by the due date smh

His lectures what is on his slideshow so you could watch the videos instead. The issue however is that his homework is sometimes nothing like what he teaches in class. He gives homework from the textbook and problems he made himself. The ones he makes himself are really bad, but quiz r easier.

Do not take this class with him unless u want to end up spending 12 hours a week on hw alone. So much hw given out each week it's honestly insane. Not to mention you have to record ur self explaining answers?? Try not to take it with Scott. To his credit the actual lectures are fine but amount of hw is insane.

He's almost like a bully. Gives a lot homework due every Sunday w/ quiz every Monday (worths 25% each). makes us record how we did the quiz including that since this class was online, there's module review questions due every Friday which is worth 10%.He substituted projects for exams which are worth 15% each. Would not recommend this class w/ him.
Structured class. Lots of help. He never put in the grade for the final exam.
Kind And Understanding, So Helpful, Amazing, Laudable

Controls is a difficult subject, but Prof. R makes sure to take it step by step so that we can keep up with it. Every week there is an online MC review quiz, a homework assignment, and an in class quiz. It sounds like a lot of work, but if you keep up with it you'll have an A. Exams are also pretty easy. Very straightforward class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's a very caring professor and ensures that he's clear on what he's teaching before he moves on. He provides lecture recordings as well as the pre-recorded videos from online classes. Willing to help you understand in the simplest way. Straight forward and clear about expectations and clearly wants you to succeed.

I really like how his class is structed, its pretty much the same thing every week. zybooks hw, quiz, lab and project. He is a great teacher and for online at least, there are no big exams. Just two open ended projects that he fully prepares you for. He also offers extra credit every week if you attend the optional coding sessions. Take him!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Very good teacher. Explains material thoroughly. Have to admit that for an intro class, It is hard for first time programmers, but if you do work, you'll get through.

He's a good prof but the material is just hard. The first half of the course is insanely easy but randomly midway through(week 9?) it skyrockets in difficulty. The projects are insanely hard to the point where half the class doesn't do them. If you have a lab later in the week, good luck getting any help on projects. Tests are okay at least.
He great at teaching but makes you put in the work. He gives out study guides which are basically the exams.
By no means is he a controls engineer. Can not teach this class at all. Your better of reading the textbook.

I enjoyed Reckinger, but beware; he practically teaches from the textbook, ans seems to not be very good at figuring out when/why students don't understand things as well as him. If you have a good sense for math and ask questions then it can be fine, but if not then class can be a struggle.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Please read this carefully. This professor thinks that students have a bachelor's degree in computer science. If you have to take him, and you probably do, get ready to teach yourself the course. The zybook used in this class does not give detail, which is why most students had hard times on the exams. Get ready to put in TIME and effort. TIME.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He has no specilization in control sytems. Basically copies from Berniker's notes which he does not understand. Comes unprepared to lecture and races through the board. Has anger issues a lot and takes it out on the class. His exams are very tough and do not at all reflect the homework. Other UIC professors have said bad things about his teaching.
Worst professor.
Heavy workload. But I did learn many in class. To know basic knowledge better, I do need many practice.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He tried,he really did. The concepts in this class are actually pretty straightforward and easy after a couple of amazing youtube videos(Brian Douglas). In the beginning the class is nice and understandable and but towards the 2nd exam the class overall become messy. He doesn't do a great job explaining complex topics and expects you just "know it"
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors in ME. All he does is scribble through the textbook and confuses himself and the whole class. This was his first time teaching 312. His grading rubric is one of the most strict I have seen. If it is not on the rubric then no points and he also does not give partial credit. Class is grade based on exams only and no curve.

Good professor; class concepts were very difficult for me. Tried my hardest by at least going for tutoring. Still performed poorly. The tests and projects were both complex. Honestly, knowing that the tests contain code writing, labs should be replaced with discussion so we get better experience at writing the code out. All I got was frustration.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I had some experience with C and C++ before taking this course. For a beginner level course, it seemed hard, not for me but for someone who really learns to program for the first time. The labs were hard. The tests are really tricky, and even though I felt confident with the material it was still tricky. I liked it because it was challenging.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: He has a teaching style similar to Dr. Shulman (take that as you may). He gives a clear idea of what is expected on exams, and his hw is a lot, but does a good job in practicing the concepts, and theyre due weekly. I honestly think hes really good at explaining concepts but I guess I'm in the minority here. Go to class and do the hw and you good.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Reckinger is a very passionate teacher however his courses are overloaded with his pride. He likes to give students labs and projects that are very hard. These labs are hard because there is little guidance within and outside of class. He provides also provides a review guide without an answer key because that is what he believes in. Not the best.

Reckinger makes this class way harder than it needs to be. All he does is copy examples of equations from the book and does not explain it very well. Unfortunately he seems to think this is the only class as IEs we have to take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He does a solid job in presenting the material but be aware that he does try to trick you on his lectures. As long as you study hard on his study guides, you should handle his exams just fine. My biggest complaint however is how many of the students had a hard time on his in lab exams. The projects were great but there were some that were very hard
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He is nice prof. This class is super hard, constant work for intro class and never got good grade. I never seen this kind of class in my life. Labs, project and exams was hard. The only thing that I got from this class is stress. the class might discharge you like me, but don't give up b/c this is the only class you will straggle.

My favorite professor at UIC! Sure the homework and exams were all very difficult due to the amount of new application questions and lack of time to finish exams, but he curves exam grades generously so that the avg grade was a B. Lectures were quite clear and his in class notes are essential for passing the class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Would not recommend at all. Constant work for an intro class. Had to spend multiple hours a day on work just to receive poor grades. Lab every week and they are graded very roughly. Spend a lot of time in lectures learning about history of computers. Iclicker needed for every class. Would never take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Reckinger did a really good job teaching this class. Uses a lot of motivating examples for the material. The content can be a bit heavy at times, but looking at the lecture capture (and the book) always helped me out considering his attendance policy. Homework is graded on completion and effort, and he posts solutions right away. Recommended.

This class is honestly just a huge waste of time. You learn a bunch of random facts of the nervous system and just try to memorize all of it for the exams. Not to mention it takes her 30 minutes to administer and finish a 10 minute quiz.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do NOT listen to the negative reviews about this professor. She is an absolute sweetheart. There are weekly quizzes and four exams (technically 5, but one is dropped). She can come off strict at first, but she is one of the most genuine and caring professors at UIC. Genuinely learned a lot in her class and regretted not attending office hours more
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: would not take her again unless I have to. She as a person is patient and soft spoken. Very nice lady, but lectures are horrible. She tends to misspeak and correct herself a lot while stuttering. it is very confusing and honestly hard to follow along sometimes. only 2 categories make up your grade, quizzes and tests. no textbook purchase required

Dr. Richmond was very nice & her lectures were pretty clear to me. As long as you practice all the material in the slides on a weekly basis you should do fine in the class. The test and quiz topics are highlighted in red on each slide.

I would say that Professor Richmond was a very kind professor and that she really cared about making sure her students understood the material. That being said, I do think her lectures were quite confusing and because they were so fast-paced, it made it hard to really grasp the material. I also feel like it was a lot to learn for exams and quizzes.

Amazing professor and amazing class. The material is very interesting, I got an A by defining the red words on all of her slides. Spent about 3-5 hrs a week for this class. Lectures are recorded which is a plus. Weekly quizzes should be helpful towards your grade, one exam and quiz is dropped. Definitely would take this class again.

Dr. Richmond is one of my favorite professors I've ever had at UIC! You can tell she truly has a passion for what she teaches, and she takes time to explain things in a way students will understand. She's good at her job and also very sweet. Almost entirely based off exams & quizzes, but she doesn't test on anything not in the Powerpoints.

Took this class asynchronously online during COVID semester. Grade mostly based on quizzes and exams. She posts weekly study guides for the quizzes. As long as you understand everything on the study guide/actually watch the lectures, you'll do well on assessments. Some lectures were a bit monotone. Extra credit was offered twice!!

The worst professor I have taken at this university. I ended the course 2 points away from an A, and was told no just explain it in your personal statement. Keep in mind we are in a global pandemic. Worst questions ever, so many grammar mistakes, AVOID HER FOR THIS CLASS AT ALL COSTS
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her class is sorely graded on exams and quizzes (no assignments or participation). Lockdown browser for every quiz and exam. Very lecture heavy and her exams are rough and include MCAT questions. PLEASE AVOID AT ALL COSTS OR IT WILL KILL YOUR GPA!!! *Plus, she talks extremely quiet so nobody can hear her! :(

She is a genuinely nice person, but a horrible lecturer. The worst I have ever had. She speaks to her undergraduate students as if they are at the graduate level, so everything she says goes right over everyone's head. Her slides are just graphs with few explanations and are very hard to comprehend.

Mostly the exams are your grade. 4 exams and then a final worth 30%. Many concepts in a short period of time. Richmond is very nice, but not the best lecturer. Her powerpoints have everything that will be on the test but they are very dense. This class takes time to understand thoroughly it isn't easy. But an A is possible. Knowing Cell bio helps
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Richmond only lectures in class, reading off the power point slides she later puts up for outside the class use. Going to the lectures are pointless because you can just study the power points outside of class since the tests are exactly off of them and not the textbook. DON'T buy the textbook, it is online and you don't use it anyways. No attendan

Dr. Richmond is a great professor. She cares about her students and their grades. If you are struggling with learning the material or are not doing well on the exams, reach out to her! The class is hard and you have to work for an A but it is definitely possible!

The nicest professor at UIC hands down. Very humble and she is willing to help her students. Her teaching is excellent, but you also have to put the time in and study. BIOS240 is not an easy class. The course is hard, not the professor. Her exam questions are fair and are about what she covers.
Such a kind lady! So down to earth. Treats you like another person and not as if shes better. I love her! She makes college meaningful.

Currently taking the class. Dr. Richmond is good at explaining  the material. She's very smart, friendly, and wants students to reach out and ask questions. Uses lecture capture, so it's very helpful to go back to after lecture. Gives opportunity for extra credit with  quizzes so it's important to take advantage of those. Haven't bought textbooks

I found this professor very clear both in explaining the material and with what she expected us to know. Focus your attention on knowing the answer to every question on her review guide; I did just that, and I felt I after the exam as if I knew the answer to every question from her portion.

She teaches her class with another professor so that should be taken into consideration. Reading the book, attending lecture, or looking at them online is required to do well on her portions of the Exams. Very clear and educational. Expect practice MCAT questions on the exams.
Needs to work on her effort

Exams are very fair and I felt that you could answer every question if you knew everything from lecture. Lecture capture is very helpful and she wants students to do well. Constantly asked if everyone was following and if anyone had questions. You get whatever grade you work for in this class

She's very helpful during office  hours and always welcomes students. Will try to look up answer if she doesn't know it herself. This is not an easy A class; it's tough. You must work hard, but it's doable. She's funny, clear, and tells you what is expected of you. Pop-quizes are extra points. No attendance. Great prof overall

The class itself is very difficult but Dr. Richmond is your best bet at doing well. All the lectures are recorded and are pretty clear. All the information you need is on the powerpoints.
