Keep in mind tht hte class itself is pretty difficult so you'll have to put in time. It is, however, a very interesting class

Worst professor at UIC. No direction given for studying, no homework, no quizzes, no extra credit. 350 points from 3 tests make your grade. Very monotone, makes an interesting topic extremely dull. She is NOT at UIC to help undergraduates.

I am currently in this class and I think Dr. Richmond is amazing professor! The powerpoints have all the information you need to do well on the exams. I currently have an A in the class and am not worried for the final exam at all!

Worst Bio Professor at UIC! She doesn't know how to speak up and she never understands questions.  Avoid at all costs or it will lower your GPA! Everyone says there is a curve but she never clearly states what it is until the end of the semester. The class has interesting information she will make dull for you.

Mumbles her entire lecture, terrible at teaching, and doesn't know how to use technology. She puts 9 chapters worth of crap on a 40 question test and expects you to know it all without giving any study materials. Only a tiny practice test with questions that aren't even on the test. For the love of god don't take her.

If you like listening to a professor whisper for a hour and a half, then by all means take her. The class material is extremely dense, there's only 3 tests to determine your grade, and there's hardly any practice test material.

Avoid if possible. Absolutely NO direction given. No practice problems,no review,power points are vague. Just 3 exams determine your entire grade. You are expected to read the text and understand it. 1 old exam is all you get as far as study material. I would NEVER recommend taking 240 with her.

She only teaches a part of the course, but the exam on the part she taught had an average of 55% with a top range of 89%. She covers way too much information for a 40 question exam and does not provide enough study direction. If you want to do well, you need to memorize everything presented in lecture.
she is a nice professor but the class is alot of info you will need to study hard to get an A

She's really nice. She wants her students to learn.  I found her lectures really interesting. Never read the book, her ppt's are detailed. She needs to speak up, or get a better mic. One of the better bio professors I had. She advises to read ahead, I never did (although I had a huge foundation). I got well above the A cutoff, huge curve

Dr. Richmond is well ground in her knowledge, but she needs to speak up! Just as some of the other reviews mentioned, her voice is sometimes difficult to hear because it is so soft. However, her tests are very fair and they are VERY closely based off of what she goes over in class. There is no ambiguity. Would recommend.
She talks really quiet but is really smart.  Everything she says is important, so you have to pay attention.  Her lectures are really well organized, but maybe too much info.
Not that bad of a class. Attend lectures and do lecture capture after and you will get a A

Went from getting below the average to a A- this is a hard class and if you are willing to put in the time, you will get the A.  Go to lecture and then do lecture capture and take detailed notes and you will be fine

She often spoke too fast in lecture. She often data dumped a lot of biochemical and molecular biology knowledge on us. She talks in a low voice. The exams are close to if not more difficult than a cell bio exam. Fails to post ppts in a timely manner. I would rather she just talk at a normal speed, record it, and post an hour+ lecture on blackboard.

I would say he is a nice person, but grading and helpfulness aren't the best. Good luck turning in an assignment and recieving an A, and be prepared for short, rude, and not helpful advice. With no helpful advice, youll have to come to terms that getting an A is likely not going to be achieved unless a miracle happens.

I loved his class! I had a research paper to do which was the “hardest” thing in the class, but it took me one day to write it when I really focused on it. The exams are off the lectures, just need to read them and watch his lectures. He is a very good teacher!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I personally found his lectures interesting but I can see the other side of it and know a lot of people would find them very lengthy and boring. You can pass without purchasing the textbook. One research paper, I think 3 exams including finals. Occasional extra credit. He writes up hilarious exams.

Honestly loved Dejonghe, really great professor. I HATED physics in highschool but I actually love it now after taking his course. I had class during his office hours and he was very accessible for other meeting times to review material. Just do the work and you'll be fine. Really cool and interesting person after talking with him during semester.

This professor was kind of biopolar, depending on how well the student actually tries to engage with and understand class material, he'd react accordingly. I thought he was really nice to me and my table bc we actually did the group probs and paid attention, but he answers questions impatiently, expecting us to understand it. I just asked TAs.

Professor was really rude. I joined the class late, and I asked to open up 2 assignments, and he told me he could, but also told me to drop the class because I wasn't going to pass. Keep checking the dates for things that are due, as he won't send out an email if assignments are due earlier or have been pushed back for later. The curve is good.

Professor DeJonghe has the biggest ego a UIC. He will belittle you for asking questions, only further inflating his already inflated ego. For a 100-level class, he expects us to have a PhD-level knowledge of physics. He is not lenient at all, no matter what situation you are in, and is the most unempathetic person at UIC. DONT take this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Genuinely does not care. If you ask him for help, he will make fun of you and walk away. If your phone even buzzes during an exam he will kick you out. If you tell him you are sick and give him a doctors, he still won't excuse you. Barley teaches, his handwriting is barley legible and he doesn't like explaining.
actually cares about students

The class isn't that bad and the weight of work is nicely distributed. There is a curve but that honestly just reflects his way of teaching. He assumes that we all understand physics intuitively, but this is an intro physics class...... His work is VERY messy, is not organized when writing his work down and its spread across the paper.
Very fast professor. Did not feel like he adequately prepared everyone for the test

Terrible. Rushes through material and occasionally scribbles on the board. I don't know why he storms through the material. When I asked if lectures are recorded, he said no in an almost laughing manner. Maybe if his lectures you might actually be able to understand the topics. Most people I talked to share the same opinions.

The worst part about the class was the weekly homework assignments. I thought the class wasn't super difficult, and Mr. DeJonghe did go through the slides fast, but I think that is mainly due to the course load. I thought the first exam was the hardest, getting easier with each passing exam. He also has online videos of him going through slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: 350 characters does not do this man justice. Professor DeJonghe is a very organized and sharp individual who provides you with top tier lectures. He works out examples, and makes the subject enjoyable. His exams do relate to the homework, group problems, etc. For reference, I never took AP Physics in HS, and the class was very simple and fun.

A good dude who deserves recognition. He understands his lectures can be fast-paced so he posts online lectures from the past as well to help out. Honestly, I had a bad relationship with math before his class but he makes it more approachable. Homework can be a lot at times, but he is more than happy to answer questions.

He is a good option for a professor. Not the perfect professor but I guarantee that if you go to class and put in effort, youll learn the material ok. The lectures are fast-paced, but i found it reasonable since a lot of content is covered. he provides a lot of helpful resources for practicing outside of class and posts solutions to most content

This dude is overrated. He needs an iPad or a tablet because his examples are really really messy and hard to understand since he uses a mouse. Long homework that doesnt even prep you for exams nor quizzes. However I hear hes the best option for physics.

Having this guy as a professor was amazing. He explains everything in short recorded lectures that are divided by topic. In these lectures, he also works out examples to ensure you understand the material. Some people like to bs the lectures for points then wonder why they do bad. He's one of the greatest gems of UIC and I wish I'd have him again.
Nice guy and seems very reasonable but overall not a great teacher, quizzes and test are not that similar to homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dude is very overrated on here. Examples are like a 6 years barely learning to write. Youd expect him to invest his time in making the material crystal clear. Lots of homework thats useless and doesnt prepare you for quizzes or exams.

The professor is a nice guy and appears to be very passionate about what he is teaching. There is a ton of homework, reading, lectures, practice problems, group problems and weekly quizzes. The quizzes are NOT at all like the homework problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Slightly overrated and disorganized but nice, understanding, honest, funny, and receptive to feedback. Accessible and helpful w his office hours. Makes physics more bearable. Workload, quizzes, and exams are rough. Read the textbook, do the lectures, HW + practice problems, attend discussion, and go to office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Labs and discussion are synchronous. Exams and quizzes aren't too bad because they are similar to the hw and problems worked in lectures. Every exam is worth 15% of your grade so make sure to do good on them. Go to office hrs if u need help. The class is not that hard, just a lot of work. Don't take it with other hard classes. JUST PRACTICE!

I took this class asynchronously and it was honestly a struggle but not too bad. TAs and profs are available almost every day and his lecture videos are really helpful. I think he's a nice guy but I rarely see him since we only meet once a week for like 15 mins. I wish he'd teach PHYS 132 :,(

Puts lots of time and effort into making the course very organized. He is understanding and will grant homework extensions (just don't abuse it). This is NOT an easy course, and you will need to put in effort. A few hours of weekly lecture videos, weekly online + written homework, weekly discussion/quiz, and lab. Actually made me enjoy physics.

He threatened my entire class with expulsion because there was an online chat discussing an exam. There weren't even any answers being shared. This little man went on a power trip and threatened me and so many of my peer's whole academic career. I would want him fired. TERRIBLE TERRIBLE TERRIBLE Human Being.

Rick is an awesome guy. He gives great lectures, answers your questions, and is available outside of class. He cares a lot about his students and makes physics actually understandable. The only thing that was tough about this class was the amount of homework given, but the homework is just like the tests so I didn't have to study!

Most blunt professor ever, gets straight to the point. As long as you understand the homework, you'll be fine. The slides have harder questions than the ones on the exams, so if you can handle those, you're set for an A.

Physics 107 is a very hard class but Prof. Dejonghe explains everything very clearly and is always available to clarify anything. Homework assignments are due every week and are very helpful. He also offers extra credit on the homework and drops one quiz. Participation with iClickers every day, he gives 3/4 points if you just submit anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. He's definitely hard, but if you do all the for-credit and optional homework you'll have a breeze. I took him both semesters, and although he uses the textbook's materials, his lectures add to it so well. Make sure to do extra well on the first exam, the later ones were significantly harder so you'll need the boost.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Rick is incredibly knowledgeable about what he teaches and he genuinely cares about his student. He puts in his best effort to help his class succeed and all he asks is that you do the same. If you pay attention, put in the work, do the problem sets on your own, and go to class, then you will have an excellent time with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Good lectures, a lot of content. Makes it easy to understand and really no bs tolerance.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Such a great professor that students from other physics professors (me included) use his notes/slides to study exclusively. He's subbed for my professor a few times and the quiz scores skyrocketed those weeks.

Awesome physics prof if you put in the work. His lectures are very clear, and it is easy to get help outside of class if you are too shy to raise your hand. Also, don't slack on the mastering physics homework and prelectures, and ALWAYS do the extra credit-- it ended up saving my grade. Also the second exam is wildly hard compared to the others.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: BY FAR one of the best professors I've had. Great lecturer, always walks you through problem-solving and gives TONS of resources to practice independently. Clearly loves the subject and cares about students (he's always available to help during office hours). Actually do mastering and written HW to prep for quizzes/tests and you're golden.

Dr. Dejonghe is one of the most kind and patient professors at UIC. I highly recommend him for anyone taking Physics I or II . Taking him again for my last semester of UIC for physics II! He holds many office hours, take advantage. Neat notes, organized lectures, answers all your questions. Notes are amazing, study them inside out for the Exams.

Class is not bad at all. Show up, take notes if you want, or don't. Examples given in class are usually harder and more specific than the ones given on the tests, so if you pay attention in class you'll do fine. Theres a ton of iclickers so it's good to show up. don't listen to negative reviews, they complain too much or don't put in the work.

Great professor, not too hard of a class. You have to put in the work and practice the optional work he gives if you want to pass. The examples he does in class are way easier than the exam questions. Expect a few quizzes, and you need the online access code for homework. An 80 or higher is an A, by the way.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Best physics107 professor! Tries his best to make everything very clear. Class requires a lot of studying, but he gives a lot of good resources- practice exams, lecture slides, homework sets. Do the odd problems in the back of the book!!! He's very helpful during office hours. Really cares about his students & wants them to be prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Amazing professor! Explains things very clearly, provides several resources like practice homework and past exams, and always on top of responding to emails and entering grades. Ironically, phys 107 was much easier than phys 105. Do the odd number problems in the back of the textbook and you will ace the exams!
Everything important is covered in lectures, just make sure you take the time outside of class to truly understand it. Lots of helpful supplemental material, dont take it for granted.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is very good at explaining the material clearly. He is very organized and stays on top of entering grades. Lots of resources on blackboard (hw, past exams, practice problems). If you put in the work, there is nothing difficult about this course. Do not go in with the mindset that this class is impossible! Taking him again for physics 107!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: First time ever taking physics and he made it difficult to understand the material. Doesn't clearly answer questions nor really teach. Group problems were done every lecture which isn't the best way to process new information. 6 quizzes 25% of your grade but drops the lowest one, they're ALL super difficult though. Rough class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: He is a great teacher! His lecture are on point & he goes over problems during lec. Homework doesn't count but do them for exams. Do his written homework he puts up on BB for extra help. Go to office hrs! I never knew how hard multiple choice questions can be on exams lol iclickers are good for extra pts if needed. Pre-lab is counted towards ur gra

The amount of MasteringPhysics kills. Good professor, can be better but still good. 80% is an A, 65% is a B. iClicker questions are very helpful. The multiple choice questions on the exam are pretty tricky though, short answer is pretty easy. His lecture slides come out of the textbook (like same visuals and everything).
He was very helpful during office hours and is just an overall chill guy. I'd recommend him as he has no accent and is pretty clear about what you should study for the exams.

I took this class as a visiting student over the summer. He just lectured from the textbook, but I did appreciate the fact that he also did examples in class rather than just deriving equations. Tests were ruthless with low averages and a hefty curve, but it never seemed to be enough. I felt like he wanted a certain percent of student to fail.

Dejonghe is a younger guy and is a new professor. This was apparently his first time teaching physics 2, plus it was over the summer so it was a very difficult semester. exams 1 & 2 averaged around 30%. He was always eager to help and answer questions and went so far as to put a hefty curve on the class. Its obvious he cares about students.

The. Oordinators make the exams so they are tough. But he is a wonderful professor. Hes great at helping and answers emails really fast. His lectures are good and easy iclicker points. Overall hes the best! Homework was on masteringphysics.
She's genuinely the best teacher and very reasonable. If you're looking for a low maintenance gen-ed to do, this class is perfect.
A really nice professor. the quizzes and exams were so easy because they were all mostly mc. you should take her if you want to save your gpa.

For sure one of the nicest teachers I've had this semester, she makes the class enjoyable. Just show up to class and take notes for the quizzes. All of the questions on the quizzes are easily answered when you take notes. The concert paper was also fairly easy to write if you actually attend a concert.

She is really passionate about her class, and that makes you want to enjoy it as much as she does. She is very flexible about absences if you let her know the reason. There isn't any homework in this class, and the tests are all online and open-note. She makes the class time really engaging, so if you want a fun class, consider taking MUS 118.

Very chill course, full of fun music facts for people who are into that. The professor has a very nonchalant and humorous personality and made the course that much more enjoyable. The work is minimal and super easy. If you show up and take notes, you will pass with an A. She was understanding if you occasionally had to miss class. 100% recommend

Your whole grade is reading and writing, but broken up into 1-2 very short things per week. Class time is spent listening to songs and discussing them along with the readings, and everyone is encouraged to share their thoughts/questions. Prof is so excited to come to class every day, and she is one of my absolute favorite teachers I've had.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Rosenberg is honestly such an enjoyable teacher who I genuinely feel I've learned so much from. She has excellent lectures and is so obviously passionate and knowledgeable about what she teaches. Class discussions were a huge part of this class but so enjoyable if you actually participate and share your thoughts!

She always comes to class with a smile. Just respect her wishes, don't be that annoying person that always has their headphones in or be on your phone during class. A lot of note taking for sure. Class is quite simple. Just have to go to one concert and write about it. Quizzes and exams are taken online. Very doable. She does seem a little fake.

This is a very very easy class, easy A as long as you take notes and watch the lectures. Professor Ruth is so sweet and her videos are interesting. She cares for her students and replies to emails which is why you should not hesitate but take her !!

I took her summer of 2023 and she was amazing. You have to take lots of notes but this class is a guaranteed A. Graded by few things: paper on a concert, two quizzes, a mid term exam and a final exam. Take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Rosenberg is probably my favorite professor ever. She makes the class very diverse and inclusive and it is apparent that her lessons are very thoughtfully put together. She loves what she teaches and it is so visible through her passionate lectures- it is so fun when a professor gets excited about what they teach
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Rosenberg is an absolute joy to have!! She's extremely knowledgeable when it comes to music. She makes her online lectures fun, easy, and exciting to watch. If you need an extra elective 100 level course, PLEASE TAKE HER!! You will not regret it.

I adore Professor Rosenberg. This is my second class with her and I cant recommend her enough! Shes very kind, caring, and attentive to students. There is clear equal respect with her and students. The classes she teaches are great and she makes them even better!

Love this class and the professor! I think she's so cool and super interesting class! Watch the lectures and take notes and you should do fine! The lectures are interesting to watch as well because she not only talks about what each artist has done but also plays their music! I discovered so many new songs i love!

Honestly, the class does take up time with readings/videos. You can definitely skim and she even notes which part of the reading to answer the response with. She's very kind and understanding when it comes to work piling up, just talk to her about it. If you like learning about music/artists, take the class. Definitely one of my favorite classes!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: 2 quizzes, 1 exam, final exam, and a paper is what your grade consist of. The only thing I didnt like about the class is the paper we have to attend a live virtual concert it cant be one that was on the past virtually which was super annoying since options are limited

I took Popular Music with her back in 2017, and I still listen to some songs that she showed us and think about that class. Truly an angel of a human. I wish I could retake the class. You can tell how passionate she is about music and it draws students in!

She always brought charm and excitement to every lecture, making the class a brighter place. The material itself was interesting, but she made sure that everyone had a chance to connect with at least something. The way she breaks up her lectures with music examples and movie clips is similarly a wonderful characteristic and made class engaging.

I took this class because of the teacher. It did not matter what the class was about. It was a bonus that the class was very interesting and fun to be in. Lots of discussions in class based on reading you get after every lecture. There are lots of short writing assignments and a large ppt project towards the end of the semester. Just try.

I took this class and realized that a teacher could actually make me want to go to class. I am not even a music major, but learning about music from Prof. Rosenberg was such a joy I signed up for another one of her classes. Best teacher I've had in UIC. Study the dashboard book provided by her and you can easily ace the tests.

"UIC may seem like an impersonal place, but once you come to my class, you'll always be a student of mine. My door is always open." One of the best professors I've ever had. She's very passionate about music and knows what she's talking about. She gave us no homework--except for one short concert report. If you love music, this class is for you.

Ruth was one of my favorite professors at UIC! She is so kind and caring, you can really tell she puts a lot of love and effort into her lectures. I highly recommend showing up to each class and take notes. If you can do that, then the class is an easy A. Study your notes a few minutes before each test and you will be fine, but do not skip class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Rosenberg is very inspirational, she knows and loves her subject. Lectures are interesting. However, the class was hard, you have to really study for the exams to get a good grade. Just two exams and two quizzes, one concert report. I enjoyed the class and very respect the professor but I had to work hard to get a good grade.

Professor Rosenberg is one of my favorite professors I've had at UIC! You can tell she is super passionate about music, which makes the class much more interesting and her lectures easy to understand. I did not buy the book, but I did attend most if not all of the lectures and got an A. I highly recommend this class with her!

Professor Rosenberg is a very caring professor and very passionate about music. There are 2 quizzes, 2 tests and a concert report. She doesn't post any of her lecture notes online so you have to come to class to know the material. The material is fun though and as long you pay attention and review the material out of class you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She does not post slides up on Blackboard anymore so you have to attend class to know what to study. Not worth buying the textbook or access code, all the music is available on YouTube. Show up to class, pay attention, and take notes, should have no issues getting an A. The paper isn't even a paper; it's a report on a concert you attended. Easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Prof. Rosenberg's American Popular Music since 1850 class was one of the easiest class I have ever taken. Attendance isn't needed and the tests/quizzes are based on the slides which are posted on Blackboard. Just memorize the slides and you will get an easy A. Only 1 paper is required in which you need to go to a concert and write your experience

Wasn't sure about the class in the beginning, but do not regret it. She made everything super easy. No homework throughout the semester. Only one 1000 word paper around the end of the semester. Would recommend.
I absolutely loved her! She was super sweet, caring, and genuinely wanted you to succeed in her course. Her lectures were clear and her exams were easy and pretty much consisted of her lecture notes.
Good class. I learned a lot. She is helpful and fair.
Great person, great teacher. And so extremely beautiful. Wish I could take a few more classes with her, I really enjoyed the one I took and it made me feel better about my degree.

she is quite boring during lectures but test/quizzes are fairly easy. most of the stuff on the exams are on the power points so i rarely used the textbook. 2 quizzes, midterm and final. there is no homework except a concert report that's due later on in the course.definitely take her if you want a easy professor.

I bought the book for a very cheap cost, and ended up not even needing the book seeing as how everything she lectured about came from the powerpoint slides, which then were notes directly from the book. So I don't mind having to spent money on the book. If you go to class everyday and take notes this is an easy A.

I was not looking forward to this class, but Professor Rosenburg makes everything easy to understand. She does say to buy the textbook, yet I never used because if you attend class the notes are what you basically need for the test. Go to class, take notes, and study them, easy A.

Professor Rosenberg was so great! She made jazz history one of my favorite classes so far. She doesn't post lecture notes on blackboard to encourage attendance, but everything she goes over in class is on the tests. There's lots of listening, but she really knows her stuff and is passionate about jazz!

She doesn't require textbooks but she makes us print out readings that are on her Blackboard. Her readings take a long time (at least 15 pages) and if you don't read you wouldn't know what's going on and you would lose participation points. WAY TOO MANY PAPERS! Topics are interesting though. And she's alright. Nice, but can seem fake

Really nice professor. Attendance is a big part of grade and important because a lot of info is covered every day. There is a LOT of reading for this class. The exams are practically the same as the practice exams that she gives.

She is a very good professor. She goes over ALL the readings and whatever she says is on her exams. The practice exams are exactly like the actual exams. If you do your work, pay attention in class and take notes you can definitely get an A. Also very easily approachable and helps a lot outside of class.

It's a tough class if you don't read all the material. Lectures are based on handouts and readings in the textbook. She plays different types of music in class and uploads them to blackboard. Listening exams can be tough. Need to know correct terminology and classification.
Easy. Helpful. Breaks everything down. Great teacher. I still remember a lot of stuff. Easy A

Don't take this. Every class consists of us listening to her ramble for 1 hr and 15 minutes. Her lectures are extremely dull and boring. At the end of the semester, we are assigned a 15 (yes, 15) minute individual presentation, a 5 page essay, AND a final exam. She doesn't use blackboard, so good luck knowing your grade at all. Please run.

I do not recommend her class. She is nice and passionate about Congo, but sometimes she can be passive-aggressive. She does not grade based on a rubric and does not post any assignments on Blackboard. She goes on a lot of tangents, and her class does not have any structure just to come to class with discussion questions based on the reading.

She's a beautiful person, but as a professor she's just lacking a few qualities. Her lectures are very boring but she doesn't assign work outside of class other than readings which is a plus. Doesn't use blackboard so you can't see your grade along the semester so you're just kinda left in the dark.

The professor is about 80. She isn't very active in her field so it's not fair of UIC to not hire someone who's current? She says weird racial things like "my ancestors were slave owners" (said to a Black student), and "I have 20% south asian DNA" (said to a South Asian student). Had to drop because she was putting me to sleep with the rambling.

Another case of a good person but bad professor. Only online resources were syllabus and an unclear citation guide. Grade in this class was 50% participation, which is fairly simple, 25% tests (straightforward if you paid attention), 25% final paper, which she WILL be nitpicky about citations for some reason... she gave out candy and donuts though!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dont recommend at all. She's horrible and communication and doesn't utilize any online resources, even blackboard. I was not able to see my grade in class ever because she doesn't use blackboard. Her everyday powerpoint read-throughs and long side stories make the class impossible. No rubrics for anything and an unhelpful syllabus. Dont take.

After taking ANTH100 with her I have a whole new appreciation for my other professors. Her lectures consist of PowerPoints with full paragraphs and long side tangents about her interests. When answering student questions, she will stand over you and call you out with conviction. She reviews papers by not giving feedback but calling you out. Don't.

Horrible professor. Terrible at communicating with her students and doesn't understand how to use technology.  She is knowledgeable on the subject, but her way of teaching is ineffective and hard to follow. She straight up reads paragraphs off slides and will go off on long side tangents and stories that aren't important. Dont recommend at all.
Tough grader, no extra credit, boring lectures, no rubric or grading criteria given, can't use computers and grades stuff really difficult for students.

The ratings for her are dumb. She talks basically the whole class, every class period, with no exception. Easy grader if you show effort. heavy readings but can probably get by with skim reading. Participate every day, you are chilling. The class is boring but if you put in an ounce of effort you will get a good grade in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took the congo class with her. The lectures are super boring

She always interrupts her students when they are asking questions & doesnt communicate her answers clearly AT ALL. She RARELY utilizes PowerPoints or ANYTHING to organize her curriculum or help students. Are we supposed to remember everything that she says? Her syllabus is 20 pages long(not included a reading schedule). She won't use Blackboard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her communication skills are lackluster and she expects you to know how she wants things without explaining how she wants things. She expected us to purchase much of the reading material, which I was not inclined to do. She spends class talking about whatever she wants to on the topic and telling the kids who get a chance to talk that they're wrong
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is my 2nd semester taking HON 125 (Congo), and she had the same criteria. 10 pg paper, 15 min presentation, LOTS OF READING, midterm(short answer). But overall, she's a very easy grader, and has very interesting, but often boring lectures. It's nice though bc even though she has discussion always, she talks all the time. But, shes passionate!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: My advice to all students is "GET OUT"

Dr. Roosevelt is a knowledgeable professor (seriously, search her up, you'll find out:)), but she is a little intimidating. Took HON 125 with her, on Rwandan Genocide, and it was pretty chill bc we would just read books (tons and TONS of pgs) and would have discussions almost every day, but she would talk all the time. Midterm (75 q's)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I learned very little in this course. In my view the professor was unable to connect to the students. She seemed distant and uncaring, and had few positive interactions. She seems nice during the first class, but was unable to personally connect with students. I gained very little information during this course and I wish I would have taken another

I had high hopes for this course, but none were reached. The lectures were boring, the professor unapproachable, and the subject dull. I would not take this course or another course with this professor again.

DO NOT TAKE HER CLASSES! Out of all of the anthropology classes I've taken this one was unbearable because of her. She just talks about stuff that is way over people's heads. She's smart don't get me wrong and she grades easily but she is so RUDE. If something's not to her liking (which you'll never know because she's not clear) she'll put you down

Boring, rude, and unfair. She would interrupt students' presentations only to insult them. We had to read 1 book/week, and some of the books were 400 pages long. The syllabus said there was no final exam, but 3 weeks before finals, she changed her mind and said there would be a final. Only returned grades for one assignment. Her lectures were dull.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Her lectures are just paragraphs on powerpoint that she reads off of the whole hour. This makes it quite hard and boring to take notes since she goes through them so fast. She wont post her lectures online thinking nobody will come to class but nobody does anyway. I never read the book and obtained all knowledge from discussion. Do not take her.
The professors professional abilities to teach are extremely poor. Her teaching style and ability to convey the material clearly is extremely poor.

She types her power points in paragraphs and reads straight off of it. She tends to think everyone is interested in Anthropology and takes it seriously when most people just need to cover a gen ed. The discussion classes dont even go over the material in class. The tests questions are mainly from the book but also from lecture. Shes very BORING.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Roosevelt is very knowledgeable but she expects every single person to be interested in her class, as if we took this class because we wanted to. Not to be rude, but this is Anthropology 100, most of us are taking the course just to fill a requirement and there were no more sociology openings. With that, she does NOT curve exam grades. Good Luck

Professor Roosevelt is a different kind of Professor. The key to success in her class is to read and participate in group discussion or else she will drill you with pop quizzes. Her lectures can be boring at times and attendance is mandatory. She is lenient with assignment due dates and there is no final. The final is turning in a 10 page paper.

Anna Roosevelt teaches from experience. She is an EXPERT on the subjects she lectures on. The class I took was about writing advanced research papers, but she chose to focus specifically on Rwanda as a class topic. I was challenged to read and write extensively, and I feel that a lot of  doors have been opened for me academically thanks to Prof. R.

I took her for an honors core requirement, she isn't a bad professor. She is clearly passionate about her area of study and is very through in her research. When you walk out of the class, you'll definitely be very knowledgeable about the subject. In terms of grading, we had two very easy quizzes and one final paper in the topic of your choice.

Interesting professor; extremely knowledgeable and experienced.  She has a unique style that some students may find difficult.  Takes attendance when she remembers, talks most of class time without bothering students.  Read nine ethnographies with a quiz after each.  One twenty page paper with attendant presentation.

While she knows a vast amount of information dealing with Anthropology, her problem is that she pushes it at you, shoving it in your face, making it seem like she is better than you.  She never teaches from the book and never follows through with assignments she actually gives.  We haven't had any tests yet and the semester is already ending.
No Comments

Interestin topic but she wasn't very thorough with explanations. Absent a lot because she's so busy. Very stuck up. Made us read 7 books but i got by reading summaries off internet. One paper and 2 exams.

Roosevelt got a bad rap from other students and even other professors, but she was always intresting and helpful to me and I will always remember her as one of my favorite professors. She gave me a lot of useful tips on my career path too.
i used to have a crippling fear of death. after taking this class, i think i'm ready for the grave.

He is a nice teacher with thorough lectures but when it comes to the quiz worksheets they are confusing. The wording felt deliberately ambiguous. We screened interesting movies and had to analyze them in the quizzes. I recommend taking notes on even the casual things he says during lectures and being very specific with your film analysis.

Professor Rubin is very knowledgeable about cinematic history and film techniques. HOWEVER!!! He is an extremely difficult grader, and the other reviewers are correct in the assessment that they expect you to know as much about the content as they do. If you do not take tedious notes on everything he says, you will do poorly.

Professor Rubin is an amazing authority on all things related to film. He knows the ins and outs of everything that is being taught and would even answer questions about film beyond the course. There were about 10 written responses and 8 quizzes but the two lowest were dropped. He really wants you to do your best and will help you do so. 10/10

Extremely tough grader-- don't expect to get an A in here. He does NOT explain things well during lectures, uses trick questions to trip you up on tests and gives a TON of homework. I do not recommend taking Rubin.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Frustrating prof. with a less-than-favorable attitude regarding an intro/appreciation course. He treats his lectures as gospel and reads them aloud from a prepared sheet. Before midterms/finals, there's a review session where he basically reads the test out loud. Don't bother taking notes until that day. Overall, not challenging and not engaging.

Overall P Rubin rocks! If youre interested in film youll enjoy/learn a lot in his course. He is passionate about film. Take lecture notes Mon, watch film Wed. You MUST take notes. Lectures are interesting. He does review before tests (ALL tests open-note) and tells you he is giving 80% of the answers. MUST attend! Extra credit for participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Mr. Rubin has a passion for teaching film and it shows. There are a lot of papers to write, so if you don't like writing this class might not be for you. There is no textbook-he is the textbook. The quizzes are open book, and attendance is mandatory. If you have any interest in film, then you will really like this class.
Professor Rubin was ok. Lectures were dry. Some of the films were dry. Some were awesome. Papers were somewhat difficult and he calls them "quizzes'. Have to go to class or you will be marked absent.

Rubin is amazing! I loved this class, he was always willing to help and listen to your views on the films watched. I can't wait to take 233 with him. Even though we had quizzes or really papers each week it was still a great class! I highly recommend it!

I had Marty for 233 and 232. He picks awesome films! Attend lectures and elaborate on interesting observations/interpretations of the films in your "quizzes." Semi-hard grader if you pay attention and have a genuine interest in film, this class is extremely interesting and enjoyable.

Mr. Rubin is the man. He is a genius on film and makes class very enjoyable. Midterm, paper, final, and weekly quiz's make up the grade. Attendance is mandatory, but class is great. Rubin is a chill and passionate guy that just wants  to educate his students better on film. If film interests you, take this class...no doubt.

Midterm and Final are absolutely impossible. He has weekly "quizes", but really its a weekly 2-3 page paper, and he grades them on an impossible scale. DO NOT TAKE. While he does care about his students, he expects them to know as much about the films as he does.
Expect to read and summarize the entire textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: this is actually the most boring class i have ever taken. if i could drop it and retake it with another professor, i would.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She's not the worse nor the best professor i've ever had. As long as you do the work you'll be ok
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Great professor who is obviously passionate about what she teaches. Great insight into commonly misinterpreted stats with the influence of big corp and unequal power. Interesting lectures, very strict on attendance,  grading not super strict if you follow instructions outlined. My book for the review was only 150 pages. No textbook.

If you are a commuter do not take her class since she does not show up to class sends out an announcement an hour before. The information you learn in the class is interesting. The class has 3 exams not cumulative, 5 annotated bibs, book review, weekly quizzes. The book review was really time consuming books are around 300 pages or more.

Professor Satra is very good at teachinglecturing about the history of medicine. Her class is one of the best classes I have taken at UIC. She shows documentaries that help explain the content even more. Don't skip class since she can give pop-quizzes throughout the week!

This teacher is so frustrating.  Communication outside of class is hard to obtain.  she is not understanding and will fail to work out any issues in class that students are having with homework.  does not curve either.  too much homework.  never uses the textbook.  first comment was probably her grading herself

She comes to class unprepared, and has too many assignments that are due at the end of the semester.  But is a tough grader. Lectures, powerpoints, discussions and readings do not have anything to do with the material of what is on the exam.

Great professors who sees the students' hardships and issues with the course, and CLEARS THEM OUT! Best sociology professor. Makes you do the right amount of work to prove yourself worthy, with tremendous aid and huge amounts  of extra credit opportunity - including wearing a costume on HW! If taking Sociology of Medicine, MUST TAKE HER. Easy A.

This class appeared to be a more open discussion on microscopes. Dr. Gao is very passionate on teaching about the various types of microscopes and how they can be used. He was also very nice to ensure that we would receive credit on attendance and graded fairly on the presentation.

You could tell he isn't familiar with the class or teaching at all. Open-book problem sets saved my grade a bit. Tests are hard, ngl. One TA was a lot more nitpicky than the other, and labs are graded half and half. If I had more time to study for tests, I would've gotten an A. Labs are very interesting to do, but hard to explain later tho.

Overall, 452 is not a very difficult class if you actually follow along with the lectures and use online resources to fill in knowledge gaps. Attendance wasn't required, but in my experience the tests often covered a larger scope of content than just the lectures, so discussion was very important. didn't use textbook but would definitely recommend.

BIOCHEM 452 is doable and easy to get an A if you spend enough time reading the textbook + lecture slides. Gao's teaching style isn't for me because he mostly reads off the lecture slides. He seems really nice tho. A lot of extra credits on exams, no quizzes, and only 2 easy projects (super easy to get full points). Remember to attend Discussions!

I didn't actually read anything about this class until I was already in it, and I needed the 160 credit, so I wasn't going to drop even if I hated it. Turn out this was actually the best class of my entire first year, cause Prof. Jen is super chill and flexible. She is also super kind and encouraging, just do your work and you're golden.
extremely easy class that doesn't take up too much time. 5 essays but very doable and a few assignments thats it.

Dr. Rupert is a top tier professor to take for ENGL 160, she's very open to letting you write about what may matter to you and gives you tons of freedom and feedback. She's extremely kind and very clearly cares about what she teaches within class. Lectures can get a little sluggish but I blame that mainly on myself and the material.

Jennifer is a great professor! Really tries to build relationships with her students; you can tell she genuinely cares and wants you to succeed. Really lenient and always willing to address any of your concerns. She loves talking with her students after class. Pretty hard to fail with her.

Professor Rupert is an amazing teacher. Her lessons were fun, even when the topics weren't personally interesting. The homework level is reasonable and enjoyable. She gives you a lot of independence in choosing topics for your papers. She grades fairly and provides good feedback! My favorite English professor of all time.

I took her ENGL 160 class. She taught civic imagination. She is a very nice, caring professor. One thing is that you have to be sure to read instructions. I submitted a paper less than the minimum of three pages and she didn't bother grading it. I got a 0 :(. When she does grade, she gives great feedback. Attendance is mandatory (graded).

amazing prof overall. her lectures do get boring which made me fall asleep a lot but she really does give points to people if effort shown. she is somewhat a hard grader but also lists her reasoning. there is lots of papers to do but if you score literally As on like 4 of them towards the end of semester ur gonna get an A. super nice and supportive
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: I love Prof Rupert, I think the work is reasonable and even fun but that is probably if you're passionate about this course, which you can become so, she inspired me to minor in GWS. Her essays are so fun to write, got to write my own story and she loved it. You won't regret it ever.

Has amazing individual connections with each student, including myself. Feedback is always positive, even if critique is given. Does a great job at uplifting all voices and giving pushback on hate when needed while still assuming one's best intentions. Horrible at formatting Blackboard. Some pacing problems but not her fault! Take her If you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I love this class with a passion. The professor makes this class so interesting and is sure to always talk to students individually about their progress. The papers and short writing assignments could seem intimidating but as long as you choose topics you are interested in, you will thrive and enjoy this class and the teacher. Overall, LOVE! 15/10!
She's a really sweet lady. Although essay writing does get a little tedious, her assignments aren't hard, and she grades really fair.

Professor Rupert is an absolute gem. I had her Spring 2023 for English 207, and she was extremely caring in and out of the classroom. Her grading criteria was clear, she would give opportunities for redo's on papers, and made sharing in class a comfortable atmosphere. She is the epitome of what a professor should be, and I'd 1,000% take her again!

Loved her class, you can tell she cares about seeing her students succeed. She's very clear about deadlines and grading critera. She grades first drafts (doesn't impact grade tho) and gives amazing feedback which helps with the final draft. Just show up to class, do the work, and you will do great in this class (+ tbh I did fine without the book).

I could write so much about professor Rupert. She is the most caring, funny, and hard working professor I have had so far. Our class was so engaging and she loved hearing our feedback. She checks in on her students too which is so nice. Don't think about it, take her class!

Dr. Rupert was the best professor that I have yet to take at UIC. Her lectures are so fascinating and there was truly never a dull moment. I absolutely adore and loved this class, I am extremely sad that it is coming to an end. There are a few papers to write, however, these types of papers are the ones you simply just want to keep writing. 10/10.

She is so caring and respectful of students, understanding of deadlines, always provides feedback, and loves to talk and accommodate her students. She will email you outside of the semester to make sure you are taken care of. Her feedback on drafts is hard but it is ALWAYS for your benefit. Just really try and I guarantee 90-100% on ever paper.

Dr. Rupert is the best professor I've met in all of UIC. I wish I could sign up for another one of her classes just so I could learn from her again. She is extremely passionate in her area of Women Studies, as well as other global issues. All of her lectures are engaging and eye-opening. Please take her class if you can! You won't regret it :)

I've had Dr. Rupert for 2 classes and she was just awesome! She brought phenomenal insight into both classes and genuinely demonstrated how much she cares about her students and our success. I would recommend anyone to take a class with her if given the opportunity!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If I had more than 350 characters, I'd write a research paper about this excellent woman. She made sure that everyone understood the papers we had to complete for class. She always reminded us that her office hours were open and she was very helpful when students needed/wanted feedback. She made class so much fun and I will genuinely miss her.

I loved having Professor Rupert as a teacher! She is awesome :) When I first started this class I thought I would receive a B or a C because I didn't think my writing would be good enough but I was wrong. Professor Rupert gave great feedback and always offered her help outside of class. She has a great personality and loves when people participate.

I love her. Her 101 class got me to major in GWS years ago. She put immense thought into her class readings and lectures. Discussions were always fruitful. She has a great sense of humor and personality. Incredibly compassionate. I don't see how anyone could not adore this woman.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: This class was my favorite class this fall! Professor Rupert really made it known what she expected from us and followed her own rules for herself. The class was incredibly interesting and thought provoking since it dealt with contemporary topics. Also she grades first drafts!! Meaning improvement in ur grade is 100% possible!
She's super friendly. Lots of reading though. Makes it possible to get an A on the second draft if you take note of the feedback given.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Great professor. Teaches with enthusiasm. Very friendly. Happy with her class.

Loved this class!!! If you can take this class, take it! Prof Rupert is so kind and allows rewrites for her papers, which can really boost your grade. Readings are interesting, as well as the topics discussed in class. There are a total of 7 papers- 5 response papers, one midterm and one final. Sounds alot, but its not bad at all! Take it!!!
Passionate prof who actually cares about what students have to say. Yes there are quite a few papers but they're usually on interesting topics and are relatively short.
Amazing Prof. Try your best to fit her in your schedule.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor Rupert's class was honestly the best class I ever took! She is extremely engaging and is super passionate about what she teaches. There are definitely readings for every class, but they were really interesting! There is a lot of writing that goes into this class, but her topics were broad allowing you to write what you wanted.

J Rupe is a great prof. She's helpful and respects students who actually ask for help. I recommend doing the readings. Most of them won't be too difficult, but it is difficult to participate in class if you don't. Take advantage of being able to submit drafts. Don't slack on that because she'll get mad if you do. Taking drafts seriously are key.

Rupert is a phenomenal Professor who is one of the few english professors to properly execute a class. I took her for Eng 117 and her class pushed me to be a better writer. My favorite part about her class was being able to redo assignments. Not because I was lazy, but rather to learn how to improve my writing. She also gives very helpful feedback!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Rupert genuinely cares about work as well as her students. She is very understanding. This trait allows her to relate to many of us. She helped me find the most optimal path in my life rather than the most comfortable path. All in all a teacher filled with compassion and vigor.

Dr. Rupert is an amazing professor. I took her twice(in 2014 and in 2015). She gives a lot of papers, but she gives great constructive feedback that will help you become a better writer. Take her class! She is not a bore and she's very passionate about the topics she teaches. I would say one of the best English professors I have ever had.

The Honors Core class she taught was so fascinating, and it was obvious that she was so passionate about the subject matter. It was one of the few classes where I looked forward to what would be watched or discussed. Jennifer is such a wonderful professor, and if you have a chance to take her, do so!

Professor Rupert is so caring and so passionate about each subject that she teaches! Her class covered several subjects ranging from hip hop music to horror movies. There are 5 short response papers, a midterm paper, and a final paper. She provides lots of feedback to help you succeed on the papers and respects the opinion of all her students!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: I adore Jennifer! Her class was interesting and insightful, giving students the opportunity to learn how the media constructs society. There was a total of 7 papers, which made the class tough, but worth it! I felt like I was learning about things that really matter, and I was excited to attack each subject.

OMG! Jennifer was amazing! I took her honors 123 course and loved every moment of it. She definitely keeps the class interesting. She helped so much with the paper project ideas and response papers. She was always available during office hours
Good class

Dr. Rupert is a great professor! At most you will do a lot of mini writing assignments and then a few big ones. There's quite a bit of reading.. You will however need to budget printing because she will want you to print 30 page articles for one class period. Always be prepared and on time or she will ask you to leave. Make an honest effort!

Best professer I have ever had! She is amazingly helpful and her classes are really interesting as well! She loves to help students outside of class as well. If you have the chance to take her you definitely should!

One of the best professors I have had! She really brings passion to the issues and inspires that in her students. This is not an easy A type class but you will get a good grade if you put in the work and learn a lot at the same time! Highly recommended!

She is very helpful and nice. Takes the time to help you out and talk to you. The class is pretty hard, you have to work hard to get an A! I got an A but worked very hard for it. Three papers , everyday reading journals, movie screening, and lots of reading. However, I learned a lot in her class.
Very good proffesor she is really sweet and extremely helpful she is also very lenient when it comes to do dates also very funny and interesting. If you take GWS 101 take her she is AMAZING!!

If taking a GWS class take her. Come to class and do the reading/journal assigment she dosent grade the journal take the exam and study for it and do the 3 papers and u'll be fine...great teacher....will go above and beyond to help her students
Dr. Russ was an amazing teacher that likes to make jokes and really feels like a friend every interaction we get.

Russ is one of the best teachers at UIC. If you have to take Eng 486, make sure you take it with him. You do a lot of fun projects. Hopefully you like to read and write. If you don't, you may want to reconsider your major. This is for the Teaching of English. He really cares about his students and gives lots of helpful information.

Great guy, absolutely loved him. He doe require a lot of reading for the course but never really checks to see if anyone does it. He's super laid back and is very understanding when it comes to deadlines. He likes to hear out everyones opinions on his teaching and the way the class is conducted and genuinely cares about everyone. Rewards effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Russ had a very different style of teaching, but in a good way. He was always kind & considerate of his students' needs. Show the effort & you'll get the grade u want. He did however give way too much reading & also treated his class like it was high school (gave reading hw before semester started, we took a field trip, etc.) But overall a good guy
A really good guy, knows every student on a first name basis. Always available for help!

Russ is hands down one of the best instructors this university has to offer. For my semester, the topic was autobiographies and it consisted of four projects. He's quick to reply to emails, he's available for extra help, gives AMAZING feedback, and an overall great guy!
He is a really good teacher, cares about his students and makes sure everyone understands everything. Ask him for feedback on your paper and he will definitely give you 100.

One of my favorite classes I've taken at UIC. Russell was a super cool professor who genuinely cares about us learning. Two books you need to read as well as assigned readings. In all, there will be 4-5 papers. The topic you choose to write about for the last paper will determine what group you will be in for the group project. Class was an easy A.

Russ was awesome! He made the class fun and exciting! We gave us an extension on one of the writing projects. He helps you and gives great feedback. I highly recommend going to his office hours because he helps even more and appreciates it when students come. He's really friendly! :)
I enjoyed Russell Mayo because English 161 was super easy and the topic was food!

Professor Rush was honestly like a breath of fresh air, I loved having him so much!!! Not only is he so sweet and understanding but his class was also interesting. He never forces anyone to participate and if you talk to him, almost any problem can be solved including attendance. Highly recommend taking him (:

He is probably the best professor I had so far. As long as you do the four essays and show up to class you will 100% pass this class with an A. He is also super understanding if you need extra time on your essays. Just email him ahead of time. Make sure to take him!

Best English teacher at UIC. Literally just do what he asks you for and you'll get an A. we only write 4 essays and he gives you the option to turn a first draft to give you feedback then just follow his instructions and youre guaranteed that A. He's really funny and you can even text his personal phone number if you need help.

This was the easiest course I've ever taken, only coz I took it with him. You only write a total of 4 essats throughout the entire semester, no homework, no tests or quizzes. With every writing assignment, he reads your essay and makes corrections and gives feedback before the actual due date. He is an easy grader, and extends deadlines.

Lectures were always really interesting and followed state of the art applications, exercises were at times difficult (you have 1-2 weeks to work on them) but proved extremely useful for understanding the materials discussed in class. Professor was always easily accessible for clearing any in class doubts.
He is an awesome, caring, sweet professor.
Lots of state of the art applications of engineering.
The class isn't mandatory to show up, quizzes and tests are online, including the final. Gives extra credit, highly recommend.
SUCH AN AMAZING PROFESSOR, THE BEST AT LOYOLA
awesome prof! Actually look forward attending his class. :) highly recommend

Professor Leach is a great lecturer. His lectures are never boring and he is very friendly and down to earth. You get participation points just for showing up to class so make sure you do. You can earn up to 40 points of extra credit by doing more research participation than is required so thats awesome. I would highly recommend taking him!

Lectures are pretty straight forward and he has a really good sense of humor. He's super approachable and willing to clarify any questions. At the end of class he does "minute papers" which count as participation points. Tests are noncumulative, based on power points & a few questions from text.  Great teacher, would definitely take again.

UPDATE: HE IS NOW TEACHING AT LOYOLA UNIVERSITY CHICAGO. I got him by accident, but I'm glad I did. He explains things very clearly, and his tests and quizzes are decently easy if you pay attention in class. He lets you do research participation for extra credit, and the final is optional. I would recommend him!
lectures don't suck, free points for showing up to class, like 2 assignments and one research project, 4 exams, and very approachable.
In this class you can get a good grade and you end up learning a LOT. Hes also really engaging and lectures are interesting. I didn't like the experiments we had to sign up for.

Lectures were fun, interactive, and awesome! All of the homework was online via an e-book. There was only two papers to do, and they were pretty straight forward. Exams were mostly just based on the lecture slides and the homework. Also, you have to participate in psychology studies, which was pretty cool and easy. Take this class if you can!
He truly is amazing. I would highly recommend you take. His TA was really cool and awesome too. Know the definitions and understand the examples and this class is a breeze.
Easy class. Did not take notes at all and still got an A. Don't know how. Ryan makes it really easy for you though and is extremely helpful

There are no questions on his test that aren't derived from the lecture slides we go over in class. He uses plenty of wit to make lectures interesting and many real life examples to make content memorable. Grading criteria is very lenient, so it's an easy A as long as you put forth enough effort.

Ryan is a great professor. I never bought the book. He had slides put up on blackboard. I never studied for the exams and quizzes and I got an A in the class. His lectures do drag most of the times. He is very funny and tries to make the class entertaining.

Ryan is a great lecturer, he is super nice, and if you have any problems you can talk to him and it's not a big deal. There are 8 quizzes and 4 exams, but they are okay. As long as you come to the lectures, and take notes, and pay attention you're good. His tests were pretty av. and he does curve them based on the top 10% scores.
Good guy. You could tell he worked hard to entertain the class as well as providing them with good and understandable information. He made the lectures really entertaining!
Great Lectures

Ryan is super laid-back and knows his stuff! The course is just an overview of Psychology and you learn a lot of interesting things with him! He drops one test, two quizzes, and there's no homework besides two term papers. The class is easy and seriously worth attending. If you're looking for an interesting but non-stressful course, here it is!

Ryan is absolutely gorgeous! He's really nice, understanding, and always willing to help. His test questions are a bit tough but if you study you'll get an A. He has 4 tests and no cumulative final. He also drops the lowest test grade, and 2 out of your 8 quizzes. Highly recommend to take him.

Pretty straightforward class. You know when the quizzes are, 10 questions all multiple choice. Drops lowest 2 quizzes. Exams are pretty easy if you study your lecture notes. Lowest Exam grade is dropped as well out of 4. Recommend taking him for Psychology 100.
Bob was great during lectures and even more when there was class engagement. Would recommend this class to those who want to improve and maybe enjoy writing a little more.
Awesome guy, no cap.
This guy is laid back. He is a fricken genius. He is young so he understands. He's kind and he's cool. Easy grading. Best professor I've ever had
Best instructor at UIC. Do yourself a favor and take his classes. Also he looks like peter parker... and he's from NY... just saying.

Bob is amazing, he makes you think outside the box when you're reading! The readings aren't too heavy but participation does matter! He notices who participates and who doesn't. Overall, if you read you'll get an easy A

Bob (as he likes to be called) is an overall great professor. Very open minded, real relaxed and laid back, loves group discussions so participation is key. Young so he's really understanding but he's no pushover either.

He is phenomenal! I've learned how to break out my shell and write freely. Classes are early in the morning but definitely worth it. He doesn't rely his teaching on a book, but rather interacts with his students. He jokes around A LOT so you will never be bored in his lectures. If you need help, go to office hours!Overall, the best teacher in UIC.

I cannot begin to explain how absolutely amazing this professor is. He made me LOVE taking an 8AM! Classes are discussion based;graded on participation. He is unlike any other teacher, believes you cannot grade someone solely on rubrics, no quizzes; young & understanding. Great discussions and outlook on life, very open-minded. TAKE HIS CLASS!!!!!

I cannot begin to explain how absolutely amazing this professor is. He made me LOVE taking an 8AM! Classes are discussion based;graded on participation. He is unlike any other teacher, believes you cannot grade someone solely on rubrics, no quizzes; young & understanding. Great discussions and outlook on life, very open-minded. TAKE HIS CLASS!!!!!!

I LOVED HIM! He was an absolute pleasure to have as a professor. One thing that I enjoy about him is that he was my Eng 161 professor and he still is in contact with me. Very easy to understand and totally chilled and laid back. I would recommend him to literally anyone. Very easy A if you show up, participate and write your papers!

This professor is beyond amazing. He's always willing to help out his students, he has enthusiasm to teach class, regardless on how early it is, and he's super laid back! Yes there are writing assignments here and there but they're not all that difficult, and he always gives amazing feedback so you can better your work. I recommend it to everyone!

This professor is my favorite! He actually understands, teaches well and knows what we want to hear. There are papers due but as long as you put your effort in and take his feedback, you'll be alright. Aside from that the class is not so hard. If you're deciding if you should take him or not, you should! I would highly recommend!

This professor is smart, laid back, and cares about his students. There isn't much work outside of class other than the writing assignments and overall it's easy to do well. Despite this course not being too difficult, I still feel like I am able to learn something. I highly recommend.

She gives SO MANY group quizzes, gives homework on topics she hasnt taught yet, has a horrible class average on tests/quizzes but refuses to change anything about her teaching style, goes way too fast during lecture so no one understands what shes saying, and answers questions poorly or not at all. DONT TAKE HER CLASS UNLESS YOU HAVE TO!!!

She developed a weird obsession with group quizzes that did nothing but hurt your grade. I understand being able to work with others in life, however, I signed up for Chemistry, not a team-building workshop. Her tests are nothing like the homework. Her study guide is useless. Always check your exams for grading mistakes. Great curve in the end.

Ryu has a kind personality and a way of communicating with students. With that said, her lectures are disorganized and she doesn't post completed lecture slides. If you rewatch the lectures, it will benefit you greatly. I didn't like the amount of group quizzes we received. If you take this class, you should hope for a great group.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: From the very beginning I emailed and met w her asking what I needed to do to pass her class bc it wasnt She told me u have time to figure it out. I re watched every lecture and spent multiple hrs studying for this class so I could pass. What really helped me tho was the curve. This semester the curve to get a C was 52.5% and a B was 72%.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you didn't take AP Chem at ALL in your high school career you need to do all the preparations you can.(Usually per week theres 3-4 chapts to read, do at least half of this before your lecture on Monday's).Lectures seemed more like a review. I barely passed my AP chem last my snr yr of HS (C) now I should pass with a B+/A-. (b/c its lit the same)

Professor Ryu does not know how to teach the course material. She just goes over lecture slides and assumes students know the material in that way. The class average for exams is a D and she still questions students on what they are doing wrong instead of questioning her own teaching skills.
Goes off topic too much, gives homework with the content she hasn't even taught yet. Class average on exam was low D and she questioned the students rather than her own mediocre teaching style
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Don't get me wrong Ryu is a nice lady but she cannot teach for her life. She teaches to where it makes sense for her, she will read off the slide and then as soon as she's done then its off to the next slide, she'll do practice problems but half the time she gets corrected by the students. The homework is extremely easy but the tests are impossible
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Ryu is super sweet and understanding however her teaching style is not ideal for such a rigorous course. She moves through the lectures extremely fast and the homework is 15x easier then the exam Her study guides are NOTHING similar to the exams. HOWEVER her curve at the end of the semester is HUGE
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Ryu is super nice, but she can't teach
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I think this was her first year at UIC and teaching this course, but that does not give her an excuse for the insanely fast paced lecture. Like it was crazy how fast she goes and at some points she does not explain the material well. Exams where difficult and harshly graded with not enough time to complete the full exam. Im just glad I got a B.
Class is SUPER boring, arguably a waste of time. She rushes through lectures and assumes you know stuff that you haven't heard of before.

honestly your best off going to a different teacher for help with chem. the other teachers just explain it way better then she does and they make sure you understand what's going on. whatever you do don't take Ryu!

Shes one of UICs best chem 122 professors and tries to make lecture as engaging as possible. Some people gave her a lower rating because she tends to go fast, but as long as you review the powerpoint (which you should for ANY chem class), youll be fine. This a science class, so youll need to do the work and study regardless of the professor.

Ryu is a nice lady, but my lord is his class hard. You have to always be on your A game to be able to get anything from her lectures, because she explains things very quickly. 50 minutes are not enough for her very long and hard exams, or at least in my opinion. I hope she changes her teaching style in future classes though.

Ryu zooms through lectures. she gives tests with an unfair amount of questions given for the allotted time. Ryu also doesn't really care if you don't understand whats going on in class if you say she's going to fast her go-to response is "we have a lot to do and not enough time" this would be a great excuse if she actually taught well. Awful Prof.
You dont actually meet him but overall good experience in the class.
You'll only meet him if you go to drop-in hours but he's so amazing. He makes everything very easy to understand and the TAs were amazing and lenient as well.
Nice professor. Explains things well and is very responsive/understanding.
He is genuinely so sweetie :) His grading is super lax and the TA's were also generally pretty lenient. The class is pretty easy but you learn good lab techniques

Professor Santus was a wonderful professor! The class has a ton of content information, I definitely recommend making mind maps to reconnect information from earlier weeks. He does make immunology way more digestible for undergrads and people with little cell bio knowledge can understand. I do wish quizzes were on the blackboard calendar.
