There are other upperclassmen and professors there to help, so the class overall was easy, just do your work and show up. Antonio's architecture projects are cool :)
Lots of random assignments but an easy class to take. Was bored 9 times/10

The worst architecture professor at UIC. Whatever he says don't listen. There are so many amazing architecture professors that should have more authority than him. His lectures do not describe what architecture is and any future classes you have showcase this. He was even worse in technologies.

The reviews make it seem like he's bad- he's not. ARCH151 is a breeze & an intro to architecture. He teaches about buildings, technology etc. These are things you'll pick up in the next two semesters anyway, which is why people hated the class (boring/busy-work), but it's better to have this class than to be dunked into cold water with ARCH105.

I felt like I wasted my time taking this class. It was stupid easy, yet attendance was mandatory and so many assignments. This class is only 2 credits. It was a waste since it did not seem like I had value in this class. Since 151 and 105 are connected, we learned pretty much the same stuff.

I did not have a bad experience with Professor Torres, but the lectures were a burden. There were many tutorials performed by the assistant students, but it seemed as a waste of time. The class was mandatory, and it was easy to pass, but every lecture has a homework assignment for it. Even when there is a guest lecturer, you have to do a worksheet.

If you're majoring in Architecture then you don't really have a choice but to take his class. The class was very easy but he was mostly rambling on and on about one topic and it would essentially take up most of the class's time. He doesn't really explain stuff well and when asked something, he comes off as condescending.

Antonio Torrest is a tough professor. He makes students' lives miserable. I guess that what he gets paid for. Nonetheless, he worked in NYC as an architect.... which gives him "some" credibility... to make UIC Arch students' lives miserable. So... should you take him? HA. You have no choice. Good luck my dudes. #RIP

Todd has trained so many amazing teachers, including my favorite high school teacher, a man who pretty much saved my life, and I can see why my teacher talked about him so highly. I went to UIC for Todd. That was the deciding factor, and it was totally worth it. Best teacher ever. He teaches you how to teach and how to care.

If you see him as the teacher for a potential class, smash that register button. He is hilarious, kind, and puts 200% into his class and students daily. It was very reading-heavy, but that's expected for an English course. I will definitely try to take a class with him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Todd is a solid professor! The course is designed to prepare you for student teaching. Todd is especially helpful at preparing you for responsibilities in the profession. From creating lessons to creating full on units Todd provides guidance and support the entire way. The one critique I have of Todd is his ambiguous grading method. It's not clear
This is my eighth year in the classroom, and each day I use something that Todd DeStigter taught me. That's the best way I can put it. If you want to learn how to teach English, this is your stop.

Best teacher I have had. And I have had many good ones. He's got to be one of the best teachers in the nation. He keeps it real. I hate to use such a banal expression, but he does. He believes in what he does, loves what he does. So inspiring.
Extremely helpful and knowledgable professor.  He makes a large effort to get to know students individually. Make sure to attend class!
AMAZING person, he keeps the class interested but gets off subject quickly, somewhat a harsh grader. but he is always there if you need help!

If all of my classes were this good, I would never want to leave school. He is the kindest, smartest, most engaging professor I've ever had. I doubt I know how important he's been in my life and in other people's. I'm really grateful to him. He challenges you and makes you a better teacher and person.
good teacher, fair grader, i recommend him, he is a fun guy!

awesome teacher...but depends on your style of learning. some people hate him, some people love him. he knows what he is doing. if u like boring traditional profs, u wont like him. u want progressive eager enthusiasitic, he da man.

I had Todd his first semester at UIC.  He really prepared me for a career in teaching.  I have been in the classroom for 9 years.  I still use his ideas.  Ask him about our trip to "Too Much Light..."  See if he remembers about the falling tv at a bar.  It was hysterical.
Todd DeStigter was the best teacher I have ever had.  Period.  This is the guy who is going to teach you how to teach.
So good - really prepares you for teaching.

You need to be present, self-motivated and diligent about your work to do well.  He is strict on attendance and work, but prepares aspiring teachers very well.  Comments and feedback are helpful and inspires you to improve as a teacher and writer.
Seems humane but probably is a tyrant behind the scenes.  Makes the ladies swoon.  Overall, non-threatening.

Very Monotone, to the point where it would be so excruciatingly disengaging. I would have to rely on outside resources to teach me properly since his methods are not adequate to have a good understanding. Also, keep in mind that his exams are difficult due to the material at times not being on the study guide.

He is fair but so boring, his voice is monotone and he does little to engage with students during lecture. His exams are difficult but not impossible. There are only 8 assignments (3 being exams) + attendance that dictate your grade so don't slack. Final exam is optional, and he offers extra credit to be added to exams through two surveys.

All the homework is relevant and he uploads the answers so you can easily see explanations of the content. Our class was moved completely online, but that didn't stop him from being super active and helpful. His lectures are concise and as long as u do the assignments and exam packets easy A. Super organized, fast, and genuinely wants u to do well

The lectures were decent, although very word heavy, but the exams were awful. The "study guides", if you can call them that, were just a bunch of words on a document that I could put together in 5 minutes. Other than that you essentially had to teach yourself. The TA's were not helpful either with their grading or discussions.

Professor Staahl was great! Although the content isn't super exciting, IMO he makes it more exciting and easy to understand. He is very reasonable with grading as well. I was dreading this class but it was actually good and I definitely recommend Dr.Staahl! Class consists of Tests (w/ drops), HW (1 dropped), and participation/attendance.

You have to be able to teach yourself the material. The study guides are copied and pasted words. As if the exams are multiple choice on definition and terms. The TA I had, graded so different than the other TAs (who were lenient). Everyone learns different. Especially after being remote for almost two years. (my two yrs of college were online)

I am slacker. I did not buy the book nor really listen to lectures. The exams were fine except for one that was math heavy. I was upset about it since there was no real practice (HW) for it until after which I thought was dumb. If you really do truly but in work, I believe its an easy A, but I did not enjoy this class and it was mainly a me issue.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Even though lecture is optional, you should still go. They tend to be very boring and confusing so you need to review and ask questions. TAs are not helpful and never really know what is going on in lecture so you should try to just ask the prof your questions.

Honestly, the lectures were boring and often times he just read off the material. Exams were worth 80% of the grade but he does drop one exam which can be final. TA's were not helpful because they often times didn't know what the professor was talking about. Went to office hours and no help. Went to TAs hours and no luck.

Professor Stahl was a great teacher. Although sometimes his lectures can get boring, he is a friendly person and is always willing to help and answer questions. The lectures can sometimes be difficult to understand so reviewing after class is definitely necessary. The class is not an easy as people make it seem, but overall it is not impossible.
Go to lecture even though you might not want to. It helps. Overall, great professor. Teaches well and is very accommodating to students.

No need to go go lecture at all. I never went and got an A. I had thought it was an easy class going on but it definetly wasn't! A lot of people I knew ended up with B's . No book jus study the powerpoints and your good

Lectures were dull and boring. Let's just get that out of the way. Discussion was essential for this course; everything you needed to know for the exam was retaught. It was extremely helpful. Power points were posted online, attendance was no mandatory, and the book was not needed. However, it is essential to take good notes and look over the PP's!
Professor Staahl is a good professor. Although the lectures can be long and dull, he explains the material very well on his slides. Never boughtused the textbook.

As a psychology minor, I enjoyed this class very much! Homework was easy and reasonable since it allowed students to review materials before class. As long as you pay attention in lecture and take notes, you should be fine! He's a great professor so I definitely would recommend him to everyone! :D

Don't buy the book. That being said, go to lectures and take really good notes or look over the PowerPoint slides he posts on Blackboard in your spare time (NOT the night before the exam). His tests reflect the slides. He drops the lowest test and homework scores. Your homework grade depends on how your TA grades. Lectures are boring; no one goes.

I missed half the lectures but he posts powerpoints online which were helpful.He gives examples in class as well to help you understand concepts.Go to discussion, nice recap of lectures.I studied day of or night before and did well on exams.He drops lowest exam and hw grade.Buying book isn't necessary.Overall, easy class and pretty cool guy.

Professor Travis was an amazing person. He was extremely helpful and he cared a lot about us. He offered his help whenever we needed it and he was always there. He always made himself available. His class was really fun. I highly recommend it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The professor is so nice. If you wanna get better at writing, I would definitely take this course. He is very logical and thoughtful about what other people say. During lectures, he wants students to participate to hear their ideas. The assignments are very low maintenance, and he can be very lenient if you are a bit late with submitting.
He takes the time to consider your questions and input during lecture and doesn't try to talk down to you. His feedback on essays is the same way. Great professor, wish he taught all of my classes.

Mr. Mandell was a very kind and interesting teacher. He was very engaging in his teaching and actually made english a viable class. He does require a bit of reading almost every week, but it's very doable. The grading rubric is very clear and his grading is very generous. He gives a lot of time for all the essays including class days.

Phenomenal professor. Understand the material, provides good and classy lectures. If you're going into his class as a freshman, it's the perfect first college English class. I would recommend trying your hardest to get his as your 160 professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: Professor Mandell was one of the better teachers I've had. He gives great feedback on essays and really cares for students. 100% recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Amazing professor! Gives good feedback and the essays weren't that hard to write.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great Professor. Makes class interesting and always gave good feedback. Highly Recommend!!

Great teacher. He gives very good feedback and will always help you with your writing. His class is set up perfectly, and it makes everyone participate without feeling pressure. Since everyone does it, the anxiety goes away! Loved his class. If you're looking for a fun, interactive class, this is it. Keep an eye out for the readings and quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Great professor very clear about his expectations for the course. Gives very good feedback on papers.
If you're a freshmen headed to UIC, I would definitely take Professor Mandell's class, It's an easy A, and he gives great feedback on papers!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very Enthusiastic! I loved going to class because he made it really interesting. There were readings due every class, it was a lot sometimes but you go over all of it no matter what. He provides feedback with every essay due and he is very helpful. 10/10 would take a class if he was teaching it.

He is very passionate about writing and wants to help every student become great writers. He cares about every student and gives everyone great feedback. Attendance and participation is important to do good in this class. Though prof Mandell is so funny that you'll breeze through lectures, so it won't feel like a torture to come to class.

Be sure to attend lectures, not everything on the syllabus he follows as he seems to not update it. Some reading, not like 50 chapters. Do everything he says and you'll pass. Also be sure to attend the sessions at the writing center for extra credit. Funny guy, cares about his teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: this guy is HILARIOUS! he always finds a way to keep the atmosphere of the classroom bright. always look on the syllabus for assignments, theres always a reading assignment (around 30 pages per day) with 2-4 written observations each. he wants all assignments printed out which is actually quite convenient because it helps with the final project.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The teacher is amazing, he's constantly trying to keep the class in a good mood. in the class (HON 121) you will have to read a avg of 30 pages every 2 days, if you write decent observations (2-4) you'll do fine in the class.

I had Professor Sherfinski for an honors class and I was about to drop it after my first class, but decided against it and stayed enrolled and honestly its the best decision I made. This dude is funny and super chill, super relaxed class and easy workload and he grades fair. Gives great advice too, I wish I could take him again.

guys he's so chill n funny like as long as u do the work and come to class u will get an A like his feedback is super helpful and the class is acc interesting and i enjoyed it and he's a really good prof. like its lowk a lotta writing but it is an eng course so that's lowk given but its not overwhelming and we have a lotta time to get it done.

Mr. Sherfinski is a fantastic professor. We had quite a bit of homework, but it was to develop our skills and wasn't just busywork. He gives great feedback as well. He's funny and always managed to make class entertaining. I was struggling with my health that semester, and he was caring and understanding with me through it all. He is my fav so far.

Great prof would def rec. He is a decent grader as long as you follow the syllabus and show effort. Hes very kind and funny and the class is enjoyable. Decent amount of assignments and he makes u print them which I preferred. Syllabus can be bit confusing but he can explain it to u if ur confused. Meets outside of class and is an easy B-A. TAKE HIM

I still remember him from freshman year (junior now)! He was a very nice, understanding, a very great guy. Gave amazing life advice too. He can seem strict but asking for feedback helps a ton and he's flexible about attendance/late work if you talk to him. Take him!!!!

He likes to connect with his students and talk with them instead of talking at them in lectures. Each lecture was different and unique. He has a rule with no phones or technology, even when just checking the time. There are a decent amount of papers but nothing overwhelming. Everything is syllabus based. He requires every assignment to be printed.
He is super chill as long as you read the syllabus, he strictly goes off of that. You have to print out every assignment so get your printer ready. Overall he is super nice and easygoing!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Sherfinski has a sense of humor that not many people get, but he's pretty easy to get along with. There are tedious assignments for each class period and we have to have them printed out by class but it's all to prepare for the final paper. Definitely one of my favorite english teachers!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Sherfinski is very sarcastic and you may not know how to interpret that. In the beginning, he will assign more readings and give harsher feedback. It becomes incredibly helpful when you are writing your final paper. If you participate, appreciate his humor, use the templates, and attend, he will grade you kindly. He is the greatest UIC professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He is genuinely an amazing person and professor. He may assign a lot of homework in the beginning but it is all worth doing and actually helps you become a better writer and reader. I believe he is a fair grader as long as you follow what he says to do. All textbooks are online. He's also funny and sarcastic a lot. 10/10 not a Swiftie though :(

Professor Sherfinski assigns the most homework I have heard of in the ENGL161 course. However, it is all really essential to developing understanding of how to write in a manner that is both easy to understand and containing all necessary information. He also starts grading very harshly, to make sure students are always giving their best work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Sherfinski was awesome. Yes, the homework did seem like a lot at times, bu this is one of the easiest courses I've taken. Homework takes less than 30 mins if you really sit down and do it. He's very understanding and easy going. Take time to build a relationship with him. He's super dope and awesome! would take this course again.

I took him back in 2018 as a requirement to be able to take eng 160. And he was great. He was my first college professor and I have to thank him for being so kind to all of us and for the ice cream!! I also loved that he took time during class to give us advice and guide us. Thank you!
Professor Sherfinski is a very nice person, clearly cares about his students, and very flexible one extensions and other things. He has a sarcastic humor that makes class fun and very lighthearted.

I loved this class. It was relatively easy for me, but that's because I read everything the professor assigned and did all of the homework on time. He's also pretty entertaining and down to earth. Definitely one of my more enjoyable courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Great professor! He is very kind and understanding and gives some good jokes here and there. No required textbooks they are all given in blackboard. He truly wants to see you succeed and help in any way you can. I highly recommend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Follow the templates from the textbook, you'll get an A

Sherfinski is genuinely one of the few professors I actually like. He has a peculiar way of teaching but he knows what he's doing and usually lets the class learn from each other, he's big on collaboration. I'd strongly recommend, he's the type of teacher that makes an 8 am worth attending.
You do not need a textbook for this class but you do need a book that only costs $12 dollars if you get in on Amazon do not buy it from the book store because it cost $15 there.
Super cool guy. He shows enthusiasm in English and helping students improve. You will do well in his class as long as you're attentive and engaged.

Professor Sherfinski cares about his students and is willing to help you grow as a writer. While the first few assignments may be rough, Sherfinski will give you the necessary feedback to become a better writer. You will definitely learn the skills you need to succeed!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Prof. Sherfinski is one of the best profs I've ever had. His lectures are easy to follow. If you attend classes and listen to him you will get A for sure. I've heard a lot about tough ENGL 161 professors at uic, I was lucky to be in prof. Sherfinski's class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Sherfinski is an absolutely fantastic professor! English 161 was a breeze in his classroom. Just stay on your deadlines, and you'll be just fine.

Sherfinski is honestly an awesome teacher. He spaces out his writing assignments and gives you time to turn it rough drafts and he looks at them and makes comments. His class is fun and he always jokes around and make it comfortable.
Awesome.

Aside from the fear of writing papers endlessly, this was a really good class. Large amount of work loads are going to come regardless of which English class you take. Prof. Sherfinski is one of the best professors at UIC. He is extremely insightful and helpful. Communication is key. If you are ever uncertain, doubtful or apprehensive talk to him.

Professor Sherfinski truly cares about his students and wants to get to know them. He is a fair grader and wants you to do well and has great feedback! Such a sweet person and makes the class interesting as he is intelligent and informed. However there are a decent amount of papers due to keep you busy!

Professor Sherfinski is hilarious! He is one of the best professors I had for english. Although he might be a tough grader he just wants you to use the book he provides in the class titled They say I say. I would recommend this course it is easy and he's very chill and funny. ask for what he's looking for in an essay and ask for his advice/help.

Sherfinski is really nice. He can be all over the place with his assignments and what he wants from it, but if you ask him personally he'll make sure you understand. Emailing him a question is good too, but for him, it's better in person. You can miss 4 classes. There's 4 papers but they're EASY! The final is your final. No test/1 group project.

Its surprising how good he is compared to the reviews below. His class, by the looks of this semester, has minimal work compared to other ENGL161 classes. He is very reasonable, real, and to the point. He gives good feedback and is pretty wacky but fun. READ THE SYLLABUS! Its a good way to keep track of assignments and due dates. Use the templates!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Lots and lots of reading with just much confusing and tedious assignments. HARD grader but wants you to achieve full potential. Avoid him if you are not a Lit major
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Lots and lots of reading with just much confusing and tedious assignments. HARD grader but wants you to achieve full potential
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I should have listened to the reviews that said he gives a lot of really tedious and unnecessary homework. Unfortunately, his class fit my schedule and I had no other choice. Hopefully the amount of homework assigned dies down soon along with my utter hatred for this class. This class also made me hate math.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: The professor is very nice and helpful. The class itself has daily reading and homework. The teacher is a hard grader but he gives constructive feedback and is always willing to help. Getting a good grade isn't easy but it is doable if you do your the homework and always give your best efforts.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Get ready to forget everything you've ever learned about writing papers in previous composition classes, because Sherfinski raises the standards to a new level. He is looking for something too specific and familiar to his own style of writing. He can be very vague, and he thinks he's being crystal clear. Asking to clarify will do little to nothing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He starts off the year as a really tough grader.  Got Cs on the first couple of assignments, but all he wants in your writing is for you to use the "They Say I Say" templates.  He wants you to get an A and will give it to you as long as you do the homework and actively participate
A difficult class, but worth it.  Interesting and funny teacher, but gave assignments almost every day, and you had to work hard on them.

While the class theme was, to my opinion, horrible and bornig (Composition and Mathematics). I ended up liking the class. Sherfinski is a professor who won't take the usual excuses and comments from students. You can get an A in the class but will really have to work for it. His class aren't boring with him teaching although the material was.
His classes are boring and expect to do a lot of homework. He is also a very tough grader so don't expect to get anywhere near an A.

Assigns A LOT of homework. Expect to be writing at least one paper every night before class. It is a lot of pointless homework as another reviewer mentioned. I've gotten 2 of my papers back so far, and I've gotten a C on both. In class, we do not discuss anything to do with the homework. It's often storytime in this class. Very sarcastic too. AVOID

I took him for ENGL161 and for many undergrads this is their last English class, so yea there will definitely be some work. Sherfinski is a fair grader though, if you turn in a bad paper he'll give you a bad grade, as simple as that. His lectures are very interesting and I found him to be very funny. If you're interested in a fun class take him.

If you want an A in his class, you have to work extremely hard. Which means, spending loads of times into the writing projects and the research paper. There's a lot of assignments at first but then it switches over to the writing projects. Very sarcastic in class and sometimes make you feel like an idiot. Not sure if I would recommend him

Prof. Sherfinksi is hilarious and make English class interesting. There's a lot of homework in the beginning of the semester, but then it winds down and becomes more about writing papers. I think Sherfinski really helped me become a better writer and he made the class worth it. Take 161 with Sherfinski!

Mr. Sherfinski is a great professor. We had a lot of homework assignments that seemed pointless but they actually helped with understanding material and becoming a better writer. The class mostly consisted of discussion on homework readings. Yes, he grades hard but you can always go in for help! I highly suggest taking his class.

He gives pointless hw that  will takes hours. He can never answer anyone's questions in a straightforward manner. Too sarcastic and very subjective towards students. He will make feel like an idiot when you come to his class. AVOID!

Mr. Sherfinski is one of those incredibly laidback, if corny, teachers who makes what you're learning incredibly fun and interesting. He's easy to talk to and there if you need extra help. The workload isn't overwhelming and he's a fair grader. I honestly miss him this semester!

Mr. Sherfinski grades extremely harsh. Ive never received anything lower than an A on a paper my whole life and he gave me D's and C's. The homeworks are so heavy and useless. Would definitely take another professor

I think Mr.Sherfinski is the best English teacher at UIC. He gave me poor grades at first but I talked to him and asked what exactly he wanted and he clearly told me, I got an A in his class. He is very nice if you're nice to him. If you're listening to your iPod or sleeping in class why would you expect him to give you an A? WAKE UP PEOPLE.

I don't know what some people are complaining about. I think he grades fairly and if you try your writing will improve and you can get an A. He is more than willing to provide commentary on a rough draft if you email him. Basically if you're a good student, you can do good in the class. I got an A.

If I had the chance to jump off a highrise building 100 times before something happened to me, I would do that than take his class.  He grades like a tyrant, he picks favorite students without actually saying it (you can tell who his favorite is by looking at different people's grades), the topic as a whole is crap, literally. AVOID AVOID AVOID.

Honestly, Mr. Sherfinski is a VERY hard grader, very unclear as to what he wants from you in papers and kind of annoying. His sarcasm after a while is tiring. The class topic, at first, seems interesting but towards the end just gets jumbled into a bunch of different topics and themes and problems. I would recommend a different teacher. Good luck!
Sherfinski is a GREAT professor! He does give homework every day but it is usually just read and point out important facts or summarize the chapter.  He makes English interesting. Take him for 161!!

Mr. Sherfinksi is one of the funniest professors on campus. ENG 161 is actually fun and engaging. He gives homework assignments daily, but they're easy to do. He gives great feedback to essays. He likes to make his students laugh and swears like a sailor, but he is a great professor. Take him for 161!

I love Mr. Sherfinski! He is really funny and nice. He is a hard grader but because of that I finally learned how to properly write! His class is NOT AN EASY CLASS. But it's really beneficial in the long run.

I have hated English all my life, but I actualy liked his class. He is not opinionated and he is willing to hear whatever you have to say. He's a funny person and laidback. He is a hard grader, but my writing has completely transformed through this class. His feedback on papers is good. Only downside is that he doesn't post grades up, but I got A.

This is one of the best English teachers I ever had. Topic of discussion was sanitation, very interesting. You will definitely learn from him. Must admit that he is not an easy teacher. Homework almost everyday and four essays; however, in the long run, its beneficial.

I was hesitant to take his course at first, but I actually liked his class. He gives good feedback/suggestions on papers and sets time aside to help you write the paper in the first place. If you feel like the work load is too much, don't be afraid to let him know and he will reduce the work for everyone; he is very reasonable!

This class is awful. The whole class is about human excrement and was gross to learn about. Sherfinski is an eccentric man who can never give a straightforward answer. There is A TON of homework. 5 writing projects and even more assignments every single day. I DO NOT recommend him to someone who wants an easy class. I wish someone told me before.
Took him for 160 and 161 great professor really wants you to do well but you must try just keep up with work and participate in class and you should get a b

He was a great teacher. everything he says is intresting. he doesnt force his idea upon you but forces you to think about things in a different way and challenge what the world has to say. he does not participate in conforming students into cookie cutter writers but infuses creativity and enlightenment.

Without a doubt this professor is on my list of toughest graders but in the end it is very beneficial. Work hard in his class and you will see much improvement in your work by the end of the semester.
He grades papers super hard. but besides that i enjoyed the class, very funny. Just a very interesting class overall.

has a weird sence of humor..very very hard grader expects alot out of you. like to talk alot about rehtorical topics that have nothing to do with ur papers. over all u have to work real hard for that A or B..likes to give a lot of C's
He is an amazing teacher.. He made learning about death interesting! Very funny and nice teacher

He was an amazing teacher. I have never liked an english class but he truly made it interesting and I actually enjoyed it. He likes to tell a lot of jokes and will move assignment due dates to a later date if the majority of the class wants him too unless it is the final research paper of course.
Great Teacher. Fun Class. Pay attention, and be prepared to answer questions. He gets mad when no one talks.

good teacher. makes a lot of useless jokes. fun. very biased. make sure to be on his good side. speak up in class. put effort in your homework. if you don't do so well on your homework, no matter how well you write on your writing projects, expect your homework grade to be written down.
Take 161 death and dying... great class. Sherfinski is a great teacher, super motivated and intelligent. He also knows a lot about music and is a big DEAD HEAD :)
Keeps the class very interesting. There are a lot of assignments throughout the semester but as long as you do them its a pretty easy A.

Makes great conversation with the classroom, I actually looked forward to class. Funny, cool, and interesting. Extremely helpful but you need to speak up. Tends to favor certain students. His class is a lot of work, he expects a lot from his students but if you work hard and take his advice, you will do well.

He is a great professor. Really funny and keeps your interest in class. The assignments are easy and quick to do, they mostly consists of short stories. He kept me awake during an 8am class and I'm not a morning person. Easy A, just come to class, participate and do the short homework assignments. He jokes around a lot, its a fun class.
He's a really great professor.  I never had as much interest in english class until I took a class with him.  Just make sure you do all your assignments, come to class on time, and participate.

He is very biased but he liked me so I don't care.  Funny guy, easy class. Just show up and show some effort and you should get an A for sure.  Easy grader too.  I actually read the materials for the first time and paid attention because he made class fun/funny.  I would love to take one of his classes again.

He rarely gives out A's in his class. I remember going to see him about a paper and he gave me comments on it. I asked him if it was A material and he unhesitantly said "yeah, of course." I got a C+ on that paper. I asked why he told me that it was an A paper, and he told me that he never remembered me coming in to see him. Do not take his class.

Sherfinski is a great professor, one of the best.  He keeps you interested in the subject and motivates you to learn.  I've taken several classes with him and I enjoyed all of them.  Definitely take his classes...you won't regret it!

Loved him.  He was interesting, loved the subject, and always pushed our class to think outside the box.  He is definitely quirky, but he was what made the class bearable.  Definitely agree with the crush on him, haha.  It's not an "easy A," he will definitely push you to be a better writer.

I have such a crush on Sherfinski. He's really nice and cool. If you participate and show some understanding of the readings then you'll be fine. My boyfriend, who had him last year, told me to take the class and I dont regret it at all. Just make sure you do the homework. Im taking him again for 161 in the fall.

Worst teacher ever. Very biased. If he likes you, he'll grade you better. Very confusing. Does not know what he wants from you. Does not help you when you come in for help. Rude. talks way too much. Rambles on. Dont take his class, unless you want to get really frustrated and stressed out. real pain in the butt. Directions are unclear.

He was a very helpful and interesting teacher. He's one to make you think a lot and you actually learn a lot from what he talks about. Over all, it was a great class since he was reasonable with the work he gives out and is very willing to work with you if you need help with your writing. I would take another class with him.

He's a good teacher. He makes a lot of jokes, some of which are good. He makes you think, but gets ticked off a bit when people don't speak up. He's really lax about homework, but it's still mandatory. I liked his reading selections.
A VERY interesting class.. BUT he's a really tough grader... I worked really hard and got a C... If I had a chance to do it over, I would have picked another class...
He is a great teacher, very passionate about the topic i would recommend him. He is a little bit odd thought and tends to make a lots of bad jokes. But I loved him.

He is a nice teacher with a sense of humor. He thinks everyone will most likely be an average student and he takes that literally when he grades your paper. So, unless you go above and beyond and every paper, expect some kind of C or low B.
Sherfinski is an amazing teacher.  Not only is he one of the funniest teachers I ever had but he really taught me how to disect my writing in order to get straight to the point.
He's very good at keeping a class interesting and is fair when it comes to assigning work.

Todd supervised my Honors project last semester as well as taught my Engl 101. He was fabulously helpful, and always had an interesting ancedote to add. He kept class interesting and his eccentricness was his highlight. Definitely a professor to choose if you're quirky.

Sherfinski is awesome! I took him for Eng 160 and 161 and I enjoyed his class the whole time. He's very personable and I'd consider him one of my friends. Classes are interesting, books are good, and you'll def. get an A if you do the work that's assigned.
awesome professor!  Very laid back and cool.  If you put some effort into it, you will definitely get an A

He laid back, wont get your papers graded on time, but that just gives you more time to turn it in.  Really cool, definitely not boring, a little eccentric but that's what makes him fun.  Don't be afraid of his crazy hair.

Such a sweetheart!!! omg it makes me want to cry. Professor Treleaven is so humble, kind, caring, and passionate about his field. He gives a lot of insight into his lessons. He wants everyone to succeed. Take him and engage with him when he asks questions!!
Needs to hold members who don't do their part accountable
I had him for IDS 495 was chill with him and he is a super kind grader and guy. Hopefully you can get him for a laid back capstone class
Professor Jim is very good. He knows a lot about his subject and gives really good advice and feedback. You have to do a group project throughout this course.

Prof.Treleaven is, in my books, one of the best, if not, the best professor I've had at UIC. He is so caring and patient with the students and helps wherever he can. If you're struggling, he is the person to go to. He is highly passionate about the subjects he teaches and extremely qualified.

CS 362 is a mess of a class. Grades do come back very slowly, but that is because Prof Troy is teaching two core classes at once. On top of that, the TA budget cuts do not help. Prof Troy is a very caring professors and his lectures are very easy to understand. He does go on a tangent at times during lecture though.
be prepared to do 20 hours of homework a week and then on top of that another 40 hours of labs and on top of that another 60 hours of homework i forgot to mention earlier
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Took CS 112 with him. Very nice, understanding professor. Attendance was worth a small percentage of the grade and was taken with IClicker. Lectures were simple and easy to follow, it was never a headache to keep up in class. 10/10
Great guy with amazing teaching skills
This guy was literally awful. Cant pay attention in his lectures. His exams aren't like the study guides. He finds it funny when people are failing. I DO NOT recommend this guy at all.
The class was disorganized and very work heavy

We took exam 1 in week 7. Grades came out a week before the final (week 15). Homeworks were also returned to us about 6-8 weeks after we had done them. Crazy timelines for such a respected professor. If you have a choice of him over anyone else, I'd rather have a terrible professor who gets grades back in ample time, personally.
Amazing syllabus. Attendance mandatory but can join online.
Great professor, specifically in regards to lecturing. Is very consistent with things like grading, class timeline/schedule, etc.

The lectures itself are extremely boring. I could never get myself to listen no matter what. Projects are easy enough. I like how you get to work w different languages and f# might seem intimidating but it really is about using the minimum resources at hand. Most of the content is recycled but it's not an extraordinary amount of work.

Time expectation for this course was unreasonable. The project descriptions are usually as confusing an unstructured as his classes, rambling and nonsensical. The only reason 341 is bearable with him is because he recycles old Hummel assignments and lectures. If this class is ever offered again only take it if you are an experienced cheater SMH.

Class organization was poor; project grades were only given in the final week, leaving us unaware of our performance throughout the course. Tests were randomized leetcode questions without any clear indication on what those problems were going to be about. Would not recommend this class.

I've had Prof Troy many times, and I can say he is very consistent. Lectures can be a bit boring, but Troy tends to give a fair amount of workload. Some complaints specifically about 351 are the fact we got our grades back for our projects very late and a lot of the content felt like 251 again. Ample time was given to complete projects though.

The class is a step up from CS251. There was no clear grading criteria or expectations set during the entire semester. He struggled at times explaining concepts and used other professors' slides, but that's ok. I wish the class/syllabus was clear and consistent. Overall, an average class with an average professor. No surprises with Troy as usual.

The quality of the lecture slides, homework assignments, projects and exams were excellent in this course. He is very knowledgeable on the subject, but had some trouble explaining clearly during lectures. Has a tendency to go on tangents which can be rather distracting, but you can learn a lot in the course if you put in effort (Python, SQL, F#).

Had to take care of a dy*ing family member. Emailed him for an extension, I guess this situation didn't warrant a response. People really like him, I personally think he doesn't care about students. Maybe I just had a bad experience with him idk. Recent changes to the CS curriculum made me feel like I got scammed out of 4 crhrs.

Very difficult professor to listen to. His lectures are exhausting. He has to say "particular", "aight", "uh", "um", "ok?" in every single sentence. More than 40% of the lecture is him just saying these words, it's so difficult for him to make a linear point without interrupting himself. Makes it hard to learn and focus in his class.

Took him for CS 341. Teaches SQL, Python and SQL, F# in that order. Lectures are a bit dull but are helpful for hw, projects, and tests. Projects can be a bit time consuming but they are interesting and challenging enough to learn. Exams make up a decent portion of the grade though. Overall the class is very well organized and he's also a nice guy.

CS 341 with Professor Troy was pretty good. I have had him for other classes, but I felt like lectures for this class were more boring. iClicker participation points were used, multiple HW assignments that were simple, and several projects that got pretty difficult once you are deep into F#. Overall a good prof, but the course material was less so.

CS 341 - F22 - Too difficult projects, Some of the Undergrad TA's who have maximum OH slots doesn't know anything, Unrealistic deadline, No late submission, No hw or proj drops, 2% HW Seems like a 10% Proj. Doesn't respond to doubts on piazza, EXTREMELY RUDE AND MAKES THE CLASS SEEM LIKE A 500 LEVEL.

Pretty good prof. He and prof Igic taught the first covid semester. He was a little impatient with the stuident questions sometimes, but not bad. A lot of homework, but interesting material. Covid vaccines, transmission, etc. I liked the class.

CS251 in general was a difficult course but Troy went very easy on us. Last semester with Professor Reckinger, the class was way more difficult that it almost doesn't seem fair how we had it. Help is given in plenty. The Jumpstart Slides are a god sent. I watched the lecture videos Prof Reckinger had made. Great class because you learn so much.

CS251 is no doubt a hard class with a lot of work to do in it. Troy lays everything out clearly in the syllabus, answers your questions, and is reasonable. Lectures are not required, but they are helpful during trees and graphs as that material is dense. Troy is great!
Made the labs easy to follow. Other than that the class was horrible because it was administered by Lillis
Good professor but using Shanon Reckingers format for 251. A little more flexibility but still stupid
Never had to read material Only watched Exam Review Lectures If you do the labs, the projects are pretty similar. Most projects take a day or two to finish, the final 2 were a little longer.

ENGR101 is a very simple course with really only one assignment which has you create a course template for you to follow in order to complete your major. The lectures are mandatory and TA ran, but were only 50 minutes long (sometimes a bit shorter) and online for me.

211 was co-taught with Troy and John Lillis, with Troy appearing to take care of the lab side of things for the course. His instructional videos, while sometimes long, did do a great job explaining what to do. Also, his explanation for one of the projects assigned was great and gave good pointers (pun not intended ha).

Prof Troy. made this class so straightforward and made it very doable to juggle a semester long project! Also, he got us to present our Arduino projects at engineering expo and it was a good practical experience (he even got us breakfast and lunch). Exams are very fair. He lays out what you need to know and that's what you'll see on the exam.

Troy is one of my favorite professors at UIC. He explains topics in a straight forward manner. His labs are really helpful, they outline a lot of the methods you will be using in your projects. As long as you go to lab, and do the projects then you should be able to get an easy A. He covers most of the midterm in class so you know what expect.

Don't start your projects too late. Try to do a little bit every day. Come to his office hours, he loves to talk and will help you clear up anything you're confused about. Super funny and approachable, very animated and strong lecturer. Would take again.

One of the easiest classes I've ever taken. Come to lab, listen to his straightforward "lecture" and learn a bunch. You don't have to go to Lecture but Lab is definitely a must. He basically holds your hand through every assignment.

Take him, you'll pass AND learn the material. He basically tells you what's gonna be on the exams so you can prepare it beforehand. He also gives you most of the code for programs so you just have to 'put it together'. Only reason I got a B is because I skipped a bunch of labs and projects.

I have taken CS 111 and CS 211 with Troy in the past and got A's, those were not so difficult classes, however, I am taking Troy this Fall 2017 for CS 342 and the projects are extremely difficult. Troy is a good person, but not so great of a teacher you have to do a lot of research and work on yourself. His rating on this website is over rated tbh

Prof Troys lectures can be a bit of a bore since he doesn't really teach many new concepts and rather, explains the project write up over and over again. But he is super helpful in lab and in office hours. His humor and excitement is a plus. Just make sure you don't get on his bad side, he can get pretty angry if you interrupt his teaching.

Troy is the best professor ever! He tells you exactly what you need to know and goes above and beyond to help you understand. 211 is project heavy- a big project is due every 2 weeks, but if you go to TAs or the tutors you can easily get help. The class is very practical and focuses on making functioning programs instead of theory. Plan your time.

Prof. Troy is a very nice man and a very good lecturer. He's also very organized. He posts all his lecture notes and sample codes in his website so if you miss a class you can easily just refer to it. He also records his discussions through the echo cam. He covers the basics really well. However, I do feel that they could improve the TAs.

professor Troy is a great guy, and he's there if you need help. However, for CS 111 I doubt you'd need help, as it is an easy course and most people get A's. I can't say I enjoyed his lectures (pretty boring), but easy to follow and makes it easier to do the assignments.

Professor: - Very good at explaining things, knows what he's talking about - Can be pretty boring at lectures Class: - Make sure to leave time for the assignments; you might find them taking longer than you anticipate - Turn things in on time - Easy A

LOVE LOVE LOVE professor Troy. He is so understanding and lenient. 14 projects given each 100 points, max points for projects was 1000 so you can skip 4 projects if you score 100 on the rest. He is the type of professor that will push back project dates if he knows that you have other CS projects due in another class. 2 easy exams. Would take again

Neat professor, very well job at explaining everything, more than happy to answer questions, very clear on what is expected, he actually gives you the algorithmsstructuresfunctions for a lot of the projects you work on, you just have to simply add them to the program then its a piece of cake, easy A, he lets u use a cheat-cheet on final

Easiet CS class. Easy A if you do the work.  You can do the programs by just tweaking the code he gives in his homepage. For CS majors though, be warned. It will not be anywhere this easy after CS 111. Consider passing out if you have general programming knowledge. All in all, best professor for Computer Science.

Super nice and understanding guy, and an even better lecturer. If you're familiar with programming, this course will be a breeze. Strict grader at first, but curve at the end was generous. TAs sucked and the labs ran weird (one TA for all labs a week instead of one for each lab time), but the labs can be done at home.

He's a super chill guy and he is able to keep me awake in class. There are projects every week so the work load gets a bit heavy if you are the procrastinating type so be careful. Other than that the exams are challenging, but not too bad.

Well Professor Troy is probably one of the best CS prof's the university has to offer. His lectures are crystal clear and his projects are extremely reasonable. Very easy to get an A as long as you don't slack off. At times you will be tempted to slack off BUT DON'T (Personal Experience).

This guy is the bomb! He's extremely flexible with projects, but at the same time he's incredibly clear in his lectures, and very helpful. His cheerful voice gets me excited, and he's the reason why I stayed in Computer Science. You go Professor Troy Troy!

Excellent professor! He knows his c++ and teaches it well! The projects were very tough but definitely doable. Class can get somewhat boring at times but if you listen you will learn a ton! He is very helpful during office hours. He has a sense of humor and is very approachable. He tests and projects are very difficult but he grades generously.
Fantastic teacher! If you go to his office hours he will help you with any lab or project assignment. He wants you to understand the material and get a good grade.
Awesome professor. His lectures are a bit dull, but he's extremely helpful and very flexible.

He is extremely nice! I just transferred to UIC and I wanted to apply for a scholarship but had no university references so I asked him and he didn't even think twice about it. If you keep up on your labs you will be fine. I just wish he explained some of the syntax a little more regarding constructors considering this is a 100 level CS course.
Awesome teacher. Explains labs really well and gives you plenty of time to do them. Tests are rather easy and he gives helpful review, in class, before each and everyone of them!!!! A+ professor!

He is a totally awesome professor. He teaches at a pace that any non-computer science major can learn java programming. I really got into Java programming and I feel well-prepared to tackle the next CS course if I wanted something to fall back on. The class was a lot of fun and he talks about real world applications in his lectures & labs.

He explains everything at a perfect pace -- nice, slow, and steady, so any student can understand. He elaborates and uses real world examples in java application programming. I'm not a computer science major, but I really liked java programming after this. I feel prepared for taking the next CS course in sequence, as something to fall back on.

I only got a B in this class because I had a large load that semester, but I found this class to be excellent. I owe my current employment to this class. The book "C++ for Java Programmers" by M. Weiss was a great resource for getting the subject matter down. Study the sections from that book that he seems to be covering and you will be golden.

Prof. Troy is the frickin man. Learned so much in his class and I feel very prepared for CS 102. He explained things at the perfect pace for me. I love how I understood just about 100% of the material as opposed to other classes where they're going so fast that you can't possibly master everything. You'll learn a lot if you work hard.

Troy is very laid back and approachable. Attendance isn't mandatory since he puts up notes and codes that he writes in class online. Same for labs unless you need help from the TAs. Exams can be difficult or easy (multiple choice questions and writing codes by hand) depending on how well you understand the math.

I'll admit the clock tiks very slowly in his lectures. You can def. get a B in this class without going to any of his lectures, just go to the labs. For tests its simple math operations, but the written portion be prepared to memorize code if u have no idea what your doing (me!).

Pretty interesting in the beginning and the course overall was pretty easy, but I think the stuff he teaches is kind of pointless and irrelevant. I don't think I'm ever going to need to know how to draw squares with a turtle in the future...

His lecture is kinda boring because he put each code he write in class online. No use to attend the class but u have to read the codes online very carefully and understand them all. The 2 tests and one final is easy. Just pretend u r the java and operate the code, and u will be fine in the test!!

Very laid back professor.. he goes so slowly and puts the material out in a very simplified and easy fashion. Our midterms were a joke.. aced it like a piece of cake and the projects weren't hard at all. Take him if you want an easy A but don't if you want to seriously learn the material. (You've got 202 to learn as well for CS majors)

He's a great professor and nice guy,and doesn't care about attendance but if you no nothing about Java and don't care much for it, you're screwed. Attend lectures (labs are just ask questions about hw so no need to attend) if you have no idea whats going on, ask for help cuz it will be tough. It's difficult if you know nothing.Must be devoted to it

Prof. Troy is by far the best professor in the CS department. I've been seven semesters at UIC and no one compares to him. He makes things look so easy. His programming assignments are so much fun. Exams are not too difficult, so if you do good on the projects you're set of an A in the class. He is very helpful also outside the classroom.
Best CS prof I had so far. I learned a lot in this class! His exams are straightforward and relatively easy. Just make sure to do your programs and you will be set for the exams.
he's hawt.. haha .. he's a very good teacher, very simple and explains everything

I did not even need to buy the textbook. Notes and examples are crystal clear. Labs are fun and easy. Programs are easy and fun too. Even is you miss a day or two, it is no biggie! Nothing to worry about at all when taking this class ;)!!!

It's another fantastic semester with Professor Troy! He's always the best professor to take ANY class with. He'll give you a challenging programming assignment, and you'll feel like doing the extra credit just for fun. If I have one wish, I would wish that there's enough Professor Troys to teach all the CS courses.
He's the nicest professor in this entire college, I would love to take another one of his classes. I learned so much from this class. :-) One of the best!
Do your programs and you'll ace the class.
good

Prof. Troy is one of the best professor UIC has to offer.  Goes out of his way most of the time to help you out.  His programming assignments were long but he gave plenty of examples.  Exams aren't bad either.  Great professor to have.
Good teacher but the T.A.'s were not as good.  If you have questions its best just to ask him.

Pat Troy is one of the best teachers at the university.  He is really nice to his students and does a good job teaching.  He grades a little bit too easy.  I don't think he's brilliant, but he has a great attitude.  He makes time for his students, even though the university has given him too much work.  He gets an A+! :)
No Comments
Prof. Troy is really a good teacher. He will go out of the way to help students. I will certainly take his class again.
Cool prof. Fair and helpfull.
No Comments
He da BEST. He is really the best teacher I had at UIC
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
Nice Professor :)

by far my favorite teacher at UIC, go to class and take notes and the tests are very reasonable and curved as well. makes a conscious effort to make lectures interesting and is very accommodating of individual students. Also no papers and minimal homework

Class was very interesting and he made it that way. He engages with the class. His HW are easy 100% points and so are his pre-tests. However, the tests are hard. You really need to understand the material. And he looks like Van Gogh if you sit at the back of the class.

Made class pretty interesting, really nice guy. However class was very hard, need to study ALOT for tests. If you do not do well on tests, you really have no other way to make up points. No papers which was good.

A great Professor- took him over the summer, thought the class and material would be difficult however, he explained everything wonderfully and made statistics a breeze. As long as you listen to what he says in class and his great explanations you will do great!

Travis is a really nice guy and he was a very good teacher for this class. Even for people who didn't like math or weren't good at it, he was unbelievably helpful and was willing to do whatever he could to help you understand the material. I mean, he is a grad student so he doesn't have decades of experience teaching, but if you did the work and we

He is a genuinely nice guy and really seems to care about students. I do agree he can be a hard grader on the papers, but overall I think you get out of the course what you put into it.  I still talk to him and he still is very nice to me. Great guy, hard class

The material he taught was very easy to understand and he certainly did try to help his students, but he is a grad student and he seemed to have no clue on how to teach the material. He graded very harshly and he did not seem to know how to facilitate notetaking. I recieved a E, however I took stats 101 during the summer session and recieved an A.

Well, this class was hard, but at no fault to Travis. It was a fairly difficult course and he was always helpful and ready to give you individual attention, however he was not really good at teaching the material exp to those students who have math anxiety. I think the other comments are too harsh, I agree he should not teach again but no need to b
Knows what she's doing but the exam times are way too short, the pace goes usually at 2 questions per minute in order to complete in time.

She gave us about 4 midterms throughout the semester (including 1 optional final). The tests also asked really odd questions so when studying for them pay attention to the miniscule details. She's alright I suppose, she definitely had her moods swings but overall she was okay. If you're a marketing major you'll enjoy her lectures!

Not that Ann is a bad person by any means, but there have been times she has been slightly rude to different students. Her exams are the strangest thing, as you are given nearly zero time to complete these questions. All in all, both her and her class are neither good nor bad, simply mid.

She's not a terrible teacher, but as one who isn't a marketing major, her lectures are pretty boring. She puts the effort in to try and engage the class through activities. Uses McGrawhill for assignments and tests. Some test questions felt odd and meaningless to include. Overall, a fairly easy course though and a safe option.

The course is overall very difficult. Even if you do attend the classes or do the work, she posts slides that literally have nothing to do with the exams in class. Speaking of exams, no review guide or nothing plus it's like 30 seconds a question because you're given only 30 minutes with like 50 questions. Good luck if you do take the class.

She is not as bad as other people say, I just wish she spoke to students better. She talks down to us if we do not know the answer or basically calls us dumb and then repeats what we just said as the correct answer. You learn a lot if you are 100% focused.

I honestly enjoyed this class a lot. She made the material interesting. She took attendance every time for points. There were a few written assignments, three exams, and a weekly homework assignment that was super easy. She answered emails very quickly and related material to current events.
Classes are super lecture heavy, and honestly her lectures were not very good. Exams were a lot more difficult than they should have been. Basically just material straight from the textbooks.

Dont take her class if you dont have to, worst teacher I have ever had. She is practically decaying and has no idea what she is talking about. She literally reads slides word for word and messes every other sentence up. Half the stuff on the test we didnt even go over in class, she says to askk questions but yells at you when you do.
Her lectures feel all over the place. Reading off slides. Structure of each class is sort of random. 2 written assignment (easy) & four exam but lowest gets dropped. Mandatory attendance.
Her exams are hard, plus she takes attendance every class. lectures are super boring.

I'm a 4.0 student last semester, took this class and exams were pure memorization and not online anymore, class assignments were easy but you'll only succeed in this class if you have great memory skills and can memorize little details from five chapters for each test.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very easy if you follow through out class. Took her online during COVID and was such an easy class. Was not a tough grader and her lecture videos were short and to the point.

Had an A throughout the entire semester in the class. One of the only professors that Had assignments due during the week of finals , I missed them by 20 minutes and had asked for an extension the next day. I have never missed a deadline for any assignments in the class. Emailed and she said nothing can be done. Was at 79.6 and wouldnt curve to B.

Very strict about deadline. She sticks to her rubric but sometimes grades so harshly. I didn't think that she lectures very well. She just reads off from her slides, which is boring unless you have a pretty decent amount of interest in retailing marketing. Also, be careful of group projects as they count most of the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took Trampass Spring of 2020. Considering you NEED this class to graduate, the angels were looking after all of us and gave us the option of CR/NC due to Covid-19. I didn't like Trampass from day 1. She mentioned that her class would be the hardest class we've ever taken throughout our college career. It's almost like she wishes failure upon us.

I would avoid this teacher for MGMT 495. The course i based on Capsim (a simulation program for running a company). Working with capsim is a great experience, but not when the teacher doesn't know anything about it! The class is based primarily off this simulation and no class time is devoted to teaching the operations in it. Also very rude!

Professor Trampas was a great professor. Coursework is very fair, no curve balls when it comes to assignments or grading. Lectures are pretty interesting as well, way better when people participate. Tests and homework are completed online. But she is very passionate about the content and loves involving students. 10/10 recommend.

Very strict about the deadline. She takes points off even if you submit the wrong format. no second chances. Mean professor. Instructions are not clear. Tough grader. No extra credit. Make you purchase all the materials. The textbooks are very expensive.

Professor Trampas was a great teacher. She made her lectures fun and she was very enthusiastic about the topic. The class consisted of online exams which you could take on your own at home or library but only during class time. She gave pop quizzes which were fairly easy if you did the readings she assigned before class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I like her lectures she makes them interesting and entertaining. I have a newfound respect for Marketing majors the subject is definitely tough but Professor Trampas makes it easier that what it actually is. She can be a bit sassy at times but she's an overall great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I didn't use the textbook much but its useful for if you wanna take your own notes or to study for quizzes. Theres a lot of group work but she's really fair with everyone and really good lecturer. Her grading can be rough but the class isn't really that hard its just work heavy. I highly recommend her for mktg classes. She also brings guest speakrs

Seems as if she got tougher this last semester bc  because of her tough quizzes. I went to every class and read all of the chapters but still managed to get bad grades. This class requires a heavy course load: quizzes, midterm-like quizzes, role plays,  and a hefty group project paper and presentation. I'm afraid of getting a C in this class now

A very good professor.

It was a pleasure taking this course. She relates the topic to the real world and likes participation from students. Follows the syllabus closely and  read the text. Interesting subject matter - come to class it's enjoyable!

Her class was informative and engaging.  Mostly lecture and discussion. She brought real world experience and related materials to every day life.  Closely followed syllabus. Honestly for a 100 level class this class is too meticulous and complex for it to be reasonable to do well. As a non-science major this class requires too much effort for you to at least pass. Dr. Baynard is extremely knowledgeable and a very serious instructor. Take her class seriously, and don't expect an easy A. One of the best instructors!

I know people are complaining about her, but honestly her teaching style is great. She provides a lot of material and is very very obvious about quizzes. Her tests are obviously tough because they ask questions that require you to remember some detailed things and people complaining on here didn't do the work. She gives you EVERYTHING you need.

Tracy's Exams & labs are extremely difficult, she's a mediocre at explaining things & is very mean at times. Some jokes are funny & rest are pointless. Don't  only study the Study guide u will fail the exams, it doesn't help at all. Study the power point slides in very detail to get an A. Labs will require Enormous amount of time to get full points

Professor Baynard always kept lectures interesting. She really cares about her students and will help out with your grade if you need it. She's very funny and will give out prizes if you participate when she asks her challenging questions.

reviews.comment: Excellent professor;  passionate about kinesiology. Enthusiastic lecturer, silly at times. Dr. Baynard is amazing!! Class is straightforward and I would highly recommended you attend lecture. The lab for this course was difficult. Quizzes were easy,exams you must study hard. Excellent Prof ! His explanations are very clear and makes you very strong in your basics. ECE 567 covers very advanced topics and very interesting as well. He is very helpful. Homeworks, Exams and Project is non trivial and you have to work for it. But, Grading is fine.
The best course that I have ever taken in UIC. Clear theoretical concepts with practical implementation in the project.

Very enthusiastic and energetic personality. Always encourages students to discover and pitch new ideas to the current trends. he is new but he is very enthusiastic about teaching and helping students build new ideas.
cool prof

The class is not engaging. The teacher reads off the slides. She has graded one assignment and it is week ten. This teacher is not reliable or understanding. Do not take the class if you don't have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is a very kind professor but dont expect a response back if you email her. She grades her nnqs hard too. The classwork is easy though. one nnq every week. one final project which is so easy, and then a 5-7 page final paper.

Prof. Webb had a lot of things going on in her personal life the semester i had her, so there were some adjustments made to the course. Overall she was a really intelligent and kind teacher, you can tell she cares about her students and the material she is teaching. The course was not difficult, but attendance and participation are mandatory.

I loved taking this class with her even though it was online. The content was incredibly valuable and important for education and Professor Webb does a great job explaining everything. You know that she cares for the well-being of her students. Although this semester, I emailed her seven times over the 5 months and not once did she respond to me.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Webb is a nice lady but not that great of a professor. Never replies to emails. She barely gave any homework which meant any grades she entered, you will need solid scores on and no quizzes or exams were given but her weekly readings were a lot and she really only had a few grades that she put in, including attendance. I honestly learned nothing.

I'm sure Professor Webb is amazing. However, that was not the case in ED this semester. She's very lecture based. I felt like she never opened up class discussions - it was always lectures which would put me to sleep. Her readings are HEAVY. The one thing I liked was that she had one synchronous day and an asynchronous one. Overall, not my fav.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Overall I feel like prof webb was okay. Shes very nice and seems like a really good person, but I felt like she was always unorganized. She also gives very few assignments, which puts your grade at risk easily.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Webb was extremely hard to reach. She never responded to emails and never even commented to let me know she received my FINAL PROJECT. Seems very careless as a professor. Very assignment heavy.

Assignment expectations are extreme for no reason. The same things can be achieved with more reasonable requirements. To be writing your final paper and not have any idea of where you stand in the class is simply not conducive to learning. But that is out of our hands, so we do our best with what we have. This class could be more reasonable
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Important topics, class discussions are good. Lots of reading and reading responses do not have clear grading criteria. Just skim the readings, lecture slides and handouts aren't really provided. I wish the course offered more than what I could get from reading the material on my own; more lecture notes, handouts, and structure/guidance
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof. Webb knows what she's talking about, she is very knowledgable in topics regarding the urban education system but at times she can come off as intimidating which stopped me from participating because I was afraid I was gonna say something wrong. There is A LOT of reading so be prepared for that, other than that you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof. Webb is my favorite prof at UIC so far. She is VERY intelligent and has a conversation-based classroom. Conversations are open to the class and usually involves the whole classroom (interesting topics). Prof. Webb is interested in student perspective and opinion and will gladly listen to what everyone has to say.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Professor Webb is one of the sweetest and understanding professors I've had. She is very intelligent and does an amazing job teaching this topic. There's lots of readings, but you can definitely pass by just skimming them.

Overall great professor. Be sure to participate at least once a week to get an A. Do not miss class because each absence will go down a half a letter grade. Talks a lot, but has great notes, so write everything she says down, especially in the beginning before midterm because its HARD. HUGE curve though. I got a D+ and it went up to B after curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Webb was very knowledgeable and the class was super interesting. If u're thinking about teaching this class really shows you what to expect. Cons are that she's a terribly slow grader so I didn't receive any grades back, it's a lot of reading, and she was so late about grading our assignments that she missed the deadline of final grades

I for one am a terrible test taker and her one exam was not difficult. The semester is now over, with only a few days til Christmas and still have not received a single grade back for the two papers and one final project. If you miss a certain amount of days she will fail you regardless of the grade you received. She assigns a lot of reading.

She was very knowledgable in this area of study, but students may have hesitated to state their opinions if they clashed with hers. She seemed to get upset by it. NO grades were posted until AFTER finals. No one in our class knew how we were doing or if we could do better to get our grades up. I would take another professor if I had the chance.

Yeah, you'll have to read a couple dozen pages a week. Yeah, you're required to come to class. If you aren't interested in urban education then don't take the class. If you are interested, go in to the class ready to contribute to the discussion. If you can do that then you'll enjoy it. She is disorganized, that's the only valid criticism here.

She honestly deserves better rating than this, I took her class as a gen Ed. I'm an engineering major from the white suburbs and she got me interested in urban education, that should tell you something. Don't take her class if you want an easy A, welcome to college.

If you can take this class with another professor do so! She is unhelpful, does not take a student's suggestions into consideration, and is very unorganized! We hardly got any assignments back in a timely manner and she became defensive when we inquired. Her tests are ridiculously hard; overall not a nice person and I do not recommend!!!

If you can avoid taking her, do it. She is the worst professor I have had. Her exams are cruel and the amount of readings she assigns her students is ridiculous. She is the professor who states "can't reply to your emails because my inbox is full". I wish I had the option of taking another professor because of the amount of stress this lady gave me

Honestly, she is a great person with personality but her class is what makes things very difficult. She assigns weekly readings almost 100-200  ages per week. She says it's not a lot but if your a full time student your honestly in trouble. She assigns to much homework that she can't even grade them on time and opts it out on the final grade

Prof. Webb is a wonderful professional who provides clear expectations while being willing to work with students' needs. She is wonderful for grad students and provides a great deal of content in ways that you can tailor to your own interests. A+
If you absolutely don't have to take ED100, please do not take this class. Prof. Webb doesn't seem to know how to teach. She is dull and dry. However, if you have a good TA, you will survive :)
