Overall the class had A LOT of weekly readings. Also participation points were taken with the iclicker during lecture. The class itself can be very boring, it really all depends on which TA you get. If they're an easy grader then you're in luck. Other than that there was also a 15 page community report, and a 30 hour field placement requirement.

Terrible professor. She gives way too many readings and acts like Ed 100 is the only class your taking at UIC and she thinks you have all the time in the world. She has an attitude and she is not helpful at all. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!

She gives out many weekly readings, over 200+ pages to read. You must go to lecture unless you want to lose participation points due to iclicker. 15 page community report on 30 hours of field work. Her class is A LOT of work, its impossible to keep up unless you have no life.
Her class isn't impossible but it is difficult and she tends to be unhelpful. Go to her office hours, I couldn't, I had classes during them. A lot of reading, like +200 pages a week, usually more.

She is too attached to readings. will assign 200-400 pages a week and spends lecture time talking at you. Midterm is close to impossible, to write 25 paragraphs total within 50 minutes...says papers are eligible for revisions but then never gives them back. While a nice PERSON, she is an AWFUL professor...

She's actually a really good teacher. She provides and extensive amount of material for students to cover and is very approachable if someone has a problem. But a lot of the readings are hefty and aren't even reviewed during class. Students aren't even tested on most of them. It is also difficult because she has a hardcore anthropology background.

Religiously assigns readings, and doesn't specify which parts of a 200+ page reading will be on a weekly descriptive 4 short answer quiz. Papers assigned were too long and meaningless. Spends entire lecture/discussion blabbering on about the readings and obvious stuff relating to race. DO NOT take her, or the class if you don't absolutely have to!

She's brilliant and really genuine. You'll learn a lot from her if you stay open minded. She gives A LOT of really long readings, like 200-300 pages a week. She assigned multiple books, and quizzes on them. I never read the books, or many of readings, but I still got a ton out her class. I would have gotten an A but I skipped the first paper.

He is hilarious with his lectures, kinda dad like in a way. He brings up many current topics in the world relating to the texts, which I enjoy. DO NOT FALL BEHIND ON THE READINGS. He does surprise quizzes but will let you know ahead. The paper criterias are clear. My only complain is that he is a slow grader, no grade the whole semester..
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He's a very sweet man, but as a teacher I wouldn't take him again. He talks very slow which you can ignore, but he never grades anything. It's almost the end of the semester and I have no clue what my grade is or the weight of the assignments because he never included that in the syllabus. Just very confusing class.

Whalen TALKS. ALOT. The entire class time is filled with rambles and lecture, but it is genuinely interesting and fun to listen to. The class is easy (light work load and flexible deadlines) but that doesn't mean you won't learn a lot. Great prof for 207
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
Professor Whalen had a way of keeping the class engaged with a joke pertaining to the readings whenever he notices the class's attention is distancing from the subject. He may go on many tangents sometimes as he's rambling about the text, but he's very entertaining with his tangents as well.

Highly recommend you take professor Whalen's class.

Professor Whalen is very knowledgeable about pop culture and the readings are surprisingly interesting. He is so flexible when it comes to deadlines and genuinely wants you to succeed. I loved how approachable he was and though he lacks in email responses, he definitely reads them and will take the time to give you a response in-person.

I loved Professor Whalen. There aren't many assignments and all you really have to do is keep up with the readings. He is very flexible with deadlines and super nice to everyone. He does tend to ramble in his lectures which may be hard to pay full attention to, but he's also pretty entertaining so it's just as hard to tune him out sometimes.

Whalen is difficult to follow during lectures and discussions. I was hardly able to come up with coherent notes because he rambles on ALOT. The texts that were read were incredibly bland, no diversity whatsoever which is a disservice. I found him to be some what condescending and completely unorganized. I do not recommend taking him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class is an easy A, especially if you have Whalen. You have to do about 2-3 papers and he likes to give pop quizzes so reading is important for this course. In class, he mainly just lectures and you don't really need to participate. Sidenote: loves sarcasm and cracking jokes, he's hilarious.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: His class was very easy and interesting, a compilation of short stories and then Frankenstein. However, he never ever ever stops talking. Any chance of a student discussion is out the window. If you can hold out, I recommend because he is an easy grader, if English is something you like. Seriously, he drones on and on. Beware, but a good class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She is a decent professor and made sure to extend deadlines for Exams due to the lateness of the lecture videos. I didn't really interact with her since you only have to attend labs via Zoom, but my TA was great and open to any questions or concerns. There were a few extra credit opportunities towards the end of the semester which really helped.
I had a great TA and both her and my TA were very understanding. She fell behind a lot on lectures this semester, but she was able to adjust the deadlines accordingly. Just make sure to do your labs.

I actually liked Pamela. She is a really nice lecturer, not the best professor I had, but trust me she could do way worst. Really interesting lectures and she had a good pick of TA's, they were all very helpful. I'm taking her again for ANTH 234. Do your labs
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Her lectures were super boring and her exams are multiple choice (5 exams). She assigns two papers that are based on the two class field trips. I never dealt with her directly because there are TAs but the class is easy overall just a little time consuming for a gened. The class is not weighted so theres opportunity to improve.
reviews.rating_tags: SO MANY PAPERS--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: While Professor Whyms can be a bit dry it is nothing unbearable. Grading criteria is clear (labs matter the most), posts grades on blackboard quickly as well. No real "Popquizzes" but what she calls "E&E" in some classes which are no harder than two questions, mostly used them for feedback to help us on tests. Would take again, she is clear but dry
Her exams are packed with a ridiculous amount of information.

Suuuuuuper boring. Reads off of a powerpoint - says nothing remotely interesting. Not upbeat at all. Did not make me want to learn in the slightest. The work was whatever, typical. Wouldn't take her again, because it was pretty hard to get through her lectures, to be honest.

Prof Whyms was ok, she wasn't the best professor I've had, but she definitely wasn't the worst. There's a lot of work in the class, but they're easy, as long as you just do them. You get mostly 100% on labs and hw just for doing them. 2 papers as well, but they were a bit hard and lengthy. tests are online and were also a bit hard :/

Lectures are really long, she simply reads off the slides.  Has truly poor communication skills (says 'um' after every other word). She assumes everyone in the class is an anthro major, which is not the case. There is no homework oppurtunity, so basically labs, tests, and two papers are your only source of grades. TA's suck too. Pam is terrible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Long lectures and she basically read off the powerpoint. When students asked her questions she never gave them an answer. There were two papers that required you to go to the zoo and the field museum. The class was overall easy but there's a lot of pointless work.

Professor Whyms was the worst professor I have ever taken at UIC, she was unethical, expected college students to pay for field trips and transportation on their own and her TA's were even worse. She was boring and was under the impression that everyone was an anthropology major. One word: EXTRA
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Whalen is an incredibly intelligent professor. He gave interesting lectures that showed he had a deep knowledge and care for what he taught. He is an incredible professor, and I will take him again if given the chance.

He has a vast knowledge of literature. Very intelligent, which shows in his lectures, and if you pay attention in his class it can be really interesting. He likes to push students to think about the meaning of the material and shares interesting and thoughtful insights about it. As a professor I feel he is genuine, he likes to see students trying.

He doesn't organize his lectures well and he tends to ramble so note-taking was difficult. He didn't facilitate many opportunities for students to participate. Exam questions were convoluted and he did not provide specific feedback on assignments. The assigned texts lacked diversity making for a monotonous course experience. Avoid.

Whalen is difficult to follow during lectures and discussions. I was hardly able to come up with coherent notes because he rambles on ALOT. The texts that were read were incredibly bland, no diversity whatsoever which is a disservice. I found him to be some what condescending and completely unorganized. I do not recommend taking him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are awesome, but beware of the exams. They are very specific and my classes mid-term average was 59%. Very tough when it comes to exams, but he as a person is very entertaining to listen to and liked to make us laugh. Be ready to read a LOT

Prof. Whalen is incredibly smart and funny. He cares about his students and wants them to become thinking, questioning adults. He also wants them to internalize the material read in his class, not simply to pass an exam but as a way to enrich their inner life. He's an easy essay grader but does assign a lot of reading. Overall, a great professor!

Whalen can seem intimidating due to his vast knowledge in so many different arenas of literature. That being said, his lectures are usually pretty fascinating if you're a lit major. You will read. A lot. Expect to finish a different book every two weeks or so, with the occasional extension offered if the class speaks up about heavy workload.

He gives a quiz every Friday solely based on summary of the text to make sure you're reading. However, the quizzes help you because he recycles the questions on the final. He hypes everything up to be super hard but the course is pretty easy if you pay attention in class. Try finding someone who took him before he recycles exams and quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Tests are annoyingly specific to little irrelevant details in texts, compares everything to dumb tv shows he likes, has horrible readings, and seems alittle prejudiced. He comes late and then flips out when students want to leave on time. He looses students assignments. Avoid.

Professor Whalen is a very intelligent professor, however his exams and quizzes are HARD. You must read and show up to class. It is the only way you'll pass. He grades tough and believes that exams are meant to be tough to get us to really focus on the reading. You do not know where you stand in the class until grades are turned in.

He is a very knowledgeable professor and always has interesting insights on the texts being read. You must be on top of reading, but that helps a lot with the papers. Genuine professor who is willing to help when students are experiencing difficulties. You can excel in the class if you participate, read closely and ask questions!

Whalen is the single most difficult English teacher with whom I have encountered. He never stays on topic, he pretty much just talks about the authors' lives. He also gives WAY too much reading at a time, and expects you to memorize quotes verbatim. He is ridiculous. AVOID AT ALL COSTS

I took this teacher for English 243 this past Fall and was worried about it's difficulty. He's a great teacher, very intelligent, but you go through a lot of material so make sure you keep up with the readings and study for the midterms and finals. You will definitely learn something in taking his class!
I have taken this teacher twive before.  I liked his teaching style so much that I am taking another class of his.  He encourages awesome group discussions and papers that are outside-the-box.

Prof. Whalen would be great to take to a baseball game, but his class is boring.  His midterms and finals are not like other 200-level English courses at UIC: they are extremely difficult.  STUDY.  If you procrastinate in his class, you're screwed.
UIC's best English Professor. Some find him dull, but those interested in the subject matter find him riveting. Subtly hilarious as well. Take him!

extremely intelligent! really knows his stuff, and he lectures very clearly. gives a lot of information during his lectures and facilitates a lot of note taking. helpful in respect to planning for midterm/final but his tests are haaarrrd. usually helps to regurgitate what profs say but not in this case. really gets you to think
GREAT professor. smart, intelligent, fascinating, cares about students.

T Whalen is awesome. He's an intelligent professor well versed in the experience of being a student, for he himself is one when it comes to literature, heck we all are. He's understanding and poignant. An all around great professor.

He is exactly what I expected an English professor to be. An intelligent, well-spoken guy that really wants his students interested. Slightly flexible if you're doing the work. It's too bad that most English majors slack off in their writing in the discipline requirement course. His was too good and his class was too bad. They missed out.
This professor has is nice, and has a sense of humor. When taking this class, ask questions on what he wants or if you don't have a clear understanding.
No Comments
Drier than sand, but tries to be helpful.

He opened the first day of class with, "I'm mean." Don't buy it. He's great! Good sense of humor; he facilitates discussion in a positive manner. He expects a lot of his students. Read, keep up, and don't be afraid to chime in with your thoughts and take a stand on the readings.
At first you think he is going to be hard but then he loosens up.  We focused on Huck Finn for nearly the entire semester, so make sure to read it and like the book.

Great guy. He is very nice and respectful. Coursework was neither hard nor was it too time-consuming. He was very active on email and Piazza. He is very understanding and creates a warm and welcoming learning environment. One of the best professors I've experienced. I highly encourage taking his class. I took CS 472 with him.

I love this man with all my heart
Goated professor for 472
SLIME
Great professor. Great class. Class structure was friendly to working students. One of the best classes I've taken at UIC.
Would take it again!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment:
Great class, great teacher. Makes sure to answer everyone's questions and everything is clear before proceeding.

Homeworks usually required more use of the debugger than coding but were very doable and I never felt like I was lost at any point.

Professor Mansky is by far one of the best professors at UIC. His lectures are clear, precise and coherent. He breaks down extremely opaque concepts so that they are easily digestible. You can make out from his demeanour that he genuinely cares about his students. He promptly responds to any emails/Piazza posts. I would definitely take him again.

Professor Mansky is always available to answer your questions, the grading criteria is clear from the beginning of the course. The course covers many topics but it is not too difficult to follow. Homeworks can be submitted twice and after the first time you get feedback on your progress. One of the best and most caring professors I have ever had.
Very precise lecture style. Also extremely sharp CS professor. Responds quickly to requests for homework help. One of the best! Caring and understanding.

Prof knows his stuff, and is very willing to help you out and understand the material. If you miss a class, be certain to look over the slides for that day, because you may get lost otherwise. No final test, project instead. CS 476 is a course on programming language design and implementation, so it's some high level material. Take good notes
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Mansky is one of the best professors I have ever had. He is very passionate about his field of work, he explains topics clearly and doesn't hesitate to give additional details and repeat explanations if students don't understand. I highly recommend taking this course if you are interested in the topic! A+++

felt like a grad level class. Lectures were atrocious; I would leave class feeling as if I didnt learn anything. Exam weight was unfair. Harsh curve. I missed 1 class came back to them doing something totally different. Good luck taking this class, you're going to need it.
Lectures are boring, bring a pillow cause it's a guarantee you'll fall asleep. He has no charisma, he's unrelatable. He seems to only help those who are doing well. Homework every week.

Very thorough about his lecture material. Stops frequently for questions and is always quick to respond on Piazza. Me being unfamiliar with the topics does feel like hitting a brick wall at times and his lectures may benefit from more concrete examples. Homework problems are usually simple and help you understand the content of the course.

The class is challenging since its a 400 level CS course but he makes it easier on you by giving relatively simple problems to do for HW. He also gives written or programming HW depending on what is being taught in the class. The whole class revolved around OCaml so be prepared to dive head first into it without much time on the basics.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This professor is good and its clear that he enjoys teaching FIN449. Only thing is that its very difficult to read his handwriting, making it difficult to study for the quizzes. The Professor also grades the assignments in a tough way. There aren't always clear expectations of what is expected of students. Great guy but class structure needs work.

Very superficial.
He does not explain at all. 
He spends a big part of the class playing games.

Professor John is a great professor, I learned a lot about investing through this class thanks to him. Attendance is not mandatory. All the assignments are group projects so pick a good group. There are like 2 quizzes. No exams.
Chill professor, content is pretty good. Group work im not a big fan of. Get a small group if possible beforehand.
He's the best professor for me so far.
This is the first ever in-person class where attendance was optional and I always wanted to come to very long lectures. 449 is soooo fun!
He is the best, makes everything easy. If you have the chance to take his classes go for it, you wont regret.

Professor Wightkin is among the top professors at UIC. He has experience in the field and will help you learn things about investing that you wouldn't simply learn on your own. If you're into investing then this class is a must. A few group project and quizzes but he's super helpful and will help you out if you don't understand something.

Awesome guy! I came in to class knowing very little about investments but he really made class a place to learn from zero. Heavy on group projects and presentations, so make sure to pick people you can rely on. Attendance is not mandatory, but you'll see that the class is always packed because people really respect him.

One of the best professors at UIC. He teaches you a lot about the stock market and helps with picking stocks for your own portfolio. He teaches you what you'll need to know for an actual job. UIC and universities, in general, should have more professors and classes like this. Would 100% recommend taking him if you have the chance.

He is the best professor I have ever taken. You will learn a lot about investing in the stock market. Professor treats everyone with respect; he truly wants his students to succeed. I wish all the professors were like him: it would make the learning process much more enjoyable.

Class is once a week. I would say this class was an easy B. I went to class half the time, and we got D's on our assignments, but ended up passing with a B. He curves alot. All of the assignments are group based and there are two quizzes (No final exam, only a project). Overall really nice guy.

Awesome teacher. Wants to make your you know it instead of making classes unnecessarily hard to follow university standards. I actually learned the material because of how the class was set up, and it was less stressful in comparison to other classes I took.

Good, informational class for those who are interested in trading. Always let class out early, 2 quizzes, numerous group projects, current event presentation, & during the whole semester you do a stock simulation. No book & cancels a lot of classes. 1st quiz is closed notes, 2nd is open notes. Overall, laid back class with insightful information.
He is the best Professor ever. The class subject was very interesting, I just wish UIC had more Finance classes like this one.
Really great professor he wants you to learn a lot and doesn't worry about grades if he could he would give everyone A's but he can't so he does his best if you do your best.

Professor is very helpful and provides lecture on content that is used in real-life. For those who are interested in stocks (trading), taking this professor will open your doors to better investing. No textbook required.  Class is once a week; gets out early too.
The best math teacher in the university. This guy is super chill. He taught a lot of real-world math/social justice issues, such as crime rate and taxes, to give us actually useful skills.

This guy is super chill. We talked about a lot of real-world math and social justice issues that really make the class engaging. As long as you pay attention and ask questions when you need to, the class is really easy. He'll drop some low grades, and you can choose either a test or a project for the final.

The couse was supposed to be easy. Some geometry, algebra and math that relates to daily life. Instead for most thr semester we calculated complicated loans. We had an exam immediately after we learned what an APY was and the whole exam was on APY's. I only recommend him if you wanna learn how to manually do taxes.

this is the goat. i was sooooo bad at math in high school i got horrible grades but i got my first As on all his tests. i actually learned the math and he is a good person personally. one time he let me borrow a calculator for another class exam.

Anthony is a great professor who makes large lectures feel small because he moves around to help students with their work. If you follow along in class, you'll be fine on the exams. He's a lenient grader and drops your lowest scores. He is super laid back, hilarious, and genuinely cares about his students, sharing valuable life tips in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Clear instructions and straightforward explanation of what needed to be done. Always offered individual help despite a large class. HW, attendance, midterm, and final were graded. SUPER EASY to pass. He cares that you understand the content. As someone who doesn't like math, he was a great professor
Great professor, simple class, it's organized well
The content is easy to understand. Watching the videos and taking notes are very helpful. You should definitely be able to pass the class.

HE WILL MAKE SURE YOU PASS! He was amazing and very helpful throughout the whole semester. As long as you pay attention, take your notes (which are printed for you) you will pass. Very helpful in office hours for homework help. Yes there is a lot of homework but it is well needed especially if you're not the best at math.

Woldeit was a great prof despite being new to UIC! He's very easy to learn from and gives pre class videos so you get an idea of the class work prior to attending. As long as you watch the video & take notes, you'll breeze through. Each vid is ~10 mins long and then you spend most of class time doing practice problems and while he helps students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: He is a nice person but his teaching technique is very poor. He goes slow enough that you don't cover enough content, and he goes fast enough that you can't understand any of the concepts. Calculus 3 is an easy course but he somehow makes it seem impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: he doesn't even grade the homework on time so you dont know  where you are in the course, the exams are worth way too much of your grade like 40% for the final exam, he doesn't even actually teach he just does some crazy confusng proof and thats lecture, his homework is not even that bad tbh but the exams r terrible

By far the most difficult class I have taken at UIC. He explains the topic and what it is useful for and then just provides a long, complicated proof of a concept without explaining the application of any of it. If you go to office hours he will explain the application capably but in a way like he is surprised you didn't intuit it on your own.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Hardest class I have taken at UIC. Other sections got to have a take home exam. Professor takes ~20 mins to explain the material of the day and then the class participate in a group activity to solve the problem that involves the material of the day, which is also not taken for credit. 60% of your grade comes from the midterm and final alone.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Goes through easy concepts in a complicated and brief way. Homeworks are complicated as well since he doesn't teach properly. Exams heavily impact your grade (60% total); he puts concepts he went through once in lecture as a 20-point question. Midterm average was 50%. I got A's in Calc 1 to 3 and Linear Algebra as well, he is so bad at teaching.

By far the hardest class I have taken at UIC. Teaches very briefly for ~20 to 25 mins and gives problems to solve in the rest of the lecture time in groups. To prepare for an exam you only have the homework (no solutions) and the exam review which is nothing like the exam. The averages for exams are around 50/100 with little to no partial credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: loved his sense of humor, his competence and knowledge. great professor

this class was during the evening, however he made it worth while and he has great humor and respect about the profession he teaches about. Offered help with internships and advice. Tests are a little daunting so make sure to study but a interesting course and teaches well.

The class is daunting, but David made it worth while. He is very knowledgable and despite 2 hours of lecturing, his humor and style of presenting kept me engaged.The exams are a little hard but if you attend class and study a good amount you should be able to do well. He's very caring and even offered help finding internships. Highly recommend!
He is the best
Awesome professor. Everything that's in the lectures gets involved in the assignments. Easy class if you remain focused and pay attention to the lectures! Overall one of my favorite classes.

2 exams (midterm and final) and one paper, one group project. He makes the lessons easy to learn, but does not use blackboard so don't expect a constant update on grades. He rounds grades and gives extra credits on exams but overall he's a great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: David is a great professor. He does lecture alot throughout class, but usually let us out like an hour early. There was a midterm and a final; both hard considering we didn't exactly know what to expect even though he did a short review session. He does take attendance, and we did use the book. One group project and a short paper which wasnt hard.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Can I take him again please.  One paper, 2 exams and a group Project. Go to class, he is very knowledgeable. Helps you if you want advice regarding what you want to do after college. Expect a lot of sarcasm, but at the same time he uses humor to engage the course. He tends to relate a lot of his subject matter to movies, thus keep that in mind.

He acts like he's very laid back but he is unorganized. He does not use blackboard. Does not respond to emails so good luck w questions. Also, you never know your grade until the end after final grades are submitted. I read every chapter on my own and went to each class  and still got a B.  A midterm, final and a easy presentation. Would not take.

i really liked mr. williams. i thought his test were kind of hard as he spent like 10 minutes reviewing before the test. definitely recommend the prison tour and he is a pretty easy grader as far as presentations. Overall, cool professor.

MUST TAKE ALL HIS CLASSES! I have taken 2 (CLJ355 and 491). EASIEST A I have ever had at UIC. Smart professor, knows his material, doesn't lecture much, plays a lot of movies/videos. Easy final. Not a hard grader at all on papers.

Nice and funny guy, Didn't care too teach that much, probably only 15-20 minutes other two hours were presentations and breaks . Final, well no one knew it was chapters 1-21, still received an A. Easy enough

Class was a really easy A I thought, but he would only lecture for 20 minutes out of the three hours and you had no idea what to expect for the final. Overall nice guy and funny I thought. Just unclear at times and random.

THIS IS THE PROFESSOR YOU WANT! He is very nice and his notes are all you need to pass his class! As long as you attend and make the class interesting youll ace it for sure! Pick his brain though, he has worked in Criminl justice awhile...he has some awesome stories! :)

HE IS A GREAT PROFESSOR! Has a lot of experience and is very knowledgeable. He is very approachable and as long as he knows who you are you will do fine in his class. His exams are fairly easy, just attend review sections . A prison visit is mandatory but it is worth it! I recommend him if yo are looking to take an elective.
All you have to do is show up and take notes.

I absolutely love this teacher. Very helpful, and knows the material really good. He has experience working in the Criminal Justice System so he explains it very clear. I wish he would teach a lot more classes!! Definitely a good pick! You will get worth your money!!! and leave with thorough knowledge of the subject!

I love this teacher, I took him for corrections, he had us go to a prison, which i really didnt want to do but it was fine. Got an A, you dont need to buy the book if you take notes and then he does a review before the tests. Alot of it is basic 101 stuff that you learn over and over again. I am taking another class with him just because its him.

This professor is great. I had him for both 210 and 355. He is so laid back and easy-going. He is always willing to help anyone out with anything, like how to apply to law school, and his experiences as a prosecutor. He is great! loved both classes!
Great professor, I really enjoyed going to prison. He is super helpful with questions pertaining to Grad school and such. I loved his class. Very down to earth, super smart guy!
BEST CRJ CLASS I HAVE EVER TAKEN.  THIS GUY GOES OUT OF HIS WAY TO HELP STUDENTS.  CANNOT STRESS ENOUGH HOW GREAT HE IS.  WORK HARD AND HE WILL NOT LET YOU DOWN.  (A+)

He's the best teacher I have ever had.  The lectures were very interesting.  Not boring at all.  I always looked forward to all of the classes.  He always answered any questions I had outside of class and he helped me sometimes with any problems I had.  If anyone gets a chance to take this class, take it.  Trust me, you'll enjoy it
He was totally awesome, easy to talk to & funny. Not to mention good looking- which made class even more interesting.

her class convinced me to major in english! she's great! very encouraging. her feedback and critique are amazing and thorough, but her actual grading isn't harsh in the slightest. tbh, it's lenient. workload is SUPER manageable, & she's very understanding abt extensions. topic (film/book adaptations) was also rly interesting. take her fr
She is a very lineant teacher and gives free As if you do the essays which can be quite long. She is very understanding and does give extra time to submit papers.

She thinks that it is the only class you're taking. If you're taking any 200-300 level courses, say bye-bye to your grades. 

The syllabus isn't set from day one, very variable and you don't know what is coming when. Taking Calculus 3, Biology, and CS courses was easier than her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: TA of Mark Chiang. Amazing TA though. I don't understand how someone could feasibly fail the class with her. During the class I asked her for help with my papers and she took 30 mins on zoom calls to go through each page and help with edits to make my B/C papers turn into A papers. If she's your TA please ask her for paper help, she's incredible.
Easy to get a good grade, you just have to put in the work. Professor wonders gives great feedback and truly wants to give out good grades. Would highly recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Wonders is an excellent professor, possibly the best I have ever had. The majority of your grade is based on the papers you write, and although topics for the papers may seem tough, she is more than willing to help you write the paper. The key to an A is to do all the homework and get her help on the papers if you are struggling.

BEST TEACHER EVER!!!!! Her class was seriously my favorite. She gave easy in class homework points and for the essays you get a peer review, then she reviews it before you turn in a final paper. She's so approachable and helpful. I got a few 100s in the class and all As on my essays. She's the best.
Great teacher. She grades you for what you can do. Your first writing assignment will be a bench mark and then she will grade you positive as long as you are improving on that work. You will love her

Brooke was a pretty hard teacher to please, she had very strict and specific with the writing styles she saw as A material.  If you go in for her office hours she helps a lot, but you slowly build from her feedback. I really worked hard in the class and ended up with an A from getting her feedback and using her advice to the best of my abilities.

He is not the worst math professor, but I REALLY dislike him. He is nice and is always willing to help. But, he explains definitions with very few examples, and randomly gives a quiz during the week which is usually harder than an exam question. Also, if you miss the quiz, it's as if you missed the week. Calc 3 isn't hard, but he makes it so.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: His lectures can get pretty boring. There's a pop quiz once a week. The class itself isn't hard. He's really accessible outside of class and if you have any confusion about anything at all, regarding any math class, he'll help you to the best of his ability. Really nice and knowledgeable. Really patient and funny at times.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Worst professor compared to all other calc professors. I literally would come to his class to take notes from another professor's notes that were posted on blackboard. He tries to do what he can but expects you to know exactly what he is talking about. I took this class to refresh my memory and that's probably the only reason why I passed.

You can't go into this class thinking it will be a total blow off, but he's a great professor who is excited about his students. I've learned more about photography in this class than I thought I would going into it as an intro class, which is really good. He's fun and really interesting professor to have.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Too many assignments and work for a beginners photography class. Teacher is nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He is a great person and really nice. If you are taking this as an easy A, do not take him! The amount of work that is needed to do well in this class is insane. He always wants you to do better (no matter what) and that reflects on your grade.  The reading are dry, ancient and boring. He will not let you out early, ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Professor Wu is very knowledgeable. The homework he assigns could be easily applied in a professional setting. He is passionate about teaching students. When it comes to grading he cares more about the process and making sure you understand the math steps, than he does about calculating the right answer. He's one of the best professors at UIC.
Great professor. As long as you don't slack off and actually pay attention in class, you'll 100% be fine. He's willing to help and very knowledgable about the topic

Professor Wu gives a lot of meaningless and busywork just for the heck of it. He does not go into depth about the materials leaving students to seek help from one another( if possible. the Majority of the students are lost too) or frustrated. This is unfortunate because his way of teaching doesn't prepare students to be knowledgeable in the course.

Dr. Wu is very knowledgeable about economic policy and the course is very applicable to real life. He is incredibly accessible for guidance outside of class and he is a generous grader. Show your work, do extra work if you don't have an economics background and ask for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His office hour is not helpful because he doesn't know nothing about what he is teaching. He just read lecture slides that he downloads from internet in class. When doing the final projects, he is always misleading and makes students to do a lot of extra meaningless work. Worst professor ever for being a so called professor and knowing nothing
Very fun OB class! I truly enjoyed how she incorporated videos/movies in teaching. Provide study guides and review sections that help the exam. I learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Best MGMT class i ever have in my academic life either in UIC and UIUC . Lecture is clear, test is easy, group project is challenging but u will gain a lot after that . and She is sweet!!!!!! I would highly recommend take her MGMT class.

Great teacher. Lectures are interesting & easy to follow. as long as you take notes and do the study guide you will pass the exams. Group projects 2 of them. She is an easy grader as long as she sees you put effort & apply what you have learned.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She was a very nice professor and very energetic. She encourages participation and takes attendance every class. As long as you follow the syllabus and come to class, it's an easy course. However, she made us do two group projects where she picked the groups, so if you don't have a solid group, completing those projects can be rough.

Very sweet and nice. If you have questions she will answer them. If you want the textbook you can get the older edition. Never used book just for group project for the case study. Exams are easy if do the study guide. Dont wait last minute to do group project. She takes attendance for points for participation so dont miss.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Really sweet, but she isn't clear in her directions and that hurt the group projects which are a lot of your final grade! She also isn't clear when she is teaching and you leave the class confused as to what to do for an assignment. I wouldn't recommend her because you won't learn too much.
The professor is nice, but her teaching methods are bad. She jumps from topics within lectures, and the case studies confused me more.
Very good teacher who truly cares. Gives good real world advice. Easy to talk to and good looking
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests? Not many--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great professor, she really knows her stuff. Be prepared because her class is engaging. A few group projects with presentation and 2 exams. Adapts to the class and really shows a lot of effort and passion for her students.
Really great professor! She cares about her students and makes an effort to make the class interesting. Her tests are straightforward if you study. Attendance is mandatory.
She rocks, go to class and participate. Easy A
Great Professor. I'd recommend her to anyone.   Attendance is mandatory, and the final paper is long. But overall, great class.
Great class!!! Fun experience and interesting information
It is a good class to take: Fun and grade A.  Especially, you can lean some useful job hunting skills and negotiating compensation packages  skills.

Her class is enjoyable and I recommend taking MGMT 453 with her. She goes the extra mile to assist students in the classroom and she also provides valuable help with job searching, graduate school, certification exams, etc.  She has a good teaching style of lecturing and incorporating student participation. Very nice and helpful professor.
She's a great teacher,  kind and always there for u. Her lecture is fun and useful. She also gives good advice about grad school application and job search. Totally recommend it!!

Despite being a professor for only a short amount of time, Professor Wu is a good professor. Attendance is mandatory, and she gives a case study to do at home every other week. The only downside is that there is a language barrier and she does get overwhelmed very easily at times when trying to explain material or situating the class.

She is very committed to a fun learning experience for the students. She requested our feedback and made changes to her teaching approach. I especially enjoyed the review sessions, they were in a game format.
SHE IS A GREAT TEACHER WITH EXTREME KNOWLEDGE, I REALLY ENJOY HER CLASSES. SHE IS FUNNY AND KIND. SHE SHARES HER EXPERIENCE WITH STUDENTS AND GIVE GREAT TIPS FOR FUTURE.
Her class is interesting. I learned a lot.
Course materials are great but listening to the class lectures may not be that helpful. You gotta be self motivated.

Simply put, the average grades were in the 20's and low 30's. Its not that this is mind blowing material. Wu is just not a good professor. Very intelligent but a horrible professor. Probably wont learn much from his class. Avoid him.
He is a very good professor, willing to help and tells his students that the exam will be based on the HW which is true but I don't get why everybody has rated him poorly here?

Everything you have heard is true!  He reads off someone else's powerpoint from years ago and his explanations are poor even if you can understand them.  The tests were hard, and I learned very little even after doing the work.  Fail everything and pass the class? Thats just dumb...

Ok professor. Ridiculous exams.  The labs are fun but very difficult, and it helps to do most of the lab report before attempting to build the circuits.Lecture is useless, but he gives out credit for attendance, which he only takes randomly.Homework review days are pointless because the TA just copies from the answer sheet that is also posted on Bb
His Lectures are useless, your  better off reading the textbook. Fast paced course, homework is ridiculous, and you will be pulling your hairs out during lab. dislike

Hes not as bad as a proffesor people say on here.  I dont know if it was just me but I was able to understand him.  He teaches with pure powerpoint slides so it kinda sucks but you get used to it.  If you want to do good in this class make sure you READ the book and take notes for yourself and you will do good.  The labs were soooo cool though. :)

Wu is a VERY hard teacher to understand. his lectures are completely useless, seriously DO NOT go to lecture... it wont help. he posts his Power points online and its alot easier to just learn by yourself in this class.  his tests are impossible, but he does do a pretty huge curve. i got a 12% on the final and got a B in the class.
Awful, horrible, careless, and non-helpful instructor. Two students with the lowest scores get an F in this class. He's just a repeating robot with a power point that someone else made.

Dr. Wu is a terrible lecturer and very hard to understand.  I think that UIC has a real problem with bringing in researchers from other countries who have little interest in teaching.  His tests are not necessarily har but poorly worded, and the language barrier is a real problem.  Avoid this teacher if you can!

This professor is terrible at lecture. He has an accent and he basically reads off the ppt slides. His exams are not very difficult if you study for them and go over homework assignments. You will have to read the book if you want to understand the material. Doing the homework will also help alot.

Poor language and teaching skills. You must read the book on your own in order to learn something. The material is taught through PPT slides and each chapter is reduced into few  slides. Students are discouraged from asking questions and going to office hours. I could say this is the worst teacher I have ever had. Avoid this professor at any cost.

Wu has one of the most difficult to understand accents I have ever heard.  The book was my teacher during this class, which fortunately worked out pretty well.  But if you go to class hoping to learn something, you'd better just bring your book and read, because even if I could understand what he was saying, he just reads the words up on the screen
This guy sucks at lecturing!!!

This guy loves covering a whole chapter in a 50-minute session using power-point. His accent is horrible. He just repeats whatever is written on the screen.  I will avoid this guy at all means for future courses.
Immature graduate student who never gave clear instructions or guidance yet was extremely demanding and unfair in his grading.

Professor Wulff is a very nice guy with a clear agenda: he wants to help.  However, he expected a lot of material to be covered in a short amount of time, appeared disorganized and the syllabus is confusing and misleading.

Somewhat unorganized and fairly dull. However, he wants to help us as students. I wouldn't take him again if I had other options, but I wouldn't feel like I was walking to my death if I needed another class with him. Is a pretty tough grader, but also a fair grader. Keep that in mind.

The class involves a ton of reading, most of which is tedious. There are a few writing assignments, which are harshly graded. Getting an A in this class requires a lot of work and understanding of the material. Nonetheless, he is more than helpful if asked outside of class.
Alex is really a good guy and an excellent teacher. He's really understanding and helps out whenever he can. He makes sure to go over everything really well so everyone can understand.
Amazing teacher! He is really helpful if you go to him.

I love Alex, but my one stipulation with him is that he has a habit of assigning too much, and then pushing back due dates. Obviously flexibility is wonderful, but things get confusing as time goes on. He's a really great guy, not an easy teacher, but a lot of fun. Highly recommended.

This class was really wonderful. Alex is a hard teacher, but he is always willing to help and really wants the best for his students. He gave us a lot of reading, which you really should do if you want to get anything out of the class-- but don't worry if you don't understand it the first time, he always goes over it with clarity and detail.

He's a good professor, he really challenges and makes you a better writer. I think his class class is worth the effort, you really walk out knowing you learned something. Although, it can be a bit challenging for first year students.
Alex challenges your writing; his style of teaching encourages you to do more and motivates you. His class is tough, and he does  expect a lot, but it's worth it.
He was helpful, but expected many assignments.
Good guy, cute but a little immature. Always willing to help. Recommended.

he was very helpful..made the material interesting.his smart and he makes you think. but! i must say he is a hard grader...so you gotta work at it. if you want to have fun...and you like english...his the prof to take.
No Comments
This guy is great. He's young and intelligent and makes learning boring material pretty interesting.

My English is not that good but I could understand all the classes. You should go to his office and have a better understanding of what he did. For the exams, you should solve all the Quizzes by your own or at least try to understand the solutions.  Do some examples and/or exercises from the book. No tough grading. Go to classes and take notes.

This is a very hard class, but I believe it could have been a lot less confusing if was taught better. Examples in class were confusing, but if you don't go to lecture you will not pass. Study the home quizzes (similar to tests). Wu grades the tests pretty easy, but still you need to study very hard. Nice guy if you go in to ask for help.

Wu isn't actually a tough professor, nor is his class extremely difficult like the past people that have rated him cut him out to be.  The take home quizzes are similar to the exams. Even if you do bad on one of the quizzes, as  long as you take the time to understand the quiz afterwards, you'll be fine. He even tries to prepare you for the exams.

He has an accent  and which is why a lot of people  get confused or lost in class. But if you are determined to pay attention,  you will find out that he isn't actually a bad professor. If you are smart and hardworking, you will be able to pull of a  B. Overall, decent professor.
good class

The assignments are definitely harder than the average homework. The exams are usually pretty challenging, but the grading done by the TA's or Professor is terrible. Hi explanations in class and teaching methods are not good, and he is not clear.

My semester, the semester before and the semester before that had over half the class fail or have gotten a D. He rarely gives partial credit and the TAs are of 0 help when seeking some sort of explanation or help from the TAs, they will say you are on the right track and that's it. The professor is confusing, skips or doesn't cover material.

He's very hard to understand in class. His examples aren't what you see on exams and skips a lot of steps during lecture. Book varies from his lectures. He doesn't teach all of the material that's covered on the exam. No curve and final is 45% of your final grade.
Very Hard class. He doesn't know how to teach, very boring. I would attend every lecture if you want to have any idea of whats going on in the class.

Course is moderately hard for first midterm, kinda simple for second midterm then it all goes downhill. Do the best you can in first 2 midterms, you'll need those points for the final. Professor knows what he's doing, but can be hard to understand. The final is worth 40% and only 3 problems. The problems on final are all symbols! class ave was 60%D

I respect him as a professor, but he will not give you any extra points if you don't do the problems his way. The material itself isn't too bad...it's his teaching style and the useless TA's that make this class more difficult. If you can take it at a community college, do so. His final in worth about 45% of your grade and he always changes it.

He's a bit hard to understand sometimes. He also might not understand you. GO TO CLASS. Everything he writes is exactly the exam (not the final tho). Attendance will clarify a lot of the little tricks he expects to know.

Tests are different from the material he teaches in class, must do extra HW outside of class to pass.  Class average was a 57% at the end and no he doesn't curve.  Hard to understand at some points but it doesn't matter, you need to learn the important stuff from the book anyways.  He is available in his office hours to help at least.

Good professor. took 203 with lemke thought i would get punished in 205. turns out wu is a very good teacher and i learned everything very well. you must do lots of problems from the book and understand the current material otherwise you will be screwed. tests will be MUCH easier if you have been studying and doing problems.

Very good professor, with very clear lectures and relatively simple exams.  His grading, however, is not easy at all.  Book work is a must considering his tests come straight from them, so if you don't do a lot of work outside of class, realize he has no problem giving you a 0/100
Really smart. He is so helpful in understanding this topic. Goes at a nice pace during class. Fair Great Professor!

Really good professor. His lectures are mostly examples from the book, but he goes over them with clarity. His tests are fair, but its your job to do the book work to do well on tests. One of the best and fair professors i've come across. Also when he does problems on the board he does it by hand or his head, no calculator needed!!!

This guy must have got hit with a power trip.  He changed the quizes to be worth 10% of grade, and yes final was worth 65% b/c average on both midterms were less than 50%.  Atleast 35% got a D or less, or withdrew.  Not the same Wu the older civil guys told me about, watch out.  But then again the alternative is lemke so take your pick.

This is teacher is not helpful at all. He does examples in class, but it is very hard to understand him. If you go to his office with questions, he will yell at you. There is no curve on his tests, and no homework assigned. Our final was 65% of our grade. Don't take him unless you have to!
One of the best at UIC hands down.
The class doesn't seem that difficult. The professor does a lot of examples and the test are fair. 65 and up is a C. Good prefessor and very willing to help!!

Had him for Strength of Materials and Structural Analysis. Fair professor. Most of the lectures are just him doing examples, which are helpful (Although sometimes he cannot finish examples which leaves you hanging). When he does examples, I recommend you follow in the book, this way you can learn the rest on your own time. No homework.
Wu explains very well.  Quiz every week.  Difficulty on exams vary.  No HW. No curve, 75% above is B.

If you want to do well in Dr. Wysocki's class, you have to read. He will respect you so much more if you do. Also, go to his office hours, he really appreciates students who seem like they actually care about their grade. He seems tough at first, but give him a chance, he's actually a great professor who really cares!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: A really good professor. Funny and full of random facts. He's a very strict grader, so you have to work a bit harder to get that A.  Don't need the book at all, just have to attend classes and take notes.

His exams r alright..if u study you will be fine..but he does not give out A's..he is very hard on grading essays, and does not have much of a curve in the end..still course overall is easy to get a B in..
I liked this class. It was very straight forward, based on the notes. 3 exams based on notes and 2 papers. Don't bother buying the book, you don't need it.

No one likes taking Communication Research  but its mandatory and I think Wysocki did a good job teaching.  He is straightforward if you take notes you will do well on the tests and he required a 10pg paper unlike other teachers who wanted 20+ pages!
Funny guy, easy class, boring at times, actually alotof the class is boring, lots of notes, easy tests

Easy class, funny professor, class can actually be fun.  Notes are important.  Kind of a pompus Jack-a$$, but I highly recommend this teacher for this class.  I think he is also teaching a 400 level class on video games..should be cool.

This is the first time and probably only time I will ever rate a teacher, but I just felt like I had to do it for this man. Mr. Wynter is an amazing professor! As a finance teacher he is extremely knowledgeable and I wished he taught all my finance classes. As a professor he is spectacular and I love his sense of humor. I would workout with him.

Teacher is cool as hell. In my opinion the best teacher for finance at UIC. Explains the material extremely well and provides many examples for students to understand. Easy grader. Midterm, final, projects, and homework.

Cool, relatable, down to earth guy. Provides some real life application of material. Show up, do HW, and study a bit for his exams, and you'll have an A. Very tough HW, but as long as you try and show effort you'll get full credit.

Professor Matthew is great! He answers all questions clearly and makes sure you succeed. He spends good amount of time on things that students have hard time understanding. Study his notes and record lectures, book needed only as reference. I wish all teachers were so easy to work with. Easy grader, class was a pleasure, he is also smoking hot!!!!

The guy loves Finance. Nice dude and try's to make sure the class gets a  hold of the material. Only problem I had with him was that I wish there were more examples given in class that related to projects and homework. All said and done, compared to some of the other professors i've had this guy is a class act.

Professor Wynter has a vast knowledge in the field of finance, not just limited to investments. The class itself was enjoyable because he took his time to make sure everyone understood the material. The material was abstract at times and without a doubt he made sure we understood it. Amazing teacher would recommend him for this course or any other.

Best Professor I have had to date.  Do not mistake easiness for weakness.  It is a class of average difficulty but he is a pro at teaching it, making it easier.  He is understanding, empathetic, and thorough.  He also has a way of getting through a good amount of material while making the pace seem slow. 100% recommended.  Great course structure.

Professor Wynter was an amazing Finance teacher. He is excited about the material and comes to class with well prepared notes and examples. He ensures all students grasp the key concepts and tests on the assignments. Would take another class with him in a second.

The course is really difficult and moves fast, but that isn't Wymans fault.  It requires loads of work on your own outside of class.  I didn't learn very much from Wyman himself, but from what I heard about the other professors who teach this course, there really isnt a better option.

If you're not doing well, you should visit him and ask for help. Dr. Wyman was very approachable which is not what other reviews said about him. GO to his office hours! He's very friendly and will definitely help you out with anything. You can get tips for quizzes too. Don't blame the professor! You're responsible for your learning.

This guy is very knowledgable about physics and is a good professor.  At first I thought he seemed like one of those strict professors, but after visiting him during office hours he came off as a pretty nice dude. However, the class itself is pretty fast paced, with tons of concepts being thrown at you every week. This class is VERY difficult.

He definitely wants to push you, but is condescending. He should understand his students more. go to his office hours after you've slaved over the hw to ask questions & demand answers even if it takes the entire office hour--no one shows up to my experience anyways. Ask questions, do the SSP's, and put in minimum one hour every night.

This man is hands down THE worst professor I have had at UIC (and I'm in my third year). He doesn't really care about the students, is super unclear, and is super condescending if you ever ask a question in class. He treats us like we are nothing compared to him. He also writes way too quickly and doesn't really explain anything as he writes.

Please avoid this professor at all costs. His lectures are not clear and he is very unapproachable. If you ask him questions he most likely will get angry. I have gotten help elsewhere and the material is much clearer than he makes it appear.  He does not seem to be invested in students' success and does not aid in the understanding of physics.

Physics 142 is a tough course at UIC. That being said, Professor Wyman's lectures were power point based and were hit and miss. It was confusing to follow some of the derivations for the different laws. If you paid attention during the examples they were helpful.  The best part of his lectures were the group problems which helped all students.

His examples are sloppy and confusing. He basically sits there and write on the projector while talking over the problems to himself instead of the students. His problems does not reflect on the problems on the exams. The exams have pretty big curve so it's not that hard to get a C by studying from the book , masteringphysics, and written homework.

Smartphysics was a better teacher than this guy. What really pissed me off is that he always said that physics was "pretty straightforward". I am someone who struggles with physics, and just assuming all the students will understand this class right away is a bad assumption to make. Worked my butt off and still did not pass this class.

Just an overall bad teacher. Worked extremely hard to receive a C. Tests were almost impossible. He did not want to be there and felt better than everyone in the room. Really did not expect such a poor teacher.
he's the worst professor ever to be born on this planet! AVOID HIM AT ALL COSTS
Doesn't really do a good job at explaining information. has students do problem in groups without really helping

Worst teacher I've ever had. Dropped at deadline because of difficulty. For Physics 1, it was super hard. Never explained things, and berated students for asking questions. He expects that students already know much of the information. Makes a hard topic much harder than it needs to be. Also, he is a hipster.

His class is hard, but phys is. I do understand why people don't like him but if they put up with his way of teaching he ia a great teacher. U do lot of grpup problems in class which helps both types of students, those who understand and those who don't. If you just want an A don't rake him, but if u want to understand the topic he is great.

The class itself is tough.  He moves through things quickly (falsely assuming everyone has a grasp of the problem at hand).  But if you attend class, and PAY ATTENTION to his EXAMPLES, and review course topics before the lecture,  you should be fine overall, make sure you do well on exams.  Pretty much all of your grade will be on that.

He is an absolutely awful professor. Avoid him at all costs. He fails to actually teach the class and rather chooses to berate and belittle the students. He thinks introductory phys students are beneath him, yet that's what he attempts to teach. I'm confused as to why he's in the profession since he loathes his classes.

Worst Professor. if u want to pass the class, read the book thoroughly, do all the exercise problems at the end of each chapter, and try to get high scores in homework and esp lab(fight for even one point). passed with B grade.
will not round grades at the end of the semester, no matter how close you are to a cutoff, he's awful at explaining things and he's a really unhelpful person

class was sort of interesting. He wont clarify things and if he does he simply repeats the same thing. i would read the book ahead of time and have a light schedule because this is a really hard course. try to take someone else and if you cant, well then you just have to tough it out
He was ok. Make sure to read the book though, it makes his lectures understandable. He has a tendency to go through examples and concepts REALLY quickly, so read the book to do well in the class.
Terrible man. Good Teacher.

Got a C in the class because I never studied for any of the exams or final. I did go to every lecture. Never told what was really going to be on exams or final. After I took the class a classmate said all of the exams and final material was on topics in his power points. Short Easy Quiz every week, tells you what to study for quizzes. Research pape

He's a nice guy that wants to help you if you are having trouble. And yup, he doesn't teach at UIC anymore. He's now teaching in Tennessee. His lecture was entertaining and he was disorganized but that's why he has the TA's so we can go to them or him if we don't understand a certain thing.
Great professor! Enjoyed the class very much! Too bad he isn't teaching at UIC anymore

This was his last semester. He was disorganized and generally seemed like he didn't care about the class. He did give us EC and a VERY easy final exam. More of a comedian than a professor. Labs are important! Take Caleb! His grading is effort based.

He is a very nice man. His lectures are very entertaining. Although geog might seem boring, he made it fun and interesting. I received an A in the class because I studied. The class is a good section to take with a rough load. Great gpa booster. I will love to have him again. Study and you will be fine. The test are far everything from the lectur

Professor Wyatt is awesome. Even with boring geography material that he has to lecture on he always figures out ways to make everyone laugh and cracks jokes. Material is not hard and exams are straight from slides and the text book. If you know material you'll get an A in this class.
Great prof. Haters gonna hate.
class contained live bobcat
Dr. Wyatt is most awesome professor that has make come to UIC. He make smile face and talk woman. He very funny head. Person must make watch on Ancient Aliens.

The material is easy, but the tests will surprise you with their difficulty so study! Dr. Wyatt is funny, easy to listen to, and clearly loves what he does. Sometimes he came off as unorganized and rushed during the lectures. Overall though, I liked having him as a professor and enjoyed coming to lectures.

Dr. Wyatt is the best professor I have had at UIC by far. He is extremely helpful and is passionate about what he does. He goes out of his way to help his students, and that has been very hard to come by when dealing with the anthro professors at UIC. I highly recommend taking a course with him. As long as you do the work, you will do well.

THIS TEACHER SUCKS. HE COMES TO CLASS EVERY SINGLE DAY UNPREPARED. ANTHROPOLOGY 102 IS THE WORST AND HARDEST 100 CLASS IN EXISTENCE. THE TESTS ARE SO DIFFICULT. I STUDIED FOR TWELVE HOURS AND GOT A C ON A TEST AND I AM USED TO RECEIVING A'S. DO NOT EVER TAKE THIS CLASS. OR THIS TEACHER PROBABLY.

This man is hilarious. He puts a real effort into his lectures and he is really passionate on the subject. It is actually enjoyable to go to lecture. Labs and the lab exam are really easy. If you pay attention and do your work the class is pretty easy.
He's funny and pretty down to earth (atheist). He's enthusiastic about the subject and you can understand him entirely. He puts questions from his lectures on his tests.

Wyatt has been by far one of my favorite professors. I think he's hilarious. He does an amazing job at taking something that can be boring and turning it into something fun.  His lectures are worth going to just for a good laugh. His powerpoints are funny. The book is necessary for the tests. The material's pretty simple. Overall, awesome class.

Really funny and charismatic professor. Great to have a teacher with an actual sense of humor... especially for a class as interesting as geography. The class is really easy and consists of weekly quizzes where you have to locate countries on a map, one paper,  and 3 exams (including final). Need a fallback class? Take GEOG 100 with Wyatt.

In a seminar class like this, attendance and reading the assigned material is a must, and be prepared to take part in discussion. Dr. Wyatt is laid back and approachable, as well as informative, and really cares about the subject as well as the students.
Good teacher

his geog 100 class is super easy!!!! I only went to class about 5 times the entire semester and 3 of those times were during exams and i got an A. Just go to discussion every week and know the bold faced words for the exam and you will be totally fine

He was awesome!  He was an actually person not some robot professor.  He cared about the students especially how they did in the class.  He honestly felt bad if the kids were not doing good and would offer to help!  We need him back @ IPFW!!
The class isn't that difficult if you keep up with the reading but in class he tends to go off topic a lot and tends to be overall not that helpful.

Xabi was pretty good, though I felt the class left something to be desired. I think I actually got worse at Spanish this semester because the course really had no rigor. I was expecting to get better at speaking since it's a conversation course, but no one really talked and the class had no camaraderie.

Xabi is very cool. He speaks clearly and slowly so you can understand him. Also, he doest always speak in spanish, he will make sure you understand in english before rating off in spanish. i enjoyed his class.

Lots of reading, we read the WHOLE book. We had to write too many essays, 3 4-page ones plus reflection papers... the movies we studied were cool though. Professor was hard but at least helpful and available unlike others I've had. Fast grader.
This class was HARD. Lots or writing required, attendance mandatory. I did learn a lot, but if you can, look for a less demanding instructor. He knows his stuff though.

Prof. Granja was nice, it's obvious he knows a lot of literature. Readings are easy but the grammar homework and essays require a LOT of time. Not an easy course, but I really enjoyed it. He grades fairly and adds lots of explanations & suggestions to your drafts to help with revision. This course was a much better experience than with other TAs.

Granja was a great Spanish teacher.  He graded very fairly, was easy to relate to, and always cheery.  He also shows up on time!  Speaks very clearly so that building vocabulary is a breeze.  I suggest taking his class!

This guy was awesome. He's very strict about the requirements of the course, not an easy A. Work hard though, and you'll find he's a fair grader and gives lots of helpful and clear advice. He's always happy & cheerful. Also nice to look at!

Granja is a good professor and makes everything easily understandable. The only problem I had in the course though, which was an introduction to analyzing Spanish literature, was that our essays were graded solely on grammar, not actual content, which was frustrating.
I loved his class. Everything is clear. You have to work hard but it's doable. Reading the stories in the book is a must though.

Very warm & caring guy. He's very relatable & understanding. If you don't plan on reading the book, you shouldn't take his class...or any Spanish course at UIC. The course, homework, exams, quizzes & composition(s) are based entirely off the book.

I took Yao's optics class out of general interest for medical imaging systems. The exam and homeworks were very straightforward from his lecture slides, and the final consisted of a presentation and paper. He began with a general understanding of optics and later discussed different methods and their applications.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Yao is a very nice person and the class content was really helpful. I took his BIOE 594, Biomedical Optical Imaging courses. He had genuine knowledge about the topic and shared interesting information. His HW/quizzes are usually from the ppt slides. Quite easy course for a grad level course.
He is one of the worst professors in BIOE department. His lectures were copy pasted from the book and he is very hard to understand.
Such a great professor! Content of lectures was interesting and clear, gives a lot of extra credit assignments. Would definetely take this professor again.
Great professor! Explains concepts clearly and makes economics easy to understand.
Would recommend. Found the lectures and slides helpful. Fun dude and explains in detail. I had some challenges in the end and he seemed very accommodating.
Don't waste your time on this stupid class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Liked his class. Also flexible on things like attendance if you talk to him.
He really cares about making you understand the topic. I found the class interesting even though econ isn't my major.
Ngl his accent was a little too thick and he talked too fast for me to follow along. Maybe its a skill issue but its still a mid class.

Good class. He gives extra credit opportunities and his tests aren't really that hard. He will even curve if the class does bad. There were iClickers but they were not graded which is nice. He speaks a little too fast though. Not a bad class at all.

Professor Chirag was very helpful. His materials are very easy to understand and he was a very generous grader. I had a B overall but due to regular attendance, he gave me an A for final grade. Would highly recommend him.
Hands down one of the best professors at UIC. I only took this class as a gen ed, but I wished I had taken this class sooner. He made me want to peruse a career in economics!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Might be difficult to understand but overall very generous and will try to get you the best possible grade, as long as you do your part.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He straight-up said he wasn't going to teach the class. He'd only go through select problems in class. He has the heaviest accent I've ever heard in my life. His exams were so hard that I think the CIA is going to use them as interrogation methods. When you'd go to him for help he would say he can't help and to refer to the book.

He encourages questions in class and cares about if students are understanding the material. He relies too much on theory through and not many examples of how statistical tests are used in real-world applications are given. The course grade only included homework, 2 exams, and a final project. Throughout the course, he gave a lot of extra credit.

The homework aligns well with the lecture handouts and the exams are similar to the study guide so its a manageable class. However, the professor goes too fast, is a bit hard to understand, and could explain things better.

Stats 535 is the worst choice i made. Unclear grading policy, unclear homework, heavy accent and bad handwriting. He is personable. But he doesn't explain in class. He seems to know nothing about what he is teaching. Also, he seems to be very impatient in class. I would avoid any course been given by him.

One of the toughest statistics classes that uic has to offer combined with a professor that doesn't teach effectively while also going off on random tangets in class. Homework was very difficult just like the exams. My friend told me not to take this class warning me how tough this class is! do not take!!!!!!!

UIC's MSCS department should be embarrassed to have him as an instructor. He is unclear with everything he teaches and is very condescending when you ask questions. I've learned to program much better from other professors at UIC.

This class is the most applicable to the real world, yet it was the hardest to get a grasp of. Professor Yang does not help the cause and for most of the class you are left learning the material on your own.

He is personable, but very disorganized, unhelpful, and too focused on theory. The course deviated from the syllabus twice during the semester. Grading criteria was never clear, and there was no feedback or explanation of grades even when asked. The course seemingly evolved from a introductory coding class to a graduate level statistics course.

This class overall is pretty hard. Min Yang is a good professor and his English isn't terrible. His hw assignments are super hard though. Find the solutions manual and you will be set because he lets you have a cheat sheet for exams and he only picks problems from the hw (just have to ask him for a cheat sheet).
Ordinary professor. Too focused on theory. The class material and textbook examples and exercises are interesting. Take the course if you need to. This course could be taught better.

Jie's lectures were solid, was very willing to answer questions and make sure you fully understood material. He also had exams graded within a couple of days.
